$\|\cdot\|_w$ extending $w$, and let $m_w$ be $1$ if $w$ is real and $2$ if $w$ is complex. For
each height-one prime $v$ of $\mathcal{O}_K$ let $K_v$ be the $v$-adic completion of $K$, with
the normalized absolute value $\|\cdot\|_v$. The adelic norm is the monoid homomorphism from the
topological idele group of $K$ over the Dedekind domain $\mathcal{O}_K$ to the real numbers under
multiplication that sends an idele $a$, with components $a_w \in K_w^\times$ and
$a_v \in K_v^\times$, to $\bigl(\prod_w \|a_w\|_w^{m_w}\bigr) \cdot \prod_v \|a_v\|_v$, where the
product over $v$ is the product of its finitely many factors different from $1$.

articles.title: Finite idele group
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain with fraction field $K$. For each
height-one prime $v$ of $R$, let $K_v$ be the $v$-adic completion of $K$ and $\mathcal{O}_v$ its
ring of integers. The finite idele group is the restricted product of the unit groups $K_v^\times$
over all height-one primes $v$ of $R$ with respect to the subgroups $\mathcal{O}_v^\times$: the
families $(x_v)_v$ with $x_v \in K_v^\times$ for every $v$ and $x_v \in \mathcal{O}_v^\times$ for
all but finitely many $v$, with componentwise multiplication and the restricted-product topology.

articles.title: Diagonal map into the finite ideles
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain with fraction field $K$.
This is the group homomorphism from $K^\times$ to the finite idele group of $R$ and $K$ that sends
$x$ to the family of its images in the $v$-adic completions $K_v$ of $K$, one for each height-one
prime $v$ of $R$.

articles.title: Finite residue field of a completed number ring
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field and $v$ a
nonzero prime ideal of its ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$. The residue field of the ring of
integers $\mathcal{O}_v$ of the $v$-adic completion $K_v$ of $K$ is finite.

articles.title: Infinite idele group
articles.statement:
For a field $K$, the infinite idele group is the product
$\prod_v K_v^\times$ of the unit groups of the completions $K_v$ of $K$ over all infinite places
$v$ of $K$, with componentwise multiplication and the product topology.

articles.title: Diagonal map into the infinite ideles
articles.statement:
For a field $K$, this is the group homomorphism
from $K^\times$ to the infinite idele group of $K$ that sends $x$ to the family of its images in the
completions $K_v$ of $K$, one for each infinite place $v$ of $K$.

articles.title: Compactness of the completed ring of integers
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field and $v$ a
nonzero prime ideal of its ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$. The ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_v$
of the $v$-adic completion $K_v$ of $K$ is a compact subset of $K_v$.

articles.title: Compactness of the local integral units
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field, let $v$ be a
height-one prime of its ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$, and let $\mathcal{O}_v$ be the ring of
integers of the $v$-adic completion $K_v$ of $K$. Then the local integral unit subgroup
$\mathcal{O}_v^\times$ is a compact subset of the unit group $K_v^\times$.

It is the unit group of the compact valuation subring $\mathcal{O}_v$.

articles.title: The local integral units are open
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain with fraction field $K$,
let $v$ be a height-one prime of $R$, and let $\mathcal{O}_v$ be the ring of integers of the
$v$-adic completion $K_v$ of $K$. Then $\mathcal{O}_v^\times$ is an open subset of the unit group
$K_v^\times$.

articles.title: Local integral unit subgroup
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain with fraction field $K$, let $v$
be a height-one prime of $R$, and let $\mathcal{O}_v$ be the ring of integers of the $v$-adic
completion $K_v$ of $K$. The local integral unit subgroup is the subgroup $\mathcal{O}_v^\times$
of $K_v^\times$, consisting of the units $u$ of $K_v$ with $u \in \mathcal{O}_v$ and
$u^{-1} \in \mathcal{O}_v$.

articles.title: Membership in the norm-one ideles
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field. An idele $a$ of $K$ (with
$R = \mathcal{O}_K$) lies in the subgroup of norm-one ideles if and only if its adelic norm
is $1$.

articles.title: Norm-one idele class group
articles.statement:
For a number field $K$, the norm-one idele class group
$C_K^1 = I_K^1 / K^\times$ is the quotient of the group $I_K^1$ of ideles of $K$ with adelic norm
$1$ by its subgroup of principal ideles, the images of the elements of $K^\times$ under the
diagonal embedding.

articles.title: Norm-one ideles
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field. The norm-one ideles of $K$ form the kernel of
the adelic norm, the subgroup of the topological idele group of $K$ (with $R = \mathcal{O}_K$)
consisting of the ideles whose adelic norm is $1$.

articles.title: Principal ideles are trivial in the norm-one idele class group
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field.
For every $x \in K^\times$, the principal idele of $x$, viewed as an element of the group $I_K^1$
of ideles of $K$ with adelic norm $1$, has trivial class in the norm-one idele class group
$C_K^1 = I_K^1 / K^\times$.

articles.title: Principal ideles of norm one
articles.statement:
For a number field $K$, this is the subgroup of the group
$I_K^1$ of ideles of $K$ with adelic norm $1$ consisting of the principal ideles, that is, of the
elements of $I_K^1$ that are images of elements of $K^\times$ under the diagonal embedding.

articles.title: The diagonal map into the ideles is injective
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field and let $R$ be a
Dedekind domain with fraction field $K$. The diagonal homomorphism from $K^\times$ to the
topological idele group of $R$ and $K$, which sends $x$ to its images in the completions of $K$ at
all infinite places of $K$ and at all height-one primes of $R$, is injective.

articles.title: Diagonal map into the ideles
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain with fraction field $K$. This
is the group homomorphism from $K^\times$ to the topological idele group of $R$ and $K$ whose
infinite component sends $x$ to its images in the completions of $K$ at all infinite places of
$K$, and whose finite component sends $x$ to its images in the $v$-adic completions $K_v$ of $K$
at all height-one primes $v$ of $R$.

articles.title: The principal ideles are discrete
articles.statement:
For a number field $K$, the subgroup of principal
ideles is discrete in the idele group of $K$, where the idele group carries the product of the
product topology at the infinite places and the restricted-product topology at the finite
places.

articles.title: Principal ideles have norm one
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field. The subgroup of principal
ideles of $K$ (with $R = \mathcal{O}_K$) is contained in the subgroup of norm-one ideles; that
is, every principal idele has adelic norm $1$.

articles.title: Principal ideles
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain with fraction field $K$. The subgroup of
principal ideles is the image of the diagonal homomorphism from $K^\times$ to the topological idele
group of $R$ and $K$, which sends $x$ to its images in the completions of $K$ at all infinite
places of $K$ and at all height-one primes of $R$.

articles.title: Topological idele class group
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain with fraction field $K$. The
topological idele class group is the quotient group of the topological idele group of $R$ and $K$
by its subgroup of principal ideles, the image of the diagonal homomorphism from $K^\times$.

articles.title: Topological idele group
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain with fraction field $K$. The
topological idele group is the product $\mathbb{I}_{K,\infty} \times \mathbb{I}_{K,f}$ of the
infinite idele group $\mathbb{I}_{K,\infty} = \prod_w K_w^\times$, the product of the unit groups
of the completions of $K$ at its infinite places $w$, and the finite idele group
$\mathbb{I}_{K,f}$, the restricted product of the unit groups $K_v^\times$ of the completions at
the height-one primes $v$ of $R$ with respect to the integral unit groups $\mathcal{O}_v^\times$.
It carries the componentwise group structure and the product of the product topology on
$\mathbb{I}_{K,\infty}$ and the restricted-product topology on $\mathbb{I}_{K,f}$.

As a group it is isomorphic to the unit group of the adele ring of $K$, but its topology differs
from the subspace topology on those units.

articles.title: Ideles as units of the adele ring
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain with fraction field $K$,
and let $\mathbb{A}_K$ be the adele ring of $K$ built from the infinite places of $K$ and the
height-one primes of $R$. For an infinite place $w$ of $K$ write $K_w$ for the completion of $K$
at $w$, and for a height-one prime $v$ of $R$ write $K_v$ for the $v$-adic completion of $K$.
This is the group isomorphism from the unit group $\mathbb{A}_K^\times$ to the topological idele
group that sends a unit adele $a$ to the idele whose component at each infinite place $w$ is the
component $a_w \in K_w^\times$ of $a$ and whose component at each height-one prime $v$ is the
component $a_v \in K_v^\times$ of $a$.

It is stated only as an isomorphism of groups: the topological idele group carries the
restricted-product topology, not the topology induced on the units of the adele ring.

articles.title: Invertible fractional ideals have nonzero absolute norm
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain
that is a free $\mathbb{Z}$-module of finite rank, and let $F$ be its field of fractions. For
every invertible fractional ideal $I$ of $R$ in $F$, the absolute norm of $I$, a rational
number, is nonzero.

articles.title: Invertible fractional ideals have positive absolute norm
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain
that is a free $\mathbb{Z}$-module of finite rank, and let $F$ be its field of fractions. For
every invertible fractional ideal $I$ of $R$ in $F$, the absolute norm of $I$, a rational
number, is positive.

articles.title: Arakelov divisor
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field with ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$. An
Arakelov divisor on $K$ is a pair $(I, r)$, where $I$ is an invertible fractional ideal of
$\mathcal{O}_K$ in $K$ and $r$ assigns a positive real number $r_w$ to each infinite place $w$
of $K$.

articles.title: Archimedean factor homomorphism
articles.statement:
For a number field $K$, the map sending an Arakelov
divisor on $K$ to its archimedean factor is a monoid homomorphism from the Arakelov divisors on
$K$, multiplied componentwise, to the positive real numbers under multiplication.

articles.title: Archimedean factor as a real number
articles.statement:
Let $D = (I, r)$ be an Arakelov divisor on a number
field $K$, and for each infinite place $w$ of $K$ let $m_w$ be $1$ if $w$ is real and $2$ if $w$
is complex. Viewed as a real number, the archimedean factor of $D$ equals the real product
$\prod_w r_w^{m_w}$ over all infinite places $w$ of $K$.

articles.title: Archimedean factor
articles.statement:
Let $D = (I, r)$ be an Arakelov divisor on a number field $K$. Its
archimedean factor is the positive real number $\prod_w r_w^{m_w}$, where the product runs over
all infinite places $w$ of $K$ and $m_w$ is $1$ if $w$ is real and $2$ if $w$ is complex.

articles.title: Finite component of a principal divisor
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field with ring of integers
$\mathcal{O}_K$. For every nonzero $x \in K$, the fractional ideal component of the principal
Arakelov divisor of $x$ is the principal fractional ideal $x\mathcal{O}_K$.

articles.title: Infinite component of a principal divisor
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field, $x \in K$ nonzero
and $w$ an infinite place of $K$. The positive real number that the principal Arakelov divisor
of $x$ assigns to $w$ is $w(x)$, the absolute value of $x$ at $w$.

articles.title: Degree-zero Arakelov divisors
articles.statement:
For a number field $K$, the degree-zero subgroup of the
group of Arakelov divisors on $K$ is the kernel of the size homomorphism, that is, the subgroup
of Arakelov divisors of size $1$.

articles.title: Large Arakelov divisors have a nonzero section
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field with $s$
complex places and discriminant $d_K$, and let $D$ be an Arakelov divisor on $K$. If the size
of $D$ is strictly greater than $(2/\pi)^s \sqrt{|d_K|}$, then the section set of $D$ contains
a nonzero element of $K$.

## Sources

- Proposition 15.9 of ATLAS `NumberTheoryI`.

articles.title: Ideal norm homomorphism
articles.statement:
For a number field $K$, the map sending an Arakelov divisor
$(I, r)$ on $K$ to the absolute norm of $I$, viewed as a positive real number, is a monoid
homomorphism from the Arakelov divisors on $K$, multiplied componentwise, to the positive real
numbers under multiplication.

articles.title: Real value of the ideal norm
articles.statement:
For every Arakelov divisor $D$ of a number field $K$ with
fractional ideal $I$, the ideal norm of $D$, viewed as a real number, equals the absolute norm
$N(I) \in \mathbb{Q}$ of $I$, viewed as a real number.

articles.title: Ideal norm of an Arakelov divisor
articles.statement:
For an Arakelov divisor $D$ of a number field $K$ with
invertible fractional ideal $I$, the ideal norm of $D$ is the absolute norm $N(I)$ of $I$,
regarded as a positive real number; it is positive because $I$ is invertible.

articles.title: Membership in the section set
articles.statement:
Let $D$ be an Arakelov divisor of a number field $K$, with
invertible fractional ideal $I$ and positive real number $r_w$ at each infinite place $w$ of $K$.
An element $x \in K$ lies in the section set of $D$ if and only if $x \in I$ and
$w(x) \le r_w$ for every infinite place $w$ of $K$.

articles.title: Archimedean part of a principal divisor
articles.statement:
For a nonzero element $x$ of a number field $K$,
this is the family that assigns to each infinite place $w$ of $K$ the positive real
number $w(x)$.

articles.title: Principal Arakelov divisor
articles.statement:
For a nonzero element $x$ of a number field $K$, the principal
Arakelov divisor of $x$ consists of the principal fractional ideal $x\mathcal{O}_K$ together with
the positive real number $w(x)$ at each infinite place $w$ of $K$.

articles.title: Principal divisor homomorphism
articles.statement:
For a number field $K$, the map sending a nonzero element
$x \in K$ to its principal Arakelov divisor is a group homomorphism from the multiplicative
group $K^\times$ to the group of Arakelov divisors of $K$.

articles.title: Principal Arakelov divisors have degree zero
articles.statement:
For a number field $K$, the subgroup of
principal Arakelov divisors of $K$ is contained in the degree-zero subgroup.

articles.title: Subgroup of principal Arakelov divisors
articles.statement:
For a number field $K$, the principal subgroup is
the image of the principal divisor homomorphism, that is, the subgroup of the group of Arakelov
divisors of $K$ consisting of the principal Arakelov divisors of the nonzero elements of $K$.

articles.title: Finiteness of section sets
articles.statement:
For every Arakelov divisor $D$ of a number field $K$, the
section set of $D$ is finite.

Multiplying by a nonzero $d \in \mathcal{O}_K$ that clears the denominators of the fractional
ideal of $D$ sends the section set into $\mathcal{O}_K$, and the bounds at the infinite places
give a uniform bound $B$ on $|\sigma(dx)|$ for all $x$ in the section set and all complex
embeddings $\sigma$ of $K$; only finitely many algebraic integers of $K$ have all conjugates of
absolute value at most $B$.

articles.title: Section set of an Arakelov divisor
articles.statement:
Let $D$ be an Arakelov divisor of a number field $K$,
with invertible fractional ideal $I$ and positive real number $r_w$ at each infinite place $w$
of $K$. The section set of $D$ is the set of $x \in I$ such that $w(x) \le r_w$ for every
infinite place $w$ of $K$.

At a complex place the bound is on $w(x)$ itself, not on $w(x)^2$; the squaring at complex
places enters only in the size of $D$.

articles.title: Size as a quotient of homomorphisms
articles.statement:
For every Arakelov divisor $D$ of a number field
$K$, the size of $D$ equals the archimedean-factor homomorphism evaluated at $D$ divided by the
ideal-norm homomorphism evaluated at $D$, the quotient taken in the group of positive reals.

articles.title: Explicit formula for the size of an Arakelov divisor
articles.statement:
Let $D = (I, (r_w)_w)$ be an
Arakelov divisor of a number field $K$, where $I$ is an invertible fractional ideal of the ring
of integers of $K$ and $r_w > 0$ for each infinite place $w$ of $K$. For each $w$ let $m_w$ be
$1$ if $w$ is real and $2$ if $w$ is complex, and let $N(I)$ be the absolute norm of $I$. Then
the size of $D$, as a real number, is

$$\frac{\prod_w r_w^{m_w}}{N(I)},$$

where the product runs over all infinite places $w$ of $K$.

articles.title: Size of an Arakelov divisor
articles.statement:
For a number field $K$, the size homomorphism sends an
Arakelov divisor $D = (I, (r_w)_w)$, with $I$ an invertible fractional ideal of the ring of
integers of $K$ and $r_w > 0$ for each infinite place $w$, to the positive real number
$\prod_w r_w^{m_w} / N(I)$, where $w$ runs over the infinite places of $K$, $m_w$ is $1$ for a
real place and $2$ for a complex place, and $N(I)$ is the absolute norm of $I$. It is a group
homomorphism from Arakelov divisors to the multiplicative group of positive reals.

articles.title: Principal Arakelov divisors have size one
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field with ring of
integers $\mathcal{O}_K$. For every nonzero $x \in K$, the principal Arakelov divisor of $x$,
formed by the principal fractional ideal $x\mathcal{O}_K$ and the values $w(x)$ at the infinite
places $w$ of $K$, has size $1$.

This is the product formula: with $m_w$ equal to $1$ at real and $2$ at complex places, the
archimedean factor $\prod_w w(x)^{m_w}$ equals $|N_{K/\mathbb{Q}}(x)|$, where $N_{K/\mathbb{Q}}$
is the field norm from $K$ to $\mathbb{Q}$, and so does the absolute norm of $x\mathcal{O}_K$.

articles.title: The Artin map factors the free-group Frobenius map
articles.statement:
Let $L/K$ be an abelian Galois
extension of number fields and $\mathfrak m$ a modulus of $K$ with finite part $\mathfrak m_0$,
such that every prime of $\mathcal O_K$ not dividing $\mathfrak m_0$ is unramified in $L$. Let
$F$ be the free group on the primes $\mathfrak p$ of $\mathcal O_K$ not dividing $\mathfrak m_0$,
and let $I^{\mathfrak m}$ be the group of fractional ideals of $K$ coprime to $\mathfrak m_0$.
Then the Artin map $I^{\mathfrak m} \to \mathrm{Gal}(L/K)$ composed with the homomorphism
$F \to I^{\mathfrak m}$ sending each generator $\mathfrak p$ to the ideal $\mathfrak p$ equals the
homomorphism $F \to \mathrm{Gal}(L/K)$ sending each generator $\mathfrak p$ to the arithmetic
Frobenius at a chosen prime of $\mathcal O_L$ above $\mathfrak p$.

articles.title: The Artin map at a prime
articles.statement:
Let $L/K$ be an abelian Galois extension of number fields and
$\mathfrak m$ a modulus of $K$ with finite part $\mathfrak m_0$, such that every prime of
$\mathcal O_K$ not dividing $\mathfrak m_0$ is unramified in $L$. For every prime $\mathfrak p$
of $\mathcal O_K$ not dividing $\mathfrak m_0$, the Artin map sends $\mathfrak p$, viewed as a
fractional ideal coprime to $\mathfrak m_0$, to the arithmetic Frobenius in $\mathrm{Gal}(L/K)$
at a chosen prime of $\mathcal O_L$ above $\mathfrak p$.

articles.title: Artin map
articles.statement:
Let $L/K$ be an abelian Galois extension of number fields and $\mathfrak m$
a modulus of $K$ with finite part $\mathfrak m_0$, such that every prime of $\mathcal O_K$ not
dividing $\mathfrak m_0$ is unramified in $L$. Let $I^{\mathfrak m}$ be the group of fractional
ideals of $K$ coprime to $\mathfrak m_0$ and $F$ the free group on the primes $\mathfrak p$ of
$\mathcal O_K$ not dividing $\mathfrak m_0$. The homomorphism $F \to I^{\mathfrak m}$ sending
each generator $\mathfrak p$ to the ideal $\mathfrak p$ is surjective, and its kernel lies in the
kernel of the homomorphism $F \to \mathrm{Gal}(L/K)$ sending each generator $\mathfrak p$ to the
arithmetic Frobenius at a chosen prime of $\mathcal O_L$ above $\mathfrak p$. The Artin map is
the homomorphism $I^{\mathfrak m} \to \mathrm{Gal}(L/K)$ induced by the second map through the
first.

articles.title: Unramified outside a modulus implies unramified at coprime primes
articles.statement:
Let $m$ be a
modulus of a number field $K$ and let $L / K$ be an extension of number fields that is
unramified outside $m$. Then every finite prime $\mathfrak p$ of $K$ not dividing the finite
part of $m$ is unramified in $\mathcal O_L$.

articles.title: The coprime primes generate the coprime ideals
articles.statement:
Let $\mathfrak m$ be a modulus of a
number field $K$, and let $I_K^{\mathfrak m}$ be the group of invertible fractional ideals
of $K$ coprime to the finite part of $\mathfrak m$. Then $I_K^{\mathfrak m}$ is generated,
as a group, by the nonzero prime ideals $\mathfrak p$ of the ring of integers
$\mathcal O_K$ that do not divide the finite part of $\mathfrak m$.

articles.title: The prime coprime units are the image of the coprime primes
articles.statement:
Let $\mathfrak m$ be a
modulus of a number field $K$, let $I_K^{\mathfrak m}$ be the group of invertible fractional
ideals of $K$ coprime to the finite part of $\mathfrak m$, and let $P$ be the set of nonzero
prime ideals of the ring of integers $\mathcal O_K$ that do not divide the finite part of
$\mathfrak m$. Then the set of prime coprime units of $\mathfrak m$ equals the range of the map
$P \to I_K^{\mathfrak m}$ sending each $\mathfrak p \in P$ to $\mathfrak p$ viewed as an element
of $I_K^{\mathfrak m}$.

## Sources

- direct native counterpart of ATLAS `primesCoprime_eq_range`.

articles.title: Prime coprime units
articles.statement:
Let $\mathfrak m$ be a modulus of a number field $K$, and let
$I_K^{\mathfrak m}$ be the group of invertible fractional ideals of $K$ coprime to the finite
part of $\mathfrak m$. The prime coprime units of $\mathfrak m$ are the elements of
$I_K^{\mathfrak m}$ of the form $\mathfrak p$, where $\mathfrak p$ is a nonzero prime ideal of
the ring of integers $\mathcal O_K$ that does not divide the finite part of $\mathfrak m$.

articles.title: Primes coprime to a modulus
articles.statement:
Let $\mathfrak m$ be a modulus of a number field $K$. The
primes coprime to $\mathfrak m$ are the nonzero prime ideals $\mathfrak p$ of the ring of
integers $\mathcal O_K$ that do not contain the finite part of $\mathfrak m$, that is, that do
not divide it. They index the generators of a free group that maps to the group of
fractional ideals coprime to the finite part of $\mathfrak m$.

articles.title: Factorization of a prime of a number field
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field with ring of
integers $\mathcal O_K$ and let $\mathfrak p$ be a height-one prime of $\mathcal O_K$. The
factorization isomorphism sends $\mathfrak p$, regarded as an invertible fractional ideal of $K$,
to the function on height-one primes of $\mathcal O_K$ that is $1$ at $\mathfrak p$ and $0$
elsewhere.

articles.title: The kernel of the free-group map lies in the commutator subgroup
articles.statement:
Let $\mathfrak m$ be
a modulus of a number field $K$, let $P$ be the set of nonzero prime ideals of the ring of
integers $\mathcal O_K$ that do not divide the finite part of $\mathfrak m$, and let
$I_K^{\mathfrak m}$ be the group of invertible fractional ideals of $K$ coprime to the finite
part of $\mathfrak m$. The kernel of the homomorphism $F(P) \to I_K^{\mathfrak m}$ from the free
group on $P$ sending each generator $\mathfrak p$ to $\mathfrak p$ is contained in the
commutator subgroup $[F(P), F(P)]$.

## Sources

- direct native counterpart of ATLAS `freeGroupToCoprime_ker_le_commutator` (source lines 429--487). The prime basis-vector computation at source lines 416--427 is replaced by `FractionalIdeal.factorizationMulEquiv_primeUnitFractionalIdeal`. The proof builds the ATLAS retraction to the abelianization through `FractionalIdeal.factorizationMulEquiv`, `Finsupp.comapDomain.addMonoidHom`, `Finsupp.toFreeAbelianGroup`, and `Abelianization.of`; the retraction itself stays private to this proof.

articles.title: Kernel containment for the free-group Frobenius map
articles.statement:
Let $L/K$ be an abelian Galois
extension of number fields and $\mathfrak m$ a modulus of $K$ with finite part $\mathfrak m_0$,
such that every prime of $\mathcal O_K$ not dividing $\mathfrak m_0$ is unramified in $L$. Let
$F$ be the free group on the primes $\mathfrak p$ of $\mathcal O_K$ not dividing $\mathfrak m_0$.
Then the kernel of the homomorphism from $F$ to the group of fractional ideals of $K$ coprime to
$\mathfrak m_0$ sending each generator $\mathfrak p$ to the ideal $\mathfrak p$ is contained in
the kernel of the homomorphism $F \to \mathrm{Gal}(L/K)$ sending each generator $\mathfrak p$ to
the arithmetic Frobenius at a chosen prime of $\mathcal O_L$ above $\mathfrak p$.

The first kernel lies in the commutator subgroup of $F$, which the second map kills because
$\mathrm{Gal}(L/K)$ is abelian.

articles.title: The kernel of the free-group map is the commutator subgroup
articles.statement:
Let $\mathfrak m$ be a
modulus of a number field $K$, let $P$ be the set of nonzero prime ideals of the ring of
integers $\mathcal O_K$ that do not divide the finite part of $\mathfrak m$, and let
$I_K^{\mathfrak m}$ be the group of invertible fractional ideals of $K$ coprime to the finite
part of $\mathfrak m$. The kernel of the homomorphism $F(P) \to I_K^{\mathfrak m}$ from the free
group on $P$ sending each generator $\mathfrak p$ to $\mathfrak p$ equals the commutator
subgroup $[F(P), F(P)]$.

The commutator subgroup lies in the kernel because $I_K^{\mathfrak m}$ is abelian.

articles.title: The free-group map on generators
articles.statement:
Let $\mathfrak m$ be a modulus of a number field $K$,
let $P$ be the set of nonzero prime ideals of the ring of integers $\mathcal O_K$ that do not
divide the finite part of $\mathfrak m$, and let $I_K^{\mathfrak m}$ be the group of invertible
fractional ideals of $K$ coprime to the finite part of $\mathfrak m$. For every
$\mathfrak p \in P$, the homomorphism $F(P) \to I_K^{\mathfrak m}$ from the free group on $P$
sends the generator attached to $\mathfrak p$ to $\mathfrak p$, viewed as an element of
$I_K^{\mathfrak m}$.

articles.title: The free group on the coprime primes surjects onto the coprime ideals
articles.statement:
Let
$\mathfrak m$ be a modulus of a number field $K$, let $P$ be the set of nonzero prime ideals
of the ring of integers $\mathcal O_K$ that do not divide the finite part of $\mathfrak m$, and
let $I_K^{\mathfrak m}$ be the group of invertible fractional ideals of $K$ coprime to the
finite part of $\mathfrak m$. The homomorphism $F(P) \to I_K^{\mathfrak m}$ from the free group
on $P$ sending each generator $\mathfrak p$ to $\mathfrak p$ is surjective.

articles.title: The free group on the coprime primes maps to the coprime ideals
articles.statement:
Let $\mathfrak m$ be
a modulus of a number field $K$, let $P$ be the set of nonzero prime ideals of the ring of
integers $\mathcal O_K$ that do not divide the finite part of $\mathfrak m$, and let
$I_K^{\mathfrak m}$ be the group of invertible fractional ideals of $K$ coprime to the finite
part of $\mathfrak m$. This is the group homomorphism $F(P) \to I_K^{\mathfrak m}$ from the free
group on $P$ that sends each generator $\mathfrak p$ to $\mathfrak p$, viewed as an element of
$I_K^{\mathfrak m}$.

articles.title: The Frobenius homomorphism on generators
articles.statement:
Let $m$ be a modulus of a number field
$K$ and let $L / K$ be a Galois extension of number fields that is unramified outside $m$.
For every finite prime $\mathfrak p$ of $K$ not dividing the finite part of $m$, the
Frobenius homomorphism from the free group on these primes to $\mathrm{Gal}(L/K)$ sends the
generator $\mathfrak p$ to the chosen Frobenius element at $\mathfrak p$.

articles.title: Frobenius homomorphism on the free group of coprime primes
articles.statement:
Let $m$ be a modulus
of a number field $K$ and let $L / K$ be a Galois extension of number fields that is
unramified outside $m$. The Frobenius homomorphism is the group homomorphism from the free
group on the finite primes of $K$ not dividing the finite part of $m$ to $\mathrm{Gal}(L/K)$
that sends each such prime $\mathfrak p$ to the chosen Frobenius element at $\mathfrak p$.

articles.title: The chosen Frobenius is an arithmetic Frobenius at an unramified prime
articles.statement:
Let $m$ be
a modulus of a number field $K$, let $L / K$ be a Galois extension of number fields that is
unramified outside $m$, and let $\mathfrak p$ be a finite prime of $K$ not dividing the
finite part of $m$, with chosen Frobenius element $\sigma \in \mathrm{Gal}(L/K)$. Then there
is a prime $\mathfrak P$ of $\mathcal O_L$ lying over $\mathfrak p$ such that
$\mathcal O_L / \mathfrak P$ is finite, $\mathfrak P$ is unramified over $\mathcal O_K$, and
$\sigma(x) \equiv x^q \pmod{\mathfrak P}$ for all $x \in \mathcal O_L$, where $q$ is the
number of elements of $\mathcal O_K / \mathfrak p$.

articles.title: Chosen Frobenius element at a coprime prime
articles.statement:
Let $m$ be a modulus of a number field
$K$, let $L / K$ be a Galois extension of number fields that is unramified outside $m$, and
let $\mathfrak p$ be a finite prime of $K$ not dividing the finite part of $m$. Fix a prime
$\mathfrak P$ of $\mathcal O_L$ lying over $\mathfrak p$. The chosen Frobenius element at
$\mathfrak p$ is a fixed element $\sigma \in \mathrm{Gal}(L/K)$ that is an arithmetic
Frobenius at $\mathfrak P$, that is, $\sigma(x) \equiv x^q \pmod{\mathfrak P}$ for all
$x \in \mathcal O_L$, where $q$ is the number of elements of $\mathcal O_K / \mathfrak p$.

The value may depend on the choice of $\mathfrak P$.

articles.title: Extensions unramified outside a modulus
articles.statement:
Let $m$ be a modulus of a number field $K$.
An extension of number fields $L / K$ is unramified outside $m$ when every finite prime
$\mathfrak p$ of $K$ not dividing the finite part of $m$ is unramified in $\mathcal O_L$,
that is, every prime of $\mathcal O_L$ lying over $\mathfrak p$ is unramified over
$\mathcal O_K$.

articles.title: Primes not dividing the modulus are coprime to it
articles.statement:
Let $\mathfrak m$ be a modulus of a
number field $K$ and let $\mathfrak p$ be a height-one prime of the ring of integers
$\mathcal O_K$ that does not contain the finite part of $\mathfrak m$. Then $\mathfrak p$, viewed
as an invertible fractional ideal of $K$, lies in the group of fractional ideals coprime to
$\mathfrak m$: its exponent at every height-one prime containing the finite part of
$\mathfrak m$ is zero.

articles.title: Membership in the prime coprime units
articles.statement:
Let $\mathfrak m$ be a modulus of a number field
$K$, and let $I_K^{\mathfrak m}$ be the group of invertible fractional ideals of $K$ coprime to
the finite part of $\mathfrak m$. An element $I$ of $I_K^{\mathfrak m}$ is a prime coprime unit
of $\mathfrak m$ if and only if $I = \mathfrak p$ for some nonzero prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ of
the ring of integers $\mathcal O_K$ that does not divide the finite part of $\mathfrak m$.

articles.title: The prime as a coprime fractional ideal
articles.statement:
Let $\mathfrak m$ be a modulus of a number
field $K$ and let $\mathfrak p$ be a height-one prime of the ring of integers $\mathcal O_K$ that
does not contain the finite part of $\mathfrak m$. This is $\mathfrak p$, viewed as an invertible
fractional ideal of $K$, regarded as an element of the group of fractional ideals coprime to
$\mathfrak m$.

articles.title: A prime as an invertible fractional ideal
articles.statement:
For a number field $K$ with ring of integers
$\mathcal O_K$ and a height-one prime $\mathfrak p$ of $\mathcal O_K$, this is $\mathfrak p$
regarded as a fractional ideal of $K$; it is nonzero, hence a unit in the group of nonzero
fractional ideals of $K$.

articles.title: Restriction of the Artin map at a prime
articles.statement:
Let $K \subseteq L \subseteq M$ be a tower of
number fields with $L/K$ and $M/K$ abelian Galois, and let $\mathfrak m$ be a modulus of $K$ with
finite part $\mathfrak m_0$ such that every prime of $\mathcal O_K$ not dividing $\mathfrak m_0$
is unramified in $L$ and in $M$. For every prime $\mathfrak p$ of $\mathcal O_K$ not dividing
$\mathfrak m_0$, restricting to $L$ the image of $\mathfrak p$ under the Artin map of $M/K$ gives
the image of $\mathfrak p$ under the Artin map of $L/K$.

articles.title: The Artin map commutes with restriction
articles.statement:
Let $K \subseteq L \subseteq M$ be a tower of
number fields with $L/K$ and $M/K$ abelian Galois, and let $\mathfrak m$ be a modulus of $K$
with finite part $\mathfrak m_0$ such that every prime of $\mathcal O_K$ not dividing
$\mathfrak m_0$ is unramified in $L$ and in $M$. Then the Artin map of $M/K$ followed by
restriction $\mathrm{Gal}(M/K) \to \mathrm{Gal}(L/K)$ equals the Artin map of $L/K$, as
homomorphisms from the group of fractional ideals of $K$ coprime to $\mathfrak m_0$ to
$\mathrm{Gal}(L/K)$.

articles.title: Restriction of Frobenius elements in a tower
articles.statement:
Let $K \subseteq L \subseteq M$ be a tower
of number fields with $L/K$ abelian Galois and $M/K$ Galois, and let $\mathfrak m$ be a modulus
of $K$ such that $L$ and $M$ are both unramified outside $\mathfrak m$. For every finite prime
$\mathfrak p$ of $K$ not dividing the finite part of $\mathfrak m$, the restriction to $L$ of the
chosen Frobenius element of $\mathfrak p$ in $\mathrm{Gal}(M/K)$ equals the chosen Frobenius
element of $\mathfrak p$ in $\mathrm{Gal}(L/K)$.

The abelianity of $L/K$ is used only to make conjugation of the Frobenius element in
$\mathrm{Gal}(L/K)$ trivial.

articles.title: The change of modulus is equivalent to the original pair
articles.statement:
Let $\mathfrak m_1$ and
$\mathfrak m_2$ be moduli of a number field $K$ with $\mathfrak m_2 \mid \mathfrak m_1$, and let
$C_1$ be a congruence subgroup for $\mathfrak m_1$. Write $I^{\mathfrak m_1}$ for the group of
nonzero fractional ideals of $K$ coprime to the finite part of $\mathfrak m_1$ and
$P_{\mathfrak m_2}$ for the ray group of $\mathfrak m_2$, and view all of these as subgroups of
the group of nonzero fractional ideals of $K$. If
$I^{\mathfrak m_1} \cap P_{\mathfrak m_2} \subseteq C_1$, then the pair $(\mathfrak m_1, C_1)$ is
equivalent to the pair $(\mathfrak m_2, C_2)$, where $C_2$ is the change of modulus of $C_1$ to
$\mathfrak m_2$.

articles.title: Ambient subgroup of a change of modulus to a divisor
articles.statement:
Let $\mathfrak m_1$ and
$\mathfrak m_2$ be moduli of a number field $K$ with $\mathfrak m_2 \mid \mathfrak m_1$, and let
$C_1$ be a congruence subgroup for $\mathfrak m_1$. Viewed as subgroups of the group of nonzero
fractional ideals of $K$, the change of modulus of $C_1$ to $\mathfrak m_2$ equals the subgroup
generated by $C_1$ and the ray group $P_{\mathfrak m_2}$ of $\mathfrak m_2$.

articles.title: Ambient subgroup of a change of modulus
articles.statement:
Let $\mathfrak m_1$ and $\mathfrak m_2$ be
moduli of a number field $K$ and let $C_1$ be a congruence subgroup for $\mathfrak m_1$. Write
$I^{\mathfrak m_2}$ for the group of nonzero fractional ideals of $K$ coprime to the finite part
of $\mathfrak m_2$ and $P_{\mathfrak m_2}$ for the ray group of $\mathfrak m_2$. Viewing all of
these as subgroups of the group of nonzero fractional ideals of $K$, the change of modulus of
$C_1$ to $\mathfrak m_2$ is the subgroup generated by $C_1 \cap I^{\mathfrak m_2}$ and
$P_{\mathfrak m_2}$.

articles.title: Change of modulus of a congruence subgroup
articles.statement:
Let $C_1$ be a congruence subgroup for a
modulus $\mathfrak m_1$ of a number field $K$, viewed as a subgroup of the group of nonzero
fractional ideals of $K$, and let $\mathfrak m_2$ be any modulus of $K$. Write
$I^{\mathfrak m_2}$ for the group of nonzero fractional ideals of $K$ coprime to the finite part
of $\mathfrak m_2$ and $P_{\mathfrak m_2} \subseteq I^{\mathfrak m_2}$ for the ray group of
$\mathfrak m_2$. The change of modulus of $C_1$ to $\mathfrak m_2$ is the congruence subgroup for
$\mathfrak m_2$ generated, inside $I^{\mathfrak m_2}$, by $C_1 \cap I^{\mathfrak m_2}$ and
$P_{\mathfrak m_2}$.

articles.title: Congruence subgroup pair
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field. A congruence subgroup pair for $K$
consists of a modulus $\mathfrak m$ of $K$ together with a congruence subgroup for
$\mathfrak m$, that is, a subgroup of the group of invertible fractional ideals of $K$ coprime to
the finite part of $\mathfrak m$ that contains the ray group of $\mathfrak m$.

articles.title: Congruence subgroup
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field and $\mathfrak m$ a modulus of $K$. A
congruence subgroup for $\mathfrak m$ is a subgroup $H$ of the group of invertible fractional
ideals of $K$ coprime to the finite part of $\mathfrak m$ such that $H$ contains the ray group
of $\mathfrak m$.

articles.title: Coprimality passes to divisors of a modulus
articles.statement:
Let $\mathfrak m_1$ and $\mathfrak m_2$ be
moduli of a number field $K$ with $\mathfrak m_2 \mid \mathfrak m_1$. Then every nonzero
fractional ideal of $K$ coprime to the finite part of $\mathfrak m_1$ is coprime to the finite
part of $\mathfrak m_2$.

articles.title: Criterion for an equivalent congruence subgroup at a divisor of the modulus
articles.statement:
Let
$\mathfrak m_1$ and $\mathfrak m_2$ be moduli of a number field $K$ with
$\mathfrak m_2 \mid \mathfrak m_1$, and let $C_1$ be a congruence subgroup for $\mathfrak m_1$.
Write $I^{\mathfrak m_1}$ for the group of nonzero fractional ideals of $K$ coprime to the finite
part of $\mathfrak m_1$ and $P_{\mathfrak m_2}$ for the ray group of $\mathfrak m_2$, and view all
of these as subgroups of the group of nonzero fractional ideals of $K$. Then there is a
congruence subgroup $C_2$ for $\mathfrak m_2$ such that the pair $(\mathfrak m_1, C_1)$ is
equivalent to the pair $(\mathfrak m_2, C_2)$ if and only if
$I^{\mathfrak m_1} \cap P_{\mathfrak m_2} \subseteq C_1$.

## Sources

- ATLAS NumberTheoryI item N422, Lemma 22.5.

articles.title: Image of a congruence subgroup in the ray class group
articles.statement:
Let $H$ be a congruence subgroup
for a modulus $\mathfrak m$ of a number field $K$, and let $\pi$ be the canonical projection from
the group of invertible fractional ideals of $K$ coprime to the finite part of $\mathfrak m$ onto
the ray class group of $\mathfrak m$. The image of $H$ is the subgroup $\pi(H)$ of the ray class
group.

articles.title: Criterion for equivalence of congruence subgroup pairs
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field, and for
a modulus $\mathfrak m$ of $K$ write $I^{\mathfrak m}$ for the group of nonzero fractional ideals
of $K$ coprime to the finite part of $\mathfrak m$. Two pairs $(\mathfrak m, H)$ and
$(\mathfrak n, H')$, each consisting of a modulus of $K$ and a congruence subgroup for it, are
equivalent if and only if $I^{\mathfrak m} \cap H' = I^{\mathfrak n} \cap H$ in the group of all
nonzero fractional ideals of $K$.

articles.title: Equivalence of congruence subgroup pairs
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field. For a modulus
$\mathfrak m$ of $K$, write $I^{\mathfrak m}$ for the group of nonzero fractional ideals of $K$
coprime to the finite part of $\mathfrak m$. Two pairs $(\mathfrak m, H)$ and $(\mathfrak n, H')$,
each consisting of a modulus of $K$ and a congruence subgroup for it, are equivalent when
$I^{\mathfrak m} \cap H' = I^{\mathfrak n} \cap H$, where both congruence subgroups are viewed as
subgroups of the group of all nonzero fractional ideals of $K$.

articles.title: Largest congruence subgroup
articles.statement:
For a modulus $\mathfrak m$ of a number field $K$, the largest
congruence subgroup for $\mathfrak m$ is the whole group of invertible fractional ideals of $K$
coprime to the finite part of $\mathfrak m$, which contains the ray group of $\mathfrak m$.

articles.title: Membership in the image of a congruence subgroup
articles.statement:
Let $H$ be a congruence subgroup for a
modulus $\mathfrak m$ of a number field $K$, and let $\pi$ be the canonical projection from the
group of invertible fractional ideals of $K$ coprime to the finite part of $\mathfrak m$ onto the
ray class group of $\mathfrak m$. An element $x$ of the ray class group lies in the image $\pi(H)$
if and only if $\pi(y) = x$ for some $y \in H$.

articles.title: The ray group consists of coprime ideals
articles.statement:
For every modulus $\mathfrak m$ of a number
field $K$, the ray group of $\mathfrak m$, viewed as a subgroup of the group of nonzero
fractional ideals of $K$, is contained in the group of nonzero fractional ideals coprime to the
finite part of $\mathfrak m$.

articles.title: A congruence subgroup contains the ray group
articles.statement:
Let $C$ be a congruence subgroup for a
modulus $\mathfrak m$ of a number field $K$. Viewed as subgroups of the group of nonzero
fractional ideals of $K$, the ray group of $\mathfrak m$ is contained in $C$.

articles.title: Ray group among all fractional ideals
articles.statement:
For a modulus $\mathfrak m$ of a number field
$K$, the ambient ray group of $\mathfrak m$ is the image of the ray group of $\mathfrak m$ under
the inclusion of the group of nonzero fractional ideals of $K$ coprime to the finite part of
$\mathfrak m$ into the group of all nonzero fractional ideals of $K$.

articles.title: Equivalence of congruence subgroup pairs is reflexive
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field. Every
pair consisting of a modulus of $K$ and a congruence subgroup for it is equivalent to itself.

articles.title: Smallest congruence subgroup
articles.statement:
For a modulus $\mathfrak m$ of a number field $K$, the
smallest congruence subgroup for $\mathfrak m$ is the ray group of $\mathfrak m$ itself, a
subgroup of the group of invertible fractional ideals of $K$ coprime to the finite part of
$\mathfrak m$.

articles.title: Equivalence of congruence subgroup pairs is symmetric
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field. If a
pair $P$, consisting of a modulus of $K$ and a congruence subgroup for it, is equivalent to such
a pair $Q$, then $Q$ is equivalent to $P$.

articles.title: Congruence subgroup as a subgroup of all invertible fractional ideals
articles.statement:
For a congruence
subgroup $H$ for a modulus $\mathfrak m$ of a number field $K$, this is the image of $H$ under the
inclusion of the group of invertible fractional ideals of $K$ coprime to the finite part of
$\mathfrak m$ into the group of all invertible fractional ideals of $K$.

articles.title: Abelian unramified extensions embed in the Hilbert class field
articles.statement:
Let $K$ and $L$ be number
fields with $L$ an extension of $K$ that is a Hilbert class field of $K$. If $M$ is a number field
that is a finite-dimensional abelian Galois extension of $K$, such that every nonzero prime ideal
of the ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$ is unramified in $\mathcal{O}_M$ and every infinite place
of $M$ is unramified over $K$, then there is a $K$-algebra homomorphism $M \to L$.

articles.title: Hilbert class field of a number field
articles.statement:
Let $K$ and $L$ be number fields with $L$ an
extension of $K$. Then $L$ is a Hilbert class field of $K$ if $L/K$ is a finite-dimensional
abelian Galois extension, every nonzero prime ideal of the ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$ is
unramified in $\mathcal{O}_L$, every infinite place of $L$ is unramified over $K$, and $L$ is
maximal with these properties: every number field $M$ that is a finite-dimensional abelian Galois
extension of $K$, such that every nonzero prime ideal of $\mathcal{O}_K$ is unramified in
$\mathcal{O}_M$ and every infinite place of $M$ is unramified over $K$, admits a $K$-algebra
homomorphism $M \to L$.

articles.title: Neukirch–Uchida theorem
articles.statement:
Let $K_1$ and $K_2$ be number fields with separable closures
$\overline{K_1}$ and $\overline{K_2}$, and let
$\varphi \colon \mathrm{Gal}(\overline{K_1}/K_1) \to \mathrm{Gal}(\overline{K_2}/K_2)$ be a group
isomorphism that is a homeomorphism for the Krull topologies. Then there is a unique field
isomorphism $\sigma \colon \overline{K_2} \to \overline{K_1}$ that maps the image of $K_2$ in
$\overline{K_2}$ onto the image of $K_1$ in $\overline{K_1}$ and satisfies
$\varphi(g) = \sigma^{-1} \circ g \circ \sigma$ for every $g \in \mathrm{Gal}(\overline{K_1}/K_1)$.

## Sources

- Jürgen Neukirch, Alexander Schmidt, Kay Wingberg. *Cohomology of Number Fields*, Theorem 12.2.1. Problem `neukirch_uchida` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Absolute value at a finite rational place
articles.statement:
For every prime $p$ and every $q \in \mathbb{Q}$,
the absolute value attached to the finite place of $\mathbb{Q}$ at $p$, evaluated at $q$, equals the
$p$-adic absolute value $|q|_p$ of $q$. Here $|0|_p = 0$, and $|q|_p = p^{-v_p(q)}$ for $q \neq 0$,
where $v_p(q)$ is the $p$-adic valuation of $q$.

articles.title: Absolute value at the infinite rational place
articles.statement:
For every $q \in \mathbb{Q}$, the absolute
value attached to the infinite place of $\mathbb{Q}$, evaluated at $q$, equals the ordinary absolute
value $|q|$ of $q$ viewed as a real number.

articles.title: Absolute value at a rational place
articles.statement:
For a place $v$ of $\mathbb{Q}$, the absolute value
$|\cdot|_v : \mathbb{Q} \to \mathbb{R}$ sends $q \in \mathbb{Q}$ to the ordinary absolute value
$|q|$ when $v$ is the infinite place. When $v$ is the finite place at a prime $p$, it sends $q$ to
the normalised $p$-adic absolute value $|q|_p$, where $|0|_p = 0$ and $|q|_p = p^{-v_p(q)}$ for
$q \neq 0$, with $v_p(q)$ the $p$-adic valuation of $q$.

articles.title: Bundled completed field at a rational place
articles.statement:
To each place $v$ of $\mathbb{Q}$ this assigns
a complete normed field: the real numbers $\mathbb{R}$ with the usual absolute value when $v$ is the
infinite place, and, when $v$ is the finite place at a prime $p$, the field $\mathbb{Q}_p$ of
$p$-adic numbers with the $p$-adic norm.

articles.title: Bundled complete normed field
articles.statement:
A complete normed field bundled with its structure: a type
$K$ together with a normed field structure on $K$ for which $K$ is complete with respect to the
metric induced by the norm. It is used to package the completed fields $\mathbb{Q}_v$ of
$\mathbb{Q}$ at its places $v$.

articles.title: Completed field at a rational place
articles.statement:
For a place $v$ of $\mathbb{Q}$, the completed field
$\mathbb{Q}_v$ is the field $\mathbb{R}$ of real numbers when $v$ is the infinite place and, when
$v$ is the finite place at a prime $p$, the field $\mathbb{Q}_p$ of $p$-adic numbers.

It is a complete normed field, with the usual absolute value on $\mathbb{R}$ and the $p$-adic norm
on $\mathbb{Q}_p$.

articles.title: The rationals are dense in each completion
articles.statement:
For every place $v$ of $\mathbb{Q}$, with
completed field $\mathbb{Q}_v$, the image of $\mathbb{Q}$ under the canonical embedding
$\mathbb{Q} \to \mathbb{Q}_v$ is dense in $\mathbb{Q}_v$.

articles.title: Density of the rationals with a place's absolute value in the completion
articles.statement:
Let $v$ be a
place of $\mathbb{Q}$, let $|\cdot|_v$ be the absolute value attached to $v$, let $\mathbb{Q}_v$ be
the completed field at $v$, and write $(\mathbb{Q}, |\cdot|_v)$ for the field $\mathbb{Q}$ equipped
with $|\cdot|_v$. The image of the canonical ring homomorphism
$(\mathbb{Q}, |\cdot|_v) \to \mathbb{Q}_v$, which sends each rational number to itself, is dense
in $\mathbb{Q}_v$.

articles.title: Norm of a rational in a completion
articles.statement:
For every place $v$ of $\mathbb{Q}$ and every
$q \in \mathbb{Q}$, the norm in the completed field $\mathbb{Q}_v$ of the image of $q$ under the
canonical embedding $\mathbb{Q} \to \mathbb{Q}_v$ equals $|q|_v$, the absolute value attached to $v$
evaluated at $q$.

articles.title: Embedding of the rationals into a completion
articles.statement:
For a place $v$ of $\mathbb{Q}$ with
completed field $\mathbb{Q}_v$, the canonical ring homomorphism $\mathbb{Q} \to \mathbb{Q}_v$ sends
each rational number to itself, viewed as a real number when $v$ is the infinite place and as a
$p$-adic number when $v$ is the finite place at a prime $p$.

articles.title: Every nontrivial absolute value on $\mathbb{Q}$ is equivalent to that of a place
articles.statement:
Let $f$
be a real-valued absolute value on $\mathbb{Q}$ that is nontrivial, that is, $f(x) \ne 1$ for some
$x \ne 0$. Then there is a place $v$ of $\mathbb{Q}$ such that $f$ is equivalent to the absolute
value $|\cdot|_v$ attached to $v$ (the ordinary absolute value at the infinite place, the
$p$-adic absolute value at the prime $p$).

Here two absolute values $f$ and $g$ on $\mathbb{Q}$ are equivalent when $f(x) \le f(y)$ holds
exactly when $g(x) \le g(y)$, for all $x, y \in \mathbb{Q}$.

articles.title: Ostrowski's theorem for $\mathbb{Q}$, indexed by places
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be a real-valued absolute
value on $\mathbb{Q}$ that is nontrivial, that is, $f(x) \ne 1$ for some $x \ne 0$. Then there is
exactly one place $v$ of $\mathbb{Q}$ such that $f$ is equivalent to the absolute value
$|\cdot|_v$ attached to $v$ (the ordinary absolute value at the infinite place, the $p$-adic
absolute value at the prime $p$).

Here two absolute values $f$ and $g$ on $\mathbb{Q}$ are equivalent when $f(x) \le f(y)$ holds
exactly when $g(x) \le g(y)$, for all $x, y \in \mathbb{Q}$.

articles.title: Places of $\mathbb{Q}$
articles.statement:
The set $M_{\mathbb{Q}}$ of places of $\mathbb{Q}$, which indexes
the inequivalent normalised absolute values on $\mathbb{Q}$. It consists of one infinite place,
corresponding to the ordinary archimedean absolute value, and one finite place for each prime
number $p$, corresponding to the $p$-adic absolute value.

articles.title: The embedding of $\mathbb{Q}$ into its completion at a place is an isometry
articles.statement:
Let $v$ be a
place of $\mathbb{Q}$, let $|\cdot|_v$ be the absolute value attached to $v$, and let
$\mathbb{Q}_v$ be the completed field at $v$. The canonical embedding of $\mathbb{Q}$, equipped
with the metric $d(x, y) = |x - y|_v$, into $\mathbb{Q}_v$ is an isometry: for all
$x, y \in \mathbb{Q}$, the distance between the images of $x$ and $y$ in $\mathbb{Q}_v$ equals
$|x - y|_v$.

articles.title: Embedding of $\mathbb{Q}$, normed by a place, into its completion
articles.statement:
For a place $v$ of
$\mathbb{Q}$, the ring homomorphism from $\mathbb{Q}$, equipped with the absolute value $|\cdot|_v$
attached to $v$ as its norm, into the completed field $\mathbb{Q}_v$ given by the canonical
embedding of $\mathbb{Q}$ ($\mathbb{Q}_v = \mathbb{R}$ at the infinite place and
$\mathbb{Q}_v = \mathbb{Q}_p$ at a prime $p$).

articles.title: Finite places as places
articles.statement:
For a number field $K$, each finite place $v$ of $K$ is regarded
as a place of $K$ via the inclusion of the finite places into the disjoint union of the infinite
and finite places of $K$.

articles.title: Infinite places as places
articles.statement:
For a number field $K$, each infinite place $v$ of $K$ is
regarded as a place of $K$ via the inclusion of the infinite places into the disjoint union of the
infinite and finite places of $K$.

articles.title: Degree-normalized absolute value at an infinite place
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field of degree
$d = [K : \mathbb{Q}]$ and let $v$ be an infinite place of $K$, with absolute value $|\cdot|_v$
and multiplicity $m_v$, equal to $1$ if $v$ is real and $2$ if $v$ is complex. The
degree-normalized absolute value at $v$ is the absolute value $x \mapsto |x|_v^{m_v/d}$ on $K$.

articles.title: Value of the degree-normalized absolute value at an infinite place
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number
field of degree $d = [K : \mathbb{Q}]$ and let $v$ be an infinite place of $K$, with absolute
value $|\cdot|_v$ and multiplicity $m_v$, equal to $1$ if $v$ is real and $2$ if $v$ is complex.
For every $x \in K$, the degree-normalized absolute value of $x$ at $v$ equals $|x|_v^{m_v/d}$.

articles.title: Degree-normalized finite absolute value through the prime ideal
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number
field of degree $d = [K : \mathbb{Q}]$, let $v$ be a finite place of $K$, and let $\mathfrak{p}$
be the nonzero prime ideal of the ring of integers of $K$ that defines $v$. For every $x \in K$,
the degree-normalized absolute value of $x$ at $v$ equals $|x|_{\mathfrak{p}}^{1/d}$, where
$|x|_{\mathfrak{p}} = N(\mathfrak{p})^{-v_{\mathfrak{p}}(x)}$ for $x \neq 0$ and
$|0|_{\mathfrak{p}} = 0$, with $N(\mathfrak{p})$ the absolute norm of $\mathfrak{p}$ and
$v_{\mathfrak{p}}$ the $\mathfrak{p}$-adic valuation.

articles.title: Degree-normalized absolute value at a complex place
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field of degree
$d = [K : \mathbb{Q}]$ and let $v$ be a complex infinite place of $K$, with absolute value
$|\cdot|_v$. For every $x \in K$, the degree-normalized absolute value of $x$ at $v$ equals
$|x|_v^{2/d}$.

articles.title: Degree-normalized absolute value at a real place
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field of degree
$d = [K : \mathbb{Q}]$ and let $v$ be a real infinite place of $K$, with absolute value
$|\cdot|_v$. For every $x \in K$, the degree-normalized absolute value of $x$ at $v$ equals
$|x|_v^{1/d}$.

articles.title: Value of the degree-normalized absolute value at a finite place
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field
of degree $d = [K : \mathbb{Q}]$ and let $v$ be a finite place of $K$, with absolute value
$|\cdot|_v$. For every $x \in K$, the degree-normalized absolute value of $x$ at $v$ equals
$|x|_v^{1/d}$.

articles.title: Degree-normalized absolute value at a finite place
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field of degree
$d = [K : \mathbb{Q}]$ and let $v$ be a finite place of $K$, with absolute value $|\cdot|_v$. The
degree-normalized absolute value at $v$ is the absolute value $x \mapsto |x|_v^{1/d}$ on $K$.

The finite-place absolute value $|\cdot|_v$ already contains the local-degree factor, so the
remaining normalization exponent is $1/d$.

articles.title: Places of a number field
articles.statement:
For a number field $K$, the places of $K$ form the disjoint union
of the infinite places of $K$ (the absolute values coming from complex embeddings of $K$) and the
finite places of $K$ (the absolute values coming from nonzero prime ideals of the ring of
integers $\mathcal{O}_K$).

articles.title: Residue norm of a finite place
articles.statement:
Let $v$ be a finite place of a number field $K$ and
$\mathfrak{p}_v$ the corresponding nonzero prime ideal of the ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$. The
residue norm $N(v)$ is the absolute norm $|\mathcal{O}_K / \mathfrak{p}_v|$ of $\mathfrak{p}_v$, the
cardinality of the residue field at $v$, regarded as a real number.

articles.title: Inclusion of coprime ideal groups under divisibility of moduli
articles.statement:
Let $m_1$ and $m_2$ be
moduli of a number field $K$ with $m_1 \mid m_2$, that is, the finite part of $m_2$ is contained
in the finite part of $m_1$ and every real place of $m_1$ is a real place of $m_2$. Then every
fractional ideal of $K$ coprime to $m_2$ is coprime to $m_1$, and this map is the inclusion
homomorphism from the group of fractional ideals coprime to $m_2$ into the group of fractional
ideals coprime to $m_1$.

articles.title: Ray class characters take the complex value $1$ on the ray group
articles.statement:
Let $m$ be a modulus
of a number field $K$ and $\chi$ a ray class character of $m$. If a nonzero fractional ideal
$\mathfrak a$ of $K$ coprime to the finite part of $m$ lies in the ray group of $m$, then the value
of $\chi$ at the ray class of $\mathfrak a$, regarded as a complex number, is $1$.

articles.title: Complex value of a ray class character
articles.statement:
For a ray class character $\chi$ of a modulus $m$
and a ray class $x$ of $m$, the complex value of $\chi$ at $x$ is $\chi(x)$, a point of the unit
circle, regarded as a complex number.

articles.title: Extension by zero of a ray class character
articles.statement:
Let $\chi$ be a ray class character of a
modulus $m$ of a number field $K$. Its extension by zero assigns to a nonzero fractional ideal
$\mathfrak a$ of $K$ the complex number $\chi([\mathfrak a])$ if $\mathfrak a$ is coprime to the
finite part of $m$, where $[\mathfrak a]$ is the ray class of $\mathfrak a$, and the value $0$
otherwise.

articles.title: Exponents of a modulus grow under divisibility
articles.statement:
Let $m_1$ and $m_2$ be moduli of a number
field $K$ with $m_1 \mid m_2$, that is, the finite part of $m_2$ is contained in the finite part
of $m_1$ and every real place of $m_1$ is a real place of $m_2$. Then for every finite prime $v$
of $K$ (a height-one prime of the ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$), the exponent of $v$ in the
finite part of $m_1$ is at most the exponent of $v$ in the finite part of $m_2$.

articles.title: Induced characters agree on coprime ideals
articles.statement:
Let $m_1$ and $m_2$ be moduli of a number
field $K$ with $m_1 \mid m_2$, that is, the finite part of $m_2$ is contained in the finite part
of $m_1$ and every real place of $m_1$ is a real place of $m_2$. Let $\chi_1$ be a ray class
character modulo $m_1$ and $\chi_2$ a ray class character modulo $m_2$. Then $\chi_2$ is induced
by $\chi_1$ if and only if, for every fractional ideal $\mathfrak{a}$ of $K$ coprime to $m_2$,
the value of $\chi_2$ on the ray class of $\mathfrak{a}$ modulo $m_2$ equals the value of
$\chi_1$ on the ray class of $\mathfrak{a}$ modulo $m_1$ (an ideal coprime to $m_2$ is also
coprime to $m_1$).

articles.title: Induced ray class character
articles.statement:
Let $m_1$ and $m_2$ be moduli of a number field $K$ with
$m_1 \mid m_2$, that is, the finite part of $m_2$ is contained in the finite part of $m_1$ and
every real place of $m_1$ is a real place of $m_2$. A ray class character $\chi_2$ modulo $m_2$
is induced by a ray class character $\chi_1$ modulo $m_1$ when $\chi_2 = \chi_1 \circ \pi$, where
$\pi$ is the level-change homomorphism from the ray class group modulo $m_2$ to the ray class
group modulo $m_1$ that sends the class of an ideal coprime to $m_2$ to its class modulo
$m_1$.

articles.title: Primitivity in terms of the level-change map
articles.statement:
Let $m$ be a modulus of a number field $K$.
A ray class character $\chi$ modulo $m$ is primitive if and only if, for every modulus $m_0$ of
$K$ with $m_0 \mid m$ (the finite part of $m$ is contained in the finite part of $m_0$ and every
real place of $m_0$ is a real place of $m$) and every ray class character $\chi_0$ modulo $m_0$
with $\chi = \chi_0 \circ \pi$, where $\pi$ is the level-change homomorphism from the ray class
group modulo $m$ to the ray class group modulo $m_0$, we have $m_0 = m$.

articles.title: Primitive ray class character
articles.statement:
Let $m$ be a modulus of a number field $K$. A ray class
character $\chi$ modulo $m$ is primitive when, for every modulus $m_0$ of $K$ with $m_0 \mid m$
(the finite part of $m$ is contained in the finite part of $m_0$ and every real place of $m_0$
is a real place of $m$) and every ray class character $\chi_0$ modulo $m_0$ by which $\chi$ is
induced, $m_0 = m$.

articles.title: The level-change map on ray classes
articles.statement:
Let $m_1$ and $m_2$ be moduli of a number field $K$
with $m_1 \mid m_2$, that is, the finite part of $m_2$ is contained in the finite part of $m_1$
and every real place of $m_1$ is a real place of $m_2$. For every fractional ideal
$\mathfrak{a}$ of $K$ coprime to $m_2$, the level-change homomorphism from the ray class group
modulo $m_2$ to the ray class group modulo $m_1$ sends the ray class of $\mathfrak{a}$ modulo
$m_2$ to the ray class of $\mathfrak{a}$ modulo $m_1$ (an ideal coprime to $m_2$ is also coprime
to $m_1$).

articles.title: Level-change map on ray class groups
articles.statement:
Let $m_1$ and $m_2$ be moduli of a number field $K$
with $m_1 \mid m_2$, that is, the finite part of $m_2$ is contained in the finite part of $m_1$
and every real place of $m_1$ is a real place of $m_2$. The inclusion of the group of fractional
ideals coprime to $m_2$ into the group of fractional ideals coprime to $m_1$ maps the ray group
modulo $m_2$ into the ray group modulo $m_1$, so it induces a group homomorphism from the ray
class group modulo $m_2$ to the ray class group modulo $m_1$, sending the class of an ideal
modulo $m_2$ to its class modulo $m_1$.

articles.title: Ray congruence to $1$ passes to divisors of the modulus
articles.statement:
Let $m_1$ and $m_2$ be moduli
of a number field $K$ with $m_1 \mid m_2$, that is, the finite part of $m_2$ is contained in the
finite part of $m_1$ and every real place of $m_1$ is a real place of $m_2$. If a nonzero element
$x$ of $K$ is congruent to $1$ modulo $m_2$ in the ray sense (its principal ideal is coprime to
$m_2$, for each prime $v$ dividing the finite part of $m_2$ either $x = 1$ or the exponent of
$v$ in $x - 1$ is at least its exponent in that finite part, and $x$ is positive at every real
place of $m_2$), then $x$ is congruent to $1$ modulo $m_1$ in the same sense.

articles.title: Pulled-back ray class characters are trivial on the ray group
articles.statement:
Let $\chi$ be a ray class
character of a modulus $m$ of a number field $K$. If a nonzero fractional ideal $\mathfrak a$ of
$K$ coprime to the finite part of $m$ lies in the ray group of $m$, then the pullback of $\chi$ to
the fractional ideals coprime to the finite part of $m$ takes the value $1$ at $\mathfrak a$.

articles.title: Pullback of a ray class character to ideals
articles.statement:
For a ray class character $\chi$ of a
modulus $m$ of a number field $K$, its pullback is the group homomorphism from the group of
nonzero fractional ideals of $K$ coprime to the finite part of $m$ to the unit circle sending
$\mathfrak a$ to $\chi([\mathfrak a])$, where $[\mathfrak a]$ is the ray class of $\mathfrak a$.

articles.title: Ray class character
articles.statement:
A ray class character of a modulus $m$ of a number field $K$ is a
group homomorphism from the ray class group of $m$ to the unit circle
$\{z \in \mathbb C : |z| = 1\}$.

articles.title: Trivial character
articles.statement:
The trivial ray class character of a modulus $m$ of a number field $K$
is the ray class character sending every ray class of $m$ to $1$.

articles.title: Multiplicative congruence to one at the finite part
articles.statement:
Let $\mathfrak m$ be a modulus of a
number field $K$, with finite part the nonzero ideal $\mathfrak m_0$ of $\mathcal O_K$. For a
nonzero prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $\mathcal O_K$, write $v_{\mathfrak p}(I)$ for the exponent of
$\mathfrak p$ in the factorization of a nonzero fractional ideal $I$ of $\mathcal O_K$, and for
$y \in K$ write $v_{\mathfrak p}(y) = v_{\mathfrak p}((y))$ (with $v_{\mathfrak p}(0) = 0$). An
element $x \in K^\times$ is congruent to $1$ at the finite part of $\mathfrak m$ when, for every
nonzero prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $\mathcal O_K$ containing $\mathfrak m_0$, either $x = 1$ or
$v_{\mathfrak p}(\mathfrak m_0) \le v_{\mathfrak p}(x - 1)$.

articles.title: Fractional ideals coprime to a modulus
articles.statement:
Let $\mathfrak m$ be a modulus of a number field
$K$, with finite part the nonzero ideal $\mathfrak m_0$ of $\mathcal O_K$. For an invertible
fractional ideal $I$ of $\mathcal O_K$ and a nonzero prime ideal $\mathfrak p$, write
$v_{\mathfrak p}(I)$ for the exponent of $\mathfrak p$ in the factorization of $I$. The fractional
ideals coprime to $\mathfrak m$ form the subgroup of the group of invertible fractional ideals of
$\mathcal O_K$ consisting of those $I$ with $v_{\mathfrak p}(I) = 0$ for every nonzero prime ideal
$\mathfrak p$ of $\mathcal O_K$ containing $\mathfrak m_0$.

articles.title: Value of the ideal-class map on a coprime ideal
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field, $\mathfrak m$ a
modulus of $K$, and $I_{\mathfrak m}$ the group of nonzero fractional ideals of $\mathcal O_K$
coprime to the finite part of $\mathfrak m$. For every $I \in I_{\mathfrak m}$, the coprime
ideal-class map sends $I$ to the class $[I]$ in the class group $\mathrm{Cl}(\mathcal O_K)$ of $I$
viewed as a nonzero fractional ideal.

articles.title: Every ideal class contains a fractional ideal coprime to the modulus
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a
number field and $\mathfrak m$ a modulus of $K$ with finite part $\mathfrak m_0$. The homomorphism
from the group of fractional ideals of $K$ coprime to $\mathfrak m_0$ (those whose exponent at
every prime dividing $\mathfrak m_0$ is $0$) to the class group of $\mathcal O_K$, sending each
such fractional ideal to its ideal class, is surjective.

## Sources

- ATLAS lines 1466--1476; Lemma 21.7 at lines 958--1010 is reused via the stronger `ClassGroup.exists_mk0_eq_and_isCoprime`.

articles.title: Ideal-class map on coprime fractional ideals
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field, $\mathfrak m$ a
modulus of $K$, and $I_{\mathfrak m}$ the group of nonzero fractional ideals of $\mathcal O_K$
coprime to the finite part of $\mathfrak m$. The coprime ideal-class map is the group homomorphism
$I_{\mathfrak m} \to \mathrm{Cl}(\mathcal O_K)$ that sends $I$ to its ideal class $[I]$: the
inclusion of $I_{\mathfrak m}$ into the group of nonzero fractional ideals followed by the class
map.

## Sources

- ATLAS `exactSeq_map4`, before the quotient lift.

articles.title: Lower bound for the exponent of a sum
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field and $\mathfrak p$ a nonzero
prime ideal of $\mathcal O_K$. For $x \in K$ write $c_{\mathfrak p}(x)$ for the exponent of
$\mathfrak p$ in the principal fractional ideal $x \mathcal O_K$, with the convention
$c_{\mathfrak p}(0) = 0$. If $x, y \in K$ satisfy $x + y \neq 0$ and $n \in \mathbb Z$ satisfies
$n \le c_{\mathfrak p}(x)$ and $n \le c_{\mathfrak p}(y)$, then $n \le c_{\mathfrak p}(x + y)$.

Only $x + y \neq 0$ is assumed: $x$ or $y$ may be zero.

articles.title: Coprime representation of ray elements
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field and $\mathfrak m$ a
modulus of $K$ with finite part $\mathfrak m_0$, a nonzero ideal of $\mathcal O_K$. Every ray
element $x$ of $\mathfrak m$ can be written as $x = a / b$ in $K$ with $a, b \in \mathcal O_K$
whose residue classes are units of $\mathcal O_K / \mathfrak m_0$.

Source (N406 §21.3): the
[`coprime_rep_exists`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/atlas-lean/blob/e8b31c5cb0bec89b487ce33fe525a2c0b0f8b9c6/v1/Atlas/NumberTheoryI/code/RayClassFields.lean#L1553-L1747)
admissible integral numerator/denominator representation with both residues units.

articles.title: Weak approximation with a finite target and prescribed signs
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field
and $\mathfrak m$ a modulus of $K$, with finite part $\mathfrak m_0$ (a nonzero ideal of
$\mathcal O_K$) and infinite part $\mathfrak m_\infty$ (a finite set of real places of $K$). For
a nonzero prime $\mathfrak p$ of $\mathcal O_K$ write $v_{\mathfrak p}$ for the
$\mathfrak p$-adic valuation on $K$ (with $v_{\mathfrak p}(0) = \infty$) and $e_{\mathfrak p}$
for the exponent of $\mathfrak p$ in $\mathfrak m_0$; for a real place $w$ write
$\sigma_w : K \to \mathbb R$ for its real embedding. Let $P$ be any set of places in
$\mathfrak m_\infty$, and let $a \in K$ be nonzero with $v_{\mathfrak p}(a) = 0$ for every
nonzero prime $\mathfrak p$ dividing $\mathfrak m_0$. Then there is a nonzero $x \in K$ such
that $v_{\mathfrak p}(x) = 0$ and $v_{\mathfrak p}(x - a) \ge e_{\mathfrak p}$ for every nonzero
prime $\mathfrak p$ dividing $\mathfrak m_0$, and such that for every $w \in \mathfrak m_\infty$,
$\sigma_w(x) > 0$ if $w \in P$ and $\sigma_w(x) < 0$ if $w \notin P$.

## Sources

- mapping toward ATLAS N406, Theorem 21.8, Section 21.3 (`weak_approx_coprime_sign_finitePart`, lines 2255--2568): the finite target `a` is lifted at source lines 2267--2275 with supported valuation-one hypothesis at 2277--2292; the finite/infinite index family below is at 2314--2385; modulus-dependent tolerances at 2388--2404; nonzero witness at 2406--2412; valuation preservation at 2414--2451; sign control at 2458--2477; and the strict absolute-value-to-discrete-valuation residue comparison at 2480--2568.

articles.title: Weak approximation with prescribed signs at a modulus
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field and
$\mathfrak m$ a modulus of $K$, with finite part $\mathfrak m_0$ (a nonzero ideal of
$\mathcal O_K$) and infinite part $\mathfrak m_\infty$ (a finite set of real places of $K$); for
a real place $w$ write $\sigma_w : K \to \mathbb R$ for its real embedding. For every set $P$ of
places in $\mathfrak m_\infty$ there is a nonzero $x \in K$ whose $\mathfrak p$-adic valuation
is $0$ for every nonzero prime $\mathfrak p$ of $\mathcal O_K$ dividing $\mathfrak m_0$, and such
that for every $w \in \mathfrak m_\infty$, $\sigma_w(x) > 0$ if $w \in P$ and $\sigma_w(x) < 0$
if $w \notin P$.

This is the special case of weak approximation with a finite target and prescribed signs in
which the target is $1$.

articles.title: Exponent of a modulus at a prime
articles.statement:
Let $\mathfrak m$ be a modulus of a number field $K$, with
finite part the nonzero ideal $\mathfrak m_0$ of $\mathcal O_K$. For a nonzero prime ideal
$\mathfrak p$ of $\mathcal O_K$, the finite exponent of $\mathfrak m$ at $\mathfrak p$ is the
integer $v_{\mathfrak p}(\mathfrak m_0)$, the exponent of $\mathfrak p$ in the prime factorization
of $\mathfrak m_0$.

articles.title: The finite ray-one subgroup
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field and $\mathfrak m$ a modulus of $K$
with finite part $\mathfrak m_0$. The finite ray-one subgroup of $\mathfrak m$ is the subgroup of
the group of ray elements of $\mathfrak m$ consisting of the $x$ that are congruent to $1$ at the
finite part of $\mathfrak m$: for every nonzero prime $\mathfrak p$ of $\mathcal O_K$ containing
$\mathfrak m_0$, either $x = 1$ or the exponent of $\mathfrak p$ in $(x - 1) \mathcal O_K$ is at
least the exponent of $\mathfrak p$ in $\mathfrak m_0$.

articles.title: Computing the finite residue map from a representation
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field and
$\mathfrak m$ a modulus of $K$ with finite part $\mathfrak m_0$. Let $x$ be a ray element of
$\mathfrak m$, and let $a, b \in \mathcal O_K$ have residue classes $\bar a, \bar b$ that are
units of $\mathcal O_K / \mathfrak m_0$ and satisfy $a / b = x$ in $K$. Then the finite residue
map of $\mathfrak m$ sends $x$ to $\bar a \bar b^{-1}$ in $(\mathcal O_K / \mathfrak m_0)^\times$.

Source (N406 §21.3): the representation-independence computation
[`coprime_rep_well_def`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/atlas-lean/blob/e8b31c5cb0bec89b487ce33fe525a2c0b0f8b9c6/v1/Atlas/NumberTheoryI/code/RayClassFields.lean#L1757-L1810)
for the finite component.

articles.title: Kernel criterion for the finite residue map
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field and $\mathfrak m$ a
modulus of $K$. A ray element $x$ of $\mathfrak m$ is sent to $1$ by the finite residue map of
$\mathfrak m$ if and only if $x$ is congruent to $1$ at the finite part of $\mathfrak m$.

Source (N406 §21.3): helper
[`finitePartMapHom_ker_iff`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/atlas-lean/blob/e8b31c5cb0bec89b487ce33fe525a2c0b0f8b9c6/v1/Atlas/NumberTheoryI/code/RayClassFields.lean#L1996-L2011).

articles.title: Valuation criterion for the finite residue map to be trivial
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field,
$\mathfrak m$ a modulus of $K$ with finite part $\mathfrak m_0$, and $z$ a ray element of
$\mathfrak m$. Suppose that at every nonzero prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $\mathcal O_K$
containing $\mathfrak m_0$, the multiplicative $\mathfrak p$-adic valuation of $z - 1$ is at most
$\exp(-e_{\mathfrak p})$, where $e_{\mathfrak p}$ is the exponent of $\mathfrak p$ in
$\mathfrak m_0$; equivalently, $z = 1$ or $z - 1$ has $\mathfrak p$-adic order at least
$e_{\mathfrak p}$. Then the finite residue map of $\mathfrak m$ sends $z$ to $1$ in
$(\mathcal O_K / \mathfrak m_0)^\times$.

## Sources

- N406, Theorem 21.8, Section 21.3 (ATLAS NumberTheoryI item N406): the native-API finite-congruence step corresponding to [`finitePartMapHom_ker_iff`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/atlas-lean/blob/e8b31c5cb0bec89b487ce33fe525a2c0b0f8b9c6/v1/Atlas/NumberTheoryI/code/RayClassFields.lean#L1996-L2011), used by the weak-approximation argument before residue/sign surjectivity and by [`theorem_21_8_quotient_iso`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/atlas-lean/blob/e8b31c5cb0bec89b487ce33fe525a2c0b0f8b9c6/v1/Atlas/NumberTheoryI/code/RayClassFields.lean#L2607-L2647). It is not the generalized weak-approximation theorem and not the final N406 result.

articles.title: Kernel of the finite residue map
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field and $\mathfrak m$ a modulus of
$K$. The kernel of the finite residue map of $\mathfrak m$ is the finite ray-one subgroup of
$\mathfrak m$.

Source (N406 §21.3): the finite kernel component used in the
[`theorem_21_8_quotient_iso`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/atlas-lean/blob/e8b31c5cb0bec89b487ce33fe525a2c0b0f8b9c6/v1/Atlas/NumberTheoryI/code/RayClassFields.lean#L2600-L2647).

articles.title: Finite residue map
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field and $\mathfrak m$ a modulus of $K$ with finite
part $\mathfrak m_0$, a nonzero ideal of $\mathcal O_K$. The finite residue map of $\mathfrak m$ is
the group homomorphism from the ray elements of $\mathfrak m$ to
$(\mathcal O_K / \mathfrak m_0)^\times$ sending $x$ to $\bar a \bar b^{-1}$, where $x = a / b$ with
$a, b \in \mathcal O_K$ whose residue classes $\bar a, \bar b$ are units of
$\mathcal O_K / \mathfrak m_0$; such $a$ and $b$ exist, and the value does not depend on their
choice.

Source (N406 §21.3): the
[`finitePartMapHom`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/atlas-lean/blob/e8b31c5cb0bec89b487ce33fe525a2c0b0f8b9c6/v1/Atlas/NumberTheoryI/code/RayClassFields.lean#L1812-L1864)
finite component of the quotient isomorphism.

articles.title: Primes dividing a modulus
articles.statement:
Let $\mathfrak m$ be a modulus of a number field $K$, with finite
part the nonzero ideal $\mathfrak m_0$ of $\mathcal O_K$. A nonzero prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ of
$\mathcal O_K$ lies in the finite support of $\mathfrak m$ when
$\mathfrak m_0 \subseteq \mathfrak p$, that is, when $\mathfrak p$ divides $\mathfrak m_0$.

articles.title: Nonzero integral ideals coprime to the modulus are coprime fractional ideals
articles.statement:
Let $K$
be a number field with ring of integers $\mathcal O_K$, let $\mathfrak m$ be a modulus of $K$
with finite part $\mathfrak m_0$, and let $I$ be a nonzero ideal of $\mathcal O_K$ with
$I + \mathfrak m_0 = \mathcal O_K$. Then $I$, viewed as an invertible fractional ideal of $K$,
belongs to the group of fractional ideals coprime to $\mathfrak m_0$: its exponent at every prime
dividing $\mathfrak m_0$ is $0$.

## Sources

- E5 `mk0` membership/count bridge for ATLAS lines 1431--1465.

articles.title: Finite part of the modulus of a real place
articles.statement:
For a real place $v$ of a number field $K$,
let $\mathfrak m_v$ be the modulus of $K$ with finite part the unit ideal $\mathcal O_K$ and
infinite part $\{v\}$. The finite part of $\mathfrak m_v$ is the unit ideal $\mathcal O_K$.

articles.title: Infinite part of the modulus of a real place
articles.statement:
For a real place $v$ of a number field $K$,
let $\mathfrak m_v$ be the modulus of $K$ with finite part the unit ideal $\mathcal O_K$ and
infinite part $\{v\}$. The infinite part of $\mathfrak m_v$ is the singleton $\{v\}$.

articles.title: Coordinates of the infinite sign map
articles.statement:
Let $m$ be a modulus of a number field $K$ with
finite set of real places $m_\infty$. For every ray element $x$ of $m$ and every $w \in m_\infty$,
the value at $w$ of the infinite sign map of $m$ applied to $x$ is the sign of $x$ at the real
place $w$.

articles.title: Trivial infinite sign means positivity at the modulus
articles.statement:
Let $m$ be a modulus of a number
field $K$ with finite set of real places $m_\infty$, and for a real place $w$ let $\sigma_w$ be
the corresponding real embedding of $K$. For every ray element $x$ of $m$, the infinite sign map
of $m$ sends $x$ to the identity if and only if $x$ is positive at the infinite part of $m$,
that is, $\sigma_w(x) > 0$ for every $w \in m_\infty$.

articles.title: Infinite sign map of a modulus
articles.statement:
Let $m$ be a modulus of a number field $K$ and let
$m_\infty$ be its finite set of real places. The infinite sign map of $m$ is the group
homomorphism from the ray elements of $m$ to the group of functions
$m_\infty \to \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$, with $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$ written multiplicatively and
the pointwise product, that sends $x$ to the function whose value at $w \in m_\infty$ is the
sign of $x$ at the real place $w$.

articles.title: The inclusion of the ray-one integral units is injective
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field
with ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$ and let $\mathfrak{m}$ be a modulus of $K$. The inclusion
homomorphism from the subgroup of ray-one integral units for $\mathfrak{m}$ into the unit group
$\mathcal{O}_K^\times$ is injective.

articles.title: Inclusion of the ray-one integral units
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field with ring of integers
$\mathcal{O}_K$ and let $\mathfrak{m}$ be a modulus of $K$. The inclusion of the ray-one integral
units for $\mathfrak{m}$ is the group homomorphism from the subgroup of ray-one integral units for
$\mathfrak{m}$ to $\mathcal{O}_K^\times$ that sends each such unit to itself.

## Sources

- ATLAS `exactSeq_map1`.

articles.title: Ray-one integral units
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field with ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$,
let $\mathfrak{m}$ be a modulus of $K$ with finite part $\mathfrak{m}_0$, and send each unit of
$\mathcal{O}_K$ to its image in the group of ray elements for $\mathfrak{m}$. For a nonzero prime
$\mathfrak{p}$ of $\mathcal{O}_K$, write $v_{\mathfrak{p}}$ for the $\mathfrak{p}$-adic valuation
of nonzero elements and nonzero ideals. The ray-one integral units for $\mathfrak{m}$ form the
subgroup of $\mathcal{O}_K^\times$ of those units $u$ whose image lies in the ray-one subgroup,
that is: for every prime $\mathfrak{p}$ dividing $\mathfrak{m}_0$, either $u = 1$ or
$v_{\mathfrak{p}}(u - 1) \ge v_{\mathfrak{p}}(\mathfrak{m}_0)$, and $u$ is positive under the
real embedding of every real place in the infinite part of $\mathfrak{m}$.

## Sources

- ATLAS `UnitsInCongruenceSubgroup`.

articles.title: Exactness of the ray sequence at the integral units
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field with ring
of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$ and let $\mathfrak{m}$ be a modulus of $K$. Write $K_{\mathfrak{m}}$
for the group of ray elements for $\mathfrak{m}$, $K_{\mathfrak{m},1}$ for its ray-one subgroup,
and $U_{\mathfrak{m},1} \subseteq \mathcal{O}_K^\times$ for the subgroup of ray-one integral units.
Consider the sequence

$$U_{\mathfrak{m},1} \to \mathcal{O}_K^\times \to K_{\mathfrak{m}}/K_{\mathfrak{m},1}$$

whose first map is the inclusion and whose second map sends a unit to the class of its image in
