$K_{\mathfrak{m}}$. For every $u \in \mathcal{O}_K^\times$, the class of $u$ is the identity if
and only if $u$ lies in the image of the first map; that is, the sequence is exact at
$\mathcal{O}_K^\times$.

## Sources

- ATLAS `exactSeq_exact_at_units`.

articles.title: Exactness at the integral units, residue-sign form
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field with ring
of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$ and let $\mathfrak{m}$ be a modulus of $K$ with finite part
$\mathfrak{m}_0$. Let $T_{\mathfrak{m}}$ be the residue-sign target of $\mathfrak{m}$: the product
of a copy of $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$, written multiplicatively, for each real place in the
infinite part of $\mathfrak{m}$, with $(\mathcal{O}_K/\mathfrak{m}_0)^\times$. Let
$\rho \colon \mathcal{O}_K^\times \to T_{\mathfrak{m}}$ send a unit to the class of its image in
the quotient of the group of ray elements for $\mathfrak{m}$ by its ray-one subgroup, followed by
the canonical isomorphism of that quotient with $T_{\mathfrak{m}}$ induced by the residue-sign
map. Then for every $u \in \mathcal{O}_K^\times$, $\rho(u) = 1$ if and only if $u$ is in the image
of the inclusion of the ray-one integral units for $\mathfrak{m}$ into $\mathcal{O}_K^\times$.

articles.title: Integral units embed injectively into field units
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field and $\mathcal{O}_K$
its ring of integers, the integral closure of $\mathbb{Z}$ in $K$. The group homomorphism
$\mathcal{O}_K^\times \to K^\times$ induced by the inclusion $\mathcal{O}_K \subseteq K$ is
injective.

articles.title: Embedding of integral units into field units
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field and $\mathcal{O}_K$ its
ring of integers, the integral closure of $\mathbb{Z}$ in $K$. This is the group homomorphism
$\mathcal{O}_K^\times \to K^\times$ induced by the inclusion $\mathcal{O}_K \subseteq K$: it sends
a unit of $\mathcal{O}_K$ to the same element regarded as a unit of $K$.

## Sources

- ATLAS `okUnitsToKUnits`.

articles.title: Ray-element image of an integral unit as a field unit
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field with
ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$, let $\mathfrak{m}$ be a modulus of $K$, and let
$u \in \mathcal{O}_K^\times$. The image of $u$ in the group of ray elements for $\mathfrak{m}$,
regarded as an element of $K^\times$, equals the image of $u$ under the embedding
$\mathcal{O}_K^\times \to K^\times$.

articles.title: Integral units embed injectively into the ray elements
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field with
ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$ and let $\mathfrak{m}$ be a modulus of $K$. The homomorphism
from $\mathcal{O}_K^\times$ to the group of ray elements for $\mathfrak{m}$ that sends a unit to
its image in $K^\times$ is injective.

articles.title: Integral units as ray elements
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field with ring of integers
$\mathcal{O}_K$, let $\mathfrak{m}$ be a modulus of $K$, and let
$K_{\mathfrak{m}} \subseteq K^\times$ be the group of ray elements for $\mathfrak{m}$. Every unit
of $\mathcal{O}_K$ has $\mathfrak{p}$-adic valuation $0$ at every prime $\mathfrak{p}$ of
$\mathcal{O}_K$, so it lies in $K_{\mathfrak{m}}$. This is the group homomorphism
$\mathcal{O}_K^\times \to K_{\mathfrak{m}}$ sending a unit $u$ to its image in $K^\times$.

## Sources

- ATLAS `okUnitsToUnitsCoprime`; ATLAS `valuation_algebraMap_unit_eq_one` is discharged inline in the definition.

articles.title: Value of the ray-quotient map on integral units
articles.statement:
Let $\mathfrak m$ be a modulus of a
number field $K$, let $K_{\mathfrak m} \le K^\times$ be the group of ray elements (elements whose
principal fractional ideal is coprime to the finite part of $\mathfrak m$) and let
$K_{\mathfrak m,1} \le K_{\mathfrak m}$ be the ray-one subgroup. For every unit $u$ of the ring of
integers $\mathcal O_K$, the map $\mathcal O_K^\times \to K_{\mathfrak m}/K_{\mathfrak m,1}$ sends
$u$ to the coset of $u$, viewed as an element of $K_{\mathfrak m}$.

articles.title: Kernel of the ray-quotient map on integral units
articles.statement:
Let $\mathfrak m$ be a modulus of a
number field $K$, let $K_{\mathfrak m} \le K^\times$ be the group of ray elements and
$K_{\mathfrak m,1} \le K_{\mathfrak m}$ the ray-one subgroup. The kernel of the homomorphism
$\mathcal O_K^\times \to K_{\mathfrak m}/K_{\mathfrak m,1}$ sending a unit of the ring of integers
$\mathcal O_K$ to its coset is the subgroup of ray-one integral units, the units of $\mathcal O_K$
that lie in $K_{\mathfrak m,1}$.

articles.title: Exactness at the ray-element quotient
articles.statement:
Let $\mathfrak m$ be a modulus of a number field
$K$, let $K_{\mathfrak m}$ be the group of ray elements (elements of $K^\times$ whose principal
ideal is coprime to the finite part of $\mathfrak m$), let $K_{\mathfrak m,1} \le K_{\mathfrak m}$
be the subgroup of ray-one elements, and let $\mathrm{Cl}_{\mathfrak m}$ be the ray class group
of $\mathfrak m$. In the sequence
$\mathcal O_K^\times \to K_{\mathfrak m}/K_{\mathfrak m,1} \to \mathrm{Cl}_{\mathfrak m}$,
where the first map sends a unit $u$ to the class of $u$ and the second sends the class of a ray
element $x$ to the ray class of the principal fractional ideal $(x)$, an element of
$K_{\mathfrak m}/K_{\mathfrak m,1}$ maps to the identity of $\mathrm{Cl}_{\mathfrak m}$ if and
only if it is the image of an integral unit.

## Sources

- ATLAS `exactSeq_exact_at_quotient`.

articles.title: Map from integral units to the ray quotient
articles.statement:
Let $\mathfrak m$ be a modulus of a number
field $K$, let $K_{\mathfrak m} \le K^\times$ be the group of ray elements (elements whose principal
fractional ideal is coprime to the finite part of $\mathfrak m$) and let
$K_{\mathfrak m,1} \le K_{\mathfrak m}$ be the ray-one subgroup. This is the group homomorphism
$\mathcal O_K^\times \to K_{\mathfrak m}/K_{\mathfrak m,1}$ sending a unit $u$ of the ring of
integers $\mathcal O_K$ to the coset of $u$, viewed as an element of $K_{\mathfrak m}$.

## Sources

- ATLAS `exactSeq_map2`.

articles.title: Value of the residue-sign map on integral units
articles.statement:
Let $\mathfrak m$ be a modulus of a
number field $K$ and let $K_{\mathfrak m} \le K^\times$ be the group of ray elements. For every unit
$u$ of the ring of integers $\mathcal O_K$, the residue-sign map on integral units sends $u$ to the
image of $u$, viewed as an element of $K_{\mathfrak m}$, under the residue-sign homomorphism on
$K_{\mathfrak m}$.

articles.title: Kernel of the residue-sign map on integral units
articles.statement:
Let $\mathfrak m$ be a modulus of a
number field $K$. The kernel of the residue-sign map on the unit group $\mathcal O_K^\times$ of the
ring of integers is the subgroup of ray-one integral units, the units of $\mathcal O_K$ whose image
in the group of ray elements modulo $\mathfrak m$ lies in its ray-one subgroup.

articles.title: Exactness at the residue-sign group
articles.statement:
Let $\mathfrak m$ be a modulus of a number field
$K$ with finite part $\mathfrak m_0$ and set of real places $\mathfrak m_\infty$, let
$\mathrm{Cl}_{\mathfrak m}$ be its ray class group, and let
$R_{\mathfrak m} = \{\pm 1\}^{\mathfrak m_\infty} \times (\mathcal O_K/\mathfrak m_0)^\times$.
Consider the maps $\mathcal O_K^\times \to R_{\mathfrak m} \to \mathrm{Cl}_{\mathfrak m}$. The
first sends a unit $u$ to its signs at the places in $\mathfrak m_\infty$ together with its class
in $(\mathcal O_K/\mathfrak m_0)^\times$. The second is the quotient-to-ray-class map transported
along the canonical isomorphism from the quotient of the ray elements by the ray-one elements
onto $R_{\mathfrak m}$, so it sends the image in $R_{\mathfrak m}$ of a ray element $x$ to the
ray class of the principal fractional ideal $(x)$. An element of $R_{\mathfrak m}$ maps to the
identity of $\mathrm{Cl}_{\mathfrak m}$ if and only if it is the image of an integral unit.

articles.title: Residue-sign map on integral units
articles.statement:
Let $\mathfrak m$ be a modulus of a number field $K$
with finite part $\mathfrak m_0$ and set of real places $\mathfrak m_\infty$, let
$K_{\mathfrak m} \le K^\times$ be the group of ray elements and let
$K_{\mathfrak m,1} \le K_{\mathfrak m}$ be the ray-one subgroup. The residue-sign map on integral
units is the group homomorphism from $\mathcal O_K^\times$ to
$(\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z)^{\mathfrak m_\infty} \times (\mathcal O_K/\mathfrak m_0)^\times$, with
$\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$ written multiplicatively, obtained by composing the map
$\mathcal O_K^\times \to K_{\mathfrak m}/K_{\mathfrak m,1}$ sending a unit to its coset with the
isomorphism from $K_{\mathfrak m}/K_{\mathfrak m,1}$ onto this group induced by the residue-sign
homomorphism on $K_{\mathfrak m}$.

articles.title: Inverses preserve congruence to one at the finite part
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field and
$\mathfrak m$ a modulus of $K$. If a ray element $x$ of $\mathfrak m$ is congruent to $1$ at the
finite part of $\mathfrak m$, then so is $x^{-1}$.

articles.title: Elements congruent to one modulo a modulus
articles.statement:
Let $\mathfrak m$ be a modulus of a number field
$K$, with finite part the nonzero ideal $\mathfrak m_0$ of $\mathcal O_K$ and infinite part the
finite set $\mathfrak m_\infty$ of real places of $K$. For a nonzero prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ of
$\mathcal O_K$, write $v_{\mathfrak p}(I)$ for the exponent of $\mathfrak p$ in the factorization
of a nonzero fractional ideal $I$ of $\mathcal O_K$, and for $y \in K$ write
$v_{\mathfrak p}(y) = v_{\mathfrak p}((y))$ (with $v_{\mathfrak p}(0) = 0$); for a real place $w$
write $\sigma_w \colon K \to \mathbb R$ for the corresponding real embedding. An element
$x \in K^\times$ is congruent to $1$ modulo $\mathfrak m$ when, for every nonzero prime ideal
$\mathfrak p$ of $\mathcal O_K$ containing $\mathfrak m_0$, $v_{\mathfrak p}(x) = 0$ and either
$x = 1$ or $v_{\mathfrak p}(\mathfrak m_0) \le v_{\mathfrak p}(x - 1)$, and $\sigma_w(x) > 0$ for
every real place $w \in \mathfrak m_\infty$.

articles.title: Membership in the ray-one integral units
articles.statement:
Let $\mathfrak m$ be a modulus of a number field
$K$ with finite part $\mathfrak m_0$ and set of real places $\mathfrak m_\infty$, and for a nonzero
prime $\mathfrak p$ of the ring of integers $\mathcal O_K$ write $v_{\mathfrak p}$ for the exponent
of $\mathfrak p$ in a fractional ideal of $K$, applied to an element through its principal
fractional ideal. A unit $u$ of $\mathcal O_K$ lies in the subgroup of ray-one integral units if
and only if $u$, viewed as an element of $K^\times$, is a ray element congruent to $1$ modulo
$\mathfrak m$: its principal fractional ideal is coprime to $\mathfrak m_0$, for every nonzero
prime $\mathfrak p$ dividing $\mathfrak m_0$ either $u = 1$ or
$v_{\mathfrak p}(u - 1) \ge v_{\mathfrak p}(\mathfrak m_0)$, and $u$ is positive under the real
embedding of every place in $\mathfrak m_\infty$.

articles.title: Membership in the positive ray elements
articles.statement:
Let $m$ be a modulus of a number field $K$ with
finite set of real places $m_\infty$, and for a real place $w$ let $\sigma_w$ be the real embedding
of $K$ at $w$. A ray element $x$ of $m$ is a positive ray element of $m$ if and only if $x$ is
positive at the infinite part of $m$, that is, $\sigma_w(x) > 0$ for every $w \in m_\infty$.

articles.title: Elements of valuation one at the primes dividing a modulus are ray elements
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a
number field, $\mathfrak m$ a modulus of $K$ with finite part $\mathfrak m_0$, and
$a \in K^\times$. If the multiplicative $\mathfrak p$-adic valuation of $a$ equals $1$ at every
nonzero prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $\mathcal O_K$ containing $\mathfrak m_0$, then $a$ is
coprime to $\mathfrak m$, that is, a ray element of $\mathfrak m$: its principal fractional ideal
$(a)$ has exponent $0$ at every such $\mathfrak p$.

## Sources

- N406 Section 21.3. This is the converse of `rayElement_valuation_eq_one`, the converse valuation criterion used to turn the controlled approximation witness into a ray element; it is a reusable bridge toward N406, not itself the full source theorem.

articles.title: Membership in the ray-one subgroup
articles.statement:
Let $m$ be a modulus of a number field $K$. A ray
element $x$ of $m$ lies in the ray-one subgroup of $m$ if and only if $x$ is congruent to $1$ at
the finite part of $m$ and $x$ is positive at every real place in the infinite part of $m$.

articles.title: Product of two elements congruent to one at the finite part
articles.statement:
Let $m$ be a modulus
of a number field $K$ and let $x, y \in K^\times$ both be congruent to $1$ at the finite
part of $m$. If moreover $x$ is a ray element of $m$, then $xy$ is congruent to $1$ at the
finite part of $m$.

articles.title: Positivity at the infinite part of a modulus
articles.statement:
Let $\mathfrak m$ be a modulus of a number
field $K$, with infinite part the finite set $\mathfrak m_\infty$ of real places of $K$. An element
$x \in K^\times$ is positive at the infinite part of $\mathfrak m$ when $\sigma_w(x) > 0$ for every
real place $w \in \mathfrak m_\infty$, where $\sigma_w \colon K \to \mathbb R$ is the real
embedding corresponding to $w$.

articles.title: Ray elements positive at the infinite part
articles.statement:
Let $m$ be a modulus of a number field $K$
with finite set of real places $m_\infty$, and for a real place $w$ let $\sigma_w$ be the real
embedding of $K$ at $w$. The positive ray elements of $m$ form the subgroup of the ray elements
of $m$ defined as the kernel of the infinite sign map of $m$; equivalently, they are the ray
elements $x$ with $\sigma_w(x) > 0$ for every $w \in m_\infty$.

articles.title: Value of the principal ray ideal map
articles.statement:
Let $\mathfrak m$ be a modulus of a number field
$K$ with ring of integers $\mathcal O_K$. For every ray element $x \in K^\times$ for
$\mathfrak m$, the image of $x$ under the principal ray ideal map, viewed as an invertible
fractional ideal of $K$, is the principal fractional ideal $x\mathcal O_K$.

articles.title: Integral units generate the unit ideal
articles.statement:
Let $\mathfrak m$ be a modulus of a number field
$K$. For every unit $u \in \mathcal O_K^\times$, viewed as a ray element of $\mathfrak m$, the
principal fractional ideal $(u)$, as an element of the group of fractional ideals coprime to
$\mathfrak m$, is the identity element $\mathcal O_K$.

## Sources

- ATLAS lines 1160--1175, an input to exactness at the quotient.

articles.title: Principal ray ideal map
articles.statement:
Let $\mathfrak m$ be a modulus of a number field $K$ with ring of
integers $\mathcal O_K$. The principal ray ideal map is the group homomorphism from the group of
ray elements for $\mathfrak m$ (the $x \in K^\times$ whose principal ideal is coprime to
$\mathfrak m$) to the group of fractional ideals coprime to $\mathfrak m$ that sends $x$ to the
principal fractional ideal $x\mathcal O_K$.

articles.title: Equal fractions give equal residues modulo the finite part
articles.statement:
Let $m$ be a modulus
of a number field $K$ with finite part $\mathfrak m_0$, an ideal of $\mathcal O_K$, and
write $\bar x$ for the image of $x \in \mathcal O_K$ in $\mathcal O_K / \mathfrak m_0$.
Let $a, b, c, d \in \mathcal O_K$ be such that $\bar a$, $\bar b$, $\bar c$ and $\bar d$
are units. If $a / b = c / d$ in $K$, then $\bar a \bar b^{-1} = \bar c \bar d^{-1}$ in
the unit group $(\mathcal O_K / \mathfrak m_0)^\times$.

articles.title: Ray class group
articles.statement:
The ray class group of a modulus $\mathfrak m$ of a number field $K$ is
the quotient of the group of nonzero fractional ideals of $K$ coprime to the finite part of
$\mathfrak m$ by the ray group of $\mathfrak m$.

articles.title: Ray class map
articles.statement:
For a modulus $\mathfrak m$ of a number field $K$, the ray class map is the
canonical quotient homomorphism from the group of nonzero fractional ideals of $K$ coprime to the
finite part of $\mathfrak m$ onto the ray class group of $\mathfrak m$, sending each such ideal to
its class modulo the ray group of $\mathfrak m$.

articles.title: The ray class exact sequence, sign and residue form
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field with ring of
integers $\mathcal O_K$, and let $\mathfrak m$ be a modulus of $K$ with finite part
$\mathfrak m_0$ (a nonzero ideal of $\mathcal O_K$) and infinite part $\mathfrak m_\infty$ (a
finite set of real places). Let $K_{\mathfrak m}$ be the group of $x \in K^\times$ whose
principal fractional ideal is coprime to $\mathfrak m_0$, and let
$K_{\mathfrak m,1} \subseteq K_{\mathfrak m}$ be the subgroup of those $x$ that are positive at
every real place in $\mathfrak m_\infty$ and satisfy, for every prime
$\mathfrak p \mid \mathfrak m_0$, either $x = 1$ or
$v_{\mathfrak p}(x - 1) \ge v_{\mathfrak p}(\mathfrak m_0)$, where $v_{\mathfrak p}$ of an
element of $K^\times$ or of a nonzero ideal is the exponent of $\mathfrak p$ in its fractional
ideal. Let $U_{\mathfrak m,1}$ be the group
of units of $\mathcal O_K$ lying in $K_{\mathfrak m,1}$, let $\mathrm{Cl}_{\mathfrak m}$ be the
ray class group (fractional ideals coprime to $\mathfrak m_0$ modulo the subgroup generated by
the principal ideals $(x)$ with $x \in K_{\mathfrak m,1}$), and let $\mathrm{Cl}(\mathcal O_K)$
be the class group. For
$x \in K_{\mathfrak m}$, let $\rho(x) \in \{\pm 1\}^{\mathfrak m_\infty} \times
(\mathcal O_K/\mathfrak m_0)^\times$ record the sign of $x$ at each real place in
$\mathfrak m_\infty$ and the residue class of $x$ modulo $\mathfrak m_0$ (the class of $a b^{-1}$
when $x = a/b$ with $a, b \in \mathcal O_K$ prime to $\mathfrak m_0$); $\rho$ is surjective with
kernel $K_{\mathfrak m,1}$. Then the sequence

$$
1 \to U_{\mathfrak m,1} \to \mathcal O_K^\times \to
\{\pm 1\}^{\mathfrak m_\infty} \times (\mathcal O_K/\mathfrak m_0)^\times
\to \mathrm{Cl}_{\mathfrak m} \to \mathrm{Cl}(\mathcal O_K) \to 1
$$

is exact, where the maps are the inclusion, the restriction of $\rho$ to units, the map sending
$\rho(x)$ to the ray class of $(x)$, and the map sending the ray class of a fractional ideal to
its ideal class.

## Sources

- ATLAS lines 1012--1480, aggregated from the separately source-backed map, exactness and surjectivity declarations (not a direct declaration port), and transported through the quotient equivalence backed by lines 2607--2647.

articles.title: The ray class exact sequence
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field with ring of
integers $\mathcal O_K$, and let $\mathfrak m$ be a modulus of $K$ with finite part
$\mathfrak m_0$ (a nonzero ideal of $\mathcal O_K$) and infinite part $\mathfrak m_\infty$ (a
finite set of real places). Let $K_{\mathfrak m}$ be the group of $x \in K^\times$ whose
principal fractional ideal is coprime to $\mathfrak m_0$, and let
$K_{\mathfrak m,1} \subseteq K_{\mathfrak m}$ be the subgroup of those $x$ that are positive at
every real place in $\mathfrak m_\infty$ and satisfy, for every prime
$\mathfrak p \mid \mathfrak m_0$, either $x = 1$ or
$v_{\mathfrak p}(x - 1) \ge v_{\mathfrak p}(\mathfrak m_0)$, where $v_{\mathfrak p}$ of an
element of $K^\times$ or of a nonzero ideal is the exponent of $\mathfrak p$ in its fractional
ideal. Let $U_{\mathfrak m,1}$ be the group
of units of $\mathcal O_K$ lying in $K_{\mathfrak m,1}$, let $\mathrm{Cl}_{\mathfrak m}$ be the
ray class group (fractional ideals coprime to $\mathfrak m_0$ modulo the subgroup generated by
the principal ideals $(x)$ with $x \in K_{\mathfrak m,1}$), and let $\mathrm{Cl}(\mathcal O_K)$
be the class group. Then the sequence

$$
1 \to U_{\mathfrak m,1} \to \mathcal O_K^\times \to K_{\mathfrak m}/K_{\mathfrak m,1}
\to \mathrm{Cl}_{\mathfrak m} \to \mathrm{Cl}(\mathcal O_K) \to 1
$$

is exact, where the maps are the inclusion, the map sending a unit to its class modulo
$K_{\mathfrak m,1}$, the map sending the class of $x$ to the ray class of $(x)$, and the map
sending the ray class of a fractional ideal to its ideal class.

## Sources

- ATLAS lines 1012--1480; this theorem aggregates the separately source-backed map, exactness and surjectivity declarations and is not a direct declaration port.

articles.title: The ideal-class map factors through the ray class group
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field,
$\mathfrak m$ a modulus of $K$, $I_{\mathfrak m}$ the group of nonzero fractional ideals of
$\mathcal O_K$ coprime to the finite part of $\mathfrak m$, $P_{\mathfrak m} \subseteq
I_{\mathfrak m}$ the ray group, and $\mathrm{Cl}_{\mathfrak m} = I_{\mathfrak m}/P_{\mathfrak m}$
the ray class group. As group homomorphisms, the quotient map $I_{\mathfrak m} \to
\mathrm{Cl}_{\mathfrak m}$ followed by the projection $\mathrm{Cl}_{\mathfrak m} \to
\mathrm{Cl}(\mathcal O_K)$ equals the coprime ideal-class map $I_{\mathfrak m} \to
\mathrm{Cl}(\mathcal O_K)$, $I \mapsto [I]$.

articles.title: Kernel of the projection from the ray class group to the class group
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number
field, $\mathfrak m$ a modulus of $K$ with finite part $\mathfrak m_0$, $I_{\mathfrak m}$ the group
of nonzero fractional ideals of $\mathcal O_K$ coprime to $\mathfrak m_0$,
$\mathrm{Cl}_{\mathfrak m}$ the ray class group, $K_{\mathfrak m}$ the group of $x \in K^\times$
with $x\mathcal O_K \in I_{\mathfrak m}$, and $K_{\mathfrak m,1} \subseteq K_{\mathfrak m}$ the
subgroup of those $x$ with $x \equiv 1 \pmod{\mathfrak m_0}$ that are positive at every real place
in $\mathfrak m$. The kernel of the projection $\mathrm{Cl}_{\mathfrak m} \to
\mathrm{Cl}(\mathcal O_K)$ equals the image of the homomorphism
$K_{\mathfrak m}/K_{\mathfrak m,1} \to \mathrm{Cl}_{\mathfrak m}$ that sends the class of $x$ to
the ray class of $x\mathcal O_K$.

## Sources

- ATLAS `exactSeq_exact_at_ray_class`.

articles.title: Projection to the class group on ray class representatives
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field,
$\mathfrak m$ a modulus of $K$, $I_{\mathfrak m}$ the group of nonzero fractional ideals of
$\mathcal O_K$ coprime to the finite part of $\mathfrak m$, and $\mathrm{Cl}_{\mathfrak m}$ the ray
class group. For every $I \in I_{\mathfrak m}$, the projection $\mathrm{Cl}_{\mathfrak m} \to
\mathrm{Cl}(\mathcal O_K)$ sends the ray class of $I$ to $[I]$, the value of the coprime
ideal-class map at $I$.

articles.title: Projecting the image of a ray element to the class group
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field,
$\mathfrak m$ a modulus of $K$ with finite part $\mathfrak m_0$, $I_{\mathfrak m}$ the group of
nonzero fractional ideals of $\mathcal O_K$ coprime to $\mathfrak m_0$, $\mathrm{Cl}_{\mathfrak m}$
the ray class group, $K_{\mathfrak m}$ the group of $x \in K^\times$ with
$x\mathcal O_K \in I_{\mathfrak m}$, and $K_{\mathfrak m,1} \subseteq K_{\mathfrak m}$ the subgroup
of those $x$ with $x \equiv 1 \pmod{\mathfrak m_0}$ that are positive at every real place in
$\mathfrak m$. For every $x \in K_{\mathfrak m}$, sending the class of $x$ through the map
$K_{\mathfrak m}/K_{\mathfrak m,1} \to \mathrm{Cl}_{\mathfrak m}$ that takes the class of $y$ to
the ray class of $y\mathcal O_K$, and then through the projection $\mathrm{Cl}_{\mathfrak m} \to
\mathrm{Cl}(\mathcal O_K)$, gives $[x\mathcal O_K]$, the value of the coprime ideal-class map at
$x\mathcal O_K \in I_{\mathfrak m}$.

articles.title: Projecting the image of a residue-sign value to the class group
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field,
$\mathfrak m$ a modulus of $K$ with finite part $\mathfrak m_0$, $I_{\mathfrak m}$ the group of
nonzero fractional ideals of $\mathcal O_K$ coprime to $\mathfrak m_0$, $\mathrm{Cl}_{\mathfrak m}$
the ray class group, and $K_{\mathfrak m}$ the group of $x \in K^\times$ with
$x\mathcal O_K \in I_{\mathfrak m}$. Let $T_{\mathfrak m}$ be the product of one group of order $2$
for each real place in $\mathfrak m$ with $(\mathcal O_K/\mathfrak m_0)^\times$, let
$\rho : K_{\mathfrak m} \to T_{\mathfrak m}$ be the residue-sign map, and let
$T_{\mathfrak m} \to \mathrm{Cl}_{\mathfrak m}$ be the residue-sign-to-ray-class map. For every
$x \in K_{\mathfrak m}$, sending $\rho(x)$ through this map and then through the projection
$\mathrm{Cl}_{\mathfrak m} \to \mathrm{Cl}(\mathcal O_K)$ gives $[x\mathcal O_K]$, the value of
the coprime ideal-class map at $x\mathcal O_K \in I_{\mathfrak m}$.

articles.title: The ray class group surjects onto the class group
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field and
$\mathfrak m$ a modulus of $K$. The homomorphism from the ray class group of $\mathfrak m$ to the
class group of $\mathcal O_K$, sending the ray class of a fractional ideal coprime to the finite
part of $\mathfrak m$ to its ideal class, is surjective.

## Sources

- ATLAS lines 1478--1480.

articles.title: Projection from the ray class group to the class group
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field,
$\mathfrak m$ a modulus of $K$, $I_{\mathfrak m}$ the group of nonzero fractional ideals of
$\mathcal O_K$ coprime to the finite part of $\mathfrak m$, $P_{\mathfrak m}$ the ray group, and
$\mathrm{Cl}_{\mathfrak m} = I_{\mathfrak m}/P_{\mathfrak m}$ the ray class group. The projection
$\mathrm{Cl}_{\mathfrak m} \to \mathrm{Cl}(\mathcal O_K)$ is the group homomorphism induced by the
coprime ideal-class map $I_{\mathfrak m} \to \mathrm{Cl}(\mathcal O_K)$, $I \mapsto [I]$, which is
trivial on $P_{\mathfrak m}$; it sends the ray class of $I$ to $[I]$.

## Sources

- ATLAS `exactSeq_map4`.

articles.title: Value of the ray-element class map
articles.statement:
Let $\mathfrak m$ be a modulus of a number field $K$
and let $\mathrm{Cl}_{\mathfrak m}$ be its ray class group. For every ray element $x$ of
$\mathfrak m$, the ray-element class map sends $x$ to the ray class in $\mathrm{Cl}_{\mathfrak m}$
of the principal fractional ideal $(x)$, viewed as a fractional ideal coprime to $\mathfrak m$.

articles.title: Ray-element class map
articles.statement:
For a modulus $\mathfrak m$ of a number field $K$, the ray-element
class map is the group homomorphism from the group of ray elements of $\mathfrak m$ to the ray
class group $\mathrm{Cl}_{\mathfrak m}$ that sends $x$ to the ray class of its principal
fractional ideal $(x)$, which is coprime to $\mathfrak m$; that is, the principal-ideal map
followed by the projection onto the ray class group.

## Sources

- ATLAS `exactSeq_map3`, before the quotient lift.

articles.title: Ray elements have order zero at the primes dividing the modulus
articles.statement:
Let $m$ be a
modulus of a number field $K$ and let $x \in K^\times$ be a ray element of $m$. Then for
every finite prime $\mathfrak p$ of $K$ dividing the finite part of $m$, the exponent of
$\mathfrak p$ in the principal fractional ideal $x \mathcal O_K$ is $0$.

articles.title: Ray elements have valuation one at the primes dividing the modulus
articles.statement:
Let $m$ be a
modulus of a number field $K$ and let $x \in K^\times$ be a ray element of $m$. Then for
every finite prime $\mathfrak p$ of $K$ dividing the finite part of $m$, the multiplicative
$\mathfrak p$-adic valuation of $x$ equals $1$.

## Sources

- N406 §21.3, the supported-finite-place fact; compare [`valuation_eq_one_of_spanSingleton_coprime'`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/atlas-lean/blob/e8b31c5cb0bec89b487ce33fe525a2c0b0f8b9c6/v1/Atlas/NumberTheoryI/code/RayClassFields.lean#L1206-L1248) and `hx_coprime`.

articles.title: The residue-sign isomorphism on classes
articles.statement:
Let $m$ be a modulus of a number field $K$. For
every ray element $x$ of $m$, the residue-sign isomorphism of $m$ sends the class of $x$ in the
quotient of the ray elements of $m$ by the ray-one subgroup to the image of $x$ under the
residue-sign map of $m$.

articles.title: The residue-sign isomorphism
articles.statement:
Let $m$ be a modulus of a number field $K$. The residue-sign
isomorphism of $m$ is the group isomorphism from the quotient of the ray elements of $m$ by the
ray-one subgroup of $m$ onto the residue-sign target of $m$ induced by the residue-sign map, which
is surjective with kernel the ray-one subgroup; it sends the class of a ray element $x$ to the
image of $x$ under the residue-sign map.

articles.title: Elements coprime to a modulus
articles.statement:
Let $\mathfrak m$ be a modulus of a number field $K$, with
finite part the nonzero ideal $\mathfrak m_0$ of $\mathcal O_K$. The elements coprime to
$\mathfrak m$ form the subgroup of $K^\times$ consisting of those $x$ whose principal fractional
ideal $(x)$ is coprime to $\mathfrak m$, that is, has exponent $0$ at every nonzero prime ideal
$\mathfrak p$ of $\mathcal O_K$ containing $\mathfrak m_0$.

articles.title: Generators of the ray group
articles.statement:
Let $\mathfrak m$ be a modulus of a number field $K$. The ray
generators of $\mathfrak m$ are the fractional ideals coprime to $\mathfrak m$ of the form $(x)$,
the principal fractional ideal of an element $x \in K^\times$ that is congruent to $1$ modulo
$\mathfrak m$.

articles.title: The ray group is the image of the ray-one elements
articles.statement:
Let $\mathfrak m$ be a modulus of a
number field $K$. The ray group of $\mathfrak m$ equals the image under the principal ray ideal
map of the subgroup of ray-one elements, that is, of the ray elements for $\mathfrak m$ that are
congruent to $1$ modulo the finite part of $\mathfrak m$ and positive at every real place in
its infinite part.

articles.title: The ray group lies in the kernel of the ideal-class map
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field,
$\mathfrak m$ a modulus of $K$, $I_{\mathfrak m}$ the group of nonzero fractional ideals of
$\mathcal O_K$ coprime to the finite part of $\mathfrak m$, and $P_{\mathfrak m} \subseteq
I_{\mathfrak m}$ the ray group. Then $P_{\mathfrak m}$ is contained in the kernel of the coprime
ideal-class map $I_{\mathfrak m} \to \mathrm{Cl}(\mathcal O_K)$, $I \mapsto [I]$: every ideal in
$P_{\mathfrak m}$ has trivial class in $\mathrm{Cl}(\mathcal O_K)$.

articles.title: The ray group of a modulus
articles.statement:
Let $\mathfrak m$ be a modulus of a number field $K$. The ray
group of $\mathfrak m$ is the subgroup of the group of fractional ideals coprime to $\mathfrak m$
generated by the principal ideals $(x)$ of the elements $x \in K^\times$ congruent to $1$ modulo
$\mathfrak m$.

articles.title: Ray-one elements have trivial ray class
articles.statement:
Let $\mathfrak m$ be a modulus of a number field
$K$. Every ray-one element of $\mathfrak m$ lies in the kernel of the ray-element class map; that
is, its principal fractional ideal has trivial class in the ray class group
$\mathrm{Cl}_{\mathfrak m}$.

articles.title: Ray-one subgroup
articles.statement:
Let $m$ be a modulus of a number field $K$. The ray-one subgroup of $m$ is
the subgroup of the ray elements of $m$ consisting of the ray elements $x$ that lie in the finite
ray-one subgroup of $m$ (those congruent to $1$ at the finite part of $m$) and in the subgroup of
ray elements positive at every real place in the infinite part of $m$.

articles.title: Exactness at the ray-element quotient (kernel form)
articles.statement:
Let $\mathfrak m$ be a modulus of a
number field $K$. The kernel of the quotient-to-ray-class map, from the quotient of the ray
elements of $\mathfrak m$ by the ray-one elements to the ray class group
$\mathrm{Cl}_{\mathfrak m}$, equals the image of the map sending each unit
$u \in \mathcal O_K^\times$ to the class of $u$ in that quotient.

## Sources

- ATLAS `exactSeq_exact_at_quotient`.

articles.title: Quotient-to-ray-class map on representatives
articles.statement:
Let $\mathfrak m$ be a modulus of a number
field $K$. For every ray element $x$ of $\mathfrak m$, the quotient-to-ray-class map sends the
class of $x$ modulo the ray-one elements to the image of $x$ under the ray-element class map.

articles.title: Exactness at the ray class group
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field, $\mathfrak m$ a modulus of
$K$ with finite part $\mathfrak m_0$, $I_{\mathfrak m}$ the group of nonzero fractional ideals of
$\mathcal O_K$ coprime to $\mathfrak m_0$, $\mathrm{Cl}_{\mathfrak m}$ the ray class group,
$K_{\mathfrak m}$ the group of $x \in K^\times$ with $x\mathcal O_K \in I_{\mathfrak m}$, and
$K_{\mathfrak m,1} \subseteq K_{\mathfrak m}$ the subgroup of those $x$ with
$x \equiv 1 \pmod{\mathfrak m_0}$ that are positive at every real place in $\mathfrak m$. The
sequence $K_{\mathfrak m}/K_{\mathfrak m,1} \to \mathrm{Cl}_{\mathfrak m} \to
\mathrm{Cl}(\mathcal O_K)$ is exact at $\mathrm{Cl}_{\mathfrak m}$, where the first map sends the
class of $x$ to the ray class of $x\mathcal O_K$ and the second is the projection: a ray class
maps to the identity of $\mathrm{Cl}(\mathcal O_K)$ if and only if it lies in the image of the
first map.

## Sources

- ATLAS `exactSeq_exact_at_ray_class`.

articles.title: Quotient-to-ray-class map
articles.statement:
For a modulus $\mathfrak m$ of a number field $K$, the
quotient-to-ray-class map is the group homomorphism from the quotient of the group of ray
elements of $\mathfrak m$ by the subgroup of ray-one elements to the ray class group
$\mathrm{Cl}_{\mathfrak m}$ induced by the ray-element class map: the class of a ray element $x$
goes to the ray class of its principal fractional ideal $(x)$. It is well defined because
ray-one elements lie in the kernel of the ray-element class map.

## Sources

- ATLAS `exactSeq_map3`.

articles.title: Components of the residue-sign map
articles.statement:
Let $m$ be a modulus of a number field $K$. For every
ray element $x$ of $m$, the image of $x$ under the residue-sign map of $m$ is the pair whose first
component is the image of $x$ under the infinite sign map of $m$ and whose second component is the
image of $x$ under the finite residue map of $m$.

articles.title: Kernel criterion for the residue-sign map
articles.statement:
Let $m$ be a modulus of a number field $K$. A
ray element $x$ of $m$ is sent to $1$ by the residue-sign map of $m$ if and only if $x$ is a ray
element congruent to $1$ modulo $m$: $x$ is a ray element of $m$, $x$ is congruent to $1$ at the
finite part of $m$, and $x$ is positive at every real place in the infinite part of $m$.

articles.title: Kernel of the residue-sign map
articles.statement:
Let $m$ be a modulus of a number field $K$. The kernel of
the residue-sign map of $m$ is the ray-one subgroup of $m$.

articles.title: Surjectivity of the residue-sign map
articles.statement:
Let $m$ be a modulus of a number field $K$. Every
element of the residue-sign target of $m$ is the image of some ray element of $m$ under the
residue-sign map of $m$.

articles.title: Residue-sign map
articles.statement:
Let $m$ be a modulus of a number field $K$. The residue-sign map of $m$
is the group homomorphism from the ray elements of $m$ to the residue-sign target of $m$ that
sends a ray element $x$ to the pair formed by the image of $x$ under the infinite sign map of $m$
and the image of $x$ under the finite residue map of $m$.

articles.title: Residue-sign target
articles.statement:
Let $m$ be a modulus of a number field $K$, with finite part the
nonzero ideal $\mathfrak{m}_0$ of the ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$ and infinite part the
finite set $S$ of real places of $K$. Let $G$ denote $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$ written
multiplicatively, let $G^S$ denote the group of functions from $S$ to $G$ (one sign for each place
in $S$), and let $(\mathcal{O}_K/\mathfrak{m}_0)^\times$ denote the unit group of the quotient ring
$\mathcal{O}_K/\mathfrak{m}_0$. The residue-sign target of $m$ is the product group
$G^S \times (\mathcal{O}_K/\mathfrak{m}_0)^\times$.

articles.title: The residue-sign transport square commutes
articles.statement:
Let $\mathfrak m$ be a modulus of a number
field $K$. The residue-sign map from the ray elements of $\mathfrak m$ to the residue-sign target,
followed by the transported residue-sign-to-ray-class map, equals the ray-element class map.

articles.title: Residue-sign-to-ray-class map through the quotient isomorphism
articles.statement:
Let $\mathfrak m$ be a
modulus of a number field $K$ with finite part $\mathfrak m_0$, let $K_{\mathfrak m}$ be the
group of elements of $K^\times$ whose principal ideal is coprime to $\mathfrak m_0$, and let
$K_{\mathfrak m,1}$ be its subgroup of elements congruent to $1$ modulo $\mathfrak m_0$ and
positive at every real place of $\mathfrak m$. Let $T_{\mathfrak m}$ be the residue-sign target
of $\mathfrak m$, let $\mathrm{Cl}_{\mathfrak m}$ be the ray class group of $\mathfrak m$, let
$\psi : K_{\mathfrak m}/K_{\mathfrak m,1} \to T_{\mathfrak m}$ be the canonical isomorphism
induced by sending $x$ to its signs at the real places of $\mathfrak m$ and its residue modulo
$\mathfrak m_0$, and let $\phi : K_{\mathfrak m}/K_{\mathfrak m,1} \to \mathrm{Cl}_{\mathfrak m}$
be the homomorphism induced by sending $x$ to the ray class of its principal ideal $(x)$. Then
for every $q \in K_{\mathfrak m}/K_{\mathfrak m,1}$, the residue-sign-to-ray-class map
$T_{\mathfrak m} \to \mathrm{Cl}_{\mathfrak m}$ sends $\psi(q)$ to $\phi(q)$.

articles.title: Kernel of the ray class map on residue-sign values
articles.statement:
Let $\mathfrak m$ be a modulus of a
number field $K$. The kernel of the residue-sign-to-ray-class map from the residue-sign target
of $\mathfrak m$ to the ray class group of $\mathfrak m$ equals the image of the homomorphism
$\mathcal O_K^\times \to$ (residue-sign target) that sends a unit $u$ to its residue-sign value,
namely its signs at the real places of $\mathfrak m$ together with its residue modulo the finite
part of $\mathfrak m$.

articles.title: Exactness at the ray class group, residue-sign form
articles.statement:
Let $\mathfrak m$ be a modulus of a
number field $K$, with finite part the nonzero ideal $\mathfrak m_0$ of $\mathcal O_K$ and infinite
part the finite set $\mathfrak m_\infty$ of real places of $K$. Let $\varphi$ be the homomorphism
from the residue-sign group $\{\pm 1\}^{\mathfrak m_\infty} \times
(\mathcal O_K/\mathfrak m_0)^\times$ to the ray class group $\mathrm{Cl}_{\mathfrak m}(K)$ that
sends the signs at the places in $\mathfrak m_\infty$ and the residue class modulo $\mathfrak m_0$
of an element $x \in K^\times$ coprime to $\mathfrak m_0$ to the ray class of the principal ideal
$(x)$, and let $\pi \colon \mathrm{Cl}_{\mathfrak m}(K) \to \mathrm{Cl}(K)$ be the projection to
the ideal class group. Then a ray class $c$ satisfies $\pi(c) = 1$ if and only if $c$ lies in the
image of $\varphi$; that is, the sequence is exact at $\mathrm{Cl}_{\mathfrak m}(K)$.

articles.title: Ray class map on residue-sign values
articles.statement:
Let $\mathfrak m$ be a modulus of a number field
$K$ and let $x$ be a ray element of $\mathfrak m$, that is, $x \in K^\times$ with principal ideal
coprime to the finite part of $\mathfrak m$. Then the residue-sign-to-ray-class map sends the
residue-sign value of $x$ (its signs at the real places of $\mathfrak m$ together with its
residue modulo the finite part) to the ray class of the principal ideal $(x)$.

articles.title: Ray class map on residues and signs
articles.statement:
Let $\mathfrak m$ be a modulus of a number field
$K$ with finite part $\mathfrak m_0$, let $K_{\mathfrak m}$ be the group of elements of $K^\times$
whose principal ideal is coprime to $\mathfrak m_0$, and let $K_{\mathfrak m,1}$ be its subgroup
of elements congruent to $1$ modulo $\mathfrak m_0$ and positive at every real place of
$\mathfrak m$. Let $T_{\mathfrak m}$ be the residue-sign target of $\mathfrak m$ and let
$\mathrm{Cl}_{\mathfrak m}$ be the ray class group of $\mathfrak m$. Let
$\psi : K_{\mathfrak m}/K_{\mathfrak m,1} \to T_{\mathfrak m}$ be the canonical isomorphism
induced by sending $x$ to its signs at the real places of $\mathfrak m$ and its residue modulo
$\mathfrak m_0$, and let $\phi : K_{\mathfrak m}/K_{\mathfrak m,1} \to \mathrm{Cl}_{\mathfrak m}$
be the homomorphism induced by sending $x \in K_{\mathfrak m}$ to the ray class of its principal
ideal $(x)$. The residue-sign-to-ray-class map is the group homomorphism
$\phi \circ \psi^{-1} : T_{\mathfrak m} \to \mathrm{Cl}_{\mathfrak m}$.

articles.title: Trivial sign at a real place means positivity
articles.statement:
Let $w$ be a real place of a number field
$K$ with real embedding $\sigma_w \colon K \to \mathbb{R}$. For every $x \in K^\times$, the sign of
$x$ at $w$, an element of $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$ written multiplicatively, is the identity if
and only if $\sigma_w(x) > 0$.

articles.title: Sign of a unit at a real place
articles.statement:
For a real place $w$ of a number field $K$, let
$\sigma_w \colon K \to \mathbb{R}$ be the corresponding real embedding. The sign at $w$ is the
group homomorphism from $K^\times$ to $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$, written multiplicatively, that
sends $x$ to the class of $0$ (the identity) if $\sigma_w(x) > 0$ and to the class of $1$
otherwise.

articles.title: Principal ideals agree exactly up to an integral unit
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field with ring
of integers $\mathcal O_K$. For all $x, y \in K^\times$, the principal fractional ideals
$x\mathcal O_K$ and $y\mathcal O_K$ are equal if and only if $x = uy$ for some unit
$u \in \mathcal O_K^\times$.

articles.title: Embedding a cyclotomic extension of the rationals
articles.statement:
A cyclotomic extension `K` of `ℚ` embeds into any characteristic-zero
field `L` containing a primitive `n`-th root of unity, sending the
distinguished root `ζ` to it.

articles.title: Homogenized cyclotomic value in a field
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field, $n$ a natural number and
$a, b$ integers such that the image of $b$ in $K$ is nonzero. Then the image in $K$ of the
homogenized cyclotomic value $\Phi_n(a, b)$ equals $b^{\varphi(n)} \Phi_n(a/b)$, where $\Phi_n$
is the $n$-th cyclotomic polynomial over $K$, $\varphi$ is Euler's totient function, and $b$
and $a/b$ are computed in $K$.

## Sources

- Ömer Avcı, *Large Zsigmondy Primes*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A62, Section 2 (notation `Φ_n(a, b)`).

articles.title: Homogenized cyclotomic value with second argument one
articles.statement:
For every natural number $n$
and every integer $a$, the homogenized cyclotomic value $\Phi_n(a, 1)$ equals $\Phi_n(a)$, the
value at $a$ of the $n$-th cyclotomic polynomial with integer coefficients.

## Sources

- Ömer Avcı, *Large Zsigmondy Primes*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A62, Section 2 (notation `Φ_n(a, b)`).

articles.title: Homogenized cyclotomic value of index one
articles.statement:
For all integers $a$ and $b$, the
homogenized cyclotomic value $\Phi_1(a, b)$ equals $a - b$.

## Sources

- Ömer Avcı, *Large Zsigmondy Primes*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A62, Lemma 3 (v) (the case `n = 1`).

articles.title: Homogenized cyclotomic value of index two
articles.statement:
For all integers $a$ and $b$, the
homogenized cyclotomic value $\Phi_2(a, b)$ equals $a + b$.

## Sources

- Ömer Avcı, *Large Zsigmondy Primes*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A62, Lemma 3 (v) (the case `n = 2`).

articles.title: Homogenized cyclotomic value
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$ and integers $a, b$, let
$c_0, \dots, c_{\varphi(n)}$ be the integer coefficients of the $n$-th cyclotomic polynomial,
whose degree is $\varphi(n)$, where $\varphi$ is Euler's totient function. The homogenized
cyclotomic value is the integer

$$\Phi_n(a, b) = \sum_{i=0}^{\varphi(n)} c_i \, a^i \, b^{\varphi(n) - i}.$$

When $b \neq 0$ it equals $b^{\varphi(n)} \Phi_n(a/b)$, where $\Phi_n$ is the $n$-th cyclotomic
polynomial.

## Sources

- Ömer Avcı, *Large Zsigmondy Primes*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A62, Section 2 (notation `Φ_n(a, b)`, Lemma 3 and the explicit values in the proof of Theorem 1).

articles.title: A zeta-twisted cyclotomic product identity
articles.statement:
For $n \ge 1$ and complex $z$, let
$\hat\Phi_n(z) = \prod_\omega (1 - z\omega)$, the product over the primitive $n$-th roots of
unity $\omega$. Let $z$ be a complex number with $|z| < 1$, let $s > 1$ be real, and let
$\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function. Then

$$
\prod_{i \ge 1} (1 - z^i)^{-1/i^s} = \prod_{i \ge 1} \hat\Phi_i(z)^{-\zeta(s)/i^s}
$$

in the sense that, as $N \to \infty$, the partial products over $1 \le i \le N$ of both sides
converge to a common limit. Here $(1 - z^i)^{-1/i^s} = \exp(-i^{-s} \log(1 - z^i))$ and
$\hat\Phi_i(z)^{-\zeta(s)/i^s} = \exp(-\zeta(s) \, i^{-s} \sum_\omega \log(1 - z\omega))$, where
$\log$ is the principal branch of the logarithm.

The exponent $-\zeta(s)/i^s$ follows arXiv:2511.16975, Theorem 2.2. The INTEGERS record shows
$-\zeta(s)/i$; with that exponent the right side would equal $1$ by the constancy of
$\prod_{n \ge 1} \hat\Phi_n(z)^{-1/n}$, while the left side does not.

## Sources

- Hartosh Singh Bal, *Constancy of an Infinite Cyclotomic Product via Ramanujan Sums*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A96, Theorem 2.

articles.title: Constancy of an infinite cyclotomic product
articles.statement:
For $n \ge 1$ and complex $z$, let
$\hat\Phi_n(z) = \prod_\omega (1 - z\omega)$, the product over the primitive $n$-th roots of
unity $\omega$; thus $\hat\Phi_1(z) = 1 - z$ and $\hat\Phi_n = \Phi_n$ for $n \ge 2$, where
$\Phi_n$ is the $n$-th cyclotomic polynomial. For every complex $z$ with $|z| < 1$, the partial
products $\prod_{n=1}^{N} \hat\Phi_n(z)^{-1/n}$ tend to $1$ as $N \to \infty$, where
$\hat\Phi_n(z)^{-1/n} = \exp\bigl(-\tfrac{1}{n} \sum_\omega \log(1 - z\omega)\bigr)$ and $\log$
is the principal branch of the logarithm.

Each factor $1 - z\omega$ has positive real part, and this branch equals $1$ at $z = 0$, as in
the paper's logarithmic-derivative proof. The paper writes the product as
$P(z) = -\prod_{n \ge 1} \Phi_n(z)^{-1/n}$; the sign absorbs $\Phi_1(z) = -(1 - z)$, and the
claim is $P(z) \equiv 1$.

## Sources

- Hartosh Singh Bal, *Constancy of an Infinite Cyclotomic Product via Ramanujan Sums*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A96, Theorem 1.

articles.title: Fields without primitive element sums have few prime factors
articles.statement:
Let $q$ and $n$ be natural
numbers with $\gcd(q, n) = 1$. If it is not the case that every finite field $L$ with $q^n$
elements contains an element $\alpha$ such that both $\alpha$ and $\alpha + \alpha^{-1}$ generate
the multiplicative group $L^\times$, then $q^n - 1$ has at most $15$ distinct prime factors.

The hypothesis $\gcd(q, n) = 1$ is added: the source derives the bound from the Liao–Li–Pu
criterion, which assumes it.

## Sources

- Gustav Kjærbye Bagger, *Hybrid Bounds for Prime Divisors*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A95, Corollary 2.

articles.title: Hybrid bound for prime divisors of $x^n - 1$
articles.statement:
The hybrid bound. Let `n = ∏_{i=1}^m p_i^{a_i}` with distinct primes `p_i` (in any order),
`x > 1`, and `ω_n = ω(x^n - 1)`. With `p_0 := 1`, let
`Π^j = {ρ prime : ρ ≡ 1 (mod p_j), ρ ≢ 1 (mod p_s) for j < s ≤ m}` and `r_{i,j}` its `i`-th
element (`Nat.nth`, `0`-indexed here). The source's
`x ≥ min_{k_0 + ⋯ + k_m = ω_n} max_{0 ≤ t ≤ m} (1 + ∏_{j ≤ t} ∏_{i ≤ k_j} r_{i,j})^{T(t)}` with
`T(t) = ∏_{s=1}^t p_s^{-a_s}` is stated equivalently, after raising to the power
`∏_{s ≤ t} p_s^{a_s}`, as the existence of a composition `k` meeting every bound. The parts `k_j`
range over `ℕ` (the source writes `k_i ∈ ℤ⁺`; with positive parts the claim fails for
`n = 3`, `x = 2`, where `x^3 - 1 = 7` and `ω_n = 1` admits no positive composition into two
parts).

## Sources

- Gustav Kjærbye Bagger, *Hybrid Bounds for Prime Divisors*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A95, Theorem 1.

articles.title: Primorials below powers of sixteen
articles.statement:
For every positive integer $w$, we have $w < 16$ if and
only if the product $p_1 p_2 \cdots p_w$ of the first $w$ primes is less than $16^w$.

## Sources

- Gustav Kjærbye Bagger, *Hybrid Bounds for Prime Divisors*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A95, Proposition 10.

articles.title: The line problem for quintic extensions
articles.statement:
Let $E_5$ be the set of $647$ prime powers listed
in the appendix of arXiv:2412.00010, the smallest being $2$ and the largest $62791$. Let $q$ be a
natural number not in $E_5$. Then for all finite fields $K$ and $L$ with $L$ an extension of $K$,
$|K| = q$ and $[L : K] = 5$, and all nonzero $\gamma_1, \gamma_2 \in L$ with
$K(\gamma_1/\gamma_2) = L$, there is $a \in K$ such that $a\gamma_2 + \gamma_1$ generates the
multiplicative group $L^\times$.

## Sources

- Gustav Kjærbye Bagger, *Hybrid Bounds for Prime Divisors*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A95, Proposition 8.

articles.title: General prime sieve for the line problem
articles.statement:
Let $q$ and $n$ be natural numbers, let $\omega$
be the number of distinct prime factors of $q^n - 1$, and let $S$ and $T$ be disjoint sets of prime
factors of $q^n - 1$, with $s = |S|$ and $r = |T|$. Let $k$ be the product of the prime factors of
$q^n - 1$ that lie in neither $S$ nor $T$, and put $\delta = 1 - \sum_{\rho \in S} 1/\rho$,
$\varepsilon = \sum_{l \in T} 1/l$ and $\mu = \varphi(k)/k$, where $\varphi$ is Euler's totient
function. Suppose that $\delta\mu > \varepsilon$ and

$$
q > (n - 1)^2 \left(\frac{2^{\omega - s - r} \mu (s - 1 + 2\delta) - \delta\mu + r -
\varepsilon}{\delta\mu - \varepsilon}\right)^2.
$$

Then for all finite fields $K$ and $L$ with $L$ an extension of $K$, $|K| = q$ and $[L : K] = n$,
and all nonzero $\gamma_1, \gamma_2 \in L$ with $K(\gamma_1/\gamma_2) = L$, there is $a \in K$
such that $a\gamma_2 + \gamma_1$ generates the multiplicative group $L^\times$.

## Sources

- Gustav Kjærbye Bagger, *Hybrid Bounds for Prime Divisors*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A95, Proposition 7, quoting Bailey, Cohen, Sutherland and Trudgian, Lemma 1.

articles.title: Cohen's modified prime sieve for the line problem
articles.statement:
Let $q$ and $n$ be natural numbers such
that $q^n - 1$ has $\omega \ge 2$ distinct prime factors. Let $S$ be a set of $s$ prime factors of
$q^n - 1$, let $l$ be a prime factor of $q^n - 1$ not in $S$, let $k$ be the product of the prime
factors of $q^n - 1$ that are neither $l$ nor in $S$, and put
$\delta = 1 - \sum_{\rho \in S} 1/\rho$. Suppose that $\delta > 1/(l\varphi(k))$, where $\varphi$ is
Euler's totient function, and

$$
q > (n - 1)^2 \left(\frac{2^{\omega - s - 1} \varphi(k) (s - 1 + 2\delta) + 1 - 1/l}
{\varphi(k)\delta - 1/l} - 1\right)^2.
$$

Then for all finite fields $K$ and $L$ with $L$ an extension of $K$, $|K| = q$ and $[L : K] = n$,
and all nonzero $\gamma_1, \gamma_2 \in L$ with $K(\gamma_1/\gamma_2) = L$, there is $a \in K$
such that $a\gamma_2 + \gamma_1$ generates the multiplicative group $L^\times$.

## Sources

- Gustav Kjærbye Bagger, *Hybrid Bounds for Prime Divisors*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A95, Proposition 6, quoting S. D. Cohen, Proposition 6.3.

articles.title: Cohen's prime sieve for the line problem
articles.statement:
Let $q$ and $n$ be natural numbers, let $\omega$
be the number of distinct prime factors of $q^n - 1$, and let $S$ be a set of $s$ prime factors of
$q^n - 1$ with $\delta = 1 - \sum_{\rho \in S} 1/\rho > 0$. Suppose that
$q > (n - 1)^2 \, 2^{2(\omega - s)} \left(\frac{s - 1}{\delta} + 2\right)^2$. Then for all finite
fields $K$ and $L$ with $L$ an extension of $K$, $|K| = q$ and $[L : K] = n$, and all nonzero
$\gamma_1, \gamma_2 \in L$ with $K(\gamma_1/\gamma_2) = L$, there is $a \in K$ such that
$a\gamma_2 + \gamma_1$ generates the multiplicative group $L^\times$.

## Sources

- Gustav Kjærbye Bagger, *Hybrid Bounds for Prime Divisors*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A95, Proposition 5, quoting S. D. Cohen, Proposition 4.3.

articles.title: Primitive element sums away from exceptional pairs
articles.statement:
Let $q$ and $n > 1$ be coprime natural
numbers, and let $\omega$ be the number of distinct prime factors of $q^n - 1$. Suppose that the
pair $(n, \omega)$ is none of the following $33$ pairs: $(2, w)$ for $1 \le w \le 11$; $(3, w)$ for
$2 \le w \le 7$; $(4, w)$ for $w \in \{2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9\}$; $(5, 3)$ and $(5, 5)$; $(6, w)$ for
$3 \le w \le 6$; $(8, 4)$ and $(8, 6)$; and $(12, 6)$. Then every finite field $L$ with $q^n$
elements contains an element $\alpha$ such that both $\alpha$ and $\alpha + \alpha^{-1}$ generate
the multiplicative group $L^\times$.

The hypotheses $n > 1$ and $\gcd(q, n) = 1$ are added. For $n = 1$ and $q = 2$ the pair $(1, 0)$
is not exceptional, yet $\mathbb{F}_2$ has no such $\alpha$; and the source derives the result from
the Liao–Li–Pu criterion, which assumes coprimality.

## Sources

- Gustav Kjærbye Bagger, *Hybrid Bounds for Prime Divisors*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A95, Proposition 12.

articles.title: Liao–Li–Pu criterion for primitive element sums
articles.statement:
Let $q$ and $n$ be coprime natural numbers
with $q^n > 2$, and let $\omega$ be the number of distinct prime factors of $q^n - 1$. If
$16^\omega < q^n$, that is $q^{n/2} > 2^{2\omega}$, then every finite field $L$ with $q^n$ elements
contains an element $\alpha$ such that both $\alpha$ and $\alpha + \alpha^{-1}$ generate the
multiplicative group $L^\times$.

The hypothesis $q^n > 2$ is added to the source's statement: for $q = 2$ and $n = 1$ the inequality
$16^0 < 2$ holds, but the only generator of $\mathbb{F}_2^\times$ is $1$, and $1 + 1^{-1} = 0$.

## Sources

- Gustav Kjærbye Bagger, *Hybrid Bounds for Prime Divisors*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A95, Proposition 9, quoting Liao, Li and Pu, Theorem 1.3.

articles.title: Finite fields with a primitive element sum
articles.statement:
For every natural number $q$, we have
$q \notin \{2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 9, 13, 25, 121\}$ if and only if every finite field $L$ with $q$
elements contains an element $\alpha$ such that both $\alpha$ and $\alpha + \alpha^{-1}$ generate
the multiplicative group $L^\times$.

## Sources

- Gustav Kjærbye Bagger, *Hybrid Bounds for Prime Divisors*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A95, Proposition 11, quoting Cohen, Oliveira e Silva, Sutherland and Trudgian, Corollary 2.

articles.title: Divisibility of $x^p - 1$ by $p$
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, let $x$ be a positive integer, and
let $\Phi_p$ be the $p$-th cyclotomic polynomial with integer coefficients. Then
$p \mid x^p - 1$ if and only if $p \mid x - 1$ and $p \mid \Phi_p(x)$.

## Sources

- Gustav Kjærbye Bagger, *Hybrid Bounds for Prime Divisors*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A95, Lemma 2.

articles.title: Divisibility of $x^{rp^a} - 1$ by $p$
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, let $r$ and $a$ be natural
numbers with $r$ coprime to $p$, let $x$ be a positive integer, and let $\Phi_p$ be the $p$-th
cyclotomic polynomial with integer coefficients. Then $p \mid x^{rp^a} - 1$ if and only if
$p \mid x^r - 1$ and $p \mid \Phi_p(x^{rp^{i-1}})$ for every $i \in \{1, \dots, a\}$.

## Sources

- Gustav Kjærbye Bagger, *Hybrid Bounds for Prime Divisors*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A95, Lemma 4.

articles.title: A common prime divisor of $y - 1$ and $\Phi_p(y^{p^{a-1}})$ is $p$
articles.statement:
Let $\rho$ and $p$ be
primes, let $a \ge 1$ be a natural number, let $y$ be a positive integer, and let $\Phi_p$ be the
$p$-th cyclotomic polynomial with integer coefficients. If $\rho \mid y - 1$ and
$\rho \mid \Phi_p(y^{p^{a-1}})$, then $\rho = p$.

## Sources

- Gustav Kjærbye Bagger, *Hybrid Bounds for Prime Divisors*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A95, Lemma 3.

articles.title: A common prime divisor of $x - 1$ and $\Phi_p(x)$ is $p$
articles.statement:
Let $\rho$ and $p$ be primes,
let $x$ be a positive integer, and let $\Phi_p$ be the $p$-th cyclotomic polynomial with integer
coefficients. If $\rho \mid x - 1$ and $\rho \mid \Phi_p(x)$, then $\rho = p$.

## Sources

- Gustav Kjærbye Bagger, *Hybrid Bounds for Prime Divisors*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A95, Lemma 1.

articles.title: Hybrid bound for prime divisors of $x^p - 1$
articles.statement:
The `p`-hybrid bound (Theorem 1 for prime `n = p`). For a prime `p`, `x > 1` and
`ω_p = ω(x^p - 1)`, let `r_{i,0}` and `r_{j,1}` enumerate the primes `≢ 1` and `≡ 1 (mod p)`
(`Nat.nth`, `0`-indexed here). The source's
`x ≥ min_{0 ≤ k < ω_p} max(1 + ∏_{i ≤ k} r_{i,0}, (1 + ∏_{i ≤ k} r_{i,0} ∏_{j ≤ ω_p - k} r_{j,1})^{1/p})`
is stated equivalently as the existence of `k < ω_p` meeting both bounds, the second after
raising to the `p`-th power.

## Sources

- Gustav Kjærbye Bagger, *Hybrid Bounds for Prime Divisors*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A95, Proposition 2.

articles.title: Prime divisors of $\Phi_p(x)$ other than $p$ are $1$ modulo $p$
articles.statement:
Let $\rho$ and $p$ be
distinct primes, let $x$ be a positive integer, and let $\Phi_p$ be the $p$-th cyclotomic
polynomial with integer coefficients. If $\rho \mid \Phi_p(x)$, then $\rho \equiv 1 \pmod p$.

## Sources

- Gustav Kjærbye Bagger, *Hybrid Bounds for Prime Divisors*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A95, Proposition 1.

articles.title: Ramified bound on prime divisors of $x^p - 1$ for prime $p$
articles.statement:
The `p`-ramified bound (Theorem 2 for prime `n = p`). For a prime `p`, `x > 1` and
`ω_p = ω(x^p - 1)`, let `r_{i,0}` and `r_{j,1}` enumerate the primes `≢ 1` and `≡ 1 (mod p)`
(`Nat.nth`, `0`-indexed here), `p = r_{b,0}`, `R^0_k = ∏_{i < k} r_{i,0}` and
`R^1_k = ∏_{j < ω_p - k} r_{j,1}`. The source's minima over `k ∈ [0, k') ∪ [k', ω_p)` (with
`k' = b + 1`) are stated as the existence of `k < ω_p` meeting both bounds, the second after
raising to the `p`-th power; `p^{-1} R^0_{k+1}` is written as the product over
`{0, …, k} \ {b}`. If `p ∤ x^p - 1`: `k ≤ b` gives `1 + R^0_k ≤ x`, `1 + R^0_k R^1_k ≤ x^p`, and
`k > b` gives `1 + p^{-1} R^0_{k+1} ≤ x`, `1 + p^{-1} R^0_{k+1} R^1_k ≤ x^p`. If `p ∣ x^p - 1`:
`k ≤ b` gives `1 + p R^0_{k-1} ≤ x`, `1 + p^2 R^0_{k-1} R^1_k ≤ x^p`, and `k > b` gives
`1 + R^0_k ≤ x`, `1 + p R^0_k R^1_k ≤ x^p`. The divisible case requires `p ≠ 2` and has `k > 0`:
`R^0_{-1}` is undefined at `k = 0`, and for `p = 2`, `x = 3` (`x^2 - 1 = 8`, `ω_2 = 1`) the only
admitted `k = 0` fails under any reading (with `R^0_{-1} := 1` the second bound reads
`1 + 4 · 3 = 13 ≤ 9`).

## Sources

- Gustav Kjærbye Bagger, *Hybrid Bounds for Prime Divisors*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A95, Proposition 3.

articles.title: Ramified bound on the number of prime divisors of $x^n - 1$
articles.statement:
The ramified bound. Let `n = ∏_{i=1}^m p_i^{a_i}` with primes `p_1 < ⋯ < p_m` (the ordering
the source fixes at the start of its Section 5), `x > 1`, `ω_n = ω(x^n - 1)`, and, with
`p_0 := 1`, let `r_{i,j}` be the `i`-th element (`Nat.nth`, `0`-indexed here) of
`Π^j = {ρ prime : ρ ≡ 1 (mod p_j), ρ ≢ 1 (mod p_s) for j < s ≤ m}`. Fix a prime factor `p_α` of
`n` and write `p_α = r_{b,τ}` with `τ ≤ m`. As in `hybrid_bound_prime_divisors`, the source's
`x ≥ min_{k_0 + ⋯ + k_m = ω_n} max_t (1 + ∏_{j ≤ t} δ_α(j) ∏_{i ≤ k_j} r_{i,j})^{T(t)}` is stated
as the existence of a composition `k` (parts in `ℕ`, not `ℤ⁺`) meeting every bound after raising
to the power `∏_{s ≤ t} p_s^{a_s}`. The factors `δ_α(j)` are applied to the block products: if
`p_α ∣ x^n - 1`, block `τ` with `k_τ < b` (`1`-indexed in the source, `k_τ ≤ b` here) has its
largest factor `r_{k_τ,τ}` replaced by `p_α`, and block `α` gains the factor `p_α^{a_α}`; if
`p_α ∤ x^n - 1`, block `τ` with `k_τ ≥ b` drops `p_α` and takes the next element instead. In
the divisible case the composition also has `k_τ > 0` (the source's `δ_α(τ)` is undefined at
`k_τ = 0`). The source's worked example (`n = 3`, `ω_3 = 10`: `x ≥ 4387` if `3 ∣ x^3 - 1`,
`x ≥ 5423` otherwise) is reproduced exactly by this reading. Definitions follow the arXiv version
(arXiv:2412.00010), whose statement matches the journal record.

## Sources

- Gustav Kjærbye Bagger, *Hybrid Bounds for Prime Divisors*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A95, Theorem 2.

articles.title: The ramified bound for $n = 2^a$
articles.statement:
Let $a \ge 1$, let $n = 2^a$, let $x > 1$ be a natural
number, let $\omega_n$ be the number of distinct prime factors of $x^n - 1$, and let
$s_1 = 2 < s_2 = 3 < s_3 = 5 < \cdots$ be the primes in increasing order. Then

$$\min\Bigl(1 + 2n \prod_{i=1}^{\omega_n} s_i,\ 1 + \prod_{i=2}^{\omega_n + 1} s_i\Bigr) \le x^n.$$

Equivalently, $x$ is at least the smaller of the $n$-th roots of these two numbers, which is the
form of the source. The source admits every positive integer $x$; at $x = 1$ the number
$x^n - 1 = 0$ has an empty prime factorization, so $\omega_n = 0$ and the bound would read
$2 \le 1$.

## Sources

- Gustav Kjærbye Bagger, *Hybrid Bounds for Prime Divisors*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A95, Theorem 3.

articles.title: A weaker ramified bound for $n = 2^a$
articles.statement:
Let $a \ge 1$, let $n = 2^a$, let $x > 1$ be a
natural number, let $\omega_n$ be the number of distinct prime factors of $x^n - 1$, and let
$s_1 = 2 < s_2 = 3 < s_3 = 5 < \cdots$ be the primes in increasing order. Then

$$\min\Bigl(1 + n \prod_{i=1}^{\omega_n} s_i,\ 1 + \prod_{i=2}^{\omega_n + 1} s_i\Bigr) \le x^n.$$

This weakens the ramified bound for $n = 2^a$, which has the factor $2n$ in place of $n$. The
extracted text of the source reads $n = 2a$; its own discussion ($n = 4$, "extends to $n = 2^a$")
shows that $n = 2^a$ is meant. As in the stronger bound, $x > 1$ replaces the source's positive
integer $x$.

## Sources

- Gustav Kjærbye Bagger, *Hybrid Bounds for Prime Divisors*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A95, Corollary 1.

articles.title: Factorization into composed cyclotomic polynomials
articles.statement:
Let $x$ be the indeterminate of the
polynomial ring $\mathbb{Z}[x]$. Let $m$ be a natural number, let $p_1, \dots, p_m$ be primes,
not necessarily distinct, let $a_1, \dots, a_m$ be natural numbers, and put
$n = \prod_{i=1}^m p_i^{a_i}$. For $1 \le i \le m$ let $x_i = x^{N_i}$ with
$N_i = \prod_{1 \le r < i} p_r^{a_r}$. Then

$$x^n - 1 = (x - 1) \prod_{i=1}^m \prod_{j=1}^{a_i} \Phi_{p_i}(x_i^{p_i^{j-1}}),$$

where $\Phi_p$ is the $p$-th cyclotomic polynomial over $\mathbb{Z}$ and $\Phi_{p_i}(\cdot)$
denotes composition of polynomials.

The source takes the prime factorization of $n$; the identity needs only that each $p_i$ is
prime. The definition of $x_i$ follows the arXiv version of the source (arXiv:2412.00010),
which the journal statement refers to as "$x_k$ as above".

## Sources

- Gustav Kjærbye Bagger, *Hybrid Bounds for Prime Divisors*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A95, Proposition 4.

articles.title: Subfields of a $p$-power cyclotomic field unramified at $p$ are trivial
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a
prime number, $e \ge 0$ an integer and $L$ a number field. Let $E_1$ and $F$ be subfields of $L$
such that $E_1$ is a $p^e$-th cyclotomic extension of $\mathbb{Q}$ and $F \subseteq E_1$. If $p$
is unramified in $F$, that is, every prime ideal of the ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_F$ lying
over $p\mathbb{Z}$ is unramified over $\mathbb{Z}$, then $F = \mathbb{Q}$.

## Sources

- the prime-power vanishing step of the N390 maximality argument (`cyclotomic_ppow_unramified_le_bot` in the primary source), which takes $e$ to be the exponent of $p$ in a positive integer $m$ and $L = \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_m)$ for a primitive $m$-th root of unity $\zeta_m$; here $e$ and $L$ are arbitrary.

articles.title: Inert primes in prime cyclotomic fields
articles.statement:
Let $\ell$ and $p$ be distinct prime numbers,
and let $K$ be a number field that is an $\ell$-th cyclotomic extension of $\mathbb{Q}$, with
ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$. Then the quotient ring $\mathcal{O}_K / p\mathcal{O}_K$ is a
field (that is, $p$ is inert in $K$) if and only if the multiplicative order of $p$ modulo
$\ell$ is $\ell - 1$.

articles.title: The $p$-free part of $m$ gives a cyclotomic field unramified at $p$
articles.statement:
Let $m \ge 1$, let
$p$ be a prime number, and let $m'$ be $m$ divided by the largest power of $p$ dividing it, so
that $m = p^a m'$ for some $a \ge 0$ with $p \nmid m'$. Then $p$ is unramified in the $m'$-th
cyclotomic field $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_{m'})$, where $\zeta_{m'}$ is a primitive $m'$-th root of
unity: every prime ideal of its ring of integers lying over $p\mathbb{Z}$ is unramified over
$\mathbb{Z}$.

articles.title: Cyclotomic fields are unramified at primes not dividing $m$
articles.statement:
Let $m \ge 1$ and let $p$ be
a prime number with $p \nmid m$. If $K$ is a number field that is an $m$-th cyclotomic extension
of $\mathbb{Q}$ (that is, $K = \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_m)$ for a primitive $m$-th root of unity
$\zeta_m$), then $p$ is unramified in $K$: every prime ideal of the ring of integers
$\mathcal{O}_K$ lying over $p\mathbb{Z}$ is unramified over $\mathbb{Z}$.

articles.title: Lehmer's theorem on the degree of 2cos(2πk/n)
articles.statement:
Let $n$ and $k$ be natural numbers with
$n > 2$ and $\gcd(k, n) = 1$. Then the $\mathbb{Q}$-subalgebra of $\mathbb{R}$ generated by the
real number $2\cos(2\pi k/n)$ has dimension $\varphi(n)/2$ as a vector space over $\mathbb{Q}$,
where $\varphi$ is Euler's totient function.

Since $n > 2$, $\varphi(n)$ is even, so $\varphi(n)/2$ is an integer. Since this dimension is
finite and positive, $2\cos(2\pi k/n)$ is algebraic over $\mathbb{Q}$ of degree $\varphi(n)/2$.

## Sources

- Pinthira Tangsupphathawat and Vichian Laohakosol, "Minimal Polynomials of Algebraic Cosine Values at Rational Multiples of π," Journal of Integer Sequences 19 (2016), Article 16.2.8, Lehmer's theorem recalled in the Introduction, lines 83–90, https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL19/Laohakosol/lao2.tex

articles.title: Lehmer's identity for the real cyclotomic polynomial
articles.statement:
Let $n > 2$ be a natural number, let
$\psi_n$ be the real cyclotomic polynomial, let $\Phi_n \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ be the $n$-th
cyclotomic polynomial, and let $\varphi$ be Euler's totient function. Then in the ring
$\mathbb{Z}[x, x^{-1}]$ of Laurent polynomials over $\mathbb{Z}$,
$x^{\varphi(n)/2} \, \psi_n(x + x^{-1}) = \Phi_n(x)$, that is,
$\psi_n(x + x^{-1}) = x^{-\varphi(n)/2} \, \Phi_n(x)$.

## Sources

- Pinthira Tangsupphathawat and Vichian Laohakosol, "Minimal Polynomials of Algebraic Cosine Values at Rational Multiples of π", Journal of Integer Sequences 19 (2016), source lines 83-90: https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL19/Laohakosol/lao2.tex

articles.title: Degree of the real cyclotomic polynomial
articles.statement:
For `2 < n`, `n.totient` is even and the `natDegree` of the real cyclotomic
polynomial `realCyclotomicPolynomial n` equals `n.totient / 2`. The `Even`
conjunct makes the source's exact half machine-visible under natural-number
division.

## Sources

- Pinthira Tangsupphathawat and Vichian Laohakosol, "Minimal Polynomials of Algebraic Cosine Values at Rational Multiples of π", Journal of Integer Sequences 19 (2016), source lines 83–90: https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL19/Laohakosol/lao2.tex

articles.title: Real cyclotomic polynomial has degree half the totient
articles.statement:
For `2 < n`, `n.totient` is even and the `natDegree` of the real cyclotomic
polynomial `realCyclotomicPolynomial n` equals `n.totient / 2`. The `Even`
conjunct makes the source's exact half machine-visible under natural-number
division.

## Sources

- Pinthira Tangsupphathawat and Vichian Laohakosol, "Minimal Polynomials of Algebraic Cosine Values at Rational Multiples of π", Journal of Integer Sequences 19 (2016), source lines 83–90: https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL19/Laohakosol/lao2.tex

articles.title: The real cyclotomic polynomial is the minimal polynomial of $\zeta + \zeta^{-1}$
articles.statement:
Let $K$
be a field of characteristic zero, let $n > 2$ be a natural number, and let $\zeta \in K$ be a
primitive $n$-th root of unity. Then the real cyclotomic polynomial $\psi_n$ equals the minimal
polynomial of $\zeta + \zeta^{-1}$ over $\mathbb{Z}$.

## Sources

- Pinthira Tangsupphathawat and Vichian Laohakosol, "Minimal Polynomials of Algebraic Cosine Values at Rational Multiples of π", Journal of Integer Sequences 19 (2016), source lines 83–90: https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL19/Laohakosol/lao2.tex

articles.title: Minimal polynomial of $2\cos(2\pi k/n)$ for $1 \le k \le n$ coprime to $n$
articles.statement:
Let $n$ and
$k$ be natural numbers with $n > 2$, $1 \le k \le n$ and $\gcd(k, n) = 1$. Then the real
cyclotomic polynomial $\psi_n$ equals the minimal polynomial over $\mathbb{Z}$ of the complex
number $2\cos(2\pi k/n)$.

The bounds $1 \le k \le n$ are not needed: the same holds for every $k$ coprime to $n$.

## Sources

- Pinthira Tangsupphathawat and Vichian Laohakosol, "Minimal Polynomials of Algebraic Cosine Values at Rational Multiples of π", Journal of Integer Sequences 19 (2016), source lines 83-90: https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL19/Laohakosol/lao2.tex

articles.title: Minimal polynomial of $2\cos(2\pi k/n)$ for $k$ coprime to $n$
articles.statement:
Let $n$ and $k$ be natural
numbers with $n > 2$ and $\gcd(k, n) = 1$. Then the real cyclotomic polynomial $\psi_n$ equals
the minimal polynomial over $\mathbb{Z}$ of the complex number $2\cos(2\pi k/n)$.

No bound on $k$ is needed, since the cosine depends only on $k$ modulo $n$.

articles.title: Real cyclotomic polynomial
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$, the real cyclotomic polynomial
$\psi_n \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ is the minimal polynomial over $\mathbb{Z}$ of the complex number
$\zeta + \zeta^{-1}$, where $\zeta = e^{2\pi i/n}$; for $n \ge 1$ this number is $2\cos(2\pi/n)$.

The definition covers every $n$ (for $n = 0$ the exponent $2\pi i/n$ is read as $0$, so
$\zeta = 1$), but results about $\psi_n$ assume $n > 2$.

## Sources

- Pinthira Tangsupphathawat and Vichian Laohakosol, "Minimal Polynomials of Algebraic Cosine Values at Rational Multiples of π", Journal of Integer Sequences 19 (2016), source lines 83-90: https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL19/Laohakosol/lao2.tex

articles.title: Characterization of the degree-$s$ subfield of the $p$-th cyclotomic field
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a
prime, let $s$ be a natural number dividing $p - 1$, and let $K$ be an intermediate field of the
$p$-th cyclotomic field $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_p)$ over $\mathbb{Q}$. Then $K$ is the degree-$s$
subfield of $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_p)$ if and only if $[K : \mathbb{Q}] = s$.

articles.title: Unique subfield of each degree in the $p$-th cyclotomic field
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime and let
$s$ be a natural number dividing $p - 1$. Then the $p$-th cyclotomic field $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_p)$
has exactly one intermediate field $K$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ with $[K : \mathbb{Q}] = s$.

articles.title: A field strictly above one cyclotomic subfield meets the other
articles.statement:
Let $n_0$, $n_1$ and $m$
be natural numbers with $n_0, n_1 \neq 0$ and $\operatorname{lcm}(n_0, n_1) = m$. Let $E_0$ and
$E_1$ be intermediate fields of the $m$-th cyclotomic field $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_m)$ over
$\mathbb{Q}$ such that $E_0$ is generated over $\mathbb{Q}$ by a primitive $n_0$-th root of unity
and $E_1$ by a primitive $n_1$-th root of unity. If $F$ is an intermediate field of
$\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_m)$ with $E_0 \subsetneq F$, then $F \cap E_1 \neq \mathbb{Q}$.

articles.title: The degree-$s$ subfield of the $p$-th cyclotomic field
articles.statement:
For a prime $p$ and a natural
number $s$ dividing $p - 1$, this is the unique intermediate field $K$ of the $p$-th cyclotomic
field $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_p)$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ with $[K : \mathbb{Q}] = s$.

articles.title: Two cyclotomic subfields whose levels have lcm $m$ generate the $m$-th cyclotomic field
articles.statement:
Let $n_0$, $n_1$ and $m$ be natural numbers with $n_0, n_1 \neq 0$ and
$\operatorname{lcm}(n_0, n_1) = m$. Let $E_0$ and $E_1$ be intermediate fields of the $m$-th
cyclotomic field $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_m)$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ such that $E_0$ is generated over
$\mathbb{Q}$ by a primitive $n_0$-th root of unity and $E_1$ by a primitive $n_1$-th root of
unity. Then the compositum of $E_0$ and $E_1$ is all of $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_m)$.

articles.title: Krasner-type lemma for the cyclotomic trace metric
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime and let $K$ be a
field generated over $\mathbb{Q}$ by a primitive $p$-th root of unity, with fixed primitive $p$-th
root of unity $\omega \in K$. Write $d(\alpha, \beta) = \lVert \alpha - \beta \rVert$ for the trace
metric on $K$, where $\lVert \gamma \rVert \ge 0$ and
$\lVert \gamma \rVert^2 = \sum_{j=1}^{p-1} \operatorname{Tr}_{K/\mathbb{Q}}(\gamma \omega^j)^2$.
Let $\alpha, \beta \in K$ and suppose that $d(\alpha, \beta) < d(\alpha, \sigma(\alpha)) / 2$ for
every automorphism $\sigma$ of $K$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ with $\sigma(\alpha) \ne \alpha$. Then
$\mathbb{Q}(\alpha) \subseteq \mathbb{Q}(\beta)$ as subfields of $K$.

Since $K / \mathbb{Q}$ is Galois, the elements $\sigma(\alpha) \ne \alpha$ are exactly the
conjugates of $\alpha$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ other than $\alpha$ itself.

## Sources

- Saettone, Zaharescu and Zhang, *On a Special Metric in Cyclotomic Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A10, Theorem 4.

articles.title: Almost all pairs in the cyclotomic box are nearly equidistant
articles.statement:
For every real
$\varepsilon > 0$ there is a natural number $A$ with the following property. Let $p$ be a prime
and $N$ a natural number with $p > A$ and $N > A$, and let $K$ be a field generated over
$\mathbb{Q}$ by a primitive $p$-th root of unity, with fixed primitive $p$-th root of unity
$\omega \in K$. Let $d(\alpha, \beta) = \lVert \alpha - \beta \rVert$ be the trace metric on $K$,
where $\lVert \gamma \rVert \ge 0$ and
$\lVert \gamma \rVert^2 = \sum_{j=1}^{p-1} \operatorname{Tr}_{K/\mathbb{Q}}(\gamma \omega^j)^2$.
Let $B(p, N)$ be the set of integer vectors $a = (a_1, \dots, a_{p-1})$ with $-N \le a_i \le N$
for all $i$, and write $\alpha_a = a_1 \omega + \dots + a_{p-1} \omega^{p-1}$. Then fewer than
$\varepsilon \lvert B(p, N) \rvert^2$ pairs $(a, b) \in B(p, N)^2$ satisfy

$$
\left| \frac{d(\alpha_a, \alpha_b)}{2 N p \sqrt{p - 1}} - \frac{1}{\sqrt{6}} \right| > \varepsilon.
$$

The constant $A$ depends only on $\varepsilon$; it is not claimed to be effectively computable.

## Sources

- Saettone, Zaharescu and Zhang, *On a Special Metric in Cyclotomic Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A10, Theorem 1.

articles.title: Diameter of the cyclotomic box
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be an odd prime, let $N$ be a natural number, and
let $K$ be a field generated over $\mathbb{Q}$ by a primitive $p$-th root of unity, with fixed
primitive $p$-th root of unity $\omega \in K$. Let $d(\alpha, \beta) = \lVert \alpha - \beta \rVert$
be the trace metric on $K$, where $\lVert \gamma \rVert \ge 0$ and
$\lVert \gamma \rVert^2 = \sum_{j=1}^{p-1} \operatorname{Tr}_{K/\mathbb{Q}}(\gamma \omega^j)^2$.
Let $B(p, N)$ be the set of integer vectors $a = (a_1, \dots, a_{p-1})$ with $-N \le a_i \le N$
for all $i$, and write $\alpha_a = a_1 \omega + \dots + a_{p-1} \omega^{p-1}$. Then
$d(\alpha_a, \alpha_b) \le 2 N p \sqrt{p - 1}$ for all $a, b \in B(p, N)$, and this bound is
attained: $d(\alpha, -\alpha) = 2 N p \sqrt{p - 1}$ for
$\alpha = N \omega - N \omega^2 + \dots + N \omega^{p-2} - N \omega^{p-1}$, the point whose
coefficient of $\omega^i$ is $(-1)^{i-1} N$.

## Sources

- Saettone, Zaharescu and Zhang, *On a Special Metric in Cyclotomic Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A10, Lemma 2.

articles.title: The cyclotomic box of radius zero
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a natural number and, for a natural number
$N$, let $B(p, N)$ be the set of integer vectors $a = (a_1, \dots, a_{p-1})$ with
$-N \le a_i \le N$ for all $i$. Then $B(p, 0) = \{0\}$: the zero vector is the only element of the
box of radius $0$.

## Sources

- Saettone, Zaharescu and Zhang, *On a Special Metric in Cyclotomic Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A10, Section 1 (the box `B(p, N)`).

articles.title: The cyclotomic box
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $p$ and $N$, the box $B(p, N)$ is the finite set
of integer vectors $a = (a_1, \dots, a_{p-1}) \in \mathbb{Z}^{p-1}$ with $-N \le a_i \le N$ for
every $i$.

The vector $a$ stands for the point $a_1 \omega + \dots + a_{p-1} \omega^{p-1}$ of the $p$-th
cyclotomic field $\mathbb{Q}(\omega)$, where $\omega$ is a primitive $p$-th root of unity.

## Sources

- Saettone, Zaharescu and Zhang, *On a Special Metric in Cyclotomic Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A10, Section 1 (the box `B(p, N)`).

articles.title: Fourth moment of the trace distance on the cyclotomic box
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, let $N$ be
a natural number, and let $K$ be a field generated over $\mathbb{Q}$ by a primitive $p$-th root of
unity, with fixed primitive $p$-th root of unity $\omega \in K$. Let $M_4(p, N)$ be the fourth
moment of the trace metric $d$ of $K$ over the box $B(p, N)$: the average of
$d(\alpha_a, \alpha_b)^4$ over all pairs $(a, b)$ of integer vectors in $\mathbb{Z}^{p-1}$ whose
coordinates lie in $[-N, N]$, where $\alpha_a = a_1 \omega + \dots + a_{p-1} \omega^{p-1}$ and
$d(\alpha, \beta)^2 = \sum_{j=1}^{p-1} \mathrm{Tr}_{K/\mathbb{Q}}((\alpha - \beta) \omega^j)^2$.
Then

$$
M_4(p, N) = \frac{2}{45} N (N + 1) (p - 1) \bigl( (2 N^2 + 2 N)
(5 p^5 - 8 p^4 + p^3 + 8 p^2 - 21 p - 18) - 3 (p^2 - p - 1)^2 \bigr).
$$

The asymptotic form $M_4(p, N) = \frac{4}{9} p^6 N^4 + O(p^5 N^4 + p^6 N^3)$ follows from this
exact formula.

## Sources

- Saettone, Zaharescu and Zhang, *On a Special Metric in Cyclotomic Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A10, Lemma 6.

articles.title: Second moment of the trace distance on the cyclotomic box
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, let $N$ be
a natural number, and let $K$ be a field generated over $\mathbb{Q}$ by a primitive $p$-th root of
unity, with fixed primitive $p$-th root of unity $\omega \in K$. Let $M_2(p, N)$ be the second
moment of the trace metric $d$ of $K$ over the box $B(p, N)$: the average of
$d(\alpha_a, \alpha_b)^2$ over all pairs $(a, b)$ of integer vectors in $\mathbb{Z}^{p-1}$ whose
coordinates lie in $[-N, N]$, where $\alpha_a = a_1 \omega + \dots + a_{p-1} \omega^{p-1}$ and
$d(\alpha, \beta)^2 = \sum_{j=1}^{p-1} \mathrm{Tr}_{K/\mathbb{Q}}((\alpha - \beta) \omega^j)^2$.
Then $M_2(p, N) = \frac{2}{3} (p^3 - 2 p^2 + 1) N (N + 1)$.

The asymptotic form $M_2(p, N) = \frac{2}{3} p^3 N^2 + O(p^2 N^2 + p^3 N)$ follows from this
exact formula.

## Sources

- Saettone, Zaharescu and Zhang, *On a Special Metric in Cyclotomic Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A10, Lemma 4.

articles.title: The zeroth moment of the trace distance is one
articles.statement:
Let $p \ge 1$ and $N$ be natural numbers,
and let $K$ be a field generated over $\mathbb{Q}$ by a primitive $p$-th root of unity, with fixed
primitive $p$-th root of unity $\omega \in K$. Let $d$ be the trace metric on $K$, given by
$d(\alpha, \beta) \ge 0$ and
$d(\alpha, \beta)^2 = \sum_{j=1}^{p-1} \mathrm{Tr}_{K/\mathbb{Q}}((\alpha - \beta) \omega^j)^2$.
Let $B(p, N)$ be the set of integer vectors $a = (a_1, \dots, a_{p-1})$ with $-N \le a_i \le N$
for all $i$, write $\alpha_a = a_1 \omega + \dots + a_{p-1} \omega^{p-1}$, and let
$M_k(p, N) = \lvert B(p, N) \rvert^{-2} \sum_{a, b \in B(p, N)} d(\alpha_a, \alpha_b)^k$ be the
$k$-th moment of $d$ over $B(p, N)$. Then $M_0(p, N) = 1$, with the convention $0^0 = 1$ for
coinciding points.

## Sources

- Saettone, Zaharescu and Zhang, *On a Special Metric in Cyclotomic Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A10, Section 6 (Definition 6.1 of arXiv:2410.22687).

articles.title: Moments of the trace distance on the cyclotomic box
articles.statement:
Let $p \ge 1$, $N$ and $k$ be natural
numbers, and let $K$ be a field generated over $\mathbb{Q}$ by a primitive $p$-th root of unity,
with fixed primitive $p$-th root of unity $\omega \in K$. Let $d$ be the trace metric on $K$, given
by $d(\alpha, \beta) \ge 0$ and
$d(\alpha, \beta)^2 = \sum_{j=1}^{p-1} \mathrm{Tr}_{K/\mathbb{Q}}((\alpha - \beta) \omega^j)^2$.
Let $B(p, N)$ be the set of integer vectors $a = (a_1, \dots, a_{p-1})$ with $-N \le a_i \le N$
