for all $i$, and write $\alpha_a = a_1 \omega + \dots + a_{p-1} \omega^{p-1}$. The $k$-th moment
of $d$ over $B(p, N)$ is the real number

$$
M_k(p, N) = \frac{1}{\lvert B(p, N) \rvert^2} \sum_{a \in B(p, N)} \sum_{b \in B(p, N)}
d(\alpha_a, \alpha_b)^k.
$$

## Sources

- Saettone, Zaharescu and Zhang, *On a Special Metric in Cyclotomic Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A10, Section 6 (Definition 6.1 of arXiv:2410.22687).

articles.title: The zero coefficient vector gives the zero lattice point
articles.statement:
Let $p \ge 1$ be a natural
number and let $K$ be a field generated over $\mathbb{Q}$ by a primitive $p$-th root of unity, with
fixed primitive $p$-th root of unity $\omega \in K$. For an integer vector
$a = (a_1, \dots, a_{p-1})$ write $\alpha_a = a_1 \omega + \dots + a_{p-1} \omega^{p-1}$. Then
$\alpha_0 = 0$.

## Sources

- Saettone, Zaharescu and Zhang, *On a Special Metric in Cyclotomic Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A10, Section 1 (the box `B(p, N)`).

articles.title: Lattice points of a cyclotomic field
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a positive integer, let $K$ be a $p$-th
cyclotomic extension of $\mathbb{Q}$, and let $\omega$ be the chosen primitive $p$-th root of
unity in $K$. For integers $a_1, \dots, a_{p-1}$, the lattice point with coefficients
$a_1, \dots, a_{p-1}$ is the element $a_1 \omega + a_2 \omega^2 + \cdots + a_{p-1} \omega^{p-1}$
of $K$.

## Sources

- Saettone, Zaharescu and Zhang, *On a Special Metric in Cyclotomic Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A10, Section 1 (the box `B(p, N)`).

articles.title: Galois invariance of the trace metric
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime and let $K$ be a $p$-th
cyclotomic extension of $\mathbb{Q}$. For every $\mathbb{Q}$-algebra automorphism $\sigma$ of $K$
and all $\alpha, \beta \in K$, the trace distance satisfies
$d(\sigma \alpha, \sigma \beta) = d(\alpha, \beta)$.

## Sources

- Saettone, Zaharescu and Zhang, *On a Special Metric in Cyclotomic Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A10, Proposition 1.

articles.title: Symmetry of the trace metric
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a positive integer and let $K$ be a $p$-th
cyclotomic extension of $\mathbb{Q}$. For all $\alpha, \beta \in K$, the trace distance satisfies
$d(\alpha, \beta) = d(\beta, \alpha)$.

## Sources

- Saettone, Zaharescu and Zhang, *On a Special Metric in Cyclotomic Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A10, Definition 2.

articles.title: Trace distance from a point to itself
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a positive integer and let $K$ be a
$p$-th cyclotomic extension of $\mathbb{Q}$. For every $\alpha \in K$, the trace distance satisfies
$d(\alpha, \alpha) = 0$.

## Sources

- Saettone, Zaharescu and Zhang, *On a Special Metric in Cyclotomic Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A10, Definition 2.

articles.title: Trace metric on a cyclotomic field
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a positive integer and let $K$ be a $p$-th
cyclotomic extension of $\mathbb{Q}$. The trace distance between $\alpha, \beta \in K$ is the real
number $d(\alpha, \beta) = \lVert \alpha - \beta \rVert$, where $\lVert \cdot \rVert$ is the trace
norm on $K$.

## Sources

- Saettone, Zaharescu and Zhang, *On a Special Metric in Cyclotomic Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A10, Definition 2 (Definition 2.2 of arXiv:2410.22687).

articles.title: The trace norm is a norm
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime and let $K$ be a $p$-th cyclotomic extension
of $\mathbb{Q}$, viewed as a $\mathbb{Q}$-vector space. The trace norm $\lVert \cdot \rVert$ on $K$
is a norm: for all $\alpha, \beta \in K$ and $q \in \mathbb{Q}$, we have
$\lVert \alpha \rVert = 0$ if and only if $\alpha = 0$,
$\lVert \alpha + \beta \rVert \le \lVert \alpha \rVert + \lVert \beta \rVert$, and
$\lVert q \alpha \rVert = |q| \, \lVert \alpha \rVert$.

## Sources

- Saettone, Zaharescu and Zhang, *On a Special Metric in Cyclotomic Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A10, Theorem 2.

articles.title: Squared trace norm in coordinates
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, let $K$ be a $p$-th cyclotomic
extension of $\mathbb{Q}$, let $\omega$ be the chosen primitive $p$-th root of unity in $K$, and
let $\mathrm{Tr}$ be the trace from $K$ to $\mathbb{Q}$. For rational numbers
$a_1, \dots, a_{p-1}$, put $\alpha = a_1 \omega + a_2 \omega^2 + \cdots + a_{p-1} \omega^{p-1}$
and $\lVert \alpha \rVert_E^2 = a_1^2 + a_2^2 + \cdots + a_{p-1}^2$. Then the squared trace
norm of $\alpha$ satisfies

$$\lVert \alpha \rVert^2 = p^2 \lVert \alpha \rVert_E^2 - (p + 1) \mathrm{Tr}(\alpha)^2,$$

and $\lVert \alpha \rVert_E^2 \le \lVert \alpha \rVert^2$.

## Sources

- Saettone, Zaharescu and Zhang, *On a Special Metric in Cyclotomic Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A10, Lemma 1.

articles.title: The squared trace norm is invariant under negation
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a positive integer and
let $K$ be a $p$-th cyclotomic extension of $\mathbb{Q}$. For every $\alpha \in K$, the squared
trace norm satisfies $\lVert -\alpha \rVert^2 = \lVert \alpha \rVert^2$.

## Sources

- Saettone, Zaharescu and Zhang, *On a Special Metric in Cyclotomic Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A10, Definition 1.

articles.title: Squared trace norm of zero
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a positive integer and let $K$ be a $p$-th
cyclotomic extension of $\mathbb{Q}$. The squared trace norm of $0 \in K$ is $0$, that is,
$\lVert 0 \rVert^2 = 0$.

## Sources

- Saettone, Zaharescu and Zhang, *On a Special Metric in Cyclotomic Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A10, Definition 1.

articles.title: Squared trace norm on a cyclotomic field
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a positive integer, let $K$ be a
$p$-th cyclotomic extension of $\mathbb{Q}$, and let $\omega$ be the chosen primitive $p$-th root
of unity in $K$. The squared trace norm of $\alpha \in K$ is the rational number

$$\lVert \alpha \rVert^2 = \sum_{j=1}^{p-1} \mathrm{Tr}_{K/\mathbb{Q}}(\alpha \omega^j)^2.$$

## Sources

- Saettone, Zaharescu and Zhang, *On a Special Metric in Cyclotomic Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A10, Definition 1 (Definition 2.1 of arXiv:2410.22687).

articles.title: Trace norm on a cyclotomic field
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a positive integer, let $K$ be a $p$-th
cyclotomic extension of $\mathbb{Q}$, and let $\omega$ be the chosen primitive $p$-th root of
unity in $K$. The trace norm of $\alpha \in K$ is the real number

$$\|\alpha\| = \sqrt{\sum_{j=1}^{p-1} \mathrm{Tr}_{K/\mathbb{Q}}(\alpha \omega^j)^2},$$

the Euclidean length of the vector
$(\mathrm{Tr}_{K/\mathbb{Q}}(\alpha \omega^j))_{1 \le j \le p-1}$.

## Sources

- Saettone, Zaharescu and Zhang, *On a Special Metric in Cyclotomic Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A10, Definition 1 (Definition 2.1 of arXiv:2410.22687).

articles.title: Primitive elements α + nβ in a prime cyclotomic field
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime and let $K$
be a $p$-th cyclotomic extension of $\mathbb{Q}$. For all $\alpha, \beta \in K$ there is a
natural number $n_0$ such that, for every natural number $n \ge n_0$, the subfields
$\mathbb{Q}(\alpha + n\beta)$ and $\mathbb{Q}(\alpha, \beta)$ of $K$ are equal.

## Sources

- Saettone, Zaharescu and Zhang, *On a Special Metric in Cyclotomic Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A10, Corollary 1.

articles.title: Concentration of trace distances in the box, quantitative form
articles.statement:
There is a real
number $C$ such that the following holds for every real $\varepsilon > 0$, every prime $p$,
every integer $N \ge 1$ and every $p$-th cyclotomic extension $K$ of $\mathbb{Q}$. Let $\omega$
be the chosen primitive $p$-th root of unity in $K$, let $d$ be the trace distance on $K$, and
let $B(p, N)$ be the set of integer vectors $a = (a_1, \dots, a_{p-1})$ with $|a_i| \le N$ for
all $i$, where $a$ stands for the point $a_1 \omega + \dots + a_{p-1} \omega^{p-1}$ of $K$.
Among all pairs $(\alpha, \beta) \in B(p, N)^2$, the proportion of pairs with

$$\left| \frac{d(\alpha, \beta)}{2 N p^{3/2}} - \frac{1}{\sqrt{6}} \right| > \varepsilon$$

is at most $C \varepsilon^{-2} (1/p + 1/N)$.

The paper takes $p$ odd; here $p = 2$ is allowed. The paper also shows that $C$ is
effectively computable; only its existence is stated here.

## Sources

- Saettone, Zaharescu and Zhang, *On a Special Metric in Cyclotomic Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A10, Theorem 5.

articles.title: Variance bound for squared trace distances in the box
articles.statement:
There is a real number $C$
such that the following holds for every prime $p$, every integer $N \ge 1$ and every $p$-th
cyclotomic extension $K$ of $\mathbb{Q}$. Let $\omega$ be the chosen primitive $p$-th root of
unity in $K$, let $d$ be the trace distance on $K$, and let $B(p, N)$ be the set of integer
vectors $a = (a_1, \dots, a_{p-1})$ with $|a_i| \le N$ for all $i$, where $a$ stands for the
point $a_1 \omega + \dots + a_{p-1} \omega^{p-1}$ of $K$. Then

$$R(p, N) = \frac{1}{|B(p, N)|^2} \sum_{\alpha, \beta \in B(p, N)}
\left( d(\alpha, \beta)^2 - \tfrac{2}{3} p^3 N^2 \right)^2 \le
C \left( p^5 N^4 + p^6 N^3 \right).$$

## Sources

- Saettone, Zaharescu and Zhang, *On a Special Metric in Cyclotomic Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A10, Lemma 7.

articles.title: Fourth-power sum of coordinate differences over a box
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime and $N$ a
natural number, and let $B(p, N)$ be the set of integer vectors $a = (a_1, \dots, a_{p-1})$
with $|a_i| \le N$ for all $i$. Then

$$\sum_{i=1}^{p-1} \sum_{j=1}^{p-1} \sum_{a, b \in B(p, N)} (a_i - b_i)^2 (a_j - b_j)^2 =
(2N+1)^{2(p-1)} \cdot \tfrac{2}{45} N (N+1) (p-1) (10N^2 p + 4N^2 + 10Np + 4N - 3).$$

This corrects the paper's printed right side, which omits the factor $(2N+1)^{2(p-1)}$: for
$p = 3$ and $N = 1$ the sum is $936$, while the printed right side is $104/9$. The paper's own
proof carries the factors $(2N+1)^{2p-4}$ and $(2N+1)^{2p-6}$ in its pieces (10) and (11), and
combining them gives the value above; the printed formula is the sum divided by
$|B(p, N)|^2 = (2N+1)^{2(p-1)}$. The paper takes $p$ an odd prime; here only $p$ prime is
assumed.

## Sources

- Saettone, Zaharescu and Zhang, *On a Special Metric in Cyclotomic Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A10, Lemma 5.

articles.title: Power sums over a symmetric interval
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $N$ and $r$, let
$S_r(N) = \sum_{a=-N}^{N} a^r$, the sum over the integers $a$ with $-N \le a \le N$. Then
$S_r(N) = 0$ for every odd $r$, and

$$S_2(N) = \frac{N(N+1)(2N+1)}{3}, \qquad S_4(N) = \frac{N(N+1)(2N+1)(3N^2+3N-1)}{15}.$$

The paper takes $N \ge 1$; here $N = 0$ is allowed.

## Sources

- Saettone, Zaharescu and Zhang, *On a Special Metric in Cyclotomic Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A10, Lemma 3.

articles.title: The zero vector lies in every box
articles.statement:
For all natural numbers $p$ and $N$, the zero vector
lies in the box $B(p, N)$, the set of integer vectors $(a_1, \dots, a_{p-1})$ with
$|a_i| \le N$ for all $i$.

## Sources

- Saettone, Zaharescu and Zhang, *On a Special Metric in Cyclotomic Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A10, Section 1 (the box `B(p, N)`).

articles.title: Order of the inertia group
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be integral domains, with $B$ an $A$-algebra
that is finite and flat as an $A$-module, and let $G$ be a finite group acting faithfully on $B$
by $A$-algebra automorphisms such that every $G$-invariant element of $B$ comes from $A$. Let
$\mathfrak p$ be a maximal ideal of $A$ and $\mathfrak P$ a maximal ideal of $B$ lying over
$\mathfrak p$. Then the inertia group of $\mathfrak P$, consisting of the $\sigma \in G$ with
$\sigma(b) - b \in \mathfrak P$ for all $b \in B$, has order $e \cdot i$, where $e$ is the
ramification index of $\mathfrak p$ in $B$ (the common ramification index of the primes of $B$
over $\mathfrak p$) and $i$ is the inseparable degree of the residue field extension
$(B/\mathfrak P)/(A/\mathfrak p)$, that is, the degree of $B/\mathfrak P$ over the separable
closure of $A/\mathfrak p$ in it.

articles.title: Generator rank of a topological group
articles.statement:
For a topological group $G$, the generator
rank $d(G)$ is the least natural number $k$ such that some finite subset $S \subseteq G$ with
$k$ elements generates a dense subgroup of $G$. If no finite subset of $G$ generates a dense
subgroup, then $d(G) = 0$ by convention.

articles.title: Finite-dimensional second cohomology mod $p$
articles.statement:
For a prime $p$ and a topological group
$G$, this is the statement that the continuous cohomology group $H^2(G, \mathbb{F}_p)$ of degree
$2$, with coefficients in the trivial representation of $G$ on $\mathbb{F}_p$, is
finite-dimensional over $\mathbb{F}_p$.

articles.title: Everywhere unramified extension
articles.statement:
Let $M/F$ be an extension of number fields, with rings
of integers $\mathcal{O}_F$ and $\mathcal{O}_M$. Then $M/F$ is everywhere unramified when every
prime ideal $\mathfrak{P}$ of $\mathcal{O}_M$ lying over a nonzero prime ideal $\mathfrak{p}$
of $\mathcal{O}_F$ has ramification index $1$ over $\mathcal{O}_F$, and every infinite place of
$M$ lying over a real place of $F$ is real.

articles.title: Galois group of the maximal unramified pro-$p$ extension
articles.statement:
For a number field $F$ and a
prime $p$, this is the group $\mathrm{Gal}(F^{\mathrm{un},p}/F)$ of field automorphisms of the
maximal unramified pro-$p$ extension $F^{\mathrm{un},p}$ of $F$ that fix $F$, under
composition and with the Krull topology.

articles.title: Maximal unramified pro-$p$ extension
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a number field, $\overline{F}$ an
algebraic closure of $F$, and $p$ a prime. The maximal unramified pro-$p$ extension
$F^{\mathrm{un},p}$ of $F$ is the compositum in $\overline{F}$ of all intermediate fields
$F \subseteq M \subseteq \overline{F}$ such that $M/F$ is finite, Galois and everywhere
unramified, and its Galois group $\mathrm{Gal}(M/F)$ is a $p$-group (each such $M$ is a
number field).

articles.title: Relation rank of a topological group
articles.statement:
For a prime $p$ and a topological group $G$, the
relation rank $r(G)$ is the dimension over $\mathbb{F}_p$ of the continuous cohomology group
$H^2(G, \mathbb{F}_p)$ of degree $2$, with coefficients in the trivial representation of $G$ on
$\mathbb{F}_p$. If this space is infinite-dimensional, then $r(G) = 0$ by convention.

articles.title: Shafarevich's relation-rank bound
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a number field, let $p$ be an odd prime,
and let $G = \mathrm{Gal}(F^{\mathrm{un},p}/F)$ be the Galois group of the maximal unramified
pro-$p$ extension of $F$. Write $d(G)$ for the generator rank and $r(G)$ for the relation rank
of $G$, $r_1$ and $r_2$ for the numbers of real and complex places of $F$, and $\delta$ for $1$
if $F$ contains a primitive $p$-th root of unity and $0$ otherwise. Then the continuous
cohomology group $H^2(G, \mathbb{F}_p)$ with trivial coefficients is finite-dimensional over
$\mathbb{F}_p$, and

$$r(G) \le d(G) + (r_1 + r_2 - 1) + \delta.$$

## Sources

- D. C. Mayer, *New number fields with known p-class tower*, Tatra Mt. Math. Publ. 64 (2015), 21–57 (Theorem 5.1, S=∅; arXiv:1510.00565); H. Koch, *Galois Theory of p-Extensions*, Springer 2002 (Theorems 11.5 and 11.8); I. R. Shafarevich, *Extensions with prescribed ramification points* (1963). Lean hypothesis: https://github.com/logical-intelligence/erdos-unit-distance (Hyp_ShafarevichRelationRankBound). Problem `shafarevich_relation_rank_bound` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Trivial representation on $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$
articles.statement:
For a natural number $p$ and a
topological group $G$, this is $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ with the discrete topology, regarded as a
continuous representation of $G$ over $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ on which every element of $G$
acts as the identity.

articles.title: The completed integer map is compatible with the rings of integers
articles.statement:
Let $L/K$ be an
extension of number fields, let $v$ be a nonzero prime ideal of $\mathcal{O}_K$ and $w$ a nonzero
prime ideal of $\mathcal{O}_L$ lying over $v$. Let $\mathcal{O}_{K_v}$ and $\mathcal{O}_{L_w}$ be
the rings of integers of the completions $K_v$ and $L_w$. For every $a \in \mathcal{O}_K$, the
canonical map $\mathcal{O}_{K_v} \to \mathcal{O}_{L_w}$ sends the image of $a$ in
$\mathcal{O}_{K_v}$ to the image in $\mathcal{O}_{L_w}$ of the image of $a$ in $\mathcal{O}_L$.

articles.title: Maximal ideals of completed integer rings lie over each other
articles.statement:
Let $L/K$ be an extension
of number fields, let $v$ be a nonzero prime ideal of $\mathcal{O}_K$ and $w$ a nonzero prime
ideal of $\mathcal{O}_L$ lying over $v$. Let $\mathcal{O}_{K_v}$ and $\mathcal{O}_{L_w}$ be the
rings of integers of the completions $K_v$ and $L_w$. Then the preimage of the maximal ideal of
$\mathcal{O}_{L_w}$ under the canonical map $\mathcal{O}_{K_v} \to \mathcal{O}_{L_w}$ is the
maximal ideal of $\mathcal{O}_{K_v}$.

articles.title: Residue map of completed integer rings
articles.statement:
Let $L/K$ be an extension of number fields, let
$v$ be a nonzero prime ideal of $\mathcal{O}_K$ and $w$ a nonzero prime ideal of $\mathcal{O}_L$
lying over $v$. Let $\mathcal{O}_{K_v}$ and $\mathcal{O}_{L_w}$ be the rings of integers of the
completions $K_v$ and $L_w$, with maximal ideals $\mathfrak{m}_v$ and $\mathfrak{m}_w$. This is
the ring homomorphism $\mathcal{O}_{K_v}/\mathfrak{m}_v \to \mathcal{O}_{L_w}/\mathfrak{m}_w$
induced by the canonical map $\mathcal{O}_{K_v} \to \mathcal{O}_{L_w}$.

articles.title: Naturality of the residue field identifications
articles.statement:
Let $L/K$ be an extension of number
fields, let $v$ be a nonzero prime ideal of $\mathcal{O}_K$ and $w$ a nonzero prime ideal of
$\mathcal{O}_L$ lying over $v$. Let $\mathcal{O}_{K_v}$ and $\mathcal{O}_{L_w}$ be the rings of
integers of the completions $K_v$ and $L_w$, with maximal ideals $\mathfrak{m}_v$ and
$\mathfrak{m}_w$. Then the two maps $\mathcal{O}_{K_v}/\mathfrak{m}_v \to \mathcal{O}_L/w$ agree:
the residue field isomorphism $\mathcal{O}_{K_v}/\mathfrak{m}_v \cong \mathcal{O}_K/v$ followed by
the map $\mathcal{O}_K/v \to \mathcal{O}_L/w$ induced by $\mathcal{O}_K \to \mathcal{O}_L$, and
the map $\mathcal{O}_{K_v}/\mathfrak{m}_v \to \mathcal{O}_{L_w}/\mathfrak{m}_w$ induced by the
canonical map $\mathcal{O}_{K_v} \to \mathcal{O}_{L_w}$ followed by the residue field isomorphism
$\mathcal{O}_{L_w}/\mathfrak{m}_w \cong \mathcal{O}_L/w$.

articles.title: Residue map of rings of integers
articles.statement:
Let $L/K$ be an extension of number fields, let $v$ be
a nonzero prime ideal of $\mathcal{O}_K$ and $w$ a nonzero prime ideal of $\mathcal{O}_L$ lying
over $v$. This is the ring homomorphism $\mathcal{O}_K/v \to \mathcal{O}_L/w$ induced by the
canonical map $\mathcal{O}_K \to \mathcal{O}_L$.

articles.title: Component at a place of the completion tensor product map
articles.statement:
Let $L/K$ be an extension of
number fields, let $v$ be a finite place of $K$, given as a height-one prime of the ring of
integers $\mathcal{O}_K$, let $K_v$ be the completion of $K$ at $v$, and let $w$ be a finite place
of $L$ lying over $v$, with completion $L_w$. Let $\iota_w : K_v \to L_w$ be the continuous ring
homomorphism extending $K \to L$. This is the $K_v$-algebra homomorphism
$K_v \otimes_K L \to L_w$ sending $x \otimes y$ to $\iota_w(x)\, y$, where $y \in L$ is viewed in
$L_w$.

articles.title: The completion tensor product map
articles.statement:
Let $L/K$ be an extension of number fields, let $v$ be a
finite place of $K$, given as a height-one prime of the ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$, and let
$K_v$ be the completion of $K$ at $v$. For each finite place $w$ of $L$ lying over $v$, let $L_w$
be the completion of $L$ at $w$ and $\iota_w : K_v \to L_w$ the continuous ring homomorphism
extending $K \to L$. This is the $K_v$-algebra homomorphism
$K_v \otimes_K L \to \prod_{w \mid v} L_w$ sending $x \otimes y$ to $(\iota_w(x)\, y)_w$, where
$y \in L$ is viewed in each $L_w$ and the product runs over the finite places of $L$ lying over
$v$.

articles.title: The local degree is the product of ramification index and inertia degree
articles.statement:
Let $L/K$ be an
extension of number fields, let $v$ be a nonzero prime ideal of $\mathcal{O}_K$ (a finite place of
$K$) and $w$ a nonzero prime ideal of $\mathcal{O}_L$ lying over $v$. Regard the completion $L_w$
as an algebra over $K_v$ via the canonical map $K_v \to L_w$. Then the dimension of $L_w$ over
$K_v$ equals $e(w \mid v) \, f(w \mid v)$, the ramification index of $w$ over $v$ times the
inertia degree of $w$ over $v$.

articles.title: Local degree is at most the global degree
articles.statement:
Let $L/K$ be an extension of number fields,
let $v$ be a nonzero prime ideal of $\mathcal{O}_K$ (a finite place of $K$) and let $w$ be a
nonzero prime ideal of $\mathcal{O}_L$ lying over $v$. Regard the $w$-adic completion $L_w$ as
an algebra over the $v$-adic completion $K_v$ via the canonical map $K_v \to L_w$. Then the
dimension of $L_w$ over $K_v$ is at most $[L : K]$.

articles.title: Global norm as a product of local norms
articles.statement:
Let $L/K$ be an extension of number fields, let
$v$ be a finite place of $K$, given as a height-one prime of the ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$,
and let $K_v$ be the completion of $K$ at $v$. For each of the finitely many finite places $w$ of
$L$ lying over $v$, regard the completion $L_w$ as a $K_v$-algebra through the continuous ring
homomorphism $K_v \to L_w$ extending $K \to L$. Then for every $\alpha \in L$, the image of the
norm $N_{L/K}(\alpha)$ in $K_v$ equals $\prod_{w \mid v} N_{L_w/K_v}(\alpha)$, where $\alpha$ is
viewed in $L_w$ and the product runs over the finite places $w$ of $L$ lying over $v$.

## Sources

- Corollary 11.24, norm part.

articles.title: Global trace as a sum of local traces
articles.statement:
Let $L/K$ be an extension of number fields, let
$v$ be a finite place of $K$, given as a height-one prime of the ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$,
and let $K_v$ be the completion of $K$ at $v$. For each of the finitely many finite places $w$ of
$L$ lying over $v$, regard the completion $L_w$ as a $K_v$-algebra through the continuous ring
homomorphism $K_v \to L_w$ extending $K \to L$. Then for every $\alpha \in L$, the image of the
trace $\operatorname{Tr}_{L/K}(\alpha)$ in $K_v$ equals
$\sum_{w \mid v} \operatorname{Tr}_{L_w/K_v}(\alpha)$, where $\alpha$ is viewed in $L_w$ and the
sum runs over the finite places $w$ of $L$ lying over $v$.

## Sources

- Corollary 11.24, trace part.

articles.title: Completion preserves the inertia degree
articles.statement:
Let $L/K$ be an extension of number fields, let
$v$ be a nonzero prime ideal of $\mathcal{O}_K$ and $w$ a nonzero prime ideal of $\mathcal{O}_L$
lying over $v$. Let $\mathcal{O}_{K_v}$ and $\mathcal{O}_{L_w}$ be the rings of integers of the
completions $K_v$ and $L_w$, with $\mathcal{O}_{L_w}$ an algebra over $\mathcal{O}_{K_v}$ via the
canonical map. Then the inertia degree of the maximal ideal of $\mathcal{O}_{L_w}$ over
$\mathcal{O}_{K_v}$ equals the inertia degree of $w$ over $v$.

articles.title: Places over a finite place correspond to primes over it
articles.statement:
Let $L/K$ be an extension of
number fields and let $v$ be a finite place of $K$, given as a height-one prime of the ring of
integers $\mathcal{O}_K$. Sending a finite place $w$ of $L$ lying over $v$ to its prime ideal of
$\mathcal{O}_L$ is a bijection from the finite places of $L$ lying over $v$ onto the set of prime
ideals of $\mathcal{O}_L$ lying over $v$.

articles.title: Finite places lying over a finite place
articles.statement:
Let $L/K$ be an extension of number fields and
let $v$ be a finite place of $K$, given as a height-one prime of the ring of integers
$\mathcal{O}_K$. The finite places of $L$ lying over $v$ form the type of height-one primes $w$ of
$\mathcal{O}_L$ that lie over $v$, that is, whose preimage in $\mathcal{O}_K$ is $v$.

articles.title: The map of completed integer rings is injective
articles.statement:
Let $L/K$ be an extension of number
fields, let $v$ be a nonzero prime ideal of $\mathcal{O}_K$ and $w$ a nonzero prime ideal of
$\mathcal{O}_L$ lying over $v$. Then the canonical map $\mathcal{O}_{K_v} \to \mathcal{O}_{L_w}$
from the ring of integers of the completion $K_v$ to the ring of integers of the completion $L_w$
is injective.

articles.title: Completion preserves the ramification index
articles.statement:
Let $L/K$ be an extension of number fields,
let $v$ be a nonzero prime ideal of $\mathcal{O}_K$ and $w$ a nonzero prime ideal of
$\mathcal{O}_L$ lying over $v$. Let $\mathcal{O}_{K_v}$ and $\mathcal{O}_{L_w}$ be the rings of
integers of the completions $K_v$ and $L_w$, with $\mathcal{O}_{L_w}$ an algebra over
$\mathcal{O}_{K_v}$ via the canonical map. Then the ramification index of the maximal ideal of
$\mathcal{O}_{L_w}$ over $\mathcal{O}_{K_v}$ equals the ramification index of $w$ over $v$.

articles.title: Base change to a finite completion as a product of completions
articles.statement:
Let $L/K$ be an extension
of number fields, $v$ a finite place of $K$ and $K_v$ the completion of $K$ at $v$; for each finite
place $w$ of $L$ lying over $v$, let $L_w$ be the completion of $L$ at $w$, a $K_v$-algebra via the
canonical map $K_v \to L_w$. This is the isomorphism of $K_v$-algebras
$K_v \otimes_K L \cong \prod_{w \mid v} L_w$ sending $x \otimes y$ to $(x y)_w$, where $x \in K_v$
and $y \in L$ are mapped into each $L_w$.

## Sources

- ATLAS N236, Theorem 11.23(5), with the tensor factors swapped; used later in N265.

articles.title: The canonical map to the product of completions is bijective
articles.statement:
Let $L/K$ be an extension of
number fields, $v$ a finite place of $K$ and $K_v$ the completion of $K$ at $v$; for each finite
place $w$ of $L$ lying over $v$, let $L_w$ be the completion of $L$ at $w$, a $K_v$-algebra via
the canonical map $K_v \to L_w$. The $K_v$-algebra map $K_v \otimes_K L \to \prod_{w \mid v} L_w$
sending $x \otimes y$ to $(x y)_w$, where $x \in K_v$ and $y \in L$ are mapped into each $L_w$,
is bijective.

articles.title: The canonical map to the product of completions is injective
articles.statement:
Let $L/K$ be an extension of
number fields, $v$ a finite place of $K$ and $K_v$ the completion of $K$ at $v$; for each finite
place $w$ of $L$ lying over $v$, let $L_w$ be the completion of $L$ at $w$, a $K_v$-algebra via
the canonical map $K_v \to L_w$. The $K_v$-algebra map $K_v \otimes_K L \to \prod_{w \mid v} L_w$
sending $x \otimes y$ to $(x y)_w$, where $x \in K_v$ and $y \in L$ are mapped into each $L_w$,
is injective.

articles.title: Coordinate law for the tensor product decomposition
articles.statement:
Let $L/K$ be an extension of number
fields, $v$ a finite place of $K$ and $K_v$ the completion of $K$ at $v$; for each finite place $w$
of $L$ lying over $v$, let $L_w$ be the completion of $L$ at $w$, a $K_v$-algebra via the canonical
map $K_v \to L_w$, and make $L \otimes_K K_v$ a $K_v$-algebra through its second factor. Consider
the isomorphism of $K_v$-algebras $L \otimes_K K_v \cong \prod_{w \mid v} L_w$ sending $a \otimes b$
to $(a b)_w$, where $a \in L$ and $b \in K_v$ are mapped into each $L_w$. For every $y \in L$ and
every finite place $w$ of $L$ lying over $v$, the $w$-coordinate of the image of $y \otimes 1$ is
the image of $y$ in $L_w$.

## Sources

- ATLAS N265, Theorem 13.5, the coordinate law for pure tensors.

articles.title: Tensor product decomposition at a finite place over the base field
articles.statement:
Let $L/K$ be an
extension of number fields, $v$ a finite place of $K$ and $K_v$ the completion of $K$ at $v$; for
each finite place $w$ of $L$ lying over $v$, let $L_w$ be the completion of $L$ at $w$. There
exists an isomorphism of $K$-algebras $L \otimes_K K_v \cong \prod_{w \mid v} L_w$.

It is obtained by restricting scalars from $K_v$ to $K$ in the isomorphism of $K_v$-algebras
$L \otimes_K K_v \cong \prod_{w \mid v} L_w$ sending $y \otimes x$ to $(y x)_w$, where $y \in L$
and $x \in K_v$ are mapped into each $L_w$, $L_w$ is a $K_v$-algebra via the canonical map
$K_v \to L_w$, and $L \otimes_K K_v$ is a $K_v$-algebra through its second factor.

articles.title: Tensor product decomposition at a finite place
articles.statement:
Let $L/K$ be an extension of number fields,
$v$ a finite place of $K$ and $K_v$ the completion of $K$ at $v$; for each finite place $w$ of $L$
lying over $v$, let $L_w$ be the completion of $L$ at $w$, a $K_v$-algebra via the canonical map
$K_v \to L_w$, and make $L \otimes_K K_v$ a $K_v$-algebra through its second factor. This is the
isomorphism of $K_v$-algebras $L \otimes_K K_v \cong \prod_{w \mid v} L_w$ sending $y \otimes x$
to $(y x)_w$, where $y \in L$ and $x \in K_v$ are mapped into each $L_w$.

## Sources

- ATLAS N265, Theorem 13.5, the finite-place $K_v$-algebra form for number fields.

articles.title: Dimension count for the base change to a finite completion
articles.statement:
Let $L/K$ be an extension of
number fields, $v$ a finite place of $K$ and $K_v$ the completion of $K$ at $v$; for each finite
place $w$ of $L$ lying over $v$, let $L_w$ be the completion of $L$ at $w$, a $K_v$-algebra via
the canonical map $K_v \to L_w$. Then $K_v \otimes_K L$ and $\prod_{w \mid v} L_w$ have the same
dimension as $K_v$-vector spaces.

articles.title: Local degrees sum to the global degree
articles.statement:
Let $L/K$ be an extension of number fields, $v$ a
finite place of $K$ and $K_v$ the completion of $K$ at $v$; for each finite place $w$ of $L$ lying
over $v$, let $L_w$ be the completion of $L$ at $w$, a $K_v$-algebra via the canonical map
$K_v \to L_w$. Then $\sum_{w \mid v} [L_w : K_v] = [L : K]$.

## Sources

- ATLAS N236, Theorem 11.23, parts (4) and (5) combined; used in N265.

articles.title: Restriction of the completion map to the rings of integers
articles.statement:
Let $L/K$ be an extension of
number fields, let $v$ be a finite place of $K$, given as a height-one prime of the ring of
integers $\mathcal{O}_K$, and let $w$ be a finite place of $L$ lying over $v$. Let $K_v$ and $L_w$
be the completions, with rings of integers $\mathcal{O}_v$ and $\mathcal{O}_w$. The continuous
ring homomorphism $K_v \to L_w$ extending $K \to L$ restricts to a ring homomorphism
$\mathcal{O}_v \to \mathcal{O}_w$.

articles.title: The completion map preserves integrality
articles.statement:
Let $L/K$ be an extension of number fields, let
$v$ be a finite place of $K$, given as a height-one prime of the ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$,
and let $w$ be a finite place of $L$ lying over $v$. The continuous ring homomorphism
$K_v \to L_w$ between the completions that extends $K \to L$ maps every element of the ring of
integers of $K_v$ into the ring of integers of $L_w$.

articles.title: Valuation of the image under the completion map
articles.statement:
Let $L/K$ be an extension of number
fields, let $v$ be a finite place of $K$, given as a height-one prime of the ring of integers
$\mathcal{O}_K$, let $w$ be a finite place of $L$ lying over $v$, and let $e$ be the ramification
index of $w$ over $v$. Let $\iota : K_v \to L_w$ be the continuous ring homomorphism between the
completions that extends $K \to L$. Then for every $x \in K_v$, the valuation of $\iota(x)$ on
$L_w$ equals the $e$-th power of the valuation of $x$ on $K_v$, where both valuations are the
multiplicative adic valuations extended to the completions.

articles.title: Bound on the number of ideals of bounded norm
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field of degree
$n = [K : \mathbb{Q}]$ with ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$, and let $M > 0$ be a real number.
The number of nonzero ideals $I$ of $\mathcal{O}_K$ whose absolute norm
$N(I) = |\mathcal{O}_K / I|$ satisfies $N(I) \le M$ is at most $(nM)^{\log_2 M}$, where the
exponent $\log_2 M$ is a real number.

## Sources

- ATLAS `NumberTheoryI:295`, *Number Theory I*, Section 14.5, Lemma 14.21. The proof derives this bound from the integer-threshold and floor variants.

articles.title: Bound on the number of ideals of bounded norm, floor form
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field of
degree $n = [K : \mathbb{Q}]$ with ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$, let $M$ be any real number,
and let $m = \max(0, \lfloor M \rfloor)$. Let $k$ be the largest natural number with
$2^k \le m$, and $k = 0$ if $m = 0$. Then the number of nonzero ideals $I$ of $\mathcal{O}_K$
whose absolute norm $N(I) = |\mathcal{O}_K / I|$ satisfies $N(I) \le M$ is at most $(nm)^k$.

For $M < 1$ there are no such ideals, since every nonzero ideal has norm at least $1$; for
$M \ge 1$ the condition $N(I) \le M$ is equivalent to $N(I) \le m$.

articles.title: Bound on the number of ideals of bounded norm, integer threshold
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number
field of degree $n = [K : \mathbb{Q}]$ with ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$, let $M$ be a natural
number, and let $k$ be the largest natural number with $2^k \le M$, with $k = 0$ if $M = 0$.
Then the number of nonzero ideals $I$ of $\mathcal{O}_K$ whose absolute norm
$N(I) = |\mathcal{O}_K / I|$ satisfies $N(I) \le M$ is at most $(nM)^k$.

## Sources

- ATLAS `NumberTheoryI:295`, *Number Theory I*, Section 14.5, Lemma 14.21; this is a discrete strengthening with an integer threshold, valid also at $M = 0$ and $M = 1$, not the source's literal positive-real statement.

articles.title: Exponential lower bound for the discriminant
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field of degree
$n = [K : \mathbb{Q}]$ and discriminant $d_K$, and let $e$ be Euler's number. Then

$$|d_K| > \frac{1}{e^2 n} \left(\frac{\pi e^2}{4}\right)^n,$$

so the absolute discriminant grows at least exponentially in the degree.

## Sources

- ATLAS `NumberTheoryI` Corollary 14.26 (second inequality).

articles.title: Absolute norm of the discriminant ideal of a number field
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number
field with ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$ and discriminant $d_K$. The absolute norm of the
discriminant ideal of $\mathcal{O}_K$ over $\mathbb{Z}$ equals $|d_K|$.

articles.title: Elements of $B$ lie in the image of $B$
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be commutative rings and $L$ a
field, with algebra maps $A \to B$, $B \to L$ and $A \to L$ forming a scalar tower. For every
$b \in B$, the image of $b$ under the algebra map $B \to L$ lies in the image of $B$ in $L$,
regarded as an $A$-submodule of $L$.

articles.title: Discriminants of tuples from $B$ lie in the extension discriminant
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be
commutative rings and $K$ and $L$ fields with $L$ finite-dimensional over $K$, with algebra maps
forming scalar towers $A \to K \to L$ and $A \to B \to L$, and let $n = [L : K]$. If
$b_1, \dots, b_n \in L$ all lie in the image of $B$ in $L$, then their discriminant
$\operatorname{disc}_{L/K}(b_1, \dots, b_n)$ lies in the extension discriminant of the tower,
an $A$-submodule of $K$.

articles.title: The extension discriminant is a lattice discriminant
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be commutative
rings and $K$ and $L$ fields with $L$ finite-dimensional over $K$, with algebra maps forming
scalar towers $A \to K \to L$ and $A \to B \to L$. The extension discriminant of the tower
equals the lattice discriminant over $A$ and $K$ of the image of $B$ in $L$, regarded as an
$A$-submodule of $L$.

articles.title: Localization of the extension discriminant
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be commutative rings and $K$
and $L$ fields, with ring maps $A \to K \to L$ and $A \to B \to L$ whose composites $A \to L$
agree, and with $L$ finite-dimensional over $K$ of degree $n$. Write $D_{B/A}$ for the
$A$-submodule of $K$ generated by the discriminants $\operatorname{disc}_{L/K}(b_1, \dots, b_n)$
of all $n$-tuples of elements of the image of $B$ in $L$. Let $S$ be a submonoid of $A$, let
$S^{-1}A$ be a localization of $A$ at $S$, and let $S^{-1}B$ be a localization of $B$ at the
image of $S$ in $B$. Suppose given ring maps $S^{-1}A \to K$, $S^{-1}A \to S^{-1}B$ and
$S^{-1}B \to L$ such that the composite $A \to S^{-1}A \to K$ is the map $A \to K$, the
composite $B \to S^{-1}B \to L$ is the map $B \to L$, and the composites
$S^{-1}A \to K \to L$ and $S^{-1}A \to S^{-1}B \to L$ agree. Then the $S^{-1}A$-submodule of
$K$ spanned by $D_{B/A}$ equals $D_{S^{-1}B/S^{-1}A}$, the $S^{-1}A$-submodule of $K$ generated
by the discriminants of $n$-tuples of elements of the image of $S^{-1}B$ in $L$.

No Dedekind, fraction-ring, integrally-closed, or separability hypotheses are used.

articles.title: Extension discriminant
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be commutative rings and $K$ and $L$ fields with $L$
finite-dimensional over $K$, with algebra maps forming scalar towers $A \to K \to L$ and
$A \to B \to L$, and let $n = [L : K]$. The extension discriminant is the $A$-submodule of $K$
spanned by the discriminants $\operatorname{disc}_{L/K}(b_1, \dots, b_n)$ of all $n$-tuples of
elements of $L$ lying in the image of $B$ in $L$.

At this level of generality it is only an $A$-submodule of $K$, not an ideal of $A$.

articles.title: Image of $B$ in $L$
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be commutative rings and $L$ a field, with algebra
maps $A \to B$, $B \to L$ and $A \to L$ forming a scalar tower. The image of $B$ in $L$ is the
range of the algebra map $B \to L$, regarded as an $A$-submodule of $L$.

articles.title: Equal discriminants force equal lattices (fraction field version)
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative
ring and $L/K$ a finite extension of fields, with $A$-algebra structures on $K$ and $L$ forming a
scalar tower $A \to K \to L$, and let $n = [L : K]$. For an $A$-submodule $M$ of $L$, let $D(M)$ be
its discriminant, the $A$-submodule of $K$ generated by the discriminants over $K$ of all $n$-tuples
of elements of $M$. Assume $K$ is the fraction field of $A$ and $L/K$ is separable. Let
$M' \subseteq M$ be $A$-submodules of $L$. Suppose that $b_1, \dots, b_n$ is a $K$-basis of $L$ with
every $b_i$ in $M$ and $M$ contained in the $A$-span of $b_1, \dots, b_n$, and that
$b'_1, \dots, b'_n$ is a $K$-basis of $L$ with every $b'_i$ in $M'$ and $M'$ contained in the
$A$-span of $b'_1, \dots, b'_n$. If $D(M') = D(M)$, then $M' = M$.

articles.title: Equal discriminants force equal lattices
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $L/K$ a finite
extension of fields, with $A$-algebra structures on $K$ and $L$ forming a scalar tower
$A \to K \to L$, and let $n = [L : K]$. For an $A$-submodule $M$ of $L$, let $D(M)$ be its
discriminant, the $A$-submodule of $K$ generated by the discriminants over $K$ of all $n$-tuples of
elements of $M$. Assume $L/K$ is separable and the map $A \to K$ is injective. Let $M' \subseteq M$
be $A$-submodules of $L$. Suppose that $b_1, \dots, b_n$ is a $K$-basis of $L$ with every $b_i$ in
$M$ and $M$ contained in the $A$-span of $b_1, \dots, b_n$, and that $b'_1, \dots, b'_n$ is a
$K$-basis of $L$ with every $b'_i$ in $M'$ and $M'$ contained in the $A$-span of
$b'_1, \dots, b'_n$. If $D(M') = D(M)$, then $M' = M$.

## Sources

- Sutherland, MIT 18.785 Number Theory I (Fall 2021), Lecture 12, Lemma 12.10.

articles.title: The discriminant of a lattice spanned by a basis
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $L/K$ a
finite extension of fields, with $A$-algebra structures on $K$ and $L$ forming a scalar tower
$A \to K \to L$, and let $n = [L : K]$. For an $A$-submodule $M$ of $L$, let $D(M)$ be its
discriminant, the $A$-submodule of $K$ generated by the discriminants over $K$ of all $n$-tuples of
elements of $M$. If $b_1, \dots, b_n$ is a $K$-basis of $L$, every $b_i$ lies in $M$ and $M$ is
contained in the $A$-span of $b_1, \dots, b_n$, then
$D(M) = A \cdot \operatorname{disc}_{L/K}(b_1, \dots, b_n)$.

articles.title: The discriminant of a sandwiched lattice is a nonzero fractional ideal
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a
commutative ring and $L/K$ a finite extension of fields, with $A$-algebra structures on $K$ and $L$
forming a scalar tower $A \to K \to L$, and let $n = [L : K]$. For an $A$-submodule $M$ of $L$, let
$D(M)$ be its discriminant, the $A$-submodule of $K$ generated by the discriminants over $K$ of all
$n$-tuples of elements of $M$. Assume $K$ is the fraction field of $A$ and $L/K$ is separable. If
$M$ contains a $K$-basis $b_1, \dots, b_n$ of $L$ and is contained in the $A$-span of a $K$-basis
$c_1, \dots, c_n$ of $L$, then $D(M)$ is a fractional ideal (there is a non-zero-divisor $a \in A$
such that $a x$ lies in the image of $A$ in $K$ for every $x \in D(M)$) and $D(M) \neq 0$.

articles.title: The discriminant of a lattice inside a basis lattice is fractional
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative
ring and $L/K$ a finite extension of fields, with $A$-algebra structures on $K$ and $L$ forming a
scalar tower $A \to K \to L$, and let $n = [L : K]$. For an $A$-submodule $M$ of $L$, let $D(M)$ be
its discriminant, the $A$-submodule of $K$ generated by the discriminants over $K$ of all $n$-tuples
of elements of $M$. Assume $K$ is the fraction field of $A$. If $M$ is contained in the $A$-span of
a $K$-basis $b_1, \dots, b_n$ of $L$, then $D(M)$ is a fractional ideal: there is a non-zero-divisor
$a \in A$ such that $a x$ lies in the image of $A$ in $K$ for every $x \in D(M)$.

articles.title: The discriminant of a lattice inside a basis lattice
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring and
$L/K$ a finite extension of fields, with $A$-algebra structures on $K$ and $L$ forming a scalar
tower $A \to K \to L$, and let $n = [L : K]$. For an $A$-submodule $M$ of $L$, let $D(M)$ be its
discriminant, the $A$-submodule of $K$ generated by the discriminants over $K$ of all $n$-tuples of
elements of $M$. If $b_1, \dots, b_n$ is a $K$-basis of $L$ and $M$ is contained in the $A$-span of
$b_1, \dots, b_n$, then $D(M) \subseteq A \cdot \operatorname{disc}_{L/K}(b_1, \dots, b_n)$.

articles.title: The discriminant of a lattice containing a basis is nonzero
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring
and $L/K$ a finite extension of fields, with $A$-algebra structures on $K$ and $L$ forming a scalar
tower $A \to K \to L$, and let $n = [L : K]$. For an $A$-submodule $M$ of $L$, let $D(M)$ be its
discriminant, the $A$-submodule of $K$ generated by the discriminants over $K$ of all $n$-tuples of
elements of $M$. Assume $L/K$ is separable. If $M$ contains a $K$-basis $b_1, \dots, b_n$ of $L$,
then $D(M) \neq 0$.

articles.title: Discriminants of tuples from a submodule
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $L/K$ a finite
extension of fields, with $A$-algebra structures on $K$ and $L$ forming a scalar tower
$A \to K \to L$, and let $n = [L : K]$. For an $A$-submodule $M$ of $L$, this is the set of all
discriminants $\operatorname{disc}_{L/K}(b_1, \dots, b_n) = \det(\operatorname{Tr}_{L/K}(b_i b_j))$
in $K$ of $n$-tuples $(b_1, \dots, b_n)$ of elements of $M$.

articles.title: Discriminant of a lattice
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $L/K$ a finite extension of
fields, with $A$-algebra structures on $K$ and $L$ forming a scalar tower $A \to K \to L$, and let
$n = [L : K]$. The discriminant $D(M)$ of an $A$-submodule $M$ of $L$ is the $A$-submodule of $K$
generated by the discriminants
$\operatorname{disc}_{L/K}(b_1, \dots, b_n) = \det(\operatorname{Tr}_{L/K}(b_i b_j))$ of all
$n$-tuples $(b_1, \dots, b_n)$ of elements of $M$.

articles.title: Membership in the image of $B$
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be commutative rings and $L$ a field,
with algebra maps $A \to B$, $B \to L$ and $A \to L$ forming a scalar tower. An element
$x \in L$ lies in the image of $B$ in $L$ if and only if $x$ is the image of some $b \in B$
under the algebra map $B \to L$.

articles.title: Minkowski's lower bound for the discriminant
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field of degree
$n = [K : \mathbb{Q}]$ with $s$ complex places and discriminant $d_K$. Then

$$|d_K| \ge \left(\frac{n^n}{n!}\right)^2 \left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)^{2s}.$$

## Sources

- ATLAS `NumberTheoryI` Corollary 14.26 (first inequality); this is Mathlib's `NumberField.abs_discr_ge'`, restated in the form used by the book.

articles.title: Comparison of the Minkowski and exponential discriminant bounds
articles.statement:
Let $n$ and $s$ be
natural numbers with $n \ne 0$ and $2s \le n$, and let $e$ be Euler's number. Then

$$\frac{1}{e^2 n} \left(\frac{\pi e^2}{4}\right)^n <
\left(\frac{n^n}{n!}\right)^2 \left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)^{2s}.$$

## Sources

- ATLAS `NumberTheoryI` Corollary 14.26 (second inequality), with $n$ the degree of a number field and $s$ its number of complex places.

articles.title: Discriminants of $F_{p^e}$ for primes $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime with
$p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$, let $e \ge 1$, let $F_n(x) = 1 + x + x^2/2 + \cdots + x^n/n$ be the
truncated logarithmic polynomial and let $\mathcal{P}_n$ be the truncated logarithmic resultant
product. If $e$ is odd, the discriminant of $F_{p^e}$ is not a square in $\mathbb{Q}$. If $e$ is
even, the discriminant of $F_{p^e}$ is not a square in $\mathbb{Q}$ if and only if the integer
$\mathcal{P}_{p^e}$ is not a square in $\mathbb{Q}$.

## Sources

- Cullinan and Gajek-Leonard, *On the Discriminants of Truncated Logarithmic Polynomials*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A39, Corollary 1.

articles.title: Finiteness of square discriminants of $F_{mq}$ with $mq \equiv 1 \pmod 4$
articles.statement:
Let
$F_n(x) = 1 + x + x^2/2 + \cdots + x^n/n$ be the truncated logarithmic polynomial and let
$m \ge 1$ be a natural number. Then there are only finitely many primes $q$ with
$mq \equiv 1 \pmod 4$ such that the discriminant of $F_{mq}$ is a square in $\mathbb{Q}$.

## Sources

- Cullinan and Gajek-Leonard, *On the Discriminants of Truncated Logarithmic Polynomials*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A39, Theorem 3.

articles.title: The scaled truncated logarithmic polynomial is $L_n F_n$
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$, let
$L_n = \operatorname{lcm}(1, 2, \dots, n)$, let $F_n(x) = 1 + x + x^2/2 + \cdots + x^n/n$ be the
truncated logarithmic polynomial and let $\tilde F_n \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ be the scaled truncated
logarithmic polynomial. Mapping the coefficients of $\tilde F_n$ from $\mathbb{Z}$ to
$\mathbb{Q}$ gives the polynomial $L_n F_n$ in $\mathbb{Q}[x]$.

## Sources

- Cullinan and Gajek-Leonard, *On the Discriminants of Truncated Logarithmic Polynomials*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A39, Section 1.

articles.title: A prime $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$ does not divide $\mathcal{P}_{p^e}$
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime with
$p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$, let $e \ge 1$, and let $\mathcal{P}_n$ be the truncated logarithmic
resultant product. Then $p$ does not divide $\mathcal{P}_{p^e}$.

## Sources

- Cullinan and Gajek-Leonard, *On the Discriminants of Truncated Logarithmic Polynomials*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A39, Theorem 4.

articles.title: An odd prime $p$ does not divide $\mathcal{P}_{p^{2e}}$
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be an odd prime, let
$e \ge 1$, and let $\mathcal{P}_n$ be the truncated logarithmic resultant product. Then $p$ does
not divide $\mathcal{P}_{p^{2e}}$.

## Sources

- Cullinan and Gajek-Leonard, *On the Discriminants of Truncated Logarithmic Polynomials*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A39, Theorem 2.

articles.title: Nonsquare discriminants of $F_{mq}$ for non-exceptional primes $q > m$
articles.statement:
Let $m$ be a
natural number, let $E_m$ be the set of exceptional primes for truncated logarithmic
discriminants, and let $F_n(x) = 1 + x + x^2/2 + \cdots + x^n/n$ be the truncated logarithmic
polynomial. If $q$ is a prime with $q \notin E_m$, $q > m$ and $mq \equiv 1 \pmod 4$, then the
discriminant of $F_{mq}$ is not a square in $\mathbb{Q}$.

## Sources

- Cullinan and Gajek-Leonard, *On the Discriminants of Truncated Logarithmic Polynomials*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A39, Theorem 5.

articles.title: Nonsquare discriminants of $F_n$ for positive $n \equiv 0, 2, 3 \pmod 4$
articles.statement:
Let
$F_n(x) = 1 + x + x^2/2 + \cdots + x^n/n$ be the truncated logarithmic polynomial and let
$n \ge 1$ be a natural number with $n \equiv 0$, $2$ or $3 \pmod 4$. Then the discriminant of
$F_n$ is not a square in $\mathbb{Q}$.

## Sources

- Cullinan and Gajek-Leonard, *On the Discriminants of Truncated Logarithmic Polynomials*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A39, Proposition 1.

articles.title: Nonsquare discriminants of $F_{3q}$, $F_{5q}$ and $F_{7q}$
articles.statement:
Let
$F_n(x) = 1 + x + x^2/2 + \cdots + x^n/n$ be the truncated logarithmic polynomial. For every
prime $q$, if $n = 3q$, $n = 5q$ or $n = 7q$, then the discriminant of $F_n$ is not a square in
$\mathbb{Q}$.

## Sources

- Cullinan and Gajek-Leonard, *On the Discriminants of Truncated Logarithmic Polynomials*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A39, Proposition 2.

articles.title: Nonsquare discriminants of truncated logarithmic polynomials
articles.statement:
Let
$F_n(x) = 1 + x + x^2/2 + \cdots + x^n/n$ be the truncated logarithmic polynomial and let
$n \ge 1$. If $n \equiv 0$, $2$ or $3 \pmod 4$, or if $n \equiv 1 \pmod 4$ and $n = p^e$ for a
prime $p$ and an odd $e$, then the discriminant of $F_n$ is not a square in $\mathbb{Q}$.

## Sources

- Cullinan and Gajek-Leonard, *On the Discriminants of Truncated Logarithmic Polynomials*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A39, Theorem 1.

articles.title: Scaled truncated logarithmic polynomial
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$, let
$L_n = \operatorname{lcm}(1, 2, \dots, n)$. The scaled truncated logarithmic polynomial is the
integer polynomial $\tilde F_n(x) = L_n + \sum_{j=1}^{n} (L_n / j)\, x^j$, where each quotient
$L_n / j$ is an integer.

## Sources

- Cullinan and Gajek-Leonard, *On the Discriminants of Truncated Logarithmic Polynomials*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A39, Section 1.

articles.title: Auxiliary product at $m = 1$
articles.statement:
The auxiliary product $X(m)$ takes the value $X(1) = 1$ at
$m = 1$; it is an empty product.

## Sources

- Cullinan and Gajek-Leonard, *On the Discriminants of Truncated Logarithmic Polynomials*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A39, Section 4.

articles.title: Auxiliary product for truncated logarithmic discriminants
articles.statement:
For a natural number $m$, let
$f_m(x) = \sum_{k=0}^{m-1} x^k$ and $g_m(x) = c_m + \sum_{j=1}^{m-1} \frac{x^j}{j}$ in
$\mathbb{Q}[x]$, where $c_m = \frac{1}{m}$ for $m \ge 1$ and $c_0 = 0$. The rational number $X(m)$
is the resultant $\operatorname{Res}(f_m, g_m)$. For $m \ge 1$, since $f_m$ is monic with roots
$\omega^k$ for $1 \le k \le m-1$, where $\omega$ is a primitive $m$-th root of unity, this is
$X(m) = \prod_{k=1}^{m-1} g_m(\omega^k)$.

## Sources

- Cullinan and Gajek-Leonard, *On the Discriminants of Truncated Logarithmic Polynomials*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A39, Section 4.

articles.title: Exceptional primes for truncated logarithmic discriminants
articles.statement:
For a natural number $m$, the
exceptional set $E_m$ is the set of primes $\ell$ with $m\ell \equiv 1 \pmod 4$ such that the
$\ell$-adic valuation of the auxiliary product $X(m)$ is positive or the $\ell$-adic valuation of
the harmonic number $Y(m) = H_m = 1 + \frac{1}{2} + \dots + \frac{1}{m}$ is positive.

The source's display joins the two valuation conditions with "and", but its text ("all prime
divisors of $X(m)$ and $Y(m)$") and its table ($E_3 = \{11\}$ with $11 \nmid X(3) = 13/36$) use
the union.

## Sources

- Cullinan and Gajek-Leonard, *On the Discriminants of Truncated Logarithmic Polynomials*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A39, Section 4.

articles.title: Least common multiple of $1, 2, 3, 4$
articles.statement:
The least common multiple of the integers from $1$
to $4$ is $L_4 = \operatorname{lcm}(1, 2, 3, 4) = 12$.

## Sources

- Cullinan and Gajek-Leonard, *On the Discriminants of Truncated Logarithmic Polynomials*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A39, Section 1.

articles.title: Least common multiple of $1, \dots, n$
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$, $L_n$ is the least common
multiple $\operatorname{lcm}(1, 2, \dots, n)$ of the integers from $1$ to $n$; in particular
$L_0 = 1$.

## Sources

- Cullinan and Gajek-Leonard, *On the Discriminants of Truncated Logarithmic Polynomials*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A39, Section 1.

articles.title: Truncated logarithmic polynomial
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$, the truncated logarithmic
polynomial is $F_n(x) = 1 + x + \frac{x^2}{2} + \dots + \frac{x^n}{n} \in \mathbb{Q}[x]$.

## Sources

- Cullinan and Gajek-Leonard, *On the Discriminants of Truncated Logarithmic Polynomials*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A39, Section 1.

articles.title: Resultant product at $n = 1$
articles.statement:
The resultant product satisfies $\mathcal{P}_1 = 1$; it is an
empty product.

## Sources

- Cullinan and Gajek-Leonard, *On the Discriminants of Truncated Logarithmic Polynomials*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A39, Equation (5).

articles.title: Positivity of the resultant product
articles.statement:
For every natural number $n \ge 1$, the resultant
product $\mathcal{P}_n$ is a positive integer.

## Sources

- Cullinan and Gajek-Leonard, *On the Discriminants of Truncated Logarithmic Polynomials*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A39, Lemma 1.

articles.title: Resultant product for truncated logarithmic polynomials
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$, let
$F_n(x) = 1 + x + \frac{x^2}{2} + \dots + \frac{x^n}{n}$, let
$L_n = \operatorname{lcm}(1, \dots, n)$, and let $\tilde F_n = L_n F_n \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$. The
integer $\mathcal{P}_n$ is the resultant $\operatorname{Res}(1 + x + \dots + x^{n-1}, \tilde F_n)$.
For $n \ge 1$ the polynomial $1 + x + \dots + x^{n-1} = F_n'$ is monic, so
$\mathcal{P}_n = \prod_{\theta} \tilde F_n(\theta)$, the product over the roots $\theta$ of $F_n'$.

## Sources

- Cullinan and Gajek-Leonard, *On the Discriminants of Truncated Logarithmic Polynomials*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A39, Equation (5).

articles.title: Isomorphism of number fields with bounded discriminant
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $n$ and $H$,
two number fields $K$ and $L$ of degree $n$ over $\mathbb{Q}$, each with discriminant of absolute
value at most $H$, are related when there exists a ring isomorphism from $K$ to $L$.

articles.title: Jacobian determinant in the quotient ring
articles.statement:
For polynomials
$E_1, \dots, E_r \in \mathbb{Q}[x_1, \dots, x_r]$, the image in the quotient ring
$\mathbb{Q}[x_1, \dots, x_r]/(E_1, \dots, E_r)$ of the Jacobian determinant
$\det(\partial E_i / \partial x_j)_{1 \le i, j \le r}$.

articles.title: The open subscheme where the Jacobian does not vanish
articles.statement:
For polynomials
$E_1, \dots, E_r \in \mathbb{Q}[x_1, \dots, x_r]$, the open subscheme of
$\operatorname{Spec} \mathbb{Q}[x_1, \dots, x_r]/(E_1, \dots, E_r)$ where the Jacobian
determinant $\det(\partial E_i / \partial x_j)$ does not vanish, that is, the basic open set of
the image of this determinant in the quotient ring.

articles.title: Isomorphism classes of number fields with bounded discriminant
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $n$
and $H$, the quotient of the type of number fields of degree $n$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ whose
discriminant has absolute value at most $H$ by the relation of being isomorphic as rings.

articles.title: Number fields of degree $n$ with discriminant bounded by $H$
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $n$ and
$H$, the type of number fields $K$ of degree $n$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ whose discriminant $d_K$
satisfies $|d_K| \le H$.

articles.title: Number fields of degree $n$
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$, the type of number fields of degree
$n$ over $\mathbb{Q}$: an element is a type $K$ with a field structure making $K$ a number field
(a field of characteristic zero that is finite-dimensional over $\mathbb{Q}$) such that
$\dim_{\mathbb{Q}} K = n$.

articles.title: Quotient of a polynomial ring by $r$ polynomials
articles.statement:
For a natural number $r$ and polynomials
$E_1, \dots, E_r \in \mathbb{Q}[x_1, \dots, x_r]$, the quotient ring
$\mathbb{Q}[x_1, \dots, x_r]/(E_1, \dots, E_r)$ of the polynomial ring by the ideal generated by
$E_1, \dots, E_r$.

articles.title: Couveignes: number fields have small models
articles.statement:
There is a positive integer $Q$ such that for
every natural number $n \ge Q$ and every number field $K$ of degree $n$ over $\mathbb{Q}$, with
discriminant $d_K$ and root discriminant $\delta_K = |d_K|^{1/n}$, there are natural numbers $r$
and $d$ with $r \le Q \log n$, $d \le Q \log n$ and $\binom{d + r}{r} \le Q n \log n$, and
polynomials $E_1, \dots, E_r \in \mathbb{Z}[x_1, \dots, x_r]$ of total degree at most $d$, all of
whose coefficients have absolute value at most $(n \delta_K)^{Q \log n}$, with the following
property. Let $X$ be the open subscheme of
$\operatorname{Spec} \mathbb{Q}[x_1, \dots, x_r]/(E_1, \dots, E_r)$ where
$\det(\partial E_i / \partial x_j) \ne 0$. Then $X$ has an irreducible component $Z$ which, with
its subscheme structure as the scheme-theoretic closure of the open set of points of $X$ lying on
no other irreducible component, is isomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec} K$.

## Sources

- J.-M. Couveignes, `Enumerating number fields`, Annals of Math, 192 (2) 2020. Statement taken from https://github.com/ImperialCollegeLondon/AnnalsChallenge. Problem `annals_enumerating_number_fields` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Couveignes: counting number fields with bounded discriminant
articles.statement:
There is a positive integer
$Q$ such that for all natural numbers $n \ge Q$ and $H \ge 1$, there are only finitely many
isomorphism classes of number fields of degree $n$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ whose discriminant has
absolute value at most $H$, and their number is at most $n^{Q n (\log n)^3} H^{Q (\log n)^3}$.

## Sources

- J.-M. Couveignes, `Enumerating number fields`, Annals of Math, 192 (2) 2020. Statement taken from https://github.com/ImperialCollegeLondon/AnnalsChallenge. Problem `annals_enumerating_number_fields` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Martinet's totally real towers
articles.statement:
There is a real constant $C > 0$ such that for every
$N \in \mathbb{N}$ there exist a natural number $d \ge N$ and a totally real number field $K$ of
degree $[K : \mathbb{Q}] = d$ whose discriminant $\Delta_K$ satisfies $|\Delta_K| \le C^d$.

## Sources

- Theorem 3.2 of T. F. Bloom, W. Sawin, C. Schildkraut, D. Zhelezov, *The sum-product conjecture is false for real numbers*, arXiv:2605.28781. Lean axiom: https://github.com/mathlib-initiative/sum_product (SumProduct.exists_totallyReal_discr_le). Underlying result: J. Martinet, *Tours de corps de classes et estimations de discriminants*, Invent. Math. 44 (1978), 65–73. Problem `martinet_totally_real_towers` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Units small away from the diagonal generate a subgroup of finite index
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a
number field and let $(u_v)$ be a family of units of the ring of integers of $F$, indexed by
the infinite places $v$ of $F$. Write $w(x)$ for the absolute value of $x$ at an infinite place
$w$. If $w(u_v) < 1$ for all infinite places $v$ and $w$ with $w \ne v$, then the subgroup of
the unit group of the ring of integers generated by the $u_v$ has finite index.

After dropping the coordinate of one infinite place, the logarithmic embeddings of the
remaining $u_v$ form a square matrix with negative off-diagonal entries and positive column
sums. It is therefore strictly diagonally dominant by columns, hence invertible, so these
units generate a subgroup of maximal rank.

articles.title: Finite unramified intermediate fields
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $L/K$ a field
extension such that the map $A \to L$ factors as $A \to K \to L$. An intermediate field $E$ of
$L/K$ is finite unramified relative to $A$ if $E$ is finite-dimensional over $K$ and the
integral closure of $A$ in $E$ is formally unramified over $A$.

articles.title: Finite unramified subfields lie in the maximal unramified subextension
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a
commutative ring and $L/K$ a field extension such that the map $A \to L$ factors as
$A \to K \to L$. Every intermediate field $E$ of $L/K$ that is finite unramified relative to $A$
is contained in the maximal unramified subextension of $L/K$ relative to $A$.

articles.title: The maximal unramified subextension is stable under automorphisms
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a
commutative ring and $L/K$ a field extension such that the map $A \to L$ factors as
$A \to K \to L$, and let $M$ be the maximal unramified subextension of $L/K$ relative to $A$.
For every $K$-algebra automorphism $\sigma$ of $L$, $\sigma(M) = M$.

articles.title: Automorphisms preserve finite unramified subfields
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring and
$L/K$ a field extension such that the map $A \to L$ factors as $A \to K \to L$. If an
intermediate field $E$ of $L/K$ is finite unramified relative to $A$, then for every
$K$-algebra automorphism $\sigma$ of $L$ the image $\sigma(E)$ is finite unramified relative
to $A$.

articles.title: Universal property of the maximal unramified subextension
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring
and $L/K$ a field extension such that the map $A \to L$ factors as $A \to K \to L$. An
intermediate field $F$ of $L/K$ contains the maximal unramified subextension of $L/K$ relative
to $A$ if and only if $F$ contains every intermediate field of $L/K$ that is finite unramified
relative to $A$.

articles.title: Maximal unramified subextension
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $L/K$ a field
extension such that the map $A \to L$ factors as $A \to K \to L$. The maximal unramified
subextension of $L/K$ relative to $A$ is the supremum, in the lattice of intermediate fields of
$L/K$, of all intermediate fields of $L/K$ that are finite unramified relative to $A$.

The supremum need not itself be finite or formally unramified.

articles.title: Odlyzko's root discriminant bound in degree at least 18
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a totally complex
number field of degree $n = [K : \mathbb{Q}] \ge 18$ and discriminant $d_K$. Then
$|d_K| \ge 8.25^n$; equivalently, the root discriminant $|d_K|^{1/n}$ of $K$ is at least $8.25$.

Minkowski's elementary argument is not strong enough; the bound comes from analysing the zeros
of the Dedekind zeta function of $K$.

## Sources

- A. M. Odlyzko, *Bounds for discriminants and related estimates for class numbers, regulators and zeros of zeta functions: a survey of recent results*, Sém. Delange-Pisot-Poitou 18(1) (1976–1977), exp. 6, <https://www.numdam.org/item/SDPP_1976-1977__18_1_A6_0/>.

articles.title: Elements of a number field are quotients of elements of an order
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number
field and $O$ an order in $K$, that is, a subring of $K$ contained in the ring of integers
$\mathcal{O}_K$ (the integral closure of $\mathbb{Z}$ in $K$) whose field of fractions is $K$.
Then for every $x \in K$ there are $a, b \in O$ with $b \neq 0$ and $x = a / b$.

articles.title: The fraction field of an order
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field and $O$ an order in $K$, that
is, a subring of $K$ contained in the ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$ (the integral closure of
$\mathbb{Z}$ in $K$) whose field of fractions is $K$. Then $K$, with the inclusion
$O \subseteq K$, is a field of fractions of $O$.

articles.title: The ring of integers is an order
articles.statement:
For every number field $K$, the ring of integers
$\mathcal{O}_K$, the integral closure of $\mathbb{Z}$ in $K$, is an order in $K$, that is, a
subring of $K$ contained in $\mathcal{O}_K$ whose field of fractions is $K$.

articles.title: Orders lie in the ring of integers
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field and $O$ an order in $K$,
that is, a subring of $K$ contained in the ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$ (the integral
closure of $\mathbb{Z}$ in $K$) whose field of fractions is $K$. Then
$O \subseteq \mathcal{O}_K$.

articles.title: Localizing the ring of integers at an unramified prime gives an étale algebra
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be
a number field with ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$, and let $p$ be a prime ideal of $\mathbb{Z}$
that is unramified in $\mathcal{O}_K$, that is, every prime ideal of $\mathcal{O}_K$ lying over $p$
is unramified over $\mathbb{Z}$. Let $S$ be the localization of $\mathcal{O}_K$ at the image of
the multiplicative set $\mathbb{Z} \setminus p$. Then $S$ is an étale algebra over the local ring
$\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}$.

The ring $S$ is semilocal: it keeps every prime of $\mathcal{O}_K$ above $p$ at once, rather than
the localization $(\mathcal{O}_K)_Q$ at a single such prime $Q$.

## Sources

- packages the primewise unramified hypothesis used in ATLAS N390, Proposition 19.14.

articles.title: Only finitely many primes ramify in a number field extension
articles.statement:
Only finitely many height-one primes of a number field ramify
in a number-field extension.

articles.title: Unramifiedness descends to smaller intermediate fields
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a number field, let
$E \subseteq F$ be intermediate fields of $L/\mathbb{Q}$, and let $\mathfrak{p}$ be an ideal of
$\mathbb{Z}$. If $\mathfrak{p}$ is unramified in $\mathcal{O}_F$, that is, every prime ideal of
$\mathcal{O}_F$ lying over $\mathfrak{p}$ is unramified over $\mathbb{Z}$, then $\mathfrak{p}$ is
unramified in $\mathcal{O}_E$.

## Sources

- ATLAS N390, Proposition 19.14.

articles.title: The contracted maximal prime is prime
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a number field, let $E$ and $F$ be
intermediate fields of $L/\mathbb{Q}$ with compositum $EF$, let $p$ be a prime ideal of
$\mathbb{Z}$ that is unramified in $\mathcal{O}_F$, and let $Q$ be a prime ideal of
$\mathcal{O}_{EF}$ lying over $p$. Then the contracted maximal prime of the normalized tensor
algebra at $Q$ is a prime ideal.

It is the preimage of the maximal ideal of the local ring $(\mathcal{O}_{EF})_Q$, which is
prime.

articles.title: Membership in the contracted maximal prime
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a number field, let $E$ and $F$ be
intermediate fields of $L/\mathbb{Q}$ with compositum $EF$, let $p$ be a prime ideal of
$\mathbb{Z}$ that is unramified in $\mathcal{O}_F$, and let $Q$ be a prime ideal of
$\mathcal{O}_{EF}$ lying over $p$. Write $R = \mathbb{Z}_{(p)}$, let $S_F$ be the localization of
$\mathcal{O}_F$ at the image of $\mathbb{Z} \setminus p$, let $C$ be the integral closure of $S_F$
in $S_F \otimes_R \operatorname{Frac}(\mathcal{O}_E)$, let $T = (\mathcal{O}_{EF})_Q$, and let
$g \colon C \to T$ be the normalized tensor map to the compositum at $Q$. An element $x \in C$
lies in the contracted maximal prime if and only if $g(x)$ lies in the maximal ideal of the local
ring $T$.

articles.title: The contracted maximal prime of the normalized tensor algebra
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a number field,
let $E$ and $F$ be intermediate fields of $L/\mathbb{Q}$ with compositum $EF$, let $p$ be a prime
ideal of $\mathbb{Z}$ that is unramified in $\mathcal{O}_F$, and let $Q$ be a prime ideal of
$\mathcal{O}_{EF}$ lying over $p$. Write $R = \mathbb{Z}_{(p)}$, let $S_F$ be the localization of
$\mathcal{O}_F$ at the image of $\mathbb{Z} \setminus p$, let $C$ be the integral closure of $S_F$
in $S_F \otimes_R \operatorname{Frac}(\mathcal{O}_E)$, let $T = (\mathcal{O}_{EF})_Q$ be the
localization of $\mathcal{O}_{EF}$ at $Q$, and let $g \colon C \to T$ be the normalized tensor map
to the compositum at $Q$. The contracted maximal prime is the ideal $g^{-1}(\mathfrak{m}_T)$ of
$C$, where $\mathfrak{m}_T$ is the maximal ideal of the local ring $T$.

It contains the kernel of $g$, and is in general strictly larger. It is intended as the prime of
$C$ at which to localize in order to recover the local factor $T$.

## Sources

- ATLAS N390, Proposition 19.14.

articles.title: The localization map restricts to the normalized tensor map
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a number field,
let $E$ and $F$ be intermediate fields of $L/\mathbb{Q}$ with compositum $EF$, let $p$ be a prime
ideal of $\mathbb{Z}$ that is unramified in $\mathcal{O}_F$, and let $Q$ be a prime ideal of
$\mathcal{O}_{EF}$ lying over $p$. Write $R = \mathbb{Z}_{(p)}$, let $S_F$ be the localization of
$\mathcal{O}_F$ at the image of $\mathbb{Z} \setminus p$, let $C$ be the integral closure of $S_F$
in $S_F \otimes_R \operatorname{Frac}(\mathcal{O}_E)$, let $T = (\mathcal{O}_{EF})_Q$, let
$g \colon C \to T$ be the normalized tensor map to the compositum at $Q$, let $\mathfrak{q}$ be the
contracted maximal prime of $C$, and let $\varphi \colon C_{\mathfrak{q}} \to T$ be the
localization map to the compositum at $Q$. Then for every $x \in C$, $\varphi$ sends the image of
$x$ in $C_{\mathfrak{q}}$ to $g(x)$.

articles.title: Value of the localization map on fractions
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a number field, let $E$ and $F$ be
intermediate fields of $L/\mathbb{Q}$ with compositum $EF$, let $p$ be a prime ideal of
$\mathbb{Z}$ that is unramified in $\mathcal{O}_F$, and let $Q$ be a prime ideal of
$\mathcal{O}_{EF}$ lying over $p$. Write $R = \mathbb{Z}_{(p)}$, let $S_F$ be the localization of
$\mathcal{O}_F$ at the image of $\mathbb{Z} \setminus p$, let $C$ be the integral closure of $S_F$
in $S_F \otimes_R \operatorname{Frac}(\mathcal{O}_E)$, let $T = (\mathcal{O}_{EF})_Q$, let
$g \colon C \to T$ be the normalized tensor map to the compositum at $Q$, let $\mathfrak{q}$ be the
contracted maximal prime of $C$, and let $\varphi \colon C_{\mathfrak{q}} \to T$ be the
localization map to the compositum at $Q$. Then for all $x \in C$, $s \in C \setminus \mathfrak{q}$
and $v \in T$, we have $\varphi(x/s) = v$ if and only if $g(x) = g(s)\,v$.

articles.title: The localization map to the compositum at a prime
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a number field, let $E$ and
$F$ be intermediate fields of $L/\mathbb{Q}$ with compositum $EF$, let $p$ be a prime ideal of
$\mathbb{Z}$ that is unramified in $\mathcal{O}_F$, and let $Q$ be a prime ideal of
$\mathcal{O}_{EF}$ lying over $p$. Write $R = \mathbb{Z}_{(p)}$, let $S_F$ be the localization of
$\mathcal{O}_F$ at the image of $\mathbb{Z} \setminus p$, let $C$ be the integral closure of $S_F$
in $S_F \otimes_R \operatorname{Frac}(\mathcal{O}_E)$, let $T = (\mathcal{O}_{EF})_Q$, let
$g \colon C \to T$ be the normalized tensor map to the compositum at $Q$, and let $\mathfrak{q}$
be the contracted maximal prime of $C$. Since $g$ sends every element of $C \setminus \mathfrak{q}$
outside the maximal ideal of the local ring $T$, hence to a unit, $g$ induces by the universal
property of localization a ring homomorphism $C_{\mathfrak{q}} \to T$, sending $x/s$ to
$g(x)\,g(s)^{-1}$.

articles.title: The normalized tensor map on simple tensors
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a number field, let $E$ and $F$ be
intermediate fields of $L/\mathbb{Q}$ with compositum $EF$, let $p$ be a prime ideal of
$\mathbb{Z}$ that is unramified in $\mathcal{O}_F$, and let $Q$ be a prime ideal of
$\mathcal{O}_{EF}$ lying over $p$. Write $R = \mathbb{Z}_{(p)}$, let $S_F$ and $S_E$ be the
localizations of $\mathcal{O}_F$ and $\mathcal{O}_E$ at the image of $\mathbb{Z} \setminus p$, let
$C$ be the integral closure of $S_F$ in $S_F \otimes_R \operatorname{Frac}(\mathcal{O}_E)$, let
$T = (\mathcal{O}_{EF})_Q$, and let $g \colon C \to T$ be the normalized tensor map to the
compositum at $Q$. Let $e \colon S_F \otimes_R S_E \to C$ be the normalization isomorphism, and
let $f_F \colon S_F \to T$ and $f_E \colon S_E \to T$ be the maps induced by the inclusions of
$\mathcal{O}_F$ and $\mathcal{O}_E$ into $\mathcal{O}_{EF}$. Then for all $x \in S_F$ and
$y \in S_E$, we have $g(e(x \otimes y)) = f_F(x)\,f_E(y)$.

articles.title: The kernel of the normalized tensor map is prime
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a number field, let $E$ and
$F$ be intermediate fields of $L/\mathbb{Q}$ with compositum $EF$, let $p$ be a prime ideal of
$\mathbb{Z}$ that is unramified in $\mathcal{O}_F$, and let $Q$ be a prime ideal of
$\mathcal{O}_{EF}$ lying over $p$. Write $R = \mathbb{Z}_{(p)}$, let $S_F$ be the localization of
$\mathcal{O}_F$ at the image of $\mathbb{Z} \setminus p$, let $C$ be the integral closure of $S_F$
in $S_F \otimes_R \operatorname{Frac}(\mathcal{O}_E)$, and let
$g \colon C \to (\mathcal{O}_{EF})_Q$ be the normalized tensor map to the compositum at $Q$. Then
the kernel of $g$ is a prime ideal of $C$.

This holds because $(\mathcal{O}_{EF})_Q$ is an integral domain. The kernel of $g$ is in general
strictly smaller than the preimage under $g$ of the maximal ideal of the local ring
$(\mathcal{O}_{EF})_Q$, which is the prime of $C$ at which to localize.

articles.title: The kernel lies in the contracted maximal ideal
articles.statement:
Let $E$ and $F$ be intermediate fields of
a number field $L$ over $\mathbb Q$, let $\mathfrak p$ be a prime ideal of $\mathbb Z$ that is
unramified in $\mathcal O_F$, and let $\mathfrak Q$ be a prime ideal of the ring of integers
$\mathcal O_{EF}$ of the compositum $EF$ of $E$ and $F$ in $L$ lying over $\mathfrak p$. Write
$R = \mathbb Z_{\mathfrak p}$ for the localization of $\mathbb Z$ at $\mathfrak p$; for
$K = E, F$ let $S_K$ be the localization of $\mathcal O_K$ at the image of
$\mathbb Z \setminus \mathfrak p$ and let $\varphi_K : S_K \to (\mathcal O_{EF})_{\mathfrak Q}$ be
the map induced by the inclusion $\mathcal O_K \subseteq \mathcal O_{EF}$; let $C$ be the integral
closure of $S_F$ in $S_F \otimes_R \operatorname{Frac}(\mathcal O_E)$; and let
$g : C \to (\mathcal O_{EF})_{\mathfrak Q}$ be the $R$-algebra homomorphism that, for $s \in S_F$
and $t \in S_E$, sends the image of $s \otimes t$ under the canonical isomorphism
$S_F \otimes_R S_E \cong C$ to $\varphi_F(s) \varphi_E(t)$. Then the kernel of $g$ is contained in
the preimage under $g$ of the maximal ideal of $(\mathcal O_{EF})_{\mathfrak Q}$.

articles.title: Map from the normalized tensor algebra to the local ring of the compositum
articles.statement:
Let $E$ and
$F$ be intermediate fields of a number field $L$ over $\mathbb Q$, let $\mathfrak p$ be a prime
ideal of $\mathbb Z$ that is unramified in $\mathcal O_F$, and let $\mathfrak Q$ be a prime ideal of
the ring of integers $\mathcal O_{EF}$ of the compositum $EF$ of $E$ and $F$ in $L$ lying over
$\mathfrak p$. Write $R = \mathbb Z_{\mathfrak p}$ for the localization of $\mathbb Z$ at
$\mathfrak p$; for $K = E, F$ write $S_K$ for the localization of $\mathcal O_K$ at the image of
$\mathbb Z \setminus \mathfrak p$ and $\varphi_K : S_K \to (\mathcal O_{EF})_{\mathfrak Q}$ for the
map induced by the inclusion $\mathcal O_K \subseteq \mathcal O_{EF}$; and let $C$ be the integral
closure of $S_F$ in $S_F \otimes_R \operatorname{Frac}(\mathcal O_E)$. This is the $R$-algebra
homomorphism $C \to (\mathcal O_{EF})_{\mathfrak Q}$ obtained by composing the inverse of the
canonical isomorphism $S_F \otimes_R S_E \cong C$ with the map
$S_F \otimes_R S_E \to (\mathcal O_{EF})_{\mathfrak Q}$ that, for $s \in S_F$ and $t \in S_E$,
sends $s \otimes t$ to $\varphi_F(s) \varphi_E(t)$.

No claim is made that this map induces an isomorphism from a localization of $C$ onto
$(\mathcal O_{EF})_{\mathfrak Q}$.

articles.title: Values of the localization-to-local-ring map on fractions
articles.statement:
Let $R \to S \to T$ be
homomorphisms of commutative rings whose algebra structures form a scalar tower, let
$\mathfrak p$ be a prime ideal of $R$, and let $\mathfrak Q$ be a prime ideal of $T$ lying over
$\mathfrak p$. Write $S_{\mathfrak p}$ for the localization of $S$ at the image of
$R \setminus \mathfrak p$, and let $\varphi : S_{\mathfrak p} \to T_{\mathfrak Q}$ be the
$S$-algebra homomorphism extending the composite $S \to T \to T_{\mathfrak Q}$. For $x \in S$,
$y$ in the image of $R \setminus \mathfrak p$ in $S$, and $z \in T_{\mathfrak Q}$, we have
$\varphi(x/y) = z$ if and only if $x = yz$ in $T_{\mathfrak Q}$, where $x$ and $y$ stand for
their images under $S \to T \to T_{\mathfrak Q}$.

articles.title: Map from the localization away from a prime to the local ring at a prime above it
articles.statement:
Let
$R \to S \to T$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings whose algebra structures form a scalar
tower, let $\mathfrak p$ be a prime ideal of $R$, and let $\mathfrak Q$ be a prime ideal of $T$
lying over $\mathfrak p$. Write $S_{\mathfrak p}$ for the localization of $S$ at the image of
$R \setminus \mathfrak p$. This is the homomorphism of $S$-algebras
$S_{\mathfrak p} \to T_{\mathfrak Q}$ extending the composite $S \to T \to T_{\mathfrak Q}$; it
exists because elements of $R \setminus \mathfrak p$ map outside $\mathfrak Q$, hence to units of
$T_{\mathfrak Q}$.

articles.title: Normalization commutes with base change along an unramified prime
articles.statement:
Let $E$ and $F$ be
number fields and let $\mathfrak p$ be a prime ideal of $\mathbb Z$ that is unramified in the ring
of integers $\mathcal O_F$. Write $R = \mathbb Z_{\mathfrak p}$ for the localization of $\mathbb Z$
at $\mathfrak p$, and for $K = E, F$ write $S_K$ for the localization of $\mathcal O_K$ at the
image of $\mathbb Z \setminus \mathfrak p$. Let $K_E$ be the fraction field of $\mathcal O_E$ and
let $\iota : S_E \to K_E$ be the canonical map. This is the isomorphism of $S_F$-algebras from
$S_F \otimes_R S_E$ onto the integral closure of $S_F$ in $S_F \otimes_R K_E$ that, for
$s \in S_F$ and $t \in S_E$, sends $s \otimes t$ to $s \otimes \iota(t)$.

It is obtained from the identification of $S_E$ with the integral closure of $R$ in $K_E$, using
that $S_F$ is étale over $R$.

articles.title: Inertia degree one for a singly generated algebra
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be commutative rings,
$B$ an $A$-algebra, and $\mathfrak q$ a maximal ideal of $B$ whose preimage $\mathfrak p$ under
$A \to B$ is maximal. If $B$ is generated as an $A$-algebra by a single element
$\pi \in \mathfrak q$, then the inertia degree of $\mathfrak q$ over $\mathfrak p$ is $1$.

The canonical map $A/\mathfrak p \to B/\mathfrak q$ is surjective, so the residue field
extension has degree one.

articles.title: Surjectivity of the residue map for a singly generated algebra
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be
commutative rings, $B$ an $A$-algebra, $\mathfrak q$ an ideal of $B$ and $\mathfrak p$ its
preimage under $A \to B$. If $B$ is generated as an $A$-algebra by a single element
$\pi \in \mathfrak q$, then the canonical map $A/\mathfrak p \to B/\mathfrak q$ is surjective.

Indeed, every element of $B$ is $f(\pi)$ for a polynomial $f$ with coefficients in $A$, and
modulo $\mathfrak q$ it agrees with the image of the constant coefficient of $f$, because $\pi$
maps to zero.

articles.title: Monic integer polynomials whose Galois group is not $S_n$
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $n$ and
$H$, $E_n(H)$ is the number of monic polynomials $f(x) = x^n + a_1 x^{n-1} + \dots + a_n$ of
degree $n$ with integer coefficients and $|a_i| \le H$ for $i = 1, \dots, n$ whose Galois group
over $\mathbb{Q}$ has order less than $n!$, that is, is not the full symmetric group $S_n$.

articles.title: Van der Waerden's conjecture (Bhargava)
articles.statement:
For every natural number $n \ge 3$ there is a
constant $C$ such that $E_n(H) \le C H^{n-1}$ for all sufficiently large natural numbers $H$,
where $E_n(H)$ is the number of monic polynomials of degree $n$ with integer coefficients, all
non-leading coefficients of absolute value at most $H$, whose Galois group over $\mathbb{Q}$
has order less than $n!$.

The degree restriction is necessary: the statement is false for $n = 2$.

## Sources
