rows, then for all distinct $i, j < L$ columns $i$ and $j$ are different.

## Sources

- R. J. Booth and D. J. Horton, *Matched Column Sets in Repetend Tables*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A26, Theorem 12.

articles.title: Two-row repetend tables of length $4$ have no matched columns
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$,
let the rows be the integers $b$ with $1 \le b < n$, $\gcd(b, n) = 1$ and multiplicative order $4$
modulo $n$, and let column $j$ be the multiset of the digits $\lfloor b^{j+1}/n \rfloor \bmod b$
over these rows. If there are exactly two rows, then for all distinct $i, j < 4$ columns $i$ and
$j$ are different.

## Sources

- R. J. Booth and D. J. Horton, *Matched Column Sets in Repetend Tables*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A26, Lemma 32.

articles.title: Two-row repetend tables of length $3$ have no matched columns
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$,
let the rows be the integers $b$ with $1 \le b < n$, $\gcd(b, n) = 1$ and multiplicative order $3$
modulo $n$, and let column $j$ be the multiset of the digits $\lfloor b^{j+1}/n \rfloor \bmod b$
over these rows. If there are exactly two rows, then for all distinct $i, j < 3$ columns $i$ and
$j$ are different.

## Sources

- R. J. Booth and D. J. Horton, *Matched Column Sets in Repetend Tables*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A26, Lemma 30.

articles.title: Repetend tables of length at most $2$ have no matched columns
articles.statement:
Let $n$ and $L \le 2$ be
natural numbers, let the rows be the integers $b$ with $1 \le b < n$, $\gcd(b, n) = 1$ and
multiplicative order $L$ modulo $n$, and let column $j$ be the multiset of the digits
$\lfloor b^{j+1}/n \rfloor \bmod b$ over these rows. If there is at least one row, then for all
distinct $i, j < L$ columns $i$ and $j$ are different.

## Sources

- R. J. Booth and D. J. Horton, *Matched Column Sets in Repetend Tables*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A26, Lemma 26.

articles.title: Order-$6$ repetend tables of $3^k t$ have no matched columns
articles.statement:
Let $k \ge 2$ and
$t \in \{1, 2\}$, and put $n = 3^k t$. Let the rows be the integers $b$ with $1 \le b < n$,
$\gcd(b, n) = 1$ and multiplicative order $6$ modulo $n$, and let column $j$ be the multiset of
the digits $\lfloor b^{j+1}/n \rfloor \bmod b$ over these rows. Then for all distinct $i, j < 6$
columns $i$ and $j$ are different.

## Sources

- R. J. Booth and D. J. Horton, *Matched Column Sets in Repetend Tables*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A26, Lemma 34.

articles.title: Columns $1$ to $4$ of the order-$6$ repetend table of $t p^k$ are pairwise different
articles.statement:
Let
$p$ be a prime with $p \equiv 1 \pmod 6$, let $k \ge 1$ and $t \in \{1, 2\}$, and put $n = t p^k$.
Let the rows be the integers $b$ with $1 \le b < n$, $\gcd(b, n) = 1$ and multiplicative order $6$
modulo $n$, and let column $j$ be the multiset of the digits $\lfloor b^{j+1}/n \rfloor \bmod b$
over these rows. Then for all distinct $i, j \in \{1, 2, 3, 4\}$ columns $i$ and $j$ are
different.

## Sources

- R. J. Booth and D. J. Horton, *Matched Column Sets in Repetend Tables*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A26, Lemma 40.

articles.title: Columns $1$, $2$, $3$ of the order-$6$ repetend table differ from columns $0$ and $5$
articles.statement:
Let
$p \equiv 1 \pmod 6$ be prime, $k \ge 1$, $t \in \{1, 2\}$ and $n = t p^k$, and let $B$ be the set
of integers $b$ with $1 \le b < n$, $\gcd(b, n) = 1$ and multiplicative order $6$ modulo $n$. For
$c \ge 0$ let column $c$ be the multiset of the digits $\lfloor b^{c+1}/n \rfloor \bmod b$ over
$b \in B$. Then for every $i \in \{1, 2, 3\}$ and $j \in \{0, 5\}$, columns $i$ and $j$ are
different multisets.

## Sources

- R. J. Booth and D. J. Horton, *Matched Column Sets in Repetend Tables*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A26, Lemma 38.

articles.title: Matching columns of a two-row repetend table
articles.statement:
Let $n$ and $L$ be natural numbers and let
$B$ be the set of integers $c$ with $1 \le c < n$, $\gcd(c, n) = 1$ and multiplicative order $L$
modulo $n$. For $c \in B$ and $k \ge 0$ let $r_k(c) = \lfloor c^{k+1}/n \rfloor \bmod c$, and let
$C_k$ be the multiset of the $r_k(c)$ over $c \in B$. Suppose $B$ has exactly two elements, $b$
and $b' \ne b$, and put $D_k = r_k(b') - r_k(b)$. Then for all $i, j \ge 0$ with $C_i = C_j$,
$D_i = D_j$ or $D_i = -D_j$, and the sum of the elements of $C_i$ equals that of $C_j$.

## Sources

- R. J. Booth and D. J. Horton, *Matched Column Sets in Repetend Tables*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A26, Lemma 28.

articles.title: Digit differences between the rows $b_1$ and $b_1^5$ of the order-$6$ table
articles.statement:
Let
$p \equiv 1 \pmod 6$ be prime, $k \ge 1$, $t \in \{1, 2\}$ and $n = t p^k$, and let $b_1 < n$
have multiplicative order $6$ modulo $n$. Put $H = 0$ if $t = 1$, $H = p^k$ if $t = 2$ and
$b_1 < p^k$, and $H = -p^k$ if $t = 2$ and $b_1 \ge p^k$. Let $b_5 = b_1^5 \bmod n$ and, for
$i \ge 0$, $D_i = r_i(b_5) - r_i(b_1)$, where $r_i(c) = \lfloor c^{i+1}/n \rfloor \bmod c$. Then
$D_0 = D_5 = 0$, $D_2 = n - b_1 - (b_1^2 \bmod n) = 1 - 2 b_1 + n - H$,
$n D_1 = (n - H) D_2$, $D_3 = D_2$ and $n D_4 = H D_2$.

## Sources

- R. J. Booth and D. J. Horton, *Matched Column Sets in Repetend Tables*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A26, Lemma 36.

articles.title: Repetend digits are symmetric under inverse indices
articles.statement:
Let $n, b, x, j, j'$ be natural
numbers and $L \ge 1$, and suppose $b$ has multiplicative order $L$ modulo $n$. For $y, c \ge 0$
put $b_y = b^y \bmod n$ and $r_{y,c} = \lfloor b_y^{c+1}/n \rfloor \bmod b_y$, the $c$-th digit
of $1/n$ in base $b_y$. If $\gcd(j, L) = 1$ and $j j' \equiv 1 \pmod L$, then
$r_{xj, j'} = r_{x, j}$.

## Sources

- R. J. Booth and D. J. Horton, *Matched Column Sets in Repetend Tables*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A26, Lemma 6.

articles.title: Differences of repetend digits
articles.statement:
Let $n \ge 1$ and $b$ be natural numbers with
$\gcd(b, n) = 1$. For $x, j \ge 0$ put $b_x = b^x \bmod n$ and
$r_{x,j} = \lfloor b_x^{j+1}/n \rfloor \bmod b_x$. Then for all natural numbers $y, m, d, e$,

$$n (r_{ym,e} - r_{y,d}) = b_{ym} b_{yme} - b_{ym(e+1)} - b_y b_{yd} + b_{y(d+1)}.$$

## Sources

- R. J. Booth and D. J. Horton, *Matched Column Sets in Repetend Tables*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A26, Lemma 7.

articles.title: Digit differences for a base of order $6p^j$ modulo $p^i$
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime with
$p \equiv 1 \pmod 6$, let $i$ and $j$ be natural numbers, and put $n = p^i$ and $Q = p^j$. Let
$B < n$ be a natural number whose multiplicative order modulo $n$ is $6Q$, let $f \in \{1, -1\}$,
and let $d$ and $e$ be natural numbers with $d \equiv 2fQ \pmod{6Q}$ and $e \equiv fQ \pmod{6Q}$.
For natural $s$ write $r_s = \lfloor B^{s+1}/n \rfloor \bmod B$ for the $s$-th base-$B$ digit of
$1/n$, and put $D = n(r_e - r_d)$. Then $D = B + (B^{d+1} \bmod n) - (B^{e+1} \bmod n)$, and
$D = 0$ or $D = n$.

The statement is made for all natural numbers $i$ and $j$.

## Sources

- R. J. Booth and D. J. Horton, *Matched Column Sets in Repetend Tables*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A26, Lemma 14.

articles.title: The last column pairs a base with its inverse
articles.statement:
Let $n$ and $L \ge 1$ be natural numbers
and let $b < n$ have multiplicative order $L$ modulo $n$. Put $b' = b^{L-1} \bmod n$, the inverse
of $b$ modulo $n$. Then $b$ and $b'$ have the same digit in column $L - 1$:
$\lfloor b'^{L}/n \rfloor \bmod b' = \lfloor b^{L}/n \rfloor \bmod b$.

## Sources

- R. J. Booth and D. J. Horton, *Matched Column Sets in Repetend Tables*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A26, Theorem 2.

articles.title: The last repetend digit is nonzero
articles.statement:
Let $n \ge 2$ and let $b \ge 2$ be prime to $n$,
with multiplicative order $L$ modulo $n$ (the repetend length of $1/n$ in base $b$). Then the
digit $\lfloor b^{(L-1)+1}/n \rfloor \bmod b$ of $1/n$ at position $L - 1$ is not $0$.

This holds for every such base, not only for the small bases $b < n$ that form the rows of the
paper's table.

## Sources

- R. J. Booth and D. J. Horton, *Matched Column Sets in Repetend Tables*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A26, Lemma 25.

articles.title: Sign balance for differences of shifted linear residues
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be prime, $j \ge 1$ and
$Q = p^j$. Let $g_1, g_2, f_1, f_2$ be natural numbers with $g_1, g_2 < Q$ and $f_1 \le f_2 < Q$
such that $p$ divides none of $g_1$, $g_2$, $g_2 - g_1$, and let $e_1, e_2$ be reals with
$0 < e_1 < e_2 < 1$. For natural $z$ put $c_i(z) = ((g_i z + f_i) \bmod Q) + e_i$ and
$d(z) = c_2(z) - c_1(z)$. Then (a) among $1 \le z \le Q - 1$, the number of $z$ with $d(z) > 0$
equals the number with $d(z) < 0$; and (b) if $f_1 \equiv 0 \pmod p$ or
$f_1 \equiv f_2 \pmod p$, the same holds among the $z$ with $1 \le z \le Q - 1$ and $p \nmid z$.

## Sources

- R. J. Booth and D. J. Horton, *Matched Column Sets in Repetend Tables*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A26, Theorem 7.

articles.title: The number of units of order $L$ is a multiple of $\varphi(L)$
articles.statement:
For natural numbers
$n \ge 1$ and $L$, the number $E(L, n)$ of elements of order $L$ in the unit group
$(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^\times$ is divisible by Euler's totient $\varphi(L)$.

## Sources

- R. J. Booth and D. J. Horton, *Matched Column Sets in Repetend Tables*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A26, Corollary 4.

articles.title: Tail bound for sums of inverse powers
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $m \ge 2$ and $s \ge 1$,
$\sum_{n = s+1}^{\infty} n^{-m} < \dfrac{1}{(m-1)\, s^{m-1}}$.

## Sources

- R. J. Booth and D. J. Horton, *Matched Column Sets in Repetend Tables*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A26, Lemma 42.

articles.title: Tu–Deng conjecture
articles.statement:
For every integer $k \ge 2$ and every nonzero residue $t$ modulo
$2^k - 1$, the number of pairs $(a, b)$ of residues modulo $2^k - 1$ with $a + b = t$ and
$w(a) + w(b) \le k - 1$ is at most $2^{k-1}$, where $w(a)$ is the binary digit sum of the
representative of $a$ in $\{0, 1, \dots, 2^k - 2\}$.

## Sources

- T. W. Cusick, Proof of the Tu-Deng Conjecture, arXiv:2608.14821 (2026), https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.14821.

articles.title: Bounds on the binary expected square-free walk length
articles.statement:
Let $L_{2,k}$ denote the number of
right-truncatable square-free numbers with exactly $k$ digits in base $2$. The real series
$E_2 = \sum_{k \ge 1} L_{2,k} / 2^k$ satisfies
$636163720502 / 2^{38} \le E_2 \le 636163930777 / 2^{38}$.

This is the series the proof of Theorem 3.8 uses. The paper's Lemma 3.7 prints the denominators
$b^k - b^{k-1}$, which for $b = 2$ would double the sum.

## Sources

- Steven J. Miller, Fei Peng, Tudor Popescu, Joshua M. Siktar, and Nawapan Wattanawanichkul, *Walking to Infinity Along Some Number Theory Sequences*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A78, Theorem 3.8.

articles.title: Walking to infinity on primes by appending decimal digits
articles.statement:
For every prime $p_0$ there is
a sequence of primes $p_0, p_1, p_2, \ldots$ starting at $p_0$ such that for every $i \ge 1$ there
are integers $n_i \ge 1$ and $k_i$ with $0 < k_i < 10^{n_i}$ and $p_i = 10^{n_i} p_{i-1} + k_i$;
that is, each term is obtained from the previous one by appending $n_i$ decimal digits on the
right.

## Sources

- Steven J. Miller, Fei Peng, Tudor Popescu, Joshua M. Siktar, and Nawapan Wattanawanichkul, *Walking to Infinity Along Some Number Theory Sequences*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A78, Theorem 2.3.

articles.title: Closed form of the extended Cunningham chain
articles.statement:
For all natural numbers $p$ and $k$, the
$k$-th term $e_k$ of the extended Cunningham chain generated by $p$ satisfies
$e_k + 1 = 2^k (p + 1)$, that is, $e_k = 2^k (p + 1) - 1$.

## Sources

- Miller, Peng, Popescu, Siktar, and Wattanawanichkul, *Walking to Infinity Along Some Number Theory Sequences*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A78, display after Definition 2.4.

articles.title: Extended Cunningham chains generated by primes contain arbitrarily long composite runs
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime and let $e_0 = p, e_1, e_2, \ldots$ be the extended Cunningham chain
generated by $p$. For every $n \ge 1$ there is $i \ge 1$ such that none of
$e_i, e_{i+1}, \ldots, e_{i+n-1}$ is prime.

Since $e_i \ge 2p + 1 \ge 5$ for $i \ge 1$, these terms are composite.

## Sources

- Steven J. Miller, Fei Peng, Tudor Popescu, Joshua M. Siktar, and Nawapan Wattanawanichkul, *Walking to Infinity Along Some Number Theory Sequences*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A78, Theorem 2.6.

articles.title: Recurrence of the extended Cunningham chain
articles.statement:
For all natural numbers $p$ and $k$, the
terms of the extended Cunningham chain generated by $p$ satisfy $e_{k+1} = 2 e_k + 1$.

## Sources

- Miller, Peng, Popescu, Siktar, and Wattanawanichkul, *Walking to Infinity Along Some Number Theory Sequences*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A78, Definition 2.4.

articles.title: First terms of the extended Cunningham chain generated by 2
articles.statement:
The extended Cunningham
chain $e_0, e_1, e_2, \ldots$ generated by $2$ has $e_1 = 5$, $e_2 = 11$ and $e_3 = 23$.

## Sources

- Miller, Peng, Popescu, Siktar, and Wattanawanichkul, *Walking to Infinity Along Some Number Theory Sequences*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A78, Definition 2.4.

articles.title: Initial term of the extended Cunningham chain
articles.statement:
For every natural number $p$, the extended
Cunningham chain generated by $p$ has initial term $e_0 = p$.

## Sources

- Miller, Peng, Popescu, Siktar, and Wattanawanichkul, *Walking to Infinity Along Some Number Theory Sequences*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A78, Definition 2.4.

articles.title: Extended Cunningham chain
articles.statement:
For a natural number $p$, the extended Cunningham chain
generated by $p$ is the sequence $e_0, e_1, e_2, \ldots$ of natural numbers given by $e_0 = p$ and
$e_k = 2 e_{k-1} + 1$ for $k \ge 1$; in binary, $e_k$ is obtained from $p$ by appending $k$ digits
$1$ on the right.

The paper requires the generator $p$ to be prime; here $p$ may be any natural number, and results
that need primality assume it explicitly.

## Sources

- Steven J. Miller, Fei Peng, Tudor Popescu, Joshua M. Siktar, and Nawapan Wattanawanichkul, *Walking to Infinity Along Some Number Theory Sequences*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A78, Definition 2.4.

articles.title: No binary prime walk to infinity in steps of one or two digits
articles.statement:
There is no sequence of
primes $p_0, p_1, p_2, \ldots$ such that for every $i \ge 0$ there are $n \in \{1, 2\}$ and a
natural number $k < 2^n$ with $p_{i+1} = 2^n p_i + k$. That is, starting from any prime, one
cannot walk to infinity on primes by appending one or two binary digits at a time on the right.

The appended blocks are the paper's $0, 1, 00, 01, 10, 11$ (a block may begin with $0$).

## Sources

- Steven J. Miller, Fei Peng, Tudor Popescu, Joshua M. Siktar, and Nawapan Wattanawanichkul, *Walking to Infinity Along Some Number Theory Sequences*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A78, Theorem 2.7.

articles.title: Small counts of right-truncatable square-free numbers
articles.statement:
Let $L_{b,k}$ denote the number of
right-truncatable square-free numbers with exactly $k$ digits in base $b$. Then $L_{2,1} = 1$,
$L_{2,2} = 2$, $L_{2,3} = 3$, $L_{2,4} = 5$ and $L_{10,1} = 6$.

## Sources

- Miller, Peng, Popescu, Siktar, and Wattanawanichkul, *Walking to Infinity Along Some Number Theory Sequences*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A78, proofs of Theorems 3.8 and 3.9.

articles.title: Counting right-truncatable square-free numbers
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $b$ and $k$,
$L_{b,k}$ is the number of right-truncatable square-free numbers with exactly $k$ digits in
base $b$: the number of natural numbers $x$ with $b^{k-1} \le x < b^k$ such that
$\lfloor x / b^{\ell} \rfloor$ is square-free for every $\ell \in \{0, \dots, k-1\}$. When
$k = 0$ the range is empty, so $L_{b,0} = 0$.

## Sources

- Steven J. Miller, Fei Peng, Tudor Popescu, Joshua M. Siktar, and Nawapan Wattanawanichkul, *Walking to Infinity Along Some Number Theory Sequences*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A78, Definition 3.6.

articles.title: A power of two minus a much smaller positive number is not a power of two
articles.statement:
Let $p$
and $k$ be natural numbers with $k \ge \lceil \log_2 (p + 1) \rceil + 2$. Then $2^k - (p + 1)$
is not a power of $2$: there is no natural number $m$ with $2^k - (p + 1) = 2^m$.

Under this hypothesis $2^k > p + 1$, so the subtraction is exact. The source assumes $p$ is
prime; the statement holds without that assumption.

## Sources

- Steven J. Miller, Fei Peng, Tudor Popescu, Joshua M. Siktar, and Nawapan Wattanawanichkul, *Walking to Infinity Along Some Number Theory Sequences*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A78, Lemma 2.5.

articles.title: Base-k expansion
articles.statement:
For a natural number $k \ge 2$ and a natural number $n$, the base-$k$
expansion of $n$ is the word $d_1 d_2 \cdots d_m$ of base-$k$ digits, most significant digit
first, with $n = \sum_{i=1}^{m} d_i k^{m-i}$ and $d_1 \neq 0$; for $n = 0$ it is the empty word.

articles.title: Value of a base-k digit word
articles.statement:
The value of a word $w = d_1 d_2 \cdots d_m$ of base-$k$
digits $d_i \in \{0, \dots, k - 1\}$, read with the most significant digit first, is
$\sum_{i=1}^{m} d_i k^{m-i}$. The empty word has value $0$.

articles.title: Multiplicatively independent bases
articles.statement:
Two natural numbers $k$ and $l$ are multiplicatively
independent when $k^m \ne l^n$ for all positive natural numbers $m$ and $n$.

articles.title: Cobham's theorem for characteristic sequences
articles.statement:
Let $k$ and $l$ be multiplicatively
independent natural numbers with $l \ge 2$, and let $S$ be a set of natural numbers that is
recognizable in base $k$ and whose characteristic sequence $n \mapsto (n \in S)$, a sequence of
truth values, is not ultimately periodic. Then $S$ is not recognizable in base $l$.

articles.title: Cobham's theorem
articles.statement:
Let $k$ and $l$ be multiplicatively independent natural numbers with
$l \ge 2$, and let $S$ be a set of natural numbers that is recognizable in base $k$ and is not
ultimately periodic. Then $S$ is not recognizable in base $l$.

## Sources

- proved via T. J. P. Krebs, *A more reasonable proof of Cobham's theorem*, arXiv:1801.06704, Section 3.
- T. Kärki, A. Lacroix, and M. Rigo, *On the Recognizability of Self-Generating Sets*, especially the remark invoking Cobham's theorem: <https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL13/Rigo/rigo6.tex>.

articles.title: Cobham's gap theorem without a separate base hypothesis
articles.statement:
Let $k$ be a natural number and
let $x_0 < x_1 < x_2 < \cdots$ be a strictly increasing sequence of natural numbers whose set of
values is recognizable in base $k$. Then either the limit superior, as $i \to \infty$, of the
ratios $x_{i+1} / x_i$ computed in the extended nonnegative reals $[0, \infty]$ (where a ratio
with denominator $0$ is $\infty$) is greater than $1$, or there is a natural number $C$ with
$x_{i+1} - x_i \le C$ for every $i$.

Recognizability in base $k$ already requires $k \ge 2$, so no separate hypothesis on $k$ is
needed.

articles.title: Cobham's gap theorem
articles.statement:
Let $k \ge 2$ be a natural number and let $x_0 < x_1 < x_2 < \cdots$
be a strictly increasing sequence of natural numbers whose set of values is recognizable in base
$k$. Then either the limit superior, as $i \to \infty$, of the ratios $x_{i+1} / x_i$ computed in
the extended nonnegative reals $[0, \infty]$ (so an unbounded limit superior is $\infty$, and a
ratio with denominator $0$ is $\infty$) is greater than $1$, or there is a natural number $C$ with
$x_{i+1} - x_i \le C$ for every $i$.

## Sources

- Kärki–Lacroix–Rigo gap theorem, lines 979–995 of <https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL13/Rigo/rigo6.tex>.

articles.title: Sets recognizable in base k
articles.statement:
For a natural number $k$, a set $S$ of natural numbers is
recognizable in base $k$ when $k \ge 2$ and some deterministic finite automaton with a nonempty
finite set of states, reading words of base-$k$ digits from the most significant digit, accepts a
word $w = d_1 d_2 \cdots d_m$ exactly when $w$ is canonical (empty, or with $d_1 \neq 0$) and its
value $\sum_{i=1}^{m} d_i k^{m-i}$ lies in $S$.

articles.title: Canonical base-k words
articles.statement:
A word of base-$k$ digits is canonical when it is empty or its
first (most significant) digit is nonzero.

articles.title: Ultimately periodic sets and their characteristic sequences
articles.statement:
A set $S$ of natural
numbers is ultimately periodic if and only if its characteristic sequence $n \mapsto (n \in S)$,
a sequence of truth values, is ultimately periodic.

articles.title: Ultimately periodic sets of natural numbers
articles.statement:
A set $S$ of natural numbers is ultimately
periodic when there are natural numbers $N$ and $p > 0$ such that, for every $n \ge N$,
$n \in S$ if and only if $n + p \in S$.

articles.title: Coefficients of Kohen's operator $\Lambda_k$
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a semiring and let $r$ and
$k \ne 0$ be natural numbers. For every Laurent polynomial $f$ in $r$ variables with coefficients
in $R$ and every $j \in \mathbb{Z}^r$, the coefficient of $x^j$ in $\Lambda_k f$ is the
coefficient of $x^{kj}$ in $f$.

## Sources

- Nadav Kohen, *A Linear Representation for Constant Term Sequences mod p^a with Applications to Uniform Recurrence*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.2, Section 2 (definition of `Λ_k`).

articles.title: Kohen's linear representation step modulo $p$
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, let $P$ be a Laurent
polynomial in $r$ variables with integer coefficients, and write $\deg P$ for the largest absolute
value of an exponent of a single variable in a monomial occurring in $P$ ($0$ if $P = 0$). Let $m$
be a natural number with $\deg P \le m + 1$. Write $T = [-m, m]^r \subseteq \mathbb{Z}^r$ and
$[x^e]F$ for the coefficient of $x^e$ in a Laurent polynomial $F$. Then for every natural number
$k < p$, every natural number $n$ and every $i \in T$,

$$[x^{-i}]P^{pn+k} \equiv \sum_{j \in T} [x^{pj - i}]P^k \cdot [x^{-j}]P^n \pmod{p}.$$

With Kohen's $a^n_i = [x^{-i}]P^n$, $\gamma(k) = (a^k_{i-pj})_{i,j \in T}$ and
$V(n) = (a^n_i)_{i \in T}$, this is the entrywise form of $\gamma(k) V(n) = V(pn + k)$ over
$\mathbb{F}_p$.

## Sources

- Nadav Kohen, *A Linear Representation for Constant Term Sequences mod p^a with Applications to Uniform Recurrence*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.2, Lemma 9 (`jis-2026-26.4.2-lem-9`).

articles.title: Kohen's linear representation step modulo $p^a$
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, let $a$ be a natural
number, and let $\tilde P$ be a Laurent polynomial in $r$ variables with integer coefficients such
that $\tilde P^p \equiv \tilde P(x^p) \pmod{p^a}$ coefficientwise, where $\tilde P(x^p)$ is
obtained from $\tilde P$ by replacing each monomial $x^e$ with $x^{pe}$. Write $\deg \tilde P$ for
the largest absolute value of an exponent of a single variable in a monomial occurring in
$\tilde P$ ($0$ if $\tilde P = 0$). Let $m$ be a natural number with $\deg \tilde P \le m + 1$,
and write $T = [-m, m]^r \subseteq \mathbb{Z}^r$ and $[x^e]F$ for the coefficient of $x^e$ in a
Laurent polynomial $F$. Then for every natural number $k < p$, every natural number $n$ and every
$i \in T$,

$$
[x^{-i}]\tilde P^{pn+k} \equiv
\sum_{j \in T} [x^{pj - i}]\tilde P^k \cdot [x^{-j}]\tilde P^n \pmod{p^a}.
$$

This is the entrywise form of Kohen's step $\tilde\gamma(k) \tilde V(n) = \tilde V(pn + k)$ over
$\mathbb{Z}/p^a\mathbb{Z}$.

## Sources

- Nadav Kohen, *A Linear Representation for Constant Term Sequences mod p^a with Applications to Uniform Recurrence*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.2, Lemma 28 (`jis-2026-26.4.2-lem-28`).

articles.title: Rowland–Zeilberger congruence
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime and let $P$ and $Q$ be Laurent
polynomials in $r$ variables with integer coefficients. Write $\operatorname{ct}[F]$ for the
constant term of a Laurent polynomial $F$ and $\Lambda_p$ for Kohen's operator, which keeps the
terms whose exponents are all divisible by $p$ and replaces $x^{pj}$ by $x^j$. Then for all
natural numbers $n$ and $k$,
$\operatorname{ct}[P^{pn+k} Q] \equiv \operatorname{ct}[P^n \Lambda_p(P^k Q)] \pmod{p}$.

The exponents $n$ and $k$ are natural numbers; the paper writes "integers", but negative powers
of a general Laurent polynomial are undefined.

## Sources

- Nadav Kohen, *A Linear Representation for Constant Term Sequences mod p^a with Applications to Uniform Recurrence*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.2, Lemma 3 (`jis-2026-26.4.2-lem-3`).

articles.title: Passing from $P$ to $\tilde P$ modulo $p^a$
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, let $a \ge 1$ and $\ell$
be natural numbers, and let $P$ and $\tilde P$ be Laurent polynomials in $r$ variables with
integer coefficients such that $P^{p^{a-1}} \equiv \tilde P(x^{p^\ell}) \pmod{p^a}$
coefficientwise, where $\tilde P(x^q)$ is obtained from $\tilde P$ by replacing each monomial
$x^e$ with $x^{qe}$. Write $\operatorname{ct}[F]$ for the constant term of a Laurent polynomial
$F$ and $\Lambda_q$ for Kohen's operator, which keeps the terms whose exponents are all divisible
by $q$ and replaces $x^{qj}$ by $x^j$. Then for every Laurent polynomial $Q$ in $r$ variables
with integer coefficients and all natural numbers $n$ and $k$,
$\operatorname{ct}[P^{p^{a-1} n + k} Q] \equiv
\operatorname{ct}[\tilde P^n \Lambda_{p^\ell}(P^k Q)] \pmod{p^a}$.

The statement holds for every natural number $k$; the paper restricts to $k < p^{a-1}$.

## Sources

- Nadav Kohen, *A Linear Representation for Constant Term Sequences mod p^a with Applications to Uniform Recurrence*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.2, Proposition 23 (`jis-2026-26.4.2-prop-23`).

articles.title: Rowland–Zeilberger congruence modulo $p^a$
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, let $a$ be a natural
number, and let $\tilde P$ be a Laurent polynomial in $r$ variables with integer coefficients
such that $\tilde P^p \equiv \tilde P(x^p) \pmod{p^a}$ coefficientwise, where $\tilde P(x^p)$
is obtained from $\tilde P$ by replacing each monomial $x^e$ with $x^{pe}$. Write
$\operatorname{ct}[F]$ for the constant term of a Laurent polynomial $F$ and $\Lambda_p$ for
Kohen's operator, which keeps the terms whose exponents are all divisible by $p$ and replaces
$x^{pj}$ by $x^j$. Then for every Laurent polynomial $Q$ in $r$ variables with integer
coefficients and all natural numbers $n$ and $k$,
$\operatorname{ct}[\tilde P^{pn+k} Q] \equiv
\operatorname{ct}[\tilde P^n \Lambda_p(\tilde P^k Q)] \pmod{p^a}$.

The statement holds for every natural number $k$; the paper states it for $k \in \mathbb{F}_p$.

## Sources

- Nadav Kohen, *A Linear Representation for Constant Term Sequences mod p^a with Applications to Uniform Recurrence*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.2, Lemma 24 (`jis-2026-26.4.2-lem-24`).

articles.title: Density-one zeros of constant terms modulo $p^a$
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, let $a$ be a natural
number, and let $\tilde P$ be a Laurent polynomial in $r$ variables with integer coefficients such
that $\tilde P^p \equiv \tilde P(x^p) \pmod{p^a}$ coefficientwise, where $\tilde P(x^p)$ is
obtained from $\tilde P$ by replacing each monomial $x^e$ with $x^{pe}$. Write
$\operatorname{ct}[F]$ for the constant term of a Laurent polynomial $F$, and suppose that $p$
divides $\operatorname{ct}[\tilde P^{n_0}]$ for some natural number $n_0$. Then for every
Laurent polynomial $Q$ in $r$ variables with integer coefficients, the set of natural numbers $n$
such that $p^a$ divides $\operatorname{ct}[\tilde P^n Q]$ has natural density $1$.

## Sources

- Nadav Kohen, *A Linear Representation for Constant Term Sequences mod p^a with Applications to Uniform Recurrence*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.2, Lemma 31 (`jis-2026-26.4.2-lem-31`).

articles.title: Density-one zeros of constant terms modulo $p$
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, let $P$ be a Laurent
polynomial in $r$ variables with integer coefficients, write $\operatorname{ct}[F]$ for the
constant term of a Laurent polynomial $F$, and suppose that $p$ divides $\operatorname{ct}[P^n]$
for some natural number $n$. Then for every Laurent polynomial $Q$ in $r$ variables with integer
coefficients, the set of natural numbers $n$ with $p \mid \operatorname{ct}[P^n Q]$ has natural
density $1$; for every natural number $L$ there is a natural number $i$ such that
$p \mid \operatorname{ct}[P^{i+t} Q]$ for all $t < L$; and either
$p \mid \operatorname{ct}[P^n Q]$ for every $n$, or the sequence of residues
$\operatorname{ct}[P^n Q] \bmod p$ in $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ is not uniformly recurrent.

## Sources

- Nadav Kohen, *A Linear Representation for Constant Term Sequences mod p^a with Applications to Uniform Recurrence*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.2, Theorem 14 (`jis-2026-26.4.2-thm-14`).

articles.title: Divisibility of constant terms of powers is decided on a bounded prefix
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a
prime, let $r$ and $d$ be natural numbers, and write $\operatorname{ct}[F]$ for the constant term
of a Laurent polynomial $F$ and $\deg F$ for the largest absolute value of an exponent of a single
variable in a monomial occurring in $F$ ($0$ if $F = 0$). There is a natural number $B$ such that
for every Laurent polynomial $P$ in $r$ variables with integer coefficients and $\deg P \le d$, if
$p$ divides $\operatorname{ct}[P^n]$ for some natural number $n$, then $p$ divides
$\operatorname{ct}[P^{n_0}]$ for some natural number $n_0 < B$.

## Sources

- Nadav Kohen, *A Linear Representation for Constant Term Sequences mod p^a with Applications to Uniform Recurrence*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.2, Proposition 12 (`jis-2026-26.4.2-prop-12`).

articles.title: Divisibility of constant terms of powers of $P$ and $\tilde P$
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, let
$a \ge 1$ and $\ell$ be natural numbers, and let $P$ and $\tilde P$ be Laurent polynomials in $r$
variables with integer coefficients such that $P^{p^{a-1}} \equiv \tilde P(x^{p^\ell}) \pmod{p^a}$
coefficientwise, where $\tilde P(x^q)$ is obtained from $\tilde P$ by replacing each monomial
$x^e$ with $x^{qe}$. Write $\operatorname{ct}[F]$ for the constant term of a Laurent polynomial
$F$. Then $p$ divides $\operatorname{ct}[P^{n_0}]$ for some natural number $n_0$ if and only if
$p$ divides $\operatorname{ct}[\tilde P^{n_1}]$ for some natural number $n_1$; moreover, for every
natural number $n_0$ with $p \mid \operatorname{ct}[P^{n_0}]$, also
$p \mid \operatorname{ct}[\tilde P^{n_0}]$.

## Sources

- Nadav Kohen, *A Linear Representation for Constant Term Sequences mod p^a with Applications to Uniform Recurrence*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.2, Lemma 22 (`jis-2026-26.4.2-lem-22`).

articles.title: Powers of $\tilde\gamma(0)$ modulo $p^a$ stabilize at a matrix unit
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime,
let $a \ge 1$, $r$ and $m$ be natural numbers, let $T = \{-m, \dots, m\}^r \subseteq \mathbb{Z}^r$,
and let $\tilde\gamma(0)$ be the $T \times T$ matrix over $\mathbb{Z}/p^a\mathbb{Z}$ whose
$(i, j)$ entry is $1$ if $i = p j$ and $0$ otherwise. Then there is $s \in \mathbb{N}$ such that for
every $s' \ge s$, $\tilde\gamma(0)^{s'}$ is the matrix whose $(0, 0)$ entry is $1$ and whose other
entries are $0$.

Kohen's Lemma 30 prints $\tilde\gamma(0)^s$; as in Lemma 11, it is read for every exponent
$s' \ge s$.

## Sources

- Nadav Kohen, *A Linear Representation for Constant Term Sequences mod p^a with Applications to Uniform Recurrence*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.2, Lemma 30 (`jis-2026-26.4.2-lem-30`).

articles.title: Powers of $\gamma(0)$ modulo $p$ stabilize at a matrix unit
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, let
$r, m \ge 0$ be natural numbers, let $T = \{-m, \dots, m\}^r \subseteq \mathbb{Z}^r$, and let
$\gamma(0)$ be the $T \times T$ matrix over $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ whose $(i, j)$ entry is $1$
if $i = p j$ and $0$ otherwise. Then there is $s \in \mathbb{N}$ such that for every $s' \ge s$,
$\gamma(0)^{s'}$ is the matrix whose $(0, 0)$ entry is $1$ and whose other entries are $0$.

## Sources

- Nadav Kohen, *A Linear Representation for Constant Term Sequences mod p^a with Applications to Uniform Recurrence*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.2, Lemma 11 (`jis-2026-26.4.2-lem-11`).

articles.title: Return to the initial coefficient vector modulo $p^a$
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, let
$a, m \in \mathbb{N}$, and let $\tilde P$ be a Laurent polynomial with integer coefficients in
variables $x_1, \dots, x_r$ such that for every $j \in \mathbb{Z}^r$ the coefficients of $x^j$ in
$\tilde P(x_1, \dots, x_r)^p$ and in $\tilde P(x_1^p, \dots, x_r^p)$ are congruent modulo $p^a$.
Suppose $\deg \tilde P \le m + 1$, where $\deg \tilde P$ is the largest absolute value of an
exponent of a single variable in a monomial occurring in $\tilde P$ (and $0$ if $\tilde P = 0$),
and let $T = \{-m, \dots, m\}^r$. Then there is $t_0 \in \mathbb{N}$ such that for every
$n \in \mathbb{N}$ for which $p$ does not divide the constant term of $\tilde P^n$, there is
$j < p^{t_0}$ such that for every $i \in T$ the coefficient of $x^{-i}$ in
$\tilde P^{p^{t_0} n + j}$ is congruent modulo $p^a$ to $1$ if $i = 0$ and to $0$ otherwise.

Equivalently, writing $\tilde V(n)$ for the vector of coefficients of $x^{-i}$ in $\tilde P^n$,
$i \in T$, reduced modulo $p^a$, some $\tilde V(p^{t_0} n + j)$ with $j < p^{t_0}$ equals
$\tilde V(0)$. This is the analogue modulo $p^a$ of Proposition 15.

## Sources

- Nadav Kohen, *A Linear Representation for Constant Term Sequences mod p^a with Applications to Uniform Recurrence*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.2, Proposition 32 (`jis-2026-26.4.2-prop-32`).

articles.title: Return to the initial coefficient vector modulo $p$
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, let
$m \in \mathbb{N}$, and let $P$ be a Laurent polynomial with integer coefficients in variables
$x_1, \dots, x_r$ with $\deg P \le m + 1$, where $\deg P$ is the largest absolute value of an
exponent of a single variable in a monomial occurring in $P$ (and $0$ if $P = 0$). Let
$T = \{-m, \dots, m\}^r$. Then there is $t_0 \in \mathbb{N}$ such that for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$
for which $p$ does not divide the constant term of $P^n$, there is $j < p^{t_0}$ such that for
every $i \in T$ the coefficient of $x^{-i}$ in $P^{p^{t_0} n + j}$ is congruent modulo $p$ to $1$
if $i = 0$ and to $0$ otherwise.

Equivalently, writing $V(n)$ for the vector of coefficients of $x^{-i}$ in $P^n$, $i \in T$,
reduced modulo $p$, the block $V(p^{t_0} n), \dots, V(p^{t_0} n + p^{t_0} - 1)$ contains $V(0)$.

## Sources

- Nadav Kohen, *A Linear Representation for Constant Term Sequences mod p^a with Applications to Uniform Recurrence*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.2, Proposition 15 (`jis-2026-26.4.2-prop-15`).

articles.title: Linear recurrence of combinations of constant terms modulo $p^a$
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime,
let $a \ge 1$, let $P, Q_1, \dots, Q_\ell$ be Laurent polynomials with integer coefficients in
$r$ variables, let $k_1, \dots, k_\ell \in \mathbb{N}$, and let
$F \colon (\mathbb{Z}/p^a\mathbb{Z})^\ell \to X$ be a map to a set $X$. Write
$\operatorname{ct}[f]$ for the constant term of $f$ and, for $n \in \mathbb{N}$, let
$b_n = F(\operatorname{ct}[P^{n+k_1} Q_1] \bmod p^a, \dots,
\operatorname{ct}[P^{n+k_\ell} Q_\ell] \bmod p^a)$. Suppose $b_n \ne F(0, \dots, 0)$ for some $n$.
Then $(b_n)$ is linearly recurrent if and only if $p \nmid \operatorname{ct}[P^n]$ for all
$n \in \mathbb{N}$, and if $p \mid \operatorname{ct}[P^n]$ for some $n$, then the set of $n$ with
$b_n = F(0, \dots, 0)$ has natural density $1$.

## Sources

- Nadav Kohen, *A Linear Representation for Constant Term Sequences mod p^a with Applications to Uniform Recurrence*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.2, Corollary 34 (`jis-2026-26.4.2-cor-34`).

articles.title: Linear recurrence of combinations of constant terms modulo $p$
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, let
$P, Q_1, \dots, Q_\ell$ be Laurent polynomials with integer coefficients in $r$ variables, let
$k_1, \dots, k_\ell \in \mathbb{N}$, and let $F \colon (\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^\ell \to X$ be a
map to a set $X$. Write $\operatorname{ct}[f]$ for the constant term of $f$ and, for
$n \in \mathbb{N}$, let
$b_n = F(\operatorname{ct}[P^{n+k_1} Q_1] \bmod p, \dots,
\operatorname{ct}[P^{n+k_\ell} Q_\ell] \bmod p)$.
Suppose $b_n \ne F(0, \dots, 0)$ for some $n$. Then $(b_n)$ is linearly recurrent if and only if
$p \nmid \operatorname{ct}[P^n]$ for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$, and if $p \mid \operatorname{ct}[P^n]$
for some $n$, then the set of $n$ with $b_n = F(0, \dots, 0)$ has natural density $1$.

## Sources

- Nadav Kohen, *A Linear Representation for Constant Term Sequences mod p^a with Applications to Uniform Recurrence*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.2, Corollary 17 (`jis-2026-26.4.2-cor-17`).

articles.title: Constant sequences are linearly recurrent
articles.statement:
For every set $\alpha$ and every $c \in \alpha$,
the constant sequence $n \mapsto c$ on $\mathbb{N}$ is linearly recurrent.

## Sources

- Nadav Kohen, *A Linear Representation for Constant Term Sequences mod p^a with Applications to Uniform Recurrence*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.2, Definition 1.

articles.title: Linear recurrence of constant terms modulo $p^a$
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, let $a \ge 1$, and
let $P, Q$ be Laurent polynomials with integer coefficients in $r$ variables; write
$\operatorname{ct}[f]$ for the constant term of $f$. Suppose $p^a \nmid \operatorname{ct}[P^n Q]$
for some $n \in \mathbb{N}$. Then the sequence $u_n = \operatorname{ct}[P^n Q] \bmod p^a$ is
linearly recurrent if and only if $p \nmid \operatorname{ct}[P^n]$ for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$, and
if $u$ is not linearly recurrent, then the set of $n$ with $p^a \mid \operatorname{ct}[P^n Q]$ has
natural density $1$.

In particular, as long as $u$ is not identically $0$, whether it is linearly recurrent does not
depend on $Q$ or $a$.

## Sources

- Nadav Kohen, *A Linear Representation for Constant Term Sequences mod p^a with Applications to Uniform Recurrence*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.2, Theorem 33 (`jis-2026-26.4.2-thm-33`).

articles.title: Linear recurrence of constant terms modulo $p$
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime and let $P, Q$ be
Laurent polynomials with integer coefficients in $r$ variables; write $\operatorname{ct}[f]$ for
the constant term of $f$. Suppose $p \nmid \operatorname{ct}[P^n Q]$ for some $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
Then the sequence $u_n = \operatorname{ct}[P^n Q] \bmod p$ is linearly recurrent if and only if
$p \nmid \operatorname{ct}[P^n]$ for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$, and if $u$ is not linearly recurrent,
then the set of $n$ with $p \mid \operatorname{ct}[P^n Q]$ has natural density $1$.

## Sources

- Nadav Kohen, *A Linear Representation for Constant Term Sequences mod p^a with Applications to Uniform Recurrence*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.2, Theorem 16 (`jis-2026-26.4.2-thm-16`).

articles.title: Linearly recurrent sequence
articles.statement:
A sequence $s = (s_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ with values in a
set $\alpha$ is linearly recurrent if there is $K \in \mathbb{N}$ such that for all
$i, i' \in \mathbb{N}$ and $\ell \ge 1$ with $s_{i'+t} = s_{i+t}$ for all $t < \ell$, there is $j$
with $0 < j \le K \ell$ and $s_{i'+j+t} = s_{i+t}$ for all $t < \ell$. That is, each occurrence
of a nonempty factor of length $\ell$ is followed by another occurrence starting at most
$K \ell$ positions later.

## Sources

- Nadav Kohen, *A Linear Representation for Constant Term Sequences mod p^a with Applications to Uniform Recurrence*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.2, Definition 1.

articles.title: Uniformly recurrent sequences are recurrent
articles.statement:
Every uniformly recurrent sequence
$s : \mathbb{N} \to \alpha$, with values in any type $\alpha$, is recurrent.

## Sources

- Nadav Kohen, *A Linear Representation for Constant Term Sequences mod p^a with Applications to Uniform Recurrence*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.2, Definition 1.

articles.title: Recurrence of constant-term sequences modulo a prime power
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, let
$a \ge 1$, and let $P$ and $Q$ be Laurent polynomials in $r$ variables with integer coefficients;
write $\mathrm{ct}[F]$ for the constant term of a Laurent polynomial $F$. If
$p \nmid \mathrm{ct}[P^{n_0}]$ for some $n_0 > 0$, then the sequence of residues
$(\mathrm{ct}[P^n Q] \bmod p^a)_{n \ge 0}$ in $\mathbb{Z}/p^a\mathbb{Z}$ is recurrent.

## Sources

- Nadav Kohen, *A Linear Representation for Constant Term Sequences mod p^a with Applications to Uniform Recurrence*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.2, Proposition 35 (`jis-2026-26.4.2-prop-35`).

articles.title: Recurrence of constant-term sequences modulo a prime
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime and let $P$ and
$Q$ be Laurent polynomials in $r$ variables with integer coefficients; write $\mathrm{ct}[F]$ for
the constant term of a Laurent polynomial $F$. If $p \nmid \mathrm{ct}[P^{n_0}]$ for some
$n_0 > 0$, then the sequence of residues $(\mathrm{ct}[P^n Q] \bmod p)_{n \ge 0}$ in
$\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ is recurrent.

## Sources

- Nadav Kohen, *A Linear Representation for Constant Term Sequences mod p^a with Applications to Uniform Recurrence*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.2, Proposition 19 (`jis-2026-26.4.2-prop-19`).

articles.title: Recurrent sequence
articles.statement:
A sequence $s : \mathbb{N} \to \alpha$ is recurrent if every
occurrence of a factor is followed by a later occurrence: for all $i, \ell \in \mathbb{N}$ there
is $j > 0$ such that $s(i + j + t) = s(i + t)$ for every $t < \ell$.

## Sources

- Nadav Kohen, *A Linear Representation for Constant Term Sequences mod p^a with Applications to Uniform Recurrence*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.2, definition before Proposition 19.

articles.title: Linearly recurrent sequences are uniformly recurrent
articles.statement:
Every linearly recurrent sequence
$s : \mathbb{N} \to \alpha$, with values in any type $\alpha$, is uniformly recurrent.

## Sources

- Nadav Kohen, *A Linear Representation for Constant Term Sequences mod p^a with Applications to Uniform Recurrence*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.2, Definition 1.

articles.title: Uniformly recurrent sequence
articles.statement:
A sequence $s : \mathbb{N} \to \alpha$ is uniformly
recurrent if for every factor $w$ there is a constant $C_w$ such that every occurrence of $w$ is
followed by another occurrence at distance at most $C_w$: for all $i, \ell \in \mathbb{N}$ there
is $C \in \mathbb{N}$ such that for every $i'$ with $s(i' + t) = s(i + t)$ for all $t < \ell$,
there is $j$ with $0 < j \le C$ and $s(i' + j + t) = s(i + t)$ for all $t < \ell$.

## Sources

- Nadav Kohen, *A Linear Representation for Constant Term Sequences mod p^a with Applications to Uniform Recurrence*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.2, Definition 1.

articles.title: Cartier operator applied to a power times a monomial
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime and $P$ a
Laurent polynomial in $r$ variables with integer coefficients. Write $\mathrm{coef}_e[F]$ for the
coefficient of $x^e$ in a Laurent polynomial $F$, $\deg F$ for the largest absolute value of an
exponent of a variable occurring in $F$, and $\Lambda_p$ for the Cartier operator with
$\mathrm{coef}_j[\Lambda_p F] = \mathrm{coef}_{pj}[F]$. Let $m \in \mathbb{N}$ with
$\deg P \le m + 1$, put $T = [-m, m]^r \subset \mathbb{Z}^r$, and let $k < p$ be a natural
number and $i \in T$. Then
$\Lambda_p(P^k x^i) = \sum_{j \in T} \mathrm{coef}_{pj - i}[P^k] \, x^j$.

In Kohen's notation $\mathrm{coef}_{pj - i}[P^k]$ is $a^k_{i - pj}$.

## Sources

- Nadav Kohen, *A Linear Representation for Constant Term Sequences mod p^a with Applications to Uniform Recurrence*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.2, Proposition 6 (`jis-2026-26.4.2-prop-6`).

articles.title: Cartier operator $\Lambda_k$ on Laurent polynomials
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a semiring and $f$ a
Laurent polynomial in $r$ variables with coefficients in $R$. For a natural number $k > 0$,
$\Lambda_k f$ keeps the terms of $f$ whose exponents are all multiples of $k$ and substitutes
$x_s^k \mapsto x_s$ for each variable, so that the coefficient of $x^j$ in $\Lambda_k f$ is the
coefficient of $x^{kj}$ in $f$ for every $j \in \mathbb{Z}^r$. For $k = 0$ it is set to
$\Lambda_0 f = 0$ (the paper uses only positive $k$).

## Sources

- Nadav Kohen, *A Linear Representation for Constant Term Sequences mod p^a with Applications to Uniform Recurrence*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.2, Section 2 (definition of `Λ_k`).

articles.title: Degree bound for the Rowland–Zeilberger states mod $p^a$
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, let $a$
be a natural number, and let $\tilde P$ and $Q_0$ be Laurent polynomials in $r$ variables with
coefficients in $\mathbb{Z}/p^a\mathbb{Z}$. Write $\deg F$ for the largest absolute value of an
exponent of a variable occurring in $F$, and $\Lambda_p$ for the operator that keeps the terms
whose exponents are all multiples of $p$ and substitutes $x_s^p \mapsto x_s$. For every finite
list $k_1, \dots, k_n$ of natural numbers with each $k_t < p$, starting from $Q_0$ and applying
$Q \mapsto \Lambda_p(\tilde P^{k_t} Q)$ for $t = 1, \dots, n$ in turn gives a Laurent polynomial
of degree at most $\max(\deg \tilde P - 1, \deg Q_0)$.

## Sources

- Nadav Kohen, *A Linear Representation for Constant Term Sequences mod p^a with Applications to Uniform Recurrence*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.2, Lemma 25 (`jis-2026-26.4.2-lem-25`).

articles.title: Degree bound for the Rowland–Zeilberger states
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime and let $P$ and $Q$
be Laurent polynomials in $r$ variables with integer coefficients. Write $\deg F$ for the largest
absolute value of an exponent of a variable occurring in $F$, and $\Lambda_p$ for the operator
that keeps the terms whose exponents are all multiples of $p$ and substitutes $x_s^p \mapsto x_s$.
For every finite list $k_1, \dots, k_n$ of natural numbers with each $k_t < p$, starting from $Q$
and applying $R \mapsto \Lambda_p(P^{k_t} R)$ for $t = 1, \dots, n$ in turn gives a Laurent
polynomial of degree at most $\max(\deg P - 1, \deg Q)$.

## Sources

- Nadav Kohen, *A Linear Representation for Constant Term Sequences mod p^a with Applications to Uniform Recurrence*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.2, Lemma 4 (`jis-2026-26.4.2-lem-4`).

articles.title: Exponent criterion for the degree of a Laurent polynomial
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a semiring, let
$r$ and $m$ be natural numbers, and let $f$ be a Laurent polynomial in $r$ variables
$x_1, \dots, x_r$ with coefficients in $R$. Then Kohen's degree of $f$ (the largest absolute
value of a single exponent occurring in $f$, or $0$ if there is none) is at most $m$ if and only
if every exponent vector $j \in \mathbb{Z}^r$ whose monomial $x^j$ has nonzero coefficient in
$f$ satisfies $|j_i| \le m$ for every $i$, that is, lies in $[-m, m]^r$.

## Sources

- Nadav Kohen, *A Linear Representation for Constant Term Sequences mod p^a with Applications to Uniform Recurrence*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.2, Section 1.1.

articles.title: Degree of a Laurent polynomial
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a semiring and let $f$ be a Laurent polynomial
in $r$ variables $x_1, \dots, x_r$ with coefficients in $R$. Kohen's degree $\deg f$ of $f$ is the
largest absolute value $|j_i|$ of a single exponent, taken over all $i$ and all exponent vectors
$j \in \mathbb{Z}^r$ whose monomial $x^j$ has nonzero coefficient in $f$, and is $0$ if there is
no such exponent (in particular for the zero polynomial). For example, over $\mathbb{Z}$ in two
variables $x, y$ one has $\deg(5x^{-3}y^{-2} + 2xy^{-1}) = 3$.

## Sources

- Nadav Kohen, *A Linear Representation for Constant Term Sequences mod p^a with Applications to Uniform Recurrence*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.2, Section 1.1.

articles.title: Occurrence of a sequence factor at a position
articles.statement:
Let $s = (s_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be a sequence and
let $i$, $\ell$ and $i'$ be natural numbers. The factor of $s$ of length $\ell$ starting at
position $i$ occurs at position $i'$ when $s_{i'+t} = s_{i+t}$ for every natural number $t < \ell$.

## Sources

- Nadav Kohen, *A Linear Representation for Constant Term Sequences mod p^a with Applications to Uniform Recurrence*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.2, Definition 1.

articles.title: Example of the ascending lexicographic order
articles.statement:
Write $(a_0, a_1, a_2, a_3, a_4)$ for the
coefficient function with finite support whose entry at index $i \le 4$ is $a_i$ and whose other
entries are $0$. Then $(1, 2, 10, 3, 7) \lt _a (1, 3, 1, 4, 7)$ in the ascending lexicographic
order: the largest index where they differ is $3$, where $3 < 4$.

## Sources

- Sungkon Chang, *Distribution of Zeckendorf Expressions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A25, Section 2 (arXiv:2308.12872v1, Section 2.2, example).

articles.title: Ascending lexicographic order
articles.statement:
For coefficient functions
$\mu, \nu \colon \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ with finite support, $\mu \lt _a \nu$ means that there
is an index $k$ with $\mu_k < \nu_k$ and $\mu_j = \nu_j$ for all $j > k$: at the largest index
where they differ, $\mu$ is smaller.

## Sources

- Sungkon Chang, *Distribution of Zeckendorf Expressions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A25, Section 2 (arXiv:2308.12872v1, Section 2.2).

articles.title: Powers of two are the only binary fundamental sequence
articles.statement:
Let
$H \colon \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers. Then
every natural number (including $0$) equals $\sum_{k \in s} H_k$ for exactly one finite set
$s \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ if and only if $H_k = 2^k$ for all $k$.

## Sources

- Sungkon Chang, *Distribution of Zeckendorf Expressions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A25, Lemma 1.

articles.title: The Fibonacci numbers are the only Zeckendorf fundamental sequence
articles.statement:
Let
$H \colon \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers, and
call a finite set $s \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ nonadjacent if $k \in s$ implies $k + 1 \notin s$.
Then every natural number (including $0$) equals $\sum_{k \in s} H_k$ for exactly one nonadjacent
finite set $s$ if and only if $H_k = F_{k+2}$ for all $k$, where $F_0 = 0$, $F_1 = 1$ and
$F_{n+2} = F_{n+1} + F_n$ are the Fibonacci numbers.

## Sources

- Sungkon Chang, *Distribution of Zeckendorf Expressions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A25, Lemma 1.

articles.title: Duality formula for binary expansions without adjacent ones
articles.statement:
For $x \in \mathbb{N}$ let
$z(x)$ be the number of $n < x$ whose binary expansion has no two adjacent digits equal to $1$.
For a finite set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$, put $\bar A = A$ if there is no $j$ with
$j, j + 1 \in A$, and otherwise $\bar A = \{k \in A : k \ge j\}$, where $j$ is the largest index
with $j, j + 1 \in A$. Then $z\bigl(\sum_{k \in A} 2^k\bigr) = \sum_{k \in \bar A} F_{k+2}$,
where $F_0 = 0$, $F_1 = 1$ and $F_{n+2} = F_{n+1} + F_n$ are the Fibonacci numbers.

## Sources

- Sungkon Chang, *Distribution of Zeckendorf Expressions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A25, Lemma 2.

articles.title: Continuity and local monotonicity of $\delta^{\ast}$
articles.statement:
Let $L$ and $\tilde L$ form a
periodic Zeckendorf pair, let $Q$ be a fundamental sequence of the collection $E^*$ determined by
$L$, and let $\tilde Q$ be a fundamental sequence of the collection $\tilde E^*$ determined by
$\tilde L$. Then the function $\delta^*$ built from $L, \tilde L, Q, \tilde Q$ is continuous on
$(0, 1)$, and at each point $x$ of the smooth set $U$ of $L, \tilde L, \tilde Q$ it is
differentiable and strictly decreasing on some neighbourhood of $x$.

## Sources

- Sungkon Chang, *Distribution of Zeckendorf Expressions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A25, Theorem 9.

articles.title: Proper blocks below a maximal block
articles.statement:
Let $L = (e_1, \dots, e_N)$ with $N \ge 2$ and
$e_1 \ne 0$, let $\varepsilon \colon \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and $b \in \mathbb{N}$ with
$\varepsilon_i = 0$ for all $i < b$, and let $\bar\beta$ be the maximal $L^*$-block starting at
index $b$. Then $\varepsilon \lt _d \bar\beta$ in the descending lexicographic order if and only if
there is $k \ge b$ such that the function equal to $\varepsilon_i$ for $i \le k$ and to $0$ for
$i > k$ is a proper $L^*$-block with support interval $[b, k]$.

## Sources

- Sungkon Chang, *Distribution of Zeckendorf Expressions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A25, Lemma 8 (arXiv:2308.12872v1, Section 3.3).

articles.title: Descending lexicographic order
articles.statement:
For coefficient functions
$\varepsilon, \varepsilon' \colon \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, $\varepsilon \lt _d \varepsilon'$
means that there is an index $k$ with $\varepsilon_k < \varepsilon'_k$ and
$\varepsilon_j = \varepsilon'_j$ for all $j < k$: at the smallest index where they differ,
$\varepsilon$ is smaller.

## Sources

- Sungkon Chang, *Distribution of Zeckendorf Expressions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A25, Section 2 (arXiv:2308.12872v1, Section 2.3).

articles.title: Monotonicity of the ratio under steep increments
articles.statement:
Let $L$ and $\tilde L$ form a periodic
Zeckendorf pair, let $Q$ be a fundamental sequence of the collection $E^*$ determined by $L$, and
let $\tilde Q$ be a fundamental sequence of the collection $\tilde E^*$ determined by $\tilde L$.
Put $\omega = Q_0$, $\tilde\omega = \tilde Q_0$ and $\gamma = \log_{\tilde\omega} \omega$, and let
$p$ be the generic exponent of $Q, \tilde Q$. Let $\varepsilon \in \tilde E^*$ with
$x = \sum_k \varepsilon_k \tilde Q_k \ge \tilde\omega$, and put
$y = \sum_k \overline{\mathrm{rev}}(\varepsilon)_k Q_k$, with $\overline{\mathrm{rev}}$ taken
with respect to $L$. If $\Delta x > 0$, $\Delta y > 0$ and
$(\omega / \tilde\omega)^p \le \Delta y / \Delta x$, then
$y / x^\gamma < (y + \Delta y) / (x + \Delta x)^\gamma$.

The hypothesis $x \ge \tilde\omega$ follows the reading of Lemma 17. As printed (for all
$\varepsilon \in \tilde E^*$) the lemma fails for $L = (1, 0)$, $\tilde L = (1, 1)$, $\varepsilon$
the coefficient function with a single $1$ at index $3$ ($x = 1/16$, $y = \omega^4$,
$y / x^\gamma = 1$), $\Delta x = 10^{-8}$ and $\Delta y = (\omega / \tilde\omega)^2 \Delta x$: the
right side is $0.99999999364\ldots$.

## Sources

- Sungkon Chang, *Distribution of Zeckendorf Expressions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A25, Lemma 18.

articles.title: Strict local maxima of $\delta^{\ast}$ at the closure points
articles.statement:
Let $L$ and $\tilde L$ form a
periodic Zeckendorf pair, let $Q$ be a fundamental sequence of the collection $E^*$ determined by
$L$, and let $\tilde Q$ be a fundamental sequence of the collection $\tilde E^*$ determined by
$\tilde L$. Let $\varepsilon \in \bar E^* \setminus E^*$, where $\bar E^*$ is the closure
collection of $L$, and put $x = \sum_k \varepsilon_k \tilde Q_k$. Then, for the function
$\delta^*$ built from $L, \tilde L, Q, \tilde Q$, we have $\delta^*(y) < \delta^*(x)$ for all
$y \ne x$ sufficiently close to $x$.

## Sources

- Sungkon Chang, *Distribution of Zeckendorf Expressions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A25, Proposition 8.

articles.title: Asymptotic form of the subcollection count
articles.statement:
Let $L$ and $\tilde L$ be lists of natural
numbers of length at least $2$ with nonzero first entries, and let $E$ and $\tilde E$ be the
periodic Zeckendorf collections they determine, with $E$ a proper subset of $\tilde E$. Let
$\tilde H$ be a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers such that
$\mu \mapsto \sum_k \mu_k \tilde H_k$ is a bijection from $\tilde E$ onto $\mathbb N$, and let
$z(x)$ be the number of natural numbers $n < x$ of the form $\sum_k \mu_k \tilde H_k$ with
$\mu \in E$. Then there are reals $\gamma$ and $\tilde\varphi$ with $0 < \gamma < 1$ and
$\tilde\varphi > 1$, and a continuous function $\Phi : \mathbb R \to \mathbb R$, such that
$z(x) \sim x^\gamma \Phi(\{\log_{\tilde\varphi} x\})$ as $x \to \infty$, where $\{t\}$ is the
fractional part of $t$, and $\Phi$ is differentiable at almost every point of $(0, 1)$.

## Sources

- Sungkon Chang, *Distribution of Zeckendorf Expressions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A25, Theorem 2 (arXiv:2308.12872v1, Section 1).

articles.title: Where $\delta^*$ attains its minimum
articles.statement:
**Where $\delta^*$ attains its minimum.** Let $L$ and $\tilde L$ be lists of natural numbers
of length at least $2$ with nonzero first entries whose periodic Zeckendorf collections satisfy
$E \subsetneq \tilde E$. Let $Q$ and $\tilde Q$ be fundamental sequences of the $L^*$-collections
$E^*$ of $L$ and $\tilde E^*$ of $\tilde L$, let $\delta^*$ be the function on $(0, 1)$ built from
$L$, $\tilde L$, $Q$ and $\tilde Q$, and let $p$ be the generic exponent of $Q$ and $\tilde Q$.
Indices start at $0$. Then there is $\varepsilon \in E^*$ with $\varepsilon_i = 0$ for every
$i \ge \max(2, p) - 1$ such that $\delta^*(\sum_k \varepsilon_k \tilde Q_k) \le \delta^*(y)$ for
all $y \in (0, 1)$. Moreover, if $p \le 2$, then $\delta^*(\tilde Q_0) \le \delta^*(y)$ for all
$y \in (0, 1)$ and $\delta^*(\tilde Q_0) = 1$.

## Sources

- Sungkon Chang, *Distribution of Zeckendorf Expressions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A25, Theorem 14.

articles.title: Decomposing $L^*$-blocks into $\tilde L^*$-blocks
articles.statement:
**Decomposing $L^*$-blocks into $\tilde L^*$-blocks.** Let $L$ and $\tilde L$ be lists of
natural numbers of length at least $2$ with nonzero first entries whose periodic Zeckendorf
collections satisfy $E \subsetneq \tilde E$. If $\zeta$ is a nonzero proper $L^*$-block with
support interval $[i, b]$, then $\zeta$ is a sum of disjoint proper $\tilde L^*$-blocks whose
support intervals all lie in $[0, b]$, one of which has support interval $[a, b]$ for some $a$.

## Sources

- Sungkon Chang, *Distribution of Zeckendorf Expressions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A25, Lemma 9 (arXiv:2308.12872v1, Section 3.3).

articles.title: Nearby expansions share long prefixes
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a list of natural numbers of length at
least $2$ with nonzero first entry, let $E^*$ be its $L^*$-collection, and let $Q$ be a strictly
decreasing sequence in $(0, 1)$ such that $\varepsilon \mapsto \sum_k \varepsilon_k Q_k$ is a
bijection from $E^*$ onto $(0, 1)$; indices start at $0$. Let $\varepsilon \in E^*$, put
$x = \sum_k \varepsilon_k Q_k$, and let $n \in \mathbb N$. Define $\inf(\varepsilon)$ as follows:
if $\varepsilon$ has infinitely many nonzero entries, then $\inf(\varepsilon) = \varepsilon$;
otherwise, with $c$ the largest index such that $\varepsilon_c \ne 0$, $\inf(\varepsilon)$ agrees
with $\varepsilon$ at indices below $c$, has entry $\varepsilon_c - 1$ at index $c$, and agrees
at indices above $c$ with the maximal $L^*$-block starting at index $c + 1$. Then there is
$\delta > 0$ such that every $\varepsilon' \in E^*$ with
$x < \sum_k \varepsilon'_k Q_k < x + \delta$ satisfies $\varepsilon'_i = \varepsilon_i$ for all
$i \le n$, and every $\varepsilon' \in E^*$ with $x - \delta < \sum_k \varepsilon'_k Q_k < x$
satisfies $\varepsilon'_i = \inf(\varepsilon)_i$ for all $i \le n$.

## Sources

- Sungkon Chang, *Distribution of Zeckendorf Expressions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A25, Lemma 5 (arXiv:2308.12872v1, Section 2.3).

articles.title: Power-law bounds for the subcollection count
articles.statement:
Let $L$ and $\tilde L$ be lists of natural
numbers of length at least $2$ with nonzero first entries, and let $E$ and $\tilde E$ be the
periodic Zeckendorf collections they determine, with $E$ a proper subset of $\tilde E$. Let
$\tilde H$ be a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers such that
$\mu \mapsto \sum_k \mu_k \tilde H_k$ is a bijection from $\tilde E$ onto $\mathbb N$, and let
$z(x)$ be the number of natural numbers $n < x$ of the form $\sum_k \mu_k \tilde H_k$ with
$\mu \in E$. Then there are reals $\gamma$, $a$ and $b$ with $0 < \gamma < 1$, $a > 0$ and $b > 0$
such that $a < z(x) / x^\gamma < b$ for all sufficiently large real $x$.

## Sources

- Sungkon Chang, *Distribution of Zeckendorf Expressions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A25, Theorem 1 (arXiv:2308.12872v1, Section 1, with the standing assumption of Section 3 that `E` is a proper subcollection).

articles.title: Real Zeckendorf expansions
articles.statement:
Let $L = (e_1, \dots, e_N)$ be a list of natural numbers with
$N \ge 2$ and $e_1 \ne 0$, and let $E^*$ be its $L^*$-collection; indices of coefficient functions
and sequences start at $0$. There is a unique strictly decreasing sequence $(Q_m)_{m \ge 0}$ in
$(0, 1)$ such that $\varepsilon \mapsto \sum_k \varepsilon_k Q_k$ is a bijection from $E^*$ onto
$(0, 1)$. Moreover, every such sequence $Q$ has the following properties: for
$\varepsilon, \delta \in E^*$, $\varepsilon \lt _d \delta$ (that is, $\varepsilon_k < \delta_k$ at
the smallest index $k$ where $\varepsilon$ and $\delta$ differ) if and only if
$\sum_k \varepsilon_k Q_k < \sum_k \delta_k Q_k$; for every $m$, $Q_m = \sum_k \bar\beta_k Q_k$,
where $\bar\beta$ is the maximal $L^*$-block starting at index $m + 1$; and if $\omega > 0$
satisfies $-1 + \sum_{k=1}^{N-1} e_k \omega^k + (1 + e_N) \omega^N = 0$, then
$Q_m = \omega^{m+1}$ for every $m$.

## Sources

- Sungkon Chang, *Distribution of Zeckendorf Expressions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A25, Theorem 6 (arXiv:2308.12872v1, Section 2.3, quoting Chang 2021).

articles.title: Zeckendorf collections are determined by their immediate predecessors
articles.statement:
Index
coefficient functions from $0$, and for $m \in \mathbb N$ let $\beta^{(m)}$ be the coefficient
function with entry $1$ at index $m$ and $0$ elsewhere. Suppose that for each $m \ge 1$ a finitely
supported coefficient function $\theta^{(m)}$ is given whose entry at index $m - 1$ is nonzero and
whose entries at all indices $j \ge m$ are $0$. Then there is a unique Zeckendorf collection $E$
such that, for every $m \ge 1$, $\theta^{(m)}$ is the immediate predecessor of $\beta^{(m)}$ in
$E$.

## Sources

- Sungkon Chang, *Distribution of Zeckendorf Expressions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A25, Theorem 3 (arXiv:2308.12872v1, Section 2.2, quoting Chang 2021).

articles.title: Fundamental sequences of Zeckendorf collections
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a Zeckendorf collection and
index coefficient functions and sequences from $0$. Suppose that, for each $m \ge 1$,
$\theta^{(m)}$ is the immediate predecessor in $E$ of the coefficient function with entry $1$ at
index $m$ and $0$ elsewhere. For a sequence $H$ write $\mathrm{eval}_H(\mu) = \sum_k \mu_k H_k$.
Then there is a unique strictly increasing sequence $H$ of positive integers such that
$\mathrm{eval}_H$ is a bijection from $E$ onto $\mathbb N$. Moreover, every such $H$ satisfies
$H_m = H_0 + \mathrm{eval}_H(\theta^{(m)})$ for all $m \ge 1$, and for all $\mu, \nu \in E$,
$\mu \lt _a \nu$ (that is, $\mu_k < \nu_k$ at the largest index $k$ where $\mu$ and $\nu$ differ)
if and only if $\mathrm{eval}_H(\mu) < \mathrm{eval}_H(\nu)$.

## Sources

- Sungkon Chang, *Distribution of Zeckendorf Expressions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A25, Theorem 5 (arXiv:2308.12872v1, Section 2.2, quoting Chang 2021).

articles.title: Reversals characterize the nonzero elements of $\bar E^\ast$
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a list of natural
numbers of length at least $2$ with nonzero first entry, let $E$ be the periodic Zeckendorf
collection determined by $L$, and let $\bar E^*$ be the closure of the collection $E^*$ determined
by $L$. For $n \in \mathbb N$ and a coefficient function $\varepsilon : \mathbb N \to \mathbb N$,
let $\mathrm{rev}_n(\varepsilon)$ be the finitely supported coefficient function whose first $n$
entries are the first $n$ entries of $\varepsilon$ in reverse order and whose other entries are
$0$. Then a nonzero coefficient function $\varepsilon : \mathbb N \to \mathbb N$ satisfies
$\mathrm{rev}_n(\varepsilon) \in E$ for every $n \in \mathbb N$ if and only if
$\varepsilon \in \bar E^*$.

This reads the source's Lemma 3 for nonzero $\varepsilon$ and counts $\bar\beta^1$, the maximal
$L^*$-block starting at the first index, as an element of $\bar E^*$. As printed (no
$\varepsilon \ne 0$, decompositions with at least one block) the lemma fails at
$\varepsilon = 0$, since $\mathrm{rev}_n(0) = 0 \in E$, and at $\varepsilon = \bar\beta^1$,
since $\mathrm{rev}_n(\bar\beta^1)$ is the maximal $L$-block $\theta^{n+1}$, which lies in $E$.

## Sources

- Sungkon Chang, *Distribution of Zeckendorf Expressions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A25, Lemma 3.

articles.title: Growth of fundamental sequences
articles.statement:
Let $L$ and $\tilde L$ be lists of natural numbers of
length at least $2$ with nonzero first entries, and let $E$ and $\tilde E$ be the periodic
Zeckendorf collections they determine, with $E$ a proper subset of $\tilde E$. Let $H$ and
$\tilde H$ be strictly increasing sequences of positive integers, indexed from $0$, such that
$\mu \mapsto \sum_k \mu_k H_k$ is a bijection from $E$ onto $\mathbb N$ and
$\mu \mapsto \sum_k \mu_k \tilde H_k$ is a bijection from $\tilde E$ onto $\mathbb N$. Then there
are reals $\alpha > 0$, $\tilde\alpha > 0$, $\varphi$, $\tilde\varphi$ and $r$ with
$1 < \varphi < \tilde\varphi$ and $0 < r < 1$ such that, as $n \to \infty$,
$H_n - \alpha \varphi^n = O(\varphi^{nr})$, $\tilde H_n - \tilde\alpha \tilde\varphi^n =
O(\tilde\varphi^{nr})$ and, with $\gamma = \log_{\tilde\varphi} \varphi$,
$H_n / \tilde H_n^{\gamma} \to \alpha / \tilde\alpha^{\gamma}$.

## Sources

- Sungkon Chang, *Distribution of Zeckendorf Expressions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A25, Theorem 7 (arXiv:2308.12872v1, Section 3.1).

articles.title: Generating function of the $L^\ast$-block-sum counts
articles.statement:
Let $L = (e_1, \dots, e_N)$ be a
list of natural numbers with $N \ge 2$ and $e_1 \ne 0$. For each $k$ let $C_k$ be the number of
coefficient functions that are sums of disjoint proper $L^*$-blocks with support intervals inside
$[1, k]$ (the zero function included), and put
$f(x) = 1 - \sum_{k=1}^{N-1} e_k x^k - (1 + e_N) x^N$. Then there is a real $r > 0$ such that for
every real $x$ with $-r < x < r$ the series $\sum_{k \ge 0} C_k x^k$ converges absolutely, with
sum $(1 - x^N) / f(x)$.

## Sources

- Sungkon Chang, *Distribution of Zeckendorf Expressions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A25, Proposition 5 (arXiv:2308.12872v1, Section 4.1).

articles.title: Infinitely many unit reductions stay in the $L^\ast$-closure
articles.statement:
Let
$L = (e_1, \dots, e_N)$ be a list of natural numbers with $N \ge 2$ and $e_1 \ne 0$, and let
$E^* \subseteq \bar E^*$ be the $L^*$-collection and the $L^*$-closure determined by $L$. Let
$\varepsilon \in \bar E^*$, and suppose it is not the case that $\varepsilon \in E^*$ and
$\varepsilon$ has finite support. Then there are infinitely many indices $r$ such that
$\varepsilon_r \ge 1$ and the coefficient function obtained from $\varepsilon$ by lowering its
entry at $r$ by one lies in $\bar E^*$.

## Sources

- Sungkon Chang, *Distribution of Zeckendorf Expressions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A25, Lemma 14.

articles.title: Transition from the subcollection count to $\delta^\ast$
articles.statement:
Let $L$ and $\tilde L$ form a
periodic Zeckendorf pair, with periodic Zeckendorf collections $E \subsetneq \tilde E$, and let
$Q$ and $\tilde Q$ be fundamental sequences of the $L^*$-collection $E^*$ and the
$\tilde L^*$-collection $\tilde E^*$. Put $\omega = Q_0$, $\tilde\omega = \tilde Q_0$ and
$\gamma = \log_{\tilde\omega} \omega$, and let $\delta^*$ be the function determined by $L$,
$\tilde L$, $Q$ and $\tilde Q$. Let $H$ and $\tilde H$ be strictly increasing sequences of
positive integers such that $\mu \mapsto \sum_k \mu_k H_k$ is a bijection from $E$ onto
$\mathbb N$ and $\mu \mapsto \sum_k \mu_k \tilde H_k$ is a bijection from $\tilde E$ onto
$\mathbb N$, and suppose $H_n \omega^n \to \alpha$ and
$\tilde H_n \tilde\omega^n \to \tilde\alpha$ as $n \to \infty$. For each natural number $x$ let
$\mu_x \in \tilde E$ satisfy $\sum_k (\mu_x)_k \tilde H_k = x$, let $n_x$ be one more than the
largest index in the support of $\mu_x$ ($n_x = 0$ if $\mu_x = 0$), and let $z(x)$ be the number
of natural numbers $n < x$ of the form $\sum_k \mu_k \tilde H_k$ with $\mu \in E$. Then, as
$x \to \infty$ through the natural numbers, $z(x) / x^\gamma$ is asymptotically equivalent to
$\delta^*(y_x) \, \alpha / \tilde\alpha^\gamma$, where $y_x = \sum_k \rho_k \tilde Q_k$ and
$\rho = \operatorname{rev}_{n_x}(\mu_x)$ lists the first $n_x$ entries of $\mu_x$ in reverse order.

Indices are zero-based.

## Sources

- Sungkon Chang, *Distribution of Zeckendorf Expressions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A25, Proposition 2.

articles.title: Immediate predecessor
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a collection of finitely supported coefficient functions
$\mathbb N \to \mathbb N$, and let $\lt _a$ be the ascending lexicographic order. A finitely supported
coefficient function $\mu$ is the immediate predecessor of $\nu$ in $E$ if $\mu \in E$,
$\mu \lt _a \nu$, and every $\xi \in E$ with $\xi \lt _a \nu$ satisfies $\xi = \mu$ or $\xi \lt _a \mu$.
That is, $\mu$ is the largest element of $E$ that is $\lt _a \nu$.

## Sources

- Sungkon Chang, *Distribution of Zeckendorf Expressions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A25, Section 2 (arXiv:2308.12872v1, Section 2.2).

articles.title: Immediate successor
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a collection of finitely supported coefficient functions
$\mathbb N \to \mathbb N$, and let $\lt _a$ be the ascending lexicographic order. A finitely supported
coefficient function $\nu$ is the immediate successor of $\mu$ in $E$ if $\nu \in E$,
$\mu \lt _a \nu$, and every $\xi \in E$ with $\mu \lt _a \xi$ satisfies $\xi = \nu$ or $\nu \lt _a \xi$.
That is, $\nu$ is the smallest element of $E$ that is $>_a \mu$.

## Sources

- Sungkon Chang, *Distribution of Zeckendorf Expressions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A25, Section 2 (arXiv:2308.12872v1, Section 2.2).

articles.title: L-blocks
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a list of natural numbers, and for each $m$ let $\theta^{m+1}$ be the
maximal $L$-block, which vanishes from index $m$ on (indices are zero-based). A finitely supported
coefficient function $\zeta$ is an $L$-block with support interval $[s, m - 1]$ if $1 \le m$,
$s < m$, and either $s = 0$ and $\zeta = \theta^{m+1}$, or $\zeta_i = \theta^{m+1}_i$ for every
$i > s$, $\zeta_s < \theta^{m+1}_s$ and $\zeta_i = 0$ for every $i < s$.

In the paper's indexing this is a block at index $n - 1$ with $n = m + 1 \ge 2$.

## Sources

- Sungkon Chang, *Distribution of Zeckendorf Expressions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A25, Definition 10 (arXiv:2308.12872v1, Section 2.2).

articles.title: Classification of the local extrema of $\delta^\ast$
articles.statement:
Let $L$ and $\tilde L$ form a
periodic Zeckendorf pair, let $Q$ and $\tilde Q$ be fundamental sequences of the $L^*$-collection
$E^*$ and the $\tilde L^*$-collection $\tilde E^*$, let $\bar E^*$ be the $L^*$-closure, and let
$\delta^*$ be the function determined by $L$, $\tilde L$, $Q$ and $\tilde Q$. For a coefficient
function $\varepsilon$ write $x_\varepsilon = \sum_k \varepsilon_k \tilde Q_k$. Then (i) for every
$\varepsilon \in \tilde E^*$ such that either $\varepsilon \notin \bar E^*$, or
$\varepsilon \in E^*$ and $\varepsilon$ has infinite support, $\delta^*$ has neither a local
minimum nor a local maximum at $x_\varepsilon$; (ii) for every $\varepsilon \in E^*$ with finite
support, $\delta^*$ has a local minimum at $x_\varepsilon$; and (iii) for every
$\varepsilon \in \bar E^* \setminus E^*$, $\delta^*$ has a local maximum at $x_\varepsilon$.

## Sources

- Sungkon Chang, *Distribution of Zeckendorf Expressions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A25, Theorem 12.

articles.title: Local minima of $\delta^\ast$ at finitely supported points
articles.statement:
Let $L$ and $\tilde L$ form a
periodic Zeckendorf pair, let $Q$ and $\tilde Q$ be fundamental sequences of the $L^*$-collection
$E^*$ and the $\tilde L^*$-collection $\tilde E^*$, and let $\delta^*$ be the function determined
by $L$, $\tilde L$, $Q$ and $\tilde Q$. If $\varepsilon \in E^*$ has finite support, then
$\delta^*$ has a local minimum at $\sum_k \varepsilon_k \tilde Q_k$.

## Sources

- Sungkon Chang, *Distribution of Zeckendorf Expressions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A25, Proposition 6.

articles.title: Sums of disjoint proper $L^\ast$-blocks
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a list of natural numbers, and for
each $s$ let $\bar\beta^{s+1}$ be the maximal $L^*$-block starting at (zero-based) index $s$. Let
$I$ be a finite or infinite set of pairs $(s, k)$ of natural numbers. A coefficient function
$\varepsilon : \mathbb N \to \mathbb N$ is the sum of the disjoint proper $L^*$-blocks with
support intervals $[s, k]$, $(s, k) \in I$, if $s \le k$ for every $(s, k) \in I$, the intervals
$[s, k]$ of distinct pairs in $I$ are pairwise disjoint, for every $(s, k) \in I$ we have
$\varepsilon_i = \bar\beta^{s+1}_i$ whenever $s \le i < k$ and
$\varepsilon_k < \bar\beta^{s+1}_k$, and $\varepsilon_i = 0$ for every index $i$ that lies in
none of the intervals.

## Sources

- Sungkon Chang, *Distribution of Zeckendorf Expressions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A25, Section 2 (arXiv:2308.12872v1, Section 2.3).

articles.title: Fundamental sequence of an $L^\ast$-collection
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a list of natural numbers with
$L^*$-collection $E^*$. A real sequence $(Q_n)_{n \ge 0}$ is a fundamental sequence of $E^*$ if
it is strictly decreasing, $0 < Q_n < 1$ for every $n$, and the map
$\varepsilon \mapsto \sum_k \varepsilon_k Q_k$ is a bijection from $E^*$ onto the open interval
$(0, 1)$.

## Sources

- Sungkon Chang, *Distribution of Zeckendorf Expressions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A25, Theorem 6 and Definition 18.

articles.title: Where $\delta^\ast$ can attain its maximum
articles.statement:
Let $L$ and $\tilde L$ be lists of natural
numbers forming a periodic Zeckendorf pair, let $N$ be the length of $L$, let $E^*$ and
$\tilde E^*$ be the collections determined by $L$ and $\tilde L$, let $\bar E^*$ be the closure
of $E^*$, and let $Q$ and $\tilde Q$ be fundamental sequences of $E^*$ and $\tilde E^*$. Let
$\delta^*$ be the function $\delta^*$ of $L$, $\tilde L$, $Q$, $\tilde Q$, and let $p$ be the
generic exponent of $Q$ and $\tilde Q$. Indices start at $0$: put $\omega = Q_0$ and
$\tilde\omega = \tilde Q_0$, write $\sum \varepsilon \tilde Q = \sum_k \varepsilon_k \tilde Q_k$
for a coefficient function $\varepsilon : \mathbb N \to \mathbb N$, and for $s \in \mathbb N$ let
$\bar\beta_s$ be the maximal $L^*$-block starting at index $s$. First, if $y \in (0, 1)$ and
$\delta^*(x) \le \delta^*(y)$ for all $x \in (0, 1)$, then $y = \sum \varepsilon \tilde Q$ for
some $\varepsilon \in \bar E^*$ with $\varepsilon \notin E^*$. Second, let $\ell \ge 1$ be a
natural number and let $\eta : \mathbb N \to \mathbb N$ be a sum of disjoint proper $L^*$-blocks
(possibly none) whose support intervals $[s, k]$ all satisfy $k < \ell - 1$. If
$\delta^*(x) \le \delta^*\bigl(\sum (\eta + \bar\beta_{\ell - 1}) \tilde Q\bigr)$ for all
$x \in (0, 1)$, then

$$
\ell < \max\left(2,\ p + 1 +
\frac{N \ln(1 / \omega) + \ln\left(1 - \sum \bar\beta_0 \tilde Q + \tilde\omega^N\right)}
{\ln(1 / \tilde\omega) - \ln(1 / \omega)}\right).
$$

In the source's one-based indexing $\bar\beta_s$ is $\bar\beta^{s+1}$, so the blocks
$\zeta^m$ of $\eta$ lie inside $[1, \ell - 1]$, the point is
$\sum (\sum_m \zeta^m + \bar\beta^\ell) \tilde Q$, and with $\varphi = 1 / \omega$,
$\tilde\varphi = 1 / \tilde\omega$ and $\rho = \sum \bar\beta^1 \tilde Q$ the right side is the
source's $\max\{2, p^*\}$.

## Sources

- Sungkon Chang, *Distribution of Zeckendorf Expressions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A25, Theorem 13.

articles.title: Periodic Zeckendorf pairs
articles.statement:
Two lists $L$ and $\tilde L$ of natural numbers form a periodic
Zeckendorf pair when both have length at least $2$ and a nonzero first entry, and the periodic
Zeckendorf collection $E$ determined by $L$ is a proper subset of the periodic Zeckendorf
collection $\tilde E$ determined by $\tilde L$.

This is the standing assumption of Sections 3 and 4 of the source.

## Sources

- Sungkon Chang, *Distribution of Zeckendorf Expressions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A25, Section 3.1.

articles.title: Proper $L^*$-blocks
articles.statement:
**Proper $L^*$-blocks.** Let $L$ be a list of natural numbers, index coefficient functions
from $1$, and let $\bar\beta^s$ be the maximal $L^*$-block starting at index $s$. For $s \ge 1$,
a function $\zeta : \mathbb N \to \mathbb N$ is a proper $L^*$-block with support interval
$[s, k]$ when $s \le k$, $\zeta_i = \bar\beta^s_i$ for all $i < k$, $\zeta_k < \bar\beta^s_k$,
and $\zeta_i = 0$ for all $i > k$. Since $\bar\beta^s$ vanishes below $s$, so does $\zeta$.

## Sources

- Sungkon Chang, *Distribution of Zeckendorf Expressions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A25, Section 2 (arXiv:2308.12872v1, Section 2.3).

articles.title: Periodic collections are Zeckendorf collections
articles.statement:
Let $L = (e_1, \dots, e_N)$ be a list of
natural numbers with $N \ge 2$ and $e_1 \ne 0$, and let $E$ be the periodic Zeckendorf collection
determined by $L$ (the sums of finitely many $L$-blocks with pairwise disjoint support
intervals). Index coefficient functions from $1$ and let $\beta^n$ be the basis coefficient
function with entry $1$ at index $n$. Then $E$ is a Zeckendorf collection, and for every
$n \ge 2$ the immediate predecessor of $\beta^n$ in $E$ is the maximal $L$-block $\theta^n$.

## Sources

- Sungkon Chang, *Distribution of Zeckendorf Expressions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A25, Theorem 4 (arXiv:2308.12872v1, Section 2.2, quoting Chang 2021).

articles.title: Zeckendorf collections
articles.statement:
Index coefficient functions from $1$, let $\beta^n$ be the basis
coefficient function with entry $1$ at index $n$, and for a coefficient function $\mu$ let
$\operatorname{res}_n(\mu)$ keep the entries of $\mu$ at indices $\le n$ and
$\operatorname{res}^n(\mu)$ keep those at indices $\ge n$, the other entries being $0$. A set $E$
of finitely supported coefficient functions $\mathbb N \to \mathbb N$ is a Zeckendorf collection
when it contains $0$ and $\beta^n$ for every $n \ge 1$, every $\mu \in E$ has only finitely many
elements of $E$ below it in the ascending lexicographic order $\lt _a$, and for every $\mu \in E$
and every immediate successor $\tilde\mu$ of $\mu$ in $E$ with $\tilde\mu \ne \beta^1 + \mu$
there is an index $n \ge 2$ such that $\operatorname{res}_{n-1}(\mu)$ is the immediate
predecessor of $\beta^n$ in $E$ and $\tilde\mu = \beta^n + \operatorname{res}^n(\mu)$.

## Sources

- Sungkon Chang, *Distribution of Zeckendorf Expressions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A25, Section 2 (arXiv:2308.12872v1, Section 2.2).
