articles.title: Formula for the $h$-full prime sum $\sum_P b_P$
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite field with $q$
elements, let $h, k, j \in \mathbb{N}$ and $\xi \in \mathbb{C}$, and let $\rho = q^{1/h}\xi^j$
be the pole parameter, where $q^{1/h}$ is a real power whose exponent $1/h$ is read as $0$
when $h = 0$. For a monic irreducible polynomial $P$ over $F$ put $|P| = q^{\deg P}$,
$K(P, h, j) = (1 - \rho^{-\deg P})/(|P|(1 - \rho^{-\deg P}) + 1)$ and
$b_P = |P| \, (\rho^{-1})^{k \deg P} \, K(P, h, j)$. Then the $h$-full prime sum $\sum_P b_P$
equals the sum of $b_P$ over all monic irreducible polynomials $P$ over $F$, taken to be $0$
when the family is not summable. Inverses use the convention $0^{-1} = 0$.

## Sources

- Juan Arévalo Gómez and Matilde Lalín, *Prime Factors with Given Multiplicity in h-Free and h-Full Polynomials over Function Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A9, Theorem 7.

articles.title: The $h$-full prime sum $\sum_P b_P$
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite field with $q$ elements, let
$h, k, j \in \mathbb{N}$ and $\xi \in \mathbb{C}$, and let $\rho = q^{1/h}\xi^j$ be the pole
parameter, where $q^{1/h}$ is a real power whose exponent $1/h$ is read as $0$ when $h = 0$.
For a monic irreducible polynomial $P$ over $F$ put $|P| = q^{\deg P}$,
$y_P = \rho^{-\deg P}$, $K(P, h, j) = (1 - y_P)/(|P|(1 - y_P) + 1)$ and
$b_P = |P| \, y_P^{k} \, K(P, h, j)$. The $h$-full prime sum is the complex number
$\sum_P b_P$ over all monic irreducible $P$, taken to be $0$ when the family $(b_P)$ is not
summable. Inverses use the convention $0^{-1} = 0$.

## Sources

- Juan Arévalo Gómez and Matilde Lalín, *Prime Factors with Given Multiplicity in h-Free and h-Full Polynomials over Function Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A9, Theorem 7.

articles.title: Formula for the pole parameter
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite set with $q$ elements, and let
$h, j \in \mathbb{N}$ and $\xi \in \mathbb{C}$. The pole parameter $q^{1/h}\xi^j$ equals the
real power $q^{1/h}$, whose exponent is the real number $1/h$ (read as $0$ when $h = 0$), viewed
as a complex number and multiplied by $\xi^j$.

## Sources

- Juan Arévalo Gómez and Matilde Lalín, *Prime Factors with Given Multiplicity in h-Free and h-Full Polynomials over Function Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A9, Section 4.

articles.title: The pole parameter $q^{1/h}\xi^j$
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite set with $q$ elements, and let
$h, j \in \mathbb{N}$ and $\xi \in \mathbb{C}$. The pole parameter is the complex number
$q^{1/h}\xi^j$, where $q^{1/h}$ is the nonnegative real $h$-th root of $q$ (for $h = 0$ the
exponent $1/h$ is read as $0$, so that $q^{1/h} = 1$).

When $F$ is a field, $h \ge 1$ and $\xi$ is a primitive $h$-th root of unity, the inverses
$(q^{1/h}\xi^j)^{-1}$ are the poles $u$ of $Z_q(u^h)$, where $Z_q(u) = 1/(1 - qu)$.

## Sources

- Juan Arévalo Gómez and Matilde Lalín, *Prime Factors with Given Multiplicity in h-Free and h-Full Polynomials over Function Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A9, Section 4.

articles.title: Formula for the $h$-full weighted mean
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite field with $q$ elements, let
$h, n \in \mathbb{N}$, $\xi \in \mathbb{C}$ and $X : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}$. Let
$N_h \cap M_n$ be the set of $h$-full monic polynomials of degree $n$ over $F$. For each $j$ let
$\rho_j = q^{1/h}\xi^j$ be the pole parameter and let
$\Pi_j = \prod_P (1 - 1/|P|)(1 + 1/(|P|(1 - \rho_j^{-\deg P})))$, the product over monic
irreducible $P$ with $|P| = q^{\deg P}$, taken to be $1$ when the family is not multipliable.
Then the $h$-full weighted mean of $X$ equals

$$\frac{q^{n/h}/h}{|N_h \cap M_n|} \sum_{j=0}^{h-1} \xi^{jn} \, \Pi_j \, X_j.$$

Here $q^{n/h}$ is a real power with real exponent $n/h$, and division by zero (including
$0^{-1}$) gives $0$.

## Sources

- Juan Arévalo Gómez and Matilde Lalín, *Prime Factors with Given Multiplicity in h-Free and h-Full Polynomials over Function Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A9, Theorems 5 and 7.

articles.title: The $h$-full weighted mean
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite field with $q$ elements, let
$h, n \in \mathbb{N}$, $\xi \in \mathbb{C}$ and $X : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}$. Let
$N_h \cap M_n$ be the set of $h$-full monic polynomials of degree $n$ over $F$. For each $j$ let
$\rho_j = q^{1/h}\xi^j$ be the pole parameter and let
$\Pi_j = \prod_P (1 - 1/|P|)(1 + 1/(|P|(1 - \rho_j^{-\deg P})))$, the product over monic
irreducible $P$ with $|P| = q^{\deg P}$, taken to be $1$ when the family is not multipliable.
The $h$-full weighted mean of $X$ is the complex number

$$\frac{q^{n/h}/h}{|N_h \cap M_n|} \sum_{j=0}^{h-1} \xi^{jn} \, \Pi_j \, X_j.$$

Here $q^{n/h}$ is a real power with real exponent $n/h$, and division by zero (including
$0^{-1}$) gives $0$.

It carries every $n$-dependent constant in Theorems 5 and 7.

## Sources

- Juan Arévalo Gómez and Matilde Lalín, *Prime Factors with Given Multiplicity in h-Free and h-Full Polynomials over Function Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A9, Theorems 5 and 7.

articles.title: $h$-full polynomials
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a field and $h \in \mathbb{N}$. The set $N_h$ of $h$-full
polynomials over $F$ consists of the monic polynomials $f$ such that $P^h$ divides $f$ for
every monic irreducible polynomial $P$ that divides $f$.

As in the source, theorem statements impose $h \ge 2$.

## Sources

- Juan Arévalo Gómez and Matilde Lalín, *Prime Factors with Given Multiplicity in h-Free and h-Full Polynomials over Function Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A9, Definitions.

articles.title: Normal order on a set of polynomials
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite field, let $U$ be a set of
polynomials over $F$, and let $g, G$ be real-valued functions on polynomials over $F$. For
$n \in \mathbb{N}$ let $M_n$ be the set of monic polynomials of degree $n$ over $F$. Then $g$
has normal order $G$ on $U$ when $g$ and $G$ are nonnegative on $U$, $G$ is
degree-nondecreasing on $U$ (for $f_1, f_2 \in U$, $\deg f_2 \le \deg f_1$ implies
$G(f_2) \le G(f_1)$, with $\deg$ the natural degree), and for every real $\varepsilon > 0$ the
number of $f \in U \cap M_n$ for which $(1 - \varepsilon)G(f) < g(f) < (1 + \varepsilon)G(f)$
fails is $o(|U \cap M_n|)$ as $n \to \infty$.

The paper takes $g, G : U \to \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$; here both are total real-valued functions,
with nonnegativity imposed on $U$.

## Sources

- Juan Arévalo Gómez and Matilde Lalín, *Prime Factors with Given Multiplicity in h-Free and h-Full Polynomials over Function Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A9, Theorem 3 (definition preceding the requested normal-order results).

articles.title: Constant functions are degree-nondecreasing
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a field and $U$ a set of
polynomials over $F$. For every real number $c$, the constant function with value $c$ is
degree-nondecreasing on $U$.

## Sources

- Juan Arévalo Gómez and Matilde Lalín, *Prime Factors with Given Multiplicity in h-Free and h-Full Polynomials over Function Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A9, Theorem 3 (definition preceding the requested normal-order results).

articles.title: Degree-nondecreasing functions
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a field, $U$ a set of polynomials over $F$ and
$G$ a real-valued function on polynomials over $F$. Then $G$ is degree-nondecreasing on $U$
when for all $f_1, f_2 \in U$ with $\deg f_2 \le \deg f_1$ we have $G(f_2) \le G(f_1)$. Here
$\deg$ is the natural degree, with $\deg 0 = 0$.

In particular $G$ takes the same value on members of $U$ of equal degree. The natural degree is
adequate because $U$ will consist of monic, hence nonzero, polynomials.

## Sources

- Juan Arévalo Gómez and Matilde Lalín, *Prime Factors with Given Multiplicity in h-Free and h-Full Polynomials over Function Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A9, Theorem 3 (definition preceding the requested normal-order results).

articles.title: Derivatives at $z = 1$ of uniform approximations
articles.statement:
Let $r > 0$, let $D$ be the open disk of
radius $r$ centred at $1$ in $\mathbb{C}$, and let $f$ and $G_n$ ($n \in \mathbb{N}$) be complex
functions analytic on $D$. Suppose there is a real constant $C$ such that
$|G_n(z) - f(z)\, n^{z-1}| \le C\, n^{\operatorname{Re} z - 2}$ for all $n \ge 1$ and all
$z \in D$. Then for every $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and every $\varepsilon > 0$, as $n \to \infty$,

$$G_n^{(k)}(1) - \frac{d^k}{dz^k}\big(f(z)\, n^{z-1}\big)\Big|_{z=1} = O(n^{\varepsilon - 1}).$$

This is the paper's Lemma 1, a corrected version of Lalín and Zhang's Lemma 3.2; Equation (11) is
the case $k = 1$. The paper's "analytic at $z = 1$" with an error term "in a neighborhood of
$z = 1$" is read as analyticity on a fixed disk on which the bound holds with one constant for all
$n \ge 1$.

## Sources

- Juan Arévalo Gómez and Matilde Lalín, *Prime Factors with Given Multiplicity in h-Free and h-Full Polynomials over Function Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A9, Lemma 1.

articles.title: Membership in $M_n$
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite field and $n \in \mathbb{N}$. A polynomial $f$ over
$F$ lies in the set $M_n$ of monic polynomials of degree $n$ over $F$ if and only if there are
$c_0, \dots, c_{n-1} \in F$ with $f = X^n + \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} c_i X^i$.

## Sources

- Juan Arévalo Gómez and Matilde Lalín, *Prime Factors with Given Multiplicity in h-Free and h-Full Polynomials over Function Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A9, Definitions.

articles.title: Membership in the set of monic irreducible polynomials
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a field. A polynomial $P$
over $F$ lies in the set $\mathcal{P}$ of monic irreducible polynomials over $F$ if and only if
$P$ is monic and irreducible.

## Sources

- Juan Arévalo Gómez and Matilde Lalín, *Prime Factors with Given Multiplicity in h-Free and h-Full Polynomials over Function Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A9, Definitions.

articles.title: Monic irreducible polynomials
articles.statement:
For a field $F$, $\mathcal{P}$ is the set of polynomials over
$F$ that are monic and irreducible; these are the prime polynomials of the paper.

## Sources

- Juan Arévalo Gómez and Matilde Lalín, *Prime Factors with Given Multiplicity in h-Free and h-Full Polynomials over Function Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A9, Definitions.

articles.title: Normal orders are nonnegative
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite field, $U$ a set of polynomials over $F$,
and $g, G$ real-valued functions on polynomials over $F$. If $g$ has normal order $G$ on $U$, then
$G(f) \ge 0$ for every $f \in U$.

This is the second defining clause of a normal order.

## Sources

- Juan Arévalo Gómez and Matilde Lalín, *Prime Factors with Given Multiplicity in h-Free and h-Full Polynomials over Function Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A9, Theorem 3 (definition preceding the requested normal-order results).

articles.title: Mean of $\omega_h$ over $h$-full polynomials
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite field with $q$ elements,
let $h \ge 2$, let $\xi \in \mathbb{C}$ be a primitive $h$-th root of unity, and let
$\varepsilon > 0$. Write $N_h \cap M_n$ for the set of monic polynomials $f$ of degree $n$ over $F$
that are $h$-full (if a monic irreducible $P$ divides $f$, then so does $P^h$), and $\omega_h(f)$
for the number of monic irreducible $P$ that divide $f$ exactly $h$ times. For monic irreducible
$P$ and $j < h$ put $|P| = q^{\deg P}$, $y_{P,j} = (q^{1/h}\xi^j)^{-\deg P}$ with $q^{1/h} > 0$,
and $K(P, h, j) = (1 - y_{P,j})/(|P|(1 - y_{P,j}) + 1)$. Let
$\kappa_j = \sum_P (K(P, h, j) - |P|^{-1})$ and
$\Pi_j = \prod_P (1 - |P|^{-1})(1 + |P|^{-1}(1 - y_{P,j})^{-1})$, with sum and product over monic
irreducible $P$, and for $X = (X_j)_j$ put
$W_n(X) = |N_h \cap M_n|^{-1} (q^{n/h}/h) \sum_{j=0}^{h-1} \xi^{jn} \Pi_j X_j$. Let $B_1$ be the
function field Mertens constant and $L_n = \log(n/h)$. Then, as $n \to \infty$, the mean
of $\omega_h$ over $N_h \cap M_n$ is $L_n + B_1 + W_n(\kappa) + O(n^{\varepsilon - 1})$.

## Sources

- Juan Arévalo Gómez and Matilde Lalín, *Prime Factors with Given Multiplicity in h-Free and h-Full Polynomials over Function Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A9, Theorem 5, Equation (8).

articles.title: Second moment of $\omega_h$ over $h$-full polynomials
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite field with $q$
elements, let $h \ge 2$, let $\xi \in \mathbb{C}$ be a primitive $h$-th root of unity, and let
$\varepsilon > 0$. Write $N_h \cap M_n$ for the set of monic polynomials $f$ of degree $n$ over $F$
that are $h$-full (if a monic irreducible $P$ divides $f$, then so does $P^h$), and $\omega_h(f)$
for the number of monic irreducible $P$ that divide $f$ exactly $h$ times. For monic irreducible
$P$ and $j < h$ put $|P| = q^{\deg P}$, $y_{P,j} = (q^{1/h}\xi^j)^{-\deg P}$ with $q^{1/h} > 0$,
and $K(P, h, j) = (1 - y_{P,j})/(|P|(1 - y_{P,j}) + 1)$. Let
$\kappa_j = \sum_P (K(P, h, j) - |P|^{-1})$ and
$\Pi_j = \prod_P (1 - |P|^{-1})(1 + |P|^{-1}(1 - y_{P,j})^{-1})$, with sum and product over monic
irreducible $P$, and for $X = (X_j)_j$ put

This follows the paper's proof: the printed constant term $C_3$ has $-W_n(Z)$ in place of

articles.title: Variance of $\omega_h$ over $h$-full polynomials
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite field with $q$
elements, let $h \ge 2$, let $\xi \in \mathbb{C}$ be a primitive $h$-th root of unity, and let
$\varepsilon > 0$. Write $N_h \cap M_n$ for the set of monic polynomials $f$ of degree $n$ over $F$
that are $h$-full (if a monic irreducible $P$ divides $f$, then so does $P^h$), and $\omega_h(f)$
for the number of monic irreducible $P$ that divide $f$ exactly $h$ times. For monic irreducible
$P$ and $j < h$ put $|P| = q^{\deg P}$, $y_{P,j} = (q^{1/h}\xi^j)^{-\deg P}$ with $q^{1/h} > 0$,

$\kappa_j = \sum_P (K(P, h, j) - |P|^{-1})$ and
$\Pi_j = \prod_P (1 - |P|^{-1})(1 + |P|^{-1}(1 - y_{P,j})^{-1})$, with sum and product over monic

The printed display writes $\omega_1$ for $\omega_h$ in the definition of the variance and omits
the factor $q^{n/h}/h$ in both weighted sums; both are restored as in Equations (8) and (9), from

articles.title: Mean of $\omega_k$ over $h$-free polynomials
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite field with $q$ elements,
let $h, k$ be natural numbers with $1 < k < h$, and let $\varepsilon > 0$. Write $S_h \cap M_n$ for
the set of monic polynomials $f$ of degree $n$ over $F$ that are $h$-free (no $P^h$ with $P$ monic
irreducible divides $f$), and $\omega_k(f)$ for the number of monic irreducible $P$ that divide $f$
exactly $k$ times. For monic irreducible $P$ put $|P| = q^{\deg P}$ and
$a_P = |P|^{h-k-1}(|P| - 1)/(|P|^h - 1)$, and let $S_{h,k} = \sum_P a_P$, the sum over monic
irreducible $P$. Then, as $n \to \infty$, the mean of $\omega_k$ over
$S_h \cap M_n$ is $S_{h,k} + O(q^{n/k - n + \varepsilon n})$.

## Sources

- Juan Arévalo Gómez and Matilde Lalín, *Prime Factors with Given Multiplicity in h-Free and h-Full Polynomials over Function Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A9, Theorem 3, Equation (6).

articles.title: Second moment of $\omega_k$ over $h$-free polynomials
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite field with $q$
elements, let $h, k$ be natural numbers with $1 < k < h$, and let $\varepsilon > 0$. Write
$S_h \cap M_n$ for the set of monic polynomials $f$ of degree $n$ over $F$ that are $h$-free (no
$P^h$ with $P$ monic irreducible divides $f$), and $\omega_k(f)$ for the number of monic
irreducible $P$ that divide $f$ exactly $k$ times. For monic irreducible $P$ put
$|P| = q^{\deg P}$ and $a_P = |P|^{h-k-1}(|P| - 1)/(|P|^h - 1)$, and let $S_{h,k} = \sum_P a_P$,
the sum over monic irreducible $P$. Then, as $n \to \infty$, the mean of $\omega_k^2$ over
$S_h \cap M_n$ is $S_{h,k}^2 - \sum_P a_P^2 + S_{h,k} + O(q^{n/k - n + \varepsilon n})$.

- Juan Arévalo Gómez and Matilde Lalín, *Prime Factors with Given Multiplicity in h-Free and h-Full Polynomials over Function Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A9, Theorem 3, Equation (7).

articles.title: Mean of $\omega_k$ over $h$-full polynomials for $k > h$
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite field with
$q$ elements, let $2 \le h < k$, let $\xi \in \mathbb{C}$ be a primitive $h$-th root of unity and
let $\varepsilon > 0$. Write $M_n$ for the set of monic polynomials of degree $n$ over $F$, $N_h$
for the set of $h$-full monic polynomials, $|P| = q^{\deg P}$, and $\omega_k(f)$ for the number of
monic irreducible $P$ dividing $f$ whose multiplicity in $f$ is exactly $k$. For $j < h$ and a
monic irreducible $P$ put $y_{P,j} = (q^{1/h}\xi^j)^{-\deg P}$, where $q^{1/h}$ is the positive
real root, $K(P, h, j) = (1 - y_{P,j})/(|P|(1 - y_{P,j}) + 1)$ and
$b_P(j) = |P| (q^{1/h}\xi^j)^{-k \deg P} K(P, h, j)$, and let
$\Pi_j = \prod_P (1 - 1/|P|)(1 + 1/(|P|(1 - y_{P,j})))$, where sums and products over $P$ run
over the monic irreducible polynomials. For $X = (X_0, \dots, X_{h-1}) \in \mathbb{C}^h$ let
$W_n(X) = |N_h \cap M_n|^{-1} (q^{n/h}/h) \sum_{j\lt h} \xi^{jn} \Pi_j X_j$. Then the mean of
$\omega_k$ over $N_h \cap M_n$ equals
$W_n\bigl(\sum_P b_P(0), \dots, \sum_P b_P(h-1)\bigr) + O(q^{-n/(h(h+1)) + \varepsilon n})$ as
$n \to \infty$.

## Sources

articles.title: Second moment of $\omega_k$ over $h$-full polynomials for $k > h$
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite
field with $q$ elements, let $2 \le h < k$, let $\xi \in \mathbb{C}$ be a primitive $h$-th root of
unity and let $\varepsilon > 0$. Write $M_n$ for the set of monic polynomials of degree $n$ over

$b_P(j) = |P| (q^{1/h}\xi^j)^{-k \deg P} K(P, h, j)$, and let
$\Pi_j = \prod_P (1 - 1/|P|)(1 + 1/(|P|(1 - y_{P,j})))$, where sums and products over $P$ run
over the monic irreducible polynomials. For $X = (X_0, \dots, X_{h-1}) \in \mathbb{C}^h$ let

articles.title: $\omega_k$ has no normal order on $h$-free polynomials for $1 < k < h$
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite
field, let $h \ge 2$ and $1 < k < h$, and let $S_h$ be the set of $h$-free monic polynomials over
$F$. Let $G$ be a real-valued function on polynomials over $F$ that is nonnegative on $S_h$ and
degree-nondecreasing on $S_h$, that is, $G(f_2) \le G(f_1)$ whenever $f_1, f_2 \in S_h$ and
$\deg f_2 \le \deg f_1$. Then $\omega_k$, the number of monic irreducible factors of multiplicity
exactly $k$, viewed as a real-valued function, does not have normal order $G$ on $S_h$.

Let $F$ be a finite
field, let $2 \le h < k$, and let $N_h$ be the set of $h$-full monic polynomials over $F$. Let

degree-nondecreasing on $N_h$, that is, $G(f_2) \le G(f_1)$ whenever $f_1, f_2 \in N_h$ and
$\deg f_2 \le \deg f_1$. Then $\omega_k$, the number of monic irreducible factors of multiplicity
exactly $k$, viewed as a real-valued function, does not have normal order $G$ on $N_h$.

articles.title: $\omega_k$ vanishes at the polynomial $1$
articles.statement:
For every field $F$ and every natural number $k$,
$\omega_k(1) = 0$, where $\omega_k(f)$ is the number of distinct monic irreducible polynomials
dividing a nonzero polynomial $f$ over $F$ with multiplicity exactly $k$.

The polynomial $1$ is a unit, so it has no monic irreducible factors.

## Sources

- Juan Arévalo Gómez and Matilde Lalín, *Prime Factors with Given Multiplicity in h-Free and h-Full Polynomials over Function Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A9, Definitions.

articles.title: $\omega_k$ vanishes at the zero polynomial
articles.statement:
For every field $F$ and every natural number $k$,
$\omega_k(0) = 0$. Here $\omega_k(f)$ is the number of distinct monic irreducible polynomials
dividing a nonzero polynomial $f$ over $F$ with multiplicity exactly $k$, and $\omega_k(0) = 0$
by convention, so this records that convention.

## Sources

- Juan Arévalo Gómez and Matilde Lalín, *Prime Factors with Given Multiplicity in h-Free and h-Full Polynomials over Function Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A9, Definitions.

articles.title: Number of prime factors of given multiplicity
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a field and $k \in \mathbb{N}$. For a
nonzero polynomial $f$ over $F$, $\omega_k(f)$ is the number of distinct monic irreducible
polynomials $P$ dividing $f$ whose multiplicity in $f$ (the largest $m$ with $P^m \mid f$) is
exactly $k$. For the zero polynomial, $\omega_k(0) = 0$ by convention.

## Sources

- Juan Arévalo Gómez and Matilde Lalín, *Prime Factors with Given Multiplicity in h-Free and h-Full Polynomials over Function Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A9, Definitions.

articles.title: Mean of $\omega_1$ over $h$-free polynomials
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite field with $q$ elements
and let $h \ge 2$. Let $\omega_1(f)$ be the number of monic irreducible $P$ dividing $f$ exactly
once, write $|P| = q^{\deg P}$, and let $B_1 = \gamma + \sum_P (\log(1 - 1/|P|) + 1/|P|)$ be the
function field Mertens constant, with $\gamma$ the Euler–Mascheroni constant, and let
$T_h = \sum_P (|P|^{h-1} - 1)/(|P|(|P|^h - 1))$, both sums over monic irreducible $P$. Then the
mean of $\omega_1$ over the $h$-free monic polynomials of degree $n$ over $F$ is
$\log n + B_1 - T_h + O(1/n)$ as $n \to \infty$.

## Sources

- Juan Arévalo Gómez and Matilde Lalín, *Prime Factors with Given Multiplicity in h-Free and h-Full Polynomials over Function Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A9, Theorem 1, Equation (4).

articles.title: Second moment of $\omega_1$ over $h$-free polynomials
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite field with $q$
elements, let $h \ge 2$ and let $\varepsilon > 0$. Let $\omega_1(f)$ be the number of monic
irreducible $P$ dividing $f$ exactly once, write $S_h \cap M_n$ for the set of $h$-free monic
polynomials of degree $n$ over $F$ and $|P| = q^{\deg P}$, and let
$B_1 = \gamma + \sum_P (\log(1 - 1/|P|) + 1/|P|)$ be the function field Mertens constant, with
$\gamma$ the Euler–Mascheroni constant, $T_h = \sum_P (|P|^{h-1} - 1)/(|P|(|P|^h - 1))$ and
$U_h = \sum_P (|P|^{h-2}(|P| - 1)/(|P|^h - 1))^2$, all sums over monic irreducible $P$. Then the
mean of $\omega_1^2$ over $S_h \cap M_n$ is $\log^2 n + C_2 \log n + C_3 + O(n^{\varepsilon - 1})$
as $n \to \infty$, where $C_2 = 2(B_1 - T_h) + 1$ and
$C_3 = B_1^2 + B_1 - \pi^2/6 - U_h + T_h^2 - (2B_1 + 1) T_h$.

The printed error $O_\varepsilon(q^n/n^{1-\varepsilon})$ is the error of the unnormalized sum in
the paper's proof; divided by $|S_h \cap M_n| = q^n/\zeta_q(h)$ for $n \ge h$, where
$\zeta_q(h) = (1 - q^{1-h})^{-1}$, it is $O_\varepsilon(n^{\varepsilon-1})$, the order that the
paper's remark (an extra factor $n^\varepsilon$ over the first moment's $O(1/n)$) and its
variance formula state.

## Sources

- Juan Arévalo Gómez and Matilde Lalín, *Prime Factors with Given Multiplicity in h-Free and h-Full Polynomials over Function Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A9, Theorem 1, Equation (5).

articles.title: Variance of $\omega_1$ over $h$-free polynomials
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite field with $q$
elements, let $h \ge 2$ and let $\varepsilon > 0$. Let $\omega_1(f)$ be the number of monic
irreducible $P$ dividing $f$ exactly once, write $|P| = q^{\deg P}$, and let
$B_1 = \gamma + \sum_P (\log(1 - 1/|P|) + 1/|P|)$ be the function field Mertens constant, with
$\gamma$ the Euler–Mascheroni constant, $T_h = \sum_P (|P|^{h-1} - 1)/(|P|(|P|^h - 1))$ and
$U_h = \sum_P (|P|^{h-2}(|P| - 1)/(|P|^h - 1))^2$, all sums over monic irreducible $P$. Then the
variance of $\omega_1$ over the $h$-free monic polynomials of degree $n$ over $F$, that is, the
mean of $\omega_1^2$ minus the square of the mean of $\omega_1$, is
$\log n + B_1 - \pi^2/6 - U_h - T_h + O(n^{\varepsilon - 1})$ as $n \to \infty$.

## Sources

- Juan Arévalo Gómez and Matilde Lalín, *Prime Factors with Given Multiplicity in h-Free and h-Full Polynomials over Function Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A9, Theorem 1.

articles.title: The polynomial $1$ is $h$-free
articles.statement:
For every field $F$ and every natural number $h \ge 1$,
the constant polynomial $1 \in F[X]$ is $h$-free: it is monic and no $h$-th power of a monic
irreducible polynomial divides it.

## Sources

- Juan Arévalo Gómez and Matilde Lalín, *Prime Factors with Given Multiplicity in h-Free and h-Full Polynomials over Function Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A9, Definitions.

articles.title: The polynomial $1$ is $h$-full
articles.statement:
For every field $F$ and every natural number $h$, the
constant polynomial $1 \in F[X]$ is $h$-full: it is monic, and whenever a monic irreducible
polynomial $P$ divides it, so does $P^h$.

The divisibility condition holds vacuously, since no irreducible polynomial divides $1$.

## Sources

- Juan Arévalo Gómez and Matilde Lalín, *Prime Factors with Given Multiplicity in h-Free and h-Full Polynomials over Function Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A9, Definitions.

articles.title: Perron's formula for degree slices of monic polynomials
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite field,
let $M_m$ be the set of monic polynomials of degree $m$ over $F$, let
$a \colon F[X] \to \mathbb{C}$, and write $c_m = \sum_{f \in M_m} a(f)$. Let $r$ be a real
number with $0 < r < 1$ such that the series $\sum_{m \ge 0} |c_m| r^m$ converges, and let
$A \colon \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ satisfy $A(u) = \sum_{m \ge 0} c_m u^m$ for every
complex $u$ with $|u| = r$. Then for every $n \ge 0$,

$$c_n = \frac{1}{2\pi i} \oint_{|u| = r} \frac{A(u)}{u^{n+1}}\, du,$$

where the circle $|u| = r$ is traversed once counterclockwise.

Convergence of $\sum |c_m| r^m$ at the single radius $r$ stands in for the paper's uniform
absolute convergence on the closed disk, and $A$ only has to agree with the series on the
circle, the only values the contour integral sees.

## Sources

- Juan Arévalo Gómez and Matilde Lalín, *Prime Factors with Given Multiplicity in h-Free and h-Full Polynomials over Function Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A9, Theorem 9.

articles.title: A nonzero polynomial has norm $q^{\deg f}$
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite field with $q$
elements. Every nonzero polynomial $f \in F[X]$ has norm $|f| = q^{\deg f}$.

## Sources

- Juan Arévalo Gómez and Matilde Lalín, *Prime Factors with Given Multiplicity in h-Free and h-Full Polynomials over Function Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A9, Introduction.

articles.title: The zero polynomial has norm $0$
articles.statement:
For every finite field $F$, the norm of the zero
polynomial in $F[X]$ is $|0| = 0$.

## Sources

- Juan Arévalo Gómez and Matilde Lalín, *Prime Factors with Given Multiplicity in h-Free and h-Full Polynomials over Function Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A9, Introduction.

articles.title: The polynomial norm $q^{\deg f}$ over a finite field
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite field with
$q$ elements. The norm of a polynomial $f \in F[X]$ is the real number $|f| = q^{\deg f}$ if
$f \neq 0$, and $|0| = 0$.

## Sources

- Juan Arévalo Gómez and Matilde Lalín, *Prime Factors with Given Multiplicity in h-Free and h-Full Polynomials over Function Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A9, Introduction.

articles.title: Selberg–Delange theorem, $h$-th power version
articles.statement:
Let $q > 1$ and $A > 0$ be real numbers,
let $h \ge 1$ be an integer, let $\xi$ be a primitive $h$-th root of unity in $\mathbb{C}$, and
let $B_z(n)$ and $C_z(n)$ be complex numbers, for $z \in \mathbb{C}$ and integers $n \ge 0$,
such that for all $z$ and $n$

$$C_z(n) = \sum_{\substack{0 \le a \le n \\ h \mid n - a}} B_z(a)\, q^{(n-a)/h}
\frac{(z)_{(n-a)/h}}{((n-a)/h)!},$$

where $(z)_m = z(z+1)\cdots(z+m-1)$ is the rising factorial. Suppose there is a constant $M$
such that for every complex $z$ with $|z| \le A$ the series
$\sum_{n \ge 0} |B_z(n)| (n+1)^{2A+2} q^{-n/h}$ converges and its sum is at most $M$. Then there
is a constant $K$ such that for every complex $z$ with $|z| \le A$ and every integer $n \ge 1$,

$$\left| C_z(n) - \frac{q^{n/h} n^{z-1}}{h^z \Gamma(z)} \sum_{j=0}^{h-1} \xi^{jn}
\sum_{a \ge 0} B_z(a) \left(q^{1/h} \xi^j\right)^{-a} \right|
\le K q^{n/h} n^{\operatorname{Re} z - 2}.$$

In terms of the generating functions $B(u, z) = \sum_{n \ge 0} B_z(n) u^n$ and
$C(u, z) = \sum_{n \ge 0} C_z(n) u^n$, and with $Z_q(u) = (1 - qu)^{-1}$, the hypothesis on
$C_z(n)$ says $C(u, z) = B(u, z) Z_q(u^h)^z$, and the inner sums are
$B((q^{1/h} \xi^j)^{-1}, z)$. The paper's $q$ is the size of the field. As in the case $h = 1$,
the weight is $(n+1)^{2A+2}$ rather than $n^{2A+2}$, so that $B_z(0)$ is bounded uniformly.

## Sources

- Juan Arévalo Gómez and Matilde Lalín, *Prime Factors with Given Multiplicity in h-Free and h-Full Polynomials over Function Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A9, Theorem 11.

articles.title: Selberg–Delange theorem for function fields
articles.statement:
Let $q > 1$ and $A > 0$ be real numbers,
and let $B_z(n)$ and $C_z(n)$ be complex numbers, for $z \in \mathbb{C}$ and integers $n \ge 0$,
such that for all $z$ and $n$

$$C_z(n) = \sum_{a=0}^{n} B_z(a)\, q^{n-a} \frac{(z)_{n-a}}{(n-a)!},$$

where $(z)_m = z(z+1)\cdots(z+m-1)$ is the rising factorial. Suppose there is a constant $M$
such that for every complex $z$ with $|z| \le A$ the series
$\sum_{n \ge 0} |B_z(n)| (n+1)^{2A+2} q^{-n}$ converges and its sum is at most $M$. Then there
is a constant $K$ such that for every complex $z$ with $|z| \le A$ and every integer $n \ge 1$,

$$\left| C_z(n) - \frac{q^n n^{z-1}}{\Gamma(z)} \sum_{a \ge 0} \frac{B_z(a)}{q^a} \right|
\le K q^n n^{\operatorname{Re} z - 2}.$$

In terms of the generating functions $B(u, z) = \sum_{n \ge 0} B_z(n) u^n$ and
$C(u, z) = \sum_{n \ge 0} C_z(n) u^n$, and with $Z_q(u) = (1 - qu)^{-1}$, the hypothesis on
$C_z(n)$ says $C(u, z) = B(u, z) Z_q(u)^z$, and the main term is
$q^n n^{z-1} B(1/q, z)/\Gamma(z)$. The paper's $q$ is the size of the field. The weight
$(n+1)^{2A+2}$ replaces the paper's $n^{2A+2}$: equivalent for $n \ge 1$, it also bounds
$B_z(0)$ uniformly, without which the conclusion fails (unbounded $B_z(0)$ along $z \to 2$
with $A = 2$).

## Sources

- Juan Arévalo Gómez and Matilde Lalín, *Prime Factors with Given Multiplicity in h-Free and h-Full Polynomials over Function Fields*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A9, Theorem 10.

articles.title: Size of the quotient of $F(T)$ by a nonzero polynomial
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a field and let
$f \in F[T]$ be a nonzero polynomial. Then the cardinality of the quotient ring $F[T]/(f)$ is
$|F|^{\deg f}$, where cardinalities are natural numbers and an infinite set has cardinality $0$.

## Sources

- W. Sawin and M. Shusterman, *On the Chowla and twin primes conjectures over $\mathbb{F}_q[T]$*, Annals of Math. 196 (2) 2022, Equation (1.1).

articles.title: Indicator of a statement
articles.statement:
For a proposition $P$, the indicator $\mathbf{1}_P$ is the real
number $1$ if $P$ holds and $0$ otherwise.

## Sources

- W. Sawin and M. Shusterman, *On the Chowla and twin primes conjectures over $\mathbb{F}_q[T]$*, Annals of Math. 196 (2) 2022, Equation (1.4).

articles.title: Monic polynomials of bounded norm
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite field and let $X$ be a real number.
This is the set of monic polynomials $f \in F[T]$ whose norm $|f| = |F[T]/(f)|$, the number of
elements of the quotient ring $F[T]/(f)$, satisfies $|f| \le X$.

articles.title: The norm of a polynomial is the size of its quotient ring
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite field and
give $F[T]$ its ring norm. For every $f \in F[T]$, the norm $|f|$ equals the number of elements of
the quotient ring $F[T]/(f)$, where an infinite quotient (the case $f = 0$) counts as $0$.

## Sources

- W. Sawin and M. Shusterman, *On the Chowla and twin primes conjectures over $\mathbb{F}_q[T]$*, Annals of Math. 196 (2) 2022, Equation (1.1).

articles.title: Norm of a nonzero polynomial
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite field and give $F[T]$ its ring norm.
For every nonzero $f \in F[T]$, the norm of $f$ is $|f| = |F|^{\deg f}$, where $|F|$ is the number
of elements of $F$.

## Sources

- W. Sawin and M. Shusterman, *On the Chowla and twin primes conjectures over $\mathbb{F}_q[T]$*, Annals of Math. 196 (2) 2022, Equation (1.1).

articles.title: Primes of $F(T)$
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite field. The primes of the polynomial ring $F[T]$ are
its monic irreducible polynomials.

## Sources

- W. Sawin and M. Shusterman, *On the Chowla and twin primes conjectures over $\mathbb{F}_q[T]$*, Annals of Math. 196 (2) 2022, the sentence after Equation (1.4).

articles.title: Singular series for twin primes in $F(T)$
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite field with $q$ elements and
let $h \in F[T]$. The Hardy–Littlewood constant of the prime pair $\{f, f + h\}$ is the infinite
product over all primes $P$ of $F[T]$ (the monic irreducible polynomials)

$$\mathfrak{S}_q(h) =
\prod_P \frac{1 - |P|^{-1} - |P|^{-1}\,\mathbf{1}_{P \nmid h}}{(1 - |P|^{-1})^2},$$

where $|P|$ is the norm of $P$ and $\mathbf{1}_{P \nmid h}$ is $1$ if $P$ does not divide $h$ and
$0$ otherwise.

The product is an unconditional infinite product of real numbers; when it does not converge its
value is taken to be $1$.

## Sources

- W. Sawin and M. Shusterman, *On the Chowla and twin primes conjectures over $\mathbb{F}_q[T]$*, Annals of Math. 196 (2) 2022, Equation (1.4).

articles.title: The norm on $F(T)$
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite field. The ring norm on the polynomial ring $F[T]$
sends $f$ to the number of elements of the quotient ring $F[T]/(f)$, written
$|f| = |F[T]/(f)|$; for $f = 0$ the quotient is infinite and $|0| = 0$. It is a ring norm: $|f| = 0$
only for $f = 0$, $|-f| = |f|$, $|f + g| \le |f| + |g|$ and $|fg| \le |f|\,|g|$.

## Sources

- W. Sawin and M. Shusterman, *On the Chowla and twin primes conjectures over $\mathbb{F}_q[T]$*, Annals of Math. 196 (2) 2022, Equation (1.1).

articles.title: Twin prime asymptotic over $\mathbb{F}_q(T)$ for large $q$
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be an odd prime and let
$q$ be a power of $p$ with $q > 685090\,p^2$; write $\mathbb{F}_q$ for the finite field with $q$
elements. Then there is a real number $\varepsilon > 0$ such that for every nonzero
$h \in \mathbb{F}_q[T]$, as $X \to \infty$ through the powers of $q$,

$$\#\{f \in \mathbb{F}_q[T] : |f| = X,\ f \text{ and } f + h \text{ are prime}\} =
\frac{\mathfrak{S}_q(h)\, X}{(\log_q X)^2} + O\bigl(X^{1 - \varepsilon}\bigr),$$

where $|f| = |\mathbb{F}_q[T]/(f)|$ is the norm of $f$, the primes of $\mathbb{F}_q[T]$ are its
monic irreducible polynomials, $\mathfrak{S}_q(h)$ is the singular series for twin primes, and
the implied constant may depend on $h$ (but $\varepsilon$ does not).

## Sources

- W. Sawin and M. Shusterman, `On the Chowla and twin primes conjectures over 𝔽_q[T]`, Annals of Math, 196 (2) 2022. Statement taken from https://github.com/ImperialCollegeLondon/AnnalsChallenge. Problem `annals_chowla_and_twin_prime_over_fq_t` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Chowla's conjecture over $\mathbb{F}_q(T)$ for large $q$
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be an odd prime, let $k \ge 1$
be a natural number, and let $q$ be a power of $p$ with $q > p^2 k^2 e^2$, where $e$ is Euler's
number; write $\mathbb{F}_q$ for the finite field with $q$ elements. Let
$h_1, \dots, h_k \in \mathbb{F}_q[T]$ be distinct polynomials. Then, as the real number $X$ tends
to $\infty$,

$$\sum_{f \text{ monic},\ |f| \le X} \mu(f + h_1)\,\mu(f + h_2) \cdots \mu(f + h_k) = o(X),$$

where the sum runs over the monic $f \in \mathbb{F}_q[T]$ of norm $|f| = |\mathbb{F}_q[T]/(f)|$ at
most $X$, and $\mu$ is the Möbius function of $\mathbb{F}_q[T]$: $\mu(g) = (-1)^r$ if $g$ is
squarefree with $r$ irreducible factors, and $\mu(g) = 0$ otherwise.

## Sources

- W. Sawin and M. Shusterman, `On the Chowla and twin primes conjectures over 𝔽_q[T]`, Annals of Math, 196 (2) 2022. Statement taken from https://github.com/ImperialCollegeLondon/AnnalsChallenge. Problem `annals_chowla_and_twin_prime_over_fq_t` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Absolute logarithmic height from the algebraic Mahler measure
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field of
characteristic zero that is an algebra over $\mathbb{Q}$, and let $x \in K$ be algebraic over
$\mathbb{Q}$. Let $d$ be the degree of the minimal polynomial of $x$ over $\mathbb{Q}$, and let
$M(x)$ be the algebraic Mahler measure of $x$, the Mahler measure of the positive primitive
integral minimal polynomial of $x$ regarded as a complex polynomial. Then the absolute
logarithmic height of $x$ equals $\log M(x) / d$.

articles.title: Logarithmic height from the roots of the minimal polynomial, for an algebraic element
articles.statement:
Let
$K$ be a field of characteristic zero and let $x \in K$ be algebraic over $\mathbb{Q}$. Let $d$ be
the degree of the minimal polynomial of $x$ over $\mathbb{Q}$, and let $P_x \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ be
the primitive integral minimal polynomial of $x$, with leading coefficient $a$. Then the absolute
logarithmic height of $x$ is

$$h(x) = \frac{1}{d}\Big(\log |a| + \sum_{z} \log^+ |z|\Big),$$

where the sum runs over the complex roots $z$ of $P_x$, counted with multiplicity, and
$\log^+ t = \max(0, \log t)$.

articles.title: Logarithmic height from the roots of the minimal polynomial
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field of
characteristic zero that is algebraic over $\mathbb{Q}$, and let $x \in K$. Let $d$ be the degree
of the minimal polynomial of $x$ over $\mathbb{Q}$, and let $P_x \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ be the
primitive integral minimal polynomial of $x$, with leading coefficient $a$. Then the absolute
logarithmic height of $x$ is

$$h(x) = \frac{1}{d}\Big(\log |a| + \sum_{z} \log^+ |z|\Big),$$

where the sum runs over the complex roots $z$ of $P_x$, counted with multiplicity, and
$\log^+ t = \max(0, \log t)$.

## Sources

- arXiv:2608.15903; equivalent formulas occur in arXiv:2304.11607, 2309.11173, 2311.13047, 2311.14001, 2607.25168, 2608.04445, and 2608.20995.

articles.title: Logarithmic height from the roots of the minimal polynomial, for an integral element
articles.statement:
Let
$K$ be a field of characteristic zero and let $x \in K$ be integral over $\mathbb{Q}$. Let $d$ be
the degree of the minimal polynomial of $x$ over $\mathbb{Q}$, and let $P_x \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ be
the primitive integral minimal polynomial of $x$, with leading coefficient $a$. Then the absolute
logarithmic height of $x$ is

$$h(x) = \frac{1}{d}\Big(\log |a| + \sum_{z} \log^+ |z|\Big),$$

where the sum runs over the complex roots $z$ of $P_x$, counted with multiplicity, and
$\log^+ t = \max(0, \log t)$.

articles.title: Multiplicative height as a Mahler measure, for an integral element
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field of
characteristic zero and let $x \in K$ be integral over $\mathbb{Q}$. Let $d$ be the degree of the
minimal polynomial of $x$ over $\mathbb{Q}$, and let $P_x \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ be the primitive
integral minimal polynomial of $x$. Then the absolute multiplicative height of $x$ is
$H(x) = M(P_x)^{1/d}$, where $M(P_x)$ is the Mahler measure of $P_x$ regarded as a polynomial
with complex coefficients.

articles.title: Absolute multiplicative height as a Mahler measure
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field of characteristic
zero that is algebraic over $\mathbb{Q}$, and let $x \in K$. Let $d$ be the degree of the minimal
polynomial of $x$ over $\mathbb{Q}$, and let $P_x \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ be the primitive integral
minimal polynomial of $x$. Then the absolute multiplicative height of $x$ is $H(x) = M(P_x)^{1/d}$,
where $M(P_x)$ is the Mahler measure of $P_x$ regarded as a polynomial with complex coefficients.

## Sources

- arXiv:2608.15891, lines 205–217; equivalent formulations also occur in arXiv:2306.11331, 2307.11849, 2307.14915, 2312.04354, 2607.28857, 2607.29208, and 2608.11904.

articles.title: The sign normalization does not change the Mahler measure
articles.statement:
For every element $x$ of a
field $K$ that is an algebra over $\mathbb{Q}$, the algebraic Mahler measure of $x$, that is the
Mahler measure of the positive primitive integral minimal polynomial of $x$, equals the Mahler
measure of the primitive integral minimal polynomial of $x$, both polynomials being regarded as
polynomials with complex coefficients.

articles.title: Algebraic Mahler measure
articles.statement:
For an element $x$ of a field $K$ that is an algebra over
$\mathbb{Q}$, the algebraic Mahler measure $M(x)$ is the Mahler measure of the positive primitive
integral minimal polynomial of $x$, regarded as a polynomial with complex coefficients. If $x$ is
not algebraic over $\mathbb{Q}$, this polynomial is the constant $1$, so $M(x) = 1$.

articles.title: One plus the logarithm of a Mahler measure above one is below it
articles.statement:
Let $x$ be an element
of a field $K$ that is an algebra over $\mathbb{Q}$, and let $M(x)$ be its algebraic Mahler
measure. If $M(x) > 1$, then $1 + \log M(x) < M(x)$.

Voutier uses this elementary inequality to pass from lower bounds for $\log M(x)$ to lower bounds
for $M(x)$.

articles.title: The algebraic Mahler measure is at least one
articles.statement:
For every element $x$ of a field $K$ that
is an algebra over $\mathbb{Q}$, the algebraic Mahler measure $M(x)$ of $x$ satisfies
$1 \le M(x)$.

This holds because the positive primitive integral minimal polynomial of $x$ has a positive
integer leading coefficient.

articles.title: An algebraic element is a root of its positive primitive integral minimal polynomial
articles.statement:
Let
$K$ be a field of characteristic zero that is an algebra over $\mathbb{Q}$, and let $x \in K$ be
algebraic over $\mathbb{Q}$. Then the positive primitive integral minimal polynomial of $x$, with
its integer coefficients mapped into $K$, vanishes at $x$.

articles.title: The positive primitive integral minimal polynomial is primitive
articles.statement:
For every element $x$ of
a field $K$ that is an algebra over $\mathbb{Q}$, the positive primitive integral minimal
polynomial of $x$ is primitive: the greatest common divisor of its integer coefficients is $1$.

articles.title: The positive primitive integral minimal polynomial has positive leading coefficient
articles.statement:
For
every element $x$ of a field $K$ that is an algebra over $\mathbb{Q}$, the leading coefficient of
the positive primitive integral minimal polynomial of $x$ is a strictly positive integer.

articles.title: The positive primitive integral minimal polynomial has the degree of the minimal polynomial
articles.statement:
**The positive primitive integral minimal polynomial has the degree of the minimal
polynomial.** For every element $x$ of a field $K$ that is an algebra over $\mathbb{Q}$, the
positive primitive integral minimal polynomial of $x$ has the same degree as the minimal
polynomial of $x$ over $\mathbb{Q}$.

Degrees are natural numbers, the zero polynomial having degree $0$; if $x$ is not algebraic over
$\mathbb{Q}$, both degrees are $0$.

articles.title: Sign normalization preserves the degree
articles.statement:
For every element $x$ of a field $K$ that is an
algebra over $\mathbb{Q}$, the positive primitive integral minimal polynomial of $x$ has the same
degree as the primitive integral minimal polynomial of $x$.

articles.title: The positive primitive integral minimal polynomial is nonzero
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field
that is a $\mathbb{Q}$-algebra. For every $x \in K$, the positive primitive integral minimal
polynomial of $x$ is not the zero polynomial.

articles.title: Positive primitive integral minimal polynomial
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field that is a
$\mathbb{Q}$-algebra, let $x \in K$, and let $p$ be the canonical primitive integral minimal
polynomial of $x$. The positive primitive integral minimal polynomial of $x$ is $-p$ if the
leading coefficient of $p$ is negative, and $p$ otherwise.

Since $p$ is nonzero, the result has positive leading coefficient. When $x$ is not algebraic
over $\mathbb{Q}$, $p$ is the constant polynomial $1$, and so is the result.

articles.title: Primitive integral minimal polynomial
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field that is an algebra over
$\mathbb{Q}$, let $x \in K$, and let $m_x \in \mathbb{Q}[X]$ be the minimal polynomial of $x$
over $\mathbb{Q}$, with $m_x = 0$ when $x$ is not algebraic over $\mathbb{Q}$. Choose a nonzero
integer $b$ such that $b\,m_x$ has integer coefficients. The primitive integral minimal polynomial
$P_x \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ of $x$ is the primitive part of $b\,m_x$: when $b\,m_x \neq 0$ it is
$b\,m_x$ divided by the nonnegative greatest common divisor of its coefficients, and when
$b\,m_x = 0$ it is $1$.

Thus for algebraic $x$, $P_x$ is a primitive polynomial with integer coefficients that is a
nonzero rational multiple of $m_x$, determined up to sign, and for nonalgebraic $x$, $P_x = 1$.
The sign is immaterial for applications to Mahler measure.

articles.title: Upper bounds for the asymptotic Dobrowolski constant
articles.statement:
For every extended real number $b$,
the asymptotic Dobrowolski constant is at most $b$ if and only if every real asymptotic
Dobrowolski coefficient $c$ satisfies $c \le b$.

articles.title: Trivial upper bound for the asymptotic Dobrowolski constant
articles.statement:
The asymptotic Dobrowolski
constant is at most $+\infty$.

This is only the trivial bound in the extended reals, not a finite estimate.

articles.title: The asymptotic Dobrowolski constant is nonnegative
articles.statement:
The asymptotic Dobrowolski constant
is at least $0$.

The bound comes from the coefficient $0$, which is an asymptotic Dobrowolski coefficient because
every Mahler measure is at least $1$.

articles.title: Asymptotic Dobrowolski constant
articles.statement:
The asymptotic Dobrowolski constant is the supremum, in
the extended real numbers $[-\infty, +\infty]$, of the set of all real asymptotic Dobrowolski
coefficients.

The supremum would be $-\infty$ if there were no coefficient and is $+\infty$ if the coefficients
are unbounded above; neither attainment nor a finite upper bound is assumed.

articles.title: Blanksby–Montgomery lower bound for the Mahler measure
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a nonzero complex
number that is algebraic over $\mathbb{Q}$ and is not a root of unity, and let $d$ be the degree
of its minimal polynomial over $\mathbb{Q}$. If $d \ge 2$, then the algebraic Mahler measure
$M(\alpha)$ satisfies $M(\alpha) > 1 + \frac{1}{52\, d \log(6d)}$, with $\log$ the natural
logarithm.

## Sources

- Blanksby--Montgomery, the strict degree-dependent bound quoted by Voutier.

articles.title: Cantor–Straus lower bound for the asymptotic Dobrowolski constant
articles.statement:
The asymptotic
Dobrowolski constant is at least $2$, as an extended real number.

## Sources

- Cantor--Straus (1982), as reported by Voutier, coefficient `2`.

articles.title: Coefficients are bounded by the asymptotic Dobrowolski constant
articles.statement:
Every real asymptotic
Dobrowolski coefficient $c$ satisfies $c \le$ the asymptotic Dobrowolski constant, as extended
real numbers.

articles.title: Dobrowolski's lower bound for the asymptotic Dobrowolski constant
articles.statement:
The asymptotic
Dobrowolski constant is at least $1$, as an extended real number.

## Sources

- Dobrowolski (1979), as reported by Voutier, coefficient `1`.

articles.title: Positivity of the Dobrowolski scale
articles.statement:
For every natural number $d \ge 3$, the Dobrowolski
scale $\left(\frac{\log \log d}{\log d}\right)^3$ is strictly positive.

articles.title: Dobrowolski scale
articles.statement:
For a natural number $d$, the Dobrowolski scale is

$$\left(\frac{\log \log d}{\log d}\right)^3,$$

with natural logarithms and the conventions $\log 0 = 0$ and $x / 0 = 0$, so that it is $0$ for
$d \le 1$.

It is used only for degrees $d \ge 3$ in the definition of asymptotic Dobrowolski coefficients.

articles.title: Strict form of asymptotic Dobrowolski coefficients
articles.statement:
A real number $c$ is an asymptotic
Dobrowolski coefficient if and only if for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there is a natural number
$D \ge 3$ such that every nonzero algebraic number $\alpha \in \mathbb{C}$ that is not a root of
unity and whose minimal polynomial over $\mathbb{Q}$ has degree $d \ge D$ satisfies

$$1 + (c - \varepsilon) \left(\frac{\log \log d}{\log d}\right)^3 < M(\alpha),$$

where $M(\alpha)$ is the Mahler measure of $\alpha$.

So the strict bounds are equivalent to the non-strict bounds in the definition.

articles.title: Coefficients are exactly the reals below the constant
articles.statement:
A real number $c$ is an asymptotic
Dobrowolski coefficient if and only if $c$ is at most the asymptotic Dobrowolski constant, as
extended real numbers.

The $\varepsilon$ in the definition makes the set of coefficients closed, so a finite constant is
itself a coefficient; this also covers the case where the coefficients are unbounded above.

articles.title: Asymptotic Dobrowolski coefficients
articles.statement:
A real number $c$ is an asymptotic Dobrowolski
coefficient if for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there is a natural number $D \ge 3$ such that every
nonzero algebraic number $\alpha \in \mathbb{C}$ that is not a root of unity and whose minimal
polynomial over $\mathbb{Q}$ has degree $d \ge D$ satisfies

$$1 + (c - \varepsilon) \left(\frac{\log \log d}{\log d}\right)^3 \le M(\alpha),$$

where $M(\alpha)$ is the Mahler measure of $\alpha$.

The degree threshold $D$ may depend on $\varepsilon$ but is uniform over all such $\alpha$.

articles.title: Louboutin's lower bound for the asymptotic Dobrowolski constant
articles.statement:
The asymptotic
Dobrowolski constant is at least $9/4$, as an extended real number.

## Sources

- Louboutin (1983), as reported by Voutier, coefficient `9/4`.

articles.title: Stewart's lower bound for the Mahler measure
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a nonzero complex number
that is algebraic over $\mathbb{Q}$ and is not a root of unity, and let $d$ be the degree of its
minimal polynomial over $\mathbb{Q}$. If $d \ge 2$, then the algebraic Mahler measure $M(\alpha)$
satisfies $M(\alpha) > 1 + \frac{1}{10000\, d \log d}$, with $\log$ the natural logarithm.

## Sources

- Stewart (1978), the strict degree-dependent bound quoted by Voutier.

articles.title: Zero is an asymptotic Dobrowolski coefficient
articles.statement:
The real number $0$ is an asymptotic
Dobrowolski coefficient: for every real $\varepsilon > 0$ there is a natural number $D \ge 3$
such that every nonzero algebraic number $\alpha \in \mathbb{C}$ that is not a root of unity and
whose minimal polynomial over $\mathbb{Q}$ has degree $d \ge D$ satisfies
$1 - \varepsilon \left(\frac{\log \log d}{\log d}\right)^3 \le M(\alpha)$, where $M(\alpha)$ is the
Mahler measure of the primitive integer minimal polynomial of $\alpha$ with positive leading
coefficient.

articles.title: Real cyclotomic integers with house between 2 and 76/33
articles.statement:
Let $n \ge 1$, let $K$ be a number
field that is a cyclotomic extension of $\mathbb{Q}$ generated by the $n$-th roots of unity, and
let $\beta \in K$ be an algebraic integer lying in the maximal real subfield of $K$. Write
$\operatorname{house}(\beta)$ for the largest absolute value of the images of $\beta$ under the
complex embeddings of $K$. If $2 < \operatorname{house}(\beta) < 76/33$, then
$\operatorname{house}(\beta)$ is one of $(\sqrt{7} + \sqrt{3})/2$, $\sqrt{5}$,
$1 + 2\cos(2\pi/7)$, $(1 + \sqrt{5})/\sqrt{2}$ and $(1 + \sqrt{13})/2$.

## Sources

- https://arxiv.org/pdf/1004.0665. Problem `cyclotomic_integer_house_between_two_and_76_33` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Real cyclotomic integers with house at most 2
articles.statement:
Let $n \ge 1$, let $K$ be a number field
that is a cyclotomic extension of $\mathbb{Q}$ generated by the $n$-th roots of unity, and let
$\beta \in K$ be an algebraic integer lying in the maximal real subfield of $K$. Write
$\operatorname{house}(\beta)$ for the largest absolute value of the images of $\beta$ under the
complex embeddings of $K$. If $\operatorname{house}(\beta) \le 2$, then
$\operatorname{house}(\beta) = 2$ or $\operatorname{house}(\beta) = 2\cos(\pi/m)$ for some
integer $m \ge 1$.

## Sources

- https://arxiv.org/pdf/1004.0665. Problem `cyclotomic_integer_house_le_two` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Dimitrov's lower bound for the house of an algebraic integer
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field
and let $\alpha \in K$ be a nonzero algebraic integer that is not a root of unity. Let $d'$ be
the number of distinct values of the argument $\arg \sigma(\alpha)$ as $\sigma$ ranges over the
ring homomorphisms $K \to \mathbb{C}$. Then the house of $\alpha$, the maximum of
$|\sigma(\alpha)|$ over these $\sigma$, is at least $2^{1/(4d')}$.

## Sources

- James McKee and Chris Smyth, Around the Unit Circle, Chapter 4, Theorem 4.1; Vesselin Dimitrov (2019). Problem `dimitrov` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Mahler measure of Lehmer's polynomial
articles.statement:
The Mahler measure of Lehmer's polynomial is at most
$1176281/1000000 = 1.176281$.

## Sources

- Lehmer (1933), the Mahler measure of Lehmer's polynomial is `1.176280818...`, hence at most `1.176281`. No root-location computation for the degree-ten example is formalized here.

articles.title: Mahler measure of a monic linear integer polynomial
articles.statement:
For every integer $a$, the
Mahler measure of the integer polynomial $X - a$ is $\max(1, |a|)$.

articles.title: Mahler measure of $X - 1$
articles.statement:
The integer polynomial $X - 1$ has Mahler measure $1$.

Since $1$ is not strictly larger than $1$, this value is excluded from the set whose
infimum is Lehmer's constant.

articles.title: Mahler measure of $X - 2$
articles.statement:
The integer polynomial $X - 2$ has Mahler measure $2$.

Since $2 > 1$, this value lies in the set whose infimum is Lehmer's constant.

articles.title: Mahler measure of an integer polynomial
articles.statement:
The Mahler measure of $f \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$
is the Mahler measure of its image in $\mathbb{C}[X]$. It equals
$|a| \prod_i \max(1, |\alpha_i|)$, where $a$ is the leading coefficient of $f$ and the
$\alpha_i$ are the complex roots of $f$ counted with multiplicity.

articles.title: Reciprocal polynomial
articles.statement:
An integer polynomial $f$ is reciprocal when reversing its
coefficients gives $f$ or $-f$, that is, when $X^d f(1/X) = f$ or $X^d f(1/X) = -f$, where $d$
is the degree of $f$, taken to be $0$ when $f = 0$.

articles.title: Lehmer's upper bound for Lehmer's constant
articles.statement:
Lehmer's constant is at most
$1176281/1000000 = 1.176281$.

## Sources

- Lehmer (1933), catalogue upper bound `C₄₀ₐ ≤ 1.176280...` from the Mahler measure of Lehmer's polynomial, rounded up at the sixth decimal place.

articles.title: Lehmer's question in terms of Lehmer's constant
articles.statement:
Lehmer's constant equals $1$ if and
only if Lehmer's question has a positive answer, that is, for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there is
an integer polynomial whose Mahler measure lies strictly between $1$ and $1 + \varepsilon$.

articles.title: Lehmer's constant bounds every Mahler measure above $1$
articles.statement:
For every integer polynomial
$f$ whose Mahler measure is strictly larger than $1$, Lehmer's constant is at most the Mahler
measure of $f$.

articles.title: Lehmer's constant is at most $2$
articles.statement:
Lehmer's constant $C_{40a}$ satisfies
$C_{40a} \le 2$.

The witness is the integer polynomial $X - 2$, whose Mahler measure is $2$.

articles.title: Lehmer's constant
articles.statement:
Writing $M(f)$ for the Mahler measure of an integer polynomial $f$,
Lehmer's constant is
$C_{40a} = \inf \{M(f) : f \in \mathbb{Z}[X],\ M(f) > 1\}$,
the infimum of the Mahler measures of integer polynomials that are strictly larger than $1$.

articles.title: Lehmer's polynomial
articles.statement:
Lehmer's polynomial is the integer polynomial
$X^{10} + X^9 - X^7 - X^6 - X^5 - X^4 - X^3 + X + 1$.

Lehmer found it in 1933. Its Mahler measure $1.176280\ldots$ is still the smallest known
Mahler measure larger than $1$.

articles.title: Lehmer's question
articles.statement:
The proposition that there are integer polynomials with
Mahler measure arbitrarily close to $1$ from above: for every real $\varepsilon > 0$ there is a
polynomial $f \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ whose Mahler measure $M(f)$ satisfies $1 < M(f) < 1 + \varepsilon$.

Lehmer asked in 1933 whether this proposition holds.

articles.title: Mahler measures above one
articles.statement:
This is the set of real numbers of the form $M(f)$, where
$f \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ is an integer polynomial whose Mahler measure $M(f)$ is strictly larger
than $1$.

articles.title: Nonzero integer polynomials have Mahler measure at least one
articles.statement:
If
$f \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ is a nonzero polynomial, then its Mahler measure satisfies $M(f) \ge 1$.

Indeed, $M(f) = |a| \prod_i \max(1, |\alpha_i|)$, where the leading coefficient $a$ of $f$ is a
nonzero integer and the $\alpha_i$ are the complex roots of $f$ counted with multiplicity, so
every factor is at least $1$.

articles.title: Lehmer's constant is at least one
articles.statement:
Lehmer's constant $L$, the infimum of the Mahler
measures strictly larger than $1$ of polynomials in $\mathbb{Z}[X]$, satisfies $1 \le L$.

This is the lower bound recorded in the catalogue for the constant $C_{40a}$.

articles.title: Smyth's theorem for nonreciprocal polynomials
articles.statement:
Let $f \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ be an integer
polynomial that is not reciprocal and whose constant term $f(0)$ is nonzero. Then the Mahler
measure of $f$ is at least the Mahler measure of Smyth's polynomial $X^3 - X - 1$.

## Sources

- Smyth (1971), as quoted in the catalogue: a nonreciprocal integer polynomial with nonzero constant term has Mahler measure at least that of `X^3 - X - 1` (the plastic number `1.324717...`).

articles.title: Smyth's polynomial
articles.statement:
Smyth's polynomial is $X^3 - X - 1 \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$.

Its Mahler measure is the plastic number $\theta_0 = 1.324717\ldots$, the real root of
$X^3 - X - 1$. Smyth proved in 1971 that every polynomial $f \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ with
$f(0) \neq 0$ that is nonreciprocal (reversing its coefficients gives neither $f$ nor $-f$)
has Mahler measure at least $\theta_0$.

articles.title: Identification of one-variable Laurent polynomials
articles.statement:
The $\mathbb{C}$-algebra isomorphism
from complex Laurent polynomials whose exponents are vectors $e \in \mathbb{Z}^1$ (functions
$\{0\} \to \mathbb{Z}$) to complex Laurent polynomials $\mathbb{C}[T, T^{-1}]$ in one variable,
induced by the additive isomorphism $\mathbb{Z}^1 \cong \mathbb{Z}$, $e \mapsto e(0)$. Writing
$X^{e}$ for the monomial with exponent vector $e$, it sends $c\,X^{e}$ to $c\,T^{e(0)}$.

articles.title: Integer vectors of length one
articles.statement:
The additive isomorphism from $\mathbb{Z}^1$, the group of
functions $\{0\} \to \mathbb{Z}$ under pointwise addition, to $\mathbb{Z}$ that sends a function
$e$ to its value $e(0)$.

articles.title: Logarithmic Mahler measure
articles.statement:
For a complex Laurent polynomial $F$ in $m$ variables, the
logarithmic Mahler measure of $F$ is the real number
$(2\pi)^{-m} \int_{[0, 2\pi]^m} \log |F(e^{i\theta_1}, \dots, e^{i\theta_m})| \, d\theta$,
the integral taken with respect to Lebesgue measure.

The cited source applies this formula to nonzero polynomials. As with Mathlib's logarithmic
Mahler measure of one-variable polynomials, the definition here is total: $\log 0 = 0$ and a
non-integrable function has integral $0$, so in particular the value at $F = 0$ is $0$.

articles.title: Normalized box integral
articles.statement:
For a function $f \colon \mathbb{R}^m \to \mathbb{R}$, the
normalized box integral of $f$ is $(2\pi)^{-m} \int_{[0, 2\pi]^m} f(x) \, dx$, the integral taken
with respect to Lebesgue measure (and equal to $0$ when $f$ is not integrable on the box).

articles.title: Phase of an exponent vector
articles.statement:
For an angle vector $\theta \in \mathbb{R}^n$ and an exponent
vector $e \in \mathbb{Z}^n$, the real phase of $e$ at $\theta$ is $\sum_{j} e_j \theta_j$.

articles.title: Torus character as a monoid homomorphism
articles.statement:
For an angle vector $\theta \in \mathbb{R}^n$,
the torus character $e \mapsto \exp\bigl(i \sum_{j} e_j \theta_j\bigr)$, viewed as a map from the
additive group $\mathbb{Z}^n$ written multiplicatively to the multiplicative monoid of
$\mathbb{C}$, is a monoid homomorphism: it sends $0$ to $1$ and sums to products.

articles.title: Torus character
articles.statement:
For an angle vector $\theta \in \mathbb{R}^n$, the torus character at
$\theta$ sends an exponent vector $e \in \mathbb{Z}^n$ to
$\exp\bigl(i \sum_{j} e_j \theta_j\bigr) \in \mathbb{C}$.

articles.title: Evaluation on the unit torus
articles.statement:
For an angle vector $\theta \in \mathbb{R}^n$, evaluation at
the point $(\exp(i\theta_1), \dots, \exp(i\theta_n))$ of the unit torus is the
$\mathbb{C}$-algebra homomorphism from complex Laurent polynomials in $n$ variables to
$\mathbb{C}$ that, writing $X^e$ for the monomial with exponent vector $e \in \mathbb{Z}^n$,
sends $\sum_e c_e X^e$ to $\sum_e c_e \exp\bigl(i \sum_{j} e_j \theta_j\bigr)$.

articles.title: Pisot number
articles.statement:
A Pisot number is a real algebraic integer greater than one whose other complex
conjugates all have norm less than one.

articles.title: Unique Pisot root of a polynomial
articles.statement:
Let $P$ be a polynomial with real coefficients and $r$ a
real number. Then $r$ is the unique Pisot root of $P$ when $r$ is a Pisot number with $P(r) = 0$
and every Pisot number $s$ with $P(s) = 0$ equals $r$.

articles.title: Absolute trace of a totally positive algebraic integer is at least one
articles.statement:
For every
complex number $\alpha$ that is a totally positive algebraic integer, the absolute trace of
$\alpha$ is at least $1$.

## Sources

- catalogue trivial lower row, by AM--GM: the absolute trace is at least the geometric mean of the conjugates, whose product is a nonzero rational integer.

articles.title: Positivity of the absolute trace
articles.statement:
If a complex number $\alpha$ is a totally positive
algebraic integer, then the absolute trace of $\alpha$ is strictly positive.

articles.title: Absolute trace
articles.statement:
The absolute trace of a complex number $\alpha$ is the real number
obtained by dividing the real part of the trace of $\alpha$ by the degree of $\alpha$. If
$\alpha$ is transcendental, its trace and its degree are both $0$, and its absolute trace is
taken to be $0$.

For algebraic $\alpha$ the trace is real, and for a totally positive algebraic integer $\alpha$
the absolute trace is the mean of the conjugates of $\alpha$.

articles.title: Classical upper bound for the Schur–Siegel–Smyth constant
articles.statement:
The Schur–Siegel–Smyth trace
constant $C_{86}$, an extended real number, satisfies $C_{86} \le 2$.

## Sources

- classical upper bound `C₈₆ ≤ 2`, from the totally positive algebraic integers `4 cos^2 (π / n)` whose absolute traces tend to `2`.

articles.title: Admissible bounds lie below the Schur–Siegel–Smyth constant
articles.statement:
Let $C_{86}$ be the
Schur–Siegel–Smyth trace constant, an extended real number. Every admissible real number $\rho$
satisfies $\rho \le C_{86}$ in the extended reals.

articles.title: Conjugates
articles.statement:
The conjugates of a complex number $\alpha$ are the roots in $\mathbb{C}$ of
its minimal polynomial over $\mathbb{Q}$, counted with multiplicity. If $\alpha$ is
transcendental, its minimal polynomial is taken to be $0$ and it has no conjugates.

articles.title: Degree of a complex number over the rationals
articles.statement:
For a complex number $\alpha$, the degree
$\deg(\alpha)$ is the natural number given by the degree of the minimal polynomial of $\alpha$ over
$\mathbb{Q}$. When $\alpha$ is transcendental its minimal polynomial is $0$ by convention, so
$\deg(\alpha) = 0$.

articles.title: Degree of a complex number
articles.statement:
The degree of a complex number $\alpha$ is the degree of its
minimal polynomial over $\mathbb{Q}$. If $\alpha$ is transcendental, its minimal polynomial is
taken to be $0$, so its degree is $0$.

articles.title: Admissible trace bounds
articles.statement:
A real number $\rho$ is admissible when $\rho \ge 0$ and only
finitely many totally positive algebraic integers $\alpha \in \mathbb{C}$ have absolute trace
less than $\rho$.

articles.title: Totally positive algebraic numbers
articles.statement:
A complex number $\alpha$ is totally positive if it is
algebraic over $\mathbb{Q}$ and every complex root of its minimal polynomial over $\mathbb{Q}$,
that is, every conjugate of $\alpha$, is a positive real number.

articles.title: One is a totally positive algebraic integer
articles.statement:
The complex number $1$ is a totally
positive algebraic integer.

articles.title: Totally positive algebraic integers
articles.statement:
A complex number $\alpha$ is a totally positive
algebraic integer when it is integral over $\mathbb{Z}$ and every conjugate of $\alpha$ (every
root in $\mathbb{C}$ of its minimal polynomial over $\mathbb{Q}$) is a strictly positive real
number.

articles.title: The Schur–Siegel–Smyth constant $\lambda_{\mathrm{SSS}}$
articles.statement:
Let $\lambda_{\mathrm{SSS}}$ be
the supremum in $\mathbb{R}$ of the set of real numbers $\lambda$ such that, for every
$\varepsilon > 0$, only finitely many complex numbers $\alpha$ are totally positive algebraic
integers with $\operatorname{tr}(\alpha) < (\lambda - \varepsilon) \deg(\alpha)$, where
$\operatorname{tr}(\alpha)$ and $\deg(\alpha)$ are the trace and the degree of $\alpha$ over
$\mathbb{Q}$ (the trace of a totally positive $\alpha$ is real). By the convention for suprema in
$\mathbb{R}$, $\lambda_{\mathrm{SSS}} = 0$ if this set is empty or unbounded above.

The set is closed downwards and contains its supremum when it is nonempty and bounded above, so
$\lambda_{\mathrm{SSS}}$ is then the greatest such $\lambda$. The source says "least real number",
but this is a typo, as the set has no lower bound. The greatest real number agrees with Orloski,
Sardari and Smith, "New lower bounds for the Schur-Siegel-Smyth trace problem"
(arXiv:2401.03252), where $\lambda_{\mathrm{SSS}}$ is the limit inferior of
$\operatorname{tr}(\alpha)/\deg(\alpha)$ over all totally positive algebraic integers $\alpha$.

articles.title: Minimal polynomial of one
articles.statement:
The minimal polynomial of $1 \in \mathbb{C}$ over $\mathbb{Q}$
is $X - 1$.

articles.title: Orloski–Sardari–Smith lower bound for the Schur–Siegel–Smyth constant
articles.statement:
The
Schur–Siegel–Smyth trace constant $C_{86}$, an extended real number, satisfies
$1.80203 \le C_{86}$.

## Sources

- Orloski--Sardari--Smith (2025), best known lower bound `1.80203 ≤ C₈₆`.

articles.title: Sardari–Orloski upper bound for the Schur–Siegel–Smyth constant
articles.statement:
The Schur–Siegel–Smyth
trace constant $C_{86}$, an extended real number, satisfies $C_{86} \le 1.8216$.

## Sources

- Sardari--Orloski (2024), best known upper bound `C₈₆ ≤ 1.8216` from explicit limiting measures.

articles.title: Schur's lower bound for the Schur–Siegel–Smyth constant
articles.statement:
The Schur–Siegel–Smyth trace
constant $C_{86}$, an extended real number, satisfies $\sqrt{e} \le C_{86}$.

## Sources

- Schur (1918), lower bound `√e ≤ C₈₆`.

articles.title: Upper bounds for the Schur–Siegel–Smyth constant
articles.statement:
For every extended real number $b$, the
Schur–Siegel–Smyth trace constant is at most $b$ if and only if every admissible real number
$c$ satisfies $c \le b$.

articles.title: Schur–Siegel–Smyth trace constant
articles.statement:
The Schur–Siegel–Smyth trace constant $C_{86}$ is
the supremum, taken in the extended reals, of the admissible real bounds: the real numbers
$\rho \ge 0$ such that only finitely many complex numbers that are totally positive algebraic
integers have absolute trace less than $\rho$.

The extended-real value is $-\infty$ for an empty admissible set and $+\infty$ for an unbounded
one; finiteness is the content of the known upper bounds.

articles.title: Smith's upper bound for the Schur–Siegel–Smyth trace constant
articles.statement:
The
Schur–Siegel–Smyth trace constant $C_{86}$, an extended real number, satisfies
$C_{86} < 1.89831$.

## Sources

- Smith (2024), strict upper bound `C₈₆ < 1.89831` (the form of Smith's theorem recorded in the neighbouring `AlgebraicIntegersWanted` file as `lambda_SSS < 1.89831`), disproving the conjectured value `2`: infinitely many totally positive algebraic integers have absolute trace below `1.89831`.

articles.title: Smyth's lower bound for the Schur–Siegel–Smyth constant
articles.statement:
The Schur–Siegel–Smyth trace
constant $C_{86}$, an extended real number, satisfies $1.7719 \le C_{86}$.

## Sources

- Smyth (1984), auxiliary-function lower bound `1.7719 ≤ C₈₆`.

articles.title: Smith's theorem on the Schur–Siegel–Smyth trace problem
articles.statement:
The Schur–Siegel–Smyth constant
satisfies $\lambda_{\mathrm{SSS}} < 1.89831$; this is Theorem 1.1 of the source.

## Sources

- A. Smith, `Algebraic integers with conjugates in a prescribed distribution`, Annals of Math, 200 (1) 2024. Statement taken from https://github.com/ImperialCollegeLondon/AnnalsChallenge. Problem `annals_algebraic_integers` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Sum of the conjugates of a complex number
articles.statement:
For a complex number $\alpha$, the trace
$\operatorname{tr}(\alpha) \in \mathbb{C}$ is the sum, counted with multiplicity, of the complex
roots of the minimal polynomial of $\alpha$ over $\mathbb{Q}$. When $\alpha$ is algebraic these
roots are the conjugates $\alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_n$ of $\alpha$, so
$\operatorname{tr}(\alpha) = \alpha_1 + \dots + \alpha_n$; when $\alpha$ is transcendental its
minimal polynomial is $0$ by convention and $\operatorname{tr}(\alpha) = 0$.

articles.title: The trace of a totally positive algebraic integer is real
articles.statement:
If $\alpha \in \mathbb{C}$ is
a totally positive algebraic integer, then the imaginary part of the trace of $\alpha$ is $0$.

articles.title: The trace of a totally positive algebraic integer has positive real part
articles.statement:
If
$\alpha \in \mathbb{C}$ is a totally positive algebraic integer, then the real part of the trace
of $\alpha$ is strictly positive.

articles.title: Trace as the sum of conjugates
articles.statement:
For $\alpha \in \mathbb{C}$, the trace of $\alpha$ is
the sum of its conjugates, that is, of the roots in $\mathbb{C}$ of the minimal polynomial of
$\alpha$ over $\mathbb{Q}$, counted with multiplicity. For transcendental $\alpha$ there are no
conjugates and the trace is $0$.

articles.title: Arithmetic term for the gcd in base $5$
articles.statement:
For all natural numbers $a, b \ge 1$,

$$
\gcd(a, b) + 1 = \left\lfloor \frac{5^{ab(ab+a+b)}}{(5^{a^2 b} - 1)(5^{a b^2} - 1)} \right\rfloor
\bmod 5^{ab},
$$

that is, $\gcd(a, b)$ is one less than the remainder of this floor modulo $5^{ab}$.

## Sources

- Mihai Prunescu and Joseph M. Shunia, *Arithmetic-Term Representations for the Greatest Common Divisor*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A96, Theorem 1.

articles.title: The gcd terms in bases $2$, $3$ and $4$
articles.statement:
Let $c \in \{2, 3, 4\}$, let $a, b \ge 1$ be
natural numbers, and put $E = ab(ab + a + b)$ and $D = (c^{a^2 b} - 1)(c^{a b^2} - 1)$. Then the
identity

$$
\gcd(a, b) = \left( \lfloor c^E / D \rfloor \bmod c^{ab} \right) - 1
$$

holds if and only if $(a, b) \ne (1, 1)$, and the identity

$$
\gcd(a, b) = \big( ((-c^E) \bmod D) \bmod c^{ab} \big) - 2
$$

holds if and only if $(a, b) \ne (1, 1)$. Both identities are read in the integers, where
$x \bmod m$ is the remainder of $x$ in $\{0, \dots, m - 1\}$ for $m > 0$, also when $x < 0$.

## Sources

- Mihai Prunescu and Joseph M. Shunia, *Arithmetic-Term Representations for the Greatest Common Divisor*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A96, Corollary 2.

articles.title: Second arithmetic term for the gcd in base $5$
articles.statement:
For all natural numbers $a, b \ge 1$,

$$
\gcd(a, b) = \Big( \big( (-5^{ab(ab+a+b)}) \bmod \big( (5^{a^2 b} - 1)(5^{a b^2} - 1) \big) \big)
\bmod 5^{ab} \Big) - 2
$$

in the integers, where $x \bmod m$ is the remainder of $x$ in $\{0, \dots, m - 1\}$ for $m > 0$,
also when $x < 0$.

## Sources

- Mihai Prunescu and Joseph M. Shunia, *Arithmetic-Term Representations for the Greatest Common Divisor*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A96, Corollary 1.

articles.title: The gcd-term sequence is bounded by $n + 1$
articles.statement:
Let $a, b \ge 1$ be natural numbers, at least
one of them greater than $1$, and let $s_{a,b}$ be the gcd-term sequence. For every natural
number $n$, $s_{a,b}(n) \le s_{1,1}(n) = n + 1$, and $s_{a,b}(n) = s_{1,1}(n)$ only if $n = 0$.

## Sources

- Mihai Prunescu and Joseph M. Shunia, *Arithmetic-Term Representations for the Greatest Common Divisor*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A96, Lemma 5.

articles.title: The gcd-term sequence is integral and recovers the gcd
articles.statement:
Let $a, b \ge 1$ be natural
numbers and let $s_{a,b}$ be the gcd-term sequence. Every value $s_{a,b}(n)$ is a natural number,
and $s_{a,b}(ab) = \gcd(a, b) + 1$.

## Sources

- Mihai Prunescu and Joseph M. Shunia, *Arithmetic-Term Representations for the Greatest Common Divisor*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A96, Lemma 4.

articles.title: Initial value of the gcd-term sequence
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $a, b \ge 1$, the gcd-term
sequence satisfies $s_{a,b}(0) = 1$.

## Sources

- Prunescu and Shunia, *Arithmetic-Term Representations for the Greatest Common Divisor*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A96, Section 2.

articles.title: The gcd-term sequence
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $a$, $b$ and $n$, $s_{a,b}(n)$ is the rational
number that is the coefficient of $z^n$ in the inverse of the formal power series
$(z^a - 1)(z^b - 1)$ over $\mathbb{Q}$. For $a, b \ge 1$ this series has constant coefficient $1$,
so $s_{a,b}$ is the coefficient sequence of $f_{a,b}(z) = 1 / ((z^a - 1)(z^b - 1))$. If $a = 0$
or $b = 0$ the series is $0$, whose inverse is taken to be $0$, so $s_{a,b}(n) = 0$.

## Sources

- Mihai Prunescu and Joseph M. Shunia, *Arithmetic-Term Representations for the Greatest Common Divisor*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A96, Section 2 (definition of `s_{a,b}`).

articles.title: Generating function of the gcd-term sequence
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $a, b \ge 1$, in the
ring $\mathbb{Q}[[z]]$ of formal power series, the gcd-term sequence $s_{a,b}$ satisfies

$$
(z^a - 1)(z^b - 1) \sum_{n \ge 0} s_{a,b}(n) z^n = 1.
$$

## Sources

- Prunescu and Shunia, *Arithmetic-Term Representations for the Greatest Common Divisor*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A96, Section 2.

articles.title: The set $T_0$ is nonnegative
articles.statement:
Every element of the set $T_0$ of reals $n / 3^k$, where
$n$ and $k$ are natural numbers, $n$ is stable and $\lVert n \rVert = 3k + 2$ (with
$\lVert n \rVert$ the integer complexity of $n$), is a nonnegative real number.

## Sources

- J. Arias de Reyna, *Arithmetical Self-Similar Compact Sets*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A21, Section 3, equation (7).

articles.title: The set $T_0$ built from stable numbers
articles.statement:
Write $\lVert n \rVert$ for the integer complexity
of a natural number $n$, and call $n$ stable when $n > 0$ and
$\lVert 3^k n \rVert = \lVert n \rVert + 3k$ for every natural number $k$. The set
$T_0 \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ consists of the reals $n / 3^k$, where $n$ and $k$ are natural numbers,
$n$ is stable and $\lVert n \rVert = 3k + 2$.

## Sources

- J. Arias de Reyna, *Arithmetical Self-Similar Compact Sets*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A21, Section 3, equation (7).

articles.title: The closure of $T_0$ is an arithmetical compact set (Theorem 2)
articles.statement:
Let $T_0$ be the set of
reals $n / 3^k$, where $n$ and $k$ are natural numbers, $n$ is stable and
$\lVert n \rVert = 3k + 2$ (with $\lVert n \rVert$ the integer complexity of $n$), and let $K$ be
the closure of $T_0$ in $\mathbb{R}$. Then $K$ is an arithmetical compact set of module $3$ and
ratio $3$, and for every natural number $n \ge 1$ the stability gauge $\lVert n \rVert_K$ of $K$
with module $3$ and ratio $3$ equals the stable complexity $\lVert n \rVert_{\mathrm{st}}$.

## Sources

- J. Arias de Reyna, *Arithmetical Self-Similar Compact Sets*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A21, Theorem 2.

articles.title: Derived sets of an arithmetical compact set are arithmetical (Proposition 7)
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be
an arithmetical compact set of module $\mu$ and ratio $\rho$. For every natural number $n$, the
$n$-th derived set $K^{(n)}$ of $K$ (the set of accumulation points, iterated $n$ times, so that
$K^{(0)} = K$) is an arithmetical compact set of module $\mu$ and ratio $\rho$.

## Sources

- J. Arias de Reyna, *Arithmetical Self-Similar Compact Sets*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A21, Proposition 7.

articles.title: Arithmetical compact sets
articles.statement:
Let $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ and let $\mu$ and $\rho$ be natural
numbers. For each natural number $j$ let $K^{(j)}$ be the $j$-th iterated derived set (the set of
accumulation points, iterated $j$ times) of $K$ and $T_j = K^{(j)} \setminus K^{(j+1)}$ its $j$-th
layer, and for a natural number $m$ let $\lVert m \rVert_K$ be the stability gauge of $K$ with
module $\mu$ and ratio $\rho$ at $m$. Then $K$ is an arithmetical compact set of module $\mu$ and
ratio $\rho$ when $K$ is a quasi-arithmetical compact set of module $\mu$ and ratio $\rho$ and the
following holds for every family of maps $\alpha \mapsto T_j[\alpha]$ ($j \in \mathbb{N}$), each
strictly decreasing on the ordinals $\alpha < \omega^\omega$ and mapping them onto $T_j$: for every
$j \in \mathbb{N}$, every ordinal $\alpha < \omega^\omega$ and all natural numbers $n$ and $k$ with
$\rho \nmid n$ and $T_{j+1}[\alpha] = n / \rho^k$, the sets
$\{T_j[\omega \alpha + r] : r \in \mathbb{N}\}$ and
$\{b (a \rho^r + 1) / \rho^{r+k} : a, b, r \in \mathbb{N},\ n = ab,\
\lVert n \rVert_K = \lVert a \rVert_K + \lVert b \rVert_K\}$ have finite symmetric difference.

Such an enumeration of a layer is unique when it exists; by Proposition 3 each layer has order
type $\omega^\omega$.

## Sources

- J. Arias de Reyna, *Arithmetical Self-Similar Compact Sets*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A21, Definition 4, displays (4) and (5).

articles.title: Stable numbers for integer complexity
articles.statement:
A natural number $n$ is stable when $n > 0$ and
$\lVert 3^k n \rVert = \lVert n \rVert + 3k$ for every natural number $k$, where $\lVert m \rVert$
is the integer complexity of $m$.

The paper quantifies over $k \ge 1$; the case $k = 0$ holds trivially.

## Sources

- J. Arias de Reyna, *Arithmetical Self-Similar Compact Sets*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A21, Section 1.

articles.title: Arithmetical compact sets are quasi-arithmetical
articles.statement:
If $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ is an
arithmetical compact set of module $\mu$ and ratio $\rho$, then $K$ is a quasi-arithmetical
compact set of module $\mu$ and ratio $\rho$.

## Sources

- J. Arias de Reyna, *Arithmetical Self-Similar Compact Sets*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A21, Definition 4.

articles.title: Multiplying by the ratio raises the gauge index by the module (Proposition 6)
articles.statement:
Let
$K \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be a quasi-arithmetical compact set of module $\mu$ and ratio $\rho$. For
each natural number $j$ let $K^{(j)}$ be the $j$-th iterated derived set of $K$ and
$T_j = K^{(j)} \setminus K^{(j+1)}$ its $j$-th layer. If $n, \ell, u, \ell', u'$ are natural
numbers with $n / \rho^\ell \in T_u$ and $\rho n / \rho^{\ell'} \in T_{u'}$, then
$\ell' \mu - u' = \ell \mu - u + \mu$ as integers.
