and $p, s \in \mathbb{N}$. The $([k]; p; s)$-generalized Padovan–Perrin recurrence is the linear
recurrence of order $s + p$ with coefficients $c_i = [i = 0] \, k_2 + [i = p] \, k_1$ for
$0 \le i < s + p$, where $[\cdot]$ is $1$ if the condition holds and $0$ otherwise: a sequence
$v \colon \mathbb{N} \to R$ solves it when $v_{n+s+p} = \sum_{i=0}^{s+p-1} c_i v_{n+i}$ for every
$n \ge 0$. For $s > 0$ this reads $v_{n+s+p} = k_1 v_{n+p} + k_2 v_n$, that is,
$v_n = k_1 v_{n-s} + k_2 v_{n-s-p}$ for $n \ge s + p$ (equation (1)).

## Sources

- Elen Viviani Pereira Spreafico, Mustapha Rachidi, and Paula Maria Machado Cruz Catarino, *On a Model of (k;p;s)-Generalized Padovan-Perrin and Fibonacci Fundamental System*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A49, equation (1).

articles.title: Recurrence for the generalized Padovan–Perrin coefficients ρ
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative
semiring, $k_1, k_2 \in R$, and $p, s \in \mathbb{N}$ with $s > 0$, and write $\rho(m, s+p)$ for
the Padovan–Perrin coefficient. For every $n \ge 0$,

$$\rho(n + s + p + 1, s + p) = k_1 \, \rho(n + p + 1, s + p) + k_2 \, \rho(n + 1, s + p),$$

that is, $\rho(m, s+p) = k_1 \rho(m - s, s+p) + k_2 \rho(m - s - p, s+p)$ for every $m > s + p$.

Together with $\rho(m, s+p) = 0$ for $m < s + p$ and $\rho(s+p, s+p) = 1$, this determines $\rho$.

## Sources

- Elen Viviani Pereira Spreafico, Mustapha Rachidi, and Paula Maria Machado Cruz Catarino, *On a Model of (k;p;s)-Generalized Padovan-Perrin and Fibonacci Fundamental System*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A49, equation (12) and Proposition 4.

articles.title: Root formula for the generalized Padovan–Perrin coefficients ρ
articles.statement:
Let $k_1, k_2$ be complex
numbers with $k_2 \neq 0$, let $p, s \ge 1$, and let $P(z) = z^{s+p} - k_1 z^p - k_2$. If $P$ is
separable, that is, has $s + p$ distinct roots $\lambda_1, \dots, \lambda_{s+p}$ in $\mathbb{C}$,
then for every $n \ge s + p$ the Padovan–Perrin coefficient satisfies

$$\rho(n, s + p) = \sum_{i=1}^{s+p} \frac{\lambda_i^{n-1}}{P'(\lambda_i)}.$$

The paper states this for the general $\rho$ of formula (12) attached to an arbitrary
characteristic polynomial $z^r - a_0 z^{r-1} - \cdots - a_{r-1}$; this is its specialization to
the $([k]; p; s)$-Padovan–Perrin coefficients, the case the paper applies.

## Sources

- Elen Viviani Pereira Spreafico, Mustapha Rachidi, and Paula Maria Machado Cruz Catarino, *On a Model of (k;p;s)-Generalized Padovan-Perrin and Fibonacci Fundamental System*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A49, Lemma 5.

articles.title: The Padovan–Perrin coefficients vanish below the order
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative
semiring, let $k_1, k_2 \in R$ and let $p, s, n$ be natural numbers with $n < s + p$. Then the
Padovan–Perrin coefficient $\rho(n, s + p)$ attached to $k_1, k_2, p, s$ equals $0$.

## Sources

- Elen Viviani Pereira Spreafico, Mustapha Rachidi, and Paula Maria Machado Cruz Catarino, *On a Model of (k;p;s)-Generalized Padovan-Perrin and Fibonacci Fundamental System*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A49, Proposition 4.

articles.title: The Padovan–Perrin coefficient $\rho(12, 3)$ equals $5$
articles.statement:
Over the integers, with
$k_1 = k_2 = 1$, $p = 1$ and $s = 2$ (the Padovan–Perrin recurrence $v_n = v_{n-2} + v_{n-3}$),
the coefficient $\rho(12, 3)$ equals $5$.

## Sources

- Elen Viviani Pereira Spreafico, Mustapha Rachidi, and Paula Maria Machado Cruz Catarino, *On a Model of (k;p;s)-Generalized Padovan-Perrin and Fibonacci Fundamental System*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A49, equation (14) and Table 1.

articles.title: Normalization of the Padovan–Perrin coefficients
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative semiring, let
$k_1, k_2 \in R$ and let $p, s$ be natural numbers with $s > 0$. Then the Padovan–Perrin
coefficient $\rho(s + p, s + p)$ attached to $k_1, k_2, p, s$ equals $1$.

## Sources

- Elen Viviani Pereira Spreafico, Mustapha Rachidi, and Paula Maria Machado Cruz Catarino, *On a Model of (k;p;s)-Generalized Padovan-Perrin and Fibonacci Fundamental System*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A49, Proposition 4.

articles.title: Padovan–Perrin coefficients
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative semiring, let $k_1, k_2 \in R$ and
let $p, s, n$ be natural numbers. The coefficient $\rho(n, s + p)$ attached to $k_1, k_2, p, s$ is
$0$ when $n < s + p$; when $n \ge s + p$ it is the sum of $\binom{a + b}{a} k_1^a k_2^b$ over all
pairs of natural numbers $a, b \le n$ with $s a + (s + p) b = n - (s + p)$. For $s > 0$ the bounds
$a, b \le n$ hold automatically.

For $s > 0$ this is the coefficient $\rho(n, r)$, $r = s + p$, of the paper's general formula (12)
for the recurrence $v_n = k_1 v_{n-s} + k_2 v_{n-s-p}$. The paper's Proposition 4 prints the
constraint as $s a + (s + p) b = n - (s + p - 1)$, which contradicts its own normalization
$\rho(s + p, s + p) = 1$ for $s \ge 2$; the constraint used here is the one of formula (12).

## Sources

- Elen Viviani Pereira Spreafico, Mustapha Rachidi, and Paula Maria Machado Cruz Catarino, *On a Model of (k;p;s)-Generalized Padovan-Perrin and Fibonacci Fundamental System*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A49, equation (12) and Proposition 4.

articles.title: Solutions agreeing on a window agree afterwards
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let
$k_1, k_2 \in R$, let $p, s$ be natural numbers and let $v, w \colon \mathbb{N} \to R$ be solutions
of the Padovan–Perrin recurrence with parameters $k_1, k_2, p, s$. Let $n_0, m_0, N$ be natural
numbers such that $v(j + n_0) = w(j + m_0)$ for every $j$ with $N \le j < N + s + p$. Then
$v(n + n_0) = w(n + m_0)$ for every $n \ge N$.

## Sources

- Elen Viviani Pereira Spreafico, Mustapha Rachidi, and Paula Maria Machado Cruz Catarino, *On a Model of (k;p;s)-Generalized Padovan-Perrin and Fibonacci Fundamental System*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A49, Lemma 1.

articles.title: The Fibonacci fundamental system spans the solutions
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let
$k_1, k_2 \in R$ and let $p, s$ be natural numbers. For $1 \le j \le s + p$ let $v^{(j)}$ be the
solution of the Padovan–Perrin recurrence with parameters $k_1, k_2, p, s$ whose initial values
are $v^{(j)}(n) = 1$ if $n + 1 = j$ and $v^{(j)}(n) = 0$ otherwise, for $n < s + p$. Then the
submodule of $R^{\mathbb{N}}$ formed by all solutions of this recurrence is the submodule spanned
by $v^{(1)}, \dots, v^{(s+p)}$.

## Sources

- Elen Viviani Pereira Spreafico, Mustapha Rachidi, and Paula Maria Machado Cruz Catarino, *On a Model of (k;p;s)-Generalized Padovan-Perrin and Fibonacci Fundamental System*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A49, Corollary 1.

articles.title: Generalized Pell numbers count compositions with two-colored ones
articles.statement:
Let $k \ge 2$ and
$n \ge 1$ be natural numbers, and let $(P_m)_{m \in \mathbb{Z}}$ be natural numbers with $P_m = 0$
for $2 - k \le m \le 0$, $P_1 = 1$, and $P_m = 2P_{m-1} + P_{m-2} + \dots + P_{m-k}$ for all
$m \ge 2$. Then the number of compositions of $n$ into parts from $\{1, \dots, k\}$, where each
part equal to $1$ carries one of two colors, equals $P_{n+1}$.

## Sources

- Jhon J. Bravo, Jose L. Herrera, and José L. Ramírez, "Combinatorial Interpretation of Generalized Pell Numbers," Journal of Integer Sequences 23 (2020), Article 20.2.1, theorem `C_k(n) = P_{n+1}^{(k)}` for `n ≥ 1`, lines 441–447, https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL23/Bravo/bravo4.tex.

articles.title: Binet asymptotics for weighted generalized Fibonacci sequences, positive-root form
articles.statement:
Let $r \ge 2$, let $A_1, \dots, A_r$ and $c_1, \dots, c_r$ be nonnegative real numbers with
$A_r > 0$ and $c_j > 0$ for some $j$, and suppose that the indices $j$ with $A_j > 0$ have
greatest common divisor $1$. Let $a_0, a_1, a_2, \dots$ be the real sequence with
$a_n = c_{n+1}$ for $0 \le n < r$ and $a_n = \sum_{j=1}^{r} A_j a_{n-j}$ for $n \ge r$, and let
$p(x) = x^r - \sum_{j=1}^{r} A_j x^{r-j}$ be its characteristic polynomial. Let $\lambda > 0$
be a root of $p$. Then there is a constant $C > 0$ such that $a_n = C \lambda^n + o(\lambda^n)$
as $n \to \infty$, and $a_{n+1} / a_n \to \lambda$.

articles.title: Binet asymptotics for weighted generalized Fibonacci sequences
articles.statement:
Let $r \ge 2$, let
$A_1, \dots, A_r$ and $c_1, \dots, c_r$ be nonnegative real numbers with $A_r > 0$ and $c_j > 0$
for some $j$, and suppose that the indices $j$ with $A_j > 0$ have greatest common divisor $1$.
Let $a_0, a_1, a_2, \dots$ be the real sequence with $a_n = c_{n+1}$ for $0 \le n < r$ and
$a_n = \sum_{j=1}^{r} A_j a_{n-j}$ for $n \ge r$, and let $p(x) = x^r - \sum_{j=1}^{r} A_j x^{r-j}$
be its characteristic polynomial. Let $\lambda > 0$ be a root of $p$ that is not a root of the
derivative $p'$, and such that every complex root $z$ of $p$ satisfies $|z| \le \lambda$, with
$|z| = \lambda$ only for $z = \lambda$. Then there is a constant $C > 0$ such that
$a_n = C \lambda^n + o(\lambda^n)$ as $n \to \infty$, and $a_{n+1} / a_n \to \lambda$.

The source indexes the sequence from $1$; the $a_n$ here is the source's $a_{n+1}$, and $A_j$,
$c_j$ are the source's weights and initial values.

## Sources

- Passawan Noppakaew and Thanakorn Prinyasart, "Complete Sequences of Weighted r-Generalized Fibonacci Powers," Journal of Integer Sequences 24 (2021), Article 21.5.4, Proposition, lines 119–126, https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL24/Prinyasart/prin3.tex. It follows from `binet_general`; the hypotheses `hlam_simple` and `hlam_dom` are unused and keep the source's shape.

articles.title: Convolution of an even number of consecutive Fibonacci step sequences
articles.statement:
Write $F^{(s)}_k$
for the Fibonacci $s$-step numbers, and write $\sum_{K(r,N)}$ for a sum over all
$(k_1, \dots, k_r) \in \mathbb{N}^r$ with $k_1 + \dots + k_r = N$. For all natural numbers
$\ell \ge 1$, $m \ge 1$ and $n \ge \ell(m + \ell - 1)$,

$$
\sum_{K(2\ell, n - \ell(m + \ell - 1))} \prod_{j=0}^{2\ell-1} F^{(m+j)}_{k_{j+1}} =
\sum_{K(\ell, n)} \prod_{j=0}^{\ell-1} \left(F^{(m+2j+1)}_{k_{j+1}} - F^{(m+2j)}_{k_{j+1}}\right).
$$

## Sources

- Robert Frontczak and Karol Gryszka, "General Convolution Sums Involving Fibonacci `m`-Step Numbers", Theorem 35.

articles.title: Triple convolution of two consecutive Fibonacci step sequences with a third
articles.statement:
Write
$F^{(s)}_k$ for the Fibonacci $s$-step numbers, and write $\sum_{K(3,N)}$ for a sum over all
$(k_1, k_2, k_3) \in \mathbb{N}^3$ with $k_1 + k_2 + k_3 = N$. For all natural numbers $m \ge 1$,
$p \ge 1$ and $n \ge m$,

$$
\sum_{K(3, n - m)} F^{(m)}_{k_1} F^{(m+1)}_{k_2} F^{(p)}_{k_3} =
\sum_{j=0}^{n} F^{(p)}_j F^{(m+1)}_{n-j} - \sum_{j=0}^{n} F^{(p)}_j F^{(m)}_{n-j}.
$$

## Sources

- Robert Frontczak and Karol Gryszka, "General Convolution Sums Involving Fibonacci `m`-Step Numbers", Theorem 25.

articles.title: Two convolution forms of the Fibonacci–tribonacci–tetranacci triple sum
articles.statement:
Write $F_k$,
$T_k$ and $Q_k$ for the Fibonacci $2$-, $3$- and $4$-step numbers, and write $\sum_{K(3,N)}$ for
a sum over all $(k_1, k_2, k_3) \in \mathbb{N}^3$ with $k_1 + k_2 + k_3 = N$. For every natural
number $n \ge 2$,

$$
\sum_{K(3, n - 2)} F_{k_1} T_{k_2} Q_{k_3} = \sum_{j=0}^{n} (T_j - F_j) Q_{n-j} =
\sum_{j=0}^{n+1} F_{n+1-j} (Q_j - T_j).
$$

## Sources

- Robert Frontczak and Karol Gryszka, "General Convolution Sums Involving Fibonacci `m`-Step Numbers", Corollary 36.

articles.title: Closed form of the Fibonacci–tribonacci–tetranacci triple sum
articles.statement:
Write $F_k$, $T_k$ and
$Q_k$ for the Fibonacci $2$-, $3$- and $4$-step numbers, and write $\sum_{K(3,n)}$ for a sum over
all $(k_1, k_2, k_3) \in \mathbb{N}^3$ with $k_1 + k_2 + k_3 = n$. For every natural number $n$,

$$
\sum_{K(3,n)} F_{k_1} T_{k_2} Q_{k_3} = Q_{n+4} + Q_{n+2} - T_{n+5} + F_{n+3}.
$$

## Sources

- Robert Frontczak and Karol Gryszka, "General Convolution Sums Involving Fibonacci `m`-Step Numbers", Theorem 26.

articles.title: Convolution of four consecutive Fibonacci step sequences
articles.statement:
Write $F^{(s)}_k$ for the
Fibonacci $s$-step numbers, and write $\sum_{K(4,N)}$ for a sum over all
$(k_1, k_2, k_3, k_4) \in \mathbb{N}^4$ with $k_1 + k_2 + k_3 + k_4 = N$. For all natural numbers
$m \ge 1$ and $n \ge 2m + 2$,

$$
\sum_{K(4, n - 2m - 2)} F^{(m)}_{k_1} F^{(m+1)}_{k_2} F^{(m+2)}_{k_3} F^{(m+3)}_{k_4} =
\sum_{j=0}^{n} \left(F^{(m+3)}_j - F^{(m+2)}_j\right) \left(F^{(m+1)}_{n-j} - F^{(m)}_{n-j}\right).
$$

The paper prints the index of the last factor on the left as $k_3$; it is corrected to $k_4$
here.

## Sources

- Robert Frontczak and Karol Gryszka, "General Convolution Sums Involving Fibonacci `m`-Step Numbers", Theorem 34.

articles.title: Convolution of an odd number of consecutive Fibonacci step sequences
articles.statement:
Write $F^{(s)}_k$
for the Fibonacci $s$-step numbers, and write $\sum_{K(r,N)}$ for a sum over all
$(k_1, \dots, k_r) \in \mathbb{N}^r$ with $k_1 + \dots + k_r = N$. For all natural numbers
$\ell \ge 1$, $m \ge 1$ and $n \ge \ell(m + \ell - 1)$,

$$
\sum_{K(2\ell+1, n - \ell(m + \ell - 1))} \prod_{j=0}^{2\ell} F^{(m+j)}_{k_{j+1}} =
\sum_{K(\ell+1, n)} F^{(m+2\ell)}_{k_{\ell+1}} \prod_{j=0}^{\ell-1}
\left(F^{(m+2j+1)}_{k_{j+1}} - F^{(m+2j)}_{k_{j+1}}\right).
$$

## Sources

- Robert Frontczak and Karol Gryszka, "General Convolution Sums Involving Fibonacci `m`-Step Numbers", Theorem 35.

articles.title: Triple convolution of Pell numbers with two consecutive Fibonacci step sequences
articles.statement:
Write
$P_k$ for the Pell numbers ($P_0 = 0$, $P_1 = 1$, $P_{k+2} = 2P_{k+1} + P_k$), $F^{(s)}_k$ for
the Fibonacci $s$-step numbers, and $\sum_{K(3,N)}$ for a sum over all
$(k_1, k_2, k_3) \in \mathbb{N}^3$ with $k_1 + k_2 + k_3 = N$. For all natural numbers $m \ge 2$
and $n \ge 1$,

$$
\sum_{K(3, n - 1)} P_{k_1} F^{(m-1)}_{k_2} F^{(m)}_{k_3} =
\sum_{j=0}^{n} F^{(m-1)}_j \left(P_{n-j} - F^{(m)}_{n-j}\right) -
\sum_{j=0}^{n-1} P_j F^{(m)}_{n-1-j}.
$$

## Sources

- Robert Frontczak and Karol Gryszka, "General Convolution Sums Involving Fibonacci `m`-Step Numbers", Theorem 21.

articles.title: Pell–Fibonacci–tribonacci triple sum via a Pell–tribonacci convolution
articles.statement:
Write $P_k$ for
the Pell numbers ($P_0 = 0$, $P_1 = 1$, $P_{k+2} = 2P_{k+1} + P_k$), $F_k$ and $T_k$ for the
Fibonacci $2$- and $3$-step numbers, and $\sum_{K(3,n)}$ for a sum over all
$(k_1, k_2, k_3) \in \mathbb{N}^3$ with $k_1 + k_2 + k_3 = n$. For every natural number $n$,

$$
\sum_{K(3,n)} P_{k_1} F_{k_2} T_{k_3} = P_{n+1} + F_{n+2} - T_{n+3} - \sum_{j=0}^{n} P_j T_{n-j}.
$$

## Sources

- Robert Frontczak and Karol Gryszka, "General Convolution Sums Involving Fibonacci `m`-Step Numbers", Corollary 23.

articles.title: Sums over compositions
articles.statement:
Given integer sequences $a_0, \dots, a_{r-1}$ and a natural
number $n$, the sum over the compositions $K(r, n)$ of $n$ into $r$ nonnegative parts is the
sum, over all $(k_0, \dots, k_{r-1}) \in \mathbb{N}^r$ with $k_0 + \dots + k_{r-1} = n$, of
$\prod_{i=0}^{r-1} a_i(k_i)$.

articles.title: Bounds on the dominant root of the k-generalized Fibonacci polynomial
articles.statement:
Let $k$ be a natural
number and let $\alpha > 1$ be a real number with $\alpha^k = \sum_{i=0}^{k-1} \alpha^i$. Then
$2 - 1/k < \alpha < 2$, and if $k \ge 4$, moreover $2 - 1/(3k) < \alpha < 2$.

## Sources

- G. P. B. Dresden and Z. Du, *A Simplified Binet Formula for k-Generalized Fibonacci Numbers*, Journal of Integer Sequences 17 (2014), Article 14.4.7, Lemma `La`, line 350, <https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL17/Dresden/dresden6.tex>.

articles.title: Simplified Binet formula for k-generalized Fibonacci numbers from an initial window
articles.statement:
Let $k \ge 2$ and let $F : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$ satisfy $F(n) = 0$ for all integers $n$ with
$2 - k \le n < 1$, $F(1) = 1$, and $F(n) = \sum_{i=0}^{k-1} F(n - 1 - i)$ for all integers
$n > 1$. Let $\alpha$ be a positive real number with $\alpha^k = \sum_{i=0}^{k-1} \alpha^i$, and
put $c = (\alpha - 1)/(2 + (k + 1)(\alpha - 2))$. Then for every integer $n \ge 2 - k$,
$F(n) = \lfloor c\,\alpha^{n-1} + 1/2 \rfloor$.

Proof: We follow Dresden–Du's recurrence and first-crossing route, replacing their appeal to
the non-dominant-root results of Miles (1960) and Miller (1971) with an exact positive weighted
invariant.

## Sources

- G. P. B. Dresden and Z. Du, *A Simplified Binet Formula for k-Generalized Fibonacci Numbers*, Journal of Integer Sequences 17 (2014), Article 14.4.7, Theorem T2, lines 209-218, <https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL17/Dresden/dresden6.tex>.

articles.title: Dresden–Du simplified Binet formula
articles.statement:
Let $k \ge 2$ and let $F : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$
satisfy $F(n) = 0$ for all integers $n < 1$, $F(1) = 1$, and
$F(n) = \sum_{i=0}^{k-1} F(n - 1 - i)$ for all integers $n > 1$. Let $\alpha$ be a positive real
number with $\alpha^k = \sum_{i=0}^{k-1} \alpha^i$, and suppose that every positive real $\beta$
with $\beta^k = \sum_{i=0}^{k-1} \beta^i$ equals $\alpha$. Put
$c = (\alpha - 1)/(2 + (k + 1)(\alpha - 2))$. Then for every integer $n \ge 2 - k$,
$F(n) = \lfloor c\,\alpha^{n-1} + 1/2 \rfloor$.

## Sources

- G. P. B. Dresden and Z. Du, *A Simplified Binet Formula for k-Generalized Fibonacci Numbers*, Journal of Integer Sequences 17 (2014), Article 14.4.7, Theorem T2, lines 209-218, <https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL17/Dresden/dresden6.tex>.

articles.title: Fibonacci numbers as a truncated binomial sum
articles.statement:
Let $F_n$ be the Fibonacci numbers
($F_0 = 0$, $F_1 = 1$, $F_{n+2} = F_{n+1} + F_n$), and for an integer $x$ and a natural number
$j$ let $\binom{x}{j} = x(x-1)\cdots(x-j+1)/j!$. For every natural number $n \ge 2$,

$$
F_n = 2^{n-2} \sum_{\ell=0}^{\lfloor (n-1)/3 \rfloor}
\left(\binom{3\ell - n}{\ell} - \binom{3\ell - n}{\ell - 1}\right) 2^{-3\ell},
$$

where the term $\binom{3\ell - n}{\ell - 1}$ is taken to be $0$ for $\ell = 0$.

## Sources

- Bakir Farhi, *Some Applications of the Lagrange Inversion Formula for the k-Fibonacci Numbers*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.1.1, Corollary 13 (`jis-2024-24.1.1-cor-13`).

articles.title: Generating-function form of the triple convolution with two consecutive step sequences
articles.statement:
For a natural number $s$ let $F^{(s)}(X) = \sum_{n \ge 0} F^{(s)}_n X^n$ be the ordinary
generating function, with rational coefficients, of the Fibonacci $s$-step numbers
$F^{(s)}_n$. For all natural numbers $m \ge 1$ and $p \ge 1$, the formal power series over
$\mathbb{Q}$ satisfy

$$
X^m F^{(m)}(X) F^{(m+1)}(X) F^{(p)}(X) = F^{(p)}(X) F^{(m+1)}(X) - F^{(p)}(X) F^{(m)}(X).
$$

## Sources

- Robert Frontczak and Karol Gryszka, "General Convolution Sums Involving Fibonacci `m`-Step Numbers", Theorem 25.

articles.title: A product identity for four consecutive Fibonacci step generating functions
articles.statement:
Let
$m \ge 1$ be a natural number. For each $k$, let $F^{(k)} = \sum_{n \ge 0} F^{(k)}_n X^n$ in
$\mathbb{Q}[[X]]$ be the ordinary generating function of the Fibonacci $k$-step numbers
$F^{(k)}_n$. Then

$$X^{2m+1} F^{(m)} F^{(m+1)} F^{(m+2)} F^{(m+3)} =
X^m F^{(m)} F^{(m+2)} F^{(m+3)} - F^{(m+1)} F^{(m+3)} + F^{(m)} F^{(m+3)}.$$

## Sources

- Robert Frontczak and Karol Gryszka, "General Convolution Sums Involving Fibonacci `m`-Step Numbers", Theorem 31.

articles.title: A product identity for three consecutive Fibonacci step generating functions
articles.statement:
Let
$m \ge 1$ be a natural number. For each $k$, let $F^{(k)} = \sum_{n \ge 0} F^{(k)}_n X^n$ in
$\mathbb{Q}[[X]]$ be the ordinary generating function of the Fibonacci $k$-step numbers
$F^{(k)}_n$. Then

$$X^{2m+1} F^{(m)} F^{(m+1)} F^{(m+2)} = X^m F^{(m)} F^{(m+2)} - F^{(m+1)} + F^{(m)}.$$

## Sources

- Robert Frontczak and Karol Gryszka, "General Convolution Sums Involving Fibonacci `m`-Step Numbers", Theorem 24.

articles.title: A product identity for Fibonacci step generating functions of orders $m$, $m+p$, $m+p+q$
articles.statement:
**A product identity for Fibonacci step generating functions of orders $m$, $m+p$,
$m+p+q$.** Let $m, p, q \ge 1$ be natural numbers. For each $k$, let
$F^{(k)} = \sum_{n \ge 0} F^{(k)}_n X^n$ in $\mathbb{Q}[[X]]$ be the ordinary generating function
of the Fibonacci $k$-step numbers $F^{(k)}_n$. Then

$$X^{2m+p} (1-X^p)(1-X^q) F^{(m)} F^{(m+p)} F^{(m+p+q)} =
X^m (1-X)(1-X^p) F^{(m)} F^{(m+p+q)} - (1-X)^2 \left(F^{(m+p)} - F^{(m)}\right).$$

## Sources

- Robert Frontczak and Karol Gryszka, "General Convolution Sums Involving Fibonacci `m`-Step Numbers", Theorem 24.

articles.title: Generating function of the Fibonacci $m$-step numbers
articles.statement:
For a natural number $m$,
$F^{(m)}(X)$ is the formal power series $\sum_{n \ge 0} F^{(m)}_n X^n$ with rational
coefficients, where $F^{(m)}_n$ is the $n$-th Fibonacci $m$-step number.

articles.title: Initial segments of the Fibonacci $m$-step sequence
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $m$ and $n$,
this is the list of integers $[F_0, F_1, \dots, F_n]$, built recursively: the list for $n = 0$
is $[0]$, the list for $n = 1$ is $[0, 1]$, and for $n \ge 2$ the list for $n$ is the list for
$n - 1$ followed by $F_n = \sum_{j=1}^{m} F_{n-j}$, where $F_i = 0$ for $i < 0$.

articles.title: Double partial sums of Fibonacci step numbers
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $p$ and $n$ with
$1 \le p \le n$, the Fibonacci $(p+1)$-step numbers $F^{(p+1)}_j$ satisfy

$$F^{(p+1)}_n - 1 = \sum_{k=0}^{p-1} \sum_{j=0}^{n-2-k} F^{(p+1)}_j,$$

where an inner sum whose upper limit is $-1$ is empty.

## Sources

- Robert Frontczak and Karol Gryszka, "General Convolution Sums Involving Fibonacci `m`-Step Numbers", Corollary 7.

articles.title: Fibonacci $m$-step numbers
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $m$ and $n$, the integer $F^{(m)}_n$ is
defined by $F^{(m)}_0 = 0$, $F^{(m)}_1 = 1$ and $F^{(m)}_n = \sum_{j=1}^{m} F^{(m)}_{n-j}$ for
$n \ge 2$, where $F^{(m)}_i = 0$ for $i < 0$.

articles.title: Convolution of the Fibonacci $6$-step numbers with the Fibonacci numbers
articles.statement:
Write
$s_n = F^{(6)}_n$ for the Fibonacci $6$-step numbers and $F_n = F^{(2)}_n$ for the Fibonacci
numbers. For every natural number $n \ge 3$,

$$5 \sum_{j=0}^{n} s_j F_{n-j} =
s_{n+3} + s_{n+1} - s_n + 3 s_{n-1} + s_{n-3} - F_{n+3} - F_{n+1}.$$

The source prints this identity divided by $5$.

## Sources

- Robert Frontczak and Karol Gryszka, "General Convolution Sums Involving Fibonacci `m`-Step Numbers", Theorem 41.

articles.title: Binomial series for the powers of the golden ratio
articles.statement:
Let $\varphi = (1 + \sqrt{5})/2$ be
the golden ratio, and for an integer $x$ and a natural number $j$ let
$\binom{x}{j} = x(x-1)\cdots(x-j+1)/j!$. For every natural number $n \ge 1$ the series
$S_n = \sum_{\ell \ge 0} \frac{1}{\ell + 1} \binom{3\ell + 2 - n}{\ell} 2^{-3\ell}$ converges
absolutely and $\varphi^n = 2^n - n \, 2^{n-3} S_n$. Moreover, the series
$\sum_{\ell \ge 0} \frac{1}{\ell + 1} \binom{3\ell + 1}{\ell} 2^{-(3\ell + 2)}$ converges
absolutely to $2 - \varphi$.

## Sources

- Bakir Farhi, *Some Applications of the Lagrange Inversion Formula for the k-Fibonacci Numbers*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.1.1, Corollary 5 (`jis-2024-24.1.1-cor-5`).

articles.title: Difference binomial series at the $k$-Fibonacci root
articles.statement:
Let $k \ge 2$ be a natural number
and $\rho > 0$ a real number with $\rho^k = 1 + \rho + \cdots + \rho^{k-1}$, and for an integer
$x$ and a natural number $j$ let $\binom{x}{j} = x(x-1)\cdots(x-j+1)/j!$. For every natural number
$n \ne 1$ the series below converges absolutely and

$$
2^{n-2} \sum_{\ell \ge 0} \left(\binom{(k+1)\ell - n}{\ell} - \binom{(k+1)\ell - n}{\ell - 1}\right)
2^{-(k+1)\ell} = \frac{\rho - 1}{(k+1)\rho - 2k} \rho^{n-1},
$$

where the term $\binom{(k+1)\ell - n}{\ell - 1}$ is taken to be $0$ for $\ell = 0$.

## Sources

- Bakir Farhi, *Some Applications of the Lagrange Inversion Formula for the k-Fibonacci Numbers*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.1.1, Theorem 8 (`jis-2024-24.1.1-thm-8`), with `As_n^{(k)}` from equation (8).

articles.title: Binomial series summed at the $k$-Fibonacci root
articles.statement:
Let $k \ge 2$ be a natural number and
$\rho > 0$ a real number with $\rho^k = 1 + \rho + \cdots + \rho^{k-1}$, and for an integer $x$
and a natural number $j$ let $\binom{x}{j} = x(x-1)\cdots(x-j+1)/j!$. Then for every integer
$a$ the series below converges absolutely and

$$
\sum_{\ell \ge 0} \binom{(k+1)\ell + a}{\ell} 2^{-(k+1)\ell} =
\frac{2^{a+1} \rho^{-a}}{(k+1)\rho - 2k}.
$$

## Sources

- Bakir Farhi, *Some Applications of the Lagrange Inversion Formula for the k-Fibonacci Numbers*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.1.1, Theorem 6 (`jis-2024-24.1.1-thm-6`).

articles.title: Jacobsthal numbers
articles.statement:
The Jacobsthal numbers are the integers $J_n$ defined by $J_0 = 0$,
$J_1 = 1$ and $J_{n+2} = J_{n+1} + 2 J_n$ for all $n \ge 0$.

articles.title: Initial values of the truncated binomial sums
articles.statement:
Let $k \ge 2$ be a natural number and let
$G_n^{(k)}$ be the truncated binomial sum. Then $G_n^{(k)} = 2^{n-2}$ for every natural number $n$
with $2 \le n \le k + 1$, and $G_{k+2}^{(k)} = 2^k - 1$.

## Sources

- Bakir Farhi, *Some Applications of the Lagrange Inversion Formula for the k-Fibonacci Numbers*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.1.1, Proposition 10 (`jis-2024-24.1.1-prop-10`).

articles.title: Recurrence for the truncated binomial sums
articles.statement:
Let $G_n^{(k)}$ be the truncated binomial
sum. For all natural numbers $k \ge 2$ and $n \ge 2$,
$G_{n+k+1}^{(k)} = 2 G_{n+k}^{(k)} - G_n^{(k)}$.

## Sources

- Bakir Farhi, *Some Applications of the Lagrange Inversion Formula for the k-Fibonacci Numbers*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.1.1, Proposition 11 (`jis-2024-24.1.1-prop-11`).

articles.title: Value $G_4^{(2)} = 3$
articles.statement:
The truncated binomial sum satisfies $G_4^{(2)} = 3$.

This is the Fibonacci number $F_4$, and $n = 4$ is the first index for which the sum defining
$G_n^{(2)}$ has two terms.

## Sources

- Bakir Farhi, *Some Applications of the Lagrange Inversion Formula for the k-Fibonacci Numbers*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.1.1, definition before Proposition 10.

articles.title: Value $G_2^{(2)} = 1$
articles.statement:
The truncated binomial sum satisfies $G_2^{(2)} = 1$.

This is the Fibonacci number $F_2$.

## Sources

- Bakir Farhi, *Some Applications of the Lagrange Inversion Formula for the k-Fibonacci Numbers*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.1.1, definition before Proposition 10.

articles.title: Truncated binomial sum $G_n^{(k)}$
articles.statement:
For an integer $x$ and a natural number $j$ let
$\binom{x}{j} = x(x-1)\cdots(x-j+1)/j!$. For natural numbers $k$ and $n$, the rational number
$G_n^{(k)}$ is

$$
G_n^{(k)} = 2^{n-2} \sum_{\ell=0}^{m}
\left(\binom{(k+1)\ell - n}{\ell} - \binom{(k+1)\ell - n}{\ell - 1}\right) 2^{-(k+1)\ell},
$$

where $m = \lfloor (n-1)/(k+1) \rfloor$ for $n \ge 1$ and $m = 0$ for $n = 0$, and the term
$\binom{(k+1)\ell - n}{\ell - 1}$ is taken to be $0$ for $\ell = 0$.

The paper defines $G_n^{(k)}$ only for $n, k \ge 2$.

## Sources

- Bakir Farhi, *Some Applications of the Lagrange Inversion Formula for the k-Fibonacci Numbers*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.1.1, definition before Proposition 10.

articles.title: Alternating binomial formula for the $k$-Fibonacci numbers
articles.statement:
Let $k \ge 2$ be a natural
number and let $F_n^{(k)}$ be the $k$-Fibonacci numbers: $F_i^{(k)} = 0$ for $i < k - 1$,
$F_{k-1}^{(k)} = 1$ and $F_{m+k}^{(k)} = F_m^{(k)} + F_{m+1}^{(k)} + \cdots + F_{m+k-1}^{(k)}$ for
every $m \ge 0$. For an integer $x$ and a natural number $j$ let
$\binom{x}{j} = x(x-1)\cdots(x-j+1)/j!$. Then for every natural number $n \ge k$,

$$
F_n^{(k)} = 2^{n-k} + \sum_{\ell=1}^{\lfloor (n-k+1)/(k+1) \rfloor} (-1)^\ell
\left(\binom{n - (\ell+1)k + 2}{\ell} - \binom{n - (\ell+1)k}{\ell - 2}\right)
2^{n - (k+1)\ell - k},
$$

where the term $\binom{n - (\ell+1)k}{\ell - 2}$ is taken to be $0$ for $\ell = 1$.

The paper assumes $n \ne 2k - 1$; for $n = 2k - 1$ the sum is empty and both sides equal
$2^{k-1}$.

## Sources

- Bakir Farhi, *Some Applications of the Lagrange Inversion Formula for the k-Fibonacci Numbers*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.1.1, Corollary 14 (`jis-2024-24.1.1-cor-14`).

articles.title: Binomial-sum formula for the $k$-Fibonacci numbers
articles.statement:
Let $k \ge 2$ and let
$(F_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be the $k$-Fibonacci sequence, given by $F_0 = \dots = F_{k-2} = 0$,
$F_{k-1} = 1$ and $F_{m+k} = F_m + F_{m+1} + \dots + F_{m+k-1}$ for all $m \ge 0$. For integers
$a$ and $j \ge 0$ write $\binom{a}{j} = a(a-1)\cdots(a-j+1)/j!$, and put $\binom{a}{-1} = 0$.
Then for every $n \ge k$,

$$F_n = 2^{n-k} \sum_{\ell=0}^{\lfloor (n-k+1)/(k+1) \rfloor} \left(\binom{(k+1)\ell+k-n-2}{\ell} -
\binom{(k+1)\ell+k-n-2}{\ell-1}\right) 2^{-(k+1)\ell}.$$

## Sources

- Bakir Farhi, *Some Applications of the Lagrange Inversion Formula for the k-Fibonacci Numbers*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.1.1, Corollary 12 (`jis-2024-24.1.1-cor-12`).

articles.title: $k$-Fibonacci numbers as truncated binomial sums
articles.statement:
Let $k \ge 2$ and let
$(F_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be the $k$-Fibonacci sequence, given by $F_0 = \dots = F_{k-2} = 0$,
$F_{k-1} = 1$ and $F_{m+k} = F_m + F_{m+1} + \dots + F_{m+k-1}$ for all $m \ge 0$. For integers
$a$ and $j \ge 0$ write $\binom{a}{j} = a(a-1)\cdots(a-j+1)/j!$, and put $\binom{a}{-1} = 0$.
For $n \ge 2$ let $G_n^{(k)}$ be the truncated binomial sum
$G_n^{(k)} = 2^{n-2} \sum_{\ell=0}^{\lfloor (n-1)/(k+1) \rfloor} \left(\binom{(k+1)\ell-n}{\ell} -
\binom{(k+1)\ell-n}{\ell-1}\right) 2^{-(k+1)\ell}$. Then $F_{n+k-2} = G_n^{(k)}$ for every
$n \ge 2$.

## Sources

- Bakir Farhi, *Some Applications of the Lagrange Inversion Formula for the k-Fibonacci Numbers*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.1.1, Theorem 9 (`jis-2024-24.1.1-thm-9`).

articles.title: Binomial series for the powers of the dominant $k$-Fibonacci root
articles.statement:
Let $k \ge 2$ and let
$\rho_k > 0$ be a real number with $\rho_k^k = 1 + \rho_k + \dots + \rho_k^{k-1}$. For integers $a$
and $j \ge 0$ write $\binom{a}{j} = a(a-1)\cdots(a-j+1)/j!$. Then for every $n \ge 1$ the series
$S = \sum_{\ell \ge 0} \frac{1}{\ell+1} \binom{k(\ell+1)+\ell-n}{\ell} 2^{-(k+1)\ell}$ converges
absolutely and $\rho_k^n = 2^n - n\, 2^{n-k-1} S$.

For $n = 1$ this is the paper's series for $\rho_k$ itself.

## Sources

- Bakir Farhi, *Some Applications of the Lagrange Inversion Formula for the k-Fibonacci Numbers*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.1.1, Theorem 3 (`jis-2024-24.1.1-thm-3`).

articles.title: Lagrange inversion formula
articles.statement:
Let $f, g : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be analytic at $z_0$.
There are $\varepsilon > 0$ and $\delta > 0$ such that for every $\alpha \in \mathbb{C}$ with
$|\alpha| < \delta$ the equation $w = z_0 + \alpha f(w)$ has exactly one solution $w$ with
$|w - z_0| < \varepsilon$, and for this solution the series
$\sum_{n \ge 1} \frac{\alpha^n}{n!} \frac{d^{n-1}}{dz^{n-1}} \bigl(f(z)^n g'(z)\bigr)\big|_{z=z_0}$
converges absolutely to $g(w) - g(z_0)$.

## Sources

- Bakir Farhi, *Some Applications of the Lagrange Inversion Formula for the k-Fibonacci Numbers*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.1.1, Theorem 1 (`jis-2024-24.1.1-thm-1`).

articles.title: Partial sums of the Fibonacci $m$-step numbers
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $m \ge 2$ and $n$,
the Fibonacci $m$-step numbers $F^{(m)}_k$ satisfy

$$(m-1) \sum_{k=0}^{n} F^{(m)}_k =
F^{(m)}_{n+m} - \sum_{k=1}^{m-2} (m-1-k) F^{(m)}_{n+k} - 1.$$

The source prints this identity divided by $m - 1$ and with coefficients $k$ in place of
$m-1-k$; its proof gives $m-1-k$, and the printed form already fails at $m = 4$, $n = 1$, where
it gives $2/3$ instead of $1$.

## Sources

- Robert Frontczak and Karol Gryszka, "General Convolution Sums Involving Fibonacci `m`-Step Numbers", Theorem 8.

articles.title: Recurrence for the N-step Fibonacci numbers
articles.statement:
For all natural numbers $N$ and $n$, the
$N$-step Fibonacci numbers $F^{(N)}$ satisfy
$F^{(N)}_{n+2} = \sum_{i=0}^{N-1} F^{(N)}_{\max(n+1-i,\,0)}$.

## Sources

- Bowman, *Compositions with an Odd Number of Parts, and Other Congruences*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.3.6, Section 4.4.

articles.title: First N-step Fibonacci number
articles.statement:
For every natural number $N$, the $N$-step Fibonacci
number $F^{(N)}_1$ equals $1$.

## Sources

- Bowman, *Compositions with an Odd Number of Parts, and Other Congruences*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.3.6, Section 4.4.

articles.title: The tribonacci number with index 5
articles.statement:
The $3$-step Fibonacci number $F^{(3)}_5$ equals $7$.

The tribonacci numbers $F^{(3)}_0, \dots, F^{(3)}_5$ are $0, 1, 1, 2, 4, 7$.

## Sources

- Bowman, *Compositions with an Odd Number of Parts, and Other Congruences*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.3.6, Section 4.4.

articles.title: Zeroth N-step Fibonacci number
articles.statement:
For every natural number $N$, the $N$-step Fibonacci
number $F^{(N)}_0$ equals $0$.

## Sources

- Bowman, *Compositions with an Odd Number of Parts, and Other Congruences*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.3.6, Section 4.4.

articles.title: N-step Fibonacci numbers
articles.statement:
For a natural number $N$, the $N$-step Fibonacci numbers
$F^{(N)}_n$ ($n \ge 0$), in the convention of Noe and Post, are defined by $F^{(N)}_0 = 0$,
$F^{(N)}_1 = 1$ and, for $n \ge 2$, $F^{(N)}_n = \sum_{i=1}^{N} F^{(N)}_{n-i}$, where a term
whose index $n - i$ is negative counts as $0$. In particular $F^{(0)}_n = 0$ for $n \ge 2$.

## Sources

- Bowman, *Compositions with an Odd Number of Parts, and Other Congruences*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.3.6, Section 4.4.

articles.title: Octanacci numbers
articles.statement:
The octanacci sequence $(f_n)_{n \ge 0}$ of natural numbers is defined by
$f_0 = f_1 = 1$, $f_n = 2^{n-1}$ for $2 \le n \le 7$, and
$f_n = f_{n-1} + f_{n-2} + \dots + f_{n-8}$ for $n \ge 8$. It begins
$1, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 255, \dots$, and its generating function is
$1/(1 - t - t^2 - \dots - t^8)$.

articles.title: Octanacci window
articles.statement:
The octanacci window is the sequence $(w_n)_{n \ge 0}$ of $8$-tuples of
natural numbers with $w_0 = (1, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64)$ and, if $w_n = (a_1, \dots, a_8)$, then
$w_{n+1} = (a_2, \dots, a_8, a_1 + a_2 + \dots + a_8)$. The octanacci numbers $f_n$ are the first
entries of these tuples, so $w_n = (f_n, f_{n+1}, \dots, f_{n+7})$.

articles.title: Convolution of the Fibonacci numbers with tribonacci minus tetranacci
articles.statement:
Write $F_n$, $T_n$
and $Q_n$ for the Fibonacci, tribonacci and tetranacci numbers, that is, the Fibonacci $m$-step
numbers $F^{(m)}_n$ for $m = 2, 3, 4$ ($F^{(m)}_0 = 0$, $F^{(m)}_1 = 1$, and each later term is the
sum of the $m$ terms before it, terms at negative indices being $0$). For every natural number
$n \ge 1$,

$$\sum_{j=0}^{n} F_j (T_{n-j} - Q_{n-j}) = \sum_{j=0}^{n-1} (F_j - T_j) Q_{n-1-j}.$$

## Sources

- Robert Frontczak and Karol Gryszka, "General Convolution Sums Involving Fibonacci `m`-Step Numbers", Corollary 11.

articles.title: Convolution of the Fibonacci and tetranacci numbers
articles.statement:
Write $F_n$ and $Q_n$ for the
Fibonacci and tetranacci numbers, that is, the Fibonacci $m$-step numbers $F^{(m)}_n$ for
$m = 2, 4$ ($F^{(m)}_0 = 0$, $F^{(m)}_1 = 1$, and each later term is the sum of the $m$ terms
before it, terms at negative indices being $0$). For every natural number $n$,

$$\sum_{j=0}^{n} F_j Q_{n-j} = Q_{n+1} + Q_{n-1} - F_{n+1},$$

where for $n = 0$ the term $Q_{n-1}$ is $Q_0 = 0$.

## Sources

- Robert Frontczak and Karol Gryszka, "General Convolution Sums Involving Fibonacci `m`-Step Numbers", Corollaries 9 and 16.

articles.title: Convolution of the Fibonacci and tribonacci numbers
articles.statement:
Write $F_n$ and $T_n$ for the
Fibonacci and tribonacci numbers, that is, the Fibonacci $m$-step numbers $F^{(m)}_n$ for
$m = 2, 3$ ($F^{(m)}_0 = 0$, $F^{(m)}_1 = 1$, and each later term is the sum of the $m$ terms
before it, terms at negative indices being $0$). For every natural number $n$,

$$\sum_{j=0}^{n} F_j T_{n-j} = T_{n+2} - F_{n+2}.$$

## Sources

- Robert Frontczak and Karol Gryszka, "General Convolution Sums Involving Fibonacci `m`-Step Numbers", Corollary 2.

articles.title: Convolution of the $m$-step Fibonacci numbers with consecutive sums of the $(m+2)$-step ones
articles.statement:
**Convolution of the $m$-step Fibonacci numbers with consecutive sums of the
$(m+2)$-step ones.** Write $F^{(m)}_n$ for the Fibonacci $m$-step numbers ($F^{(m)}_0 = 0$,
$F^{(m)}_1 = 1$, and each later term is the sum of the $m$ terms before it, terms at negative
indices being $0$). For all natural numbers $m \ge 1$ and $n \ge m$,

$$\sum_{j=0}^{n-m-1} F^{(m)}_j \bigl(F^{(m+2)}_{n-m-j} + F^{(m+2)}_{n-m-j-1}\bigr) =
F^{(m+2)}_n - F^{(m)}_n.$$

## Sources

- Robert Frontczak and Karol Gryszka, "General Convolution Sums Involving Fibonacci `m`-Step Numbers", Corollary 4.

articles.title: Convolution of the $m$-step and $(m-2)$-step Fibonacci numbers via Jacobsthal numbers
articles.statement:
Write $F^{(m)}_n$ for the Fibonacci $m$-step numbers ($F^{(m)}_0 = 0$, $F^{(m)}_1 = 1$, and each
later term is the sum of the $m$ terms before it, terms at negative indices being $0$), and $J_n$
for the Jacobsthal numbers ($J_0 = 0$, $J_1 = 1$, $J_{n+2} = J_{n+1} + 2 J_n$). For all natural
numbers $m \ge 3$ and $n \ge 2$,

$$\sum_{j=0}^{n} F^{(m)}_j F^{(m-2)}_{n-j} =
J_{n-1} + \sum_{j=0}^{n-2} J_j \bigl(F^{(m-2)}_{n-j} - F^{(m)}_{n-2-j}\bigr).$$

## Sources

- Robert Frontczak and Karol Gryszka, "General Convolution Sums Involving Fibonacci `m`-Step Numbers", Theorem 19.

articles.title: Truncated convolution of the $m$-step and $(m+1)$-step Fibonacci numbers
articles.statement:
Write
$F^{(m)}_n$ for the Fibonacci $m$-step numbers ($F^{(m)}_0 = 0$, $F^{(m)}_1 = 1$, and each later
term is the sum of the $m$ terms before it, terms at negative indices being $0$). For all natural
numbers $m \ge 1$ and $n \ge m$,

$$\sum_{j=0}^{n-m} F^{(m)}_j F^{(m+1)}_{n-m-j} = F^{(m+1)}_n - F^{(m)}_n.$$

## Sources

- Robert Frontczak and Karol Gryszka, "General Convolution Sums Involving Fibonacci `m`-Step Numbers", Theorem 1.

articles.title: Convolution of the $(m-1)$-step and $m$-step Fibonacci numbers against powers of two
articles.statement:
Write $F^{(m)}_n$ for the Fibonacci $m$-step numbers ($F^{(m)}_0 = 0$, $F^{(m)}_1 = 1$, and each
later term is the sum of the $m$ terms before it, terms at negative indices being $0$). For all
natural numbers $m \ge 2$ and $n \ge 2$,

$$\sum_{j=0}^{n} F^{(m-1)}_j F^{(m)}_{n-j} =
\sum_{j=0}^{n-2} 2^j \bigl(F^{(m-1)}_{n-1-j} - F^{(m)}_{n-2-j}\bigr).$$

## Sources

- Robert Frontczak and Karol Gryszka, "General Convolution Sums Involving Fibonacci `m`-Step Numbers", Theorem 12.

articles.title: Exchange identity for convolutions of $(m-2)$-, $(m-1)$- and $m$-step Fibonacci numbers
articles.statement:
Write $F^{(m)}_n$ for the Fibonacci $m$-step numbers ($F^{(m)}_0 = 0$, $F^{(m)}_1 = 1$, and each
later term is the sum of the $m$ terms before it, terms at negative indices being $0$). For all
natural numbers $m \ge 3$ and $n \ge 1$,

$$\sum_{j=0}^{n} F^{(m-2)}_j \bigl(F^{(m)}_{n-j} - F^{(m-1)}_{n-j}\bigr) =
\sum_{j=0}^{n-1} F^{(m)}_j \bigl(F^{(m-1)}_{n-1-j} - F^{(m-2)}_{n-1-j}\bigr).$$

## Sources

- Robert Frontczak and Karol Gryszka, "General Convolution Sums Involving Fibonacci `m`-Step Numbers", Theorem 10.

articles.title: Sum of $2m + 2$ consecutive Fibonacci $m$-step numbers
articles.statement:
Write $F^{(m)}_n$ for the
Fibonacci $m$-step numbers ($F^{(m)}_0 = 0$, $F^{(m)}_1 = 1$, and each later term is the sum of
the $m$ terms before it, terms at negative indices being $0$). For every natural number $m \ge 2$
and every natural number $n$,

$$\sum_{k=0}^{2m+1} F^{(m)}_{n+k} = 4 F^{(m)}_{n+2m}.$$

## Sources

- Robert Frontczak and Karol Gryszka, "General Convolution Sums Involving Fibonacci `m`-Step Numbers", Lemma 39.

articles.title: Alternating sum of differences of $2m$-step and $(2m-2)$-step Fibonacci numbers
articles.statement:
Write
$F^{(m)}_n$ for the Fibonacci $m$-step numbers ($F^{(m)}_0 = 0$, $F^{(m)}_1 = 1$, and each later
term is the sum of the $m$ terms before it, terms at negative indices being $0$). For all natural
numbers $m \ge 2$ and $n \ge 2m - 1$,

$$\sum_{j=0}^{n-1} (-1)^j \bigl(F^{(2m)}_j - F^{(2m-2)}_j\bigr) =
(-1)^{n+1} \sum_{j=0}^{n-2m+1} F^{(2m)}_j F^{(2m-2)}_{n-2m+1-j}.$$

## Sources

- Robert Frontczak and Karol Gryszka, "General Convolution Sums Involving Fibonacci `m`-Step Numbers", Theorem 15.

articles.title: Alternating sums of differences of odd-order Fibonacci step numbers
articles.statement:
Let $F^{(k)}_j$ be
the $j$-th Fibonacci $k$-step number: the sequence starts $F^{(k)}_0 = 0$, $F^{(k)}_1 = 1$, and each
later term is the sum of the $k$ terms before it (terms of negative index being $0$). For all
natural numbers $m$ and $n$ with $m \ge 1$ and $n \ge 2m$,

$$\sum_{j=0}^{n-1} (-1)^{j+1} \bigl(F^{(2m+1)}_j - F^{(2m-1)}_j\bigr) =
(-1)^n \sum_{j=0}^{n-2m} F^{(2m+1)}_j \, F^{(2m-1)}_{n-2m-j}.$$

## Sources

- Robert Frontczak and Karol Gryszka, "General Convolution Sums Involving Fibonacci `m`-Step Numbers", Theorem 17.

articles.title: Convolution of the Pell numbers with the Fibonacci numbers
articles.statement:
Let $\mathcal{P}_j$ be the
Pell numbers ($\mathcal{P}_0 = 0$, $\mathcal{P}_1 = 1$,
$\mathcal{P}_{j+2} = 2\mathcal{P}_{j+1} + \mathcal{P}_j$) and $F_j$ the Fibonacci numbers
($F_0 = 0$, $F_1 = 1$, $F_{j+2} = F_{j+1} + F_j$), that is, the Fibonacci $2$-step numbers. For
every natural number $n$,

$$\sum_{j=0}^{n} \mathcal{P}_j \, F_{n-j} = \mathcal{P}_n - F_n.$$

## Sources

- Robert Frontczak and Karol Gryszka, "General Convolution Sums Involving Fibonacci `m`-Step Numbers", Corollary 22.

articles.title: Iterated convolution of Fibonacci $m$-step and $(m+p)$-step numbers
articles.statement:
Let $F^{(k)}_j$ be
the $j$-th Fibonacci $k$-step number: the sequence starts $F^{(k)}_0 = 0$, $F^{(k)}_1 = 1$, and each
later term is the sum of the $k$ terms before it (terms of negative index being $0$). For all
natural numbers $m$, $p$ and $n$ with $m \ge 1$ and $n \ge m$,

$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1} \sum_{j=0}^{n-m-k} F^{(m)}_j \, F^{(m+p)}_{n-m-k-j} =
F^{(m+p)}_n - F^{(m)}_n,$$

where an inner sum whose upper limit $n - m - k$ is negative counts as $0$.

## Sources

- Robert Frontczak and Karol Gryszka, "General Convolution Sums Involving Fibonacci `m`-Step Numbers", Theorem 3.

articles.title: Convolution of the Fibonacci 4-step and 5-step numbers
articles.statement:
Let $Q_j$ and $P_j$ be the
Fibonacci $4$-step and $5$-step numbers, where the Fibonacci $k$-step numbers start $0, 1$ and
each later term is the sum of the $k$ terms before it (terms of negative index being $0$). For
every natural number $n$,

$$\sum_{j=0}^{n} Q_j \, P_{n-j} = P_{n+4} - Q_{n+4}.$$

## Sources

- Robert Frontczak and Karol Gryszka, "General Convolution Sums Involving Fibonacci `m`-Step Numbers", Corollary 2.

articles.title: Convolution of the Fibonacci 3-step numbers with differences of 4- and 5-step numbers
articles.statement:
Let $T_j$, $Q_j$ and $P_j$ be the Fibonacci $3$-, $4$- and $5$-step numbers, where the Fibonacci
$k$-step numbers start $0, 1$ and each later term is the sum of the $k$ terms before it (terms of
negative index being $0$). For every natural number $n \ge 1$,

$$\sum_{j=0}^{n} T_j \bigl(Q_{n-j} - P_{n-j}\bigr) =
\sum_{j=0}^{n-1} \bigl(T_j - Q_j\bigr) P_{n-1-j}.$$

## Sources

- Robert Frontczak and Karol Gryszka, "General Convolution Sums Involving Fibonacci `m`-Step Numbers", Corollary 11.

articles.title: Convolution of the Fibonacci 3-step and 4-step numbers as a sum weighted by powers of 2
articles.statement:
Let $T_j$ and $Q_j$ be the Fibonacci $3$-step and $4$-step numbers, where the Fibonacci $k$-step
numbers start $0, 1$ and each later term is the sum of the $k$ terms before it (terms of negative
index being $0$). For every natural number $n$,

$$\sum_{j=0}^{n+2} T_j \, Q_{n+2-j} = \sum_{j=0}^{n} 2^j \bigl(T_{n+1-j} - Q_{n-j}\bigr).$$

This is the case $m = 4$ of the paper's Theorem 12 with $n$ replaced by $n + 2$. The paper prints
$Q_{n-j}$ in place of $Q_{n+2-j}$ on the left; as printed, the identity fails at $n = 0$, where
the left side is $0$ and the right side is $1$.

## Sources

- Robert Frontczak and Karol Gryszka, "General Convolution Sums Involving Fibonacci `m`-Step Numbers", Corollary 13.

articles.title: Convolution of the Fibonacci 3-step and 4-step numbers
articles.statement:
Let $T_j$ and $Q_j$ be the
Fibonacci $3$-step and $4$-step numbers, where the Fibonacci $k$-step numbers start $0, 1$ and
each later term is the sum of the $k$ terms before it (terms of negative index being $0$). For
every natural number $n$,

$$\sum_{j=0}^{n} T_j \, Q_{n-j} = Q_{n+3} - T_{n+3}.$$

## Sources

- Robert Frontczak and Karol Gryszka, "General Convolution Sums Involving Fibonacci `m`-Step Numbers", Corollary 2.

articles.title: Difference of the Fibonacci 3-step and 2-step numbers as a convolution
articles.statement:
Let $F_j$ and
$T_j$ be the Fibonacci $2$-step and $3$-step numbers, where the Fibonacci $k$-step numbers start
$0, 1$ and each later term is the sum of the $k$ terms before it (terms of negative index being
$0$). For every natural number $n \ge 1$,

$$T_{n+1} - F_{n+1} = \sum_{j=0}^{n-1} T_j \, F_{n-1-j}.$$

## Sources

- Robert Frontczak and Karol Gryszka, "General Convolution Sums Involving Fibonacci `m`-Step Numbers", Corollary 11.

articles.title: Triple convolution of the Fibonacci 2-, 4- and 5-step numbers
articles.statement:
Let $F_j$, $Q_j$ and $P_j$
be the Fibonacci $2$-, $4$- and $5$-step numbers, where the Fibonacci $k$-step numbers start
$0, 1$ and each later term is the sum of the $k$ terms before it (terms of negative index being
$0$). For every natural number $n \ge 5$,

$$2 \sum_{k_1 + k_2 + k_3 = n - 5} F_{k_1} Q_{k_2} P_{k_3}
= -2Q_n - 2Q_{n-2} + P_{n+1} + P_{n-2} - F_{n+1} + 2F_n,$$

where the sum runs over all triples $(k_1, k_2, k_3)$ of natural numbers with
$k_1 + k_2 + k_3 = n - 5$.

The paper prints this identity with a factor $\tfrac{1}{2}$ on part of the right side.

## Sources

- Robert Frontczak and Karol Gryszka, "General Convolution Sums Involving Fibonacci `m`-Step Numbers", Theorem 28.

articles.title: Triple convolution of the Fibonacci 2-, 3- and 5-step numbers
articles.statement:
Let $F_j$, $T_j$ and $P_j$
be the Fibonacci $2$-, $3$- and $5$-step numbers, where the Fibonacci $k$-step numbers start
$0, 1$ and each later term is the sum of the $k$ terms before it (terms of negative index being
$0$). For every natural number $n \ge 5$,

$$2 \sum_{k_1 + k_2 + k_3 = n - 5} F_{k_1} T_{k_2} P_{k_3} =
P_n - P_{n-1} + P_{n-2} - T_n - T_{n-2} + F_{n-1},$$

where the sum runs over all triples $(k_1, k_2, k_3)$ of natural numbers with
$k_1 + k_2 + k_3 = n - 5$.

The paper prints this identity with a factor $\tfrac{1}{2}$.

## Sources

- Robert Frontczak and Karol Gryszka, "General Convolution Sums Involving Fibonacci `m`-Step Numbers", Theorem 29.

articles.title: Four-fold convolution of the Fibonacci, tribonacci, tetranacci and pentanacci numbers
articles.statement:
Write $F_n$, $T_n$, $Q_n$ and $P_n$ for the Fibonacci $m$-step numbers $F^{(m)}_n$ with
$m = 2, 3, 4, 5$ respectively. For every integer $n \ge 5$,
$2 \sum F_{k_1} T_{k_2} Q_{k_3} P_{k_4} = P_{n+4} - P_{n+3} + P_{n+2} + T_{n+3} + T_{n+1} -
F_n - 2Q_{n+3} - 2Q_{n+1}$, where the sum runs over all $4$-tuples $(k_1, k_2, k_3, k_4)$ of
nonnegative integers with $k_1 + k_2 + k_3 + k_4 = n - 5$.

The source prints this identity with a factor $1/2$; it is stated here multiplied by $2$.

## Sources

- Robert Frontczak and Karol Gryszka, "General Convolution Sums Involving Fibonacci `m`-Step Numbers", Theorem 32.

articles.title: Closed form for the Pell–Fibonacci–tribonacci triple convolution
articles.statement:
Write $\mathcal{P}_n$
for the Pell numbers, $F_n$ for the Fibonacci numbers and $T_n$ for the tribonacci numbers (the
Fibonacci $m$-step numbers $F^{(m)}_n$ with $m = 2$ and $m = 3$). For every integer $n \ge 0$,
$2 \sum \mathcal{P}_{k_1} F_{k_2} T_{k_3} = \mathcal{P}_{n+1} - T_{n+3} - T_{n+2} + 2F_{n+2}$,
where the sum runs over all triples $(k_1, k_2, k_3)$ of nonnegative integers with
$k_1 + k_2 + k_3 = n$.

The source prints this identity with a factor $1/2$; it is stated here multiplied by $2$.

## Sources

- Robert Frontczak and Karol Gryszka, "General Convolution Sums Involving Fibonacci `m`-Step Numbers", Corollary 23.

articles.title: Triple convolution of the tribonacci, tetranacci and pentanacci numbers
articles.statement:
Write $T_n$,
$Q_n$ and $P_n$ for the Fibonacci $m$-step numbers $F^{(m)}_n$ with $m = 3, 4, 5$ respectively.
For every integer $n \ge 7$,
$2 \sum T_{k_1} Q_{k_2} P_{k_3} = P_n + P_{n-2} + P_{n-4} + T_n - T_{n-2} - 2Q_n$, where the sum
runs over all triples $(k_1, k_2, k_3)$ of nonnegative integers with $k_1 + k_2 + k_3 = n - 7$.

The source prints this identity with a factor $1/2$; it is stated here multiplied by $2$.

## Sources

- Robert Frontczak and Karol Gryszka, "General Convolution Sums Involving Fibonacci `m`-Step Numbers", Theorem 27.

articles.title: Convolution of the Fibonacci and pentanacci numbers
articles.statement:
Write $F_n$ for the Fibonacci numbers
and $P_n$ for the pentanacci numbers (the Fibonacci $m$-step numbers $F^{(m)}_n$ with $m = 2$ and
$m = 5$). For every integer $n \ge 0$,
$2 \sum_{j=0}^{n} F_j P_{n-j} = P_{n+2} + P_{n-1} - F_{n+2}$, where $P_{n-1}$ is read as
$P_0 = 0$ when $n = 0$.

The source prints this identity with a factor $1/2$; it is stated here multiplied by $2$.

## Sources

- Robert Frontczak and Karol Gryszka, "General Convolution Sums Involving Fibonacci `m`-Step Numbers", Corollary 9.

articles.title: Convolution of the Jacobsthal and tribonacci numbers
articles.statement:
Write $J_n$ for the Jacobsthal
numbers ($J_0 = 0$, $J_1 = 1$, $J_{n+2} = J_{n+1} + 2J_n$) and $T_n$ for the tribonacci numbers
(the Fibonacci $3$-step numbers $F^{(3)}_n$). For every integer $n \ge 0$,
$2 \sum_{j=0}^{n} J_j T_{n-j} = 2J_{n+1} + J_{n+2} - T_{n+3} - T_{n+1}$.

The source prints this identity with a factor $1/2$ on part of the right-hand side; it is stated
here multiplied by $2$.

## Sources

- Robert Frontczak and Karol Gryszka, "General Convolution Sums Involving Fibonacci `m`-Step Numbers", Corollary 20.

articles.title: Alternating sum of the tribonacci numbers
articles.statement:
Write $T_n$ for the tribonacci numbers (the
Fibonacci $3$-step numbers $F^{(3)}_n$). For every integer $n \ge 0$,
$2 \sum_{j=0}^{n} (-1)^j T_j = (-1)^n (T_{n+1} - T_{n-1}) - 1$, where $T_{n-1}$ is read as
$T_0 = 0$ when $n = 0$.

The source prints this identity with a factor $1/2$; it is stated here multiplied by $2$.

## Sources

- Robert Frontczak and Karol Gryszka, "General Convolution Sums Involving Fibonacci `m`-Step Numbers", Corollary 18.

articles.title: Convolution of the pentanacci and tribonacci numbers, second closed form
articles.statement:
Write $P_n$ for
the pentanacci numbers and $T_n$ for the tribonacci numbers (the Fibonacci $m$-step numbers
$F^{(m)}_n$ with $m = 5$ and $m = 3$). For every integer $n \ge 0$,
$2 \sum_{j=0}^{n} P_j T_{n-j} = -P_{n+7} + 2P_{n+6} - P_{n+5} + 2P_{n+4} + P_{n+3} - T_{n+4} +
T_{n+2}$.

The source prints this identity with a factor $1/2$; it is stated here multiplied by $2$.

## Sources

- Robert Frontczak and Karol Gryszka, "General Convolution Sums Involving Fibonacci `m`-Step Numbers", Corollary 18.

articles.title: Convolution of the pentanacci and tribonacci numbers
articles.statement:
Write $P_n$ for the pentanacci
numbers and $T_n$ for the tribonacci numbers (the Fibonacci $m$-step numbers $F^{(m)}_n$ with
$m = 5$ and $m = 3$). For every integer $n \ge 0$,
$2 \sum_{j=0}^{n} P_j T_{n-j} = P_{n+3} + P_{n+1} + P_{n-1} - T_{n+3} - T_{n+1}$, where
$P_{n-1}$ is read as $P_0 = 0$ when $n = 0$.

The source prints this identity with a factor $1/2$; it is stated here multiplied by $2$.

## Sources

- Robert Frontczak and Karol Gryszka, "General Convolution Sums Involving Fibonacci `m`-Step Numbers", Corollary 9.

articles.title: Power-weighted convolution of Fibonacci $m$-step numbers
articles.statement:
Let $m \ge 1$ and let
$F \colon \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ satisfy $F(0) = 0$, $F(1) = 1$ and
$F(k) = \sum_{j=1}^{m} F(k - j)$ for every $k \ge 2$, where a term $F(k - j)$ with $j > k$ is
read as $F(0) = 0$. Then for every natural number $n$,

$$\sum_{j=0}^{n} 2^j F(n - j) = 2^{n+m-1} - F(n + 1 + m),$$

where the subtraction on the right is taken in $\mathbb{N}$ (truncated at $0$).

The initial conditions are those of the paper's definition of Fibonacci $m$-step numbers
(lines 126–133), whose values at negative indices are $0$. The paper states the theorem for
$m \ge 3$; the cases $m = 1$ and $m = 2$ also hold, so the hypothesis here is $m \ge 1$.

## Sources

- Robert Frontczak and Karol Gryszka, "General Convolution Sums Involving Fibonacci m-Step Numbers," Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.8.8, Theorem, lines 453–459, https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL27/Gryszka/gryszka12.tex

articles.title: $k$-generalized Lucas numbers at the lowest index
articles.statement:
For every natural number $k \ge 3$,
the $k$-generalized Lucas number $L^{(k)}_{2-k}$ equals $0$.

articles.title: $k$-generalized Lucas numbers vanish at negative indices
articles.statement:
For every natural number
$k \ge 3$ and every integer $n$ with $2 - k \le n \le -1$, the $k$-generalized Lucas number
$L^{(k)}_n$ equals $0$.

articles.title: $k$-generalized Lucas numbers at index one
articles.statement:
For every natural number $k \ge 2$, the
$k$-generalized Lucas number $L^{(k)}_1$ equals $1$.

articles.title: Recurrence for the $k$-generalized Lucas numbers
articles.statement:
For every natural number $k \ge 2$ and
every integer $n \ge 2$, the $k$-generalized Lucas numbers satisfy
$L^{(k)}_n = \sum_{i=0}^{k-1} L^{(k)}_{n-k+i}$, that is, $L^{(k)}_n$ is the sum
$L^{(k)}_{n-1} + \dots + L^{(k)}_{n-k}$ of the $k$ preceding values.

articles.title: $k$-generalized Lucas numbers at index zero
articles.statement:
For every natural number $k \ge 2$, the
$k$-generalized Lucas number $L^{(k)}_0$ equals $2$.

articles.title: $k$-generalized Lucas numbers
articles.statement:
For a natural number $k \ge 2$, the $k$-generalized Lucas
numbers $L^{(k)}_n$ are the natural numbers indexed by the integers $n \ge 2 - k$ given by
$L^{(k)}_n = 0$ for $2 - k \le n \le -1$, $L^{(k)}_0 = 2$, $L^{(k)}_1 = 1$, and
$L^{(k)}_n = L^{(k)}_{n-1} + L^{(k)}_{n-2} + \dots + L^{(k)}_{n-k}$ for every integer $n \ge 2$. No
value is assigned at indices below $2 - k$.

articles.title: Finite prefixes of the n-step Lucas numbers
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $n$ and $m$, this is the
list $[L^{(n)}_1, \dots, L^{(n)}_m]$ of length $m$ (empty for $m = 0$), where
$L^{(n)}_k = 2^k - 1$ for $1 \le k \le n$ and $L^{(n)}_k$ is the sum of the $n$ preceding terms
for $k \ge n + 1$. For $n = 0$ every term is $0$.

## Sources

- <https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL14/Saito/saito22.tex>.

articles.title: n-step Lucas numbers
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $n \ge 1$ and $m$, the $n$-step Lucas number
$L^{(n)}_m$ is defined by $L^{(n)}_0 = 0$, $L^{(n)}_m = 2^m - 1$ for $1 \le m \le n$, and
$L^{(n)}_m = \sum_{i=1}^{n} L^{(n)}_{m-i}$ for $m \ge n + 1$. For $n = 0$ we set
$L^{(0)}_m = 0$ for every $m$.

The source defines $L^{(n)}_m$ only for $m \ge 1$; the value $L^{(n)}_0 = 0$ is a convention.

## Sources

- <https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL14/Saito/saito22.tex>.

articles.title: First tile of a bracelet
articles.statement:
For a natural number $p$, a first tile records the tile of a
bracelet that covers cell $1$ of the circular board, together with its phase (which cell of the
tile covers cell $1$). It is one of: a curved square, in phase $1$; a curved $p$-mino of length
$p + 1$ in phase $r + 1$ for some $0 \le r \le p$; a curved $p$-tile of length $p + 1$ in color
$c$ for some $0 \le c < p$ and phase $r + 1$ for some $0 \le r \le p$; or a curved $p$-tile of
length $l$ in color $c$ for some $0 \le c < p$ and some natural number $l$, starting at cell $1$
(phase $1$).

The restriction $l \ge p + 2$ on the last kind is not part of this type; the bracelet sets
impose it.

## Sources

- Amine Belkhir and Elif Tan, *Combinatorial Insights into Leonardo `p`-Numbers and Lucas-Leonardo `p`-Numbers*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A57, Section 3.

articles.title: Counting Leonardo $p$-tilings
articles.statement:
For all natural numbers $p \ge 1$ and $n$, let $K_{p,n}$ be
the set of linear tilings of an $n$-board by squares (length $1$), $p$-minos (length $p + 1$) and
at most one $p$-tile, which comes in one of $p$ colors, has length at least $p + 1$ and can only
be the initial piece. Then the number of tilings in $K_{p,n}$ equals the Leonardo $p$-number
$\mathcal{L}_{p,n}$, the generalized Leonardo $p$-number $\mathcal{L}_{p,k}(n)$ at $k = p$:
$\mathcal{L}_{p,n} = 1$ for $n \le p$ and
$\mathcal{L}_{p,n} = \mathcal{L}_{p,n-1} + \mathcal{L}_{p,n-p-1} + p$ for $n > p$.

## Sources

- Amine Belkhir and Elif Tan, *Combinatorial Insights into Leonardo `p`-Numbers and Lucas-Leonardo `p`-Numbers*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A57, Proposition 1.

articles.title: Counting Lucas–Leonardo bracelets
articles.statement:
For all natural numbers $p \ge 1$ and $n \ge 1$, let
$B_{p,n}$ be the set of tilings of a circular $n$-board by curved squares (length $1$), curved
$p$-minos (length $p + 1$) and at most one curved $p$-tile in one of $p$ colors, which if present
is the tile covering cell $1$ and either has length $p + 1$, in any of its $p + 1$ phases, or has
length at least $p + 2$ and starts at cell $1$. Then the number of bracelets in $B_{p,n}$ equals
the Lucas–Leonardo $p$-number $R_{p,n}$, given by $R_{p,0} = p^2 + p + 1$, $R_{p,i} = 1$ for
$1 \le i \le p$ and $R_{p,n} = R_{p,n-1} + R_{p,n-p-1} + p$ for $n > p$.

## Sources

- Amine Belkhir and Elif Tan, *Combinatorial Insights into Leonardo `p`-Numbers and Lucas-Leonardo `p`-Numbers*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A57, Proposition 12.

articles.title: Entries of the powers of the companion matrix $Q_p$
articles.statement:
Let $p \ge 2$ and $n$ be natural
numbers, and index the rows and columns of the $(2p+1) \times (2p+1)$ companion matrix $Q_p$ by
$0, 1, \dots, 2p$. Then for all indices $a$ and $b$, the entry $(a, b)$ of $Q_p^n$ equals
$A_p(n + 1 - b)$ if $a = 0$, equals $B_p(n - p + 1 + a - b)$ if $1 \le a \le p - 1$, and equals
$-A_p(n - (2p - a) - b)$ if $p \le a \le 2p$. Here $A_p, B_p : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$ are the
sequences satisfying $S(t) = S(t-1) + S(t-p) - S(t-2p-1)$ for every integer $t$, with
$A_p(t) = 1$ for $1 \le t \le p$ and $A_p(t) = 0$ for $-p \le t \le 0$, and with $B_p(t) = 1$ for
$1 \le t \le p$ and for $t = -p+1$ and $B_p(t) = 0$ for the other $-p \le t \le 0$.

## Sources

- "On Generalized Leonardo `p`-Numbers", Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.4.6, Theorem 9.

articles.title: The companion matrix $Q_p$
articles.statement:
For a natural number $p$, $Q_p$ is the $(2p+1) \times (2p+1)$
integer matrix with rows and columns indexed by $0, 1, \dots, 2p$ whose entry $(2p, 0)$ is $-1$,
whose other entries $(0, 0)$, $(p-1, 0)$ and $(i, i+1)$ for $0 \le i < 2p$ are $1$, and whose
remaining entries are $0$.

articles.title: Fibonacci $p$-numbers as differences of $A_p$
articles.statement:
For all natural numbers $p \ge 1$ and
$n \ge 1$, the Fibonacci $p$-number $F_p(n)$ equals $A_p(n) - A_p(n-p)$. Here
$A_p : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$ is the sequence with $A_p(t) = 0$ for $-p \le t \le 0$,
$A_p(t) = 1$ for $1 \le t \le p$, and $A_p(t) = A_p(t-1) + A_p(t-p) - A_p(t-2p-1)$ for every
integer $t$.

## Sources

- "On Generalized Leonardo `p`-Numbers", Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.4.6, Theorem 5.

articles.title: Binomial sum formula for Fibonacci p-numbers
articles.statement:
For all natural numbers $p \ge 1$ and $n$,
the Fibonacci $p$-numbers $F_p$ satisfy

$$F_p(n+1) = \sum_{i=0}^{\lfloor n/(p+1) \rfloor} \binom{n-ip}{i}.$$

The paper (Theorem 8, quoting Kuhapatanakul) also gives the form
$F_p(n) = \sum_{i=0}^{\lfloor (n-1)/(p+1) \rfloor} \binom{n-1-ip}{i}$, which is the same identity
with $n$ shifted by one. The paper allows all natural $p$, but at $p = 0$ the sequence is
identically zero ($F_0(1) = F_0(0) + F_0(0) = 0$) while the sum at $n = 0$ is
$\binom{0}{0} = 1$, so $p \ge 1$ is assumed.

## Sources

- Clemens Schütz and Kristian Kelly, *An Explicit Formula for Supergeneralized Leonardo `p`-numbers*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.8.2, Theorem 8 (Kuhapatanakul).

articles.title: Convolution identity for sequences in $H(p)$
articles.statement:
Let $p \ge 2$ be a natural number and let
$\mathcal{H} : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$ be a sequence in $H(p)$, that is,
$\mathcal{H}(t) = \mathcal{H}(t-1) + \mathcal{H}(t-p) - \mathcal{H}(t-2p-1)$ for every integer
$t$. Then for all natural numbers $m \ge 1$ and $n \ge 1$,

$$
\mathcal{H}(m+n) = \mathcal{H}(m)A_p(n+1) + \sum_{i=1}^{p-1} \mathcal{H}(m-i)B_p(n-p+i+1) -
\sum_{i=0}^{p} \mathcal{H}(m-p-i)A_p(n-p+i),
$$

where $A_p, B_p : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$ are the sequences in $H(p)$ with $A_p(t) = 1$ for
$1 \le t \le p$ and $A_p(t) = 0$ for $-p \le t \le 0$, and with $B_p(t) = 1$ for $1 \le t \le p$
and for $t = -p+1$ and $B_p(t) = 0$ for the other $-p \le t \le 0$.

## Sources

- "On Generalized Leonardo `p`-Numbers", Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.4.6, Corollary 11.

articles.title: Backward evaluation of the $H(p)$ recurrence
articles.statement:
For a natural number $p$, a function
$s : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, this is the list of the values at
$-p-n, \dots, p$ of the sequence $H$ that equals $s$ on $[-p, p]$ and continues to the left by
$H(t) = H(t+2p) + H(t+p+1) - H(t+2p+1)$ for $t < -p$, which is the $H(p)$ recurrence
$H(u) = H(u-1) + H(u-p) - H(u-2p-1)$ at $u = t+2p+1$ solved for $H(t)$. Each step prepends one
value to the previous list.

For $p = 0$, where this rule is circular, every prepended value equals $s(0)$.

articles.title: Forward evaluation of the $H(p)$ recurrence
articles.statement:
For a natural number $p$, a function
$s : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, this is the list of the $2p + n + 1$
values at $-p, -p+1, \dots, p+n$ (the entry at position $i$ is the value at $i - p$) of the
sequence $H$ that equals $s$ on $[-p, p]$ and continues by the $H(p)$ recurrence
$H(t) = H(t-1) + H(t-p) - H(t-2p-1)$ for $t > p$. Each step appends one value to the previous
list, so evaluation takes polynomial time.

For $p = 0$, where this rule is circular, every appended value is $0$.

articles.title: Two-sided extension of initial values by the $H(p)$ recurrence
articles.statement:
For a natural number
$p \ge 1$ and a function $s : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$, this is the unique function
$H : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$ that agrees with $s$ on $[-p, p]$ and satisfies
$H(t) = H(t-1) + H(t-p) - H(t-2p-1)$ for every integer $t$: its values at $t > p$ are computed
forward and its values at $t < -p$ backward from this recurrence. For $p = 0$ its value is $s(0)$
at every $t \le 0$ and $0$ at every $t > 0$.

articles.title: Binomial addition formula for hyper Leonardo $p$-numbers
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $p \ge 1$,
$n \ge 1$, $m \ge 1$ and $k \ge m$, the hyper Leonardo $p$-numbers satisfy

$$\mathcal{L}^{(k)}_{p,n+m} = \sum_{i=0}^{m} \binom{m}{i} \mathcal{L}^{(k-i)}_{p,n+i}.$$

## Sources

- Amine Belkhir and Elif Tan, *Combinatorial Insights into Leonardo `p`-Numbers and Lucas-Leonardo `p`-Numbers*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A57, Proposition 9.

articles.title: Recurrence for the hyper Leonardo $p$-numbers
articles.statement:
Let $p \ge 1$ be a natural number. For all
natural numbers $n \ge 1$ and $k \ge 1$, the hyper Leonardo $p$-numbers satisfy
$\mathcal{L}^{(k)}_{p,n} = \mathcal{L}^{(k)}_{p,n-1} + \mathcal{L}^{(k-1)}_{p,n}$, and for every
natural number $n$, $\mathcal{L}^{(0)}_{p,n} = \mathcal{L}_{p,n}$, where $\mathcal{L}_{p,n}$ is the
Leonardo $p$-number: $\mathcal{L}_{p,n} = 1$ for $n \le p$ and
$\mathcal{L}_{p,n} = \mathcal{L}_{p,n-1} + \mathcal{L}_{p,n-p-1} + p$ for $n > p$.

## Sources

- Amine Belkhir and Elif Tan, *Combinatorial Insights into Leonardo `p`-Numbers and Lucas-Leonardo `p`-Numbers*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A57, Proposition 10.

articles.title: Hyper Leonardo $p$-numbers at $n = 0$
articles.statement:
For all natural numbers $p$ and $k$, the hyper
Leonardo $p$-number $\mathcal{L}^{(k)}_{p,0}$ equals $1$.

## Sources

- Belkhir and Tan, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A57, display (12) and Proposition 10.

articles.title: Hyper Leonardo $p$-numbers
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $p$, $n$ and $k$, the hyper Leonardo
$p$-number is the integer

$$\mathcal{L}^{(k)}_{p,n} = (p + 1) \sum_{i=0}^{\lfloor n/(p+1) \rfloor}
\binom{n + k - pi}{i + k} - p \binom{n + k}{k}.$$

## Sources

- Amine Belkhir and Elif Tan, *Combinatorial Insights into Leonardo `p`-Numbers and Lucas-Leonardo `p`-Numbers*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A57, display (12) (quoting Belaggoun and Belbachir).

articles.title: Hyper Lucas–Leonardo numbers from hyper Leonardo numbers
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $p \ge 1$,
$n > p$ and $k \ge 1$, the hyper Lucas–Leonardo $p$-number $R^{(k)}_{p,n}$ and the hyper
Leonardo $p$-numbers $\mathcal{L}^{(k)}_{p,n}$ satisfy

$$R^{(k)}_{p,n} = (p + 1) \mathcal{L}^{(k)}_{p,n} - p \mathcal{L}^{(k)}_{p,n-1} +
p^2 \binom{n + k - 1}{k - 1}.$$

The paper prints the binomial as $\binom{n + k - 1}{k}$, which is false: at $p = 1$, $n = 2$,
$k = 1$ one has $R^{(1)}_{1,2} = 9$ while the printed right side is $10$. The paper's own proof
ends with $p^2 \binom{n + k - 1}{k - 1}$.

## Sources

- Amine Belkhir and Elif Tan, *Combinatorial Insights into Leonardo `p`-Numbers and Lucas-Leonardo `p`-Numbers*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A57, Proposition 20.

articles.title: Hyper Lucas–Leonardo numbers from incomplete ones
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $p \ge 1$, $n > p$
and $k \ge 1$, write $R_{p,m}$ for the Lucas–Leonardo $p$-numbers and $R_{p,m}(j)$ for the
incomplete Lucas–Leonardo $p$-numbers. Then the hyper Lucas–Leonardo $p$-number $R^{(k)}_{p,n}$
satisfies

$$R^{(k)}_{p,n} = R_{p,n+(p+1)k} - R_{p,n+(p+1)k}(k - 1) - p \binom{n + k}{k}.$$

## Sources

- Amine Belkhir and Elif Tan, *Combinatorial Insights into Leonardo `p`-Numbers and Lucas-Leonardo `p`-Numbers*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A57, Proposition 19.

articles.title: Hyper Lucas–Leonardo $p$-numbers at $n = 0$
articles.statement:
For all natural numbers $p$ and $k$, the
hyper Lucas–Leonardo $p$-number $R^{(k)}_{p,0}$ equals $p^2 + p + 1$.

For $k = 0$ this is the initial value $R_{p,0} = p^2 + p + 1$ of the Lucas–Leonardo $p$-numbers.

## Sources

- Belkhir and Tan, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A57, Definition 2.

articles.title: Hyper Lucas-Leonardo p-numbers of order zero
articles.statement:
For all natural numbers $p$ and $n$, the
hyper Lucas-Leonardo $p$-number of order $0$ equals the Lucas-Leonardo $p$-number:
$R^{(0)}_{p,n} = R_{p,n}$.

## Sources

- Belkhir and Tan, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A57, Definition 2.

articles.title: Hyper Lucas-Leonardo p-numbers
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $p$, $n$ and $k$, the hyper
Lucas-Leonardo $p$-number $R^{(k)}_{p,n}$ is the rational number defined by
$R^{(0)}_{p,n} = R_{p,n}$, the Lucas-Leonardo $p$-number; $R^{(k)}_{p,0} = p^2 + p + 1$ for
$k \ge 1$; and, for $n \ge 1$ and $k \ge 1$,

$$
R^{(k)}_{p,n} = (p + 1) \sum_{i=0}^{\lfloor n/(p+1) \rfloor} \frac{n + (p+1)k}{n + k - pi}
\binom{n + k - pi}{i + k} - p \binom{n + k}{k}.
$$

For $p = 2$ this reproduces the values listed in the paper. For $p = 1$ the listed values $122$
(for $R^{(1)}_{1,7}$), $101, 186, 308$ (for $R^{(2)}_{1,5}, R^{(2)}_{1,6}, R^{(2)}_{1,7}$) and
$220, 406, 714$ (for $R^{(3)}_{1,5}, R^{(3)}_{1,6}, R^{(3)}_{1,7}$) are misprints: the definition
gives $142$; $111, 196, 338$; and $230, 426, 764$, the values that the recurrence
$R^{(k)}_{1,n} = R^{(k)}_{1,n-1} + R^{(k-1)}_{1,n}$ produces from the paper's own earlier
entries.

## Sources

- Amine Belkhir and Elif Tan, *Combinatorial Insights into Leonardo `p`-Numbers and Lucas-Leonardo `p`-Numbers*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A57, Definition 2.

articles.title: Recurrence for incomplete Leonardo p-numbers
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $p \ge 1$, $n > p$ and
$k \le \lfloor n/(p+1) \rfloor$, the incomplete Leonardo $p$-numbers $\mathcal{L}_{p,m}(j)$
satisfy

$$
\mathcal{L}_{p,n}(k + 1) = \mathcal{L}_{p,n-1}(k + 1) + \mathcal{L}_{p,n-p-1}(k) + p.
$$

## Sources

- Amine Belkhir and Elif Tan, *Combinatorial Insights into Leonardo `p`-Numbers and Lucas-Leonardo `p`-Numbers*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A57, Proposition 6.

articles.title: Incomplete Leonardo p-numbers at zero
articles.statement:
For all natural numbers $p$ and $n$, the
incomplete Leonardo $p$-number $\mathcal{L}_{p,n}(0)$ equals $1$.

## Sources

- Belkhir and Tan, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A57, display (4).

articles.title: Incomplete Leonardo p-numbers
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $p$, $n$ and $k$, the incomplete
Leonardo $p$-number is the integer

$$
\mathcal{L}_{p,n}(k) = (p + 1) \sum_{i=0}^{k} \binom{\max(n - pi, 0)}{i} - p.
$$

On the paper's range $0 \le k \le \lfloor n/(p+1) \rfloor$ the maximum is always $n - pi$.

## Sources

- Amine Belkhir and Elif Tan, *Combinatorial Insights into Leonardo `p`-Numbers and Lucas-Leonardo `p`-Numbers*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A57, display (4).

articles.title: Recurrence for incomplete Lucas-Leonardo p-numbers
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $p \ge 1$,
$n > p + 1$ and $k \le \lfloor n/(p+1) \rfloor$, the incomplete Lucas-Leonardo $p$-numbers
$R_{p,m}(j)$ satisfy

$$
R_{p,n}(k + 1) = R_{p,n-1}(k + 1) + R_{p,n-p-1}(k) + p.
$$

At $n = p + 1$ the term $R_{p,0}(k)$ would contain the undefined summand
$\frac{0}{0} \binom{0}{0}$, so that case is excluded.

## Sources

- Amine Belkhir and Elif Tan, *Combinatorial Insights into Leonardo `p`-Numbers and Lucas-Leonardo `p`-Numbers*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A57, Proposition 17.

articles.title: Incomplete Lucas-Leonardo p-numbers at zero
articles.statement:
For every natural number $p$ and every
natural number $n \ge 1$, the incomplete Lucas-Leonardo $p$-number $R_{p,n}(0)$ equals $1$.

## Sources

- Belkhir and Tan, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A57, display (8).

articles.title: Incomplete Lucas-Leonardo p-numbers
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $p$, $n$ and $k$, the
incomplete Lucas-Leonardo $p$-number is the rational number

$$
R_{p,n}(k) = (p + 1) \sum_{i=0}^{k} \frac{n}{m_i} \binom{m_i}{i} - p, \qquad m_i = \max(n - pi, 0),
$$

where a summand with $m_i = 0$ is taken to be $0$. On the paper's range
$0 \le k \le \lfloor n/(p+1) \rfloor$ with $n \ge 1$, every $m_i$ is positive.

## Sources

- Amine Belkhir and Elif Tan, *Combinatorial Insights into Leonardo `p`-Numbers and Lucas-Leonardo `p`-Numbers*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A57, display (8).

articles.title: Length of the first tile of a bracelet
articles.statement:
For a natural number $p$, the length of the first
tile of a bracelet is $1$ for a curved square, $p + 1$ for a curved $p$-mino in any phase,
$p + 1$ for a curved $p$-tile of length $p + 1$ in any color and phase, and $l$ for a curved
$p$-tile of length $l$ (in any color) starting at cell $1$.

## Sources

- Belkhir and Tan, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A57, Section 3.

articles.title: Leonardo p-numbers split into incomplete and hyper parts
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $p \ge 1$,
$n > p$ and $k \ge 1$, let $N = n + (p + 1)k$. Then

$$
\mathcal{L}_{p,N} = \mathcal{L}_{p,N}(k - 1) + \mathcal{L}^{(k)}_{p,n} + p \binom{n + k}{k},
$$

where $\mathcal{L}_{p,N}$ is the Leonardo $p$-number (the generalized Leonardo $p$-numbers with
additive constant $p$: $\mathcal{L}_{p,m} = 1$ for $m \le p$ and
$\mathcal{L}_{p,m} = \mathcal{L}_{p,m-1} + \mathcal{L}_{p,m-p-1} + p$ for $m > p$),
$\mathcal{L}_{p,N}(k - 1)$ is the incomplete Leonardo $p$-number and $\mathcal{L}^{(k)}_{p,n}$ is
the hyper Leonardo $p$-number.

## Sources

- Amine Belkhir and Elif Tan, *Combinatorial Insights into Leonardo `p`-Numbers and Lucas-Leonardo `p`-Numbers*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A57, Proposition 11.

articles.title: Generalized Leonardo $p$-numbers in terms of Fibonacci $p$-numbers
articles.statement:
For all natural
numbers $p$, $k$ and $n$ with $p \ge 1$ and $k \ge 1$, the generalized Leonardo $p$-number
$\mathcal{L}_{p,k}(n)$ and the Fibonacci $p$-number $F_p(n+1)$ satisfy
$\mathcal{L}_{p,k}(n) = (k+1)F_p(n+1) - k$.

## Sources

- "On Generalized Leonardo `p`-Numbers", Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.4.6, Theorem 2.

articles.title: Honsberger-type identity for generalized Leonardo $p$-numbers
articles.statement:
Let $p$, $k$, $m$ and $n$
be natural numbers with $p, k, m, n \ge 1$. Write $\mathcal{L}$ for the generalized Leonardo
$p$-numbers $\mathcal{L}_{p,k}$, extended to negative integers by $\mathcal{L}(t) = -k$ for
$t < 0$. Then

$$
\mathcal{L}(m)\mathcal{L}(n+1) + \sum_{i=1}^{p} \mathcal{L}(m-i)\mathcal{L}(n-p+i) =
(k+1)\mathcal{L}(m+n+1) - k\bigl(\mathcal{L}(m+p) + \mathcal{L}(n+p+1)\bigr) + pk^2 + k.
$$

The arguments that occur are at least $-p$, and on $[-p, -1]$ the value $-k$ is the one forced by
the recurrence $\mathcal{L}(t) = \mathcal{L}(t-1) + \mathcal{L}(t-p-1) + k$ read backwards. The
paper prints the summation index as $j$ in $\mathcal{L}(m-j)$; it is corrected to $i$ here.

## Sources

- "On Generalized Leonardo `p`-Numbers", Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.4.6, Theorem 13.

articles.title: Homogeneous recurrence for the Leonardo $p$-numbers
articles.statement:
Let $p \ge 1$ and write
$\mathcal{L}_{p,n}$ for the Leonardo $p$-number $\mathcal{L}_{p,p}(n)$, the generalized Leonardo
$p$-number with $k = p$. Then $\mathcal{L}_{p,n} = \mathcal{L}_{p,n-1} + \mathcal{L}_{p,n-p} -
\mathcal{L}_{p,n-2p-1}$ for every $n \ge 2p + 1$, $\mathcal{L}_{p,i} = 1$ for every $i \le p$,
and $\mathcal{L}_{p,p+j} = (j + 1) + jp$ for every $j$ with $1 \le j \le p$.

## Sources

- Amine Belkhir and Elif Tan, *Combinatorial Insights into Leonardo `p`-Numbers and Lucas-Leonardo `p`-Numbers*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A57, Proposition 2.

articles.title: Generalized Leonardo $p$-numbers
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $p$ and $k$, the generalized
Leonardo $p$-numbers are the integers $\mathcal{L}_{p,k}(n)$, $n \in \mathbb{N}$, given by
$\mathcal{L}_{p,k}(n) = 1$ for $0 \le n \le p$ and
$\mathcal{L}_{p,k}(n) = \mathcal{L}_{p,k}(n-1) + \mathcal{L}_{p,k}(n-p-1) + k$ for $n > p$.

articles.title: Initial values of the generalized Leonardo $p$-numbers
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $p$, $k$
and $n$, this is the list of integers $(\mathcal{L}_{p,k}(0), \mathcal{L}_{p,k}(1), \dots,
\mathcal{L}_{p,k}(n))$ of length $n + 1$, where $\mathcal{L}_{p,k}(i) = 1$ for $0 \le i \le p$
and $\mathcal{L}_{p,k}(i) = \mathcal{L}_{p,k}(i-1) + \mathcal{L}_{p,k}(i-p-1) + k$ for $i > p$.

articles.title: Generalized Leonardo $p$-numbers at integer arguments
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $p$ and $k$
and an integer $z$, the value is the generalized Leonardo $p$-number $\mathcal{L}_{p,k}(z)$ if
$z \ge 0$, and $-k$ if $z < 0$.

For $-p \le z \le -1$ these are the values $\mathcal{L}_{p,k}(z) = -k$ obtained by running the
recurrence $\mathcal{L}_{p,k}(n) = \mathcal{L}_{p,k}(n-1) + \mathcal{L}_{p,k}(n-p-1) + k$
backwards; below $-p$ they need not be, but Theorem 13 of the source only uses arguments
$z \ge -p$.

articles.title: Leonardo $p$-tilings
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $p$ and $n$, the tiling set $K_{p,n}$ consists
of the linear tilings of an $n$-board by squares (length $1$), $p$-minos (length $p + 1$) and at
most one $p$-tile, which comes in one of $p$ colors, has length at least $p + 1$, and can only be
the initial piece. A tiling is recorded as its initial $p$-tile, given by its color and length,
if there is one, followed by the sequence of the remaining pieces read from left to right, each a
square or a $p$-mino; the lengths of all pieces sum to $n$.

## Sources

- Amine Belkhir and Elif Tan, *Combinatorial Insights into Leonardo `p`-Numbers and Lucas-Leonardo `p`-Numbers*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A57, Definition 1 and the set `K_{p,n}` before Proposition 1.

articles.title: Lucas–Leonardo bracelets
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $p$ and $n$, the bracelet set $B_{p,n}$
consists of the tilings of a circular $n$-board by curved squares (length $1$), curved $p$-minos
(length $p + 1$) and at most one curved $p$-tile, which comes in one of $p$ colors and has either
length $p + 1$, in any of its $p + 1$ phases, or length $l \ge p + 2$, starting at cell $1$; a
$p$-tile, if present, is the first tile. A bracelet is recorded as its first tile, the one
covering cell $1$, together with its phase, followed by the sequence of the remaining pieces read
clockwise, each a curved square or a curved $p$-mino; the lengths of all pieces sum to $n$. In
particular $B_{p,0}$ is empty.

The source sets $|B_{p,0}| = p^2 + p + 1$ by convention; that value is not modelled here.

## Sources

- Amine Belkhir and Elif Tan, *Combinatorial Insights into Leonardo `p`-Numbers and Lucas-Leonardo `p`-Numbers*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A57, Section 3, the set `B_{p,n}` before Proposition 12.

articles.title: Lucas-Leonardo $p$-numbers from Leonardo $p$-numbers
articles.statement:
Let $p \ge 1$, let $R_{p,n}$ denote
the Lucas-Leonardo $p$-numbers, and let $\mathcal{L}_{p,n}$ denote the Leonardo $p$-numbers
$\mathcal{L}_{p,p}(n)$ (the generalized Leonardo $p$-numbers with $k = p$), extended to $n = -1$
by $\mathcal{L}_{p,-1} = -p$. Then $R_{p,n} = (p + 1) \mathcal{L}_{p,n} - p \mathcal{L}_{p,n-1}$
for every natural number $n$.

## Sources

- Amine Belkhir and Elif Tan, *Combinatorial Insights into Leonardo `p`-Numbers and Lucas-Leonardo `p`-Numbers*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A57, Proposition 14.

articles.title: Lucas-Leonardo $p$-numbers from Lucas $p$-numbers
articles.statement:
For every $p \ge 1$ and every
natural number $n$, the Lucas-Leonardo $p$-number $R_{p,n}$ and the Lucas $p$-number $L_{p,n}$
satisfy $R_{p,n} = (p + 1) L_{p,n} - p$.

## Sources

- Amine Belkhir and Elif Tan, *Combinatorial Insights into Leonardo `p`-Numbers and Lucas-Leonardo `p`-Numbers*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A57, Proposition 13.

articles.title: Lucas-Leonardo $p$-numbers at indices $1$ to $p$
articles.statement:
For every natural number $p$ and every
$n$ with $1 \le n \le p$, the Lucas-Leonardo $p$-number $R_{p,n}$ equals $1$.

## Sources

- Belkhir and Tan, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A57, display (5).

articles.title: Recurrence for the Lucas-Leonardo $p$-numbers
articles.statement:
For every natural number $p$, write
$R_{p,n}$ for the Lucas-Leonardo $p$-numbers. Then $R_{p,n} = R_{p,n-1} + R_{p,n-p-1} + p$ for
every $n > p$.

## Sources

- Belkhir and Tan, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A57, display (5).

articles.title: Initial Lucas-Leonardo $p$-number
articles.statement:
For every natural number $p$, the Lucas-Leonardo
