coefficient of $q^n$ in $\Delta$. Let $N_w = 1$ for $w \le 2$, let $N_w$ be the absolute value of
the numerator of $\sigma_{w-1}(0)$ for $w \ge 3$, and let $N'_k$ be the largest divisor of $N_k$
that is coprime to $N_{k-12i}$ for every $1 \le i \le \lfloor k/12 \rfloor$. For rationals $x, y$
and a positive integer $N$, $x \equiv y \pmod{N}$ means that $(x - y)/N$ has denominator coprime
to $N$. Let $m = \lfloor k/12 \rfloor - 1$ if $k \equiv 2 \pmod{12}$ and
$m = \lfloor k/12 \rfloor$ otherwise, let $C$ be the $m \times m$ matrix
$\bigl(c_i(j)/\sigma_{k-12i-1}(0)\bigr)_{1 \le i, j \le m}$, and let
$(\gamma_1, \dots, \gamma_m) = (\sigma_{k-1}(1), \dots, \sigma_{k-1}(m))\, C^{-1}$. Then for every
$n \ge 1$, $\sigma_{k-1}(n) \equiv
\sum_{i=1}^m \bigl(\gamma_i/\sigma_{k-12i-1}(0)\bigr)\, c_i(n) \pmod{N'_k}$.

## Sources

- Qing Lu, *Explicit Congruences for Modular Forms of Higher Weights*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.5.1, Corollary 3 (`jis-2026-26.5.1-cor-3`).

articles.title: Hecke operator as an additive homomorphism
articles.statement: The Hecke operator `T(g)` as an additive monoid homomorphism.

articles.title: Hecke operator as a function on fixed points
articles.statement: The Hecke operator `T(g)` as a function on fixed points.

articles.title: Hecke operator
articles.statement: The Hecke operator `T(g)` as a linear map on fixed points.

articles.title: Invariance under a subgroup of the modular group
articles.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a subgroup of
$\mathrm{SL}(2, \mathbb{Z})$. A function $f \colon \mathbb{H} \to \mathbb{C}$ on the upper
half-plane is invariant under $\Gamma$ when $f(\gamma \cdot \tau) = f(\tau)$ for every
$\gamma \in \Gamma$ and every $\tau \in \mathbb{H}$, where $\gamma$ acts on $\mathbb{H}$ by
Möbius transformations.

articles.title: Meromorphy at the cusps
articles.statement:
A function $f \colon \mathbb{H} \to \mathbb{C}$ on the upper
half-plane is meromorphic at the cusps when, for every $\gamma \in \mathrm{SL}(2, \mathbb{Z})$,
the function $\tau \mapsto f(\gamma \cdot \tau)$ is meromorphic at infinity, where $\gamma$ acts
on $\mathbb{H}$ by Möbius transformations.

articles.title: Meromorphy at infinity
articles.statement:
A function $f \colon \mathbb{H} \to \mathbb{C}$ on the upper
half-plane is meromorphic at infinity when there are a positive integer $N$ and a function
$g \colon \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ meromorphic at $0$ such that
$f(\tau) = g(e^{2 \pi i \tau / N})$ for every $\tau \in \mathbb{H}$ with sufficiently large
imaginary part.

articles.title: Meromorphy on the upper half-plane
articles.statement:
A function $f \colon \mathbb{H} \to \mathbb{C}$ on
the upper half-plane is meromorphic when there is a function $g \colon \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$
that is meromorphic on the open set $\{z \in \mathbb{C} : \operatorname{Im} z > 0\}$ and
satisfies $g(\tau) = f(\tau)$ for every $\tau \in \mathbb{H}$.

articles.title: Modular functions
articles.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a subgroup of $\mathrm{SL}(2, \mathbb{Z})$. A function
$f \colon \mathbb{H} \to \mathbb{C}$ on the upper half-plane is a modular function for $\Gamma$
when it is meromorphic on $\mathbb{H}$, invariant under $\Gamma$, and meromorphic at the cusps.

No congruence hypothesis is assumed on $\Gamma$.

articles.title: Parabolic elements of SL(2, ℤ) are conjugate to ± powers of T
articles.statement:
Every element of `SL(2, ℤ)` whose trace squares to `4` is, up to a sign,
conjugate to a power of the translation `T`.

articles.title: Reduction mod p maps Γ(N) onto SL(2, ℤ/pℤ) when p does not divide N
articles.statement:
If `p` does not divide `N`, then reduction modulo `p` maps `Γ(N)` onto
`SL(2, ZMod p)`.

articles.title: Membership in a subgroup joined with a central involution
articles.statement:
Membership in the join of a subgroup with the cyclic subgroup generated
by a central involution.

This is the computation behind "up to sign" arguments: for a subgroup
`Γ` of `SL(2, ℤ)`, an element lies in `Γ` adjoined with `-1` exactly when
it or its negative lies in `Γ`. The same pattern recurs for any group with
a central involution: spin groups, dihedral groups, and congruence
subgroups.

articles.title: −1 lies in Γ₁(N) exactly when N ≤ 2
articles.statement: `-1` lies in `Γ₁(N)` if and only if `N ≤ 2`.

articles.title: 1 is a strict period of Γ₀(N)
articles.statement:
`1` is a strict period of `Γ₀(N)`: the translation matrix `T` lies in
`Γ₀(N)`, and the strict periods then contain the integer multiples of `1`.

articles.title: Admissible exponents of a local-exponent family
articles.statement:
For a local-exponent family $F$ with
local exponents $m_i$ ($i \in \iota$), the set of admissible exponents of $F$ is the set of real
numbers $\delta \ge 0$ such that $F$ is admissible at $\delta$, that is, $m_i \le \delta$ for
every index $i$.

articles.title: Families dominating the Selberg exceptional spectrum
articles.statement:
A local-exponent family $F$ with
local exponents $m_i$ ($i \in \iota$) dominates the Selberg archimedean slice when, for every
congruence subgroup $\Gamma$ of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ and every eigenvalue $\lambda$ of the
hyperbolic Laplacian on $L^2(\Gamma \backslash \mathbb{H})$ with $0 < \lambda < 1/4$, there is an
index $i$ with $m_i = \sqrt{1/4 - \lambda}$.

This is the precise anchor needed for the comparison with Selberg's constant; it is a hypothesis
on a proposed genuine family, not a definition of one.

articles.title: Local exponents are bounded by the Ramanujan exponent
articles.statement:
For every local-exponent family $F$
and every index $i$, the local exponent $m_i$ of $F$ at $i$ is at most the Ramanujan exponent of
$F$.

articles.title: Exponent set of a local-exponent family
articles.statement:
For a local-exponent family $F$ indexed by a type
$\iota$, with local exponents $m(i)$ for $i \in \iota$, the exponent set of $F$ is the set of real
numbers $\{0\} \cup \{m(i) : i \in \iota\}$.

The adjoined $0$ makes the supremum of this set the correct value when $\iota$ is empty and in the
tempered case, where every local exponent is $0$.

articles.title: Generalized Ramanujan conjecture for a family
articles.statement:
A local-exponent family $F$ satisfies the
Generalized Ramanujan conclusion when every local exponent $m_i$ of $F$ ($i \in \iota$) is zero.

articles.title: Hecke bound from a Satake pair at a finite place
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field, $v$ a finite
place of $K$ with residue norm $N(v)$, and $t, \delta$ real numbers with $0 \le t \le \delta$. If
complex numbers $\alpha, \beta$ form a Satake pair with local exponent $t$ at residue cardinality
$N(v)$, then $|\alpha + \beta| \le 2 N(v)^\delta$.

articles.title: Hecke bound from a Satake pair
articles.statement:
Let $N \ge 1$ and $t, \delta$ be real numbers with
$0 \le t \le \delta$. If complex numbers $\alpha, \beta$ form a Satake pair with local exponent
$t$ at residue cardinality $N$, then $|\alpha + \beta| \le 2 N^\delta$.

The catalogue also records the sharper expression $N^\delta + N^{-\delta}$; the bound proved here
is its displayed consequence $2N^\delta$.

articles.title: Admissibility is a bound by the Ramanujan exponent
articles.statement:
For every local-exponent family $F$ and
every real $\delta \ge 0$, $F$ is admissible at $\delta$ if and only if the Ramanujan exponent of
$F$ is at most $\delta$.

articles.title: The Ramanujan exponent is admissible
articles.statement:
For every local-exponent family $F$, $F$ is admissible
at its Ramanujan exponent: every local exponent of $F$ is at most the Ramanujan exponent of $F$.

articles.title: Admissibility of an exponent for a local-exponent family
articles.statement:
A local-exponent family $F$ is
admissible at a real number $\delta$ (Hypothesis $H_2(\delta)$ for $F$) when every local exponent
$m_i$ of $F$ ($i \in \iota$) is at most $\delta$.

articles.title: Satake pairs with a given local exponent
articles.statement:
For real numbers $N$ and $t$, a pair
$(\alpha, \beta)$ of complex numbers is in arithmetic Satake normalization with local exponent $t$
at residue cardinality $N$ when $|\alpha\beta| = 1$, $|\alpha| = N^t$ and $|\beta| = N^{-t}$.

articles.title: Family of local exponents
articles.statement:
A local-exponent family indexed by a type $\iota$ is a function
$m : \iota \to \mathbb{R}$, the local Langlands exponents, with $0 \le m(i) \le 1/2$ for every
$i \in \iota$.

The upper bound $1/2$ is the Jacquet--Shalika range for genuine cuspidal data. The index type is
part of the data, so the exponent of such a family is a construction attached to the family, not
a definition of the fixed Ramanujan exponent $\delta_2$ of $\mathrm{GL}_2$.

articles.title: The Ramanujan exponent is the infimum of the admissible exponents
articles.statement:
For every
local-exponent family $F$, the Ramanujan exponent of $F$ equals the infimum of the admissible
exponents of $F$, that is, of the set of real numbers $\delta \ge 0$ such that every local
exponent of $F$ is at most $\delta$.

articles.title: The Ramanujan exponent vanishes exactly in the tempered case
articles.statement:
For every local-exponent
family $F$, the Ramanujan exponent of $F$ is $0$ if and only if $F$ satisfies the generalized
Ramanujan conclusion, that is, every local exponent of $F$ is $0$.

articles.title: Admissible exponents bound the Ramanujan exponent
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a local-exponent family and
let $\delta \ge 0$ be a real number. If $\delta$ is admissible for $F$, that is, every local
exponent of $F$ is at most $\delta$, then the Ramanujan exponent of $F$ is at most $\delta$.

articles.title: The Selberg family's exponent is Selberg's constant
articles.statement:
The Ramanujan exponent of the
canonical Selberg family of archimedean exponents is exactly Selberg's congruence spectral-gap
constant.

This identifies the currently anchored archimedean slice; it does not identify that slice with
the full Ramanujan exponent.

articles.title: Ramanujan exponent of a local-exponent family
articles.statement:
The Ramanujan exponent of a local-exponent
family $F$ with local exponents $m(i)$, $i \in \iota$, is the supremum of the set
$\{0\} \cup \{m(i) : i \in \iota\}$. It is the supremum of the local exponents when $\iota$ is
nonempty, and $0$ when $\iota$ is empty.

For the eventual genuine family of cuspidal local components of $\mathrm{GL}_2$ this will be the
Ramanujan exponent $\delta_2$; for other families it is only the supremum of the given
exponents.

articles.title: Selberg's constant is at most every dominating family's exponent
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a
local-exponent family that dominates the Selberg archimedean slice, that is, for every
congruence subgroup $\Gamma$ of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ and every Laplace eigenvalue
$\lambda \in (0, 1/4)$ of $\Gamma$, the gap $\sqrt{1/4 - \lambda}$ is one of the local exponents
of $F$. Then Selberg's constant is at most the Ramanujan exponent of $F$.

For the genuine cuspidal family this is the archimedean comparison of Selberg's constant with the
Ramanujan exponent $\delta_2$; it is not an equality of constants.

articles.title: Selberg family of archimedean exponents
articles.statement:
The Selberg family is the local-exponent family
indexed by the exceptional-eigenvalue witnesses, the pairs $(\Gamma, \lambda)$ of a congruence
subgroup $\Gamma$ of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ and a Laplace eigenvalue $\lambda \in (0, 1/4)$
of $\Gamma$, whose local exponent at $(\Gamma, \lambda)$ is $\sqrt{1/4 - \lambda}$.

articles.title: Selberg gap of an exceptional eigenvalue
articles.statement:
For an exceptional-eigenvalue witness, a
congruence subgroup $\Gamma$ of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ with a Laplace eigenvalue
$\lambda \in (0, 1/4)$, the Selberg gap is $\sqrt{1/4 - \lambda}$: the archimedean local exponent
$\theta$ forced by $\lambda$, written as $\lambda = 1/4 - \theta^2$.

articles.title: Exceptional Selberg eigenvalue witnesses
articles.statement:
The type of pairs $(\Gamma, \lambda)$ where
$\Gamma$ is a congruence subgroup of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ and $\lambda$ is a real
eigenvalue of the hyperbolic Laplacian on $L^2(\Gamma \backslash \mathbb{H})$ with
$0 < \lambda < 1/4$.

Morally, these pairs index archimedean local components over $\mathbb{Q}$; their
identification with genuine cuspidal automorphic local components is a modelling assumption.

articles.title: Exceptional eigenvalues bound Selberg-dominating exponents from below
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a
local-exponent family that dominates the Selberg archimedean slice. If $\Gamma$ is a congruence
subgroup of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ and $\lambda$ is a real eigenvalue of the hyperbolic
Laplacian on $L^2(\Gamma \backslash \mathbb{H})$ with $0 < \lambda < 1/4$, then
$\sqrt{1/4 - \lambda}$ is at most the Ramanujan exponent of $F$.

articles.title: Normalisation of the Ramanujan τ-function
articles.statement:
The Ramanujan τ-function satisfies
$\tau(1) = 1$: the coefficient of $q$ in the $q$-expansion of the modular discriminant $\Delta$
is $1$.

articles.title: Ramanujan–Petersson conjecture for τ (Deligne's theorem)
articles.statement:
For every prime $p$, the
Ramanujan τ-function satisfies $|\tau(p)| \le 2p^{11/2}$, where $|\cdot|$ is the absolute value
of a complex number.

## Sources

- S. Ramanujan, 'On certain arithmetical functions', Trans. Cambridge Philos. Soc. 22 (1916) 159–184. H. Petersson, 'Theorie der automorphen Formen beliebiger reeller Dimension und ihre Darstellung durch eine neue Art Poincaréscher Reihen', Math. Ann. 103 (1930) 369–436. P. Deligne, 'Formes modulaires et représentations ℓ-adiques', Séminaire Bourbaki 1968/69: Exposés 347–363, Lecture Notes in Math. 179, Springer (1971). P. Deligne, 'La conjecture de Weil. I', Publ. Math. IHÉS 43 (1974) 273–307. Background: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramanujan%E2%80%93Petersson_conjecture. Problem `ramanujan_petersson` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Ramanujan τ-function
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$, $\tau(n)$ is the complex number given by
the coefficient of $q^n$ in the $q$-expansion of the modular discriminant $\Delta = \eta^{24}$,
where $\eta$ is the Dedekind eta function and $q = e^{2\pi i z}$.

articles.title: Normalized cusp form coefficient at one
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be a cusp form of weight
$k \in \mathbb{Z}$ for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$, with $q$-expansion
$f(z) = \sum_{n \ge 0} a_f(n) e^{2\pi i n z}$, and let $\lambda_f$ be its normalized Fourier
coefficients. Then $\lambda_f(1) = a_f(1)$, the coefficient of $e^{2\pi i z}$ in the
$q$-expansion of $f$.

## Sources

- Guodong Hua, *The General Divisor Problem of Cusp Form Coefficients over Arithmetic Progressions*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A3, Section 1.

articles.title: Normalized Fourier coefficients of a cusp form
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be a cusp form of weight
$k \in \mathbb{Z}$ for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$, with $q$-expansion
$f(z) = \sum_{n \ge 0} a_f(n) e(nz)$, where $e(z) = e^{2\pi i z}$. For each natural number $n$,
the normalized Fourier coefficient of $f$ is the complex number
$\lambda_f(n) = a_f(n) / n^{(k-1)/2}$, where $n^{(k-1)/2}$ is the real power.

At $n = 0$ the real power follows $0^0 = 1$ and $0^s = 0$ for $s \ne 0$, and division by $0$
gives $0$.

## Sources

- Guodong Hua, *The General Divisor Problem of Cusp Form Coefficients over Arithmetic Progressions*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A3, Section 1 (Fourier expansion of `f ∈ H_k^*`).

articles.title: Normalized Hecke eigenform
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be a cusp form of weight $k \in \mathbb{Z}$ for
$\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$, with normalized Fourier coefficients $\lambda_f$. Then $f$ is a
normalized Hecke eigenform when $\lambda_f(1) = 1$ and, for all positive integers $m$ and $n$,
$\lambda_f(m) \lambda_f(n) = \sum_{d \mid \gcd(m, n)} \lambda_f(mn/d^2)$, the sum running over the
positive divisors $d$ of $\gcd(m, n)$. The set of these forms is denoted $H_k^*$.

At level one this is equivalent to $f$ being a simultaneous eigenform of all Hecke operators
normalized by $a_f(1) = 1$, where $f(z) = \sum_{n \ge 0} a_f(n) e^{2\pi i n z}$ is the
$q$-expansion of $f$.

## Sources

- Guodong Hua, *The General Divisor Problem of Cusp Form Coefficients over Arithmetic Progressions*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A3, Section 1, Equation (1).

articles.title: Hecke relation at the square of a prime
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be a normalized Hecke eigenform of weight
$k \in \mathbb{Z}$ for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$, with normalized Fourier coefficients
$\lambda_f$. Then $\lambda_f(p)^2 = \lambda_f(p^2) + 1$ for every prime $p$.

## Sources

- Guodong Hua, *The General Divisor Problem of Cusp Form Coefficients over Arithmetic Progressions*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A3, Equation (1) with `m = n = p`.

articles.title: Rankin–Selberg coefficients as a sum over square divisors
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be a cusp form of
weight $k \in \mathbb{Z}$ for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$, with normalized Fourier coefficients
$\lambda_f$ and Rankin–Selberg coefficients $\lambda_{f \times f}$. For every natural number $n$,
$\lambda_{f \times f}(n) = \sum_d \lambda_f(n/d)^2$, where $d$ runs over the positive divisors of
$n$ that are perfect squares (so the sum is empty when $n = 0$).

## Sources

- Guodong Hua, *The General Divisor Problem of Cusp Form Coefficients over Arithmetic Progressions*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A3, Section 1.

articles.title: Rankin–Selberg coefficient at one
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be a cusp form of weight $k \in \mathbb{Z}$ for
$\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$, with normalized Fourier coefficients $\lambda_f$ and Rankin–Selberg
coefficients $\lambda_{f \times f}$. Then $\lambda_{f \times f}(1) = \lambda_f(1)^2$.

## Sources

- Guodong Hua, *The General Divisor Problem of Cusp Form Coefficients over Arithmetic Progressions*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A3, Section 1.

articles.title: Rankin–Selberg coefficients at primes
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be a cusp form of weight $k \in \mathbb{Z}$
for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$, with normalized Fourier coefficients $\lambda_f$ and
Rankin–Selberg coefficients $\lambda_{f \times f}$. Then $\lambda_{f \times f}(p) = \lambda_f(p)^2$
for every prime $p$.

## Sources

- Guodong Hua, *The General Divisor Problem of Cusp Form Coefficients over Arithmetic Progressions*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A3, Section 1.

articles.title: Rankin–Selberg coefficients
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be a cusp form of weight $k \in \mathbb{Z}$ for
$\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$, with normalized Fourier coefficients $\lambda_f$. The Rankin–Selberg
coefficients of $f$ form the arithmetic function $\lambda_{f \times f}$ with
$\lambda_{f \times f}(0) = 0$ and, for $n \ge 1$,
$\lambda_{f \times f}(n) = \sum_{l^2 m = n} \lambda_f(m)^2$, the sum running over the pairs of
positive integers $(l, m)$ with $l^2 m = n$; equivalently, $\lambda_{f \times f}(n)$ is the sum of
$\lambda_f(n/d)^2$ over the positive divisors $d$ of $n$ that are perfect squares.

These are the Dirichlet coefficients of
$L(f \times f, s) = \zeta(2s) \sum_{n \ge 1} \lambda_f(n)^2 n^{-s}$. The $w$-th power of
$\lambda_{f \times f}$ under Dirichlet convolution is denoted $\lambda_{w, f \times f}$.

## Sources

- Guodong Hua, *The General Divisor Problem of Cusp Form Coefficients over Arithmetic Progressions*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A3, Section 1 (definition of `λ_{f×f}` and `λ_{w,f×f}`).

articles.title: Sums of squared normalized coefficients at perfect powers in arithmetic progressions
articles.statement:
Let
$f$ be a normalized Hecke eigenform of weight $k \in \mathbb{Z}$ for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$,
with normalized Fourier coefficients $\lambda_f$, let $j \ge 2$ be an integer, and put
$\delta = 92/597$ if $j = 2$ and $\delta = 92/(69(j-1)(j+3) + 247)$ if $j \ge 3$. Then there are
real numbers $c_q > 0$, one for each prime $q$, with the following property: for every
$\varepsilon > 0$ there is a real constant $C$ such that for every prime $q$, every natural
number $l$ coprime to $q$ and every real $x \ge 1$ with $q \le x^{3\delta/4}$,
$\bigl|\sum_{n} \lambda_f(n^j)^2 - c_q x / \varphi(q)\bigr| \le
C q x^{1 - 3\delta/2 + \varepsilon}$, where $n$ runs over the integers $1 \le n \le x$ with
$n \equiv l \pmod q$ and $\varphi$ is Euler's totient function.

Hua quotes this result from Zou et al. [52, Theorem 1]. The constant $c_q$ is allowed to depend
on $q$, a weaker reading of the printed main term, whose constant does not depend on $q$; the
constant $C$ depends only on $f$, $j$ and $\varepsilon$.

## Sources

- Guodong Hua, *The General Divisor Problem of Cusp Form Coefficients over Arithmetic Progressions*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A3, Theorem 1.1.

articles.title: Sums of Rankin–Selberg convolution powers in arithmetic progressions
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be a
normalized Hecke eigenform of weight $k \in \mathbb{Z}$ for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$, with
Rankin–Selberg coefficients $\lambda_{f \times f}$, let $w \ge 2$ be an integer, write
$\lambda_{w, f \times f}$ for the $w$-fold Dirichlet convolution power of $\lambda_{f \times f}$,
and put $\vartheta_w = 92/(247w + 10)$. Then there are real polynomials $P_q$, one for each prime
$q$, each of degree $w - 1$ with positive leading coefficient, with the following property: for
every $\varepsilon > 0$ there is a real constant $C$ such that for every prime $q$, every natural
number $l$ coprime to $q$ and every real $x \ge 1$ with $q \le x^{\vartheta_w}$,
$\bigl|\sum_{n} \lambda_{w, f \times f}(n) - (x / \varphi(q)) P_q(\log x)\bigr| \le
C q x^{1 - 3\vartheta_w/2 + \varepsilon}$, where $n$ runs over the integers $1 \le n \le x$ with
$n \equiv l \pmod q$, $\varphi$ is Euler's totient function and $\log$ is the natural logarithm.

The printed hypothesis $q \ll x^{\vartheta_w}$ is read as $q \le x^{\vartheta_w}$, and the
polynomial is allowed to depend on $q$; the constant $C$ depends only on $f$, $w$ and
$\varepsilon$.

## Sources

- Guodong Hua, *The General Divisor Problem of Cusp Form Coefficients over Arithmetic Progressions*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A3, Theorem 1.3.

articles.title: Sums of Rankin–Selberg convolution powers twisted by a primitive character
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be a
level-one cusp form of weight $k$ that is a normalized Hecke eigenform, let $\lambda_{f\times f}$
be its Rankin–Selberg coefficients, let $w \ge 2$, let $\lambda_{w,f\times f}$ be the $w$-th
power of $\lambda_{f\times f}$ under Dirichlet convolution, and put
$\vartheta_w = 92/(247w + 10)$. For every $\varepsilon > 0$ there is a constant $C$ such that for
every prime $q$, every primitive Dirichlet character $\chi$ modulo $q$ and every real $x \ge 1$
with $q \le x^{\vartheta_w}$,

$$
\Bigl|\sum_{1 \le n \le x} \lambda_{w,f\times f}(n)\,\chi(n)\Bigr| \le
C\,q\,x^{1 - 3\vartheta_w/2 + \varepsilon}.
$$

## Sources

- Guodong Hua, *The General Divisor Problem of Cusp Form Coefficients over Arithmetic Progressions*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A3, Proposition 4.1.

articles.title: Sums of Rankin–Selberg convolution powers twisted by the principal character
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be a
level-one cusp form of weight $k$ that is a normalized Hecke eigenform, let $\lambda_{f\times f}$
be its Rankin–Selberg coefficients, let $w \ge 2$, let $\lambda_{w,f\times f}$ be the $w$-th
power of $\lambda_{f\times f}$ under Dirichlet convolution, and for a prime $q$ let $\chi_0$ be
the principal Dirichlet character modulo $q$. There are real polynomials $P_q$, one for each
prime $q$, each of degree $w - 1$, such that for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there is a constant $C$
with

$$
\Bigl|\sum_{1 \le n \le x} \lambda_{w,f\times f}(n)\,\chi_0(n) - x\,P_q(\log x)\Bigr| \le
C\,x^{1 - 210/(317w + 115) + \varepsilon}
$$

for every prime $q$ and every real $x \ge q$.

## Sources

- Guodong Hua, *The General Divisor Problem of Cusp Form Coefficients over Arithmetic Progressions*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A3, Proposition 4.2.

articles.title: Hua's theorem on squared Rankin–Selberg coefficients in arithmetic progressions
articles.statement:
Let $f$
be a level-one cusp form of weight $k$ that is a normalized Hecke eigenform, let
$\lambda_{f\times f}$ be its Rankin–Selberg coefficients, let $\varphi$ be Euler's totient
function, and put $\eta = 23/261$. There are real polynomials $P_q$, one for each prime $q$, each
of degree $1$ with positive leading coefficient, such that for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there is a
constant $C$ with

$$
\Bigl|\sum_{\substack{1 \le n \le x \\ n \equiv l \ (\mathrm{mod}\ q)}} \lambda_{f\times f}(n)^2 -
\frac{x}{\varphi(q)}\,P_q(\log x)\Bigr| \le C\,q\,x^{1 - 3\eta/2 + \varepsilon}
$$

for every prime $q$, every natural number $l$ coprime to $q$ and every real $x \ge 1$ with
$q \le x^{\eta}$.

## Sources

- Guodong Hua, *The General Divisor Problem of Cusp Form Coefficients over Arithmetic Progressions*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A3, Theorem 1.2.

articles.title: Sums of squared Rankin–Selberg coefficients twisted by a primitive character
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be
a level-one cusp form of weight $k$ that is a normalized Hecke eigenform, let
$\lambda_{f\times f}$ be its Rankin–Selberg coefficients, and put $\eta = 23/261$. For every
$\varepsilon > 0$ there is a constant $C$ such that for every prime $q$, every primitive Dirichlet
character $\chi$ modulo $q$ and every real $x \ge 1$ with $q \le x^{\eta}$,

$$
\Bigl|\sum_{1 \le n \le x} \lambda_{f\times f}(n)^2\,\chi(n)\Bigr| \le
C\,q\,x^{1 - 3\eta/2 + \varepsilon}.
$$

## Sources

- Guodong Hua, *The General Divisor Problem of Cusp Form Coefficients over Arithmetic Progressions*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A3, Proposition 3.1.

articles.title: Sums of squared Rankin–Selberg coefficients twisted by the principal character
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be
a level-one cusp form of weight $k$ that is a normalized Hecke eigenform, let
$\lambda_{f\times f}$ be its Rankin–Selberg coefficients, and for a prime $q$ let $\chi_0$ be the
principal Dirichlet character modulo $q$. There are real polynomials $P_q$, one for each prime
$q$, each of degree $1$ with positive leading coefficient, such that for every $\varepsilon > 0$
there is a constant $C$ with

$$
\Bigl|\sum_{1 \le n \le x} \lambda_{f\times f}(n)^2\,\chi_0(n) - x\,P_q(\log x)\Bigr| \le
C\,x^{179/209 + \varepsilon}
$$

for every prime $q$ and every real $x \ge q$.

## Sources

- Guodong Hua, *The General Divisor Problem of Cusp Form Coefficients over Arithmetic Progressions*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A3, Proposition 3.2.

articles.title: Congruence gaps are bounded by Selberg's constant
articles.statement:
For every congruence subgroup
$\Gamma$ of $\mathrm{SL}(2, \mathbb{Z})$, the gap parameter $\theta(\Gamma)$ is at most the
Selberg constant $C_{61}$.

articles.title: Gap parameter of a subgroup of the modular group
articles.statement:
For a subgroup $\Gamma$ of
$\mathrm{SL}(2, \mathbb{Z})$, the gap parameter $\theta(\Gamma)$ is the supremum of the set of
gap contributions of $\Gamma$: the number $0$ together with $\sqrt{1/4 - \lambda}$ for every
real eigenvalue $\lambda$ of the hyperbolic Laplacian for $\Gamma$ with $0 < \lambda < 1/4$.

articles.title: Gap contributions of a subgroup of the modular group
articles.statement:
For a subgroup $\Gamma$ of
$\mathrm{SL}(2, \mathbb{Z})$, the set of gap contributions of $\Gamma$ is the set of real
numbers consisting of $0$ together with $\sqrt{1/4 - \lambda}$ for every real eigenvalue
$\lambda$ of the hyperbolic Laplacian for $\Gamma$ with $0 < \lambda < 1/4$ (an exceptional
eigenvalue).

articles.title: Zero extension from the upper half plane
articles.statement:
For a function $f$ from the upper half plane
to $\mathbb{C}$, its zero extension is the function from $\mathbb{C}$ to $\mathbb{C}$ that takes
the value $f(z)$ at every $z$ with $\operatorname{Im} z > 0$ and the value $0$ at every other
point.

It is used to read coordinate derivatives of $f$ in the interior.

articles.title: Standard fundamental domain of the modular group
articles.statement:
The standard fundamental domain for
$\mathrm{SL}(2, \mathbb{Z})$ is the set of points $z$ of the upper half plane with
$|\operatorname{Re} z| \le 1/2$ and $|z| \ge 1$.

articles.title: The hyperbolic Laplacian kills constants
articles.statement:
For every complex number $c$ and every
point $z$ of the upper half plane, the hyperbolic Laplacian of the constant function with
value $c$ at $z$ is $0$.

articles.title: Hyperbolic Laplacian of the squared imaginary part
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be the function on the upper
half plane given by $f(u) = (\operatorname{Im} u)^2$, viewed as a complex number. Then for
every point $z$ of the upper half plane the hyperbolic Laplacian of $f$ at $z$ equals
$-2 (\operatorname{Im} z)^2$.

This is a non-holomorphic check: the value is not zero, whereas with complex derivatives the
computation would collapse by Cauchy--Riemann.

articles.title: Hyperbolic Laplacian
articles.statement:
For a function $f$ from the upper half plane to $\mathbb{C}$ and a
point $z = x + iy$ of the upper half plane, the hyperbolic Laplacian of $f$ at $z$ is

$$\Delta f(z) = -y^2 \left(\partial_x \partial_x f(z) + \partial_y \partial_y f(z)\right),$$

where, for a function $g$ from the upper half plane to $\mathbb{C}$, $\partial_x g(z)$ and
$\partial_y g(z)$ are the real Fréchet derivatives at $z$ of the zero extension of $g$ to
$\mathbb{C}$, applied to the vectors $1$ and $i$ respectively (taken to be $0$ where that
extension is not real differentiable).

On smooth functions this agrees with the coordinate formula
$-y^2 (\partial^2 f / \partial x^2 + \partial^2 f / \partial y^2)$ at every interior point.

articles.title: The modular group is a congruence subgroup
articles.statement:
The full group
$\mathrm{SL}(2, \mathbb{Z})$, as a subgroup of itself, is a congruence subgroup.

It contains the principal congruence subgroup of level $1$, which is the whole group.

articles.title: Congruence subgroup of the modular group
articles.statement:
A subgroup $\Gamma$ of
$\mathrm{SL}(2, \mathbb{Z})$ is a congruence subgroup if there is a positive integer $N$
such that every $\gamma \in \mathrm{SL}(2, \mathbb{Z})$ whose entries are congruent modulo
$N$ to those of the identity matrix lies in $\Gamma$; that is, $\Gamma$ contains the
principal congruence subgroup of level $N$.

articles.title: Finite coset covers of the modular group
articles.statement:
A finite set
$s \subseteq \mathrm{SL}(2, \mathbb{Z})$ covers $\mathrm{SL}(2, \mathbb{Z})$ by cosets of a subgroup
$\Gamma$ when every $g \in \mathrm{SL}(2, \mathbb{Z})$ can be written as $g = \gamma a$ with
$\gamma \in \Gamma$ and $a \in s$, that is, when the cosets $\Gamma a$ with $a \in s$ cover
$\mathrm{SL}(2, \mathbb{Z})$. The elements of $s$ need not lie in distinct cosets.

articles.title: Eigenvalues of the hyperbolic Laplacian on a modular quotient
articles.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a subgroup
of $\mathrm{SL}(2, \mathbb{Z})$. A real number $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of the hyperbolic
Laplacian $\Delta$ for $\Gamma$ when there is a function $f \colon \mathbb{H} \to \mathbb{C}$ on
the upper half plane $\mathbb{H}$ such that $f$ is not identically zero, $f$ is the restriction of
a function on $\mathbb{C}$ that is twice continuously differentiable in the real sense on the
upper half plane, $f(\gamma z) = f(z)$ for every $\gamma \in \Gamma$ and every $z \in \mathbb{H}$
(Möbius action), $f$ is square-integrable on $\Gamma \backslash \mathbb{H}$, and
$\Delta f(z) = \lambda f(z)$ for every $z \in \mathbb{H}$.

articles.title: Square-integrable functions on a modular quotient
articles.statement:
For a subgroup $\Gamma$ of
$\mathrm{SL}(2, \mathbb{Z})$, a function $f \colon \mathbb{H} \to \mathbb{C}$ is
square-integrable on $\Gamma \backslash \mathbb{H}$ when there is a finite set
$s \subseteq \mathrm{SL}(2, \mathbb{Z})$ whose cosets $\Gamma a$, $a \in s$, cover
$\mathrm{SL}(2, \mathbb{Z})$, such that

$$\int_{U} |f(z)|^2 \, d\mu(z) < \infty, \qquad U = \bigcup_{a \in s} a \cdot \mathcal{F},$$

where $\mathcal{F} = \{z \in \mathbb{H} : |\operatorname{Re} z| \le 1/2,\ |z| \ge 1\}$ is the
standard fundamental domain of $\mathrm{SL}(2, \mathbb{Z})$, $a \cdot \mathcal{F}$ is its image
under the Möbius action of $a$, and $\mu$ is the hyperbolic area measure $dx \, dy / y^2$ on
$\mathbb{H}$.

articles.title: Twice continuously differentiable functions on the upper half-plane
articles.statement:
A function
$f \colon \mathbb{H} \to \mathbb{C}$ is smooth (of order two) when it is the restriction of a
function $F \colon \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ that is twice continuously differentiable, in the real
sense, on the open set $\{z \in \mathbb{C} : \operatorname{Im} z > 0\}$.

Differentiability is real, not complex: eigenfunctions of the Laplacian need not be holomorphic.

articles.title: Kim–Sarnak eigenvalue bound
articles.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a congruence subgroup of
$\mathrm{SL}(2, \mathbb{Z})$ and let $\lambda$ be a real eigenvalue of the hyperbolic Laplacian
$\Delta$ for $\Gamma$, that is, $\Delta f = \lambda f$ for some nonzero, twice continuously
differentiable, $\Gamma$-invariant function $f$ on the upper half plane that is square-integrable
on $\Gamma \backslash \mathbb{H}$. Then $\lambda$ does not lie in the open interval
$(0, 975/4096)$: either $\lambda \le 0$ or $\lambda \ge 975/4096$.

## Sources

- Kim--Sarnak (2003), as recorded in Kim--Ramakrishnan (2003): no eigenvalue of a congruence subgroup lies in `(0, 975/4096)`.

articles.title: Kim–Sarnak bound on the spectral-gap constant
articles.statement:
Selberg's congruence spectral-gap constant
$C_{61}$ is at most $7/64$.

## Sources

- Kim--Sarnak bound `λ₁(Γ) ≥ 975/4096 = 1/4 - (7/64)^2`, catalogue best upper row `C₆₁ ≤ 7/64`.

articles.title: Partial derivative in the imaginary direction
articles.statement:
For a function
$f \colon \mathbb{H} \to \mathbb{C}$ and a point $z \in \mathbb{H}$, $\partial_y f(z)$ is the real
Fréchet derivative at $z$ of the zero extension of $f$ to $\mathbb{C}$, applied to the vector $i$.
When the zero extension is real-differentiable at $z$ this is the partial derivative of $f$ with
respect to $y = \operatorname{Im} z$; otherwise the value is $0$.

articles.title: Partial derivative in the real direction
articles.statement:
For a function
$f \colon \mathbb{H} \to \mathbb{C}$ and a point $z \in \mathbb{H}$, $\partial_x f(z)$ is the real
Fréchet derivative at $z$ of the zero extension of $f$ to $\mathbb{C}$, applied to the vector $1$.
When the zero extension is real-differentiable at $z$ this is the partial derivative of $f$ with
respect to $x = \operatorname{Re} z$; otherwise the value is $0$.

Real, not complex, differentiability is essential: with complex derivatives the two second
derivatives in the hyperbolic Laplacian would cancel by the Cauchy–Riemann equations, and the
Laplacian would vanish identically.

articles.title: Selberg's constant vanishes exactly under Selberg's eigenvalue conjecture
articles.statement:
Selberg's
constant $C_{61}$ equals $0$ if and only if Selberg's eigenvalue conjecture holds, that is, if and
only if no congruence subgroup of $\mathrm{SL}(2, \mathbb{Z})$ has an eigenvalue $\lambda$ with
$0 < \lambda < 1/4$.

articles.title: Selberg's constant is at most one half
articles.statement:
Selberg's constant $C_{61}$ satisfies
$C_{61} \le 1/2$.

This elementary bound follows directly from the definition.

articles.title: Selberg's congruence spectral-gap constant
articles.statement:
Selberg's constant $C_{61}$ is the supremum of
the gap parameters $\theta(\Gamma)$ over all congruence subgroups $\Gamma$ of
$\mathrm{SL}(2, \mathbb{Z})$, where $\theta(\Gamma)$ is the supremum of $0$ and of the numbers
$\sqrt{1/4 - \lambda}$ for the eigenvalues $\lambda$ of $\Gamma$ with $0 < \lambda < 1/4$.

articles.title: Selberg's eigenvalue conjecture
articles.statement:
No congruence subgroup $\Gamma$ of
$\mathrm{SL}(2, \mathbb{Z})$ has an eigenvalue $\lambda$ with $0 < \lambda < 1/4$: for every
congruence subgroup $\Gamma$ and every eigenvalue $\lambda$ of $\Gamma$, either $\lambda \le 0$ or
$\lambda \ge 1/4$.

Here eigenvalues are realized by smooth square-integrable eigenfunctions, which captures the
discrete spectrum of the hyperbolic Laplacian.

articles.title: Selberg's 3/16 theorem
articles.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a congruence subgroup of
$\mathrm{SL}(2, \mathbb{Z})$ and let $\lambda$ be a real eigenvalue of the hyperbolic Laplacian
$\Delta$ for $\Gamma$, that is, $\Delta f = \lambda f$ for some nonzero, twice continuously
differentiable, $\Gamma$-invariant function $f$ on the upper half plane that is square-integrable
on $\Gamma \backslash \mathbb{H}$. Then $\lambda$ does not lie in the open interval
$(0, 3/16)$: either $\lambda \le 0$ or $\lambda \ge 3/16$.

## Sources

- Selberg, as recorded in Luo--Rudnick--Sarnak (1995): every eigenvalue of a congruence subgroup in the model is either `0`-side excluded or at least `3/16`; stated here as the absence of eigenvalues in `(0, 3/16)`.

articles.title: Selberg's bound on the spectral-gap constant
articles.statement:
Selberg's congruence spectral-gap constant
$C_{61}$ is at most $1/4$.

## Sources

- Selberg's theorem `λ₁(Γ) ≥ 3/16`, catalogue upper row `C₆₁ ≤ 1/4`.

articles.title: Exceptional eigenvalues bound the gap parameter
articles.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a subgroup of
$\mathrm{SL}(2, \mathbb{Z})$ and let $\lambda$ be a real eigenvalue of the hyperbolic
Laplacian on $L^2(\Gamma \backslash \mathbb{H})$ with $0 < \lambda < 1/4$. Then
$\sqrt{1/4 - \lambda}$ is at most the gap parameter $\theta(\Gamma)$ of $\Gamma$.

articles.title: Exceptional eigenvalues bound Selberg's constant
articles.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a congruence
subgroup of $\mathrm{SL}(2, \mathbb{Z})$ and let $\lambda$ be a real eigenvalue of the
hyperbolic Laplacian on $L^2(\Gamma \backslash \mathbb{H})$ with $0 < \lambda < 1/4$.
Then $\sqrt{1/4 - \lambda}$ is at most Selberg's constant $C_{61}$.

articles.title: Taylor–Wiles patching datum
articles.statement:
A Taylor–Wiles patching datum: a patching level for every `n`, with the
relation ideal at level `n` generated by `(1 + Xⱼ)^(ℓⁿ) - 1`.
This structure records an indexed family of finite-level data.

articles.title: Level of a Taylor–Wiles patching datum
articles.statement:
One level of a Taylor–Wiles patching datum: a finite module `N` over the
power series ring `𝒪⟦X₁, …, Xᵣ⟧`, with a surjective algebra map `ψ` to `R`
killing the `φ`-images of the variables, a surjective `ψ`-semilinear map
`π : N → M` whose kernel is the span of the `φ (Xᵢ)`, and a finite family
`b` spanning `N` with relations exactly `J`.

articles.title: Cusp form norm agrees with the modular form norm
articles.statement:
The coercion of the norm of a cusp form is the norm of its coercion as a
modular form.

articles.title: Norm trick for modular forms
articles.statement:
The norm trick: two modular forms satisfying a commutation relation under
the slash action of `ℋ` give rise to a modular form `Φ` of level `ℋ` with
`Φ * G = F * norm ℋ G`.

articles.title: Γ₀(2) has index 3 in SL(2, ℤ)
articles.statement:
The index of `Γ₀(2)` in `SL(2, ℤ)` is 3: the cosets are classified by
the first column mod 2, and there are three nonzero vectors in `(ZMod 2)²`.

articles.title: Norm of a cusp form vanishes only for the zero form
articles.statement:
The norm of a cusp form vanishes if and only if the form itself vanishes:
the norm is a product of translates, and a translate of a nonzero form is
nonzero.

articles.title: Norm of a cusp form
articles.statement:
The product norm of a cusp form: for `𝒢` of finite relative index in `ℋ`,
the product of the `ℋ / 𝒢`-translates of `f`, viewed as a cusp form on the
larger group `ℋ` at weight `k * [ℋ : 𝒢]`. This lifts Mathlib's
`ModularForm.norm` to cusp forms; the only new work is checking vanishing
at the cusps, which follows because each translate is a cusp form.

articles.title: No nonzero weight-two cusp forms on Γ₀(2)
articles.statement:
Every weight-two cusp form on `Γ₀(2)` is zero. Take the norm of `f`
to `Γ₀(1)`: it has weight `2 * [Γ₀(1) : Γ₀(2)] = 6`, hence vanishes by the
level-one dimension formula, and the norm vanishes only when `f` does.

articles.title: No nonzero weight-two cusp forms of level one
articles.statement:
Every weight-two cusp form on `Γ₀(1)` is zero: `Γ₀(1)` is the full
modular group, and the dimension formula gives rank zero below weight 12.

articles.title: Constant term of Ramanujan's theta function
articles.statement:
For all positive integers $i$ and $j$, the
integer power series $f(q^i, q^j) = \sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} q^{i n(n+1)/2 + j n(n-1)/2}$ has
constant term $1$: only $n = 0$ contributes to $q^0$.

## Sources

- Subhajit Bandyopadhyay and Nayandeep Deka Baruah, *Arithmetic Identities for Some Analogs of the 5-Core Partition Function*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.4.5, Section 1.

articles.title: Two identities for the 5-core counts
articles.statement:
Let $f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$ and let
$c_5(n)$ be the coefficient of $q^n$ in $f_5^5 / f_1$. For every natural number $n$,
$c_5(4n+1) = c_5(2n)$ and $c_5(5n+4) = 5\, c_5(n)$.

## Sources

- Subhajit Bandyopadhyay and Nayandeep Deka Baruah, *Arithmetic Identities for Some Analogs of the 5-Core Partition Function*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.4.5, Lemma 11 (`jis-2024-24.4.5-lem-11`).

articles.title: The 5-core counts
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$, $c_5(n)$ is the coefficient of $q^n$ in the
integer power series $f_5^5 / f_1$, where $f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$ is the Euler
product. The series $f_5^5 / f_1$ is the generating function of 5-core partitions.

## Sources

- Subhajit Bandyopadhyay and Nayandeep Deka Baruah, *Arithmetic Identities for Some Analogs of the 5-Core Partition Function*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.4.5, Section 1, equation for `∑ c_t(n) q^n` with `t = 5` (OEIS A053723).

articles.title: Generating function of the 5-core counts
articles.statement:
Let $f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$ and
let $c_5(n)$ be the coefficient of $q^n$ in $f_5^5 / f_1$. Then, as integer power series,
$\left(\sum_{n \ge 0} c_5(n) q^n\right) f_1 = f_5^5$, where $f_1$ is written as the pentagonal
series $\sum_{j \in \mathbb{Z}} (-1)^j q^{j(3j-1)/2}$.

## Sources

- Subhajit Bandyopadhyay and Nayandeep Deka Baruah, *Arithmetic Identities for Some Analogs of the 5-Core Partition Function*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.4.5, Section 1.

articles.title: Generating function of the $\varphi$-analog of the 5-core counts
articles.statement:
Let
$\varphi(q) = \sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} q^{n^2}$ and let $\bar a_5(n)$ be the coefficient of $q^n$
in $\varphi(-q^5)^5 / \varphi(-q)$. Then, as integer power series,
$\left(\sum_{n \ge 0} \bar a_5(n) q^n\right) \varphi(-q) = \varphi(-q^5)^5$.

## Sources

- Subhajit Bandyopadhyay and Nayandeep Deka Baruah, *Arithmetic Identities for Some Analogs of the 5-Core Partition Function*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.4.5, Section 1, equation (at).

articles.title: Generating function of the $\psi$-analog of the 5-core counts
articles.statement:
Let
$\psi(q) = \sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} q^{n(2n-1)}$ and let $\bar b_5(n)$ be the coefficient of $q^n$
in $\psi(-q^5)^5 / \psi(-q)$. Then, as integer power series,
$\left(\sum_{n \ge 0} \bar b_5(n) q^n\right) \psi(-q) = \psi(-q^5)^5$.

## Sources

- Subhajit Bandyopadhyay and Nayandeep Deka Baruah, *Arithmetic Identities for Some Analogs of the 5-Core Partition Function*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.4.5, Section 1, equation (bt).

articles.title: Congruences for the $\varphi$-analog of the 5-core counts
articles.statement:
Let
$\varphi(q) = \sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} q^{n^2}$ and let $\bar a_5(n)$ be the coefficient of $q^n$
in $\varphi(-q^5)^5 / \varphi(-q)$. For every natural number $k \ge 2$ and every natural number
$n$, $\bar a_5(20n+6) \equiv 0 \pmod{10}$, $\bar a_5(20n+14) \equiv 0 \pmod{10}$ and
$4\, \bar a_5(5^k n) \equiv 5\, \bar a_5(n) - \bar a_5(5n) \pmod{5^k}$.

## Sources

- Subhajit Bandyopadhyay and Nayandeep Deka Baruah, *Arithmetic Identities for Some Analogs of the 5-Core Partition Function*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.4.5, Corollary 3 (`jis-2024-24.4.5-cor-3`).

articles.title: The $\varphi$-analog of the 5-core counts in terms of the 5-core counts
articles.statement:
Let
$f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$, let $c_5(n)$ be the coefficient of $q^n$ in $f_5^5 / f_1$,
let $\varphi(q) = \sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} q^{n^2}$ and let $\bar a_5(n)$ be the coefficient of
$q^n$ in $\varphi(-q^5)^5 / \varphi(-q)$. For every natural number $n$,
$\bar a_5(5n+2) = 4\, c_5(5n+1)$, $\bar a_5(5n+3) = 4\, c_5(5n+2)$,
$\bar a_5(10n+1) = 2\, c_5(10n)$, $\bar a_5(10n+9) = 2\, c_5(10n+8)$,
$\bar a_5(20n+6) = 10\, c_5(10n+2)$ and $\bar a_5(20n+14) = 10\, c_5(10n+6)$.

## Sources

- Subhajit Bandyopadhyay and Nayandeep Deka Baruah, *Arithmetic Identities for Some Analogs of the 5-Core Partition Function*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.4.5, Theorem 2 (`jis-2024-24.4.5-thm-2`).

articles.title: The $\varphi$-analog in terms of the $\psi$-analog of the 5-core counts
articles.statement:
Let
$\varphi(q) = \sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} q^{n^2}$ and $\psi(q) = \sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} q^{n(2n-1)}$,
and let $\bar a_5(n)$ and $\bar b_5(n)$ be the coefficients of $q^n$ in
$\varphi(-q^5)^5 / \varphi(-q)$ and $\psi(-q^5)^5 / \psi(-q)$ respectively. For every natural
number $n$, $\bar a_5(20n+6) = 20\, \bar b_5(10n)$ and
$\bar a_5(20n+14) = 20\, \bar b_5(10n+4)$.

## Sources

- Subhajit Bandyopadhyay and Nayandeep Deka Baruah, *Arithmetic Identities for Some Analogs of the 5-Core Partition Function*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.4.5, Corollary 7 (`jis-2024-24.4.5-cor-7`).

articles.title: Recurrence for the $\varphi$-analog of the 5-core counts along powers of 5
articles.statement:
Let
$\varphi(q) = \sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} q^{n^2}$ and let $\bar a_5(n)$ be the coefficient of $q^n$
in $\varphi(-q^5)^5 / \varphi(-q)$. For every natural number $k \ge 2$ and every natural number
$n$, $\bar a_5(5^k n) = \frac{5^k - 1}{4}\, \bar a_5(5n) - \frac{5^k - 5}{4}\, \bar a_5(n)$.
Both quotients are integers.

## Sources

- Subhajit Bandyopadhyay and Nayandeep Deka Baruah, *Arithmetic Identities for Some Analogs of the 5-Core Partition Function*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.4.5, Theorem 2 (`jis-2024-24.4.5-thm-2`).

articles.title: The φ-analog of the 5-core partition function
articles.statement:
Let
$\varphi(q) = \sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} q^{n^2}$ be Ramanujan's theta function. For a natural
number $n$, $\bar a_5(n)$ is the coefficient of $q^n$ in the integer power series
$\varphi^5(-q^5)/\varphi(-q)$ (the denominator has constant term $1$, so the quotient is a power
series).

## Sources

- Subhajit Bandyopadhyay and Nayandeep Deka Baruah, *Arithmetic Identities for Some Analogs of the 5-Core Partition Function*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.4.5, Section 1, equation (at) (OEIS A368490).

articles.title: Congruences for the ψ-analog of the 5-core partition function
articles.statement:
Let
$\bar b_5(n)$ be the coefficient of $q^n$ in $\psi^5(-q^5)/\psi(-q)$, where
$\psi(q) = \sum_{n \ge 0} q^{n(n+1)/2}$. For every integer $k \ge 2$ and every natural number
$n$, $4 \bar b_5(5^k(n+3) - 3) \equiv 5 \bar b_5(n) - \bar b_5(5n+12) \pmod{5^k}$, and both
$\bar b_5(5^k(20n+18) - 3)$ and $\bar b_5(5^k(20n+22) - 3)$ are divisible by $(5^k - 1)/4$.

## Sources

- Subhajit Bandyopadhyay and Nayandeep Deka Baruah, *Arithmetic Identities for Some Analogs of the 5-Core Partition Function*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.4.5, Corollary 8 (`jis-2024-24.4.5-cor-8`).

articles.title: A recurrence for the ψ-analog of the 5-core partition function along powers of 5
articles.statement:
Let
$\bar b_5(n)$ be the coefficient of $q^n$ in $\psi^5(-q^5)/\psi(-q)$, where
$\psi(q) = \sum_{n \ge 0} q^{n(n+1)/2}$. For every integer $k \ge 2$ and every natural number
$n$, $\bar b_5(5^k(n+3) - 3) = \frac{5^k - 1}{4} \bar b_5(5n+12) - \frac{5^k - 5}{4} \bar b_5(n)$;
both quotients are integers.

## Sources

- Subhajit Bandyopadhyay and Nayandeep Deka Baruah, *Arithmetic Identities for Some Analogs of the 5-Core Partition Function*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.4.5, Theorem 4 (`jis-2024-24.4.5-thm-4`).

articles.title: A doubling identity for the ψ-analog of the 5-core partition function
articles.statement:
Let
$\bar b_5(n)$ be the coefficient of $q^n$ in $\psi^5(-q^5)/\psi(-q)$, where
$\psi(q) = \sum_{n \ge 0} q^{n(n+1)/2}$. For every natural number $n$,
$\bar b_5(4n+3) = 2 \bar b_5(2n)$.

## Sources

- Subhajit Bandyopadhyay and Nayandeep Deka Baruah, *Arithmetic Identities for Some Analogs of the 5-Core Partition Function*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.4.5, Theorem 4 (`jis-2024-24.4.5-thm-4`).

articles.title: Identities relating the ψ-analog to the 5-core counts and the φ-analog
Sign densities of the ψ-analog of the 5-core partition function
articles.statement:
Let
$\bar b_5(n)$ be the coefficient of $q^n$ in $\psi^5(-q^5)/\psi(-q)$, where
$\psi(q) = \sum_{n \ge 0} q^{n(n+1)/2}$, and let the lower density of a set $S$ of natural numbers
be $\liminf_{N \to \infty} |S \cap \{0, \dots, N - 1\}|/N$. The set of positive integers $n$ with
$\bar b_5(n) = 0$ has lower density at least $3/10$, the set of positive $n$ with
$\bar b_5(n) > 0$ has lower density at least $52/100$, and the set of positive $n$ with
$\bar b_5(n) < 0$ has lower density at least $1/10$.

## Sources

- Subhajit Bandyopadhyay and Nayandeep Deka Baruah, *Arithmetic Identities for Some Analogs of the 5-Core Partition Function*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.4.5, Corollary 6 (`jis-2024-24.4.5-cor-6`).

articles.title: The ψ-analog of the 5-core partition function
articles.statement:
Let
$\psi(q) = \sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} q^{2n^2 - n} = \sum_{n \ge 0} q^{n(n+1)/2}$ be Ramanujan's theta
function. For a natural number $n$, $\bar b_5(n)$ is the coefficient of $q^n$ in the integer
power series $\psi^5(-q^5)/\psi(-q)$ (the denominator has constant term $1$, so the quotient is
a power series).

## Sources

- Subhajit Bandyopadhyay and Nayandeep Deka Baruah, *Arithmetic Identities for Some Analogs of the 5-Core Partition Function*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.4.5, Section 1, equation (bt) (OEIS A368495).

articles.title: Ramanujan's general theta function at powers of q
articles.statement:
For positive integers $i$ and $j$,
$f(q^i, q^j)$ is the integer power series $\sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} q^{i n(n+1)/2 + j n(n-1)/2}$,
that is, Ramanujan's $f(a, b) = \sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} a^{n(n+1)/2} b^{n(n-1)/2}$ at $a = q^i$
and $b = q^j$.

Since $i, j \ge 1$, only integers $n$ with $|n| \le m$ contribute to the coefficient of $q^m$, so
each coefficient is a finite count.

## Sources

- Subhajit Bandyopadhyay and Nayandeep Deka Baruah, *Arithmetic Identities for Some Analogs of the 5-Core Partition Function*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.4.5, Section 1 (definition of `f(a, b)`).

articles.title: 5-dissections of Ramanujan's theta functions φ and ψ
articles.statement:
Let
$f(a, b) = \sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} a^{n(n+1)/2} b^{n(n-1)/2}$ be Ramanujan's general theta
function, $\varphi(q) = f(q, q)$ and $\psi(q) = f(q, q^3)$. As integer power series in $q$,
$\varphi(q) = \varphi(q^{25}) + 2q f(q^{15}, q^{35}) + 2q^4 f(q^5, q^{45})$ and
$\psi(q) = f(q^{10}, q^{15}) + q f(q^5, q^{20}) + q^3 \psi(q^{25})$.

Lemma 10 of the source also gives a 5-dissection of $\prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^m)^{-1}$ via the
Rogers–Ramanujan continued fraction; that part is not included.

## Sources

- Subhajit Bandyopadhyay and Nayandeep Deka Baruah, *Arithmetic Identities for Some Analogs of the 5-Core Partition Function*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.4.5, Lemma 10 (`jis-2024-24.4.5-lem-10`).

articles.title: Theta-function identities of level 5
articles.statement:
Let $f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$,
$f(q) = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - (-q)^m)$ (so that $f(-q) = f_1$),
$\chi(-q) = \prod_{m \ge 0} (1 - q^{2m+1})$ and $\chi(q) = \prod_{m \ge 0} (1 + q^{2m+1})$. Let
$f(a, b) = \sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} a^{n(n+1)/2} b^{n(n-1)/2}$ be Ramanujan's general theta
function, $\varphi(q) = f(q, q)$ and $\psi(q) = f(q, q^3)$. Then, as integer power series in
$q$ (every denominator below has constant term $1$):
$\varphi^5(q^5)/\varphi(q) + 4q f^5(q^5)/f(q) = \varphi(q) \varphi^3(q^5)$;
$\varphi^2(q) - \varphi^2(q^5) = 4q \chi(q) f_5 f_{20}$;
$\psi^5(-q^5)/\psi(-q) - \psi^5(q^5)/\psi(q) = 4q^3 \psi^5(q^{10})/\psi(q^2) + 2q f_{20}^5/f_4$;
$\psi^2(q) - q \psi^2(q^5) = f_5 \varphi(-q^5)/\chi(-q) = f(q, q^4) f(q^2, q^3)$;
$f_5^5/f_1 - 4q^3 f_{20}^5/f_4 = f^5(q^5)/f(q) + 2q f_{10}^5/f_2$; and
$f_2^2/f_1^4 = f_{10}^2/f_5^4 + 4q f_2 f_{10}^5/(f_1^3 f_5^5)$.

## Sources

- Subhajit Bandyopadhyay and Nayandeep Deka Baruah, *Arithmetic Identities for Some Analogs of the 5-Core Partition Function*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.4.5, Lemma 9 (`jis-2024-24.4.5-lem-9`).

articles.title: Generating function identity for generalized cubic partition numbers
articles.statement:
Let
$f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$ be the Euler products and $a_c(n)$ the generalized cubic
partition numbers. For every natural number $c$,
$f_1 f_2^{c-1} \sum_{n \ge 0} a_c(n) q^n = 1$ as integer power series in $q$, where for
$c = 0$ the exponent $c - 1$ is truncated to $0$.

## Sources

- Russelle Guadalupe, *A Note on Congruences for Generalized Cubic Partitions Modulo Primes*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A20, Section 1.

articles.title: Generalized cubic partition congruences modulo primes $p \ge 7$, $p \equiv 3, 7 \pmod 8$
articles.statement:
Let $a_c(n)$ be the generalized cubic partition numbers and let $p \ge 7$ be a prime with
$p \equiv 3$ or $p \equiv 7 \pmod 8$. Then
$a_{p-6}\bigl(pn + 13(p^2 - 1)/24\bigr) \equiv 0 \pmod p$ for every natural number $n$.

Since $24 \mid p^2 - 1$, the shift $13(p^2 - 1)/24$ is a natural number.

## Sources

- Russelle Guadalupe, *A Note on Congruences for Generalized Cubic Partitions Modulo Primes*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A20, Theorem 3, Equation (13).

articles.title: Generalized cubic partition congruences for primes $p \equiv 5, 7 \pmod 8$
articles.statement:
Let $a_c(n)$
be the generalized cubic partition numbers, let $p$ be a prime with $p \equiv 5$ or
$p \equiv 7 \pmod 8$, and let $l$ be a natural number with $p \mid 8l + 3$. Then
$a_{p-4}(pn + l) \equiv 0 \pmod p$ for every natural number $n$.

The source assumes $0 \le l \le p - 1$; the statement for a larger $l$ follows from the one for
$l \bmod p$, which satisfies the same divisibility.

## Sources

- Russelle Guadalupe, *A Note on Congruences for Generalized Cubic Partitions Modulo Primes*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A20, Theorem 2, Equation (9).

articles.title: Amdeberhan–Sellers–Singh congruences
articles.statement:
For every natural number $n$, the generalized
cubic partition numbers satisfy $a_3(7n + 4) \equiv 0 \pmod{7}$ and
$a_5(11n + 10) \equiv 0 \pmod{11}$.

## Sources

- Russelle Guadalupe, *A Note on Congruences for Generalized Cubic Partitions Modulo Primes*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A20, Theorem 1 (quoting Amdeberhan, Sellers, and Singh), Equations (1) and (2).

articles.title: Generalized cubic partitions of zero
articles.statement:
For every natural number $c$, the generalized
cubic partition number $a_c(0)$ equals $1$.

## Sources

- Russelle Guadalupe, *A Note on Congruences for Generalized Cubic Partitions Modulo Primes*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A20, Section 1.

articles.title: Generalized cubic partition numbers
articles.statement:
Let $f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$ be the
Euler products. For natural numbers $c$ and $n$, $a_c(n)$ is the integer coefficient of $q^n$
in the generating function of generalized cubic partitions, the power series
$1/(f_1 f_2^{c-1})$. For $c \ge 1$ it is the number of partitions of $n$ whose even parts may
each come in $c$ colors; $c = 1$ gives the partition numbers and $c = 2$ Chan's cubic
partition numbers. For $c = 0$ the exponent $c - 1$ is truncated to $0$, so $a_0(n)$ is also
the number of partitions of $n$.

## Sources

- Russelle Guadalupe, *A Note on Congruences for Generalized Cubic Partitions Modulo Primes*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A20, Section 1.

articles.title: Generating function of generalized cubic partitions
articles.statement:
Let
$f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$ be the Euler products. For a natural number $c$, this is
the integer power series $1/(f_1 f_2^{c-1})$ in $q$, the inverse of $f_1 f_2^{c-1}$ (whose
constant term is $1$). For $c \ge 1$ its coefficient of $q^n$ is the number of partitions of
$n$ whose even parts may each come in $c$ colors. For $c = 0$ the exponent $c - 1$ is
truncated to $0$, so the series is then the inverse of $f_1$.

## Sources

- Russelle Guadalupe, *A Note on Congruences for Generalized Cubic Partitions Modulo Primes*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A20, Section 1.

articles.title: A level-10 Euler-product identity
articles.statement:
Let $f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$ in the ring of
integer power series in $q$. Then
$f_2^5 f_5^2 = f_1^5 f_5 f_{10} + 5q f_1^2 f_2 f_{10}^4$.

Dividing both sides by $f_1^5 f_2^2 f_{10}^2$ gives the form in the source,
$f_2^3 f_5^2/(f_1^5 f_{10}^2) = f_5/(f_2^2 f_{10}) + 5q f_{10}^2/(f_1^3 f_2)$.

## Sources

- Bipul Kumar Sarmah and Satyajit Gayan, *Congruences for F-partitions with 4 Repetitions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A17, Lemma 5, eq. (17).

articles.title: Parity of $\varphi_4(4n+1)$
articles.statement:
Let $\varphi_4(n)$ be the number of generalized Frobenius
partitions of $n$ in which each integer appears at most $4$ times in each row. For every natural
number $n$, $\varphi_4(4n + 1)$ is odd if and only if $2n = 5k(3k + 1)$ for some integer $k$,
that is, $n = 5k(3k \pm 1)/2$ for some integer $k$.

## Sources

- Bipul Kumar Sarmah and Satyajit Gayan, *Congruences for F-partitions with 4 Repetitions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A17, Theorem 4.

articles.title: $\varphi_4(4n+3)$ is even
articles.statement:
Let $\varphi_4(n)$ be the number of generalized Frobenius
partitions of $n$ in which each integer appears at most $4$ times in each row. For every natural
number $n$, $\varphi_4(4n + 3) \equiv 0 \pmod 2$.

## Sources

- Bipul Kumar Sarmah and Satyajit Gayan, *Congruences for F-partitions with 4 Repetitions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A17, Theorem 2.

articles.title: $\varphi_4(10n+1)$ modulo $5$
articles.statement:
Let $\varphi_4(n)$ be the number of generalized Frobenius
partitions of $n$ in which each integer appears at most $4$ times in each row, and let $n$ be a
natural number. If $n = k(3k + 1)$ for an integer $k$, then
$\varphi_4(10n + 1) \equiv k + 1 \pmod 5$; if there is no such integer $k$, then
$\varphi_4(10n + 1) \equiv 0 \pmod 5$.

## Sources

- Bipul Kumar Sarmah and Satyajit Gayan, *Congruences for F-partitions with 4 Repetitions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A17, Theorem 6.

articles.title: $\varphi_4(10n+6)$ is divisible by $5$
articles.statement:
Let $\varphi_4(n)$ be the number of generalized
Frobenius partitions of $n$ in which each integer appears at most $4$ times in each row. For every
natural number $n$, $\varphi_4(10n + 6) \equiv 0 \pmod 5$.

## Sources

- Bipul Kumar Sarmah and Satyajit Gayan, *Congruences for F-partitions with 4 Repetitions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A17, Theorem 5.

articles.title: The 2-dissection of the generating function of $\varphi_4$
articles.statement:
Let $\varphi_4(n)$ be the
number of generalized Frobenius partitions of $n$ in which each integer appears at most $4$ times
in each row, and let $f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$ in the ring of integer power series in
$q$. Then

$$f_1^{12} f_4^4 f_5 f_{10}^2 \sum_{n \ge 0} \varphi_4(2n)\, q^n =
f_1^3 f_2^{10} f_4^2 f_5^2 f_{10} + 2q f_2^{15} f_5 f_{20}^2 - 8q f_1^5 f_4^{10} f_{10}^3$$

and

$$f_1^6 f_4^2 f_5^2 \sum_{n \ge 0} \varphi_4(2n + 1)\, q^n = f_2^7 f_{10}^2.$$

Dividing by the Euler products on the left gives the quotient forms of the source, for example
$\sum_{n \ge 0} \varphi_4(2n + 1)\, q^n = f_2^7 f_{10}^2 / (f_1^6 f_4^2 f_5^2)$.

## Sources

- Bipul Kumar Sarmah and Satyajit Gayan, *Congruences for F-partitions with 4 Repetitions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A17, Theorem 1, eqs. (3) and (4).

articles.title: $\varphi_4(2N+1)$ is even when $5 \nmid N$
articles.statement:
Let $\varphi_4(n)$ be the number of generalized
Frobenius partitions of $n$ in which each integer appears at most $4$ times in each row. For every
positive integer $N$ not divisible by $5$, $\varphi_4(2N + 1) \equiv 0 \pmod 2$.

## Sources

- Bipul Kumar Sarmah and Satyajit Gayan, *Congruences for F-partitions with 4 Repetitions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A17, Theorem 3.

articles.title: Initial values of $\varphi_4$
articles.statement:
Let $\varphi_4(n)$ be the number of generalized Frobenius
partitions of $n$ in which each integer appears at most $4$ times in each row. Then
$\varphi_4(0) = 1$ (the empty array) and $\varphi_4(1) = 1$ (the single column with both entries
$0$).

## Sources

- Bipul Kumar Sarmah and Satyajit Gayan, *Congruences for F-partitions with 4 Repetitions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A17, Section 1 (definition of `φ_k(n)`).

articles.title: Frobenius partitions with at most $k$ repetitions
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $k$ and $n$,
$\varphi_k(n)$ is the number of generalized Frobenius partitions of $n$ in which each integer
appears at most $k$ times in each row. Concretely, $\varphi_k(n)$ is the number of pairs of
functions $m_1, m_2 \colon \{0, 1, \dots, n\} \to \{0, 1, \dots, k\}$ with
$\sum_i m_1(i) = \sum_i m_2(i)$ and $\sum_i (i + 1)\, m_1(i) + \sum_i i\, m_2(i) = n$.

Here a generalized Frobenius partition of $n$ is a two-rowed array of nonnegative integers with
$r$ columns, both rows nonincreasing, whose entries sum to $n - r$; its entries are at most $n$,
and $m_1(i)$, $m_2(i)$ count how often $i$ appears in the top and bottom rows.

## Sources

- Bipul Kumar Sarmah and Satyajit Gayan, *Congruences for F-partitions with 4 Repetitions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A17, Section 1 (definition of `φ_k(n)`, after Andrews).

articles.title: A 2-dissection of the reciprocal Euler product of levels 1 and 5
articles.statement:
Let
$f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$ in the ring of integer power series in $q$. Then

$$f_2^{10} f_8^2 f_{10}^3 f_{20} = f_1^3 f_2^3 f_4^4 f_5 f_8^2 f_{10}^2 f_{20} -
2q f_1^3 f_2 f_4^6 f_5 f_8^2 f_{20}^3 + 5q f_1^3 f_2^2 f_4^3 f_5 f_8^2 f_{10}^3 f_{20}^2 +
2q^2 f_1^3 f_4^9 f_5 f_{10} f_{40}^2.$$

Dividing both sides by $f_1^3 f_5 f_2^{10} f_8^2 f_{10}^3 f_{20}$ gives the form in the source,
$1/(f_1^3 f_5) = f_4^4/(f_2^7 f_{10}) - 2q f_4^6 f_{20}^2/(f_2^9 f_{10}^3) +
5q f_4^3 f_{20}/f_2^8 + 2q^2 f_4^9 f_{40}^2/(f_2^{10} f_8^2 f_{10}^2 f_{20})$.

## Sources

- Bipul Kumar Sarmah and Satyajit Gayan, *Congruences for F-partitions with 4 Repetitions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A17, Lemma 4, eq. (15).

articles.title: Ramanujan's theta product identity for $ab = cd$
articles.statement:
Let
$f(a,b) = \sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} a^{n(n+1)/2} b^{n(n-1)/2}$ be Ramanujan's general theta
function. If $a, b, c, d$ are complex numbers with $a \ne 0$, $|ab| < 1$ and $ab = cd$, then

$$f(a,b)\,f(c,d) = f(ad,bc)\,f(ac,bd) + a\,f(c/a, a^2bd)\,f(d/a, a^2bc).$$

In each of the six theta functions the two arguments have product of modulus $|ab|$ or
$|ab|^2$, which is less than $1$, so every series converges.

## Sources

- Bipul Kumar Sarmah and Satyajit Gayan, *Congruences for F-partitions with 4 Repetitions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A17, Lemma 1, eq. (12), quoting Berndt, *Ramanujan's Notebooks, Part III*, p. 45, Entry 29.

articles.title: The 2-dissection of $f_3/f_1^3$
articles.statement:
Write $f_k = (q^k; q^k)_\infty$ for the Euler products. In
the ring of integer power series in $q$,

$$
f_3 f_2^9 f_{12}^2 = f_1^3 f_4^6 f_6^3 + 3q f_1^3 f_2^2 f_4^2 f_6 f_{12}^4.
$$

Since each $f_k$ with $k \ge 1$ has constant term $1$ and is therefore invertible, this is the
identity $f_3 / f_1^3 = f_4^6 f_6^3 / (f_2^9 f_{12}^2) + 3q f_4^2 f_6 f_{12}^2 / f_2^7$ with both
sides multiplied by $f_1^3 f_2^9 f_{12}^2$.

## Sources

- Manjil P. Saikia and James A. Sellers, *Generalizing Recent Results of Kathiravan, Majumdar, Sangale, and Srinivas on `(ℓ, k)`-regular Partitions*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.6.1, Lemma 8 (`jis-2025-25.6.1-lem-8`).

articles.title: The 2-dissection of $f_3^2/f_1^2$
articles.statement:
Write $f_k = (q^k; q^k)_\infty$ for the Euler products.
In the ring of integer power series in $q$,

$$
f_3^2 f_2^5 f_8 f_{12} f_{24} = f_1^2 f_4^4 f_6 f_{12}^3 + 2q f_1^2 f_2 f_4 f_6^2 f_8^2 f_{24}^2.
$$

Since each $f_k$ with $k \ge 1$ has constant term $1$ and is therefore invertible, this is the
identity $f_3^2 / f_1^2 = f_4^4 f_6 f_{12}^2 / (f_2^5 f_8 f_{24}) +
2q f_4 f_6^2 f_8 f_{24} / (f_2^4 f_{12})$ with both sides multiplied by
$f_1^2 f_2^5 f_8 f_{12} f_{24}$.

## Sources

- Manjil P. Saikia and James A. Sellers, *Generalizing Recent Results of Kathiravan, Majumdar, Sangale, and Srinivas on `(ℓ, k)`-regular Partitions*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.6.1, Lemma 9 (`jis-2025-25.6.1-lem-9`).

articles.title: The 2-dissection of $f_9/f_1$
articles.statement:
Write $f_k = (q^k; q^k)_\infty$ for the Euler products. In
the ring of integer power series in $q$,

$$
f_9 f_2^3 f_6 f_{12} f_{36} = f_1 f_2 f_{12}^4 f_{18} + q f_1 f_4^2 f_6^2 f_{36}^2.
$$

Since each $f_k$ with $k \ge 1$ has constant term $1$ and is therefore invertible, this is the
identity $f_9 / f_1 = f_{12}^3 f_{18} / (f_2^2 f_6 f_{36}) + q f_4^2 f_6 f_{36} / (f_2^3 f_{12})$
with both sides multiplied by $f_1 f_2^3 f_6 f_{12} f_{36}$.

## Sources

- Manjil P. Saikia and James A. Sellers, *Generalizing Recent Results of Kathiravan, Majumdar, Sangale, and Srinivas on `(ℓ, k)`-regular Partitions*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.6.1, Lemma 7 (`jis-2025-25.6.1-lem-7`).

articles.title: The 2-dissection of $1/(f_1 f_3)$
articles.statement:
Write $f_k = (q^k; q^k)_\infty$ for the Euler
products. In the ring of integer power series in $q$,

$$
f_2^4 f_4 f_6^4 f_8^2 f_{12} f_{24}^2 =
f_1 f_3 f_2^2 f_8^4 f_{12}^6 + q f_1 f_3 f_4^6 f_6^2 f_{24}^4.
$$

Since each $f_k$ with $k \ge 1$ has constant term $1$ and is therefore invertible, this is the
identity $1 / (f_1 f_3) = f_8^2 f_{12}^5 / (f_2^2 f_4 f_6^4 f_{24}^2) +
q f_4^5 f_{24}^2 / (f_2^4 f_6^2 f_8^2 f_{12})$ with both sides multiplied by
$f_1 f_3 f_2^4 f_4 f_6^4 f_8^2 f_{12} f_{24}^2$.

## Sources

- Manjil P. Saikia and James A. Sellers, *Generalizing Recent Results of Kathiravan, Majumdar, Sangale, and Srinivas on `(ℓ, k)`-regular Partitions*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.6.1, Lemma 11 (`jis-2025-25.6.1-lem-11`).

articles.title: The 2-dissections of $1/f_1^4$, $1/f_1^8$ and $1/f_1^{12}$
articles.statement:
Write
$f_k = (q^k; q^k)_\infty$ for the Euler products. In the ring of integer power series in $q$,
the following three identities hold:

$$
f_2^{14} f_8^4 = f_1^4 f_4^{14} + 4q f_1^4 f_2^4 f_4^2 f_8^8,
$$



$$
f_2^{28} f_8^8 = f_1^8 f_4^{28} + 8q f_1^8 f_2^4 f_4^{16} f_8^8 + 16q^2 f_1^8 f_2^8 f_4^4 f_8^{16},
$$



$$
f_2^{42} f_8^{12} = f_1^{12} f_4^{42} + 12q f_1^{12} f_2^4 f_4^{30} f_8^8 +
48q^2 f_1^{12} f_2^8 f_4^{18} f_8^{16} + 64q^3 f_1^{12} f_2^{12} f_4^6 f_8^{24}.
$$

Since each $f_k$ with $k \ge 1$ has constant term $1$ and is therefore invertible, dividing by
$f_1^4 f_2^{14} f_8^4$, $f_1^8 f_2^{28} f_8^8$ and $f_1^{12} f_2^{42} f_8^{12}$ respectively turns
these into the 2-dissections
$1/f_1^4 = f_4^{14}/(f_2^{14} f_8^4) + 4q f_4^2 f_8^4/f_2^{10}$,
$1/f_1^8 = f_4^{28}/(f_2^{28} f_8^8) + 8q f_4^{16}/f_2^{24} + 16q^2 f_4^4 f_8^8/f_2^{20}$ and
$1/f_1^{12} = f_4^{42}/(f_2^{42} f_8^{12}) + 12q f_4^{30}/(f_2^{38} f_8^4) +
48q^2 f_4^{18} f_8^4/f_2^{34} + 64q^3 f_4^6 f_8^{12}/f_2^{30}$.

## Sources

- Manjil P. Saikia and James A. Sellers, *Generalizing Recent Results of Kathiravan, Majumdar, Sangale, and Srinivas on `(ℓ, k)`-regular Partitions*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.6.1, Lemma 10 (`jis-2025-25.6.1-lem-10`).

articles.title: An internal congruence modulo $4$ for $b_{4,9}$
articles.statement:
Let $b_{4,9}(n)$ be the number of
partitions of $n$ with no part divisible by $4$ or by $9$. For every natural number $n$,
$b_{4,9}(16n + 1) \equiv b_{4,9}(4n + 1) \pmod 4$.

## Sources

- Manjil P. Saikia and James A. Sellers, *Generalizing Recent Results of Kathiravan, Majumdar, Sangale, and Srinivas on `(ℓ, k)`-regular Partitions*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.6.1, Theorem 13 (`jis-2025-25.6.1-thm-13`).

articles.title: Congruences modulo $12$ for $b_{4,9}$ along powers of $2$
articles.statement:
Let $b_{4,9}(n)$ be the
number of partitions of $n$ with no part divisible by $4$ or by $9$. For all natural numbers
$\alpha \ge 3$ and $n$, $b_{4,9}(2^\alpha n + 6 \cdot 2^{\alpha - 3} + 1) \equiv 0 \pmod{12}$.

## Sources

- Manjil P. Saikia and James A. Sellers, *Generalizing Recent Results of Kathiravan, Majumdar, Sangale, and Srinivas on `(ℓ, k)`-regular Partitions*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.6.1, Theorem 3 (`jis-2025-25.6.1-thm-3`).

articles.title: Generating function of $b_{4,9}$ at odd arguments
articles.statement:
Let $b_{4,9}(n)$ be the number of
partitions of $n$ with no part divisible by $4$ or by $9$, and write $f_k = (q^k; q^k)_\infty$
for the Euler products. In the ring of integer power series in $q$,

$$
f_1^3 f_6 \sum_{n \ge 0} b_{4,9}(2n + 1) q^n = f_2^3 f_3.
$$

Since $f_1$ and $f_6$ have constant term $1$ and are therefore invertible, this says
$\sum_{n \ge 0} b_{4,9}(2n + 1) q^n = f_2^3 f_3 / (f_1^3 f_6)$.

## Sources

- Manjil P. Saikia and James A. Sellers, *Generalizing Recent Results of Kathiravan, Majumdar, Sangale, and Srinivas on `(ℓ, k)`-regular Partitions*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.6.1, Theorem 12 (`jis-2025-25.6.1-thm-12`).

articles.title: $b_{4,9}(16n + 13)$ is divisible by $4$
articles.statement:
Let $b_{4,9}(n)$ be the number of partitions of
$n$ with no part divisible by $4$ or by $9$. For every natural number $n$,
$b_{4,9}(16n + 13) \equiv 0 \pmod 4$.

## Sources

- Manjil P. Saikia and James A. Sellers, *Generalizing Recent Results of Kathiravan, Majumdar, Sangale, and Srinivas on `(ℓ, k)`-regular Partitions*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.6.1, Theorem 14 (`jis-2025-25.6.1-thm-14`).

articles.title: $b_{4,9}(32n + 25)$ is divisible by $4$
articles.statement:
Let $b_{4,9}(n)$ be the number of partitions of
$n$ with no part divisible by $4$ or by $9$. For every natural number $n$,
$b_{4,9}(32n + 25) \equiv 0 \pmod 4$.

## Sources

- Manjil P. Saikia and James A. Sellers, *Generalizing Recent Results of Kathiravan, Majumdar, Sangale, and Srinivas on `(ℓ, k)`-regular Partitions*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.6.1, Theorem 15 (`jis-2025-25.6.1-thm-15`).

articles.title: The $(4, 9)$-regular partition count at zero
articles.statement:
The number $b_{4,9}(0)$ of
$(4, 9)$-regular partitions of $0$, that is, partitions of $0$ none of whose parts is divisible by
$4$ or by $9$, equals $1$: the only such partition is the empty partition.

## Sources

- Manjil P. Saikia and James A. Sellers, *Generalizing Recent Results of Kathiravan, Majumdar, Sangale, and Srinivas on `(ℓ, k)`-regular Partitions*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.6.1, Section 1 (definition of `b_{ℓ,k}(n)`).

articles.title: Parity of $(4, p)$-regular partitions in nonresidue progressions
articles.statement:
Let $p \ge 5$ be a
prime and let $r$ be a natural number such that $8r + 1$ is not a square modulo $p$ (a quadratic
nonresidue). Write $b_{4,p}(m)$ for the number of $(4, p)$-regular partitions of $m$, that is,
partitions of $m$ none of whose parts is divisible by $4$ or by $p$. Then
$b_{4,p}(pn + r) \equiv 0 \pmod 2$ for every natural number $n$.

Restricting $r$ to natural numbers loses nothing: every residue class modulo $p$ has a
natural-number representative.

## Sources

- Manjil P. Saikia and James A. Sellers, *Generalizing Recent Results of Kathiravan, Majumdar, Sangale, and Srinivas on `(ℓ, k)`-regular Partitions*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.6.1, Theorem 1 (`jis-2025-25.6.1-thm-1`).

articles.title: For small $n$ every partition is $(\ell, k)$-regular
articles.statement:
Let $\ell$, $k$ and $n$ be natural
numbers with $n < \ell$ and $n < k$, and write $b_{\ell,k}(n)$ for the number of
$(\ell, k)$-regular partitions of $n$ (partitions none of whose parts is divisible by $\ell$ or by
$k$) and $p(n)$ for the number of all partitions of $n$. Then every partition of $n$ is
$(\ell, k)$-regular, so $b_{\ell,k}(n) = p(n)$.

## Sources

- Manjil P. Saikia and James A. Sellers, *Generalizing Recent Results of Kathiravan, Majumdar, Sangale, and Srinivas on `(ℓ, k)`-regular Partitions*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.6.1, Section 1 (definition of `b_{ℓ,k}(n)`).

articles.title: Parity of $(2, p)$-regular partitions in nonresidue progressions
articles.statement:
Let $p \ge 5$ be a
prime and let $r$ be a natural number such that $24r + 1$ is not a square modulo $p$ (a quadratic
nonresidue). Write $b_{2,p}(m)$ for the number of $(2, p)$-regular partitions of $m$, that is,
partitions of $m$ none of whose parts is divisible by $2$ or by $p$. Then
$b_{2,p}(pn + r) \equiv 0 \pmod 2$ for every natural number $n$.

## Sources

- Manjil P. Saikia and James A. Sellers, *Generalizing Recent Results of Kathiravan, Majumdar, Sangale, and Srinivas on `(ℓ, k)`-regular Partitions*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.6.1, Theorem 2 (`jis-2025-25.6.1-thm-2`).

articles.title: Number of $(\ell, k)$-regular partitions
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $\ell$, $k$ and $n$,
$b_{\ell,k}(n)$ is the number of $(\ell, k)$-regular partitions of $n$, that is, partitions of
$n$ none of whose parts is divisible by $\ell$ or by $k$.

## Sources

- Manjil P. Saikia and James A. Sellers, *Generalizing Recent Results of Kathiravan, Majumdar, Sangale, and Srinivas on `(ℓ, k)`-regular Partitions*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.6.1, Section 1 (definition of `b_{ℓ,k}(n)`).

articles.title: Lifting partition congruences to mex partition functions
articles.statement:
For a partition $\lambda$, a
positive integer $A$ and a natural number $c$, let $\operatorname{mex}_{A,c}(\lambda)$ be the
smallest positive integer congruent to $c$ modulo $A$ that is not a part of $\lambda$, and let
$p_{A,c}(N)$ be the number of partitions $\lambda$ of $N$ with
$\operatorname{mex}_{A,c}(\lambda) \equiv c \pmod{2A}$. Let $p(N)$ be the number of partitions of
$N$. Let $m$, $a$ and $b$ be natural numbers with $m \ge 1$ and $b < a$, and suppose that $m$
divides $p(an + b)$ for every natural number $n$. Then for every integer $t \ge 1$ and every
natural number $n$, $m$ divides both $p_{at,at}(an + b)$ and $p_{2at,at}(an + b)$.

Because $b < a$, the hypothesis covers the whole residue class of $b$ modulo $a$; for $b \ge a$
the lift would need $p$ at arguments below $b$, which the hypothesis does not cover.

The proof follows the Andrews–Newman mex decomposition used by Barman and Singh: remove one copy
of every forced earlier mex candidate. The exact-mex fibers then telescope, while every removed
prefix sum remains a multiple of $a$.

## Sources

- Rupam Barman and Ajit Singh, "Mex-Related Partition Functions of Andrews and Newman," Journal of Integer Sequences 24 (2021), Article 21.6.3, Theorem, lines 172–182, https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL24/Barman/barman3.tex

articles.title: Mex-related partition function of Andrews and Newman
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $A$, $a$ and $n$,
$p_{A,a}(n)$ is the number of partitions $\lambda$ of $n$ such that
$\operatorname{mex}_{A,a}(\lambda) \equiv a \pmod{2A}$, where $\operatorname{mex}_{A,a}(\lambda)$
is the smallest positive integer congruent to $a$ modulo $A$ that is not a part of $\lambda$, and
$0$ if there is no such integer.

articles.title: Mex of a partition in a residue class
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $A$, $a$ and $n$ and a
partition $\lambda$ of $n$, $\operatorname{mex}_{A,a}(\lambda)$ is the smallest positive integer
congruent to $a$ modulo $A$ that is not a part of $\lambda$, and $0$ if there is no such integer
(which happens only when $A = 0$).

articles.title: Least inverse of 24 modulo a power
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $p$ and $k$, $\delta_{p,k}$ is the
least natural number $\delta$ with $24\delta \equiv 1 \pmod{p^k}$, and $0$ if there is no such
$\delta$, which happens exactly when $p^k$ and $24$ have a common factor greater than $1$.

articles.title: Ramanujan congruences for mex-related partition functions
articles.statement:
For a positive integer $A$, a
natural number $a$ and a partition $\lambda$, let $\operatorname{mex}_{A,a}(\lambda)$ be the
smallest positive integer congruent to $a$ modulo $A$ that is not a part of $\lambda$; let
$p_{A,a}(N)$ be the number of partitions $\lambda$ of $N$ with
$\operatorname{mex}_{A,a}(\lambda) \equiv a \pmod{2A}$; and let $\delta_{p,k}$ be the least
natural number $\delta$ with $24\delta \equiv 1 \pmod{p^k}$. Then for all natural numbers
$k \ge 1$, $t \ge 1$ and $n$, for each $p \in \{5, 7, 11\}$ and for both $A = p^k t$ and
$A = 2p^k t$,

$$p_{A,\,p^k t}(p^k n + \delta_{p,k}) \equiv 0 \pmod{p^{e}},$$

where $e = k$ for $p = 5$ and $p = 11$, and $e = \lfloor k/2 \rfloor + 1$ for $p = 7$.

## Sources

- Barman–Singh, JIS 24 (2021), Art. 21.6.3, corollary.

articles.title: The 3-dissection of $f_1^3$
articles.statement:
For $k \ge 1$ let $f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$, an
integer power series in $q$. Then

$$
f_1^3 f_3 f_6^2 f_9^3 f_{18}^3 = f_6^3 f_9^9 + 4 q^3 f_3^3 f_{18}^9 - 3 q f_3 f_6^2 f_9^6 f_{18}^3.
$$

Dividing by $f_3 f_6^2 f_9^3 f_{18}^3$ gives
$f_1^3 = \frac{f_6 f_9^6}{f_3 f_{18}^3} + 4q^3 \frac{f_3^2 f_{18}^6}{f_6^2 f_9^3} - 3q f_9^3$.

## Sources

- S. Shivaprasada Nayaka, B. N. Dharmendra, and M. C. Mahesh Kumar, *Divisibility Properties for Overcubic Partition Triples*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A80, Lemma 2, eq. (41).

articles.title: The 2-dissection of $f_1^2$
articles.statement:
For $k \ge 1$ let $f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$, an
integer power series in $q$. Then

$$f_1^2 f_4^2 f_8 f_{16}^2 = f_2 f_8^6 - 2 q f_2 f_4^2 f_{16}^4.$$

Dividing by $f_4^2 f_8 f_{16}^2$ gives
$f_1^2 = \frac{f_2 f_8^5}{f_4^2 f_{16}^2} - 2q \frac{f_2 f_{16}^2}{f_8}$.

## Sources

- S. Shivaprasada Nayaka, B. N. Dharmendra, and M. C. Mahesh Kumar, *Divisibility Properties for Overcubic Partition Triples*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A80, Lemma 1, eq. (39).

articles.title: The 2-dissection of $1/f_1^2$
articles.statement:
For $k \ge 1$ let
$f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$, an integer power series in $q$. Then

$$f_2^5 f_8 f_{16}^2 = f_1^2 f_8^6 + 2 q f_1^2 f_4^2 f_{16}^4.$$

Dividing by $f_1^2 f_2^5 f_8 f_{16}^2$ gives
$\frac{1}{f_1^2} = \frac{f_8^5}{f_2^5 f_{16}^2} + 2q \frac{f_4^2 f_{16}^2}{f_2^5 f_8}$.

## Sources

- S. Shivaprasada Nayaka, B. N. Dharmendra, and M. C. Mahesh Kumar, *Divisibility Properties for Overcubic Partition Triples*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A80, Lemma 1, eq. (40).

articles.title: Congruences for overcubic partition triples at arguments congruent to 8 modulo 16
articles.statement:
Let
