articles.title: Odd designated-summand partitions of zero
articles.statement:
The odd designated-summand partition function
satisfies $\mathrm{PD}_2(0) = 1$.

## Sources

- James A. Sellers, *New Infinite Families of Congruences Modulo Powers of 2 for 2-Regular Partitions with Designated Summands*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A16, Section 2, eq. (1).

articles.title: The odd designated-summand partition function
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$, the integer
$\mathrm{PD}_2(n)$ is defined as the coefficient of $q^n$ in the integer power series
$f_4 f_6^2 / (f_1 f_3 f_{12})$, where $f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$ is the Euler product
(the denominator has constant coefficient $1$, so it is invertible). It counts the partitions of
$n$ with designated summands in which all parts are odd.

## Sources

- James A. Sellers, *New Infinite Families of Congruences Modulo Powers of 2 for 2-Regular Partitions with Designated Summands*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A16, Sections 1-2, eq. (1).

articles.title: Generating function of odd designated-summand partitions
articles.statement:
For $k \ge 1$ let
$f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$ be the Euler product. This is the integer power series
$f_4 f_6^2 / (f_1 f_3 f_{12})$ in $q$, where the denominator $f_1 f_3 f_{12}$ is invertible
because its constant coefficient is $1$. It is the generating function
$\sum_{n \ge 0} \mathrm{PD}_2(n) q^n$ of the numbers $\mathrm{PD}_2(n)$ of partitions of $n$ with
designated summands into odd parts.

## Sources

- James A. Sellers, *New Infinite Families of Congruences Modulo Powers of 2 for 2-Regular Partitions with Designated Summands*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A16, Section 2, eq. (1) (quoting G. E. Andrews, R. P. Lewis, and J. Lovejoy, *Partitions with designated summands*, Acta Arith. 105 (2002)).

articles.title: Power-of-five congruence modulo 24 for partitions with distinct even parts
articles.statement:
Write
$\mathrm{ped}(m)$ for the number of partitions of $m$ in which the even parts are distinct (odd
parts may repeat). For all natural numbers $k \ge 1$ and $n$,

$$
\mathrm{ped}(9n+7) \equiv \mathrm{ped}\left(9 \cdot 5^{2k} n + \frac{57 \cdot 5^{2k} - 1}{8}\right)
  \pmod{24}.
$$

The quotient is exact, since $57 \cdot 5^{2k} - 1$ is divisible by $8$.

## Sources

- Hemjyoti Nath, *New Congruences for Partitions Where the Even Parts Are Distinct*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A79, Theorem 1.1.

articles.title: Congruences modulo 24 for partitions with distinct even parts
articles.statement:
Write $\mathrm{ped}(m)$ for the
number of partitions of $m$ in which the even parts are distinct (odd parts may repeat). For every
natural number $n$, each of $\mathrm{ped}(225n+43)$, $\mathrm{ped}(225n+88)$,
$\mathrm{ped}(225n+133)$ and $\mathrm{ped}(225n+223)$ is congruent to $0$ modulo $24$.

## Sources

- Hemjyoti Nath, *New Congruences for Partitions Where the Even Parts Are Distinct*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A79, Theorem 1.1.

articles.title: Andrews' identity for the first Rogers–Ramanujan series
articles.statement:
Let $q$ be a complex number with
$|q| < 1$, write $(q;q)_j = \prod_{i=1}^{j} (1 - q^i)$ for $j \ge 0$, and let
$(q^2;q^2)_\infty = \prod_{n=0}^{\infty} (1 - q^{2n+2})$ be the infinite q-Pochhammer symbol. Then

$$(q^2;q^2)_\infty \sum_{j=0}^{\infty} \frac{q^{j^2}}{(q;q)_j} = \sum_{\lambda \in \mathbb{Z}}
\left(q^{60\lambda^2+4\lambda} - q^{60\lambda^2+44\lambda+8} + q^{60\lambda^2+16\lambda+1} -
q^{60\lambda^2+64\lambda+17}\right).$$

All exponents on the right are nonnegative for integer $\lambda$.

## Sources

- John Greene and James A. Sellers, *Extending Recent Parity Results of Nyirenda and Mugwangwavari for Partitions with Initial Repetitions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A32, Theorem 10, quoting Andrews.

articles.title: Andrews' identity for the second Rogers–Ramanujan series
articles.statement:
Let $q$ be a complex number
with $|q| < 1$, write $(q;q)_j = \prod_{i=1}^{j} (1 - q^i)$ for $j \ge 0$, and let
$(q^2;q^2)_\infty = \prod_{n=0}^{\infty} (1 - q^{2n+2})$ be the infinite q-Pochhammer symbol. Then

$$(q^2;q^2)_\infty \sum_{j=0}^{\infty} \frac{q^{j^2+j}}{(q;q)_j} = \sum_{\lambda \in \mathbb{Z}}
\left(q^{60\lambda^2+8\lambda} - q^{60\lambda^2+32\lambda+4} + q^{60\lambda^2+28\lambda+3} -
q^{60\lambda^2+52\lambda+11}\right).$$

All exponents on the right are nonnegative for integer $\lambda$.

## Sources

- John Greene and James A. Sellers, *Extending Recent Parity Results of Nyirenda and Mugwangwavari for Partitions with Initial Repetitions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A32, Theorem 12, quoting Andrews.

articles.title: Andrews' theorem on partitions with initial repetitions
articles.statement:
Let $k \ge 1$ and $n \ge 0$ be
integers. Say that a partition has initial $k$-repetitions if, whenever a part $j$ appears at
least $k$ times, every integer $i$ with $1 \le i < j$ appears at least $k$ times. Then the number
of partitions of $n$ with initial $k$-repetitions equals the number of partitions of $n$ into parts
not divisible by $2k$, and this number equals the number of partitions of $n$ in which no part
appears more than $2k - 1$ times.

## Sources

- John Greene and James A. Sellers, *Extending Recent Parity Results of Nyirenda and Mugwangwavari for Partitions with Initial Repetitions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A32, Theorem 1, quoting Andrews.

articles.title: Residues $r$ with $16r + 1$ and $8r + 1$ both non-squares modulo $p$
articles.statement:
For every prime $p$,
the number of integers $r$ with $1 \le r \le p - 1$ such that neither $16r + 1$ nor $8r + 1$ is a
square modulo $p$ equals $\lfloor p/4 \rfloor$.

Here $0$ counts as a square modulo $p$, so "not a square" means "quadratic nonresidue". The paper
assumes $p \ge 5$; for $p = 2$ and $p = 3$ both sides are $0$. If $0$ were counted as a non-square,
the count at $p = 5$ would be $2$ instead of $1$.

## Sources

- John Greene and James A. Sellers, *Extending Recent Parity Results of Nyirenda and Mugwangwavari for Partitions with Initial Repetitions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A32, Theorem 5.

articles.title: Residues $r$ with $12r + 1$ and $8r + 1$ both non-squares modulo $p$
articles.statement:
For every prime $p$,
let $N$ be the number of integers $r$ with $1 \le r \le p - 1$ such that neither $12r + 1$ nor
$8r + 1$ is a square modulo $p$. Then $N = \lfloor p/4 \rfloor - 1$ if $p \equiv 5 \pmod{24}$,
$N = \lfloor p/4 \rfloor + 1$ if $p \equiv 11 \pmod{24}$, and $N = \lfloor p/4 \rfloor$ otherwise.

Here $0$ counts as a square modulo $p$, so "not a square" means "quadratic nonresidue". The paper
assumes $p \ge 5$; for $p = 2$ and $p = 3$ both sides are $0$. If $0$ were counted as a non-square,
the count at $p = 5$ would be $2$ instead of $0$.

## Sources

- John Greene and James A. Sellers, *Extending Recent Parity Results of Nyirenda and Mugwangwavari for Partitions with Initial Repetitions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A32, Theorem 8.

articles.title: Counting $r$ with $mr + 1$ and $nr + 1$ both quadratic nonresidues
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be an odd
prime, write $\left(\frac{a}{p}\right)$ for the Legendre symbol of an integer $a$, and let $m$ and
$n$ be integers with $p \nmid mn(n - m)$. If $N$ is the number of integers $r$ with
$0 \le r \le p - 1$ such that $\left(\frac{mr+1}{p}\right) = \left(\frac{nr+1}{p}\right) = -1$, then

$$4N = 4\left\lfloor \frac{p}{4} \right\rfloor -
\left(\left(\frac{m}{p}\right) - \left(\frac{n-m}{p}\right)\right)
\left(\left(\frac{n}{p}\right) - \left(\frac{m-n}{p}\right)\right).$$

## Sources

- John Greene and James A. Sellers, *Extending Recent Parity Results of Nyirenda and Mugwangwavari for Partitions with Initial Repetitions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A32, Lemma 1.

articles.title: Parity of $c_2(5n + 2)$
articles.statement:
Let $c_2(m)$ be the number of partitions of $m$ for which there
is an integer $j$ with $1 \le j \le m$ such that $j$ appears exactly $j$ times, every part other
than $j$ is at least $2j + 1$, and every even part that is at least $2j + 2$ appears only once.
Nyirenda and Mugwangwavari: for every integer $n \ge 0$, the number $c_2(5n + 2)$ is even.

## Sources

- John Greene and James A. Sellers, *Extending Recent Parity Results of Nyirenda and Mugwangwavari for Partitions with Initial Repetitions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A32, Theorem 3.

articles.title: Parity of $c_2(pn + r)$ for primes $p \ge 5$
articles.statement:
Let $c_2(m)$ be the number of partitions of
$m$ for which there is an integer $j$ with $1 \le j \le m$ such that $j$ appears exactly $j$
times, every part other than $j$ is at least $2j + 1$, and every even part that is at least
$2j + 2$ appears only once. Let $p \ge 5$ be a prime and let $r$ be an integer with
$1 \le r \le p - 1$ such that neither $16r + 1$ nor $8r + 1$ is a square modulo $p$. Then
$c_2(pn + r)$ is even for every integer $n \ge 0$.

Here $0$ counts as a square modulo $p$, so the hypothesis says that $16r + 1$ and $8r + 1$ are
quadratic nonresidues modulo $p$.

## Sources

- John Greene and James A. Sellers, *Extending Recent Parity Results of Nyirenda and Mugwangwavari for Partitions with Initial Repetitions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A32, Theorem 4.

articles.title: The partition function $c_2$ of Nyirenda and Mugwangwavari
articles.statement:
For an integer $n \ge 0$,
$c_2(n)$ is the number of partitions of $n$ for which there is an integer $j$ with
$1 \le j \le n$ such that $j$ appears exactly $j$ times, every part other than $j$ is at least
$2j + 1$, and every even part that is at least $2j + 2$ appears only once.

Odd parts that are at least $2j + 1$ may appear any number of times.

## Sources

- John Greene and James A. Sellers, *Extending Recent Parity Results of Nyirenda and Mugwangwavari for Partitions with Initial Repetitions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A32, Section 3 (definition of `c₂`, from Nyirenda and Mugwangwavari).

articles.title: Parity of $c_3(11n + 5)$, $c_3(11n + 7)$ and $c_3(11n + 9)$
articles.statement:
Let $c_3(m)$ be the number
of partitions of $m$ for which there is an integer $j$ with $1 \le j \le m$ such that the part $1$
appears exactly $j^2$ or $j^2 + 1$ times, the odd parts greater than $1$ are distinct, the even
parts are distinct, and every even part greater than $2j$ is divisible by $4$ and at least
$4j + 4$. Nyirenda and Mugwangwavari: for every integer $n \ge 0$, the numbers $c_3(11n + 5)$,
$c_3(11n + 7)$ and $c_3(11n + 9)$ are all even.

## Sources

- John Greene and James A. Sellers, *Extending Recent Parity Results of Nyirenda and Mugwangwavari for Partitions with Initial Repetitions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A32, Theorem 6.

articles.title: Parity of $c_3$ on residue classes modulo a prime
articles.statement:
Let $c_3$ be the initial-repetitions
partition function of Nyirenda and Mugwangwavari. Let $p \ge 5$ be a prime and let $r$ be an
integer with $1 \le r \le p - 1$ such that neither $12r + 1$ nor $8r + 1$ is a square modulo $p$.
Then $c_3(pn + r)$ is even for every integer $n \ge 0$.

Here $x$ is a square modulo $p$ when $x \equiv y^2 \pmod{p}$ for some integer $y$, so multiples
of $p$ count as squares.

## Sources

- John Greene and James A. Sellers, *Extending Recent Parity Results of Nyirenda and Mugwangwavari for Partitions with Initial Repetitions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A32, Theorem 7.

articles.title: The initial-repetitions partition function $c_3$
articles.statement:
For $n \ge 0$, $c_3(n)$ is the number
of partitions of $n$ for which there is an integer $j$ with $1 \le j \le n$ such that the part $1$
appears exactly $j^2$ or $j^2 + 1$ times, every odd part larger than $1$ appears exactly once,
every even part appears exactly once, and every even part greater than $2j$ is at least $4j + 4$
and divisible by $4$.

## Sources

- John Greene and James A. Sellers, *Extending Recent Parity Results of Nyirenda and Mugwangwavari for Partitions with Initial Repetitions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A32, Section 3 (definition of `c₃`, from Nyirenda and Mugwangwavari).

articles.title: $c_8(N)$ is even when $15N + 1$ is not a square
articles.statement:
Let $c_8$ be the initial-repetitions
partition function of Nyirenda and Mugwangwavari. For every integer $N \ge 0$ such that $15N + 1$
is not a perfect square, $c_8(N)$ is even.

## Sources

- John Greene and James A. Sellers, *Extending Recent Parity Results of Nyirenda and Mugwangwavari for Partitions with Initial Repetitions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A32, Theorem 11.

articles.title: $c_8$ is even on six residue classes modulo $49$
articles.statement:
Let $c_8$ be the initial-repetitions
partition function of Nyirenda and Mugwangwavari. For every integer $n \ge 0$ and every
$r \in \{6, 20, 27, 34, 41, 48\}$, the number $c_8(49n + r)$ is even.

This result is due to Nyirenda and Mugwangwavari.

## Sources

- John Greene and James A. Sellers, *Extending Recent Parity Results of Nyirenda and Mugwangwavari for Partitions with Initial Repetitions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A32, Theorem 9.

articles.title: $c_8'(N)$ is even when $15N + 4$ is not a square
articles.statement:
Let $c_8'$ be the partition function
that counts partitions with a possibly distinguished part. For every integer $N \ge 0$ such that
$15N + 4$ is not a perfect square, $c_8'(N)$ is even.

## Sources

- John Greene and James A. Sellers, *Extending Recent Parity Results of Nyirenda and Mugwangwavari for Partitions with Initial Repetitions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A32, Theorem 13.

articles.title: Parity of $c_8$ on residue classes modulo a prime
articles.statement:
Let $c_8$ be the initial-repetitions
partition function of Nyirenda and Mugwangwavari. Let $p \ge 7$ be a prime and let $r$ be an
integer with $1 \le r \le p - 1$ such that $15r + 1$ is not a square modulo $p$. Then
$c_8(pn + r)$ is even for every integer $n \ge 0$.

Here $x$ is a square modulo $p$ when $x \equiv y^2 \pmod{p}$ for some integer $y$, so multiples
of $p$ count as squares.

## Sources

- John Greene and James A. Sellers, *Extending Recent Parity Results of Nyirenda and Mugwangwavari for Partitions with Initial Repetitions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A32, Corollary 2.

articles.title: Parity of $c_8'$ on residue classes modulo a prime
articles.statement:
Let $c_8'$ be the partition function
that counts partitions with a possibly distinguished part. Let $p \ge 7$ be a prime and let $r$ be
an integer with $1 \le r \le p - 1$ such that $15r + 4$ is not a square modulo $p$. Then
$c_8'(pn + r)$ is even for every integer $n \ge 0$.

Here $x$ is a square modulo $p$ when $x \equiv y^2 \pmod{p}$ for some integer $y$, so multiples
of $p$ count as squares.

## Sources

- John Greene and James A. Sellers, *Extending Recent Parity Results of Nyirenda and Mugwangwavari for Partitions with Initial Repetitions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A32, Corollary 4.

articles.title: Parity of $c_8'$ on residue classes modulo powers of $2$
articles.statement:
Let $c_8'$ be the partition
function that counts partitions with a possibly distinguished part, and let $k \ge 1$, $n \ge 0$
and $r \ge 0$ be integers. If $r < 2^{2k}$ and $15r \equiv 2^{2k-1} - 4 \pmod{2^{2k}}$, then
$c_8'(2^{2k} n + r)$ is even. If $r < 2^{2k}$ and
$15r \equiv 2^{2k-1} + 2^{2k-2} - 4 \pmod{2^{2k}}$, then $c_8'(2^{2k} n + r)$ is even. If
$r < 2^{2k+1}$ and $15r \equiv 2^{2k} + 2^{2k-2} - 4 \pmod{2^{2k+1}}$, then
$c_8'(2^{2k+1} n + r)$ is even.

These $r$ are the paper's least nonnegative residues $r'_{k,1}$, $r'_{k,2}$, $r'_{k,3}$.

## Sources

- John Greene and James A. Sellers, *Extending Recent Parity Results of Nyirenda and Mugwangwavari for Partitions with Initial Repetitions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A32, Corollary 3.

articles.title: The initial-repetitions partition function $c_8'$
articles.statement:
For $n \ge 0$, $c_8'(n)$ is the number
of partitions of $n$ into distinct even parts plus the sum, over $m = 1, \dots, n$, of the number
of partitions of $n$ in which every even number $2i$ with $1 \le i \le m$ is a part, every even
part at most $m$ appears at most twice, every odd part at most $m$ appears exactly once, and every
part greater than $m$ is even and appears exactly once.

Equivalently, $c_8'(n)$ counts partitions of $n$ with a possibly distinguished part: either all
parts are even and distinct and no part is distinguished, or a part $2m$ is distinguished and the
conditions above hold for $m$.

## Sources

- John Greene and James A. Sellers, *Extending Recent Parity Results of Nyirenda and Mugwangwavari for Partitions with Initial Repetitions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A32, Section 4 (definition of `c₈'`).

articles.title: Parity of $c_8$ on residue classes modulo powers of $2$
articles.statement:
Let $c_8$ be the
initial-repetitions partition function of Nyirenda and Mugwangwavari, and let $k \ge 1$,
$n \ge 0$ and $r \ge 0$ be integers. If $r < 2^{2k}$ and $15r \equiv 2^{2k-1} - 1 \pmod{2^{2k}}$,
then $c_8(2^{2k} n + r)$ is even. If $r < 2^{2k}$ and
$15r \equiv 2^{2k-1} + 2^{2k-2} - 1 \pmod{2^{2k}}$, then $c_8(2^{2k} n + r)$ is even. If
$r < 2^{2k+1}$ and $15r \equiv 2^{2k} + 2^{2k-2} - 1 \pmod{2^{2k+1}}$, then
$c_8(2^{2k+1} n + r)$ is even.

These $r$ are the paper's least nonnegative residues $r_{k,1}$, $r_{k,2}$, $r_{k,3}$.

## Sources

- John Greene and James A. Sellers, *Extending Recent Parity Results of Nyirenda and Mugwangwavari for Partitions with Initial Repetitions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A32, Corollary 1.

articles.title: The partition function $c_8$
articles.statement:
For $n \ge 0$, $c_8(n)$ is the number of partitions of $n$
such that either (a) all parts are even and distinct, or (b) for some positive integer $j$, the
largest odd part is $2j - 1$, every positive odd integer $i \le j$ appears once or twice, every
odd integer $i$ with $j < i \le 2j - 1$ appears exactly once, all even parts are distinct, and
every even part greater than $j$ is at least $2j + 2$.

For $j = 1$ the paper's clauses "the largest odd part $2j - 1$ appears once" and "odd integers
$\le j$ appear once or twice" conflict; the second governs, as in the generating function
$(q^2;q^2)_\infty \sum_n q^{n^2}/(q;q)_n$ the paper uses (the other reading gives $c_8(2) = 1$,
contradicting Theorem 11 of the paper since $31$ is not a square).

## Sources

- John Greene and James A. Sellers, *Extending Recent Parity Results of Nyirenda and Mugwangwavari for Partitions with Initial Repetitions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A32, Section 3 (definition of `c₈`, from Nyirenda and Mugwangwavari).

articles.title: Small values of the partition functions $c_2$, $c_3$, $c_8$ and $c_8'$
articles.statement:
We have
$c_2(0) = 0$, $c_2(1) = 1$, $c_3(1) = 1$, $c_8(0) = c_8(1) = 1$, $c_8'(0) = 1$ and $c_8'(1) = 0$.

## Sources

- John Greene and James A. Sellers, *Extending Recent Parity Results of Nyirenda and Mugwangwavari for Partitions with Initial Repetitions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A32, Sections 3 and 4 (definitions of `c₂`, `c₃`, `c₈`, `c₈'`).

articles.title: Residues that are squares modulo $2^{2k}$ but not modulo $2^{2k+1}$
articles.statement:
Let $k \ge 0$ and let
$x$ be an integer with $0 \le x < 2^{2k+1}$, where the exponent $2k - 2$ is truncated at $0$. Then
$x$ is a square modulo $2^{2k}$ but not a square modulo $2^{2k+1}$ if and only if
$x = 2^{2k} + 2^{2k-2}$.

For $k \ge 1$ this is the unique such residue; for $k = 0$ both sides of the equivalence are false.

## Sources

- John Greene and James A. Sellers, *Extending Recent Parity Results of Nyirenda and Mugwangwavari for Partitions with Initial Repetitions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A32, Lemma 3.

articles.title: Residues that are squares modulo $2^{2k-1}$ but not modulo $2^{2k}$
articles.statement:
Let $k \ge 0$ and let
$x$ be an integer with $0 \le x < 2^{2k}$, where the exponents $2k - 1$ and $2k - 2$ are truncated
at $0$. Then $x$ is a square modulo $2^{2k-1}$ but not a square modulo $2^{2k}$ if and only if
$x = 2^{2k-1}$ or $x = 2^{2k-1} + 2^{2k-2}$.

For $k \ge 1$ these are exactly two residues; for $k = 0$ both sides of the equivalence are false.

## Sources

- John Greene and James A. Sellers, *Extending Recent Parity Results of Nyirenda and Mugwangwavari for Partitions with Initial Repetitions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A32, Lemma 2.

articles.title: 3-dissection of $f_1 f_2$
articles.statement:
Let $f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$ denote the Euler
products in $\mathbb{Z}[[q]]$. Then
$f_1 f_2 f_3 f_6 f_9^2 f_{18}^2 = f_6^2 f_9^6 - q f_3 f_6 f_9^3 f_{18}^3 -
2 q^2 f_3^2 f_{18}^6$.

Since each $f_k$ with $k \ge 1$ has constant term $1$, dividing both sides by
$f_3 f_6 f_9^2 f_{18}^2$ shows that this is equivalent to
$f_1 f_2 = f_6 f_9^4 / (f_3 f_{18}^2) - q f_9 f_{18} - 2 q^2 f_3 f_{18}^4 / (f_6 f_9^2)$.

## Sources

- James A. Sellers, *Elementary Proofs of Congruences for POND and PEND Partitions*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.4.7, Lemma 8 (`jis-2024-24.4.7-lem-8`).

articles.title: 3-dissection of $f_2 / (f_1 f_4)$
articles.statement:
Let $f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$ denote the
Euler products in $\mathbb{Z}[[q]]$. Then
$f_2 f_3^4 f_9^3 f_{12}^4 f_{18}^3 f_{36}^3 = f_1 f_3^2 f_4 f_{12}^2 f_{18}^{12} +
q f_1 f_3 f_4 f_6^2 f_9^3 f_{12} f_{18}^6 f_{36}^3 + q^2 f_1 f_4 f_6^4 f_9^6 f_{36}^6$.

Since each $f_k$ with $k \ge 1$ has constant term $1$, dividing both sides by
$f_1 f_3^4 f_4 f_9^3 f_{12}^4 f_{18}^3 f_{36}^3$ shows that this is equivalent to
$f_2 / (f_1 f_4) = f_{18}^9 / (f_3^2 f_9^3 f_{12}^2 f_{36}^3) +
q f_6^2 f_{18}^3 / (f_3^3 f_{12}^3) + q^2 f_6^4 f_9^3 f_{36}^3 / (f_3^4 f_{12}^4 f_{18}^3)$.

## Sources

- James A. Sellers, *Elementary Proofs of Congruences for POND and PEND Partitions*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.4.7, Lemma 7 (`jis-2024-24.4.7-lem-7`).

articles.title: 3-dissection of $f_2 / f_1^2$
articles.statement:
Let $f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$ denote the
Euler products in $\mathbb{Z}[[q]]$. Then
$f_2 f_3^8 f_{18}^3 = f_1^2 f_6^4 f_9^6 + 2 q f_1^2 f_3 f_6^3 f_9^3 f_{18}^3 +
4 q^2 f_1^2 f_3^2 f_6^2 f_{18}^6$.

Since each $f_k$ with $k \ge 1$ has constant term $1$, dividing both sides by
$f_1^2 f_3^8 f_{18}^3$ shows that this is equivalent to
$f_2 / f_1^2 = f_6^4 f_9^6 / (f_3^8 f_{18}^3) + 2 q f_6^3 f_9^3 / f_3^7 +
4 q^2 f_6^2 f_{18}^3 / f_3^6$.

## Sources

- James A. Sellers, *Elementary Proofs of Congruences for POND and PEND Partitions*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.4.7, Lemma 11 (`jis-2024-24.4.7-lem-11`).

articles.title: 3-dissection of $f_2^2 / f_1$
articles.statement:
Let $f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$ denote the
Euler products in $\mathbb{Z}[[q]]$. Then
$f_2^2 f_3 f_9 f_{18} = f_1 f_6 f_9^3 + q f_1 f_3 f_{18}^3$.

Since each $f_k$ with $k \ge 1$ has constant term $1$, dividing both sides by
$f_1 f_3 f_9 f_{18}$ shows that this is equivalent to
$f_2^2 / f_1 = f_6 f_9^2 / (f_3 f_{18}) + q f_{18}^2 / f_9$.

## Sources

- James A. Sellers, *Elementary Proofs of Congruences for POND and PEND Partitions*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.4.7, Lemma 10 (`jis-2024-24.4.7-lem-10`).

articles.title: 2-dissection of $f_3^3 / f_1$
articles.statement:
Let $f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$ denote the
Euler products in $\mathbb{Z}[[q]]$. Then
$f_2^2 f_3^3 f_4 f_{12} - q f_1 f_2^2 f_{12}^4 = f_1 f_4^4 f_6^2$.

Since each $f_k$ with $k \ge 1$ has constant term $1$, dividing both sides by
$f_1 f_2^2 f_4 f_{12}$ shows that this is equivalent to
$f_3^3 / f_1 - q f_{12}^3 / f_4 = f_4^3 f_6^2 / (f_2^2 f_{12})$.

## Sources

- James A. Sellers, *Elementary Proofs of Congruences for POND and PEND Partitions*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.4.7, Lemma 15 (`jis-2024-24.4.7-lem-15`).

articles.title: 3-dissection of $f_4 / f_1$
articles.statement:
Let $f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$ denote the
Euler products in $\mathbb{Z}[[q]]$. Then
$f_3^4 f_4 f_{18}^2 f_{36}^2 = f_1 f_3 f_{12} f_{18}^6 + q f_1 f_6^2 f_9^3 f_{36}^3 +
2 q^2 f_1 f_3 f_6 f_{18}^3 f_{36}^3$.

Since each $f_k$ with $k \ge 1$ has constant term $1$, dividing both sides by
$f_1 f_3^4 f_{18}^2 f_{36}^2$ shows that this is equivalent to
$f_4 / f_1 = f_{12} f_{18}^4 / (f_3^3 f_{36}^2) + q f_6^2 f_9^3 f_{36} / (f_3^4 f_{18}^2) +
2 q^2 f_6 f_{18} f_{36} / f_3^3$.

## Sources

- James A. Sellers, *Elementary Proofs of Congruences for POND and PEND Partitions*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.4.7, Lemma 13 (`jis-2024-24.4.7-lem-13`).

articles.title: The PEND condition
articles.statement:
A multiset $s$ of natural numbers (the parts of a partition)
satisfies the PEND condition when no even number occurs in $s$ exactly once; equivalently,
every even part that occurs in $s$ has multiplicity at least $2$, so the even parts are not
distinct.

## Sources

- James A. Sellers, *Elementary Proofs of Congruences for POND and PEND Partitions*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.4.7, Section 1.

articles.title: Examples of POND and PEND parts
articles.statement:
The multisets of parts $\{1, 1\}$ and $\{2\}$ satisfy
the POND condition, while $\{1\}$ and $\{2, 1\}$ do not; the multisets $\{1\}$ and $\{2, 2\}$
satisfy the PEND condition, while $\{2\}$ and $\{2, 4\}$ do not.

## Sources

- James A. Sellers, *Elementary Proofs of Congruences for POND and PEND Partitions*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.4.7, Section 1.

articles.title: The POND condition
articles.statement:
A multiset $s$ of natural numbers (the parts of a partition)
satisfies the POND condition when no odd number occurs in $s$ exactly once; equivalently,
every odd part that occurs in $s$ has multiplicity at least $2$, so the odd parts are not
distinct.

## Sources

- James A. Sellers, *Elementary Proofs of Congruences for POND and PEND Partitions*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.4.7, Section 1.

articles.title: 3-dissection of $1 / (f_1 f_2)$
articles.statement:
Let $f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$ denote the
Euler products in $\mathbb{Z}[[q]]$. Then
$f_3^6 f_6^6 f_9^3 f_{18}^3 = f_1 f_2 f_6^4 f_9^{12} + q f_1 f_2 f_3 f_6^3 f_9^9 f_{18}^3 +
3 q^2 f_1 f_2 f_3^2 f_6^2 f_9^6 f_{18}^6 - 2 q^3 f_1 f_2 f_3^3 f_6 f_9^3 f_{18}^9 +
4 q^4 f_1 f_2 f_3^4 f_{18}^{12}$.

Since each $f_k$ with $k \ge 1$ has constant term $1$, dividing both sides by
$f_1 f_2 f_3^6 f_6^6 f_9^3 f_{18}^3$ shows that this is equivalent to
$1 / (f_1 f_2) = f_9^9 / (f_3^6 f_6^2 f_{18}^3) + q f_9^6 / (f_3^5 f_6^3) +
3 q^2 f_9^3 f_{18}^3 / (f_3^4 f_6^4) - 2 q^3 f_{18}^6 / (f_3^3 f_6^5) +
4 q^4 f_{18}^9 / (f_3^2 f_6^6 f_9^3)$.

## Sources

- James A. Sellers, *Elementary Proofs of Congruences for POND and PEND Partitions*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.4.7, Lemma 9 (`jis-2024-24.4.7-lem-9`).

articles.title: Generating function for PEND partitions
articles.statement:
Let $\mathrm{pend}(n)$ be the number of PEND
partitions of $n$, and let $f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$. Then, as integer power series
in $q$, $f_1 f_4 f_6 \sum_{n \ge 0} \mathrm{pend}(n) q^n = f_2 f_{12}$. This is the identity
$\sum_{n \ge 0} \mathrm{pend}(n) q^n = f_2 f_{12} / (f_1 f_4 f_6)$ with the denominator cleared.

## Sources

- James A. Sellers, *Elementary Proofs of Congruences for POND and PEND Partitions*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.4.7, Theorem 18 (`jis-2024-24.4.7-thm-18`).

articles.title: Infinite family of congruences modulo 3 for PEND partitions
articles.statement:
Let $\mathrm{pend}(m)$ be
the number of PEND partitions of $m$. For all natural numbers $\alpha \ge 1$ and $n$,
$\mathrm{pend}\left(3^{2\alpha+1} n + (17 \cdot 3^{2\alpha} - 1)/8\right) \equiv 0 \pmod{3}$.

The division by $8$ is exact, since $3^{2\alpha} \equiv 1 \pmod{8}$.

## Sources

- James A. Sellers, *Elementary Proofs of Congruences for POND and PEND Partitions*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.4.7, Theorem 6 (`jis-2024-24.4.7-thm-6`).

articles.title: Internal congruence modulo 3 for PEND partitions
articles.statement:
Let $\mathrm{pend}(m)$ be the number
of PEND partitions of $m$. For every natural number $n$,
$\mathrm{pend}(27n + 10) \equiv \mathrm{pend}(3n + 1) \pmod{3}$.

## Sources

- James A. Sellers, *Elementary Proofs of Congruences for POND and PEND Partitions*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.4.7, Theorem 4 (`jis-2024-24.4.7-thm-4`).

articles.title: Congruence modulo 3 for PEND partitions of 27n + 19
articles.statement:
Let $\mathrm{pend}(m)$ be the
number of PEND partitions of $m$. For every natural number $n$,
$\mathrm{pend}(27n + 19) \equiv 0 \pmod{3}$.

## Sources

- James A. Sellers, *Elementary Proofs of Congruences for POND and PEND Partitions*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.4.7, Theorem 2 (`jis-2024-24.4.7-thm-2`).

articles.title: PEND partitions of zero
articles.statement:
The number of PEND partitions of $0$ is $1$, that is,
$\mathrm{pend}(0) = 1$.

## Sources

- James A. Sellers, *Elementary Proofs of Congruences for POND and PEND Partitions*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.4.7, Section 1 (OEIS A265254).

articles.title: The PEND partition function
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$, $\mathrm{pend}(n)$ is the number
of PEND partitions of $n$: partitions of $n$ in which every even part that occurs appears at
least twice (OEIS A265254).

## Sources

- James A. Sellers, *Elementary Proofs of Congruences for POND and PEND Partitions*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.4.7, Section 1.

articles.title: Congruences modulo 2, 3 and 4 for POND partitions
articles.statement:
Let $\mathrm{pond}(m)$ be the number
of POND partitions of $m$. For every natural number $n$, $\mathrm{pond}(3n + 2) \equiv 0 \pmod{2}$,
$\mathrm{pond}(27n + 26) \equiv 0 \pmod{3}$ and $\mathrm{pond}(3n + 1) \equiv 0 \pmod{4}$.

## Sources

- James A. Sellers, *Elementary Proofs of Congruences for POND and PEND Partitions*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.4.7, Theorem 1 (`jis-2024-24.4.7-thm-1`).

articles.title: Generating function for POND partitions
articles.statement:
Let $\mathrm{pond}(n)$ be the number of POND
partitions of $n$, and let $f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$. Then, as integer power series
in $q$, $f_2^2 f_3 f_{12} \sum_{n \ge 0} \mathrm{pond}(n) q^n = f_4 f_6^2$. This is the identity
$\sum_{n \ge 0} \mathrm{pond}(n) q^n = f_4 f_6^2 / (f_2^2 f_3 f_{12})$ with the denominator
cleared.

## Sources

- James A. Sellers, *Elementary Proofs of Congruences for POND and PEND Partitions*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.4.7, Theorem 17 (`jis-2024-24.4.7-thm-17`).

articles.title: Infinite family of congruences modulo 3 for POND partitions
articles.statement:
Let $\mathrm{pond}(m)$ be
the number of POND partitions of $m$. For all natural numbers $\alpha \ge 1$ and $n$,
$\mathrm{pond}\left(3^{2\alpha+1} n + (23 \cdot 3^{2\alpha} + 1)/8\right) \equiv 0 \pmod{3}$.

The division by $8$ is exact, since $3^{2\alpha} \equiv 1 \pmod{8}$.

## Sources

- James A. Sellers, *Elementary Proofs of Congruences for POND and PEND Partitions*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.4.7, Theorem 5 (`jis-2024-24.4.7-thm-5`).

articles.title: Internal congruence modulo 3 for POND partitions
articles.statement:
Let $\mathrm{pond}(m)$ be the number
of POND partitions of $m$. For every natural number $n$,
$\mathrm{pond}(27n + 17) \equiv \mathrm{pond}(3n + 2) \pmod{3}$.

## Sources

- James A. Sellers, *Elementary Proofs of Congruences for POND and PEND Partitions*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.4.7, Theorem 3 (`jis-2024-24.4.7-thm-3`).

articles.title: The number of POND partitions of zero
articles.statement:
The number $\mathrm{pond}(0)$ of POND
partitions of $0$ equals $1$: the only partition of $0$ is the empty partition, and it is POND.

## Sources

- James A. Sellers, *Elementary Proofs of Congruences for POND and PEND Partitions*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.4.7, Section 1 (OEIS A265256).

articles.title: Number of POND partitions
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$, $\mathrm{pond}(n)$ is the number of
partitions of $n$ that are POND, that is, in which every odd part that occurs has multiplicity
at least $2$ (OEIS A265256).

## Sources

- James A. Sellers, *Elementary Proofs of Congruences for POND and PEND Partitions*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.4.7, Section 1.

articles.title: Prime-power congruence for powers of Euler products
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, let
$j, k, m \ge 1$ be natural numbers, and let $f_m = \prod_{i \ge 1} (1 - q^{mi})$. Then for every
natural number $n$, the coefficient of $q^n$ in $f_m^{p^j k}$ is congruent modulo $p^j$ to the
coefficient of $q^n$ in $f_{pm}^{p^{j-1} k}$.

## Sources

- James A. Sellers, *Elementary Proofs of Congruences for POND and PEND Partitions*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.4.7, Lemma 16 (`jis-2024-24.4.7-lem-16`).

articles.title: Vanishing coefficients of Jacobi's cube series
articles.statement:
Let $J(X)$ be Jacobi's cube series. If a
natural number $b$ is not of the form $t(t+1)/2$ for any natural number $t$, then the coefficient
of $X^b$ in $J(X)$ is $0$.

articles.title: Coefficients of Jacobi's cube series at triangular numbers
articles.statement:
Let $J(X)$ be Jacobi's cube
series. For every natural number $t$, the coefficient of $X^{t(t+1)/2}$ in $J(X)$ is
$(-1)^t (2t+1)$.

articles.title: Partition congruences from a power of Euler's series
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, let $r < p$ be
a natural number, and let $E(X) = \sum_{k \in \mathbb{Z}} (-1)^k X^{k(3k-1)/2}$ be Euler's
pentagonal series in $\mathbb{Z}[[X]]$. If $p$ divides the coefficient of $X^{pm+r}$ in
$E(X)^{p-1}$ for every natural number $m$, then $p$ divides the number of partitions of $pm + r$
for every natural number $m$.

articles.title: Jacobi's cube series
articles.statement:
Jacobi's cube series is the formal power series
$J(X) = \sum_{t \ge 0} (-1)^t (2t+1) X^{t(t+1)/2}$ in $\mathbb{Z}[[X]]$: for each natural
number $t$ its coefficient at the triangular number $t(t+1)/2$ is $(-1)^t (2t+1)$, and all its
other coefficients are $0$.

articles.title: Jacobi's cube identity
articles.statement:
Let $E(X) = \sum_{k \in \mathbb{Z}} (-1)^k X^{k(3k-1)/2}$ be
Euler's pentagonal series and $J(X) = \sum_{t \ge 0} (-1)^t (2t+1) X^{t(t+1)/2}$ Jacobi's cube
series, both in $\mathbb{Z}[[X]]$. Then $E(X)^3 = J(X)$.

articles.title: Ramanujan's congruence modulo 11
articles.statement:
For every natural number $m$, the number of partitions
of $11m + 6$ is divisible by $11$.

Proof: We follow Hirschhorn's Section 2 residue-section argument, using Euler's
pentagonal number theorem and Jacobi's cube identity.

## Sources

- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramanujan%27s_congruences

articles.title: Ramanujan's congruence modulo 5
articles.statement:
For every natural number $m$, the number of partitions
of $5m + 4$ is divisible by $5$.

## Sources

- Hartosh Singh Bal and Gaurav Bhatnagar, JIS 27 (2024), Art. 24.1.6, lines 801–804. Live source: https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL27/Bhatnagar/bhat4.tex

articles.title: Ramanujan's congruence modulo 7
articles.statement:
For every natural number $m$, the number of partitions
of $7m + 5$ is divisible by $7$.

## Sources

- S. Ramanujan, "Some properties of p(n), the number of partitions of n", Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society 19 (1919), 207–210, where the congruence is stated and proved. The proof follows Ramanujan's argument there: the sixth power of Euler's product is the square of Jacobi's cube series, and a sum of two squares divisible by 7 has both terms divisible by 7.

articles.title: Twice a triangular number
articles.statement: For every natural number $a$, $2\binom{a+1}{2} = a(a+1)$.

articles.title: Four 2-dissections of quotients of Euler products
articles.statement:
Write
$f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$ for the Euler products in the ring of integer power series
in $q$. Then

$$
f_3 f_2^2 f_8 f_{12} f_{16} f_{24} f_{48} =
f_1 \left(f_4 f_6 f_{16}^2 f_{24}^3 + q f_6 f_8^3 f_{12} f_{48}^2\right),
$$



$$
f_1^3 f_4 f_6^2 f_{12} = f_3 \left(f_4^4 f_6^2 - 3 q f_2^2 f_{12}^4\right),
$$



$$
f_5 f_2^3 f_8 f_{20} f_{40} = f_1 \left(f_2 f_8^2 f_{20}^3 + q f_4^3 f_{10} f_{40}^2\right),
$$



$$
f_1 f_4 f_8 f_{10}^3 f_{40} = f_5 \left(f_2 f_8^2 f_{20}^3 - q f_4^3 f_{10} f_{40}^2\right).
$$

These are the 2-dissections of $f_3 / f_1$, $f_1^3 / f_3$, $f_5 / f_1$ and $f_1 / f_5$ with the
denominators cleared; for example, the first is
$f_3 / f_1 = \frac{f_4 f_6 f_{16} f_{24}^2}{f_2^2 f_8 f_{12} f_{48}} +
q \frac{f_6 f_8^2 f_{48}}{f_2^2 f_{16} f_{24}}$ multiplied by
$f_1 f_2^2 f_8 f_{12} f_{16} f_{24} f_{48}$.

## Sources

- Pujashree Buragohain and Nipen Saikia, *Some New Congruences for l-Regular Cubic Partitions with Odd Parts Overlined*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A101, Lemma 3, eqs. (9), (10), (13), (14).

articles.title: Congruences modulo 16 for 8-regular cubic partitions with odd parts overlined
articles.statement:
Write
$f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$ for the Euler products in the ring of integer power series
in $q$, and $a_8(n)$ for the $n$th coefficient of $f_2 f_8^2 f_{32} / (f_1^2 f_4 f_{16})$, the
number of $8$-regular cubic partitions of $n$ with odd parts overlined. Let $p \ge 5$ be a prime
with Legendre symbol $\left(\frac{-6}{p}\right) = -1$, let $s = (p - 1)/6$ if $p \equiv 1 \pmod 6$
and $s = (-p - 1)/6$ otherwise, and let $\delta \ge 0$. Then, comparing coefficients of power
series in $q$,

$$
f_8 \sum_{n \ge 0} a_8\left(4p^{2\delta} n + \frac{25p^{2\delta} - 7}{6}\right) q^n \equiv
8 (-1)^{\delta s} f_1 f_{16}^2 \pmod{16},
$$

and for all $n \ge 0$ and $1 \le t \le p - 1$,

$$
a_8\left(4p^{2\delta+2} n + 4p^{2\delta+1} t + \frac{25p^{2\delta+2} - 7}{6}\right) \equiv 0
\pmod{16}.
$$

The divisions by $6$ are exact. With $\psi(q^8) = f_{16}^2 / f_8$, the first congruence is
the paper's $\sum_n a_8(\ldots) q^n \equiv 8 (-1)^{\delta s} f_1 \psi(q^8) \pmod{16}$
multiplied by $f_8$.

## Sources

- Pujashree Buragohain and Nipen Saikia, *Some New Congruences for l-Regular Cubic Partitions with Odd Parts Overlined*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A101, Theorem 12, eqs. (105), (106).

articles.title: Congruences modulo 4 and 8 for 8-regular cubic partitions with odd parts overlined
articles.statement:
Write
$f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$ for the Euler products in the ring of integer power series
in $q$, and $a_8(n)$ for the $n$th coefficient of $f_2 f_8^2 f_{32} / (f_1^2 f_4 f_{16})$, the
number of $8$-regular cubic partitions of $n$ with odd parts overlined. Let $p \ge 5$ be a prime
with Legendre symbol $\left(\frac{-3}{p}\right) = -1$, let $s = (p - 1)/6$ if $p \equiv 1 \pmod 6$
and $s = (-p - 1)/6$ otherwise, and let $\delta \ge 0$. Then, comparing coefficients of power
series in $q$,

$$
f_4 \sum_{n \ge 0} a_8\left(4p^{2\delta} n + \frac{13p^{2\delta} - 7}{6}\right) q^n \equiv
2 (-1)^{\delta s} f_1 f_8^2 \pmod{4},
$$



$$
f_1 \sum_{n \ge 0} a_8\left(4p^{2\delta} n + \frac{19p^{2\delta} - 7}{6}\right) q^n \equiv
4 (-1)^{\delta s} f_2^2 f_{16} \pmod{8},
$$

and for all $n \ge 0$ and $1 \le t \le p - 1$,

$$
a_8\left(4p^{2\delta+2} n + 4p^{2\delta+1} t + \frac{13p^{2\delta+2} - 7}{6}\right) \equiv 0
\pmod{4},
$$



$$
a_8\left(4p^{2\delta+2} n + 4p^{2\delta+1} t + \frac{19p^{2\delta+2} - 7}{6}\right) \equiv 0
\pmod{8}.
$$

The divisions by $6$ are exact. With $\psi(q) = f_2^2 / f_1$ and $\psi(q^4) = f_8^2 / f_4$, the
power series congruences are the paper's $\sum_n a_8(\ldots) q^n \equiv 2 (-1)^{\delta s} f_1
\psi(q^4) \pmod{4}$ and $\sum_n a_8(\ldots) q^n \equiv 4 (-1)^{\delta s} \psi(q) f_{16} \pmod{8}$,
multiplied by $f_4$ and by $f_1$.

articles.title: Congruences modulo 16 and 8 for 5-regular cubic partitions with odd parts overlined
articles.statement:
Let
$a_5(n)$ be the number of $5$-regular cubic partitions of $n$ with odd parts overlined, that is,
the $n$th coefficient of $f_2 f_5^2 f_{20} / (f_1^2 f_4 f_{10})$, where
$f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$. Then for every $n \ge 0$, $16$ divides $a_5(8n + 7)$, and
$8$ divides $a_5(20n + 2j + 1)$ for each $j = 1, \ldots, 9$.

## Sources

- Pujashree Buragohain and Nipen Saikia, *Some New Congruences for l-Regular Cubic Partitions with Odd Parts Overlined*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A101, Corollary 3, eqs. (76), (77).

articles.title: Congruences modulo 4 for 5-regular cubic partitions with odd parts overlined
articles.statement:
Write
$f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$ for the Euler products in the ring of integer power series
in $q$, and $a_5(n)$ for the $n$th coefficient of $f_2 f_5^2 f_{20} / (f_1^2 f_4 f_{10})$, the
number of $5$-regular cubic partitions of $n$ with odd parts overlined. Let $p \ge 5$ be a prime
with Legendre symbol $\left(\frac{-15}{p}\right) = -1$, let $s = (p - 1)/6$ if
$p \equiv 1 \pmod 6$ and $s = (-p - 1)/6$ otherwise, and let $\delta \ge 0$. Then, comparing

$$

\equiv 2 (-1)^{(\delta+1) s} f_1 f_{40}^2 \pmod{4},
$$

and for all $n \ge 0$ and $1 \le t \le p - 1$,

$$
a_5\left(16p^{2\delta+2} n + 16p^{2\delta+1} t + \frac{122p^{2\delta+2} - 2}{3}\right) \equiv 0

articles.title: Congruences modulo 8, 56 and 24 for 4-regular cubic partitions with odd parts overlined
articles.statement:
Let $a_4(n)$ be the number of $4$-regular cubic partitions of $n$ with odd parts overlined, that
is, the $n$th coefficient of $f_2 f_4^2 f_{16} / (f_1^2 f_4 f_8)$, where
$f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$. Then for every $n \ge 0$, $8$ divides $a_4(4n + 3)$, $56$
divides $a_4(28n + 4j + 3)$ for each $j = 1, \ldots, 6$, and $24$ divides $a_4(36n + 19)$.

## Sources

- Pujashree Buragohain and Nipen Saikia, *Some New Congruences for l-Regular Cubic Partitions with Odd Parts Overlined*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A101, Corollary 2, eqs. (55)–(57).

articles.title: Congruences modulo 4 for 4-regular cubic partitions with odd parts overlined
articles.statement:
Write
$f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$ for the Euler products in the ring of integer power series
in $q$, and $a_4(n)$ for the $n$th coefficient of $f_2 f_4^2 f_{16} / (f_1^2 f_4 f_8)$, the
number of $4$-regular cubic partitions of $n$ with odd parts overlined. Let $p \ge 5$ be a prime
with Legendre symbol $\left(\frac{-2}{p}\right) = -1$ and let $\delta \ge 0$. Then for every
$n \ge 0$, $a_4(4p^{2\delta} n + (3p^{2\delta} - 1)/2)$ is congruent modulo $4$ to twice the
coefficient of $q^n$ in $f_1 f_8$, and for all $n \ge 0$ and $1 \le t \le p - 1$,

$$
a_4\left(4p^{2\delta+2} n + 4p^{2\delta+1} t + \frac{3p^{2\delta+2} - 1}{2}\right) \equiv 0
\pmod{4}.
$$

articles.title: Generating function for $\ell$-regular cubic partitions with odd parts overlined
articles.statement:
Let
$\ell \ge 1$, write $f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$ for the Euler products in the ring of
integer power series in $q$, and let $a_\ell(n)$ be the $n$th coefficient of
$f_2 f_\ell^2 f_{4\ell} / (f_1^2 f_4 f_{2\ell})$ (the denominator has constant term $1$, so it
is invertible). Then

$$
f_1^2 f_4 f_{2\ell} \sum_{n \ge 0} a_\ell(n) q^n = f_2 f_\ell^2 f_{4\ell}.
$$

For $\ell > 2$ the paper identifies $a_\ell(n)$ with the number of $\ell$-regular cubic
partitions of $n$ with odd parts overlined.

## Sources

- Pujashree Buragohain and Nipen Saikia, *Some New Congruences for l-Regular Cubic Partitions with Odd Parts Overlined*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A101, Section 1, eq. (2).

articles.title: Congruences modulo 4 for regular cubic partitions with odd parts overlined
articles.statement:
Write
$f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$ for the Euler products in the ring of integer power series
in $q$. For $\ell \ge 1$ let $a_\ell(n)$ be the $n$th coefficient of
$f_2 f_\ell^2 f_{4\ell} / (f_1^2 f_4 f_{2\ell})$; for $\ell > 2$ this is the number of
$\ell$-regular cubic partitions of $n$ with odd parts overlined. Then for all natural numbers
$k$ and $n$: (i) if $k > 1$, then $4$ divides $a_{2k}(4n + 3)$; (ii) if $k \ge 1$, then $4$
divides $a_{2k+1}(4n + 2)$; (iii) if $k > 0$, then $4$ divides $a_{4k}(4n + 2)$; (iv) if
$k > 0$, then $4$ divides $a_{4k+1}(4n + 3)$.

## Sources

- Pujashree Buragohain and Nipen Saikia, *Some New Congruences for l-Regular Cubic Partitions with Odd Parts Overlined*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A101, Theorem 5, eqs. (17)–(20).

articles.title: Congruence modulo 8 for 9-regular cubic partitions with odd parts overlined
articles.statement:
For every
$n \ge 0$, the number $a_9(4n + 3)$ of $9$-regular cubic partitions of $4n + 3$ with odd parts
overlined is divisible by $8$.

## Sources

- Pujashree Buragohain and Nipen Saikia, *Some New Congruences for l-Regular Cubic Partitions with Odd Parts Overlined*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A101, Corollary 4, eq. (118).

articles.title: Congruences modulo 4 for 9-regular cubic partitions with odd parts overlined
articles.statement:
Let
$a_9(n)$ be the number of $9$-regular cubic partitions of $n$ with odd parts overlined, and let
$f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$. Let $p \ge 5$ be a prime with Legendre symbol
$\left(\frac{-2}{p}\right) = -1$, and let $\delta \ge 0$. Then for every $n \ge 0$,

$$a_9\left(8p^{2\delta} n + \frac{19p^{2\delta} - 4}{3}\right) \equiv 2c_n \pmod 4,$$

where $c_n$ is the coefficient of $q^n$ in $f_1 f_{18}$, and for all $n \ge 0$ and all $t$ with
$1 \le t \le p - 1$,

$$a_9\left(8p^{2\delta+2} n + 8p^{2\delta+1} t + \frac{19p^{2\delta+2} - 4}{3}\right)
\equiv 0 \pmod 4.$$

The divisions by $3$ are exact.

## Sources

- Pujashree Buragohain and Nipen Saikia, *Some New Congruences for l-Regular Cubic Partitions with Odd Parts Overlined*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A101, Theorem 13, eq. (110) and the unnumbered congruence after it.

articles.title: Congruences modulo 16 for 16-regular cubic partitions with odd parts overlined
articles.statement:
Let
$a_{16}(n)$ be the number of $16$-regular cubic partitions of $n$ with odd parts overlined, and
let $f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$. Let $p \ge 5$ be a prime with Legendre symbol
$\left(\frac{-2}{p}\right) = -1$, and let $\delta \ge 0$. Then for every $n \ge 0$,

$$a_{16}\left(4p^{2\delta} n + \frac{11p^{2\delta} - 5}{2}\right) \equiv 8c_n \pmod{16},$$

where $c_n$ is the coefficient of $q^n$ in $f_1 f_{32}$, and for all $n \ge 0$ and all $t$ with
$1 \le t \le p - 1$,

$$a_{16}\left(4p^{2\delta+2} n + 4p^{2\delta+1} t + \frac{11p^{2\delta+2} - 5}{2}\right)
\equiv 0 \pmod{16}.$$

The divisions by $2$ are exact.

## Sources

- Pujashree Buragohain and Nipen Saikia, *Some New Congruences for l-Regular Cubic Partitions with Odd Parts Overlined*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A101, Theorem 14, eq. (119) and the unnumbered congruence after it.

articles.title: Congruences modulo 18 and 12 for 3-regular cubic partitions with odd parts overlined
articles.statement:
Let $a_3(n)$ be the number of $3$-regular cubic partitions of $n$ with odd parts overlined.
For every $n \ge 0$, $a_3(8n + 5)$ is divisible by $18$, and $a_3(16n + 11)$ and
$a_3(16n + 15)$ are divisible by $12$.

## Sources

- Pujashree Buragohain and Nipen Saikia, *Some New Congruences for l-Regular Cubic Partitions with Odd Parts Overlined*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A101, Corollary 1, eqs. (39)–(41).

articles.title: Congruences modulo 6 for 3-regular cubic partitions with odd parts overlined
articles.statement:
Let
$a_3(n)$ be the number of $3$-regular cubic partitions of $n$ with odd parts overlined, and let
$f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$. Let $p \ge 5$ be a prime with Legendre symbol
$\left(\frac{-3}{p}\right) = -1$, and let $\delta \ge 0$. Then for every $n \ge 0$,

articles.title: Congruences modulo 12 for 3-regular cubic partitions with odd parts overlined
articles.statement:
Let
$a_3(n)$ be the number of $3$-regular cubic partitions of $n$ with odd parts overlined, and let
$f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$. Let $p \ge 5$ be a prime with Legendre symbol
