articles.title: Constant term of the overlined ℓ-regular cubic partition numbers
articles.statement:
For every natural number
$\ell \ge 1$, the coefficient $a_\ell(0)$ of $q^0$ in the generating function of $\ell$-regular
cubic partitions with odd parts overlined equals $1$.

## Sources

- Pujashree Buragohain and Nipen Saikia, *Some New Congruences for l-Regular Cubic Partitions with Odd Parts Overlined*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A101, Section 1, eq. (2).

articles.title: ℓ-regular cubic partitions with odd parts overlined
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $\ell$ and $n$,
$a_\ell(n)$ is the coefficient of $q^n$ in the integer power series

$$\frac{f_2 f_\ell^2 f_{4\ell}}{f_1^2 f_4 f_{2\ell}}, \qquad f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km}).$$

The quotient is meaningful for $\ell \ge 1$, where the denominator has constant term $1$. For
$\ell > 2$, the range the paper considers, $a_\ell(n)$ is the number of $\ell$-regular cubic
partitions of $n$ in which the first occurrence of each distinct odd part may be overlined; for
example, $a_3(5) = 18$.

## Sources

- Pujashree Buragohain and Nipen Saikia, *Some New Congruences for l-Regular Cubic Partitions with Odd Parts Overlined*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A101, Section 1, eq. (2).

articles.title: Generating function of ℓ-regular cubic partitions with odd parts overlined
articles.statement:
For a natural
number $\ell$, this is the integer power series

$$\frac{f_2 f_\ell^2 f_{4\ell}}{f_1^2 f_4 f_{2\ell}}, \qquad f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km}).$$

It is meaningful for $\ell \ge 1$, where the denominator has constant term $1$ and so is
invertible. For $\ell > 2$, the range the paper considers, its coefficient of $q^n$ is the number
of $\ell$-regular cubic partitions of $n$ with odd parts overlined.

## Sources

- Pujashree Buragohain and Nipen Saikia, *Some New Congruences for l-Regular Cubic Partitions with Odd Parts Overlined*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A101, Section 1, eq. (2).

articles.title: Double coset representatives for $\Gamma_0(N)$
articles.statement:
Let $N$ be a natural number such that
either $N$ is squarefree, or $N$ is even and $N/2$ is squarefree. Write $\Gamma_0(N)$ for the
group of matrices in $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ whose lower left entry is divisible by $N$, and
$T = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$. Then for every
$\gamma \in \mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ there is exactly one natural number $\delta$ dividing $N$
for which there exist $A \in \Gamma_0(N)$ and an integer $h$ with

$$\gamma = A \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ \delta & 1 \end{pmatrix} T^h.$$

Equivalently, the matrices $\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ \delta & 1 \end{pmatrix}$ with
$\delta \mid N$ form a complete set of representatives, without repetition, of the double cosets
$\Gamma_0(N) \backslash \mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z}) / \Gamma_\infty$, where $\Gamma_\infty$ is
generated by $T$; adding $-I$ to $\Gamma_\infty$ changes nothing, as $-I \in \Gamma_0(N)$.

## Sources

- Murugan P and Fathima S. N, *Arithmetic Density of Certain ℓ-Regular Overpartitions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A3, Lemma 3, quoting Wang, Lemma 4.3. "`N / 2` is squarefree" is read with `2 ∣ N`.

articles.title: Prime-power congruence for truncated Euler products
articles.statement:
Let $s$ and $t$ be positive integers,
let $p$ be a prime and let $N$ be a natural number. Then every coefficient of the polynomial

$$\Big(\prod_{m=1}^{N} (1 - X^{sm})\Big)^{p^t} - \Big(\prod_{m=1}^{N} (1 - X^{spm})\Big)^{p^{t-1}}$$

in $\mathbb{Z}[X]$ is divisible by $p^t$.

Since the truncated products agree with the infinite products in all degrees up to $N$, letting
$N$ grow gives the congruence of formal power series
$\prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{sm})^{p^t} \equiv \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{spm})^{p^{t-1}} \pmod{p^t}$.

## Sources

- Murugan P and Fathima S. N, *Arithmetic Density of Certain ℓ-Regular Overpartitions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A3, Lemma 1.

articles.title: Truncated generating function for $\ell$-regular overpartitions
articles.statement:
Let $\ell \ge 1$, $N$ and
$n \le N$ be natural numbers, and let $A_\ell(n)$ be the number of overpartitions of $n$ with no
part divisible by $\ell$. Then the coefficient of $X^n$ in the polynomial

$$\prod_{1 \le k \le N,\ \ell \nmid k} \Big((1 + X^k) \sum_{i=0}^{N} X^{ki}\Big) \in \mathbb{N}[X]$$

equals $A_\ell(n)$.

This is a finite-polynomial form of the generating function
$\sum_{n \ge 0} A_\ell(n) q^n = \prod_{k \ge 1,\ \ell \nmid k} (1 + q^k)/(1 - q^k)$: each
geometric series is cut off at $i = N$, and only coefficients up to degree $N$ are compared.

## Sources

- Murugan P and Fathima S. N, *Arithmetic Density of Certain ℓ-Regular Overpartitions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A3, Identity (1).

articles.title: Two $\ell$-regular overpartitions of one
articles.statement:
For every natural number $\ell \ge 2$, the number
$A_\ell(1)$ of overpartitions of $1$ with no part divisible by $\ell$ equals $2$: they are the
single part $1$, without and with an overline.

Among positive $\ell$, the hypothesis $\ell \ge 2$ says exactly that $\ell$ does not divide the
sole part $1$.

## Sources

- Murugan P and Fathima S. N, *Arithmetic Density of Certain ℓ-Regular Overpartitions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A3, Identity (1).

articles.title: One $\ell$-regular overpartition of zero
articles.statement:
For every natural number $\ell$, the number
$A_\ell(0)$ of overpartitions of $0$ with no part divisible by $\ell$ equals $1$: the only one is
the empty overpartition.

The statement also covers $\ell = 0$, a harmless extension of the paper's positive regularity
parameter.

## Sources

- Murugan P and Fathima S. N, *Arithmetic Density of Certain ℓ-Regular Overpartitions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A3, Identity (1).

articles.title: Number of $\ell$-regular overpartitions
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $\ell$ and $n$, $A_\ell(n)$ is
the number of overpartitions of $n$ in which no part is divisible by $\ell$.

No positivity restriction is placed on $\ell$; for $\ell = 0$ every overpartition of $n$ is
counted, since parts are positive.

## Sources

- Murugan P and Fathima S. N, *Arithmetic Density of Certain ℓ-Regular Overpartitions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A3, Identity (1).

articles.title: $\ell$-regular overpartitions vanish modulo $4$ along families of primes
articles.statement:
For a natural
number $\ell$, let $A_\ell(m)$ be the number of overpartitions of $m$ with no part divisible by
$\ell$. Let $\ell \equiv 3 \pmod 4$, let $k$, $n$ and $j$ be natural numbers, and let
$p_1, \dots, p_{k+1}$ be primes, not necessarily distinct, each greater than $2$ and congruent
to $3$ modulo $4$. If $j \not\equiv 0 \pmod{p_{k+1}}$, then

$$A_\ell\big(p_1^2 \cdots p_k^2 \, p_{k+1} \, (p_{k+1}(4n + 1) + 4j)\big) \equiv 0 \pmod 4.$$

The paper takes $j$ to be an integer; here $j$ is a natural number.

## Sources

- Murugan P and Fathima S. N, *Arithmetic Density of Certain ℓ-Regular Overpartitions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A3, Theorem 5.

articles.title: $\ell$-regular overpartitions vanish modulo $4$ on progressions modulo $4\ell$
articles.statement:
For a
natural number $\ell$, let $A_\ell(m)$ be the number of overpartitions of $m$ with no part
divisible by $\ell$. Let $\ell \equiv 3 \pmod 4$, and let $n$ and $j$ be natural numbers with
$j \not\equiv (\ell - 3)/4 \pmod{\ell}$. Then $A_\ell(4\ell n + 4j + 3) \equiv 0 \pmod 4$.

## Sources

- Murugan P and Fathima S. N, *Arithmetic Density of Certain ℓ-Regular Overpartitions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A3, Theorem 6.

articles.title: $\ell$-regular overpartitions vanish modulo $4$ along powers of one prime
articles.statement:
For a natural
number $\ell$, let $A_\ell(m)$ be the number of overpartitions of $m$ with no part divisible by
$\ell$. Let $\ell \equiv 3 \pmod 4$, and let $p > 2$ be a prime with $p \not\equiv 1 \pmod 6$.
Then for all natural numbers $k$, $n$ and $j$ with $j \not\equiv 0 \pmod p$,

$$A_\ell\big(p^{2k+2}(4n + 1) + 4j \, p^{2k+1}\big) \equiv 0 \pmod 4.$$

The condition modulo $6$ is the one printed in the paper; it is not replaced by the condition
$p \equiv 3 \pmod 4$ of Theorem 5.

## Sources

- Murugan P and Fathima S. N, *Arithmetic Density of Certain ℓ-Regular Overpartitions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A3, Corollary 1.

articles.title: $p$-regular overpartitions are almost always divisible by $2^j$
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be an odd prime,
let $j \ge 1$, and let $A_p(n)$ be the number of overpartitions of $n$ with no part divisible by
$p$. Then

$$\lim_{X \to \infty} \frac{\#\{n : 0 \le n \le X,\ 2^j \mid A_p(n)\}}{X} = 1,$$

where $X$ runs over the natural numbers.

## Sources

- Murugan P and Fathima S. N, *Arithmetic Density of Certain ℓ-Regular Overpartitions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A3, Theorem 1.

articles.title: Ramanujan-type congruences modulo 7 for 7-regular overpartitions
articles.statement:
Write $A_7(m)$ for the
number of overpartitions of $m$ none of whose parts is divisible by $7$. For every natural number
$n$, we have $A_7(16n+4) \equiv 0 \pmod 7$; $A_7(64n+i) \equiv 0 \pmod 7$ for every natural
number $i < 64$ with $i \equiv 4 \pmod{32}$; $A_7(256n+i) \equiv 0 \pmod 7$ for every natural
number $i < 256$ with $i \equiv 4 \pmod{32}$; and $A_7(1024n+i) \equiv 0 \pmod 7$ for every
natural number $i < 1024$ with $i \equiv 4 \pmod{32}$.

## Sources

- Murugan P and Fathima S. N, *Arithmetic Density of Certain ℓ-Regular Overpartitions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A3, Theorem 8.

articles.title: Self-similarity modulo 7 of 7-regular overpartition counts
articles.statement:
Write $A_7(m)$ for the number
of overpartitions of $m$ none of whose parts is divisible by $7$. For all natural numbers $n$
and $k$, $A_7(7^{2k}(4n+3)) \equiv A_7(4n+3) \pmod 7$.

## Sources

- Murugan P and Fathima S. N, *Arithmetic Density of Certain ℓ-Regular Overpartitions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A3, Theorem 7.

articles.title: Almost all $3p$-regular overpartition counts are divisible by $2^j$
articles.statement:
Write $A_\ell(m)$ for
the number of overpartitions of $m$ none of whose parts is divisible by $\ell$. Let $p$ be an
odd prime and let $j \ge 1$. Then the number of natural numbers $n$ with $0 \le n \le X$ and
$2^j \mid A_{3p}(n)$, divided by $X$, tends to $1$ as the natural number $X$ tends to infinity.

## Sources

- Murugan P and Fathima S. N, *Arithmetic Density of Certain ℓ-Regular Overpartitions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A3, Theorem 2.

articles.title: Congruences modulo powers of two for $3 \cdot 2^\alpha$-regular overpartitions
articles.statement:
Write
$A_\ell(m)$ for the number of overpartitions of $m$ none of whose parts is divisible by $\ell$.
For every natural number $\alpha \ge 1$ there is a natural number $c$ with the following
property. Let $d \ge 1$ be a natural number, let $p_1, \dots, p_{c+d}$ be distinct primes, each
coprime to $6$, and let $n$ be a natural number that is divisible by $24$ and coprime to every
$p_i$. Then $A_{3 \cdot 2^\alpha}(p_1 p_2 \cdots p_{c+d} \, n / 24) \equiv 0 \pmod{2^d}$.

The hypothesis that $24$ divides $n$ makes the argument an integer; the paper reads this value
off a series in $q^{24}$.

## Sources

- Murugan P and Fathima S. N, *Arithmetic Density of Certain ℓ-Regular Overpartitions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A3, Theorem 4.

articles.title: Almost all $3 \cdot 2^\alpha$-regular overpartition counts are divisible by $2^j$
articles.statement:
Write
$A_\ell(m)$ for the number of overpartitions of $m$ none of whose parts is divisible by $\ell$.
Let $\alpha \ge 1$ and $j \ge \alpha + 1$ be natural numbers. Then the number of natural numbers
$n$ with $0 \le n \le X$ and $2^j \mid A_{3 \cdot 2^\alpha}(n)$, divided by $X$, tends to $1$ as
the natural number $X$ tends to infinity.

## Sources

- Murugan P and Fathima S. N, *Arithmetic Density of Certain ℓ-Regular Overpartitions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A3, Theorem 3.

articles.title: A congruence for 9-regular partitions at $4n + 1$
articles.statement:
Let $R_9(m)$ denote the number of
partitions of $m$ in which no part is divisible by $9$. For every positive integer $n$,
$R_9(4n + 1) \equiv R_9(n) \pmod 3$.

## Sources

- S. Sriram and A. David Christopher, *Congruences Relating Regular Partition Functions, a Generalized Tau Function, and Partition Function Weighted Composition Sums*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A39, Theorem 19.

articles.title: Iterated congruences for 9-regular partitions modulo 3
articles.statement:
Let $R_9(m)$ denote the number of
partitions of $m$ in which no part is divisible by $9$, and let $N_s = (4^s - 1)/3$. For all
positive integers $r$ and $s$, $R_9((r - 1) 4^{s-1} + N_s) \equiv R_9(r) \pmod 3$,
$R_9(N_s) \equiv 1 \pmod 3$, $R_9(4^{s-1} + N_s) \equiv 2 \pmod 3$ and
$R_9(2 \cdot 4^{s-1} + N_s) \equiv 0 \pmod 3$.

## Sources

- S. Sriram and A. David Christopher, *Congruences Relating Regular Partition Functions, a Generalized Tau Function, and Partition Function Weighted Composition Sums*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A39, Corollary 5.

articles.title: 9-regular partitions modulo 3 and the divisor sum
articles.statement:
Let $R_9(m)$ denote the number of
partitions of $m$ in which no part is divisible by $9$, and let $\sigma(m)$ be the sum of the
positive divisors of $m$. For every positive integer $n$, $R_9(n) \equiv \sigma(3n + 1) \pmod 3$.

## Sources

- S. Sriram and A. David Christopher, *Congruences Relating Regular Partition Functions, a Generalized Tau Function, and Partition Function Weighted Composition Sums*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A39, Corollary 2.

articles.title: Prime-regular partitions and the generalized tau function
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime and $n$ a
natural number. Let $R_p(n)$ be the number of partitions of $n$ in which no part is divisible by
$p$, and let $\tau_k(m)$ be the generalized tau function, the coefficient of $q^m$ in
$q \prod_{j \ge 1} (1 - q^j)^k$. Then $R_p(n) \equiv \tau_{p-1}(n + 1) \pmod p$.

## Sources

- S. Sriram and A. David Christopher, *Congruences Relating Regular Partition Functions, a Generalized Tau Function, and Partition Function Weighted Composition Sums*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A39, Theorem 20.

articles.title: 25-regular partitions modulo 5 and the divisor sum
articles.statement:
Let $R_{25}(m)$ denote the number of
partitions of $m$ in which no part is divisible by $25$, and let $\sigma(m)$ be the sum of the
positive divisors of $m$. For every positive integer $n$,
$R_{25}(n) \equiv (n + 1) \, \sigma(n + 1) \pmod 5$.

## Sources

- S. Sriram and A. David Christopher, *Congruences Relating Regular Partition Functions, a Generalized Tau Function, and Partition Function Weighted Composition Sums*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A39, Corollary 3.

articles.title: $2^s$-regular partitions and the generalized tau function modulo 2
articles.statement:
Let $s$ be a positive
integer and $n$ a natural number. Let $R_{2^s}(n)$ be the number of partitions of $n$ in which no
part is divisible by $2^s$, and let $\tau_k(m)$ be the generalized tau function, the coefficient
of $q^m$ in $q \prod_{j \ge 1} (1 - q^j)^k$. Then $R_{2^s}(n) \equiv \tau_{2^s - 1}(n + 1) \pmod 2$.

## Sources

- S. Sriram and A. David Christopher, *Congruences Relating Regular Partition Functions, a Generalized Tau Function, and Partition Function Weighted Composition Sums*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A39, Theorem 5.

articles.title: Binomial coefficients $\binom{n+k}{k}$ modulo an odd prime
articles.statement:
Let $l$ be an odd prime, $k$
an integer with $1 \le k < l$, $n$ a natural number, and $r$ the remainder of $n$ modulo $l$. If
$r \le l - k - 1$, then $\binom{n+k}{k} \equiv (-1)^r \binom{l-k-1}{r} \pmod l$; otherwise
$\binom{n+k}{k} \equiv 0 \pmod l$.

## Sources

- S. Sriram and A. David Christopher, *Congruences Relating Regular Partition Functions, a Generalized Tau Function, and Partition Function Weighted Composition Sums*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A39, Lemma 1.

articles.title: Euler's product has constant term $1$
articles.statement:
The constant coefficient of the integer power
series $\prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - X^m)$ in $\mathbb{Z}[[X]]$ is $1$.

## Sources

- Euler's pentagonal number theorem as used in Sriram and Christopher, *Congruences Relating Regular Partition Functions, a Generalized Tau Function, and Partition Function Weighted Composition Sums*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A39, identity (1).

articles.title: Parity of $\tau_{14}$ and $\tau_6$ at odd arguments
articles.statement:
Let $\tau_k(m)$ be the generalized
tau function, the coefficient of $q^m$ in $q \prod_{j \ge 1} (1 - q^j)^k$, and let $R_8(n)$ be
the number of partitions of $n$ in which no part is divisible by $8$. For every positive integer
$n$: (a) $\tau_{14}(2n + 1) \equiv R_8(n) \pmod 2$; (b) $\tau_6(2n + 1)$ is odd if and only if
$n$ is a triangular number, that is, $n = m(m + 1)/2$ for some natural number $m$.

## Sources

- S. Sriram and A. David Christopher, *Congruences Relating Regular Partition Functions, a Generalized Tau Function, and Partition Function Weighted Composition Sums*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A39, Theorem 4.

articles.title: Vanishing of the generalized tau function modulo $|k|/d$
articles.statement:
Let $\tau_k(n)$ be the
generalized tau function, the coefficient of $q^n$ in $q \prod_{j \ge 1} (1 - q^j)^k$. Let $k$ be
an integer with $|k| \ge 2$ and $d$ a natural number dividing $|k|$ with $d < |k|$. Then for all
natural numbers $m$ and $r$ with $\gcd(r, |k|/d) = 1$,
$\tau_k(|k| m + d r + 1) \equiv 0 \pmod{|k|/d}$.

## Sources

- S. Sriram and A. David Christopher, *Congruences Relating Regular Partition Functions, a Generalized Tau Function, and Partition Function Weighted Composition Sums*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A39, Proposition 3.

articles.title: Vanishing of $\tau_k(n)$ modulo the prime $k - 1$
articles.statement:
Let $n \ge 1$ and let $k$ be a natural
number such that $k - 1$ is prime. For an integer $t$ let $P(t) = t(3t - 1)/2$ be the generalized
pentagonal number. If $k - 1$ does not divide $n - 1 - P(t)$ for any integer $t$ with
$P(t) \le n - 1$, then the generalized tau function satisfies $\tau_k(n) \equiv 0 \pmod{k - 1}$.

## Sources

- S. Sriram and A. David Christopher, *Congruences Relating Regular Partition Functions, a Generalized Tau Function, and Partition Function Weighted Composition Sums*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A39, Proposition 1.

articles.title: The generalized tau function for natural exponents
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $k$ and $n$,
$\tau_k(n)$ is the coefficient of $q^n$ in the integer power series
$q \bigl(\prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^m)\bigr)^k$.

## Sources

- Sriram and Christopher, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A39, Definition 1.1.

articles.title: $\tau_{-k}$ and partition convolutions modulo a prime
articles.statement:
Let $l$ be an odd prime, let $k$ be a
natural number with $2 \le k < l$, let $n$ be a natural number, and write $p(s)$ for the number of
partitions of $s$. Then

$$\tau_{-k}(n + 1) \equiv \sum_{s=0}^{\lfloor n/l \rfloor} \tau_{l-k}(n - ls + 1)\, p(s) \pmod{l},$$

and the composition sum $\sum p(a_1) p(a_2) \cdots p(a_k)$, taken over all $k$-tuples
$(a_1, \dots, a_k)$ of natural numbers with $a_1 + \cdots + a_k = n$, is congruent modulo $l$ to
the same right-hand side.

The record prints $\tau_{l-k}(t)$ in place of $\tau_{l-k}(t + 1)$, writing $n = t + ls$; that is
false. The proof's identity
$\prod (1 - q^m)^{-k} \equiv \prod (1 - q^m)^{l-k} (1 - q^{lm})^{-1} \pmod{l}$ together with
Definition 1.1 ($\prod (1 - q^m)^j = \sum \tau_j(t + 1) q^t$) gives $\tau_{l-k}(t + 1)$;
Corollary 4.3 (the record's Corollary 6) uses this shifted form, $\omega(t) = \tau_1(t + 1)$.

## Sources

- S. Sriram and A. David Christopher, *Congruences Relating Regular Partition Functions, a Generalized Tau Function, and Partition Function Weighted Composition Sums*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A39, Theorem 21.

articles.title: The generalized tau function at $1$
articles.statement:
For every integer $k$, $\tau_k(1) = 1$.

## Sources

- Sriram and Christopher, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A39, Definition 1.1.

articles.title: Generalized tau at a prime power modulo the prime
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, let $s \ge 1$ and
$n \ge 0$ be natural numbers, and for an integer $t$ let $P(t) = t(3t - 1)/2$ be the generalized
pentagonal number. Then $\tau_{p^s}(n + 1)$ is congruent modulo $p$ to the sum of $(-1)^t$ over
the integers $t$ with $-n \le t \le n$ and $n = p^s P(t)$.

Since $P$ is injective, this sum has at most one term: $\tau_{p^s}(n + 1) \equiv (-1)^t \pmod{p}$
if $n = p^s P(t)$, and $\tau_{p^s}(n + 1) \equiv 0 \pmod{p}$ if $n$ is not of this form.

## Sources

- S. Sriram and A. David Christopher, *Congruences Relating Regular Partition Functions, a Generalized Tau Function, and Partition Function Weighted Composition Sums*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A39, Theorem 15.

articles.title: Generalized tau at $p^2 + 1$ modulo $p$
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be an odd prime and $n$ a natural number,
and for an integer $j$ let $P(j) = j(3j - 1)/2$ be the generalized pentagonal number. Then
$\tau_{p^2 + 1}(n + 1)$ is congruent modulo $p$ to the sum of $(-1)^{r + s}$ over the pairs of
integers $(r, s)$ with $-n \le r, s \le n$ and $n = P(r) + p^2 P(s)$.

The record prints the condition as $n + 1 = P(r) + p^2 P(s)$; that is false, and the proof's
identity $\sum \tau_{p^2+1}(n + 1) q^n \equiv \prod (1 - q^m)(1 - q^{p^2 m}) \pmod{p}$ gives the
index $n$.

## Sources

- S. Sriram and A. David Christopher, *Congruences Relating Regular Partition Functions, a Generalized Tau Function, and Partition Function Weighted Composition Sums*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A39, Theorem 18.

articles.title: Partition formulas for the generalized tau function
articles.statement:
Let $k \ge 1$ and $n \ge 0$ be natural
numbers. For a partition $\lambda$ of $n$ and a part $a$ of $\lambda$, write $f_a$ for the number
of times $a$ occurs in $\lambda$. Then

$$\tau_k(n + 1) = \sum_{\lambda} \prod_{a} (-1)^{f_a} \binom{k}{f_a},$$

where $\lambda$ runs over the partitions of $n$ with $f_a \le k$ for every part $a$ and the
product runs over the distinct parts $a$ of $\lambda$, and

$$\tau_{-k}(n + 1) = \sum_{\lambda} \prod_{a} \binom{f_a + k - 1}{k - 1},$$

where $\lambda$ runs over all partitions of $n$ and the product again runs over the distinct parts
$a$ of $\lambda$.

## Sources

- S. Sriram and A. David Christopher, *Congruences Relating Regular Partition Functions, a Generalized Tau Function, and Partition Function Weighted Composition Sums*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A39, Theorem 1.

articles.title: Parity of the generalized tau function via part frequencies
articles.statement:
Let $k \ge 1$ and $n \ge 0$ be
natural numbers, and let $A$ be the set of integers $a$ with $1 \le a \le k$ and $\binom{k}{a}$
odd. Then $\tau_k(n + 1)$ is congruent modulo $2$ to the number of partitions of $n$ in which the
number of times each part occurs lies in $A$.

## Sources

- S. Sriram and A. David Christopher, *Congruences Relating Regular Partition Functions, a Generalized Tau Function, and Partition Function Weighted Composition Sums*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A39, Theorem 2.

articles.title: Generalized tau at $2p + 1$ modulo $p$
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be an odd prime and $n$ a natural number,
and for an integer $j$ let $P(j) = j(3j - 1)/2$ be the generalized pentagonal number. Then
$\tau_{2p + 1}(n + 1)$ is congruent modulo $p$ to the sum of $(-1)^{r + s + t}$ over the triples
of integers $(r, s, t)$ with $-n \le r, s, t \le n$ and $n = P(r) + p(P(s) + P(t))$.

The record prints the condition as $n + 1 = P(r) + p(P(s) + P(t))$; that is false, and the
proof's identity $\sum \tau_{2p+1}(n + 1) q^n \equiv \prod (1 - q^m)(1 - q^{pm})^2 \pmod{p}$
gives the index $n$.

## Sources

- S. Sriram and A. David Christopher, *Congruences Relating Regular Partition Functions, a Generalized Tau Function, and Partition Function Weighted Composition Sums*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A39, Theorem 17.

articles.title: $\tau_{2p}(n + 1)$ vanishes modulo $p$ when $p \nmid n$
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be an odd prime and $n$ a
natural number not divisible by $p$. Then $\tau_{2p}(n + 1) \equiv 0 \pmod{p}$.

The record prints the hypothesis as $p \nmid n + 1$; that is false, and the corollary follows from
Theorem 3.26 (the record's Theorem 16) in its corrected form, which forces $p \mid n$ for a nonzero
residue.

## Sources

- S. Sriram and A. David Christopher, *Congruences Relating Regular Partition Functions, a Generalized Tau Function, and Partition Function Weighted Composition Sums*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A39, Corollary 4.

articles.title: Generalized tau function $\tau_{2p}$ modulo $p$
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be an odd prime, let $\tau_k$ be
the generalized tau function, and for an integer $r$ let $P(r) = r(3r - 1)/2$ be the generalized
pentagonal number. For every integer $n \ge 0$,

$$\tau_{2p}(n + 1) \equiv \sum (-1)^{r + s} \pmod p,$$

the sum running over the pairs of integers $r, s$ with $|r| \le n$, $|s| \le n$ and
$n = p\,(P(r) + P(s))$.

The paper prints the side condition as $n + 1 = p(P(r) + P(s))$, which is false: at $n = 0$ the
left side is $\tau_{2p}(1) = 1$ while that sum is empty. The identity
$\sum_{n \ge 0} \tau_{2p}(n + 1) q^n \equiv \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{pm})^2 \pmod p$ from the
paper's proof gives $n = p(P(r) + P(s))$.

## Sources

- S. Sriram and A. David Christopher, *Congruences Relating Regular Partition Functions, a Generalized Tau Function, and Partition Function Weighted Composition Sums*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A39, Theorem 16.

articles.title: Generalized tau function at zero
articles.statement:
For every integer $k$, $\tau_k(0) = 0$, where $\tau_k$
is the generalized tau function: the series $q \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^m)^k$ has no constant term.

## Sources

- Sriram and Christopher, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A39, Definition 1.1.

articles.title: Generalized tau function
articles.statement:
For an integer $k$ and a natural number $n$, the generalized tau
function $\tau_k(n)$ is the coefficient of $q^n$ in the integer power series
$q \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^m)^k$. For negative $k$ the power is taken in the group of units of
$\mathbb{Z}[[q]]$, where $\prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^m)$ is invertible because its constant term is $1$.

The paper requires $k \ne 0$; $k = 0$ gives $\tau_0(1) = 1$ and $\tau_0(n) = 0$ for $n \ne 1$.
$\tau_{24}$ is Ramanujan's tau function, and $\tau_1(n + 1)$ is Euler's $\omega(n)$, the
coefficient of $q^n$ in $\prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^m)$.

## Sources

- Sriram and Christopher, *Congruences Relating Regular Partition Functions, a Generalized Tau Function, and Partition Function Weighted Composition Sums*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A39, Definition 1.1, equation (2).

articles.title: Euler's product is a unit in $\mathbb{Z}((X))$
articles.statement:
Euler's pentagonal series
$\sum_{k \in \mathbb{Z}} (-1)^k X^{k(3k - 1)/2}$, which equals $\prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - X^m)$, is a
unit of the ring $\mathbb{Z}[[X]]$ of formal power series with integer coefficients, so all its
integer powers are defined.

## Sources

- Sriram and Christopher, *Congruences Relating Regular Partition Functions, a Generalized Tau Function, and Partition Function Weighted Composition Sums*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A39, Definition 1.1 (negative exponents).

articles.title: Divisibility of $n\,\tau_k(n + 1)$ by $|k|$
articles.statement:
Let $\tau_k$ be the generalized tau function.
For every positive integer $n$ and every integer $k$ with $|k| \ge 2$,
$n\,\tau_k(n + 1) \equiv 0 \pmod{|k|}$.

## Sources

- S. Sriram and A. David Christopher, *Congruences Relating Regular Partition Functions, a Generalized Tau Function, and Partition Function Weighted Composition Sums*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A39, Proposition 2.

articles.title: Parity of the $4$-regular partition function
articles.statement:
For a positive integer $n$, let $R_4(n)$ be
the number of partitions of $n$ with no part divisible by $4$. Then $R_4(n)$ is odd if and only if
$n$ is a triangular number, that is, $n = m(m + 1)/2$ for some integer $m \ge 0$.

## Sources

- S. Sriram and A. David Christopher, *Congruences Relating Regular Partition Functions, a Generalized Tau Function, and Partition Function Weighted Composition Sums*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A39, Theorem 3.

articles.title: Partition composition sums vanishing modulo a prime
articles.statement:
Let $p(a)$ be the number of
partitions of $a$. Let $\ell \ge 5$ be a prime and $m \ge 0$ an integer such that
$m \not\equiv 0 \pmod{\ell}$ and $m \not\equiv (-1)^r \binom{\ell - 3}{r} \pmod{\ell}$ for every
integer $r$ with $0 \le r \le (\ell - 3)/2$. Then every integer $n \ge 0$ with
$n \equiv m \pmod{\ell}$ satisfies

$$\sum_{a_1 + \cdots + a_{\ell - 3} = n} p(a_1) \cdots p(a_{\ell - 3}) \equiv 0 \pmod{\ell},$$

the sum running over all $(\ell - 3)$-tuples $(a_1, \dots, a_{\ell - 3})$ of nonnegative integers
with sum $n$.

## Sources

- S. Sriram and A. David Christopher, *Congruences Relating Regular Partition Functions, a Generalized Tau Function, and Partition Function Weighted Composition Sums*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A39, Corollary 7.

articles.title: Partition convolution modulo $3$
articles.statement:
Let $p(a)$ be the number of partitions of $a$, and let
$\omega(t)$ be the coefficient of $q^t$ in Euler's product $\prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^m)$. For every
integer $n \ge 0$,

$$\sum_{a + b = n} p(a)\, p(b) \equiv \sum_{0 \le s \le n/3} \omega(n - 3s)\, p(s) \pmod 3,$$

the left sum running over pairs $(a, b)$ of nonnegative integers and the right one over integers
$s$.

## Sources

- S. Sriram and A. David Christopher, *Congruences Relating Regular Partition Functions, a Generalized Tau Function, and Partition Function Weighted Composition Sums*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A39, Corollary 6.

articles.title: Ramanujan's tau function modulo divisors of $24$
articles.statement:
Let $\tau(n) = \tau_{24}(n)$ be
Ramanujan's tau function, the generalized tau function with $k = 24$. For every integer
$m \ge 0$: $\tau(24m + r + 1) \equiv 0 \pmod{24}$ for $r \in \{1, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19, 23\}$;
$\tau(24m + r + 1) \equiv 0 \pmod 6$ for $r \in \{4, 20\}$;
$\tau(24m + r + 1) \equiv 0 \pmod 8$ for $r \in \{3, 6, 9, 15\}$;
$\tau(24m + r + 1) \equiv 0 \pmod 3$ for $r \in \{8, 16\}$; and
$\tau(24m + 13) \equiv 0 \pmod 2$.

The paper prints the moduli of the second, fourth and fifth congruences as $12$, $6$ and $4$,
which is false (for instance $\tau(5) = 4830$ is not divisible by $12$); the moduli used are
$24/\gcd(r, 24)$, which the paper's Proposition 2.4 at $k = 24$ gives. The first and third
congruences are as printed.

## Sources

- S. Sriram and A. David Christopher, *Congruences Relating Regular Partition Functions, a Generalized Tau Function, and Partition Function Weighted Composition Sums*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A39, Proposition 4.

articles.title: Ramanujan's congruence modulo $7$
articles.statement:
Let $\tau(n) = \tau_{24}(n)$ be Ramanujan's tau
function, the generalized tau function with $k = 24$. For every positive integer $n$,
$\tau(7n) \equiv 0 \pmod 7$.

## Sources

- S. Sriram and A. David Christopher, *Congruences Relating Regular Partition Functions, a Generalized Tau Function, and Partition Function Weighted Composition Sums*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A39, Corollary 8.

articles.title: Ramanujan's $\tau$ modulo $25$ via $5$-regular partitions
articles.statement:
Let $\tau = \tau_{24}$ be
Ramanujan's tau function, where $\tau_k$ is the generalized tau function. Let $R_5(m)$ be the
number of partitions of $m$ with no part divisible by $5$, and let $P(t) = t(3t - 1)/2$ for
integers $t$. For every integer $n \ge 1$,

$$\tau(n + 1) \equiv \sum (-1)^{s + t} (2s + 1) R_5\big(n - 5s(s + 1)/2 - 5P(t)\big) \pmod{25},$$

the sum running over all integers $s \ge 0$ and $t$ with $5s(s + 1)/2 + 5P(t) \le n$.

## Sources

- S. Sriram and A. David Christopher, *Congruences Relating Regular Partition Functions, a Generalized Tau Function, and Partition Function Weighted Composition Sums*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A39, Theorem 14.

articles.title: Ramanujan's $\tau$ modulo $3$ via $9$-regular partitions
articles.statement:
Let $\tau = \tau_{24}$ be
Ramanujan's tau function, where $\tau_k$ is the generalized tau function, and let $R_9(m)$ be
the number of partitions of $m$ with no part divisible by $9$. For every integer $n \ge 1$,
$\tau(n + 1) \equiv R_9(n/3) \pmod 3$ if $3$ divides $n$, and $\tau(n + 1) \equiv 0 \pmod 3$
otherwise.

## Sources

- S. Sriram and A. David Christopher, *Congruences Relating Regular Partition Functions, a Generalized Tau Function, and Partition Function Weighted Composition Sums*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A39, Theorem 6.

articles.title: Ramanujan's $\tau$ modulo $23$ via pentagonal numbers
articles.statement:
Let $\tau = \tau_{24}$ be
Ramanujan's tau function, where $\tau_k$ is the generalized tau function, and let
$P(r) = r(3r - 1)/2$ for integers $r$. For every integer $n \ge 1$, $\tau(n + 1)$ is congruent
modulo $23$ to the sum of $(-1)^{r + s}$ over all pairs of integers $(r, s)$ with
$P(r) + 23P(s) = n$.

## Sources

- S. Sriram and A. David Christopher, *Congruences Relating Regular Partition Functions, a Generalized Tau Function, and Partition Function Weighted Composition Sums*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A39, Theorem 13.

articles.title: Ramanujan's $\tau$ modulo $11$ via pentagonal numbers
articles.statement:
Let $\tau = \tau_{24}$ be Ramanujan's
tau function, where $\tau_k$ is the generalized tau function, and let $P(r) = r(3r - 1)/2$ for
integers $r$. For every integer $n \ge 1$, $\tau(n + 1)$ is congruent modulo $11$ to the sum of
$(-1)^{l + m + s + r}$ over all quadruples of integers $(l, m, s, r)$ with
$P(l) + P(m) + 11P(s) + 11P(r) = n$.

## Sources

- S. Sriram and A. David Christopher, *Congruences Relating Regular Partition Functions, a Generalized Tau Function, and Partition Function Weighted Composition Sums*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A39, Theorem 9.

articles.title: Ramanujan's $\tau$ modulo $17$ via $\tau_7$
articles.statement:
Let $\tau = \tau_{24}$ be Ramanujan's tau
function, where $\tau_k$ is the generalized tau function, and let $P(r) = r(3r - 1)/2$ for
integers $r$. For every integer $n \ge 1$,

$$\tau(n + 1) \equiv \sum_{17P(r) \le n} (-1)^r \tau_7(n - 17P(r) + 1) \pmod{17},$$

the sum running over all integers $r$ with $17P(r) \le n$.

The source record prints $\tau_7(s)$ in place of $\tau_7(s + 1)$, where $n = 17P(r) + s$;
that version is false at $n = 1$. The shifted index comes from the identity
$\prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^m)^7 (1 - q^{17m}) = \sum_{r, s} (-1)^r \tau_7(s + 1) q^{17P(r) + s}$,
which follows from Definition 1.1 and is used in the proof.

## Sources

- S. Sriram and A. David Christopher, *Congruences Relating Regular Partition Functions, a Generalized Tau Function, and Partition Function Weighted Composition Sums*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A39, Theorem 11.

articles.title: Ramanujan's $\tau$ modulo $19$ via $\tau_5$
articles.statement:
Let $\tau = \tau_{24}$ be Ramanujan's tau
function, where $\tau_k$ is the generalized tau function, and let $P(r) = r(3r - 1)/2$ for
integers $r$. For every integer $n \ge 1$,

$$\tau(n + 1) \equiv \sum_{19P(r) \le n} (-1)^r \tau_5(n - 19P(r) + 1) \pmod{19},$$

the sum running over all integers $r$ with $19P(r) \le n$.

The source record prints $\tau_5(s)$ in place of $\tau_5(s + 1)$, where $n = 19P(r) + s$;
that version is false at $n = 1$. The shifted index comes from the identity
$\prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^m)^5 (1 - q^{19m}) = \sum_{r, s} (-1)^r \tau_5(s + 1) q^{19P(r) + s}$,
which follows from Definition 1.1 and is used in the proof.

## Sources

- S. Sriram and A. David Christopher, *Congruences Relating Regular Partition Functions, a Generalized Tau Function, and Partition Function Weighted Composition Sums*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A39, Theorem 12.

articles.title: Ramanujan's $\tau$ modulo $13$ via $\tau_{11}$
articles.statement:
Let $\tau = \tau_{24}$ be Ramanujan's tau
function, where $\tau_k$ is the generalized tau function, and let $P(r) = r(3r - 1)/2$ for
integers $r$. For every integer $n \ge 1$,

$$\tau(n + 1) \equiv \sum_{13P(r) \le n} (-1)^r \tau_{11}(n - 13P(r) + 1) \pmod{13},$$

the sum running over all integers $r$ with $13P(r) \le n$.

The source record prints $\tau_{11}(s)$ in place of $\tau_{11}(s + 1)$, where $n = 13P(r) + s$;

## Sources

- S. Sriram and A. David Christopher, *Congruences Relating Regular Partition Functions, a Generalized Tau Function, and Partition Function Weighted Composition Sums*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A39, Theorem 10.

articles.title: Ramanujan's $\tau$ modulo $7$ via triangular numbers
articles.statement:
Let $\tau = \tau_{24}$ be Ramanujan's
tau function, where $\tau_k$ is the generalized tau function. For every integer $n \ge 1$,
$\tau(n + 1)$ is congruent modulo $7$ to the sum of $(-1)^{m + r} (2m + 1)(2r + 1)$ over all
pairs of integers $m, r \ge 0$ with $m(m + 1)/2 + 7r(r + 1)/2 = n$.

## Sources

- S. Sriram and A. David Christopher, *Congruences Relating Regular Partition Functions, a Generalized Tau Function, and Partition Function Weighted Composition Sums*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A39, Theorem 8.

articles.title: Ramanujan's $\tau$ modulo $5$ via $25$-regular partitions
articles.statement:
Let $\tau = \tau_{24}$ be
Ramanujan's tau function, where $\tau_k$ is the generalized tau function, and let $R_{25}(n)$ be
the number of partitions of $n$ with no part divisible by $25$. For every integer $n \ge 1$,
$\tau(n + 1) \equiv R_{25}(n) \pmod 5$.

## Sources

- S. Sriram and A. David Christopher, *Congruences Relating Regular Partition Functions, a Generalized Tau Function, and Partition Function Weighted Composition Sums*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A39, Theorem 7.

articles.title: Ramanujan's congruence $\tau(3n) \equiv 0 \pmod 3$
articles.statement:
Let $\tau = \tau_{24}$ be Ramanujan's
tau function, where $\tau_k$ is the generalized tau function. For every integer $n \ge 1$,
$\tau(3n) \equiv 0 \pmod 3$.

## Sources

- S. Sriram and A. David Christopher, *Congruences Relating Regular Partition Functions, a Generalized Tau Function, and Partition Function Weighted Composition Sums*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A39, Corollary 1.

articles.title: Three congruences modulo 4 for $\overline{\mathrm{spt2}}$
articles.statement:
Let $\overline{\mathrm{spt2}}(n)$
be the number of smallest parts in the overpartitions of $n$ whose smallest part is even and not
overlined. For every natural number $n$, each of $\overline{\mathrm{spt2}}(36n + 30)$,
$\overline{\mathrm{spt2}}(48n + 34)$ and $\overline{\mathrm{spt2}}(72n + 42)$ is divisible by $4$.

## Sources

- Robson da Silva, *Extending Congruences for the Number of Smallest Parts in Overpartitions with Smallest Part Even*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A62, Theorem 1.

articles.title: Overpartitions with odd smallest part contribute nothing
articles.statement:
If $O$ is an overpartition of
$n$ with at least one part and the smallest part of $O$ is odd, then the smallest-even-part
contribution of $O$ is $0$.

## Sources

- Robson da Silva, *Extending Congruences for the Number of Smallest Parts in Overpartitions with Smallest Part Even*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A62, Section 1.

articles.title: Smallest-even-part contribution of an overpartition
articles.statement:
For an overpartition $O$ of $n$,
let $s$ be the smallest part of $O$. The contribution of $O$ is the number of copies of $s$ in
$O$ if $s$ is even and not overlined, and $0$ otherwise; the empty overpartition, which has no
smallest part, contributes $0$.

## Sources

- Robson da Silva, *Extending Congruences for the Number of Smallest Parts in Overpartitions with Smallest Part Even*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A62, Section 1 (definition of `spt2‾(n)`).

articles.title: Congruences modulo 4 for $\overline{\mathrm{spt2}}$ along powers of 2
articles.statement:
Let
$\overline{\mathrm{spt2}}(N)$ be the number of smallest parts in the overpartitions of $N$ whose
smallest part is even and not overlined. For all natural numbers $j$ and $n$,
$\overline{\mathrm{spt2}}(N)$ is divisible by $4$ for each of the six values
$N = 2^{j+4} n + 7 \cdot 2^{j+1}$, $N = 2^{j+2} \cdot 9 n + 15 \cdot 2^{j+1}$,
$N = 2^{j+4} \cdot 3 n + 17 \cdot 2^{j+1}$, $N = 2^{j+3} \cdot 9 n + 21 \cdot 2^{j+1}$,
$N = 2^{j+4} \cdot 5 n + 17 \cdot 2^{j+1}$ and $N = 2^{j+4} \cdot 5 n + 33 \cdot 2^{j+1}$.

## Sources

- Robson da Silva, *Extending Congruences for the Number of Smallest Parts in Overpartitions with Smallest Part Even*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A62, Theorem 2.

articles.title: Congruences modulo 4 for $\overline{\mathrm{spt2}}$ at primes $p \equiv 5, 7 \pmod 8$
articles.statement:
Let
$\overline{\mathrm{spt2}}(N)$ be the number of smallest parts in the overpartitions of $N$ whose
smallest part is even and not overlined. Let $p > 3$ be a prime with $p \equiv 5 \pmod 8$ or
$p \equiv 7 \pmod 8$. Then for all natural numbers $k$ and $m$ with $p \nmid m$, the number
$\overline{\mathrm{spt2}}(32 p^{2k+1} m + 24 p^{2k+2})$ is divisible by $4$.

## Sources

- Robson da Silva, *Extending Congruences for the Number of Smallest Parts in Overpartitions with Smallest Part Even*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A62, Theorem 3.

articles.title: $\overline{\mathrm{spt2}}$ vanishes at zero
articles.statement:
Let $\overline{\mathrm{spt2}}(n)$ be the
number of smallest parts in the overpartitions of $n$ whose smallest part is even and not
overlined. Then $\overline{\mathrm{spt2}}(0) = 0$: the only overpartition of $0$ is empty and has
no smallest part.

## Sources

- Robson da Silva, *Extending Congruences for the Number of Smallest Parts in Overpartitions with Smallest Part Even*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A62, Section 1.

articles.title: Number of smallest even parts in overpartitions
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$,
$\overline{\mathrm{spt2}}(n)$ is the number of smallest parts in the overpartitions of $n$ whose
smallest part is even and not overlined: the sum, over all overpartitions $O$ of $n$, of the
smallest-even-part contribution of $O$, which is the number of copies of the smallest part $s$
of $O$ when $s$ is even and not overlined, and $0$ otherwise (in particular when $O$ is empty).
For example $\overline{\mathrm{spt2}}(4) = 3$, from $4$ and $2 + 2$, while $\overline{2} + 2$
does not count; the values for $n = 0, \dots, 8$ are $0, 0, 1, 0, 3, 2, 6, 6, 15$.

## Sources

- Robson da Silva, *Extending Congruences for the Number of Smallest Parts in Overpartitions with Smallest Part Even*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A62, Section 1.

articles.title: The 3-dissection of $f_1^3$ for complex $q$
articles.statement:
Let $q$ be a complex number with $|q| < 1$, and
for $k \ge 1$ let $f_k = (q^k; q^k)_\infty = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$ be the raw infinite
q-Pochhammer product with $a = q^k$ and base $q^k$. Then

$$
f_1^3 = \frac{f_6 f_9^6}{f_3 f_{18}^3} + 4 q^3 \frac{f_3^2 f_{18}^6}{f_6^2 f_9^3} - 3 q f_9^3.
$$

## Sources

- Robson da Silva, *Extending Congruences for the Number of Smallest Parts in Overpartitions with Smallest Part Even*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A62, Lemma 2.

articles.title: The 3-dissection of $f_1 f_2$ for complex $q$
articles.statement:
Let $q$ be a complex number with $|q| < 1$,
and for $k \ge 1$ let $f_k = (q^k; q^k)_\infty = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$ be the raw
infinite q-Pochhammer product with $a = q^k$ and base $q^k$. Then

$$
f_1 f_2 = \frac{f_6 f_9^4}{f_3 f_{18}^2} - q f_9 f_{18} - 2 q^2 \frac{f_3 f_{18}^4}{f_6 f_9^2}.
$$

## Sources

- Robson da Silva, *Extending Congruences for the Number of Smallest Parts in Overpartitions with Smallest Part Even*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A62, Lemma 2.

articles.title: The 3-dissection of $f_4/f_1$ for complex $q$
articles.statement:
Let $q$ be a complex number with $|q| < 1$,
and for $k \ge 1$ let $f_k = (q^k; q^k)_\infty = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$ be the raw
infinite q-Pochhammer product with $a = q^k$ and base $q^k$. Then

$$
\frac{f_4}{f_1} = \frac{f_{12} f_{18}^4}{f_3^3 f_{36}^2} +
q \frac{f_6^2 f_9^3 f_{36}}{f_3^4 f_{18}^2} + 2 q^2 \frac{f_6 f_{18} f_{36}}{f_3^3}.
$$

## Sources

- Robson da Silva, *Extending Congruences for the Number of Smallest Parts in Overpartitions with Smallest Part Even*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A62, Lemma 2.

articles.title: 2-dissection of the reciprocal square of Euler's product
articles.statement:
Let $q$ be a complex number with
$|q| < 1$, and for $k \ge 1$ let $f_k = (q^k; q^k)_\infty = \prod_{n=0}^{\infty} (1 - q^k (q^k)^n)$
be the raw infinite q-Pochhammer product. Then

$$\frac{1}{f_1^2} = \frac{f_8^5}{f_2^5 f_{16}^2} + 2q \frac{f_4^2 f_{16}^2}{f_2^5 f_8}.$$

## Sources

- Robson da Silva, *Extending Congruences for the Number of Smallest Parts in Overpartitions with Smallest Part Even*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A62, Lemma 1.

articles.title: 2-dissection of the square of Euler's product
articles.statement:
Let $q$ be a complex number with $|q| < 1$,
and for $k \ge 1$ let $f_k = (q^k; q^k)_\infty = \prod_{n=0}^{\infty} (1 - q^k (q^k)^n)$ be the
raw infinite q-Pochhammer product. Then

$$f_1^2 = \frac{f_2 f_8^5}{f_4^2 f_{16}^2} - 2q \frac{f_2 f_{16}^2}{f_8}.$$

## Sources

- Robson da Silva, *Extending Congruences for the Number of Smallest Parts in Overpartitions with Smallest Part Even*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A62, Lemma 1.

articles.title: 3-dissection of the product form of Ramanujan's phi function at negated argument
articles.statement:
Let $q$ be
a complex number with $|q| < 1$, and for $k \ge 1$ let
$f_k = (q^k; q^k)_\infty = \prod_{n=0}^{\infty} (1 - q^k (q^k)^n)$ be the raw infinite
q-Pochhammer product. Then

$$\frac{f_1^2}{f_2} = \frac{f_9^2}{f_{18}} - 2q \frac{f_3 f_{18}^2}{f_6 f_9}.$$

Here $f_1^2/f_2$ is the product form of $\varphi(-q)$, where
$\varphi(q) = \sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} q^{n^2}$ is Ramanujan's theta function.

## Sources

- Robson da Silva, *Extending Congruences for the Number of Smallest Parts in Overpartitions with Smallest Part Even*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A62, Lemma 5.

articles.title: 3-dissection of the product form of Ramanujan's psi function at negated argument
articles.statement:
Let $q$ be
a complex number with $|q| < 1$, and for $k \ge 1$ let
$f_k = (q^k; q^k)_\infty = \prod_{n=0}^{\infty} (1 - q^k (q^k)^n)$ be the raw infinite
q-Pochhammer product. Then

$$\frac{f_1 f_4}{f_2} = \frac{f_3 f_{12} f_{18}^5}{f_6^2 f_9^2 f_{36}^2} -
q \frac{f_9 f_{36}}{f_{18}}.$$

Here $f_1 f_4/f_2$ is the product form of $\psi(-q)$, where
$\psi(q) = \sum_{n \ge 0} q^{n(n+1)/2}$ is Ramanujan's theta function.

## Sources

- Robson da Silva, *Extending Congruences for the Number of Smallest Parts in Overpartitions with Smallest Part Even*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A62, Lemma 4.

articles.title: 3-dissection of the product form of Ramanujan's psi function
articles.statement:
Let $q$ be a complex number
with $|q| < 1$, and for $k \ge 1$ let
$f_k = (q^k; q^k)_\infty = \prod_{n=0}^{\infty} (1 - q^k (q^k)^n)$ be the raw infinite
q-Pochhammer product. Then

$$\frac{f_2^2}{f_1} = \frac{f_6 f_9^2}{f_3 f_{18}} + q \frac{f_{18}^2}{f_9}.$$

Here $f_2^2/f_1$ is the product form of Ramanujan's theta function
$\psi(q) = \sum_{n \ge 0} q^{n(n+1)/2}$.

## Sources

- Robson da Silva, *Extending Congruences for the Number of Smallest Parts in Overpartitions with Smallest Part Even*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A62, Lemma 3.

articles.title: Bounded bilateral series
articles.statement:
Given functions $e, w : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$, the
bounded bilateral series of $e$ and $w$ is the power series over $\mathbb{Z}$ whose
coefficient of $q^n$, for each natural number $n$, is the sum of $w(m)$ over the integers
$m$ with $-n-1 \le m \le n+1$ and $e(m) = n$.

It agrees with the bilateral series $\sum_{m \in \mathbb{Z}} w(m) q^{e(m)}$ whenever $e$
takes no negative values and, for every natural number $n$, every integer $m$ with $e(m) = n$
satisfies $|m| \le n + 1$, as holds for the quadratic exponents used in Lemmas 1, 3 and 5 of
the source; it is not intended for other exponents.

## Sources

- Bishnu Paudel, James A. Sellers, and Haiyang Wang, *Extending Recent Work of Nath, Saikia, and Sarma on k-Tuple ℓ-Regular Partitions*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A4, Encoding for Lemmas 1, 3, and 5.

articles.title: Coefficients of the bounded bilateral series
articles.statement:
For all functions
$e, w : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$ and every natural number $n$, the coefficient of $q^n$ in
the bounded bilateral series of $e$ and $w$ equals the sum of $w(m)$ over the integers $m$
with $-n-1 \le m \le n+1$ and $e(m) = n$.

## Sources

- Bishnu Paudel, James A. Sellers, and Haiyang Wang, *Extending Recent Work of Nath, Saikia, and Sarma on k-Tuple ℓ-Regular Partitions*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A4, Encoding for Lemmas 1, 3, and 5.

articles.title: Coefficients of the positive unilateral series
articles.statement:
For all functions
$e : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Z}$ and every natural number
$n$, the coefficient of $q^n$ in the positive unilateral series of $e$ and $w$ equals the sum
of $w(m)$ over the natural numbers $m$ with $1 \le m \le n$ and $e(m) = n$.

## Sources

- Bishnu Paudel, James A. Sellers, and Haiyang Wang, *Extending Recent Work of Nath, Saikia, and Sarma on k-Tuple ℓ-Regular Partitions*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A4, Encoding for Lemma 5 and Corollary 3.

articles.title: Toh's 3-dissection of $f_2^3 / f_1^3$
articles.statement:
For $k \ge 1$ let
$f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$ be the Euler product, an integer power series in $q$. Then

$$
f_2^3 f_3^8 f_9 f_{18} = f_1^3 \bigl(f_3^7 f_6 f_9 f_{18} + 3q f_6^4 f_9^6 +
6q^2 f_3 f_6^3 f_9^3 f_{18}^3 + 12q^3 f_3^2 f_6^2 f_{18}^6\bigr).
$$

Since each $f_k$ has constant term $1$ and so is invertible, this is the identity
$f_2^3/f_1^3 = f_6/f_3 + 3q f_6^4 f_9^5/(f_3^8 f_{18}) + 6q^2 f_6^3 f_9^2 f_{18}^2/f_3^7 +
12q^3 f_6^2 f_{18}^5/(f_3^6 f_9)$ with both sides multiplied by $f_1^3 f_3^8 f_9 f_{18}$.

## Sources

- Mohammed L. Nadji and Moussa Ahmia, *Congruences for l-Regular Tripartitions for l in {2,3}*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A86, Lemma 1, eq. (3).

articles.title: One tuple of $\ell$-regular partitions of total zero
articles.statement:
For all natural numbers $\ell$
and $k$, writing $T_{\ell,k}(n)$ for the number of $k$-tuples of $\ell$-regular partitions
with total $n$, we have $T_{\ell,k}(0) = 1$: the only such tuple of total $0$ is the tuple of
empty partitions.

## Sources

- Bishnu Paudel, James A. Sellers, and Haiyang Wang, *Extending Recent Work of Nath, Saikia, and Sarma on k-Tuple ℓ-Regular Partitions*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A4, Introduction (definition of `T_{ℓ,k}`).

articles.title: Recurrence for tuples of $\ell$-regular partitions
articles.statement:
For all natural numbers $\ell$, $k$
and $n$, writing $r_\ell(i)$ for the number of $\ell$-regular partitions of $i$ and
$T_{\ell,k}(n)$ for the number of $k$-tuples of $\ell$-regular partitions with total $n$,

$$T_{\ell,k+1}(n) = \sum_{i=0}^{n} r_\ell(i) \, T_{\ell,k}(n-i).$$

## Sources

- Bishnu Paudel, James A. Sellers, and Haiyang Wang, *Extending Recent Work of Nath, Saikia, and Sarma on k-Tuple ℓ-Regular Partitions*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A4, Introduction (definition of `T_{ℓ,k}`).

articles.title: The empty tuple of $\ell$-regular partitions
articles.statement:
For all natural numbers $\ell$ and $n$,
writing $T_{\ell,k}(n)$ for the number of $k$-tuples of $\ell$-regular partitions with total
$n$, we have $T_{\ell,0}(n) = 1$ if $n = 0$ and $T_{\ell,0}(n) = 0$ otherwise.

## Sources

- Bishnu Paudel, James A. Sellers, and Haiyang Wang, *Extending Recent Work of Nath, Saikia, and Sarma on k-Tuple ℓ-Regular Partitions*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A4, Introduction (definition of `T_{ℓ,k}`).

articles.title: Number of $k$-tuples of $\ell$-regular partitions
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $\ell$, $k$ and
$n$, the number $T_{\ell,k}(n)$ is defined by recursion on $k$: $T_{\ell,0}(n)$ is $1$ if
$n = 0$ and $0$ otherwise, and

$$T_{\ell,k+1}(n) = \sum_{i=0}^{n} r_\ell(i) \, T_{\ell,k}(n-i),$$

where $r_\ell(i)$ is the number of $\ell$-regular partitions of $i$.

Peeling off the first component in this way, $T_{\ell,k}(n)$ counts the $k$-tuples
$(\lambda_1, \dots, \lambda_k)$ of $\ell$-regular partitions of $n_1, \dots, n_k$ with
$n_1 + \dots + n_k = n$.

## Sources

- Bishnu Paudel, James A. Sellers, and Haiyang Wang, *Extending Recent Work of Nath, Saikia, and Sarma on k-Tuple ℓ-Regular Partitions*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A4, Introduction (definition of `T_{ℓ,k}`).

articles.title: Prime-power congruences for $k$-tuples of $\ell$-regular partitions
articles.statement:
Write $T_{\ell,k}(n)$
for the number of $k$-tuples of $\ell$-regular partitions with total $n$. Let $p$ be a prime,
let $m$, $\ell$ and $s$ be positive integers, let $\alpha \ge s$ and $r$ be natural numbers
with $1 \le r \le p^s - 1$. Then for every natural number $n$,

$$T_{\ell,p^\alpha m}(p^s n + r) \equiv 0 \pmod{p^{\alpha - s + 1}}.$$

Since $s$ is positive, the hypothesis $\alpha \ge s$ also gives $\alpha \ge 1$.

## Sources

- Bishnu Paudel, James A. Sellers, and Haiyang Wang, *Extending Recent Work of Nath, Saikia, and Sarma on k-Tuple ℓ-Regular Partitions*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A4, Theorem 3, equation thm.gen1.1.

articles.title: Zero has one $\ell$-regular partition
articles.statement:
For every natural number $\ell$, the number of
$\ell$-regular partitions of $0$ is $1$; the only one is the empty partition.

## Sources

- Bishnu Paudel, James A. Sellers, and Haiyang Wang, *Extending Recent Work of Nath, Saikia, and Sarma on k-Tuple ℓ-Regular Partitions*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A4, Introduction (definition of ℓ-regular partitions).

articles.title: Number of $\ell$-regular partitions
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $\ell$ and $n$, the number of
$\ell$-regular partitions of $n$ is the number of partitions of $n$ none of whose parts is
divisible by $\ell$.

## Sources

- Bishnu Paudel, James A. Sellers, and Haiyang Wang, *Extending Recent Work of Nath, Saikia, and Sarma on k-Tuple ℓ-Regular Partitions*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A4, Introduction (definition of ℓ-regular partitions).

articles.title: The Nath–Saikia–Sarma conjecture
articles.statement:
Let $T_2(n)$ be the number of triples of 2-regular
partitions (partitions with no even part) whose sizes add up to $n$. Let $p \ge 5$ be a prime
with Legendre symbol $\left(\frac{-2}{p}\right) = -1$, and let $t$ be a positive integer with
$\gcd(t, 6) = 1$ and $p \mid t$. Then for every natural number $n$ and every $j$ with
$1 \le j \le p - 1$,

$$T_2\left(9t^2 n + \frac{9t^2 j}{p} + \frac{57t^2 - 1}{8}\right) \equiv 0 \pmod{6}.$$

Both fractions are integers under these hypotheses.

## Sources

- Bishnu Paudel, James A. Sellers, and Haiyang Wang, *Extending Recent Work of Nath, Saikia, and Sarma on k-Tuple ℓ-Regular Partitions*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A4, Corollary 1 (Conjecture conj.nss).

articles.title: The 3-dissection of $1/f_1^3$
articles.statement:
For $k \ge 1$ let $f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$ be
the Euler product, an integer power series in $q$. Then

$$
f_3^{12} = f_1^3 f_9^3 \bigl(f_1^6 + 9q f_1^3 f_9^3 + 27q^2 f_9^6\bigr)
$$

and

$$
f_3^{14} f_6^4 f_9^3 f_{18}^6 = f_1^3 \bigl(f_6^6 f_9^{18} + 3q f_3 f_6^5 f_9^{15} f_{18}^3 +
9q^2 f_3^2 f_6^4 f_9^{12} f_{18}^6 + 8q^3 f_3^3 f_6^3 f_9^9 f_{18}^9 +
12q^4 f_3^4 f_6^2 f_9^6 f_{18}^{12} + 16q^6 f_3^6 f_{18}^{18}\bigr).
$$

Since each $f_k$ has constant term $1$ and so is invertible, these are the identities
$1/f_1^3 = (f_9^3/f_3^{12})(f_1^6 + 9q f_1^3 f_9^3 + 27q^2 f_9^6)$ and
$1/f_1^3 = f_6^2 f_9^{15}/(f_3^{14} f_{18}^6) + 3q f_6 f_9^{12}/(f_3^{13} f_{18}^3) +
9q^2 f_9^9/f_3^{12} + 8q^3 f_9^6 f_{18}^3/(f_3^{11} f_6) +
12q^4 f_9^3 f_{18}^6/(f_3^{10} f_6^2) + 16q^6 f_{18}^{12}/(f_3^8 f_6^4 f_9^3)$, multiplied by
$f_1^3 f_3^{12}$ and by $f_1^3 f_3^{14} f_6^4 f_9^3 f_{18}^6$ respectively.

## Sources

- Mohammed L. Nadji and Moussa Ahmia, *Congruences for l-Regular Tripartitions for l in {2,3}*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A86, Lemma 3, eq. (6).

articles.title: Truncated one-sided series
articles.statement:
For functions $e : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and
$w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Z}$, this is the integer power series whose coefficient of $q^n$ is
the sum of $w(m)$ over the integers $m$ with $1 \le m \le n$ and $e(m) = n$.

When $e(m) \ge m$ for every $m \ge 1$, as for the square exponents in Lemma 5 and
Corollary 3, this series is $\sum_{m \ge 1} w(m) q^{e(m)}$.

## Sources

- Bishnu Paudel, James A. Sellers, and Haiyang Wang, *Extending Recent Work of Nath, Saikia, and Sarma on k-Tuple ℓ-Regular Partitions*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A4, Encoding for Lemma 5 and Corollary 3.

articles.title: A fifth-power Euler product identity
articles.statement:
Write $f_k = \prod_{i \ge 1} (1 - q^{ki})$ for the
Euler products, as integer power series in $q$. Then

$$f_1^5 = f_2^2 \sum_{m \in \mathbb{Z}} (6m + 1)\, q^{m(3m+1)/2}.$$

This is the identity $f_1^5 / f_2^2 = \sum_{m \in \mathbb{Z}} (6m + 1)\, q^{m(3m+1)/2}$ with the
denominator cleared. The coefficient of $q^n$ in the sum is computed over the integers $m$ with
$|m| \le n + 1$, which include every solution of $m(3m+1)/2 = n$.

## Sources

- Bishnu Paudel, James A. Sellers, and Haiyang Wang, *Extending Recent Work of Nath, Saikia, and Sarma on k-Tuple ℓ-Regular Partitions*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A4, Lemma 3, equation f15/f22.

articles.title: Iterated prime-power congruence for Euler products
articles.statement:
For a natural number $l$ write
$f_l = \prod_{i \ge 1} (1 - q^{li})$, an integer power series in $q$. Let $p$ be a prime and let
$k, l, s, m$ be natural numbers with $l \ge 1$, $s \ge 1$, $m \ge 1$ and $s \le k$. Then for
every natural number $n$, the coefficients of $q^n$ in $f_l^{p^k m}$ and in
$f_{l p^s}^{p^{k-s} m}$ are congruent modulo $p^{k-s+1}$.

## Sources

- Bishnu Paudel, James A. Sellers, and Haiyang Wang, *Extending Recent Work of Nath, Saikia, and Sarma on k-Tuple ℓ-Regular Partitions*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A4, Lemma 7, equation cor.modp^k.

articles.title: Gauss's theta identity for the Euler products
articles.statement:
Write $f_k = \prod_{i \ge 1} (1 - q^{ki})$
for the Euler products, as integer power series in $q$, and let
$\theta = \sum_{m \in \mathbb{Z}} (-1)^m q^{m^2}$. Then $f_1^2 = f_2\, \theta$ and
$\theta = 1 + 2 \sum_{m \ge 1} (-1)^m q^{m^2}$.

The coefficient of $q^n$ in each sum is computed over the indices $m$ with $|m| \le n + 1$
(respectively $1 \le m \le n$), which include every solution of $m^2 = n$.

## Sources

- Bishnu Paudel, James A. Sellers, and Haiyang Wang, *Extending Recent Work of Nath, Saikia, and Sarma on k-Tuple ℓ-Regular Partitions*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A4, Lemma 5, equation f12/f2.

articles.title: The theta identity for the second Euler product
articles.statement:
Write
$f_k = \prod_{i \ge 1} (1 - q^{ki})$ for the Euler products, as integer power series in $q$. Then

$$f_2^2 = f_4 \left(1 + 2 \sum_{n \ge 1} (-1)^n q^{2n^2}\right).$$

This is the identity for $f_2^2 / f_4$ with the denominator cleared.

## Sources

- Bishnu Paudel, James A. Sellers, and Haiyang Wang, *Extending Recent Work of Nath, Saikia, and Sarma on k-Tuple ℓ-Regular Partitions*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A4, Corollary 3, equation f22/f4.

articles.title: Cui–Gu $p$-dissection of $f_1$
articles.statement:
Let $p \ge 5$ be a prime, let $s = (p - 1)/6$ if
$p \equiv 1 \pmod 6$ and $s = (-p - 1)/6$ otherwise, and let $q$ be a complex number with
$|q| < 1$. Write $f_k = (q^k; q^k)_\infty = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$, let
$f(a, b) = \sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} a^{n(n+1)/2} b^{n(n-1)/2}$ be Ramanujan's theta function, and
let $K$ be the set of integers $k$ with $(1 - p)/2 \le k \le (p - 1)/2$ and $k \ne s$. Then

$$
f_1 = \sum_{k \in K} (-1)^k q^{k(3k+1)/2}
f\bigl(-q^{(3p^2 + (6k+1)p)/2}, -q^{(3p^2 - (6k+1)p)/2}\bigr) +
(-1)^s q^{(p^2-1)/24} f_{p^2}.
$$

All the divisions are exact and all the exponents of $q$ are nonnegative integers.

## Sources

- Mohammed L. Nadji and Moussa Ahmia, *Congruences for l-Regular Tripartitions for l in {2,3}*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A86, Lemma 5, eq. (8), quoting S. Cui and N. Gu, *Arithmetic Properties of ℓ-Regular Partitions*, Adv. Appl. Math. 51 (2013), 507–523, Theorem 2.2. The same identity is Nayaka, Dharmendra and Mahesh Kumar, *Divisibility Properties for Overcubic Partition Triples*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A80, Lemma 4, eq. (43).

articles.title: Cui–Gu $p$-dissection of $\psi(q)$
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be an odd prime and $q$ a complex number with
$|q| < 1$, let $f(a, b) = \sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} a^{n(n+1)/2} b^{n(n-1)/2}$ be Ramanujan's theta
function, and let $\psi(q) = f(q, q^3)$. Then

$$
\psi(q) = \sum_{k=0}^{(p-3)/2} q^{k(k+1)/2}
f\bigl(q^{(p^2 + (2k+1)p)/2}, q^{(p^2 - (2k+1)p)/2}\bigr) + q^{(p^2-1)/8} \psi(q^{p^2}),
$$

and $(m^2 + m)/2 \not\equiv (p^2 - 1)/8 \pmod p$ for every integer $m$ with
$0 \le m \le (p - 3)/2$. All the divisions are exact.

## Sources

- Mohammed L. Nadji and Moussa Ahmia, *Congruences for l-Regular Tripartitions for l in {2,3}*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A86, Lemma 4, eq. (7), quoting S. Cui and N. Gu, *Arithmetic Properties of ℓ-Regular Partitions*, Adv. Appl. Math. 51 (2013), 507–523, Theorem 2.1.

articles.title: The number of $\ell$-regular tripartitions of $1$
articles.statement:
For every natural number $\ell \ne 1$,
the number $T_\ell(1)$ of $\ell$-regular tripartitions of $1$ is $3$: the single part $1$ lies in
one of the three components.

## Sources

- Mohammed L. Nadji and Moussa Ahmia, *Congruences for l-Regular Tripartitions for l in {2,3}*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A86 (definition of `T_ℓ(n)`).

articles.title: Congruences modulo 3 and 9 for 3-regular tripartitions
articles.statement:
Let $T_3(m)$ be the number of
$3$-regular tripartitions of $m$. For every natural number $n$, $3 \mid T_3(3n + 1)$ and
$9 \mid T_3(3n + 2)$.

## Sources

- Mohammed L. Nadji and Moussa Ahmia, *Congruences for l-Regular Tripartitions for l in {2,3}*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A86, Corollary 2 (congruences (53), (54)).

articles.title: A congruence modulo 3 for 3-regular tripartitions at primes $p \equiv 3 \pmod 4$
articles.statement:
Let
$T_3(m)$ be the number of $3$-regular tripartitions of $m$, and let $p$ be a prime with
$p \equiv 3 \pmod 4$. For all natural numbers $\alpha$ and $n$ and every integer $i$ with
$1 \le i \le p - 1$,

$$
T_3\Bigl(3 p^{2\alpha+1} (p n + i) + \frac{p^{2\alpha+2} - 1}{4}\Bigr) \equiv 0 \pmod 3,
$$

where the division by $4$ is exact.

## Sources

- Mohammed L. Nadji and Moussa Ahmia, *Congruences for l-Regular Tripartitions for l in {2,3}*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A86, Theorem 5 (congruence (55)).

articles.title: A congruence modulo 6 for 3-regular tripartitions
articles.statement:
Let $T_3(m)$ be the number of
$3$-regular tripartitions of $m$. For every natural number $n$, $6 \mid T_3(6n + 4)$.

## Sources

- Mohammed L. Nadji and Moussa Ahmia, *Congruences for l-Regular Tripartitions for l in {2,3}*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A86, Corollary 3 (congruence (64)).

articles.title: The 3-dissection of the generating function of 3-regular tripartitions
articles.statement:
Let $T_3(n)$ be
the number of $3$-regular tripartitions of $n$, and for $k \ge 1$ let
$f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$ be the Euler product. Then, as integer power series in $q$,

$$
f_1^{11} f_2^4 f_3^3 f_6^6 \sum_{n \ge 0} T_3(3n) q^n =
f_2^6 f_3^{18} + 8q f_1^3 f_2^3 f_3^9 f_6^9 + 16q^2 f_1^6 f_6^{18},
$$



$$
f_1^{10} f_2^2 f_6^3 \sum_{n \ge 0} T_3(3n + 1) q^n = 3 f_2^3 f_3^{12} + 12q f_1^3 f_3^3 f_6^9
$$

and

$$
f_1^9 \sum_{n \ge 0} T_3(3n + 2) q^n = 9 f_3^9.
$$

Since each $f_k$ has constant term $1$ and so is invertible, these are the identities
$\sum T_3(3n) q^n = f_2^2 f_3^{15}/(f_1^{11} f_6^6) + 8q f_3^6 f_6^3/(f_1^8 f_2) +
16q^2 f_6^{12}/(f_1^5 f_2^4 f_3^3)$,
$\sum T_3(3n + 1) q^n = 3 f_2 f_3^{12}/(f_1^{10} f_6^3) + 12q f_3^3 f_6^6/(f_1^7 f_2^2)$ and
$\sum T_3(3n + 2) q^n = 9 f_3^9/f_1^9$ with the denominators cleared.

## Sources

- Mohammed L. Nadji and Moussa Ahmia, *Congruences for l-Regular Tripartitions for l in {2,3}*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A86, Theorem 4, eqs. (49)–(51).

articles.title: Congruences modulo 3 and 6 for 2-regular tripartitions
articles.statement:
Let $T_2(m)$ be the number of
$2$-regular tripartitions of $m$. For every natural number $n$, $3 \mid T_2(3n + 1)$ and
$6 \mid T_2(3n + 2)$.

## Sources

- Mohammed L. Nadji and Moussa Ahmia, *Congruences for l-Regular Tripartitions for l in {2,3}*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A86, Corollary 1.

articles.title: Mod 12 congruences for 2-regular tripartitions
articles.statement:
Let $T_2(n)$ be the number of 2-regular
tripartitions of $n$. For all natural numbers $\alpha$ and $n$, put
$A_\alpha = \sum_{i=0}^{2\alpha+1} 3^{2i}$ and $B_\alpha = \sum_{i=0}^{2\alpha} 3^{2i}$. Then $12$
divides each of $T_2(3^{4\alpha+4} n + A_\alpha + 3^{4\alpha+3})$,
$T_2(3^{4\alpha+4} n + A_\alpha + 2 \cdot 3^{4\alpha+3})$,
$T_2(3^{4\alpha+2} n + B_\alpha + 3^{4\alpha+1})$ and
$T_2(3^{4\alpha+2} n + B_\alpha + 2 \cdot 3^{4\alpha+1})$.

## Sources

- Mohammed L. Nadji and Moussa Ahmia, *Congruences for l-Regular Tripartitions for l in {2,3}*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A86, Theorem 3, eqs. (31)–(34).

articles.title: Even 2-regular tripartition counts for odd primes
articles.statement:
Let $T_2(n)$ be the number of 2-regular
tripartitions of $n$. For every odd prime $p$, all natural numbers $\alpha$ and $n$, and every $i$
with $1 \le i \le p - 1$, the number
$T_2\bigl(9 p^{2\alpha+1} (p n + i) + (9 p^{2\alpha+2} - 1)/8\bigr)$ is even (the division is
exact).

## Sources

- Mohammed L. Nadji and Moussa Ahmia, *Congruences for l-Regular Tripartitions for l in {2,3}*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A86, Theorem 2 (congruence (21)).

articles.title: Even 2-regular tripartition counts for primes at least 5
articles.statement:
Let $T_2(n)$ be the number of
2-regular tripartitions of $n$. For every prime $p \ge 5$, all natural numbers $\alpha$ and $n$,
and every $i$ with $1 \le i \le p - 1$, the number
$T_2\bigl(3 p^{2\alpha+1} (p n + i) + (p^{2\alpha+2} - 1)/8\bigr)$ is even (the division is
exact).

## Sources

- Mohammed L. Nadji and Moussa Ahmia, *Congruences for l-Regular Tripartitions for l in {2,3}*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A86, Theorem 1 (congruence (13)).

articles.title: The 3-dissection of the 2-regular tripartition generating function
articles.statement:
Let $T_2(n)$ be the
number of 2-regular tripartitions of $n$ and $f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$. In the ring
$\mathbb{Z}[[q]]$ of integer power series,
$f_1^6 f_3 \sum_{n \ge 0} T_2(3n) q^n = f_1^5 f_2 f_3 + 12 q f_2^2 f_6^5$,
$f_1^8 f_6 \sum_{n \ge 0} T_2(3n + 1) q^n = 3 f_2^4 f_3^5$ and
$f_1^7 \sum_{n \ge 0} T_2(3n + 2) q^n = 6 f_2^3 f_3^2 f_6^2$.

Since each $f_k$ with $k \ge 1$ is invertible in $\mathbb{Z}[[q]]$, these say
$\sum_{n \ge 0} T_2(3n) q^n = f_2 / f_1 + 12 q f_2^2 f_6^5 / (f_1^6 f_3)$,
$\sum_{n \ge 0} T_2(3n + 1) q^n = 3 f_2^4 f_3^5 / (f_1^8 f_6)$ and
$\sum_{n \ge 0} T_2(3n + 2) q^n = 6 f_2^3 f_3^2 f_6^2 / f_1^7$.

## Sources

- Mohammed L. Nadji and Moussa Ahmia, *Congruences for l-Regular Tripartitions for l in {2,3}*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A86, Lemma 7, eqs. (10)–(12).

articles.title: The regular tripartition count at zero
articles.statement:
For every natural number $\ell$, $T_\ell(0) = 1$,
where $T_\ell(n)$ is the number of $\ell$-regular tripartitions of $n$: the only tripartition of
$0$ is the triple of empty partitions.

## Sources

- Mohammed L. Nadji and Moussa Ahmia, *Congruences for l-Regular Tripartitions for l in {2,3}*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A86 (definition of `T_ℓ(n)`).

articles.title: Regular tripartition counts
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $\ell$ and $n$, $T_\ell(n)$ is the number
of triples $(\lambda_1, \lambda_2, \lambda_3)$ of integer partitions with
$|\lambda_1| + |\lambda_2| + |\lambda_3| = n$ in which no part of any $\lambda_i$ is divisible by
$\ell$; these triples are the $\ell$-regular tripartitions of $n$.

## Sources

- Mohammed L. Nadji and Moussa Ahmia, *Congruences for l-Regular Tripartitions for l in {2,3}*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A86, Section 1, definition of `T_ℓ(n)` (with generating function `f_ℓ³ / f_1³`, Section 1, eq. (1)).

articles.title: A signed Euler product identity
articles.statement:
Write $f_k = \prod_{i \ge 1} (1 - q^{ki})$ for the Euler
products, as integer power series in $q$, and let $(-q;-q)_\infty = \prod_{i \ge 1} (1 - (-q)^i)$
be $f_1$ with $q$ replaced by $-q$. Then

$$(-q;-q)_\infty \, f_1 f_4 = f_2^3.$$

This is the identity $(-q;-q)_\infty = f_2^3 / (f_1 f_4)$ with the denominator cleared.

## Sources

- Bishnu Paudel, James A. Sellers, and Haiyang Wang, *Extending Recent Work of Nath, Saikia, and Sarma on k-Tuple ℓ-Regular Partitions*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A4, Lemma 4, equation f1-q.

articles.title: Triples of $\ell$-regular partitions
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $\ell$ and $n$,
$T_\ell(n) = T_{\ell,3}(n)$ is the number of triples $(\lambda_1, \lambda_2, \lambda_3)$ of
$\ell$-regular partitions (partitions with no part divisible by $\ell$) whose sizes add up to
$n$.

## Sources

- Bishnu Paudel, James A. Sellers, and Haiyang Wang, *Extending Recent Work of Nath, Saikia, and Sarma on k-Tuple ℓ-Regular Partitions*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A4, Introduction (definition of `T_ℓ`).

articles.title: Congruences modulo 24 for triples of 2-regular partitions
articles.statement:
Let $T_2(n)$ be the number of
triples of 2-regular partitions (partitions with no even part) whose sizes add up to $n$. If
$t$ is a positive integer with $\gcd(t, 6) = 1$ and $N \in \{33, 57\}$, then for every natural
number $n$,

$$T_2\left(9n + \frac{N t^2 - 1}{8}\right) \equiv 0 \pmod{24}.$$

Here $N t^2 - 1$ is divisible by $8$, so the fraction is an integer.

## Sources

- Bishnu Paudel, James A. Sellers, and Haiyang Wang, *Extending Recent Work of Nath, Saikia, and Sarma on k-Tuple ℓ-Regular Partitions*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A4, Theorem 1, equation T29n24.

articles.title: Prime-power congruences modulo 24 for triples of 2-regular partitions
articles.statement:
Let $T_2(n)$ be
the number of triples of 2-regular partitions (partitions with no even part) whose sizes add up
to $n$. Let $p \ne 3$ be a prime with $p \equiv 3$, $5$ or $7 \pmod 8$. Then for all natural
numbers $n$ and $\alpha$ with $p \nmid n$,

$$T_2\left(9 p^{2\alpha+1} n + \frac{9 p^{2\alpha+2} - 1}{8}\right) \equiv 0 \pmod{24}.$$

Since $p$ is odd, the fraction is an integer.

## Sources

- Bishnu Paudel, James A. Sellers, and Haiyang Wang, *Extending Recent Work of Nath, Saikia, and Sarma on k-Tuple ℓ-Regular Partitions*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A4, Corollary 2, equation cor.9pmod24.

articles.title: Parity of triples of 2-regular partitions
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$, let $T_2(n)$ be the
number of triples of $2$-regular partitions (partitions with no even part) whose sizes add up to
$n$. Then $T_2(n)$ is odd if and only if $n$ is a triangular number, that is, $n = m(m+1)/2$
for some natural number $m$.

Allowing integer $m$ gives no new values, since $m$ and $-m-1$ give the same triangular number.

## Sources

- Bishnu Paudel, James A. Sellers, and Haiyang Wang, *Extending Recent Work of Nath, Saikia, and Sarma on k-Tuple ℓ-Regular Partitions*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A4, Lemma 8, equation mod2.

articles.title: Congruences modulo 8 and 24 for triples of 2-regular partitions
articles.statement:
Let $T_2(n)$ be the
number of triples of $2$-regular partitions (partitions with no even part) whose sizes add up to
$n$. Let $p$ be a prime with $p \equiv 3$, $5$ or $7 \pmod 8$, and let $n$ and $\alpha$ be
natural numbers with $p \nmid n$. Then

$$T_2\left(p^{2\alpha+1} n + \frac{p^{2\alpha+2}-1}{8}\right) \equiv 0 \pmod 8,$$

and if moreover $3 \nmid n$, this value is also $\equiv 0 \pmod{24}$.

The division by $8$ is exact because $p$ is odd.

## Sources

- Bishnu Paudel, James A. Sellers, and Haiyang Wang, *Extending Recent Work of Nath, Saikia, and Sarma on k-Tuple ℓ-Regular Partitions*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A4, Theorem 2, equations thm.p357mod8 and mod24.

articles.title: The first recurrence value of Garvan's matrix
articles.statement:
The entry of Garvan's matrix
$(m_{i,j})$ in row $8$ and column $3$, the first entry computed by the recurrence rather than
read from the tables, is $m_{8,3} = 2464$.

## Sources

- D. S. Gireesh, C. Shivashankar, and B. Hemanthkumar, *On 2-Color Partitions in Which the Parts of One Color Are Restricted to Multiples of 7^k*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A94, Section 1.

articles.title: Initial entries of the first row of Garvan's matrix
articles.statement:
The first two entries of the first
row of Garvan's matrix $(m_{i,j})$ are $m_{1,1} = 7$ and $m_{1,2} = 7^2 = 49$.

## Sources

- D. S. Gireesh, C. Shivashankar, and B. Hemanthkumar, *On 2-Color Partitions in Which the Parts of One Color Are Restricted to Multiples of 7^k*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A94, Section 1, Table 1.

articles.title: Recurrence for Garvan's matrix
articles.statement:
For all natural numbers $i \ge 8$ and $j \ge 3$, the
entries of Garvan's matrix $(m_{i,j})$ satisfy

$$m_{i,j} = 7m_{i-3,j-1} + 35m_{i-2,j-1} + 49m_{i-1,j-1} + m_{i-7,j-2} + 7m_{i-6,j-2} +
21m_{i-5,j-2} + 49m_{i-4,j-2} + 147m_{i-3,j-2} + 343m_{i-2,j-2} + 343m_{i-1,j-2}.$$

## Sources

- D. S. Gireesh, C. Shivashankar, and B. Hemanthkumar, *On 2-Color Partitions in Which the Parts of One Color Are Restricted to Multiples of 7^k*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A94, Section 1.

articles.title: Garvan's matrix
articles.statement:
Garvan's matrix $(m_{i,j})_{i,j \ge 1}$ is the array of natural
numbers defined as follows. For $1 \le i \le 7$, $m_{i,j}$ is the entry in row $i$ and column
$j$ of the tabulated rows of Garvan's matrix (Tables 1 and 2 of the source), and $0$ beyond the
printed columns. For $i \ge 8$, $m_{i,1} = m_{i,2} = 0$ and, for $j \ge 3$,

$$m_{i,j} = 7m_{i-3,j-1} + 35m_{i-2,j-1} + 49m_{i-1,j-1} + m_{i-7,j-2} + 7m_{i-6,j-2} +
21m_{i-5,j-2} + 49m_{i-4,j-2} + 147m_{i-3,j-2} + 343m_{i-2,j-2} + 343m_{i-1,j-2}.$$

Entries with $i = 0$ or $j = 0$ are set to $0$.

Lemma 1 of the source identifies these numbers as the coefficients of Garvan's modular
expansion; that identity is a separate statement and is not part of this definition.

## Sources

- D. S. Gireesh, C. Shivashankar, and B. Hemanthkumar, *On 2-Color Partitions in Which the Parts of One Color Are Restricted to Multiples of 7^k*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A94, Section 1.

articles.title: Tabulated rows of Garvan's matrix
articles.statement:
For $1 \le i \le 7$ and $j \ge 1$, the value at
$(i, j)$ is the $j$-th entry of row $i$ in the list below, and $0$ if row $i$ has fewer than
$j$ entries (row $i$ has $2i$ entries). The value is $0$ if $i = 0$, $j = 0$ or $i > 7$.

- Row $1$: $7, 7^2$.
- Row $2$: $10, 9 \cdot 7^2, 2 \cdot 7^4, 7^5$.
- Row $3$: $3, 114 \cdot 7, 85 \cdot 7^3, 24 \cdot 7^5, 3 \cdot 7^7, 7^8$.
- Row $4$: $0, 82 \cdot 7, 176 \cdot 7^3, 845 \cdot 7^4, 272 \cdot 7^6, 46 \cdot 7^8,
  4 \cdot 7^{10}, 7^{11}$.
- Row $5$: $0, 190, 1265 \cdot 7^2, 1895 \cdot 7^4, 1233 \cdot 7^6, 3025 \cdot 7^7,
  620 \cdot 7^9, 75 \cdot 7^{11}, 5 \cdot 7^{13}, 7^{14}$.
- Row $6$: $0, 27, 736 \cdot 7^2, 16782 \cdot 7^3, 20424 \cdot 7^5, 12825 \cdot 7^7,
  4770 \cdot 7^9, 7830 \cdot 7^{10}, 1178 \cdot 7^{12}, 111 \cdot 7^{14}, 6 \cdot 7^{16},
  7^{17}$.
- Row $7$: $0, 1, 253 \cdot 7^2, 1902 \cdot 7^4, 4246 \cdot 7^6, 31540 \cdot 7^7,
  19302 \cdot 7^9, 7501 \cdot 7^{11}, 1944 \cdot 7^{13}, 2397 \cdot 7^{14}, 285 \cdot 7^{16},
  22 \cdot 7^{18}, 7^{20}, 7^{20}$.

These are rows $1$ to $7$ of Garvan's matrix as printed in Tables 1 and 2 of the source.

## Sources

- D. S. Gireesh, C. Shivashankar, and B. Hemanthkumar, *On 2-Color Partitions in Which the Parts of One Color Are Restricted to Multiples of 7^k*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A94, Section 1, Tables 1 and 2.

articles.title: Initial entries of Garvan's first coefficient vector
articles.statement:
The first of Garvan's coefficient
vectors, $x_1$, has entries $x_{1,1} = 7$, $x_{1,2} = 7^2 = 49$ and $x_{1,3} = 0$.

## Sources

- D. S. Gireesh, C. Shivashankar, and B. Hemanthkumar, *On 2-Color Partitions in Which the Parts of One Color Are Restricted to Multiples of 7^k*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A94, Section 1.

articles.title: Garvan's coefficient vectors
articles.statement:
Let $(m_{i,j})$ be Garvan's matrix. Garvan's coefficient
vectors $x_k = (x_{k,1}, x_{k,2}, \dots)$ for $k \ge 1$ are defined by $x_{1,1} = 7$,
$x_{1,2} = 7^2$ and $x_{1,i} = 0$ for $i \ge 3$, and, for $k \ge 1$ and $i \ge 1$, by

$$x_{k+1,i} = \sum_{j=1}^{7^k} x_{k,j}\, m_{4j,j+i}$$

if $k$ is odd and

$$x_{k+1,i} = \sum_{j=1}^{7^k} x_{k,j}\, m_{4j+1,j+i}$$

if $k$ is even. Values at index $0$ are conventions outside the source's range.

The source sums over all $j \ge 1$; the cut at $7^k$ loses nothing, since $m_{i,j} = 0$ for
$j > 2i$, so the largest index of a nonzero entry of $x_{k+1}$ is at most $7$ times that of
$x_k$ plus $2$, which stays below $7^{k+1}$.

## Sources

- D. S. Gireesh, C. Shivashankar, and B. Hemanthkumar, *On 2-Color Partitions in Which the Parts of One Color Are Restricted to Multiples of 7^k*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A94, Section 1.

articles.title: Initial coefficient vector for even powers of 7
articles.statement:
For all natural numbers $k$ and $j$,
the first coefficient vector of Theorem 3 agrees with Garvan's coefficient vector $x_{2k-1}$:
$y^{(2k)}_{1,j} = x_{2k-1,j}$. For $k = 0$ the index $2k - 1$ is read as $0$.

## Sources

- D. S. Gireesh, C. Shivashankar, and B. Hemanthkumar, *On 2-Color Partitions in Which the Parts of One Color Are Restricted to Multiples of 7^k*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A94, Theorem 3.

articles.title: Coefficient vectors for even powers of 7
articles.statement:
Let $(m_{i,j})$ be Garvan's matrix and
$x_k$ Garvan's coefficient vectors, and fix $k \ge 1$. The coefficient vectors
$y^{(2k)}_\beta = (y^{(2k)}_{\beta,1}, y^{(2k)}_{\beta,2}, \dots)$ of Theorem 3, $\beta \ge 1$,
are defined by $y^{(2k)}_{1,j} = x_{2k-1,j}$ and, for $\beta \ge 1$,

$$y^{(2k)}_{\beta+1,j} = \sum_{i=1}^{7^{2k+\beta-2}} y^{(2k)}_{\beta,i}\, m_{4i,i+j}$$

if $\beta$ is odd and

$$y^{(2k)}_{\beta+1,j} = \sum_{i=1}^{7^{2k+\beta-2}} y^{(2k)}_{\beta,i}\, m_{4i+2,i+j}$$

if $\beta$ is even. The definition also assigns conventional values for $k = 0$ and
$\beta = 0$.

The source sums over all $i \ge 1$; the cut at $7^{2k+\beta-2}$ lies above the support of
$y^{(2k)}_\beta$, since each step maps the largest index $s$ of a nonzero entry to at most
$7s + 4$.

## Sources

- D. S. Gireesh, C. Shivashankar, and B. Hemanthkumar, *On 2-Color Partitions in Which the Parts of One Color Are Restricted to Multiples of 7^k*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A94, Theorem 3.

articles.title: Initial coefficient vector for odd powers of 7
articles.statement:
For all natural numbers $k$ and $j$,
the first coefficient vector of Theorem 2 agrees with Garvan's coefficient vector $x_{2k-1}$:
$y^{(2k-1)}_{1,j} = x_{2k-1,j}$. For $k = 0$ the index $2k - 1$ is read as $0$.

## Sources

- D. S. Gireesh, C. Shivashankar, and B. Hemanthkumar, *On 2-Color Partitions in Which the Parts of One Color Are Restricted to Multiples of 7^k*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A94, Theorem 2.

articles.title: Coefficient vectors for odd powers of 7
articles.statement:
For $k \ge 1$ and $\beta \ge 1$ the vectors
