$y^{(2k-1)}_\beta = (y^{(2k-1)}_{\beta,1}, y^{(2k-1)}_{\beta,2}, \dots)$ are built from Garvan's
vector $x_{2k-1}$ and Garvan's matrix $m_{i,j}$: $y^{(2k-1)}_{1,j} = x_{2k-1,j}$ and

$$y^{(2k-1)}_{\beta+1,j} = \sum_{i=1}^{7^{2k+\beta-2}} y^{(2k-1)}_{\beta,i}\, m_{4i+1,i+j}.$$

The index $\beta = 0$ gives $0$, and for $k = 0$ every entry is $0$.

The sum over $i$ stops at $7^{2k+\beta-2}$, above the support of $y^{(2k-1)}_\beta$ (each step
maps support $s$ into $7s + 2$).

## Sources

- D. S. Gireesh, C. Shivashankar, and B. Hemanthkumar, *On 2-Color Partitions in Which the Parts of One Color Are Restricted to Multiples of 7^k*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A94, Theorem 2.

articles.title: Huffing identities for three eta quotients
articles.statement:
Let
$f_k = \prod_{n \ge 1} (1 - q^{kn})$ in $\mathbb{Q}[[q]]$, let $H$ be the huffing operator
$H\bigl(\sum_n p_n q^n\bigr) = \sum_n p_{7n} q^{7n}$, and let $m_{i,j}$ be Garvan's matrix. For
every $i \ge 1$,

$$H\Bigl(\frac{q^{i+2} f_7^{4i}}{f_1^{4i+1}}\Bigr)
= \sum_{j=1}^{7i+4} m_{4i+1,i+j}\, \frac{q^{7j} f_{49}^{4j-1}}{f_7^{4j}},$$



$$H\Bigl(\frac{q^{i+4} f_7^{4i}}{f_1^{4i+2}}\Bigr)
= \sum_{j=1}^{7i+4} m_{4i+2,i+j}\, \frac{q^{7j} f_{49}^{4j-2}}{f_7^{4j}},$$



$$H\Bigl(\frac{q^{i} f_7^{4i}}{f_1^{4i}}\Bigr)
= \sum_{j=1}^{7i+4} m_{4i,i+j}\, \frac{q^{7j} f_{49}^{4j}}{f_7^{4j}}.$$

These are identities of formal power series over $\mathbb{Q}$. The sums stop at $j = 7i + 4$,
beyond which the coefficients $m$ vanish.

## Sources

- D. S. Gireesh, C. Shivashankar, and B. Hemanthkumar, *On 2-Color Partitions in Which the Parts of One Color Are Restricted to Multiples of 7^k*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A94, Lemma 2.

articles.title: Garvan's huffing identities for powers of $\xi$
articles.statement:
Let
$f_k = \prod_{n \ge 1} (1 - q^{kn})$ in $\mathbb{Q}[[q]]$, let $H$ be the huffing operator
$H\bigl(\sum_n p_n q^n\bigr) = \sum_n p_{7n} q^{7n}$, and let $m_{i,j}$ be Garvan's matrix. Write
$\xi^{-a} = q^{2a} f_{49}^a / f_1^a$ and $T^{-b} = q^{7b} f_{49}^{4b} / f_7^{4b}$ for the
negative powers of $\xi = f_1 / (q^2 f_{49})$ and $T = f_7^4 / (q^7 f_{49}^4)$, which are formal
power series. For every $i \ge 1$,

$$H(\xi^{-i}) = \sum_{j=1}^{2i} m_{i,j}\, T^{-j}$$

and

$$H(\xi^{-4i}) = \sum_{j=1}^{7i} m_{4i,i+j}\, T^{-i-j}.$$

These are identities of formal power series over $\mathbb{Q}$. The sums stop at $j = 2i$,
resp. $j = 7i$, beyond which the coefficients $m$ vanish.

## Sources

- D. S. Gireesh, C. Shivashankar, and B. Hemanthkumar, *On 2-Color Partitions in Which the Parts of One Color Are Restricted to Multiples of 7^k*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A94, Lemma 1.

articles.title: Garvan's 7-adic bounds for the matrix $m_{i,j}$
articles.statement:
Let $m_{i,j}$ be Garvan's matrix. For
all $i, j \ge 1$, $7^{\lfloor (7j - 2i - 1)/4 \rfloor}$ divides $m_{i,j}$, and in particular
$7^{\lfloor (7j - i - 1)/4 \rfloor}$ divides $m_{4i,i+j}$, $7^{\lfloor (7j - i - 3)/4 \rfloor}$
divides $m_{4i+1,i+j}$ and $7^{\lfloor (7j - i - 5)/4 \rfloor}$ divides $m_{4i+2,i+j}$. A negative
exponent is replaced by $0$, which gives the same statement.

The paper states the bounds as $\pi(n) \ge e$ for the $7$-adic valuation $\pi$ (with
$\pi(0) = \infty$), which is the divisibility $7^e \mid n$. Its bracket is read as the floor: the
ceiling reading fails, since $m_{2,1} = 10$ is not divisible by $7^{\lceil 2/4 \rceil} = 7$.

## Sources

- D. S. Gireesh, C. Shivashankar, and B. Hemanthkumar, *On 2-Color Partitions in Which the Parts of One Color Are Restricted to Multiples of 7^k*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A94, Lemma 3.

articles.title: Garvan's 7-adic bounds for the vectors $x_k$
articles.statement:
Let $x_k = (x_{k,1}, x_{k,2}, \dots)$ be
Garvan's coefficient vectors and $\pi$ the $7$-adic valuation. Then $\pi(x_{1,1}) = 1$,
$\pi(x_{1,2}) = 2$, and for all $k, j \ge 1$, $7^{k + 1 + \lfloor (7j-4)/4 \rfloor}$ divides
$x_{2k+1,j}$ and $7^{k + 1 + \lfloor (7j-6)/4 \rfloor}$ divides $x_{2k,j}$.

## Sources

- D. S. Gireesh, C. Shivashankar, and B. Hemanthkumar, *On 2-Color Partitions in Which the Parts of One Color Are Restricted to Multiples of 7^k*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A94, Lemma 4.

articles.title: 7-adic bounds for the vectors $y^{(2k)}_\beta$
articles.statement:
Let $y^{(2k)}_\beta$ be the coefficient
vectors for even powers of $7$, built from Garvan's vectors and matrix. For all $k, j \ge 1$ and
$\beta \ge 0$, $7^{k + \beta + \lfloor (7j-7)/4 \rfloor}$ divides $y^{(2k)}_{2\beta+1,j}$ and
$7^{k + \beta + 1 + \lfloor (7j-7)/4 \rfloor}$ divides $y^{(2k)}_{2\beta+2,j}$.

## Sources

- D. S. Gireesh, C. Shivashankar, and B. Hemanthkumar, *On 2-Color Partitions in Which the Parts of One Color Are Restricted to Multiples of 7^k*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A94, Lemma 5.

articles.title: 7-adic bounds for the vectors $y^{(2k-1)}_\beta$
articles.statement:
Let $y^{(2k-1)}_\beta$ be the
coefficient vectors for odd powers of $7$, built from Garvan's vectors and matrix. For all
$k, j \ge 1$ and $\beta \ge 0$, $7^{k + \lfloor (7j-7)/4 \rfloor}$ divides $y^{(2k-1)}_{\beta+1,j}$.

## Sources

- D. S. Gireesh, C. Shivashankar, and B. Hemanthkumar, *On 2-Color Partitions in Which the Parts of One Color Are Restricted to Multiples of 7^k*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A94, Lemma 6.

articles.title: Two-color partitions below the modulus
articles.statement:
Let $p_{1,\ell}(n)$ be the number of 2-color
partitions of $n$ in which the parts of the second color are multiples of $\ell$, and $p(n)$ the
number of partitions of $n$. For all natural numbers $\ell$ and $n$ with $n < \ell$, the second
color is unavailable and $p_{1,\ell}(n) = p(n)$.

## Sources

- D. S. Gireesh, C. Shivashankar, and B. Hemanthkumar, *On 2-Color Partitions in Which the Parts of One Color Are Restricted to Multiples of 7^k*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A94, Section 1.

articles.title: Generating functions for $p_{1,7^{2k-1}}$ on progressions
articles.statement:
Let $p_{1,\ell}(n)$ be the
number of 2-color partitions of $n$ in which the parts of the second color are multiples of
$\ell$, let $f_k = \prod_{n \ge 1} (1 - q^{kn})$ in $\mathbb{Q}[[q]]$, and let $y^{(2k-1)}_\beta$
be the coefficient vectors for odd powers of $7$. For all $k \ge 1$ and $\beta \ge 0$, with
$N = 7^{2k+\beta-1}$,

$$\sum_{n \ge 0} p_{1,7^{2k-1}}\Bigl(N n + \frac{16 N + 7^{2k-1} + 1}{24}\Bigr) q^n
= \sum_{i=1}^{N} y^{(2k-1)}_{\beta+1,i}\, q^{i-1} \frac{f_7^{4i-1}}{f_1^{4i+1}}$$

as formal power series over $\mathbb{Q}$.

The numerator $16 N + 7^{2k-1} + 1$ is divisible by $24$. The sum over $i$ stops at $N$, above
the support of $y^{(2k-1)}_{\beta+1}$.

## Sources

- D. S. Gireesh, C. Shivashankar, and B. Hemanthkumar, *On 2-Color Partitions in Which the Parts of One Color Are Restricted to Multiples of 7^k*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A94, Theorem 2.

articles.title: Generating functions for $p_{1,7^{2k}}$ on progressions
articles.statement:
Let $p_{1,\ell}(n)$ be the
number of 2-color partitions of $n$ in which the parts of the second color are multiples of
$\ell$, let $f_k = \prod_{n \ge 1} (1 - q^{kn})$ in $\mathbb{Q}[[q]]$, and let $y^{(2k)}_\beta$ be
the coefficient vectors for even powers of $7$. For all $k \ge 1$ and $\beta \ge 0$, with
$N = 7^{2k+2\beta-1}$,

$$\sum_{n \ge 0} p_{1,7^{2k}}\Bigl(N n + \frac{10 N + 7^{2k} + 1}{24}\Bigr) q^n
= \sum_{i=1}^{7N} y^{(2k)}_{2\beta+1,i}\, q^{i-1} \frac{f_7^{4i-2}}{f_1^{4i}}$$

and

$$\sum_{n \ge 0} p_{1,7^{2k}}\Bigl(7N n + \frac{22 \cdot 7N + 7^{2k} + 1}{24}\Bigr) q^n
= \sum_{j=1}^{49N} y^{(2k)}_{2\beta+2,j}\, q^{j-1} \frac{f_7^{4j}}{f_1^{4j+2}}$$

as formal power series over $\mathbb{Q}$.

Both numerators are divisible by $24$. The sums stop at $7N$, resp. $49N$, above the supports of
the vectors.

## Sources

- D. S. Gireesh, C. Shivashankar, and B. Hemanthkumar, *On 2-Color Partitions in Which the Parts of One Color Are Restricted to Multiples of 7^k*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A94, Theorem 3.

articles.title: Congruences for two-color partitions modulo powers of 7
articles.statement:
For all natural numbers $n$,
$\beta$ and $k \ge 1$, the two-color partition count $p_{1,\ell}$ satisfies

$$
p_{1,7^{2k-1}}(7^{2k+\beta-1} n + (16 \cdot 7^{2k+\beta-1} + 7^{2k-1} + 1)/24)
\equiv 0 \pmod{7^k},
$$



$$
p_{1,7^{2k}}(7^{2k+2\beta-1} n + (10 \cdot 7^{2k+2\beta-1} + 7^{2k} + 1)/24)
\equiv 0 \pmod{7^{k+\beta}},
$$



$$
p_{1,7^{2k}}(7^{2k+2\beta} n + (22 \cdot 7^{2k+2\beta} + 7^{2k} + 1)/24)
\equiv 0 \pmod{7^{k+\beta+1}},
$$

and, for each $r \in \{3, 4, 6\}$,

$$
p_{1,7^{2k}}(7^{2k+2\beta+1} n + ((24r + 22) \cdot 7^{2k+2\beta} + 7^{2k} + 1)/24)
\equiv 0 \pmod{7^{k+\beta+2}}.
$$

Each numerator is divisible by $24$, so every division above is exact.

## Sources

- D. S. Gireesh, C. Shivashankar, and B. Hemanthkumar, *On 2-Color Partitions in Which the Parts of One Color Are Restricted to Multiples of 7^k*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A94, Theorem 1, congruences (6)-(9).

articles.title: The two-color partition count at zero
articles.statement:
For every natural number $\ell$, including
$\ell = 0$, the two-color partition count $p_{1,\ell}$ satisfies $p_{1,\ell}(0) = 1$.

## Sources

- D. S. Gireesh, C. Shivashankar, and B. Hemanthkumar, *On 2-Color Partitions in Which the Parts of One Color Are Restricted to Multiples of 7^k*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A94, Section 1.

articles.title: Two-color partitions with one color restricted to multiples
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $\ell$
and $n$, let $p(m)$ be the number of partitions of $m$, and define

$$
p_{1,\ell}(n) = \sum_{j=0}^{\lfloor n/\ell \rfloor} p(n - \ell j)\, p(j).
$$

For $\ell > 0$ this is the number of 2-color partitions of $n$ in which the parts of the second
color are multiples of $\ell$, that is, the coefficient of $q^n$ in $1/(f_1 f_\ell)$, where
$f_m = \prod_{j \ge 1} (1 - q^{mj})$. For $\ell = 0$ the bound $\lfloor n/0 \rfloor$ is taken to
be $0$, so $p_{1,0}(n) = p(n)$; this is a convention with no generating-function meaning. The
source uses $\ell = 7^k$.

## Sources

- D. S. Gireesh, C. Shivashankar, and B. Hemanthkumar, *On 2-Color Partitions in Which the Parts of One Color Are Restricted to Multiples of 7^k*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A94, Section 1.

articles.title: First coefficients of the mock theta function $\lambda$
articles.statement:
Write
$\lambda(q) = \sum_{n \ge 0} P_\lambda(n) q^n$ for the sixth-order mock theta function $\lambda$.
Then $P_\lambda(0) = 1$ and $P_\lambda(1) = -1$.

## Sources

- Sabi Biswas and Nipen Saikia, *Arithmetic Properties of the Coefficients of Some Mock Theta Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A72, Equation (3).

articles.title: First coefficients of the mock theta function $\sigma$
articles.statement:
Write
$\sigma(q) = \sum_{n \ge 0} P_\sigma(n) q^n$ for the sixth-order mock theta function $\sigma$.
Then $P_\sigma(0) = 0$ and $P_\sigma(1) = 1$.

## Sources

- Sabi Biswas and Nipen Saikia, *Arithmetic Properties of the Coefficients of Some Mock Theta Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A72, Equation (2).

articles.title: First coefficients of the mock theta function $v$
articles.statement:
Write
$v(q) = \sum_{n \ge 0} P_v(n) q^n$ for the eighth-order mock theta function $v$. Then
$P_v(0) = 0$ and $P_v(1) = 1$.

## Sources

- Sabi Biswas and Nipen Saikia, *Arithmetic Properties of the Coefficients of Some Mock Theta Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A72, Equation (4).

articles.title: First coefficients of Ramanujan's theta function $\psi$
articles.statement:
Let
$\psi(q) = f(q, q^3) = \sum_{m \in \mathbb{Z}} q^{m(m+1)/2 + 3m(m-1)/2}$, where $f$ is
Ramanujan's general theta function. The coefficients of $q^0$, $q^1$, $q^2$, $q^3$ in $\psi(q)$
are $1$, $1$, $0$, $1$.

## Sources

- Sabi Biswas and Nipen Saikia, *Arithmetic Properties of the Coefficients of Some Mock Theta Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A72, Equation (10).

articles.title: The $p$-dissection of $f_1^3$
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be an odd prime and, for $k \ge 1$, let
$f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$. Then, as integer power series,

$$
f_1^3 = \sum_{k=0,\ k \ne (p-1)/2}^{p-1} (-1)^k q^{k(k+1)/2}
\sum_{n \ge 0} (-1)^n (2pn + 2k + 1) q^{pn(pn+2k+1)/2} +
p (-1)^{(p-1)/2} q^{(p^2-1)/8} f_{p^2}^3.
$$

Moreover, $(k^2 + k)/2 \not\equiv (p^2 - 1)/8 \pmod p$ for every integer $k$ with
$0 \le k \le p - 1$ and $k \ne (p-1)/2$.

## Sources

- Sabi Biswas and Nipen Saikia, *Arithmetic Properties of the Coefficients of Some Mock Theta Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A72, Lemma 3.

articles.title: The $p$-dissection of $f_1$
articles.statement:
Let $p \ge 5$ be a prime, let
$f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$ for $k \ge 1$, and let
$f(a, b) = \sum_{m \in \mathbb{Z}} a^{m(m+1)/2} b^{m(m-1)/2}$ be Ramanujan's general theta
function. Put $c = (p-1)/6$ if $p \equiv 1 \pmod 6$ and $c = (-p-1)/6$ otherwise. Then, as
integer power series,

$$
f_1 = \sum_{t=-(p-1)/2,\ t \ne c}^{(p-1)/2} (-1)^t q^{(3t^2+t)/2}
f\bigl(-q^{(3p^2+(6t+1)p)/2}, -q^{(3p^2-(6t+1)p)/2}\bigr) +
(-1)^c q^{(p^2-1)/24} f_{p^2}.
$$

Moreover, $(3t^2 + t)/2 \not\equiv (p^2 - 1)/24 \pmod p$ for every integer $t$ with
$-(p-1)/2 \le t \le (p-1)/2$ and $t \ne c$.

## Sources

- Sabi Biswas and Nipen Saikia, *Arithmetic Properties of the Coefficients of Some Mock Theta Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A72, Lemma 2.

articles.title: Even-index coefficients of the mock theta function $\lambda$
articles.statement:
Write
$\lambda(q) = \sum_{n \ge 0} P_\lambda(n) q^n$ for the sixth-order mock theta function $\lambda$,
let $f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$, and let $b_2^3(m)$ be the coefficient of $q^m$ in
$(f_2/f_1)^3$. Then for every $n \ge 0$,

$$
P_\lambda(2n) = b_2^3(n) + 2 \sum_{k \ge 1,\ 3k^2 \le n} (-1)^k b_2^3(n - 3k^2).
$$

## Sources

- Sabi Biswas and Nipen Saikia, *Arithmetic Properties of the Coefficients of Some Mock Theta Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A72, Theorem 8.

articles.title: Coefficients of the mock theta function $\lambda$ at indices $6n+2$
articles.statement:
Write
$\lambda(q) = \sum_{n \ge 0} P_\lambda(n) q^n$ for the sixth-order mock theta function $\lambda$,
let $f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$, and let $\overline{p}_3(j)$ be the coefficient of
$q^j$ in $(f_2/f_1^2)^3$. Then for every $n \ge 0$,

$$
P_\lambda(6n+2) = 3 \sum_{m \ge 0,\ 3m(m+1)/2 \le n} (-1)^m (2m+1)\,
\overline{p}_3\bigl(n - 3m(m+1)/2\bigr) +
6 \sum_{m \ge 0} \sum_{k \ge 1,\ 3k^2 + 3m(m+1)/2 \le n} (-1)^{m+k} (2m+1)\,
\overline{p}_3\bigl(n - 3k^2 - 3m(m+1)/2\bigr).
$$

## Sources

- Sabi Biswas and Nipen Saikia, *Arithmetic Properties of the Coefficients of Some Mock Theta Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A72, Theorem 9.

articles.title: The sixth-order mock theta function $\lambda$
articles.statement:
With
$(a; b)_n = \prod_{k=0}^{n-1} (1 - a b^k)$, the mock theta function $\lambda$ is the integer
power series

$$
\lambda(q) = \sum_{n \ge 0} \frac{(-1)^n q^n (q; q^2)_n}{(-q; q)_n}.
$$

The $n$th summand has order $n$, so the coefficient of $q^m$ only involves the summands with
$n \le m$.

## Sources

- Sabi Biswas and Nipen Saikia, *Arithmetic Properties of the Coefficients of Some Mock Theta Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A72, Equation (3).

articles.title: Congruences modulo 2 for the mock theta function $\sigma$
articles.statement:
Write
$\sigma(q) = \sum_{n \ge 0} P_\sigma(n) q^n$ for the sixth-order mock theta function $\sigma$ and
let $f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$. Let $p \ge 5$ be a prime with Legendre symbol
$\left(\frac{-2}{p}\right) = -1$ and let $\alpha \ge 0$ be an integer. Then, coefficientwise,

$$
f_3 \sum_{n \ge 0} P_\sigma\Bigl(2 p^{2\alpha} n + \frac{11 p^{2\alpha} + 1}{12}\Bigr) q^n
\equiv f_2 f_6^2 \pmod 2,
$$

and for all integers $n \ge 0$ and all integers $j$ with $1 \le j \le p - 1$,

$$
P_\sigma\Bigl(2 p^{2\alpha+2} n + 2 p^{2\alpha+1} j + \frac{11 p^{2\alpha+2} + 1}{12}\Bigr)
\equiv 0 \pmod 2.
$$

Since $f_2 f_6^2 / f_3 = f_2 \psi(q^3)$ with $\psi(q) = \sum_{n \ge 0} q^{n(n+1)/2}$, the first
congruence says that the series of $P_\sigma(2 p^{2\alpha} n + (11 p^{2\alpha} + 1)/12)$ is
congruent to $f_2 \psi(q^3)$ modulo $2$. The division by $12$ is exact since
$p^2 \equiv 1 \pmod{24}$.

## Sources

- Sabi Biswas and Nipen Saikia, *Arithmetic Properties of the Coefficients of Some Mock Theta Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A72, Theorem 6.

articles.title: Sum formula for the odd-indexed coefficients of $\sigma(q)$
articles.statement:
Let $P_\sigma(n)$ be the
coefficient of $q^n$ in the sixth-order mock theta function $\sigma(q)$, for $k \ge 1$ let
$f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$, and let $b_2^2(k)$ be the coefficient of $q^k$ in the
integer power series $(f_2 / f_1)^2$. Then for every $n \ge 0$,
$P_\sigma(2n+1) = \sum_{m \ge 0,\ (3m^2+3m)/2 \le n} b_2^2\bigl(n - (3m^2+3m)/2\bigr)$.

## Sources

- Sabi Biswas and Nipen Saikia, *Arithmetic Properties of the Coefficients of Some Mock Theta Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A72, Theorem 7.

articles.title: Generating function for the odd-indexed coefficients of $\sigma(q)$
articles.statement:
Let $P_\sigma(n)$
be the coefficient of $q^n$ in the sixth-order mock theta function $\sigma(q)$, and for
$k \ge 1$ let $f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$. Then, as integer power series,
$f_1^2 f_3 \sum_{n \ge 0} P_\sigma(2n+1) q^n = f_2^2 f_6^2$, that is,
$\sum_{n \ge 0} P_\sigma(2n+1) q^n = f_2^2 f_6^2 / (f_1^2 f_3)$.

## Sources

- Sabi Biswas and Nipen Saikia, *Arithmetic Properties of the Coefficients of Some Mock Theta Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A72, Theorem 5.

articles.title: The sixth-order mock theta function $\sigma(q)$
articles.statement:
The mock theta function
$\sigma(q) = \sum_{n \ge 0} q^{(n+1)(n+2)/2} (-q; q)_n / (q; q^2)_{n+1}$, where
$(-q; q)_n = \prod_{k=1}^{n} (1 + q^k)$ and $(q; q^2)_{n+1} = \prod_{k=0}^{n} (1 - q^{2k+1})$, is
taken as a power series in $q$ with integer coefficients.

The $n$th summand has order $(n+1)(n+2)/2 > n$, so the coefficient of $q^m$ only involves the
summands with $n \le m$.

## Sources

- Sabi Biswas and Nipen Saikia, *Arithmetic Properties of the Coefficients of Some Mock Theta Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A72, Equation (2).

articles.title: The coefficients of $q^{6n+5}$ in $v(q)$ are divisible by 3
articles.statement:
Let $P_v(n)$ be the
coefficient of $q^n$ in the eighth-order mock theta function $v(q)$. Then
$P_v(6n+5) \equiv 0 \pmod 3$ for every $n \ge 0$.

## Sources

- Sabi Biswas and Nipen Saikia, *Arithmetic Properties of the Coefficients of Some Mock Theta Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A72, Theorem 2 (i).

articles.title: Infinite family of congruences modulo 6 for $v(q)$
articles.statement:
Let $P_v(n)$ be the coefficient of
$q^n$ in the eighth-order mock theta function $v(q)$, and for $k \ge 1$ let
$f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$. Let $p \ge 5$ be a prime whose Legendre symbol
$\left(\frac{-18}{p}\right)$ equals $-1$, and let $\alpha \ge 0$ be an integer. Then for every
$n \ge 0$, $P_v\bigl(6 p^{2\alpha} n + (19 p^{2\alpha} + 1)/4\bigr)$ is congruent modulo $6$ to
the coefficient of $q^n$ in $3 f_1 f_6^3$. Moreover, for every $n \ge 0$ and every $j$ with
$1 \le j \le p - 1$,
$P_v\bigl(6 p^{2\alpha+2} n + 6 p^{2\alpha+1} j + (19 p^{2\alpha+2} + 1)/4\bigr) \equiv 0 \pmod 6$.

The divisions by $4$ are exact since $p^2 \equiv 1 \pmod 8$.

## Sources

- Sabi Biswas and Nipen Saikia, *Arithmetic Properties of the Coefficients of Some Mock Theta Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A72, Theorem 2 (iii), Equations (23) and (24).

articles.title: Infinite family of congruences modulo 2 for $v(q)$
articles.statement:
Let $P_v(n)$ be the coefficient of
$q^n$ in the eighth-order mock theta function $v(q)$, and for $k \ge 1$ let
$f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$. Let $p \ge 3$ be a prime whose Legendre symbol
$\left(\frac{-2}{p}\right)$ equals $-1$, and let $\alpha \ge 0$ be an integer. Then the integer
power series $f_1 \sum_{n \ge 0} P_v\bigl(2 p^{2\alpha} n + (3 p^{2\alpha} + 1)/4\bigr) q^n$ and
$f_2 f_4^2$ have congruent coefficients modulo $2$. Moreover, for every $n \ge 0$ and every $j$
with $1 \le j \le p - 1$,
$P_v\bigl(2 p^{2\alpha+2} n + 2 p^{2\alpha+1} j + (3 p^{2\alpha+2} + 1)/4\bigr) \equiv 0 \pmod 2$.

The divisions by $4$ are exact since $p^2 \equiv 1 \pmod 8$. Since $f_1$ has an inverse with
integer coefficients, the first congruence says that
$\sum_{n \ge 0} P_v(2 p^{2\alpha} n + (3 p^{2\alpha} + 1)/4) q^n \equiv \psi(q) \psi(q^2) \pmod 2$,
where $\psi(q) = \sum_{n \ge 0} q^{n(n+1)/2}$, so that $\psi(q) \psi(q^2) = f_2 f_4^2 / f_1$.

## Sources

- Sabi Biswas and Nipen Saikia, *Arithmetic Properties of the Coefficients of Some Mock Theta Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A72, Theorem 2 (ii), Equations (21) and (22).

articles.title: Sum formula for the odd-indexed coefficients of $v(q)$
articles.statement:
Let $P_v(n)$ be the coefficient
of $q^n$ in the eighth-order mock theta function $v(q)$, for $k \ge 1$ let
$f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$, and let $b_4^1(k)$ be the coefficient of $q^k$ in the
integer power series $f_4 / f_1$. Then for every $n \ge 0$,
$P_v(2n+1) = \sum_{m \ge 0,\ m(m+1) \le n} b_4^1\bigl(n - m(m+1)\bigr)$.

## Sources

- Sabi Biswas and Nipen Saikia, *Arithmetic Properties of the Coefficients of Some Mock Theta Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A72, Theorem 3.

articles.title: Generating function for the odd-indexed coefficients of $v(q)$
articles.statement:
Let $P_v(n)$ be the
coefficient of $q^n$ in the eighth-order mock theta function $v(q)$, and for $k \ge 1$ let
$f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$. Then, as integer power series,
$f_1 f_2 \sum_{n \ge 0} P_v(2n+1) q^n = f_4^3$, that is,
$\sum_{n \ge 0} P_v(2n+1) q^n = f_4^3 / (f_1 f_2)$.

## Sources

- Sabi Biswas and Nipen Saikia, *Arithmetic Properties of the Coefficients of Some Mock Theta Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A72, Theorem 1.

articles.title: Sum formula for the coefficients of $q^{6n+5}$ in $v(q)$
articles.statement:
Let $P_v(n)$ be the
coefficient of $q^n$ in the eighth-order mock theta function $v(q)$, for $k \ge 1$ let
$f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$, and let $b_6^3(k)$ be the coefficient of $q^k$ in the
integer power series $(f_6 / f_1)^3$. Then for every $n \ge 0$,
$P_v(6n+5) = 3 b_6^3(n) + 3 \sum_{m \ge 1,\ 2m(3m+1) \le n} (-1)^m b_6^3\bigl(n - 2m(3m+1)\bigr) +
3 \sum_{m \ge 1,\ 2m(3m-1) \le n} (-1)^m b_6^3\bigl(n - 2m(3m-1)\bigr)$.

## Sources

- Sabi Biswas and Nipen Saikia, *Arithmetic Properties of the Coefficients of Some Mock Theta Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A72, Theorem 4.

articles.title: The eighth-order mock theta function $v(q)$
articles.statement:
The mock theta function
$v(q) = \sum_{n \ge 0} q^{(n+1)^2} (-q; q^2)_n / (q; q^2)_{n+1}$, where
$(-q; q^2)_n = \prod_{k=0}^{n-1} (1 + q^{2k+1})$ and
$(q; q^2)_{n+1} = \prod_{k=0}^{n} (1 - q^{2k+1})$, is taken as a power series in $q$ with integer
coefficients.

The $n$th summand has order $(n+1)^2$, so the coefficient of $q^m$ only involves the summands
with $n \le m$.

## Sources

- Sabi Biswas and Nipen Saikia, *Arithmetic Properties of the Coefficients of Some Mock Theta Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A72, Equation (4).

articles.title: The p-dissection of Ramanujan's psi function
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be an odd prime, let $f(c, d)$ be
Ramanujan's theta function and $\psi(q) = f(q, q^3)$. Then, as integer power series,
$\psi(q) = \sum_{m=0}^{(p-3)/2} q^{(m^2+m)/2} f(q^{(p^2+(2m+1)p)/2}, q^{(p^2-(2m+1)p)/2}) +
q^{(p^2-1)/8} f(q^{p^2}, q^{3p^2})$, where the last factor is $\psi(q^{p^2})$. Moreover
$(m^2+m)/2 \not\equiv (p^2-1)/8 \pmod p$ for every integer $m$ with $0 \le m \le (p-3)/2$.

The paper quotes this from Cui and Gu, Theorem 2.1.

## Sources

- Sabi Biswas and Nipen Saikia, *Arithmetic Properties of the Coefficients of Some Mock Theta Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A72, Lemma 1.

articles.title: Ramanujan's theta function at monomial arguments
articles.statement:
For an integer $\varepsilon$ and natural
numbers $a$ and $b$, $f(\varepsilon q^a, \varepsilon q^b)$ is the integer power series in $q$
whose coefficient of $q^n$ is the sum of $\varepsilon^{m^2}$ over the integers $m$ with
$|m| \le n + 1$ and $a \cdot m(m+1)/2 + b \cdot m(m-1)/2 = n$.

When $a + b \ge 1$ the exponent $a \cdot m(m+1)/2 + b \cdot m(m-1)/2$ is at least
$|m|(|m|-1)/2$, so the bound $|m| \le n + 1$ excludes no term and this is Ramanujan's
$f(c, d) = \sum_{m \in \mathbb{Z}} c^{m(m+1)/2} d^{m(m-1)/2}$ at $c = \varepsilon q^a$ and
$d = \varepsilon q^b$; the definition is meant for $a + b \ge 1$. Special cases are
$\psi(q) = f(q, q^3)$ and $f(-q) = f(-q, -q^2)$, which equals
$(q; q)_\infty = \prod_{k \ge 1} (1 - q^k)$.

## Sources

- Sabi Biswas and Nipen Saikia, *Arithmetic Properties of the Coefficients of Some Mock Theta Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A72, Section 2 (definition of `f(c, d)`, Equations (10) and (11)).

articles.title: Glaisher's congruences for divisor sums over squares and triangular numbers
articles.statement:
Let
$n \ge 1$ be a natural number. Write $\sigma(m)$ for the sum of the positive divisors of $m$
and $\bar\sigma_3(m) = \sum_{d \mid m,\ m/d \text{ odd}} d^3$, and set
$\sigma(m) = \bar\sigma_3(m) = 0$ for every integer $m \le 0$. Then the following hold. If
$5 \nmid n$, then $\sum_{j=0}^{n} \sigma(2n+1-j(j+1)) \equiv 0 \pmod 5$. The sum
$\sum_{j=0}^{n} \sigma(n-j(j+1)/2)$ is congruent modulo $4$ to $n$ if $n = k(k+1)/2$ for some
natural number $k$, and to $0$ otherwise. If $5 \nmid n$ and $n \equiv 2$ or $3 \pmod 4$, then
$\sigma(n) + 2\sum_{j=1}^{n} \sigma(n-j^2) \equiv 0 \pmod 5$. If $n$ is coprime to $3$, then
$\sum_{j=0}^{n+1} \bar\sigma_3(n+1-j(j+1)/2) \equiv 0 \pmod 9$.

## Sources

- Hartosh Singh Bal and Gaurav Bhatnagar, *Glaisher's Divisors and Infinite Products*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.1.6, Theorem 20 (`jis-2024-24.1.6-thm-20`).

articles.title: Glaisher's divisor functions as series-divisors
articles.statement:
Let $n$ be a natural number. For a
positive integer $m$, write $\sigma(m)$ for the sum of the divisors of $m$, $d_B(m)$ and
$d_C(m)$ for the sums of the odd and of the even divisors of $m$, $d_D(m)$ and $d_E(m)$ for the
sums of the divisors $d$ of $m$ with $m/d$ odd and with $m/d$ even,
$d_F(m) = \sum_{d \mid m} (-1)^{d-1} d$ and $d_G(m) = \sum_{d \mid m} (-1)^{m/d-1} d$, and set all
of these to $0$ at $m = 0$. Let $p(m)$, $p_o(m)$, $p_e(m)$ and $p_d(m)$ be the numbers of
partitions of $m$, of partitions of $m$ into odd parts, into even parts and into distinct parts,
let $\bar p(m)$ be the number of overpartitions of $m$, let $r(m)$ be the number of integers $k$
with $k^2 = m$, and let $t(m)$ be the number of natural numbers $k$ with $k(k+1)/2 = m$. Then
$d_C(n) = 2 d_E(n)$, and, with every sum running over $1 \le i \le n$,
$n\,p(n) = \sum_i \sigma(i)\,p(n-i)$, $n\,p_o(n) = \sum_i d_B(i)\,p_o(n-i)$,
$n\,p_e(n) = \sum_i d_C(i)\,p_e(n-i)$, $n\,\bar p(n) = \sum_i 2 d_D(i)\,\bar p(n-i)$,
$n\,r(n) = \sum_i (-1)^{i+1} 2 d_D(i)\,r(n-i)$, $n\,t(n) = \sum_i d_F(i)\,t(n-i)$ and
$n\,p_d(n) = \sum_i d_G(i)\,p_d(n-i)$.

In the language of the source, these recurrences say that $\sigma$, $d_B$, $d_C$, $2 d_D$,
$i \mapsto (-1)^{i+1} 2 d_D(i)$, $d_F$ and $d_G$ are the series-divisors of the generating
functions of $p$, $p_o$, $p_e$, $\bar p$, $\varphi(q) = \sum_{k \in \mathbb{Z}} q^{k^2}$,
$\psi(q) = \sum_{k \ge 0} q^{k(k+1)/2}$ and $p_d$ respectively.

## Sources

- Hartosh Singh Bal and Gaurav Bhatnagar, *Glaisher's Divisors and Infinite Products*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.1.6, Theorem 9 (`jis-2024-24.1.6-thm-9`).

articles.title: Recurrences for partitions into even or distinct parts and for overpartitions
articles.statement:
Let $n$
be a natural number. Let $p_e(m)$, $p_o(m)$ and $p_d(m)$ be the numbers of partitions of $m$
into even parts, into odd parts and into distinct parts, and let $\bar p(m)$ be the number of
overpartitions of $m$. For a positive integer $m$, write $\sigma(m)$ for the sum of the divisors
of $m$, $\sigma(m/2)$ for $\sigma$ evaluated at $m/2$ when $m$ is even and for $0$ when $m$ is
odd, $d_B(m)$ and $d_C(m)$ for the sums of the odd and of the even divisors of $m$, $d_D(m)$ for
the sum of the divisors $d$ of $m$ with $m/d$ odd, and $d_G(m) = \sum_{d \mid m} (-1)^{m/d-1} d$.
Then, with every sum running over $1 \le i \le n$,
$n\,p_e(n) = \sum_i d_C(i)\,p_e(n-i) = 2\sum_i \sigma(i/2)\,p_e(n-i)$,
$n\,p_d(n) = \sum_i d_B(i)\,p_o(n-i) = \sum_i d_G(i)\,p_d(n-i) =
\sum_i (\sigma(i) - 2\sigma(i/2))\,p_d(n-i)$, and
$n\,\bar p(n) = 2\sum_i d_D(i)\,\bar p(n-i) = 2\sum_i (\sigma(i) - \sigma(i/2))\,\bar p(n-i)$.

## Sources

- Hartosh Singh Bal and Gaurav Bhatnagar, *Glaisher's Divisors and Infinite Products*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.1.6, Theorem 10 (`jis-2024-24.1.6-thm-10`).

articles.title: Six divisor-function identities from the power recursion lemma
articles.statement:
Let $n \ge 1$ be a
natural number. Write $\sigma(m)$ for the sum of the positive divisors of $m$,
$\bar\sigma_3(m) = \sum_{d \mid m,\ m/d \text{ odd}} d^3$,
$\tilde\sigma_3(m) = \sum_{d \mid m} (-1)^{d-1} d^3$ and $S(m) = \sigma(m) - 4\sigma(m/4)$, where
$\sigma(m/4) = 0$ unless $4 \mid m$; all of these are $0$ at every integer $m \le 0$. Then
$2n\,\sigma(2n+1) = \sum_{j=1}^{n} (5j(j+1) - 2n)\,\sigma(2n+1-j(j+1))$; the number
$n\,S(n) - 2\sum_{j=1}^{n} (5j^2 - n)\,S(n-j^2)$ is $n$ if $n$ is a perfect square and $0$
otherwise;
$n\,\bar\sigma_3(n+1) = \sum_{j=1}^{n+1} (9j(j+1)/2 - n)\,\bar\sigma_3(n+1-j(j+1)/2)$; the
number $n\,\tilde\sigma_3(n) - 2\sum_{j=1}^{n} (-1)^j (9j^2 - n)\,\tilde\sigma_3(n-j^2)$ is
$(-1)^{n-1} n$ if $n$ is a perfect square and $0$ otherwise;
$\sum_{j=0}^{n+1} (3j - n)\,\sigma(2j+1)\,\bar\sigma_3(n+1-j) = 0$; and
$n\,(\tilde\sigma_3(n) + (-1)^n S(n)) =
8\sum_{j=1}^{n-1} (3j - n)(-1)^j S(j)\,\tilde\sigma_3(n-j)$.

## Sources

- Hartosh Singh Bal and Gaurav Bhatnagar, *Glaisher's Divisors and Infinite Products*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.1.6, Theorem 19 (`jis-2024-24.1.6-thm-19`).

articles.title: Six recursions for Glaisher's divisor functions from the theta functions
articles.statement:
Let $n \ge 1$
be a natural number. Write $\sigma(m)$ for the sum of the positive divisors of $m$, $d_D(m)$ for
the sum of the divisors $d$ of $m$ with $m/d$ odd, $d_F(m) = \sum_{d \mid m} (-1)^{d-1} d$,
$\bar\sigma_3(m) = \sum_{d \mid m,\ m/d \text{ odd}} d^3$,
$\tilde\sigma_3(m) = \sum_{d \mid m} (-1)^{d-1} d^3$ and $S(m) = \sigma(m) - 4\sigma(m/4)$, where
$\sigma(m/4) = 0$ unless $4 \mid m$; all of these are $0$ at every integer $m \le 0$. Then
$d_D(n) + 2\sum_{j=1}^{n} (-1)^j d_D(n-j^2)$ is $(-1)^{n-1} n$ if $n$ is a perfect square and
$0$ otherwise; $\sum_{j=0}^{n} d_F(n-j(j+1)/2)$ is $n$ if $n = k(k+1)/2$ for some natural number
$k$ and $0$ otherwise; $8\sum_{j=1}^{n-1} (-1)^{j+1} d_D(j)\,S(n-j) = n\,S(n) + (-1)^n d_D(n)$;
$4\sum_{j=1}^{n} d_F(j)\,\sigma(2n+1-2j) = n\,\sigma(2n+1)$;
$16\sum_{j=1}^{n-1} d_D(j)\,\tilde\sigma_3(n-j) = d_D(n) - n\,\tilde\sigma_3(n)$; and
$8\sum_{j=1}^{n} d_F(j)\,\bar\sigma_3(n+1-j) = n\,\bar\sigma_3(n+1)$.

These recursions come from the theta functions $\varphi(q) = \sum_{k \in \mathbb{Z}} q^{k^2}$ and
$\psi(q) = \sum_{k \ge 0} q^{k(k+1)/2}$.

## Sources

- Hartosh Singh Bal and Gaurav Bhatnagar, *Glaisher's Divisors and Infinite Products*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.1.6, Theorem 14 (`jis-2024-24.1.6-thm-14`).

articles.title: Overpartition formulas for a divisor sum with odd cofactors
articles.statement:
Let $n$ be a natural number.
Write $\sigma(m)$ for the sum of the positive divisors of $m$, $\sigma(m/2)$ for $\sigma$
evaluated at $m/2$ when $m$ is even and for $0$ when $m$ is odd, and $d_D(m)$ for the sum of the
divisors $d$ of $m$ with $m/d$ odd, with $\sigma(0) = d_D(0) = 0$; let $\bar p(m)$ be the number
of overpartitions of $m$. Then $2 d_D(n) = 2(\sigma(n) - \sigma(n/2)) = n\,\bar p(n) +
2\sum_{i \ge 1,\ i^2 \le n} (-1)^i (n - i^2)\,\bar p(n - i^2)$ and
$2\sum_{i=1}^{n} d_D(n-i)\,d_D(i) =
\sum_{i \ge 1,\ i^2 \le n} (-1)^{i+1} i^2 (n - i^2)\,\bar p(n - i^2)$.

## Sources

- Hartosh Singh Bal and Gaurav Bhatnagar, *Glaisher's Divisors and Infinite Products*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.1.6, Theorem 26 (`jis-2024-24.1.6-thm-26`).

articles.title: Overpartitions modulo $8$ and a convolution of divisor sums
articles.statement:
Let $\bar p(k)$ be the
number of overpartitions of $k$, and let $d_D(k)$ be the sum of the divisors $d$ of $k$ for which
$k/d$ is odd. Then $\bar p(4m+3) \equiv 0 \pmod 8$ for every natural number $m$ if and only if
$\sum_{i=1}^{4m-1} d_D(i)\,d_D(4m-i) \equiv 0 \pmod 4$ for every natural number $m$.

## Sources

- Hartosh Singh Bal and Gaurav Bhatnagar, *Glaisher's Divisors and Infinite Products*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.1.6, Theorem 30 (`jis-2024-24.1.6-thm-30`).

articles.title: Ramanujan's congruence modulo $5$ and a convolution of divisor sums
articles.statement:
Let $p(k)$ be the
number of partitions of $k$ and $\sigma(k)$ the sum of the positive divisors of $k$. Then
$p(5m+4) \equiv 0 \pmod 5$ for every natural number $m$ if and only if
$\sum_{i=1}^{5m} \sigma(i)\,\sigma(5m+1-i) \equiv 0 \pmod 5$ for every natural number $m$.

## Sources

- Hartosh Singh Bal and Gaurav Bhatnagar, *Glaisher's Divisors and Infinite Products*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.1.6, Theorem 28 (`jis-2024-24.1.6-thm-28`).

articles.title: Power recursion lemma for positive exponents
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field of characteristic zero,
let $A \in K[[X]]$ be a formal power series, and let $u$ and $v$ be positive integers. Write
$a_u(k)$ and $a_v(k)$ for the coefficients of $X^k$ in $A^u$ and $A^v$. Then for every natural
number $n$,

$$\sum_{k=0}^{n} \left(n - \left(\frac{u}{v} + 1\right) k\right) a_u(n-k)\, a_v(k) = 0.$$

## Sources

- Hartosh Singh Bal and Gaurav Bhatnagar, *Glaisher's Divisors and Infinite Products*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.1.6, Lemma 17 (`jis-2024-24.1.6-lem-17`).

articles.title: Power recursion lemma for nonzero integer exponents
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field of characteristic
zero, let $A$ be an invertible formal power series in $K[[X]]$, and let $u$ and $v$ be nonzero
integers. Write $a_u(k)$ and $a_v(k)$ for the coefficients of $X^k$ in $A^u$ and $A^v$. Then for
every natural number $n$,

$$\sum_{k=0}^{n} \left(n - \left(\frac{u}{v} + 1\right) k\right) a_u(n-k)\, a_v(k) = 0.$$

Invertibility of $A$ is assumed so that the negative powers $A^u$, $A^v$ make sense.

## Sources

- Hartosh Singh Bal and Gaurav Bhatnagar, *Glaisher's Divisors and Infinite Products*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.1.6, Lemma 17 (`jis-2024-24.1.6-lem-17`).

articles.title: Series-divisors add under multiplication
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $A$, $B$
be formal power series over $R$ with coefficients $a(n)$, $b(n)$. Suppose $s_A, s_B$ are maps
$\mathbb{N} \to R$ with $n\,a(n) = \sum_{i=1}^{n} s_A(i)\,a(n-i)$ and
$n\,b(n) = \sum_{i=1}^{n} s_B(i)\,b(n-i)$ for every $n \ge 0$ (that is, $s_A$ and $s_B$ are
series-divisors of $A$ and $B$). Then, writing $c(n)$ for the coefficients of $AB$,
$n\,c(n) = \sum_{i=1}^{n} \bigl(s_A(i) + s_B(i)\bigr)\,c(n-i)$ for every $n \ge 0$, so $s_A + s_B$
is a series-divisor of $AB$.

## Sources

- Hartosh Singh Bal and Gaurav Bhatnagar, *Glaisher's Divisors and Infinite Products*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.1.6, Lemma 2 (`jis-2024-24.1.6-lem-2`).

articles.title: Calculus of series-divisors
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $A$ be a formal power
series over $R$, write $[q^k]F$ for the coefficient of $q^k$ in a power series $F$, and let
$s : \mathbb{N} \to R$ satisfy $n\,[q^n]A = \sum_{i=1}^{n} s(i)\,[q^{n-i}]A$ for every $n \ge 0$
(that is, $s$ is a series-divisor of $A$). Then the following hold for every $n \ge 0$:
(a) for every power series $B$ over $R$ with $AB = 1$,
$n\,[q^n]B = \sum_{i=1}^{n} \bigl(-s(i)\bigr)\,[q^{n-i}]B$;
(b) $n\,[q^n]A(-q) = \sum_{i=1}^{n} (-1)^i s(i)\,[q^{n-i}]A(-q)$;
(c) for every integer $m \ge 1$, $n\,[q^n]A(q^m) = \sum_{i=1}^{n} t_m(i)\,[q^{n-i}]A(q^m)$,
where $t_m(i) = m\,s(i/m)$ if $m \mid i$ and $t_m(i) = 0$ otherwise;
(d) for every integer $m \ge 0$, $n\,[q^n]A^m = \sum_{i=1}^{n} m\,s(i)\,[q^{n-i}]A^m$.

## Sources

- Hartosh Singh Bal and Gaurav Bhatnagar, *Glaisher's Divisors and Infinite Products*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.1.6, Proposition 3 (`jis-2024-24.1.6-prop-3`).

articles.title: Convolution identities for the series-divisor of an invertible series
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a
commutative ring and let $A$, $B$ be formal power series over $R$ with coefficients $a(k)$,
$b(k)$ and $AB = 1$. Let $s : \mathbb{N} \to R$ satisfy $s(0) = 0$ and
$k\,a(k) = \sum_{i=1}^{k} s(i)\,a(k-i)$ for every $k \ge 0$ (that is, $s$ is a series-divisor
of $A$). Then for every $n \ge 0$,

$$s(n) = \sum_{i=0}^{n} (n-i)\,a(n-i)\,b(i)$$

and

$$\sum_{i=1}^{n} s(n-i)\,s(i) = -\sum_{i=1}^{n} i\,(n-i)\,a(n-i)\,b(i).$$

## Sources

- Hartosh Singh Bal and Gaurav Bhatnagar, *Glaisher's Divisors and Infinite Products*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.1.6, Lemma 25 (`jis-2024-24.1.6-lem-25`).

articles.title: Coefficient recursion for powers of a power series
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let
$A$ be a formal power series over $R$ with coefficients $a(k)$, and let $s : \mathbb{N} \to R$
satisfy $k\,a(k) = \sum_{i=1}^{k} s(i)\,a(k-i)$ for every $k \ge 0$ (that is, $s$ is a
series-divisor of $A$). For natural numbers $m$ and $k$, write $a_m(k)$ for the coefficient of
$q^k$ in $A^m$. Then for all natural numbers $m$ and $n$,
$n\,a_m(n) = m \sum_{j=1}^{n} s(j)\,a_m(n-j)$.

## Sources

- in Corollary 4 the printed summand `σ^A(i)` is read as `σ^A(j)` (the summation index).
- Hartosh Singh Bal and Gaurav Bhatnagar, *Glaisher's Divisors and Infinite Products*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.1.6, Corollary 4 (`jis-2024-24.1.6-cor-4`).

articles.title: A congruence modulo 5 for divisor sums over triangular shifts
articles.statement:
Let $\sigma$ be the
sum-of-divisors function, with $\sigma(r) = 0$ for $r \le 0$. For every integer $n \ge 1$, the sum
$\sum_{j=0}^{n} \sigma\bigl(2n + 1 - j(j+1)\bigr)$ is congruent to $1$ modulo $5$ if
$n = 5k(k+1)/2$ for some integer $k \ge 0$, and to $0$ modulo $5$ otherwise.

## Sources

- Hartosh Singh Bal and Gaurav Bhatnagar, *Glaisher's Divisors and Infinite Products*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.1.6, Theorem 23 (`jis-2024-24.1.6-thm-23`).

articles.title: Recurrences for sums of squares and sums of triangular numbers
articles.statement:
Let $m \ge 1$ be an
integer. For $n \ge 0$, let $r_m(n)$ be the number of $x \in \mathbb{Z}^m$ with
$x_1^2 + \dots + x_m^2 = n$, and let $t_m(n)$ be the number of $x \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}^m$ with
$\sum_{i=1}^{m} x_i(x_i+1)/2 = n$. Let $\sigma$ be the sum-of-divisors function, and set
$\sigma(j/2) = 0$ when $j$ is odd. Then for every $n \ge 0$,

$$n\,r_m(n) = m \sum_{j=1}^{n} 2(-1)^{j+1}\bigl(\sigma(j) - \sigma(j/2)\bigr)\,r_m(n-j)$$

and

$$n\,t_m(n) = m \sum_{j=1}^{n} \bigl(\sigma(j) - 4\sigma(j/2)\bigr)\,t_m(n-j).$$

## Sources

- Hartosh Singh Bal and Gaurav Bhatnagar, *Glaisher's Divisors and Infinite Products*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.1.6, Theorem 11 (`jis-2024-24.1.6-thm-11`).

articles.title: Eventual hyperbolicity for colored partitions
articles.statement:
Let $r \ge 1$ and $d \ge 1$ be integers. For
$m \in \mathbb{N}$ let

$$
C_r(m) = \sum_{m_1 + \dots + m_r = m} p(m_1) \cdots p(m_r)
$$

be the number of $r$-colored partitions of $m$, where the sum runs over all $r$-tuples of natural
numbers with sum $m$ and $p$ is the partition function. Then for all sufficiently large $n$ the
Jensen polynomial $J^{d,n}(X) = \sum_{j=0}^{d} \binom{d}{j} C_r(n + j) X^j$ is hyperbolic: the
number of its real roots, counted with multiplicity, equals its degree.

In the source, $C_r(n)$ is the coefficient of $q^{tn}$ in $1/(q^t; q^t)_\infty^r$ for any
$t \ge 1$; the source also proves a Hermite-limit statement and higher order Turán inequalities,
which are not part of this statement.

## Sources

- Jashan Bal, Fern Haraldson, Joshua Males and Ian Thompson, *Jensen Polynomials Associated with Wright's Circle Method: Hyperbolicity and Turán Inequalities*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A36, Theorem 3, part 1.

articles.title: Hyperbolicity of Jensen polynomials from a log-ratio expansion
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$, $A$ and
$\delta$ be sequences of positive real numbers indexed by $n \in \mathbb{N}$ with
$\delta(n) \to 0$, let $d \ge 1$ be an integer, and for $3 \le j \le d$ let $g_j$ be a real
sequence with $g_j(n) = o(\delta(n)^j)$ as $n \to \infty$. Suppose that for every natural number
$k \le d$,

$$
\log \frac{\alpha(n + k)}{\alpha(n)} = A(n) k - \delta(n)^2 k^2 + \sum_{j=3}^{d} g_j(n) k^j +
o(\delta(n)^d)
$$

as $n \to \infty$. Then for all sufficiently large $n$ the Jensen polynomial
$J_\alpha^{d,n}(X) = \sum_{j=0}^{d} \binom{d}{j} \alpha(n + j) X^j$ is hyperbolic: the number of
its real roots, counted with multiplicity, equals its degree.

The source also proves that suitably renormalized Jensen polynomials converge to the Hermite
polynomials; that conclusion is not part of this statement.

## Sources

- Jashan Bal, Fern Haraldson, Joshua Males and Ian Thompson, *Jensen Polynomials Associated with Wright's Circle Method: Hyperbolicity and Turán Inequalities*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A36, Theorem 5, quoted there from Griffin, Ono, Rolen and Zagier.

articles.title: Eventual hyperbolicity for partitions into parts $\equiv a \pmod{p}$
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime,
let $a$ be an integer with $1 \le a < p$, and let $d \ge 1$ be an integer. For $m \in \mathbb{N}$
let $b_{a,p}(m)$ be the number of partitions of $m$ all of whose parts are congruent to $a$
modulo $p$. Then for all sufficiently large $n$ the Jensen polynomial
$J^{d,n}(X) = \sum_{j=0}^{d} \binom{d}{j} b_{a,p}(n + j) X^j$ is hyperbolic: the number of its
real roots, counted with multiplicity, equals its degree.

In the source, $b_{a,p}(n)$ is the coefficient of $q^n$ in $1/(q^a; q^p)_\infty$, and the case
$a = 0$ is also admitted there, although $(1; q^p)_\infty = 0$; the source also gives an asymptotic
formula, a Hermite-limit statement and higher order Turán inequalities, which are not part of
this statement.

## Sources

- Jashan Bal, Fern Haraldson, Joshua Males and Ian Thompson, *Jensen Polynomials Associated with Wright's Circle Method: Hyperbolicity and Turán Inequalities*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A36, Theorem 4, part 2.

articles.title: An integral formula for $\log \Gamma(1/N)$
articles.statement:
For every real number $N > 0$,

$$
\int_0^\infty \left( \frac{e^{-x}}{x \left(1 - e^{-N x}\right)} - \frac{1}{N x^2} -
\left( \frac{1}{2} - \frac{1}{N} \right) \frac{e^{-x}}{x} \right) dx =
\log \Gamma\left( \frac{1}{N} \right) + \left( \frac{1}{2} - \frac{1}{N} \right) \log \frac{1}{N} -
\frac{1}{2} \log (2\pi).
$$

## Sources

- Jashan Bal, Fern Haraldson, Joshua Males and Ian Thompson, *Jensen Polynomials Associated with Wright's Circle Method: Hyperbolicity and Turán Inequalities*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A36, Lemma 2.

articles.title: A twisted sum of digamma values
articles.statement:
Let $p$ and $k$ be natural numbers with $1 \le k < p$,
and let $\psi = \Gamma'/\Gamma$ be the digamma function. Then

$$
\sum_{\alpha=1}^{p} e^{2\pi i k \alpha / p} \, \psi\left( \frac{\alpha}{p} \right) =
p \operatorname{Log}\left( 1 - e^{2\pi i k / p} \right),
$$

where $\operatorname{Log}$ is the principal branch of the complex logarithm.

## Sources

- Jashan Bal, Fern Haraldson, Joshua Males and Ian Thompson, *Jensen Polynomials Associated with Wright's Circle Method: Hyperbolicity and Turán Inequalities*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A36, Lemma 3.

articles.title: Jacobi's identity for the cube of Euler's product
articles.statement:
For every complex number $q$ with
$|q| < 1$, the series $\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} (-1)^n (2n+1) q^{n(n+1)/2}$ converges
unconditionally to $(q;q)_\infty^3$, the cube of the infinite q-Pochhammer symbol
$(q;q)_\infty = \prod_{n=0}^{\infty} (1 - q^{n+1})$.

## Sources

- Robson da Silva and James A. Sellers, "Parity Considerations for the Mex-Related Partition Functions of Andrews and Newman", <https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL23/Sellers/sellers52.tex>, lines 150-161 (equation `Jacobi` of the lemma; Eq. (1.3.24) of Berndt).

articles.title: Convergence of the product in Andrews' triple product identity
articles.statement:
Let $q$ be a complex
number with $|q| < 1$, and let $k$ and $i$ be natural numbers with $0 < i \le k$. Then the infinite
product

$$\prod_{n=0}^{\infty} \left(1 - q^{(2k+1)(n+1)}\right) \left(1 - q^{(2k+1)n + i}\right)
\left(1 - q^{(2k+1)(n+1) - i}\right)$$

is multipliable: its products over finite sets of indices converge in $\mathbb{C}$
(unconditional convergence, where the limit is not required to be nonzero).

articles.title: Convergence of the series in Andrews' triple product identity
articles.statement:
Let $q$ be a complex
number with $|q| < 1$, and let $k$ and $i$ be natural numbers with $i \le k$. Then the bilateral
series

$$\sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} (-1)^n q^{(2k+1)n(n+1)/2 - in}$$

is summable over $\mathbb{Z}$.

articles.title: Andrews' form of the Jacobi triple product identity
articles.statement:
Let $q$ be a complex number with
$|q| < 1$, and let $k$ and $i$ be natural numbers with $0 < i \le k$. Then

$$\sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} (-1)^n q^{(2k+1)n(n+1)/2 - in} =
\prod_{n=0}^{\infty} \left(1 - q^{(2k+1)(n+1)}\right) \left(1 - q^{(2k+1)n + i}\right)
\left(1 - q^{(2k+1)(n+1) - i}\right).$$

## Sources

- Aritram Dhar, Avi Mukhopadhyay, and Rishabh Sarma, "Generalization of the Extended Minimal Excludant of Andrews and Newman," Journal of Integer Sequences 26 (2023), Article 23.3.7, Theorem (Andrews, An98 p. 22, label JTP1), lines 459–462, https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL26/Sarma/sarma5.tex

articles.title: Symmetry of the Jacobi theta product under $x \mapsto q/x$
articles.statement:
Write
$(a; q)_\infty = \prod_{n \ge 0} (1 - a q^n)$ for the infinite $q$-Pochhammer symbol and
$j(x; q) = (x; q)_\infty \, (q/x; q)_\infty \, (q; q)_\infty$ for the product-form Jacobi theta
function. For all complex numbers $x$ and $q$ with $0 < |q| < 1$, $j(q/x; q) = j(x; q)$.
This includes $x = 0$, where $q/0$ is read as $0$.

articles.title: Jacobi theta product with vanishing first argument
articles.statement:
Write
$(a; q)_\infty = \prod_{n \ge 0} (1 - a q^n)$ for the infinite $q$-Pochhammer symbol and
$j(x; q) = (x; q)_\infty \, (q/x; q)_\infty \, (q; q)_\infty$ for the product-form Jacobi theta
function. For every complex number $q$ with $|q| < 1$, $j(0; q) = (q; q)_\infty$.
Here $q/0$ is read as $0$, so the first two factors of $j(0; q)$ both equal $(0; q)_\infty = 1$.

articles.title: Jacobi theta product at nome zero
articles.statement:
Write $(a; q)_\infty = \prod_{n \ge 0} (1 - a q^n)$
for the infinite $q$-Pochhammer symbol and
$j(x; q) = (x; q)_\infty \, (q/x; q)_\infty \, (q; q)_\infty$ for the product-form Jacobi theta
function, where $|q| < 1$. For every complex number $x$, $j(x; 0) = (x; 0)_\infty$: since
$0/x = 0$ (also for $x = 0$, reading $0/0$ as $0$), the last two factors of $j(x; 0)$ both equal
$(0; 0)_\infty = 1$.

articles.title: Jacobi theta function, product form
articles.statement:
For complex numbers $x$ and $q$ with $|q| < 1$,

$$j(x; q) = (x; q)_\infty \, (q/x; q)_\infty \, (q; q)_\infty,$$

where $(a; q)_\infty = \prod_{n \ge 0} (1 - a q^n)$ is the infinite $q$-Pochhammer symbol.
Division by zero is read as $q/0 = 0$, so $j(0; q) = (q; q)_\infty$.

articles.title: Jacobi triple product identity
articles.statement:
For complex numbers $z \ne 0$ and $q$ with $|q| < 1$,
the bilateral series $\sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} z^n q^{n^2}$ is summable, the family of factors
$(1 - q^{2n+2})(1 + z q^{2n+1})(1 + z^{-1} q^{2n+1})$, $n \ge 0$, is multipliable, and

$$\sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} z^n q^{n^2} =
\prod_{n \ge 0} (1 - q^{2n+2})(1 + z q^{2n+1})(1 + z^{-1} q^{2n+1}).$$

## Sources

- Aritram Dhar, Avi Mukhopadhyay, and Rishabh Sarma, "Generalization of the Extended Minimal Excludant of Andrews and Newman," Journal of Integer Sequences 26 (2023), Article 23.3.7, theorem at source lines 455-458 of <https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL26/Sarma/sarma5.tex>.

articles.title: The Lambert-type series $\hat L_m$
articles.statement:
For a complex number $q$ with $|q| < 1$ and an
integer $m \ge 1$, $\hat L_m(q) = \sum_{n \ge 1} q^{mn} / (1 + q^{2n})^m$, where the sum is
taken to be $0$ if the series is not summable.

## Sources

- Gerhold.

articles.title: Summability of the Lambert-type series $\hat L_m$
articles.statement:
For a complex number $q$ with
$|q| < 1$ and an integer $m \ge 1$, this predicate holds when the series
$\sum_{n \ge 1} q^{mn} / (1 + q^{2n})^m$ is summable in $\mathbb{C}$.

## Sources

- Gerhold.

articles.title: Terms of the Lambert-type series $\hat L_m$
articles.statement:
For a complex number $q$ with $|q| < 1$,
an integer $m \ge 1$ and a natural number $k$, the term of index $k$ is
$q^{m(k+1)} / (1 + q^{2(k+1)})^m$, that is, $q^{mn} / (1 + q^{2n})^m$ with $n = k + 1$.

## Sources

- Gerhold.

articles.title: The weighted Lambert series $f$
articles.statement:
For a complex number $q$ with $|q| < 1$, the weighted
Lambert series is $f(q) = \sum_{n \ge 1} n q^n / (1 - q^n)$.

articles.title: Terms of the power-weighted Lambert series $f_\mu$
articles.statement:
For a complex number $q$ with
$|q| < 1$, an integer $\mu \ge 1$ and a natural number $k$, the term of index $k$ is
$n^\mu q^n / (1 - q^n)$ with $n = k + 1$. These are the terms of the power-weighted Lambert series
$f_\mu(q) = \sum_{n \ge 1} n^\mu q^n / (1 - q^n)$.

articles.title: The power-weighted Lambert series $f_\mu$
articles.statement:
For a complex number $q$ with $|q| < 1$ and an
integer $\mu \ge 1$, the power-weighted Lambert series is
$f_\mu(q) = \sum_{n \ge 1} n^\mu q^n / (1 - q^n)$.

articles.title: Terms of the weighted Lambert series $f$
articles.statement:
For a complex number $q$ with $|q| < 1$ and a
natural number $k$, the term of index $k$ is $n q^n / (1 - q^n)$ with $n = k + 1$. These are the
terms of the weighted Lambert series $f(q) = \sum_{n \ge 1} n q^n / (1 - q^n)$.

articles.title: The weighted Lambert series $g$
articles.statement:
For a complex number $q$ with $|q| < 1$, the weighted
Lambert series is $g(q) = \sum_{n \ge 1} n q^n / (1 + q^n)$.

articles.title: Terms of the power-weighted Lambert series $g_\mu$
articles.statement:
For a complex number $q$ with
$|q| < 1$, an integer $\mu \ge 1$ and a natural number $k$, the term of index $k$ is
$n^\mu q^n / (1 + q^n)$ with $n = k + 1$. These are the terms of the power-weighted Lambert series
$g_\mu(q) = \sum_{n \ge 1} n^\mu q^n / (1 + q^n)$.

articles.title: The power-weighted Lambert series $g_\mu$
articles.statement:
For a complex number $q$ with $|q| < 1$ and an
integer $\mu \ge 1$, the power-weighted Lambert series is
$g_\mu(q) = \sum_{n \ge 1} n^\mu q^n / (1 + q^n)$.

articles.title: Terms of the weighted Lambert series $g$
articles.statement:
For a complex number $q$ with $|q| < 1$ and a
natural number $k$, the term of index $k$ is $n q^n / (1 + q^n)$ with $n = k + 1$. These are the
terms of the weighted Lambert series $g(q) = \sum_{n \ge 1} n q^n / (1 + q^n)$.

articles.title: Terms of the Lambert family $L_m$
articles.statement:
For a complex number $q$ with $|q| < 1$, an integer
$m \ge 1$ and a natural number $k$, the term of index $k$ is $q^{mn} / (1 - q^{2n})^m$ with
$n = k + 1$. These are the terms of $L_m(q) = \sum_{n \ge 1} q^{mn} / (1 - q^{2n})^m$.

articles.title: The Lambert family $L_m$
articles.statement:
For a complex number $q$ with $|q| < 1$ and an integer $m \ge 1$,
the Lambert family is $L_m(q) = \sum_{n \ge 1} q^{mn} / (1 - q^{2n})^m$.

articles.title: Lambert series summand
articles.statement:
For a complex number $q$ with $|q| < 1$ and a natural number $k$,
the $k$-th summand of the basic Lambert series is $q^{k+1} / (1 - q^{k+1})$, that is, the term
$q^n / (1 - q^n)$ with $n = k + 1$.

articles.title: Lambert series
articles.statement:
For a complex number $q$ with $|q| < 1$, the basic Lambert series is
$L(q) = \sum_{n \ge 1} q^n / (1 - q^n)$.

articles.title: The Lambert-type series $L_m^*$
articles.statement:
**The Lambert-type series $L_m^*$.** For a complex number $q$ with $|q| < 1$ and an integer
$m \ge 1$, $L_m^*(q) = \sum_{n \ge 1} q^{(2n-1)m} / (1 - q^{2n-1})^{2m}$, where the sum is taken
to be $0$ if the series is not summable.

## Sources

- Gerhold.

articles.title: Summability of the Lambert-type series $L_m^*$
articles.statement:
**Summability of the Lambert-type series $L_m^*$.** For a complex number $q$ with $|q| < 1$
and an integer $m \ge 1$, this predicate holds when the series
$\sum_{n \ge 1} q^{(2n-1)m} / (1 - q^{2n-1})^{2m}$ is summable in $\mathbb{C}$.

## Sources

- Gerhold.

articles.title: Terms of the Lambert-type series $L_m^*$
articles.statement:
**Terms of the Lambert-type series $L_m^*$.** For a complex number $q$ with $|q| < 1$, an
integer $m \ge 1$ and a natural number $k$, the term of index $k$ is
$q^{(2k+1)m} / (1 - q^{2k+1})^{2m}$, that is, $q^{(2n-1)m} / (1 - q^{2n-1})^{2m}$ with $n = k + 1$.

## Sources

- Gerhold.

articles.title: The Lambert-type series $\tilde L_m$
articles.statement:
For a complex number $q$ with $|q| < 1$ and an
integer $m \ge 1$, $\tilde L_m(q) = \sum_{n \ge 1} q^{(2n-1)m} / (1 + q^{2n-1})^{2m}$, where the
sum is taken to be $0$ if the series is not summable.

## Sources

- Gerhold.

articles.title: Summability of the Lambert-type series $\tilde L_m$
articles.statement:
For a complex number $q$ with
$|q| < 1$ and an integer $m \ge 1$, this predicate holds when the series
$\sum_{n \ge 1} q^{(2n-1)m} / (1 + q^{2n-1})^{2m}$ is summable in $\mathbb{C}$.

## Sources

- Gerhold.

articles.title: Terms of the Lambert-type series $\tilde L_m$
articles.statement:
For a complex number $q$ with $|q| < 1$,
an integer $m \ge 1$ and a natural number $k$, the term of index $k$ is
$q^{(2k+1)m} / (1 + q^{2k+1})^{2m}$, that is, $q^{(2n-1)m} / (1 + q^{2n-1})^{2m}$ with $n = k + 1$.

## Sources

- Gerhold.

articles.title: Constant term of the Euler products
articles.statement:
For every natural number $k \ge 1$, the integer power
series $f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$ has constant coefficient $1$.

## Sources

- S. Shivaprasada Nayaka, B. N. Dharmendra, and M. C. Mahesh Kumar, *Divisibility Properties for Overcubic Partition Triples*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A80, Section 1 (notation `E_k`); James A. Sellers, *Elementary Proofs of Congruences for POND and PEND Partitions*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.4.7, Section 2.

articles.title: Convergence of the infinite q-Pochhammer product
articles.statement:
For all complex numbers $a$ and $q$ with
$|q| < 1$, the infinite product $\prod_{n=0}^{\infty} (1 - a q^n)$ converges unconditionally to
the infinite q-Pochhammer symbol $(a;q)_\infty$: the products of the factors $1 - a q^n$ over
finite sets of indices $n$ tend to $(a;q)_\infty$.

No nonvanishing hypothesis is imposed, so the cases where some factor is zero (and the product
is $0$) are included.

## Sources

- `2607.10576:D01`, where the infinite product $(a;q)_\infty$ is used under $|q| < 1$.

articles.title: Pentagonal series expansion of the first Euler product
articles.statement:
The Euler product
$f_1 = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^m)$ equals the pentagonal series
$\sum_{j \in \mathbb{Z}} (-1)^j q^{j(3j-1)/2}$ as an integer power series.

## Sources

- James A. Sellers, *Elementary Proofs of Congruences for POND and PEND Partitions*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.4.7, Section 2.

articles.title: The Euler products of partition theory
articles.statement:
For a natural number $k$, the Euler product
$f_k = (q^k; q^k)_\infty = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$ is this infinite product in the ring of
integer power series in $q$, taken in the coefficientwise topology. It is used for $k \ge 1$.

## Sources

- James A. Sellers, *Elementary Proofs of Congruences for POND and PEND Partitions*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.4.7, Section 2.

articles.title: The q-Pochhammer symbol vanishes at a = 1 and q = 0
articles.statement:
The infinite q-Pochhammer symbol
satisfies $(1;0)_\infty = 0$, because its factor for $n = 0$ is $1 - 1 \cdot 0^0 = 0$ (with the
convention $0^0 = 1$).

articles.title: The raw q-Pochhammer product at a = 2 and q = 1 equals 1
articles.statement:
The raw infinite q-Pochhammer
product at $a = 2$ and $q = 1$ equals $1$.

Every factor $1 - 2 \cdot 1^n$ equals $-1$, so the finite partial products alternate between $-1$
and $1$ and the product does not converge; the value $1$ is the default that the unconditional
product takes in that case, not a limit of partial products. The q-Pochhammer symbol
$(a;q)_\infty$, which requires $|q| < 1$, excludes such arguments.

articles.title: Raw infinite q-Pochhammer product
articles.statement:
For complex numbers $a$ and $q$, the raw infinite
q-Pochhammer product is the unconditional infinite product $\prod_{n=0}^{\infty} (1 - a q^n)$,
defined for every $q$: when this product does not converge unconditionally (in particular for
most $q$ with $|q| \ge 1$), its value is $1$ by convention.

articles.title: The q-Pochhammer symbol with a = 0
articles.statement:
For every complex number $q$ with $|q| < 1$,
$(0;q)_\infty = 1$, since every factor $1 - 0 \cdot q^n$ equals $1$.

articles.title: Infinite q-Pochhammer symbol
articles.statement:
For complex numbers $a$ and $q$ with $|q| < 1$, the infinite
q-Pochhammer symbol is $(a;q)_\infty = \prod_{n=0}^{\infty} (1 - a q^n)$, the unconditional
infinite product of the factors $1 - a q^n$.

The hypothesis $|q| < 1$ is an argument of the definition, so the symbol cannot be applied to
$q$ outside the open unit disk.

## Sources

- `2607.10576:D01` / `2608.13818:D02` jointly define `(a;q)_∞ := ∏_{j=0}^{∞} (1 - a·q^j)` for complex `a, q` with `‖q‖ < 1`.

articles.title: Oddness of the Jacobi theta function $\theta_1$
articles.statement:
For all complex numbers $z$ and $\tau$
with $\operatorname{Im} \tau > 0$, the Jacobi theta function satisfies
$\theta_1(-z \mid \tau) = -\theta_1(z \mid \tau)$.

## Sources

- A. Vanitha, Nasser Abdo Saeed Bulkhali, and M. P. Chaudhary, *On a Ramanujan’s Continued Fraction of Order Sixteen and New Eisenstein Series Identities*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A16, Section 3, Equation (11).

articles.title: Raw Jacobi theta function $\theta_1$
articles.statement:
For complex numbers $z$ and $\tau$, the raw Jacobi
theta function is

$$\theta_1(z \mid \tau) = 2 \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} (-1)^n e^{\pi i \tau (2n+1)^2/4} \sin((2n+1) z)$$

when this series is summable, and $0$ otherwise. With $q = e^{2 \pi i \tau}$, the factor
$e^{\pi i \tau (2n+1)^2/4}$ is $q^{(2n+1)^2/8}$.

The value $0$ for a non-summable series is a convention; it occurs, for example, at $\tau = 0$
and $z = \pi/2$. The intended object is the Jacobi theta function on the upper half-plane
$\operatorname{Im} \tau > 0$, where the series converges for every $z$.

## Sources

- A. Vanitha, Nasser Abdo Saeed Bulkhali, and M. P. Chaudhary, *On a Ramanujan’s Continued Fraction of Order Sixteen and New Eisenstein Series Identities*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A16, Section 3, Equation (11).

articles.title: The Jacobi theta function $\theta_1$ vanishes at $z = 0$
articles.statement:
For every complex number $\tau$
with $\operatorname{Im} \tau > 0$, the Jacobi theta function satisfies $\theta_1(0 \mid \tau) = 0$.

## Sources

- A. Vanitha, Nasser Abdo Saeed Bulkhali, and M. P. Chaudhary, *On a Ramanujan’s Continued Fraction of Order Sixteen and New Eisenstein Series Identities*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A16, Section 3, Equation (11).

articles.title: Jacobi theta function $\theta_1$
articles.statement:
For complex numbers $z$ and $\tau$ with
$\operatorname{Im} \tau > 0$, the Jacobi theta function is

$$\theta_1(z \mid \tau) = 2 \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} (-1)^n e^{\pi i \tau (2n+1)^2/4} \sin((2n+1) z).$$

With $q = e^{2 \pi i \tau}$, the factor $e^{\pi i \tau (2n+1)^2/4}$ is $q^{(2n+1)^2/8}$.

On the upper half-plane $\operatorname{Im} \tau > 0$ the series converges for every $z$.

## Sources

- A. Vanitha, Nasser Abdo Saeed Bulkhali, and M. P. Chaudhary, *On a Ramanujan’s Continued Fraction of Order Sixteen and New Eisenstein Series Identities*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A16, Section 3, Equation (11).

articles.title: Odd Lambert series for Ramanujan's continued fractions of order sixteen
articles.statement:
Write
$(a; q)_\infty = \prod_{n \ge 0} (1 - a q^n)$ and $(a, b; q)_\infty = (a; q)_\infty (b; q)_\infty$.
For a complex number $q$ with $|q| < 1$, put
$S(a, b) = \sum_{k \ge 0} (q^{a(2k+1)} + q^{b(2k+1)}) / (1 - q^{16(2k+1)})$, a sum over the odd
multiples $n = 2k + 1$, and
$E = q^4 (q^{32}; q^{32})_\infty^4 / (q^{16}; q^{16})_\infty^2$,
$I_1 = q (q^6, q^{26}; q^{32})_\infty / (q^{10}, q^{22}; q^{32})_\infty$ and
$I_2 = q^3 (q^2, q^{30}; q^{32})_\infty / (q^{14}, q^{18}; q^{32})_\infty$. Then
$S(3, 5) - S(11, 13) = E (I_1 + 1/I_1)$ and $S(1, 7) - S(9, 15) = E (I_2 + 1/I_2)$.
At $q = 0$, where $I_1 = I_2 = 0$, the quotients $1/I_1$ and $1/I_2$ are read as $0$ and both
sides of each identity are $0$.

Here $I_1$ and $I_2$ are $I_1(q^2)$ and $I_2(q^2)$ for Ramanujan's continued fractions of order
sixteen $I_1(q) = q^{1/2} (q^3, q^{13}; q^{16})_\infty / (q^5, q^{11}; q^{16})_\infty$ and
$I_2(q) = q^{3/2} (q, q^{15}; q^{16})_\infty / (q^7, q^9; q^{16})_\infty$, and $E$ is the eta
quotient $\eta^4(32\tau) / \eta^2(16\tau)$ for $q = e^{2 \pi i \tau}$, where
$\eta(\tau) = q^{1/24} (q; q)_\infty$.

## Sources

- A. Vanitha, Nasser Abdo Saeed Bulkhali, and M. P. Chaudhary, *On a Ramanujan’s Continued Fraction of Order Sixteen and New Eisenstein Series Identities*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A16, Theorem 2, Equations (54)-(55).

articles.title: Lambert series of order sixteen twisted by the Legendre symbol modulo $3$
articles.statement:
Write
$(a; q)_\infty = \prod_{n \ge 0} (1 - a q^n)$,
$(a_1, \dots, a_k; q)_\infty = (a_1; q)_\infty \cdots (a_k; q)_\infty$ and
$f_k = (q^k; q^k)_\infty$, and let $\left(\frac{n}{3}\right)$ be the Legendre symbol modulo $3$.
For every complex number $q$ with $|q| < 1$,

$$\sum_{n \ge 1} \left(\frac{n}{3}\right) \frac{q^n - q^{7n} - q^{9n} + q^{15n}}{1 - q^{16n}} =
\frac{q f_8^2 f_{48} (q^6, q^{10}; q^{16})_\infty (q, q^7, q^9, q^{15}; q^{16})_\infty}
{f_{16} (q^3, q^{21}, q^{27}, q^{45}; q^{48})_\infty}$$

and

$$\sum_{n \ge 1} \left(\frac{n}{3}\right) \frac{q^{3n} - q^{5n} - q^{11n} + q^{13n}}{1 - q^{16n}} =
\frac{q^3 f_8^2 f_{48} (q^2, q^{14}; q^{16})_\infty (q^3, q^5, q^{11}, q^{13}; q^{16})_\infty}
{f_{16} (q^9, q^{15}, q^{33}, q^{39}; q^{48})_\infty}.$$

## Sources

- A. Vanitha, Nasser Abdo Saeed Bulkhali, and M. P. Chaudhary, *On a Ramanujan’s Continued Fraction of Order Sixteen and New Eisenstein Series Identities*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A16, Theorem 4, Equations (64)-(65).

articles.title: Sine Lambert series of order sixteen as quotients of theta functions
articles.statement:
Let $\tau$ and $z$
be complex numbers with $\operatorname{Im} \tau > 0$ and
$|\operatorname{Im} z| < \pi \operatorname{Im} \tau$, let $q = e^{2 \pi i \tau}$, write
$\theta(w) = \theta_1(w \mid 16\tau)$ for the Jacobi theta function $\theta_1$, and let $\theta'$
be the derivative of $\theta$. Then

$$\sum_{n \ge 1} \frac{q^n - q^{7n} - q^{9n} + q^{15n}}{1 - q^{16n}} \sin 2nz =
\frac{-\theta'(0) \theta(8\pi\tau) \theta(6\pi\tau) \theta(2z)}
{4 \theta(z + \pi\tau) \theta(z - \pi\tau) \theta(z + 7\pi\tau) \theta(z - 7\pi\tau)}$$

and

$$\sum_{n \ge 1} \frac{q^{3n} - q^{5n} - q^{11n} + q^{13n}}{1 - q^{16n}} \sin 2nz =
\frac{-\theta'(0) \theta(2\pi\tau) \theta(8\pi\tau) \theta(2z)}
{4 \theta(z + 3\pi\tau) \theta(z - 3\pi\tau) \theta(z + 5\pi\tau) \theta(z - 5\pi\tau)}.$$

Under these hypotheses the series converge and the denominators do not vanish.

## Sources

- A. Vanitha, Nasser Abdo Saeed Bulkhali, and M. P. Chaudhary, *On a Ramanujan’s Continued Fraction of Order Sixteen and New Eisenstein Series Identities*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A16, Lemma 2 of Section 5, Equations (59)-(60).

articles.title: Weighted Lambert series for the continued fractions of order sixteen
articles.statement:
Write
$(a; q)_\infty = \prod_{n \ge 0} (1 - a q^n)$,
$(a_1, \dots, a_k; q)_\infty = (a_1; q)_\infty \cdots (a_k; q)_\infty$ and
$f_k = (q^k; q^k)_\infty$. For every complex number $q$ with $|q| < 1$,

$$\sum_{n \ge 1} n \frac{q^n - q^{7n} - q^{9n} + q^{15n}}{1 - q^{16n}} =
\frac{q f_{16}^2 f_8^2 (q^6, q^{10}; q^{16})_\infty}{(q, q^7, q^9, q^{15}; q^{16})_\infty^2}$$

and

$$\sum_{n \ge 1} n \frac{q^{3n} - q^{5n} - q^{11n} + q^{13n}}{1 - q^{16n}} =
\frac{q^3 f_{16}^2 f_8^2 (q^2, q^{14}; q^{16})_\infty}
{(q^3, q^5, q^{11}, q^{13}; q^{16})_\infty^2}.$$

## Sources

- A. Vanitha, Nasser Abdo Saeed Bulkhali, and M. P. Chaudhary, *On a Ramanujan’s Continued Fraction of Order Sixteen and New Eisenstein Series Identities*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A16, Theorem 3, Equations (62)-(63).

articles.title: Product forms of Ramanujan's theta functions $\psi$, $f$ and $\chi$
articles.statement:
Write
$(a; q)_\infty = \prod_{n \ge 0} (1 - a q^n)$ and $f_k = (q^k; q^k)_\infty$, and let
$f(a, b) = \sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} a^{n(n+1)/2} b^{n(n-1)/2}$ be Ramanujan's general theta
function. For every complex number $q$ with $|q| < 1$,
$f(q, q^3) = f_2^2 / f_1$, $f(q, -q^2) = f_2^3 / (f_1 f_4)$, $(-q; q^2)_\infty = f_2^2 / (f_1 f_4)$
and $(q; q^2)_\infty = f_1 / f_2$.

In Ramanujan's notation (Berndt, Part III, Chapter 16), with $\psi(q) = f(q, q^3)$,
$f(q) = f(q, -q^2)$ and $\chi(q) = (-q; q^2)_\infty$, these read $\psi(q) = f_2^2 / f_1$,
$f(q) = f_2^3 / (f_1 f_4)$, $\chi(q) = f_2^2 / (f_1 f_4)$ and $\chi(-q) = f_1 / f_2$.

## Sources

- A. Vanitha, Nasser Abdo Saeed Bulkhali, and M. P. Chaudhary, *On a Ramanujan’s Continued Fraction of Order Sixteen and New Eisenstein Series Identities*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A16, Lemma 1.

articles.title: Ramanujan's Entry 30 (i)–(iii) for the general theta function
articles.statement:
Let
$f(a, b) = \sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} a^{n(n+1)/2} b^{n(n-1)/2}$ be Ramanujan's general theta
function and $\psi(q) = f(q, q^3)$. For all complex numbers $a$ and $b$ with $|ab| < 1$,
$f(a, ab^2) f(b, a^2 b) = f(a, b) \psi(ab)$ and $f(a, b) + f(-a, -b) = 2 f(a^3 b, a b^3)$, and if
moreover $a \ne 0$, then $f(a, b) - f(-a, -b) = 2a f(b/a, a^5 b^3)$.

## Sources

- A. Vanitha, Nasser Abdo Saeed Bulkhali, and M. P. Chaudhary, *On a Ramanujan’s Continued Fraction of Order Sixteen and New Eisenstein Series Identities*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A16, Lemma 1 record, quoting Berndt, Part III, Entry 30 (i)-(iii).

articles.title: Ramanujan's function $k$ at $q$ and $q^2$ as an eta quotient
articles.statement:
For every complex number
$q$ with $0 < |q| < 1$, Ramanujan's function $k$ satisfies

$$
\frac{k(q)}{k(q^2)} - \frac{k(q^2)}{k(q)} =
\frac{(q;q)_\infty (q^5;q^5)_\infty^3}{q\,(q^{10};q^{10})_\infty^4},
$$

where $(a;x)_\infty = \prod_{n \ge 0} (1 - a x^n)$ is the infinite q-Pochhammer product.

## Sources

- Russelle Guadalupe, *New Proofs of Certain Theta Function Identities via Ramanujan's Function*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A41, Lemma 3.

articles.title: Eta-quotient expressions for Ramanujan's function $k$
articles.statement:
Let $q$ be a complex number with
$0 < |q| < 1$, write $f_m = (q^m;q^m)_\infty = \prod_{n \ge 1} (1 - q^{mn})$ for $m \ge 1$, and let
$k = k(q)$ be the value of Ramanujan's function. Then

$$
\frac{f_2 f_5^5}{q f_1 f_{10}^5} = \frac{1}{k} - k, \qquad
\frac{f_2^4 f_5^2}{q f_1^2 f_{10}^4} = \frac{1}{k} + 1 - k, \qquad
\frac{f_1^3 f_5}{q f_2 f_{10}^3} = \frac{1}{k} - 4 - k.
$$

## Sources

- Russelle Guadalupe, *New Proofs of Certain Theta Function Identities via Ramanujan's Function*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A41, Lemma 2, Equations (5)-(7).

articles.title: Modular equation of degree 2 for Ramanujan's function $k$
articles.statement:
For every complex number $q$
with $|q| < 1$, the values $X = k(q)$ and $Y = k(q^2)$ of Ramanujan's function satisfy
$X^2 - Y + 2XY + X^2 Y + Y^2 = 0$.

## Sources

- Russelle Guadalupe, *New Proofs of Certain Theta Function Identities via Ramanujan's Function*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A41, Theorem 4.

articles.title: Ramanujan's function $k$ vanishes at $0$
articles.statement:
Ramanujan's function satisfies $k(0) = 0$.

## Sources

- Russelle Guadalupe, *New Proofs of Certain Theta Function Identities via Ramanujan's Function*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A41, Section 1 (product representation of `k(q)`).

articles.title: Ramanujan's function $k(q)$
articles.statement:
For a complex number $q$, Ramanujan's function is

$$
k(q) = \frac{q\,(q;q^{10})_\infty (q^2;q^{10})_\infty (q^8;q^{10})_\infty (q^9;q^{10})_\infty}
{(q^3;q^{10})_\infty (q^4;q^{10})_\infty (q^6;q^{10})_\infty (q^7;q^{10})_\infty},
$$

where $(a;x)_\infty$ is the raw infinite q-Pochhammer product $\prod_{n \ge 0} (1 - a x^n)$
(equal to $1$ by convention when this product does not converge unconditionally), and a
quotient by $0$ is read as $0$.

For $|q| < 1$ this is the product representation of $k(q) = r(q)\,r(q^2)^2$, where $r$ is the
Rogers–Ramanujan continued fraction.

## Sources

- Russelle Guadalupe, *New Proofs of Certain Theta Function Identities via Ramanujan's Function*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A41, Section 1 (product representation of `k(q)`).

articles.title: Ramanujan's level-10 theta function identities
articles.statement:
For complex $x$ with $|x| < 1$, let
$\varphi(x) = \sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} x^{n^2}$, $\psi(x) = \sum_{n \ge 0} x^{n(n+1)/2}$ and
$f(-x) = \prod_{n \ge 1} (1 - x^n)$, so that $f(x) = \prod_{n \ge 1} (1 - (-x)^n)$. Then for
every complex number $q$ with $|q| < 1$,

$$
\frac{\varphi(q)^5}{\varphi(q^5)} + \frac{\varphi(-q^2)^5}{\varphi(-q^{10})} +
2\,\frac{f(q)^5}{f(q^5)} = 4\,\frac{\psi(q)^5}{\psi(q^5)}
$$

and

$$
\varphi(q)^2 \varphi(q^5)^2 - \varphi(-q)^2 \varphi(-q^5)^2 - 16 q^3 \psi(q^2)^2 \psi(q^{10})^2 =
8 q\, f(-q^2)^2 f(-q^{10})^2.
$$

## Sources

- Russelle Guadalupe, *New Proofs of Certain Theta Function Identities via Ramanujan's Function*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A41, Theorem 1, Equations (3) and (4).

articles.title: Ramanujan's theta series diverges at $a = b = 1$
articles.statement:
The series
$\sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} a^{n(n+1)/2} b^{n(n-1)/2}$ of Ramanujan's general theta function is
not summable at $a = b = 1$, since every one of its terms equals $1$.

articles.title: The raw Ramanujan theta sum vanishes at $a = b = 1$
articles.statement:
The raw Ramanujan theta sum
$\sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} a^{n(n+1)/2} b^{n(n-1)/2}$, which is assigned the value $0$ whenever
the series is not summable, equals $0$ at $a = b = 1$, because there every term equals $1$ and
the series is not summable.

articles.title: Raw Ramanujan theta sum
articles.statement:
For complex numbers $a$ and $b$, the raw Ramanujan theta sum is
$\sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} a^{n(n+1)/2} b^{n(n-1)/2}$ when this series is summable, and $0$
otherwise.

The value $0$ for a non-summable series is a convention. Ramanujan's general theta function,
which requires the series to be summable, is the intended object.

articles.title: Absolute convergence of Ramanujan's general theta series
articles.statement:
For all complex numbers $a$
and $b$ with $|ab| < 1$, the series $\sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} |a^{n(n+1)/2} b^{n(n-1)/2}|$ of
the absolute values of the terms of Ramanujan's general theta function converges.

## Sources

- arXiv:2607.26471, `Oliver_identities.tex` ll. 127-130.

articles.title: Summand of Ramanujan's general theta function
articles.statement:
For complex numbers $a$, $b$ and an
integer $n$, this is the term $a^{n(n+1)/2} b^{n(n-1)/2}$ of index $n$ in Ramanujan's general
theta function $f(a,b) = \sum_{k \in \mathbb{Z}} a^{k(k+1)/2} b^{k(k-1)/2}$.

Both exponents $n(n+1)/2$ and $n(n-1)/2$ are nonnegative integers for every integer $n$, so
the term is a product of ordinary powers with natural-number exponents.

## Sources

- the common definition in arXiv:2305.14988, arXiv:2309.06689, arXiv:2312.15513, arXiv:2502.17312, and arXiv:2607.26471.

articles.title: Ramanujan's general theta function
articles.statement:
For complex numbers $a$ and $b$ such that the series
$\sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} a^{n(n+1)/2} b^{n(n-1)/2}$ is summable, Ramanujan's general theta
function is its sum $f(a,b) = \sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} a^{n(n+1)/2} b^{n(n-1)/2}$.

articles.title: The Rogers–Ramanujan continued fraction vanishes at zero
articles.statement:
The real Rogers–Ramanujan
continued fraction $R$ satisfies $R(0) = 0$.

## Sources

- S. E. Gladun and M. P. Chaudhary, *Connecting Ramanujan's Theta Functions, the Rogers-Ramanujan Continued Fraction, and the Golden Ratio*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A43, Section 1 (the Rogers-Ramanujan continued fraction formula).

articles.title: The real Rogers–Ramanujan continued fraction
articles.statement:
For a real number $x$,

$$
R(x) = x^{1/5} \prod_{n \ge 0}
\frac{(1 - x^{5n+1})(1 - x^{5n+4})}{(1 - x^{5n+2})(1 - x^{5n+3})},
$$

where $x^{1/5}$ is the real power function (the nonnegative fifth root for $x \ge 0$, and
$|x|^{1/5} \cos(\pi/5)$ for $x < 0$), a factor whose denominator is $0$ is read as $0$, and the
infinite product is taken to be $1$ when it does not converge unconditionally. For $0 \le x < 1$
this is the product formula
$R(x) = x^{1/5} (x; x^5)_\infty (x^4; x^5)_\infty / ((x^2; x^5)_\infty (x^3; x^5)_\infty)$ of the
Rogers–Ramanujan continued fraction, where $(c; q)_\infty = \prod_{m \ge 0} (1 - c q^m)$.

## Sources

- S. E. Gladun and M. P. Chaudhary, *Connecting Ramanujan's Theta Functions, the Rogers-Ramanujan Continued Fraction, and the Golden Ratio*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A43, Section 1 (the Rogers-Ramanujan continued fraction formula).

articles.title: Golden-ratio relation for the Rogers–Ramanujan continued fraction
articles.statement:
Let $t > 0$, and put
$q = e^{-\pi t}$ and $q' = e^{-\pi/t}$. Let $\psi(x) = \sum_{n \ge 0} x^{n(n+1)/2}$ and
$E(x) = (x; x)_\infty = \prod_{n \ge 1} (1 - x^n)$, and set
$\tau(q) = \psi(q) - 5q^3 \psi(q^{25})$, $\rho(q) = \psi(q)^2 - 5q\,\psi(q^5)^2$ and

$$
g(0) = \frac{16\psi(q)^5 - \tau(q)\bigl(\tau(q)^4 + 5\tau(q)^2\rho(q) +
5\rho(q)^2\bigr)}{5\psi(q^5)}.
$$

Let $\Phi = (\sqrt{5} + 1)/2$, let $R$ be the real Rogers–Ramanujan continued fraction, and put
$U = \bigl(R(q)\,R(q'^{4/5})\bigr)^{5/2}$ and $V = \bigl(R(q)/R(q'^{4/5})\bigr)^{5/2}$. Then

$$
\Bigl(\sqrt{\Phi} - \frac{1}{\sqrt{\Phi}}\Bigr)\Bigl(U + \frac{1}{U}\Bigr) +
\Bigl(\sqrt{\Phi} + \frac{1}{\sqrt{\Phi}}\Bigr)\Bigl(V - \frac{1}{V}\Bigr) =
\frac{g(0)}{\sqrt{q}\,\bigl(E(q)\,E(q^5)\bigr)^2}.
$$

This is Theorem 1 of the source on the imaginary axis $z = it$, where $q = e^{\pi i z}$ and
$q' = e^{\pi i z'}$ with $z z' = -1$.

## Sources

- S. E. Gladun and M. P. Chaudhary, *Connecting Ramanujan's Theta Functions, the Rogers-Ramanujan Continued Fraction, and the Golden Ratio*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A43, Theorem 1, Equation (3).

articles.title: Eta-quotient form of the Gladun–Chaudhary theta coefficient
articles.statement:
In the ring of integer
power series in $q$, let $\psi(q) = \sum_{m \ge 0} q^{m(m+1)/2}$ be the triangular theta series
and $E_k = (q^k; q^k)_\infty$ the Euler products, and set $\tau(q) = \psi(q) - 5q^3\psi(q^{25})$
and $\rho(q) = \psi(q)^2 - 5q\,\psi(q^5)^2$. Then

$$
\bigl(16\psi(q)^5 - \tau(q)\bigl(\tau(q)^4 + 5\tau(q)^2\rho(q) + 5\rho(q)^2\bigr)\bigr)E_5E_{25} =
5\psi(q^5)\bigl(E_5^6 + 20q\,E_1^4E_{25}^2 + 110q^2E_1^3E_{25}^3 + 350q^3E_1^2E_{25}^4 +
600q^4E_1E_{25}^5 + 625q^5E_{25}^6\bigr).
$$

This is Theorem 2 of the source, which writes
$g(0) = \bigl(16\psi(q)^5 - \tau(q)(\tau(q)^4 + 5\tau(q)^2\rho(q) + 5\rho(q)^2)\bigr)/(5\psi(q^5))$
as $E_5^5/E_{25} + 20q\,E_1^4E_{25}/E_5 + 110q^2E_1^3E_{25}^2/E_5 + 350q^3E_1^2E_{25}^3/E_5 +
600q^4E_1E_{25}^4/E_5 + 625q^5E_{25}^5/E_5$, multiplied through by $5\psi(q^5)E_5E_{25}$.

## Sources

- S. E. Gladun and M. P. Chaudhary, *Connecting Ramanujan's Theta Functions, the Rogers-Ramanujan Continued Fraction, and the Golden Ratio*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A43, Theorem 2.

articles.title: Eta-quotients of Ramanujan's theta functions
articles.statement:
Let $q$ be a complex number with
$|q| < 1$. Write $(a;q)_\infty = \prod_{n \ge 0} (1 - a q^n)$ and $f_k = (q^k;q^k)_\infty$, and
let $f(a,b) = \sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} a^{n(n+1)/2} b^{n(n-1)/2}$ be Ramanujan's theta function.
Then $f(q,q) f_1^2 f_4^2 = f_2^5$, $f(q,q^3) f_1 = f_2^2$, $f(-q,-q) f_2 = f_1^2$,
$f(-q,-q^3) f_2 = f_1 f_4$, $f(q,-q^2) f_1 f_4 = f_2^3$, $(-q;q^2)_\infty f_1 f_4 = f_2^2$ and
$(q;q^2)_\infty f_2 = f_1$.

These are the classical eta-quotients $\varphi(q) = f_2^5/(f_1^2 f_4^2)$, $\psi(q) = f_2^2/f_1$,
$\varphi(-q) = f_1^2/f_2$, $\psi(-q) = f_1 f_4/f_2$, $f(q) = f_2^3/(f_1 f_4)$,
$\chi(q) = f_2^2/(f_1 f_4)$ and $\chi(-q) = f_1/f_2$ with the denominators cleared, where
$\varphi(q) = f(q,q)$, $\psi(q) = f(q,q^3)$, $f(q) = f(q,-q^2)$ and $\chi(q) = (-q;q^2)_\infty$.

## Sources

- A. Vanitha, M. P. Chaudhary, and Madiha Khanum, *Modular Relations for the Rogers-Ramanujan-Slater Type Functions of Order Eighteen with Applications to Partitions*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A103, Lemma 1 (quoted from Berndt).

articles.title: Ramanujan's theta function: sum of products when $ab = cd$
articles.statement:
Let
$f(a,b) = \sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} a^{n(n+1)/2} b^{n(n-1)/2}$ be Ramanujan's theta function. For
complex numbers $a, b, c, d$ with $ab = cd$ and $|ab| < 1$,
$f(a,b) f(c,d) + f(-a,-b) f(-c,-d) = 2 f(ac,bd) f(ad,bc)$.

This is Entry 29(i) of Berndt's *Ramanujan's Notebooks*; the hypothesis $|ab| < 1$ makes all
the theta series converge.

## Sources

- A. Vanitha, M. P. Chaudhary, and Madiha Khanum, *Modular Relations for the Rogers-Ramanujan-Slater Type Functions of Order Eighteen with Applications to Partitions*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A103, Lemma 2, Equation (6).

articles.title: Ramanujan's theta function: difference of products when $ab = cd$
articles.statement:
Let
$f(a,b) = \sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} a^{n(n+1)/2} b^{n(n-1)/2}$ be Ramanujan's theta function. For
complex numbers $a, b, c, d$ with $ab = cd$, $|ab| < 1$, $c \ne 0$ and $d \ne 0$,
$f(a,b) f(c,d) - f(-a,-b) f(-c,-d) = 2a \, f(b/c, ac^2 d) \, f(b/d, acd^2)$.

This is Entry 29(ii) of Berndt's *Ramanujan's Notebooks*, where the second arguments are written
$(c/b)abcd = ac^2 d$ and $(d/b)abcd = acd^2$.

## Sources

- A. Vanitha, M. P. Chaudhary, and Madiha Khanum, *Modular Relations for the Rogers-Ramanujan-Slater Type Functions of Order Eighteen with Applications to Partitions*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A103, Lemma 2, Equation (7).

articles.title: Ramanujan's theta function at $(q, q^5)$
articles.statement:
Let
$f(a,b) = \sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} a^{n(n+1)/2} b^{n(n-1)/2}$ be Ramanujan's theta function and
$(a;q)_\infty = \prod_{n \ge 0} (1 - a q^n)$. For every complex number $q$ with $|q| < 1$,
$f(q,q^5) = (-q;q^2)_\infty \, f(-q^3,-q^9)$, that is, $f(q,q^5) = \chi(q) \psi(-q^3)$ with
$\chi(q) = (-q;q^2)_\infty$ and $\psi(q) = f(q,q^3)$.

## Sources

- A. Vanitha, M. P. Chaudhary, and Madiha Khanum, *Modular Relations for the Rogers-Ramanujan-Slater Type Functions of Order Eighteen with Applications to Partitions*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A103, Lemma 3, Equation (9).
