articles.title: Fourth moment of the $L$-function modulo $4$
articles.statement:
Let $\chi$ be a nontrivial Dirichlet
character modulo $4$ and let $\varepsilon > 0$. Then there is a real constant $C$ such that for
every real $T \ge 1$, $\int_1^T |L(1/2 + it, \chi)|^4 \, dt \le C\, T^{1 + \varepsilon}$.

## Sources

- Naveen K. Godara and Prashant Tiwari, *The Higher Power Moments of the Coefficients of the Dedekind Zeta Function over a Polynomial in Six Variables*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A101, Lemma 5, third display.

articles.title: Higher six-squares moments over a non-normal cubic field
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field of
degree $3$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ with negative discriminant and let $\ell \ge 4$. For $n \ge 1$ let
$a_K(n)$ be the number of ideals of the ring of integers of $K$ of absolute norm $n$ and $r_6(n)$
the number of representations of $n$ as a sum of six squares of integers, and for real $x$ let
$S_\ell(x) = \sum_{1 \le n \le x} r_6(n)\, a_K(n)^\ell$. Let
$a_{0,\ell} = 1 + \sum_{i=1}^{\lfloor \ell/2 \rfloor} \binom{\ell}{2i} C_i$, with $C_i$ the
$i$-th Catalan number, and let $a_{3,\ell}$ be the sum over the integers
$1 \le i \le \lfloor (\ell - 1)/2 \rfloor$ of $\binom{\ell}{2i+1}$ times the integer part of
$4\,(2i+1)!/((i-1)!\,(i+3)!)$. Then there is a real polynomial $P$ of degree
$a_{0,\ell} + a_{3,\ell} - 1$ such that for every $\varepsilon > 0$,
$S_\ell(x) - x^3 P(\log x) = O(x^{3 - 2/3^\ell + \varepsilon})$ as $x \to \infty$.

Such a field is not normal over $\mathbb{Q}$. The polynomial is called $P_\ell$ for even $\ell$
and $Q_\ell$ for odd $\ell$ in the source.

## Sources

- Naveen K. Godara and Prashant Tiwari, *The Higher Power Moments of the Coefficients of the Dedekind Zeta Function over a Polynomial in Six Variables*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A101, Theorem 2.

articles.title: The six-squares moment vanishes below $1$
articles.statement:
For every number field $K$, every natural
number $\ell$ and every real $x < 1$, the six-squares moment
$S_\ell(x) = \sum_{1 \le n \le x} r_6(n)\, a_K(n)^\ell$ equals $0$, where $r_6(n)$ is the number
of representations of $n$ as a sum of six squares of integers and $a_K(n)$ is the number of
ideals of the ring of integers of $K$ of absolute norm $n$.

## Sources

- Naveen K. Godara and Prashant Tiwari, *The Higher Power Moments of the Coefficients of the Dedekind Zeta Function over a Polynomial in Six Variables*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A101, Section 1, equation (4).

articles.title: Second and third six-squares moments over a cubic field of negative discriminant
articles.statement:
Let
$K$ be a number field of degree $3$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ with negative discriminant. For $n \ge 1$
let $a_K(n)$ be the number of ideals of the ring of integers of $K$ of absolute norm $n$ and
$r_6(n)$ the number of representations of $n$ as a sum of six squares of integers, and for real
$x$ and natural $\ell$ let $S_\ell(x) = \sum_{1 \le n \le x} r_6(n)\, a_K(n)^\ell$. Then there
are real constants $c_1, c_2$ such that for every $\varepsilon > 0$,
$S_2(x) = c_1 x^3 + c_2 x^3 \log x + O(x^{25/9 + \varepsilon})$ as $x \to \infty$, and there is
a real polynomial $P$ of degree $4$ such that for every $\varepsilon > 0$,
$S_3(x) = x^3 P(\log x) + O(x^{79/27 + \varepsilon})$ as $x \to \infty$.

A cubic field of negative discriminant is not normal over $\mathbb{Q}$.

## Sources

- Naveen K. Godara and Prashant Tiwari, *The Higher Power Moments of the Coefficients of the Dedekind Zeta Function over a Polynomial in Six Variables*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A101, Theorem 1.

articles.title: Six-squares moments of Dedekind zeta coefficients
articles.statement:
For a number field $K$, a natural
number $\ell$ and a real number $x$, the moment is the real number
$S_\ell(x) = \sum_{1 \le n \le x} r_6(n)\, a_K(n)^\ell$, where $n$ runs over the integers in
$[1, x]$, $a_K(n)$ is the number of ideals of the ring of integers of $K$ of absolute norm $n$,
and $r_6(n)$ is the coefficient of $q^n$ in $\theta(q)^6$, with
$\theta(q) = \sum_{m \in \mathbb{Z}} q^{m^2}$; that is, $r_6(n)$ is the number of representations
of $n$ as a sum of six squares of integers.

## Sources

- Naveen K. Godara and Prashant Tiwari, *The Higher Power Moments of the Coefficients of the Dedekind Zeta Function over a Polynomial in Six Variables*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A101, Section 1, equation (4), and Section 2, equation (12).

articles.title: Continuity of the Perron kernel integrand
articles.statement:
Let $y > 0$ and $c \ne 0$ be real numbers.
Then the function from $\mathbb{R}$ to $\mathbb{C}$ sending $t$ to $y^{c+it}/(c+it)$, where
$y^{c+it}$ is the complex power, is continuous.

articles.title: Splitting off the pole of the Perron kernel quotient
articles.statement:
Let $y > 0$ be real and let
$s \ne 0$ be complex. Then $y^s/s = R_y(s) + 1/s$, where $R_y(s) = \log y \cdot E_1(s \log y)$
is the Perron remainder and $E_1(u) = \int_0^1 e^{tu}\,dt$.

articles.title: Continuity of the averaging operator at zero
articles.statement:
The function
$E_1 : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ given by $E_1(u) = \int_0^1 e^{tu}\,dt$ is continuous at $0$.

articles.title: Continuity of the averaging operator
articles.statement:
The function $E_1 : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ given
by $E_1(u) = \int_0^1 e^{tu}\,dt$ is continuous.

articles.title: The averaging operator is entire
articles.statement:
The function $E_1 : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ given by
$E_1(u) = \int_0^1 e^{tu}\,dt$ is complex differentiable at every point of $\mathbb{C}$.

articles.title: The averaging operator as a difference quotient
articles.statement:
Let $E_1(u) = \int_0^1 e^{tu}\,dt$ for
$u \in \mathbb{C}$. Then $E_1(u) = (e^u - 1)/u$ for every nonzero complex number $u$.

articles.title: Derivative of the averaging operator
articles.statement:
Let $E_1(u) = \int_0^1 e^{tu}\,dt$ for
$u \in \mathbb{C}$. For every $x_0 \in \mathbb{C}$, the function $E_1$ has complex derivative
$\int_0^1 t\,e^{t x_0}\,dt$ at $x_0$.

articles.title: Linear bound for the averaging operator near zero
articles.statement:
Let $E_1(u) = \int_0^1 e^{tu}\,dt$ for
$u \in \mathbb{C}$. For every complex number $v$ with $|v| \le 1$, we have
$|E_1(v) - 1| \le |v|$.

articles.title: Value of the averaging operator at zero
articles.statement:
Let $E_1(u) = \int_0^1 e^{tu}\,dt$ for
$u \in \mathbb{C}$. Then $E_1(0) = 1$.

articles.title: The averaging operator $E_1$
articles.statement:
For a complex number $u$, define
$E_1(u) = \int_0^1 e^{tu}\,dt$, the integral being over real $t$ from $0$ to $1$.

articles.title: Integral formula for $e^w - 1$
articles.statement:
For every complex number $w$,

$$e^w - 1 = w \int_0^1 e^{tw}\,dt,$$

where $t$ ranges over the real interval $[0, 1]$.

articles.title: Horizontal side bound for the Perron integrand on $(c, U)$
articles.statement:
Let $y > 0$ with
$\log y \ne 0$, let $c \le U$ and $T > 0$ be real numbers, and let $\tau = T$ or $\tau = -T$.
Then

$$\left|\int_c^U \frac{y^{x+i\tau}}{x+i\tau}\,dx\right|
\le \frac{\exp(U\log y)-\exp(c\log y)}{T\log y},$$

where $y^s = \exp(s \log y)$ is the principal complex power.

No sign condition on $\log y$ is assumed.

articles.title: Horizontal side bound for the Perron integrand when $y > 1$
articles.statement:
Let $y > 1$, let $U > 0$,
$c > 0$ and $T > 0$ be real numbers, and let $\tau = T$ or $\tau = -T$. Then

$$\left|\int_{-U}^{c} \frac{y^{x+i\tau}}{x+i\tau}\,dx\right| \le \frac{\exp(c\log y)}{T\log y},$$

where $y^s = \exp(s \log y)$ is the principal complex power. The bound does not depend on $U$.

articles.title: Integral of $\exp(Lx)$
articles.statement:
For real numbers $L \ne 0$, $a$ and $b$,

$$\int_a^b \exp(Lx)\,dx = \frac{\exp(Lb) - \exp(La)}{L},$$

where the integral is oriented: $\int_a^b = -\int_b^a$ when $a > b$.

articles.title: Modulus of a complex power of a positive real
articles.statement:
For every real $y > 0$ and every complex
number $s$, $|y^s| = \exp(\operatorname{Re}(s) \log y)$, where $y^s$ is the principal complex
power.

articles.title: Truncated Perron bound for $y > 1$
articles.statement:
Let $y > 1$, $c > 0$ and $T > 0$ be real numbers, and
let $K(y, c, T) = \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{-T}^{T} \frac{y^{c+it}}{c+it}\,dt$ be the truncated Perron
kernel. Then

$$|K(y, c, T) - 1| \le \frac{\exp(c \log y)}{\pi T \log y}.$$

Here $y^s$ is the principal complex power.

articles.title: Truncated Perron bound for $0 < y < 1$
articles.statement:
Let $0 < y < 1$, $c > 0$ and $T > 0$ be real
numbers, and let $K(y, c, T) = \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{-T}^{T} \frac{y^{c+it}}{c+it}\,dt$ be the
truncated Perron kernel. Then

$$|K(y, c, T)| \le \frac{\exp(c \log y)}{\pi T |\log y|}.$$

Here $y^s$ is the principal complex power.

articles.title: Truncated Perron formula
articles.statement:
Let $y > 0$ with $y \ne 1$, and let $c > 0$ and $T > 0$ be real
numbers. Let $K(y, c, T) = \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{-T}^{T} \frac{y^{c+it}}{c+it}\,dt$ be the truncated
Perron kernel, and let $\delta(y) = 1$ if $y > 1$ and $\delta(y) = 0$ if $y < 1$. Then

$$|K(y, c, T) - \delta(y)| \le \frac{\exp(c \log y)}{\pi T |\log y|}.$$

Here $y^s$ is the principal complex power.

articles.title: Truncated Perron kernel
articles.statement:
For real numbers $y$, $c$ and $T$, the truncated Perron kernel is
the complex number

$$K(y, c, T) = \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{-T}^{T} \frac{y^{c+it}}{c+it}\,dt,$$

where $y^s$ is the principal complex power of $y$ viewed as a complex number.

Writing $s = c + it$, this is $\frac{1}{2\pi i}\int_{c-iT}^{c+iT} \frac{y^s}{s}\,ds$ along the
vertical segment.

articles.title: The Perron remainder is entire
articles.statement:
For a real number $y$, the Perron remainder is the
function $R_y(s) = \log y \int_0^1 e^{ts\log y}\,dt$ of $s \in \mathbb{C}$, where
$\log y = \log|y|$ for $y \ne 0$ and $\log 0 = 0$. For every real $y$, the function $R_y$ is
complex differentiable at every point of $\mathbb{C}$.

articles.title: The Perron remainder as a difference quotient
articles.statement:
For every real $y > 0$ and every complex
$s \neq 0$, the Perron remainder $R_y$ satisfies $R_y(s) = (y^s - 1)/s$, where
$y^s = e^{s \log y}$.

articles.title: Slope of the Perron remainder at the origin
articles.statement:
For every real $y$ and every complex
$h \neq 0$, the Perron remainder $R_y$ satisfies

$$\frac{R_y(h) - R_y(0)}{h} = (\log y)^2 \int_0^1 t \, E_1(t h \log y)\,dt,$$

where $E_1(u) = \int_0^1 e^{\tau u}\,d\tau$ is the averaging operator and $\log$ is the real
logarithm (extended by $\log 0 = 0$ and $\log y = \log |y|$ for $y < 0$).

articles.title: Perron remainder
articles.statement:
For a real number $y$ and a complex number $s$, the Perron remainder is
$R_y(s) = \log y \cdot E_1(s \log y)$, where $E_1(u) = \int_0^1 e^{tu}\,dt$ is the averaging
operator and $\log$ is the real logarithm (extended by $\log 0 = 0$ and $\log y = \log |y|$ for
$y < 0$).

The function $R_y$ is entire, and for $y > 0$ it agrees with $(y^s - 1)/s$ for $s \neq 0$.

articles.title: Rectangle integral of $y^s/s$ around the origin
articles.statement:
Let $y, U, c, T$ be real numbers with
$y > 0$, $U > 0$, $c > 0$ and $T > 0$, and write $y^s = e^{s \log y}$. Then

$$\int_{-U}^{c} \frac{y^{x - iT}}{x - iT}\,dx - \int_{-U}^{c} \frac{y^{x + iT}}{x + iT}\,dx +
i \left( \int_{-T}^{T} \frac{y^{c + it}}{c + it}\,dt -
\int_{-T}^{T} \frac{y^{-U + it}}{-U + it}\,dt \right) = 2\pi i,$$

that is, the integral of $y^s/s$ over the positively oriented boundary of the rectangle with
corners $-U - iT$ and $c + iT$ equals $2\pi i$.

The identity holds for every $y > 0$; it is used to close the Perron contour to the left when
$y > 1$.

articles.title: Rectangle integral of $y^s/s$ with the pole outside
articles.statement:
Let $y, U, c, T$ be real numbers with
$y > 0$, $0 < c < U$ and $T > 0$, and write $y^s = e^{s \log y}$. Then

$$\int_{c}^{U} \frac{y^{x - iT}}{x - iT}\,dx - \int_{c}^{U} \frac{y^{x + iT}}{x + iT}\,dx +
i \left( \int_{-T}^{T} \frac{y^{U + it}}{U + it}\,dt -
\int_{-T}^{T} \frac{y^{c + it}}{c + it}\,dt \right) = 0,$$

that is, the integral of $y^s/s$ over the positively oriented boundary of the rectangle with
corners $c - iT$ and $U + iT$ vanishes.

The identity holds for every $y > 0$; it is used to close the Perron contour to the right when
$y < 1$.

articles.title: Bound for the integral of $y^s/s$ along the left vertical side
articles.statement:
Let $y, U, T$ be real
numbers with $y > 0$, $U > 0$ and $T > 0$, and write $y^s = e^{s \log y}$. Then

$$\left| \int_{-T}^{T} \frac{y^{-U + it}}{-U + it}\,dt \right| \le
2T \cdot \frac{e^{-U \log y}}{U},$$

that is, at most $2T y^{-U}/U$. This is the vertical segment bound at real part $-U$.

articles.title: Bound for the integral of $y^s/s$ along the right vertical side
articles.statement:
Let $y, U, T$ be real
numbers with $y > 0$, $U > 0$ and $T > 0$, and write $y^s = e^{s \log y}$. Then

$$\left| \int_{-T}^{T} \frac{y^{U + it}}{U + it}\,dt \right| \le
2T \cdot \frac{e^{U \log y}}{U},$$

that is, at most $2T y^{U}/U$. This is the vertical segment bound at real part $U$.

articles.title: Bound for the integral of $y^s/s$ along a vertical segment
articles.statement:
Let $y, d, T$ be real numbers
with $y > 0$, $d \neq 0$ and $T > 0$, and write $y^s = e^{s \log y}$. Then

$$\left| \int_{-T}^{T} \frac{y^{d + it}}{d + it}\,dt \right| \le
2T \cdot \frac{e^{d \log y}}{|d|},$$

that is, at most $2T y^d/|d|$.

articles.title: Functional equation of the Dirichlet beta function
articles.statement:
Let $\chi$ be the non-principal
Dirichlet character modulo $4$, so $\chi(1) = 1$, $\chi(3) = -1$ and $\chi(0) = \chi(2) = 0$; let
$\beta(s) = L(s, \chi)$ be its Dirichlet $L$-function (the Dirichlet beta function, continued to
all of $\mathbb{C}$); and put $E^*(s) = 2\,\Gamma(s)\,\beta(s) / (\pi/2)^s$. Then the functions
$\cos(\pi r/2)\, E^*(1 - r)$, $(\pi/2)^r E^*(r) / \Gamma(r)$ and
$\cos(\pi r/2)\, (\pi/2)^{r-1}\, \Gamma(1 - r)\, \beta(1 - r)$ of $r \in \mathbb{C}$ are
meromorphic on $\mathbb{C}$, and outside a closed discrete subset of $\mathbb{C}$ we have
$\cos(\pi r/2)\, E^*(1 - r) = 2\beta(r) = (\pi/2)^r E^*(r) / \Gamma(r)$ and
$\beta(r) = \cos(\pi r/2)\, (\pi/2)^{r-1}\, \Gamma(1 - r)\, \beta(1 - r)$.

## Sources

- Bruce C. Berndt, Ramanujan's Notebooks, Part I, Chapter 7.

articles.title: Burgess's bound for Dirichlet central values
articles.statement:
The number $3/16$ is an admissible
conductor-aspect exponent for primitive Dirichlet characters: for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there are
a real number $C > 0$ and a natural number $Q$ such that for every positive integer $q \ge Q$ and
every primitive Dirichlet character $\chi$ modulo $q$, the analytically continued Dirichlet
$L$-function satisfies $|L(1/2, \chi)| \le C q^{3/16 + \varepsilon}$.

## Sources

- Petrow and Young, *The Weyl bound for Dirichlet L-functions of cube-free conductor*, Annals of Mathematics 192 (2020), introduction equation (1.2), quoting Burgess's 1963 theorem.

articles.title: Petrow–Young Weyl bound on the critical line
articles.statement:
For every real $\varepsilon > 0$ there is a
real number $C$ such that for every cube-free natural number $q$ (that is, $q > 0$ and $p^3$ does
not divide $q$ for any prime $p$), every primitive Dirichlet character $\chi$ modulo $q$ and
every real $t$, the analytically continued Dirichlet $L$-function satisfies

$$|L(1/2 + it, \chi)| \le C \, q^{1/6 + \varepsilon} (1 + |t|)^{1/6 + \varepsilon}.$$

This is Corollary 1.3 of the source.

## Sources

- I. Petrow and M. P. Young, `The Weyl bound for Dirichlet L-functions of cube-free conductor`, Annals of Math, 192 (2) 2020. Statement taken from https://github.com/ImperialCollegeLondon/AnnalsChallenge. Problem `annals_dirichlet_weyl_bound` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Admissible exponents bound the Dirichlet subconvexity exponent
articles.statement:
If a real number $\theta$
is an admissible conductor-aspect exponent for primitive Dirichlet characters, then the
conductor-aspect Dirichlet subconvexity exponent is at most $\theta$, as extended real numbers.

articles.title: The Dirichlet subconvexity exponent is at most 3/16
articles.statement:
The conductor-aspect Dirichlet
subconvexity exponent, an extended real number, is at most $3/16$.

## Sources

- teorth/optimizationproblems, constant 62b, citing Burgess (1963) through Petrow--Young (2020).

articles.title: The Dirichlet subconvexity exponent is nonnegative
articles.statement:
The conductor-aspect Dirichlet
subconvexity exponent, an extended real number, is at least $0$. This holds by construction:
every admissible exponent is nonnegative, and if no real exponent is admissible, the exponent is
the infimum of the empty set, which is $+\infty$.

articles.title: The conductor-aspect Dirichlet subconvexity exponent
articles.statement:
The infimum, taken in the extended
real numbers, of the set of all real $\theta$ that are admissible conductor-aspect exponents for
primitive Dirichlet characters. If no real number is admissible, this infimum is $+\infty$.

articles.title: Central-value exponents on a set of levels
articles.statement:
Let $S$ be a set of natural numbers and
$\theta$ a real number. Then $\theta$ is a central-value exponent on $S$ if $\theta \ge 0$ and for
every $\varepsilon > 0$ there are a real number $C > 0$ and a natural number $Q$ such that for
every positive $q \in S$ with $q \ge Q$ and every primitive Dirichlet character $\chi$ modulo $q$,
the analytically continued Dirichlet $L$-function satisfies
$|L(1/2, \chi)| \le C q^{\theta + \varepsilon}$.

The constants $C$ and $Q$ may depend on $\varepsilon$, but not on the level or the character.

articles.title: Admissible exponents for Dirichlet central values
articles.statement:
A real number $\theta$ is an admissible
conductor-aspect exponent for primitive Dirichlet characters if it is a central-value exponent on
the set of all natural numbers: $\theta \ge 0$, and for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there are a real
number $C > 0$ and a natural number $Q$ such that for every positive integer $q \ge Q$ and every
primitive Dirichlet character $\chi$ modulo $q$, the analytically continued Dirichlet
$L$-function satisfies $|L(1/2, \chi)| \le C q^{\theta + \varepsilon}$.

articles.title: Petrow–Young Weyl bound for central values
articles.statement:
The number $1/6$ is a central-value exponent
on the set of cube-free levels, the natural numbers $q > 0$ such that $p^3$ does not divide $q$
for any prime $p$: for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there are a real number $C > 0$ and a natural
number $Q$ such that for every cube-free $q \ge Q$ and every primitive Dirichlet character $\chi$
modulo $q$, the analytically continued Dirichlet $L$-function satisfies
$|L(1/2, \chi)| \le C q^{1/6 + \varepsilon}$.

## Sources

- Petrow and Young, *The Weyl bound for Dirichlet L-functions of cube-free conductor*, Annals of Mathematics 192 (2020), abstract and introduction.

articles.title: Cyclic sum formula for multiple zeta-star values
articles.statement:
Let $l \ge 1$ and let $k_0, \dots, k_{l-1}$
be positive integers, not all equal to $1$, with subscripts read modulo $l$, and put
$K = k_0 + \cdots + k_{l-1}$. Write $\zeta^\star$ for the multiple zeta-star value and $\zeta$ for
the strict multiple zeta value. Suppose that for each $0 \le j \le l - 1$ and each natural number
$i$ an index $\mathbf{c}_{j,i}$ is given that is admissible or empty, and that for
$1 \le i \le k_j - 1$ its entries are $(k_j - i + 1, k_{j+1}, \dots, k_{j+l-1}, i)$, the run
$k_{j+1}, \dots, k_{j+l-1}$ being empty when $l = 1$. Let $\mathbf{t}$ be an index, admissible
or empty, whose only entry is $K + 1$. Then

$$
\sum_{j=0}^{l-1} \sum_{i=1}^{k_j - 1} \zeta^\star(\mathbf{c}_{j,i}) = K \, \zeta(\mathbf{t}).
$$

## Sources

- S. Saito, T. Tanaka, and N. Wakabayashi, "Combinatorial Remarks on the Cyclic Sum Formula for Multiple Zeta Values", Journal of Integer Sequences 14 (2011), Article 11.2.4, Theorem `thm:CSF_MZSVs`, line 869, <https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL14/Saito/saito22.tex>.

articles.title: Cyclic sum formula for strict multiple zeta values of indices
articles.statement:
Let $k = (k_1, \dots, k_l)$
be a nonempty list of positive integers, not all equal to $1$, with subscripts read modulo $l$,
and write $\zeta$ for the strict multiple zeta value. For $1 \le j \le l$ and
$1 \le i \le k_j - 1$ the left-hand index of the cyclic sum formula of $k$ at $(j, i)$ is
$(k_j - i + 1, k_{j+1}, \dots, k_{j+l-1}, i)$, and its right-hand index at $j$ is
$(k_j + 1, k_{j+1}, \dots, k_{j+l-1})$; the run $k_{j+1}, \dots, k_{j+l-1}$ is empty when
$l = 1$. Then

$$
\sum_{j=1}^{l} \sum_{i=1}^{k_j - 1} \zeta(k_j - i + 1, k_{j+1}, \dots, k_{j+l-1}, i)
= \sum_{j=1}^{l} \zeta(k_j + 1, k_{j+1}, \dots, k_{j+l-1}),
$$

where the inner sum is empty when $k_j = 1$.

articles.title: Cyclic sum formula (Hoffman–Ohno)
articles.statement:
For a finite list $(n_1, \dots, n_r)$ of natural numbers
let $\zeta(n_1, \dots, n_r)$ be the sum of $(m_1^{n_1} \cdots m_r^{n_r})^{-1}$ over all integers
$m_1 > m_2 > \cdots > m_r > 0$, taken to be $0$ when this family is not summable. Let
$k = (k_1, \dots, k_l)$ be a nonempty list of positive integers, not all equal to $1$, with
subscripts read modulo $l$. Then

$$
\sum_{j=1}^{l} \sum_{i=1}^{k_j - 1} \zeta(k_j - i + 1, k_{j+1}, \dots, k_{j+l-1}, i)
= \sum_{j=1}^{l} \zeta(k_j + 1, k_{j+1}, \dots, k_{j+l-1}),
$$

where the inner sum is empty when $k_j = 1$ and the run $k_{j+1}, \dots, k_{j+l-1}$ is empty
when $l = 1$.

## Sources

- Shingo Saito, Tatsushi Tanaka, and Noriko Wakabayashi, "Combinatorial Remarks on the Cyclic Sum Formula for Multiple Zeta Values," Journal of Integer Sequences 14 (2011), Article 11.2.4, Theorem `thm:CSF` ("Cyclic sum formula," first proved by Hoffman-Ohno), lines 242–248; index set `check{I}^1` at lines 150–166, <https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL14/Saito/saito22.tex>.

articles.title: Left-hand indices of the cyclic sum formula are admissible or empty
articles.statement:
For every list
$k = (k_1, \dots, k_l)$ of positive integers, every $1 \le j \le l$ and every natural number $i$,
the left-hand index of the cyclic sum formula of $k$ at $(j, i)$ is admissible or empty.

articles.title: Left-hand indices of the cyclic sum formula
articles.statement:
Let $k = (k_1, \dots, k_l)$ be a list of
positive integers, with subscripts read modulo $l$. For $1 \le j \le l$ and a natural number
$i$, the left-hand index of $k$ at $(j, i)$ is the index
$(k_j - i + 1, k_{j+1}, \dots, k_{j+l-1}, i)$ when $1 \le i \le k_j - 1$, and the index $(2)$
otherwise. The run $k_{j+1}, \dots, k_{j+l-1}$ is empty when $l = 1$.

articles.title: Right-hand indices of the cyclic sum formula are admissible or empty
articles.statement:
For every list
$k = (k_1, \dots, k_l)$ of positive integers and every $1 \le j \le l$, the right-hand index of
the cyclic sum formula of $k$ at $j$ is admissible or empty.

articles.title: Right-hand indices of the cyclic sum formula
articles.statement:
Let $k = (k_1, \dots, k_l)$ be a list of
positive integers, with subscripts read modulo $l$. For $1 \le j \le l$, the right-hand index of
$k$ at $j$ is the index $(k_j + 1, k_{j+1}, \dots, k_{j+l-1})$, where the run
$k_{j+1}, \dots, k_{j+l-1}$ is empty when $l = 1$.

articles.title: The index of a list of positive integers
Nested sums of reciprocal squares
articles.statement:
For every natural number $k$, the multiple zeta-star
value

$$\zeta^\star(\{2\}^k) =
\sum_{n_1 \ge n_2 \ge \cdots \ge n_k \ge 1} \frac{1}{n_1^2 n_2^2 \cdots n_k^2},$$

which is $1$ for $k = 0$, satisfies

$$\zeta^\star(\{2\}^k) = \frac{2\pi^{2k} |(2^{2k-1} - 1) B_{2k}|}{(2k)!} =
2\,(1 - 2^{1-2k})\,\zeta(2k),$$

where $B_{2k}$ is the $2k$-th Bernoulli number and $\zeta$ is the Riemann zeta function. The
right-hand side is $2\eta(2k)$ for Dirichlet's eta function $\eta(s) = (1 - 2^{1-s})\,\zeta(s)$;
at $k = 0$ all three expressions equal $1$, since $\zeta(0) = -1/2$.

## Sources

- Serge Iovleff, *About Some Nested Sums of Reciprocal Squared Numbers*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A114, Theorem 2.

articles.title: Faà di Bruno's formula for Taylor coefficients
articles.statement:
Let $f, g : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$,
let $a \in \mathbb{R}$ and let $n$ be a natural number. Suppose that $g$ is $n$ times continuously
differentiable on a neighbourhood of $a$ and that $f$ is $n$ times continuously differentiable on a
neighbourhood of $g(a)$. For a partition $\pi$ of $n$, let $m_i(\pi)$ be the number of parts of
$\pi$ equal to $i$, and let $\ell(\pi) = m_1(\pi) + \cdots + m_n(\pi)$ be its number of parts. Then

$$\frac{(f \circ g)^{(n)}(a)}{n!} = \sum_{\pi} \frac{\ell(\pi)!}{\prod_{i=1}^{n} m_i(\pi)!} \cdot
\frac{f^{(\ell(\pi))}(g(a))}{\ell(\pi)!} \cdot
\prod_{i=1}^{n} \Bigl(\frac{g^{(i)}(a)}{i!}\Bigr)^{m_i(\pi)},$$

where the sum runs over all partitions $\pi$ of $n$.

## Sources

- Serge Iovleff, *About Some Nested Sums of Reciprocal Squared Numbers*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A114, Corollary 1 (quoted as Corollary 4 from the paper's reference [8]).

articles.title: Strictly nested sums of reciprocal odd squares
articles.statement:
For every natural number $k$,

$$\sum_{i_1 > i_2 > \cdots > i_k \ge 1} \prod_{j=1}^{k} \frac{1}{(2 i_j - 1)^2} =
\frac{(\pi/2)^{2k}}{(2k)!},$$

where the sum runs over all strictly decreasing $k$-tuples $(i_1, \ldots, i_k)$ of positive
integers. For $k = 0$ the sum has the single empty term and both sides equal $1$.

The source states the identity for $k > 0$; the case $k = 0$ is included here.

## Sources

- Serge Iovleff, *About Some Nested Sums of Reciprocal Squared Numbers*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A114, Corollary 2.

articles.title: Nested sums of reciprocal odd squares
articles.statement:
For every natural number $k$,

$$\sum_{i_1 \ge i_2 \ge \cdots \ge i_k \ge 1} \prod_{j=1}^{k} \frac{1}{(2 i_j - 1)^2} =
\frac{(\pi/2)^{2k} E^*_{2k}}{(2k)!},$$

where the sum runs over all weakly decreasing $k$-tuples $(i_1, \ldots, i_k)$ of positive integers
and $E^*_{2k} = \sec^{(2k)}(0)$ is the $2k$-th derivative at $0$ of $\sec x = 1/\cos x$ (the Euler
zig number, OEIS A000364). For $k = 0$ the sum has the single empty term and both sides equal $1$.

The source also claims that the sum equals $(\pi/4)\,\beta(2k+1)$, where $\beta$ is Dirichlet's beta
function; this is false as printed and is not stated here: at $k = 0$ the sum is $1$ but
$(\pi/4)\,\beta(1) = \pi^2/16$, and at $k = 1$ it is $\pi^2/8$ but $(\pi/4)\,\beta(3) = \pi^4/128$
(the correct factor is $4/\pi$).

## Sources

- Serge Iovleff, *About Some Nested Sums of Reciprocal Squared Numbers*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A114, Theorem 1.

articles.title: Decomposition of finite multiple zeta values into level-$N$ pieces
articles.statement:
Let $N \ge 1$ and
let $k = (k_1, \dots, k_r)$ be a finite sequence of natural numbers (entries equal to $0$ are
allowed) of weight $w = k_1 + \dots + k_r$. For a prime $p$ put
$\zeta_p(k) = \sum_{0 < m_1 < \dots < m_r < p} m_1^{-k_1} \cdots m_r^{-k_r}$ in
$\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$, and for $0 \le j < N$ and a finite sequence $l$ let
$\zeta^{[j]}_{p,N}(l)$ be the colored finite multiple harmonic sum of level $N$ of $l$ with every
color equal to the class of $-jp$ modulo $N$. Then for all sufficiently large primes $p$

$$
\zeta_p(k) = N^w \sum_{0 \le i_1 \le \dots \le i_{N-1} \le r} \prod_{j=0}^{N-1}
\zeta^{[j]}_{p,N}(k_{i_j + 1}, \dots, k_{i_{j+1}}),
$$

where $i_0 = 0$, $i_N = r$, and $(k_{i_j + 1}, \dots, k_{i_{j+1}})$ is empty when
$i_j = i_{j+1}$.

## Sources

- Seki, *Regular Primes, Non-Wieferich Primes, and Finite Multiple Zeta Values of Level N*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A22, Proposition 1.

articles.title: Colored finite multiple harmonic sum of the empty index
articles.statement:
For all natural numbers $p$
and $N$, the colored finite multiple harmonic sum $\zeta^{\varnothing}_{p,N}(\varnothing)$ of the
empty index, with the empty tuple of colors, equals $1$ in $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$.

## Sources

- Seki, *Regular Primes, Non-Wieferich Primes, and Finite Multiple Zeta Values of Level N*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A22, Section 2.2 (`ζ^∅_{p,N}(∅) = 1`).

articles.title: Colored finite multiple harmonic sums
articles.statement:
Let $p$ and $N$ be natural numbers, let
$k = (k_1, \dots, k_r)$ be a finite sequence of natural numbers and let
$\alpha = (\alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_r) \in (\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})^r$. The colored finite multiple
harmonic sum $\zeta^{\alpha}_{p,N}(k) \in \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ is the sum of
$m_1^{-k_1} \cdots m_r^{-k_r}$ over all integers $0 < m_1 < \dots < m_r < p$ with
$m_i \equiv \alpha_i \pmod N$ for every $i$.

Here $m^{-1}$ is the inverse of $m$ in $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$; when $p$ is prime every
$0 < m < p$ is invertible, and for other $p$ non-units get a conventional value.

## Sources

- Seki, *Regular Primes, Non-Wieferich Primes, and Finite Multiple Zeta Values of Level N*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A22, Section 2.2 (definition of `ζ^α_{p,N}(k)`).

articles.title: Criterion for a uniform bound on the least non-vanishing Bernoulli index
articles.statement:
The following
are equivalent:
(a) there is a natural number $M$ such that for every prime $p \ge 5$ there is an odd integer
$k$ with $3 \le k \le M$, $k < p$ and $p \nmid \operatorname{num}(B_{p-k})$;
(b) there is a natural number $M \ge 5$ such that only finitely many primes $p$ satisfy $k < p$
and $p \mid \operatorname{num}(B_{p-k})$ for every odd integer $k$ with $3 \le k \le M$.

Here $B_n$ is the $n$-th Bernoulli number, with $B_1 = +1/2$ (only even indices $n \ge 2$ occur),
and $\operatorname{num}(B_n)$ is its numerator in lowest terms.

Condition (a) says that the least such $k$, the source's $g_p$, is bounded uniformly in $p$;
condition (b) says that $\bigcap_{3 \le k \le M,\ k \text{ odd}} I(k)$ is finite, where $I(k)$ is
the set of primes $p > k$ with $p \mid \operatorname{num}(B_{p-k})$.

## Sources

- Seki, *Regular Primes, Non-Wieferich Primes, and Finite Multiple Zeta Values of Level N*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A22, Lemma 4.

articles.title: Criterion for a uniform bound on the least non-Wieferich base
articles.statement:
The following are
equivalent:
(a) there is a natural number $M$ such that for every odd prime $p$ there is an integer $N$ with
$1 \le N \le M$, $p \nmid N$ and $p^2 \nmid N^{p-1} - 1$;
(b) there is a natural number $M \ge 3$ such that only finitely many primes $p$ satisfy
$p^2 \mid N^{p-1} - 1$ for every integer $N$ with $2 \le N \le M$.

For $p \nmid N$ the condition $p^2 \nmid N^{p-1} - 1$ says that $p$ does not divide the Fermat
quotient $q_p(N) = (N^{p-1} - 1)/p$, so (a) bounds, uniformly in $p$, the least such base $N$;
(b) says that $\bigcap_{N=2}^{M} W(N)$ is finite, where $W(N)$ is the set of primes $p$ with
$N^{p-1} \equiv 1 \pmod{p^2}$.

## Sources

- Seki, *Regular Primes, Non-Wieferich Primes, and Finite Multiple Zeta Values of Level N*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A22, Lemma 3.

articles.title: Regular and non-Wieferich primes give non-vanishing finite multiple zeta values
articles.statement:
(i) Suppose that infinitely many odd primes $p$ are regular, in the sense that $p$ does not
divide the class number of any $p$-th cyclotomic field over $\mathbb{Q}$. Then for every
natural number $w \notin \{1, 2, 4\}$ there is an index $k = (k_1, \dots, k_r)$ of positive
integers with $k_1 + \dots + k_r = w$ such that
$\zeta_p(k) = \sum_{0 < m_1 < \dots < m_r < p} m_1^{-k_1} \cdots m_r^{-k_r}$ is non-zero in
$\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ for infinitely many primes $p$.
(ii) Suppose that infinitely many primes are not Wieferich primes. Then for every even $N > 0$
and every natural number $w$ there are an index $k = (k_1, \dots, k_r)$ of positive integers with
$k_1 + \dots + k_r = w$ and a color map $c$ from $\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$ to
$(\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})^r \cup \{\varnothing\}$ such that the $p$-component
$\zeta^{c}_{p,N}(k)$ of the finite multiple zeta value of level $N$ with color map $c$ is
non-zero in $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ for infinitely many primes $p$.

The weight $w = 0$ is allowed (the empty index has value $1$); the paper takes $w$ positive.

## Sources

- Seki, *Regular Primes, Non-Wieferich Primes, and Finite Multiple Zeta Values of Level N*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A22, Proposition 2.

articles.title: Raising the level of finite multiple zeta values
articles.statement:
Let $N$ and $M$ be positive integers
with $N \mid M$, let $k = (k_1, \dots, k_r)$ be an index of positive integers of weight
$w = k_1 + \dots + k_r$, and let $c$ be a color map from $\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$ to
$(\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})^r \cup \{\varnothing\}$. Write $\zeta^{c}_{p,N}(k)$ for the
$p$-component of the finite multiple zeta value of level $N$ with color map $c$. Then there are
rationals $q_1, \dots, q_n$, indices $k^{(1)}, \dots, k^{(n)}$ of positive integers, each of
weight $w$, and color maps $c_1, \dots, c_n$ of level $M$ (each $c_i$ from
$\mathbb{Z}/M\mathbb{Z}$ to $(\mathbb{Z}/M\mathbb{Z})^{r_i} \cup \{\varnothing\}$, where $r_i$
is the depth of $k^{(i)}$) such that for all sufficiently large primes $p$

$$
\zeta^{c}_{p,N}(k) = \sum_{i=1}^{n} q_i \, \zeta^{c_i}_{p,M}(k^{(i)}) \quad \text{in }
\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z},
$$

where a rational $q = a/b$ in lowest terms with $b > 0$ is read modulo $p$ as $a b^{-1}$.

## Sources

- Seki, *Regular Primes, Non-Wieferich Primes, and Finite Multiple Zeta Values of Level N*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A22, Lemma 2.

articles.title: A small odd $k$ with $p \nmid B_{p-k}$
articles.statement:
For every prime $p \ge 11$ there is an odd
integer $k \ge 3$ such that $p$ does not divide the numerator of the Bernoulli number $B_{p-k}$
and $k \le (p-3)/2$ if $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$, while $k \le (p-5)/2$ if
$p \equiv 3 \pmod 4$.

Equivalently, the least such odd $k$ is at most this bound. Since $p - k$ is even and at least
$2$, the convention for $B_1$ does not matter.

## Sources

- Seki, *Regular Primes, Non-Wieferich Primes, and Finite Multiple Zeta Values of Level N*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A22, Proposition 5.

articles.title: Wieferich's criterion for the first case of Fermat's Last Theorem
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime
that is not a Wieferich prime, that is, $p^2 \nmid 2^{p-1} - 1$. Then there are no integers
$x, y, z$ with $p \nmid xyz$ and $x^p + y^p = z^p$.

## Sources

- Seki, *Regular Primes, Non-Wieferich Primes, and Finite Multiple Zeta Values of Level N*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A22, Theorem 2.

articles.title: Kummer's theorem for regular primes
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be an odd prime and let $K$ be a $p$-th
cyclotomic field over $\mathbb{Q}$ (a number field generated over $\mathbb{Q}$ by a primitive
$p$-th root of unity). If $p$ does not divide the class number of $K$, then Fermat's Last Theorem
holds for the exponent $p$: there are no positive integers $a, b, c$ with $a^p + b^p = c^p$.

## Sources

- Seki, *Regular Primes, Non-Wieferich Primes, and Finite Multiple Zeta Values of Level N*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A22, Theorem 1.

articles.title: Skula–Dobson–Ichimura congruence for the Fermat quotient of $2$
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be an odd prime
and $N$ a positive integer with $p \nmid N$. Write $q_p(2) = (2^{p-1} - 1)/p$ for the Fermat
quotient of $2$, and for integers $i \ge 0$ and $M \ge 1$ let $s_p(i, M) \in \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$
be the sum of $m^{-1}$ over the integers $m$ with $0 < m < p$ and $ip/M < m < (i+1)p/M$. Then
$(N + 1)\, q_p(2) \equiv -\sum_{0 \le j < N/2} s_p(2j, 2N) \pmod{p}$.

## Sources

- Seki, *Regular Primes, Non-Wieferich Primes, and Finite Multiple Zeta Values of Level N*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A22, Theorem 3.

articles.title: Reversal for finite multiple zeta values of level $N$
articles.statement:
Let $N \ge 1$, let
$k = (k_1, \dots, k_r)$ be a tuple of natural numbers of weight $w = k_1 + \dots + k_r$, and let
$c$ be a color map, which sends each $a \in \mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$ either to $\emptyset$ or to a
tuple in $(\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})^r$. Write $k^{\leftarrow} = (k_r, \dots, k_1)$, and let
$c^{\leftarrow}$ be the color map with $c^{\leftarrow}(a) = (a - \alpha_r, \dots, a - \alpha_1)$
when $c(a) = (\alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_r)$ and $c^{\leftarrow}(a) = \emptyset$ when
$c(a) = \emptyset$. Then for all but finitely many primes $p$, the $p$-components of the finite
multiple zeta values of level $N$ with these color maps satisfy
$\zeta^{c}_{\mathcal{A},N}(k)_p = (-1)^w \zeta^{c^{\leftarrow}}_{\mathcal{A},N}(k^{\leftarrow})_p$
in $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$.

## Sources

- Seki, *Regular Primes, Non-Wieferich Primes, and Finite Multiple Zeta Values of Level N*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A22, Proposition 1.

articles.title: The empty color map gives zero
articles.statement:
For all natural numbers $p$ and $N$ and every tuple
$k = (k_1, \dots, k_r)$ of natural numbers, if $c$ is the color map sending every
$a \in \mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$ to $\emptyset$, then the $p$-component $\zeta^c_{\mathcal{A},N}(k)_p$
of the finite multiple zeta value of level $N$ with color map $c$ is $0$.

## Sources

- Seki, *Regular Primes, Non-Wieferich Primes, and Finite Multiple Zeta Values of Level N*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A22, Definition 2.1.

articles.title: A constant color map gives the colored harmonic sum
articles.statement:
For all natural numbers $p$ and $N$,
every tuple $k = (k_1, \dots, k_r)$ of natural numbers and every
$\alpha \in (\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})^r$, if $c$ is the color map sending every
$a \in \mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$ to $\alpha$, then the $p$-component $\zeta^c_{\mathcal{A},N}(k)_p$
of the finite multiple zeta value of level $N$ with color map $c$ equals the colored finite
multiple harmonic sum $\zeta^{\alpha}_{p,N}(k)$.

## Sources

- Seki, *Regular Primes, Non-Wieferich Primes, and Finite Multiple Zeta Values of Level N*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A22, Definition 2.1.

articles.title: Finite multiple zeta value of level $N$ with a color map
articles.statement:
Let $p$ and $N$ be natural
numbers, $k = (k_1, \dots, k_r)$ a tuple of natural numbers, and $c$ a color map, which sends
each $a \in \mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$ either to $\emptyset$ or to a tuple in
$(\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})^r$. The $p$-component
$\zeta^c_{\mathcal{A},N}(k)_p \in \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ is the colored finite multiple harmonic
sum $\zeta^{\alpha}_{p,N}(k)$ when $c(p \bmod N) = \alpha$ is a tuple, and $0$ when
$c(p \bmod N) = \emptyset$.

Color maps are taken on all of $\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$; only their values at units matter for all
but finitely many $p$.

## Sources

- Seki, *Regular Primes, Non-Wieferich Primes, and Finite Multiple Zeta Values of Level N*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A22, Definition 2.1 (finite multiple zeta values of level `N` with color map).

articles.title: Sums over a subinterval of $(0, p)$ as colored finite multiple zeta values
articles.statement:
Let
$N \ge 1$, $0 \le j < N$, and let $k = (k_1, \dots, k_r)$ be a tuple of natural numbers of weight
$w = k_1 + \dots + k_r$. For a prime $p$ and $\alpha \in (\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})^r$ let
$\zeta^{\alpha}_{p,N}(k) \in \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ be the colored finite multiple harmonic sum,
the sum of $1/(m_1^{k_1} \cdots m_r^{k_r})$ over the integers $0 < m_1 < \dots < m_r < p$ with
$m_i \equiv \alpha_i \pmod{N}$ for all $i$. Then for all but finitely many primes $p$, with
$\alpha = (-jp, \dots, -jp) \in (\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})^r$,
$\sum 1/(m_1^{k_1} \cdots m_r^{k_r}) = N^w \zeta^{\alpha}_{p,N}(k)$ in $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$,
where the sum is over the integers $m_1, \dots, m_r$ with
$jp/N < m_1 < \dots < m_r < (j+1)p/N$.

The entries of $k$ may be $0$; the paper's indices have positive entries.

## Sources

- Seki, *Regular Primes, Non-Wieferich Primes, and Finite Multiple Zeta Values of Level N*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A22, Lemma 1.

articles.title: Level-$12$ colored finite zeta values and Bernoulli numbers
articles.statement:
Let $k \ge 3$ be odd. For a
prime $p > k$ write $Z_p(k) = B_{p-k}/k \in \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$, where $B_n$ is the $n$-th
Bernoulli number, and for $\alpha \in \mathbb{Z}/12\mathbb{Z}$ let
$\zeta^{\alpha}_{p,12}(k) \in \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ be the sum of $m^{-k}$ over $0 < m < p$ with
$m \equiv \alpha \pmod{12}$. Then for all but finitely many primes $p$, in $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$,
$2\zeta^{-2p}_{p,12}(k) = (2^{-k} - 3^{-k} - 4^{-k} + 12^{-k}) Z_p(k)$ and
$2\zeta^{-3p}_{p,12}(k) = (3^{-k} - 4^{-k} - 6^{-k} + 12^{-k}) Z_p(k)$.

## Sources

- Seki, *Regular Primes, Non-Wieferich Primes, and Finite Multiple Zeta Values of Level N*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A22, Proposition 3.

articles.title: Generalized Goldbach series for height one multiple zeta values
articles.statement:
Let $k \ge 1$ be an
integer. Write $\zeta(s, \{1\}^j)$ for the height one multiple zeta function, $\zeta$ for the
Riemann zeta function, $c(k, m)$ for the unsigned Stirling numbers of the first kind,
$H_k = \sum_{i=1}^{k} 1/i$ for the $k$-th harmonic number and
$H_{k,k} = \sum_{i=1}^{k} (-1)^{i-1} \binom{k}{i} i^{-k}$ for the Roman harmonic number. Then the
series $\sum_{j \ge 0} \bigl(k^j \zeta(k + 1, \{1\}^j) - \frac{1}{k! \, k}\bigr)$ is summable with
sum $\frac{1}{k!} \bigl(\sum_{m=0}^{k-1} c(k, m) \, \zeta(k + 1 - m) + H_k\bigr)$, and the series
$\sum_{j \ge 0} (-1)^j \bigl(k^j \zeta(k + 1, \{1\}^j) - \frac{1}{k! \, k}\bigr)$ is summable with
sum $\frac{H_{k,k}}{k} - \frac{1}{2 \, k! \, k}$.

## Sources

- Paul Thomas Young, *Series of Height One Multiple Zeta Functions*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A43, Theorem 2.

articles.title: Height one multiple zeta series weighted by powers of a natural number
articles.statement:
Let $n \ge 0$ be
an integer. Write $\zeta(s, \{1\}^j)$ for the height one multiple zeta function, $\zeta$ for the
Riemann zeta function, $c(n, m)$ for the unsigned Stirling numbers of the first kind and
$B_j^{(k)}(x)$ for the poly-Bernoulli polynomials. For every complex $s$ with
$\operatorname{Re} s > n + 1$, the series $\sum_{j \ge 0} \zeta(s, \{1\}^j) \, n^j$ (with $0^0 = 1$)
is summable with sum $\frac{1}{n!} \sum_{m=0}^{n} c(n, m) \, \zeta(s - m)$. For every complex $s$
with $\operatorname{Re} s > 1$, the series $\sum_{j \ge 0} B_j^{(-n)}(-1) \, \zeta(s + n, \{1\}^j)$
is summable with sum $\zeta(s)$.

The source states the second identity with $C_j^{(-n)} = B_j^{(-n)}(1)$, where its poly-Bernoulli
polynomials have the generating function with $e^{-xt}$; with the factor $e^{xt}$ used here this
coefficient is $B_j^{(-n)}(-1)$.

## Sources

- Paul Thomas Young, *Series of Height One Multiple Zeta Functions*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A43, Corollary 1.

articles.title: Expansion of the multiple Hurwitz zeta function in height one multiple zeta values
articles.statement:
Let
$r$ and $s$ be complex numbers with $\operatorname{Re} s > 1$, $|r - 1| < |s - 1|$ and
$\operatorname{Re} r < \operatorname{Re} s$. Write $\zeta(s, \{1\}^j)$ for the height one multiple
zeta function and $\zeta_r(s)$ for the multiple Hurwitz zeta function of order $r$. Then the series
$\sum_{j \ge 0} \zeta(s, \{1\}^j) \, (r - 1)^j$ is summable with sum $\zeta_r(s)$.

## Sources

- Paul Thomas Young, *Series of Height One Multiple Zeta Functions*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A43, Theorem 1.

articles.title: Expansion of the hyperharmonic zeta function in height one multiple zeta values
articles.statement:
Let $r$
and $s$ be complex numbers with $\operatorname{Re} s > 0$, $|r| < |s|$ and
$\operatorname{Re} r < \operatorname{Re} s$. Write $\zeta(s, \{1\}^j)$ for the height one multiple
zeta function, $H_m^{[r]}(k)$ for the generalized hyperharmonic numbers and
$H_m^{[r]} = H_m^{[r]}(1)$; equivalently, $H_m^{[r]}$ is the derivative of $\binom{m + r - 1}{m}$
with respect to $r$. Then the series $\sum_{j \ge 0} (j + 1) \, \zeta(s + 1, \{1\}^j) \, r^j$ is
summable with sum the hyperharmonic zeta function $\sigma(r, s) = \sum_{m \ge 1} H_m^{[r]} m^{-s}$.

## Sources

- Paul Thomas Young, *Series of Height One Multiple Zeta Functions*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A43, Theorem 3, second equality.

articles.title: Linear Laurent coefficient of the height one multiple zeta function
articles.statement:
Let $j \ge 1$ be an
integer, write $\zeta(s, \{1\}^{j-1})$ for the height one multiple zeta function and $\zeta_r(s)$
for the multiple Hurwitz zeta function of order $r$. There are complex numbers
$c_0, \dots, c_{j-1}$ and a function $F$ analytic at $s = 1$ such that
$\zeta(s, \{1\}^{j-1}) = \sum_{i=0}^{j-1} c_i (s - 1)^{-(i+1)} + F(s)$ for all $s$ near $1$
with $\operatorname{Re} s > 1$, and

$$-F'(1) = \int_0^1 \bigl((1 - r) \, \zeta_r(j + 2) - \zeta_r(j + 1)\bigr) \, dr - a_{j+1},$$

where $a_{j+1}$ is the coefficient of $s^{j+1}$ in the Taylor expansion of $1/\Gamma(s + 1)$
at $s = 0$.

The number $-F'(1)$ generalizes the first Stieltjes constant $\gamma_1$: for $j = 1$ and
$\operatorname{Re} s > 1$, $\zeta(s, \{1\}^0)$ equals the Riemann zeta function $\zeta(s)$, whose
Laurent expansion at $s = 1$ is $\zeta(s) = \frac{1}{s - 1} + \gamma - \gamma_1 (s - 1) + \cdots$
with Euler's constant $\gamma$, so $-F'(1) = \gamma_1$.

## Sources

- Paul Thomas Young, *Series of Height One Multiple Zeta Functions*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A43, Corollary 3.

articles.title: Height one multiple zeta function of depth one
articles.statement:
For every complex number $s$, the height
one multiple zeta function $\zeta(s, \{1\}^j)$ at $j = 0$ is the Dirichlet series of the Riemann
zeta function: $\zeta(s, \{1\}^0) = \sum_{n \ge 0} (n + 1)^{-s}$.

## Sources

- Paul Thomas Young, *Series of Height One Multiple Zeta Functions*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A43, Section 1.

articles.title: Height one multiple zeta function
articles.statement:
For a complex number $s$ and an integer $j \ge 0$, the
height one multiple zeta function is

$$\zeta(s, \{1\}^j) = \sum_{n \ge 0} (n + 1)^{-s} \sum_{T} \prod_{m \in T} \frac{1}{m},$$

where $T$ runs over the $j$-element subsets of $\{1, \dots, n\}$. Writing $n_1 = n + 1$ and
$T = \{n_2, \dots, n_{j+1}\}$, this is
$\zeta(s, \{1\}^j) = \sum_{n_1 > \cdots > n_{j+1} \ge 1} n_1^{-s} (n_2 \cdots n_{j+1})^{-1}$, which
converges for $\operatorname{Re} s > 1$.

## Sources

- Paul Thomas Young, *Series of Height One Multiple Zeta Functions*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A43, Section 1.

articles.title: Multiple Hurwitz zeta function of order zero
articles.statement:
For every complex number $s$, the multiple
Hurwitz zeta function of order $0$ is identically one: $\zeta_0(s) = 1$.

## Sources

- Paul Thomas Young, *Series of Height One Multiple Zeta Functions*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A43, Section 2, Equation (2.2).

articles.title: Multiple Hurwitz zeta function
articles.statement:
For complex numbers $r$ and $s$, the multiple Hurwitz zeta
function of order $r$, with Hurwitz parameter $a = 1$, is the Dirichlet series

$$\zeta_r(s) = \sum_{m \ge 0} \binom{m + r - 1}{m} (m + 1)^{-s},$$

where $\binom{m + r - 1}{m} = r (r + 1) \cdots (r + m - 1) / m!$. The series converges for
$\operatorname{Re} r < \operatorname{Re} s$.

## Sources

- Paul Thomas Young, *Series of Height One Multiple Zeta Functions*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A43, Section 2, Equation (2.2).

articles.title: Shifted alternating series of height one multiple zeta values
articles.statement:
Let $k \ge -1$ and
$p \ge 0$ be integers, write $\zeta(s, \{1\}^p)$ for the height one multiple zeta function and
$\zeta_r(s)$ for the multiple Hurwitz zeta function of order $r$. Then the partial sums of the
series $\nu_{k,p} = \sum_{n \ge 2} \frac{(-1)^n \, \zeta(n, \{1\}^p)}{n + k}$ converge to
$\int_0^1 (1 - r)^{k+1} \, \zeta_r(p + 2) \, dr$.

## Sources

- Paul Thomas Young, *Series of Height One Multiple Zeta Functions*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A43, Theorem 4.

articles.title: Height one multiple zeta series weighted by powers of a negative integer
articles.statement:
Let $r \ge 1$
be an integer and let $\zeta(s, \{1\}^j)$ denote the height one multiple zeta function. For
every complex number $s$ with $\operatorname{Re} s > r + 1$,

$$\sum_{j \ge 0} \zeta(s, \{1\}^j) (-r)^j = \sum_{m=0}^{r-1} \binom{r-1}{m} (-1)^m (m+1)^{-s}.$$

For every integer $k > r + 1$,

$$\sum_{j \ge 0} \zeta(k, \{1\}^j) (-r)^j = \frac{H_{r,k-1}}{r},$$

where $H_{r,k-1} = \sum_{i=1}^{r} (-1)^{i-1} \binom{r}{i} i^{-(k-1)}$ is the rational Roman
harmonic number (Equation (2.18)).

## Sources

- Paul Thomas Young, *Series of Height One Multiple Zeta Functions*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A43, Corollary 2.

articles.title: Hoffman basis of $\mathfrak{H}^1$
articles.statement:
Let $\mathfrak{H} = \mathbb{Q}\langle x, y \rangle$ be
the free associative $\mathbb{Q}$-algebra on two generators $x$ and $y$, let $\mathfrak{H}^1$ be
the $\mathbb{Q}$-linear span of the empty word and the words ending in $y$ (a subalgebra), and
for each positive integer $k$ let $z_k = x^{k-1} y$. The family of monomials
$z_{k_1} z_{k_2} \cdots z_{k_r}$, indexed by all indices $(k_1, \dots, k_r)$ of positive integers
including the empty index (whose monomial is the empty word $1$), is a basis of $\mathfrak{H}^1$
over $\mathbb{Q}$.

## Sources

- M. E. Hoffman, *The Algebra of Multiple Harmonic Series*, J. Algebra 194 (1997), 477–495, DOI 10.1006/jabr.1997.7127.

articles.title: The subalgebra $\mathfrak{H}^1$
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{Q}\langle x, y\rangle$ be the free
associative $\mathbb{Q}$-algebra on two letters $x$ and $y$, whose monomials are the words in
$x$ and $y$. The subalgebra $\mathfrak{H}^1$ of $\mathbb{Q}\langle x, y\rangle$ is the
$\mathbb{Q}$-linear span of the words that are empty or end in $y$; equivalently, it consists
of the polynomials in which every word with nonzero coefficient is empty or ends in $y$.

articles.title: Hoffman monomial basis of $\mathfrak{H}^0$
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{Q}\langle x, y\rangle$ be the free
associative $\mathbb{Q}$-algebra on two letters $x$ and $y$, and let $\mathfrak{H}^0$ be its
subalgebra consisting of the $\mathbb{Q}$-linear combinations of the empty word and of words that
begin with $x$ and end with $y$. For $k \ge 1$ put $z_k = x^{k-1} y$, and for an index
$\mathbf{k} = (k_1, \dots, k_r)$ of positive integers (possibly empty) put
$z_{\mathbf{k}} = z_{k_1} \cdots z_{k_r}$, with $z_{\mathbf{k}} = 1$ for the empty index. Call
$\mathbf{k}$ admissible if $r \ge 1$ and $k_1 \ge 2$. Then there is a $\mathbb{Q}$-basis of
$\mathfrak{H}^0$, indexed by the indices that are empty or admissible, whose element at each such
index $\mathbf{k}$ is $z_{\mathbf{k}}$.

## Sources

- M. E. Hoffman, *The Algebra of Multiple Harmonic Series*, J. Algebra 194 (1997), 477–495, DOI 10.1006/jabr.1997.7127.

articles.title: The subalgebra $\mathfrak{H}^0$
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbb{Q}\langle x, y\rangle$ be the free
associative $\mathbb{Q}$-algebra on two letters $x$ and $y$, whose monomials are the words in
$x$ and $y$. The subalgebra $\mathfrak{H}^0$ of $\mathbb{Q}\langle x, y\rangle$ is the
$\mathbb{Q}$-linear span of the words that are empty or begin with $x$ and end in $y$;
equivalently, it consists of the polynomials in which every word with nonzero coefficient is
empty or begins with $x$ and ends in $y$.

articles.title: The type of empty or admissible indices
articles.statement:
The type whose elements are the indices that
are admissible, that is, nonempty with first entry at least $2$, or that have no entries.

articles.title: Words of $\mathfrak{H}^1$
articles.statement:
A word $w$ in the two letters $x$ and $y$ is an
$\mathfrak{H}^1$-word when $w$ is empty or $w = uy$ for some word $u$, that is, when $w$ is
empty or ends in $y$.

articles.title: Empty or admissible indices
articles.statement:
An index is empty-or-admissible when it is admissible, that
is, nonempty with first entry at least $2$, or when it has no entries.

articles.title: Words of $\mathfrak{H}^0$
articles.statement:
A word $w$ in the two letters $x$ and $y$ is an
$\mathfrak{H}^0$-word when $w$ is empty or $w = xuy$ for some word $u$, that is, when $w$ is
empty or begins with $x$ and ends in $y$.

articles.title: Entries of an index as positive integers
articles.statement:
For an index $(k_1, \dots, k_r)$, this is the
list $(k_1, \dots, k_r)$ of its entries in order, each regarded as a positive integer.

articles.title: The monoid of $\mathfrak{H}^1$-words
articles.statement:
This is the submonoid of the free monoid on the two
letters $x$ and $y$ consisting of the words that are empty or end in $y$.

articles.title: The monoid of $\mathfrak{H}^0$-words
articles.statement:
This is the submonoid of the free monoid on the two
letters $x$ and $y$ consisting of the words that are empty or begin with $x$ and end in $y$.

articles.title: The letter $x$ as a word
articles.statement:
In the free monoid on the two letters $x$ and $y$, with $x$
represented by the Boolean value false and $y$ by true, this is the word of length one
consisting of the letter $x$.

articles.title: The letter $y$ as a word
articles.statement:
In the free monoid on the two letters $x$ and $y$, this is the
word of length one consisting of the single letter $y$.

The letters are encoded as booleans, with $x$ as false and $y$ as true.

articles.title: Hoffman monomial of an index
articles.statement:
For an index $\mathbf{k} = (k_1, \dots, k_r)$ of positive
integers, this is the monomial $z_{k_1} z_{k_2} \cdots z_{k_r}$ with coefficient $1$ in the free
associative algebra $\mathbb{Q}\langle x, y \rangle$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ on two noncommuting letters
$x$ and $y$, where $z_k = x^{k-1} y$. In other words, it is the Hoffman word of $\mathbf{k}$ viewed
as an element of $\mathbb{Q}\langle x, y \rangle$. The empty index gives $1$.

articles.title: Hoffman word of a list of positive integers
articles.statement:
For a finite list $(k_1, \dots, k_r)$ of
positive integers, this is the word $z_{k_1} z_{k_2} \cdots z_{k_r}$ in the free monoid on the two
letters $x$ and $y$, where $z_k = x^{k-1} y$ is the Hoffman block of $k$. The empty list gives the
empty word.

articles.title: Hoffman word of an index
articles.statement:
For an index $\mathbf{k} = (k_1, \dots, k_r)$ of positive
integers, the Hoffman word of $\mathbf{k}$ is $z_{k_1} z_{k_2} \cdots z_{k_r}$ in the free monoid on
the two letters $x$ and $y$, where $z_k = x^{k-1} y$. The empty index gives the empty word.

articles.title: Empty strictly decreasing tuple
articles.statement:
The unique strictly decreasing tuple of positive natural
numbers of length zero, namely the empty tuple.

articles.title: Empty weakly decreasing tuple
articles.statement:
The unique weakly decreasing tuple of positive natural
numbers of length zero, namely the empty tuple.

articles.title: Empty multiple-zeta index
articles.statement:
The empty multiple-zeta index, which has no entries and weight
zero.

## Sources

- arXiv:2307.09867, empty-index convention.

articles.title: Entry of a multiple-zeta index
articles.statement:
For a multiple-zeta index $k = (k_0, \dots, k_{d-1})$ of
depth $d$ and $0 \le i < d$, the entry of $k$ at $i$ is the positive natural number $k_i$.

articles.title: Admissible or empty index
articles.statement:
A multiple-zeta index is admissible or empty when it is
admissible (nonempty with first entry at least two) or has depth zero, that is, has no entries.

The strict multiple-zeta value and the multiple-zeta-star value are defined on these indices.

articles.title: Repeated indices with entry at least two are admissible or empty
articles.statement:
For every natural
number $k$ and every positive natural number $e \ge 2$, the index $\{e\}^k$ consisting of $k$
entries all equal to $e$ is admissible or empty.

## Sources

- Iovleff, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A114, Section 1 (`ζ*({2}^k)`).

articles.title: Repeated index
articles.statement:
For a natural number $k$ and a positive natural number $e$, the index
$\{e\}^k = (e, \dots, e)$ consisting of $k$ entries all equal to $e$, so of weight $ke$.

For $e = 2$ its multiple-zeta-star value is $\zeta^\star(\{2\}^k)$.

## Sources

- Serge Iovleff, *About Some Nested Sums of Reciprocal Squared Numbers*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A114, Section 1 (notation `ζ*({2}^k)` and `ζ({2}^k)`).

articles.title: Star and strict summands agree on strictly decreasing tuples
articles.statement:
For a multiple-zeta index
$k$ of depth $d$ and a strictly decreasing tuple $m$ of $d$ positive natural numbers, the star
summand of $k$ at $m$, with $m$ regarded as a weakly decreasing tuple, equals the strict summand
of $k$ at $m$.

articles.title: Multiple-zeta-star summand
articles.statement:
For a multiple-zeta index $k = (k_0, \dots, k_{d-1})$ of
depth $d$ and a weakly decreasing tuple $m = (m_0, \dots, m_{d-1})$ of positive natural numbers,
the star summand of $k$ at $m$ is the real number $\left(\prod_{i\lt d} m_i^{k_i}\right)^{-1}$.

## Sources

- arXiv:2307.09867, lines 61–65, and arXiv:2309.07569v2, lines 84–87.

articles.title: Multiple-zeta-star value of the empty index
articles.statement:
The multiple-zeta-star value of the empty
index is $1$.

## Sources

- arXiv:2307.09867, lines 166–167.

articles.title: Multiple zeta-star value
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbf{k} = (k_0, \dots, k_{r-1})$ be an index of depth
$r$ that is admissible ($r \ge 1$ and $k_0 \ge 2$) or empty. Its multiple zeta-star value is the
real number

$$\zeta^\star(\mathbf{k}) = \sum_{m_0 \ge \dots \ge m_{r-1} \ge 1} \prod_{i=0}^{r-1} m_i^{-k_i}$$

where the sum runs over all weakly decreasing $r$-tuples $(m_0, \dots, m_{r-1})$ of positive
integers. The sum is unconditional, with value $0$ by convention when the family is not
summable.

## Sources

- arXiv:2307.09867, lines 61–65, and arXiv:2309.07569v2, lines 84–87.

articles.title: Strictly decreasing tuples
articles.statement:
For a natural number $r$, a strictly decreasing $r$-tuple is a
tuple $(m_0, \dots, m_{r-1})$ of positive integers with $m_0 > m_1 > \dots > m_{r-1}$.

## Sources

- arXiv:2307.09867, lines 60–63, and arXiv:2309.07569, lines 76–80.

articles.title: Multiple zeta summand
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbf{k} = (k_0, \dots, k_{r-1})$ be an index of depth $r$
and let $(m_0, \dots, m_{r-1})$ be a strictly decreasing $r$-tuple of positive integers. The
summand attached to $\mathbf{k}$ and this tuple is the real number
$\left(\prod_{i=0}^{r-1} m_i^{k_i}\right)^{-1}$.

## Sources

- arXiv:2307.09867, lines 60–63, and arXiv:2309.07569, lines 76–80.

articles.title: Multiple zeta value
articles.statement:
Let $\mathbf{k} = (k_0, \dots, k_{r-1})$ be an index of depth $r$
that is admissible ($r \ge 1$ and $k_0 \ge 2$) or empty. Its multiple zeta value is the real
number

$$\zeta(\mathbf{k}) = \sum_{m_0 > m_1 > \dots > m_{r-1} \ge 1} \prod_{i=0}^{r-1} m_i^{-k_i}$$

where the sum runs over all strictly decreasing $r$-tuples $(m_0, \dots, m_{r-1})$ of positive
integers. The sum is unconditional, with value $0$ by convention when the family is not
summable.

## Sources

- arXiv:2307.09867, lines 60–63, and arXiv:2309.07569, lines 76–80.

articles.title: Strictly decreasing tuples as weakly decreasing tuples
Weakly decreasing tuples
articles.statement:
For a natural number $r$, a weakly decreasing $r$-tuple is a
tuple $(m_0, \dots, m_{r-1})$ of positive integers with $m_0 \ge m_1 \ge \dots \ge m_{r-1}$.

## Sources

- arXiv:2307.09867, lines 61–65, and arXiv:2309.07569v2, lines 84–87.

articles.title: Depth of an index
articles.statement:
The depth of an index $(k_1, \ldots, k_r)$ is its number of
entries $r$.

## Sources

- clause D4 (`2608.10675:D01`, `2307.09867:D01`).

articles.title: Entries of an index
articles.statement:
The entries of an index $(k_1, \ldots, k_r)$ form the list
$[k_1, \ldots, k_r]$ of its terms, in order.

## Sources

- clause D2 (`2608.10675:D01`, `2307.09867:D01`).

articles.title: Height of an index
articles.statement:
The height of an index $(k_1, \ldots, k_r)$ is the number of
positions $i$ with $1 \le i \le r$ and $k_i \ge 2$.

## Sources

- clause D5 (`2307.09867:D01`).

articles.title: Hoffman block
articles.statement:
For a positive integer $k$, the Hoffman block $z_k = x^{k-1} y$ is the
word in the free monoid on two letters $x$ and $y$ consisting of $k - 1$ copies of $x$ followed
by one $y$.

The free monoid is taken on the booleans, with false standing for $x$ and true for $y$.

## Sources

- `2307.09867:D05`.

articles.title: Multiple-zeta index
articles.statement:
An index is a finite sequence $(k_1, \ldots, k_r)$ of positive
integers with $r \ge 0$, so the empty sequence is allowed. It is represented as a natural
number $n$ together with a composition of $n$, that is, a sequence of positive integers with
sum $n$.

## Sources

- clause D1 (`2608.10675:D01`, `2307.09867:D01`).

articles.title: Admissible list
articles.statement:
A list $[k_1, \ldots, k_r]$ of natural numbers is admissible when it
is nonempty ($r \ge 1$), $k_1 \ge 2$, and $k_i > 0$ for every $i$ with $2 \le i \le r$.

This is the admissibility condition for multiple-zeta indices in decreasing summation order.

## Sources

- `2307.09867:D01`.

articles.title: Admissibility of an index via its entries
articles.statement:
An index is admissible if and only if the
list of its entries is an admissible list.

articles.title: Admissible index
articles.statement:
An index $(k_1, \ldots, k_r)$ is admissible when it is nonempty
($r \ge 1$) and its first entry satisfies $k_1 \ge 2$.

## Sources

- clause D6 (`2307.09867:D01`).

articles.title: Hoffman block as a list
articles.statement:
For every positive integer $k$, the list of letters of the
Hoffman block $z_k$ consists of $k - 1$ copies of $x$ (false) followed by one $y$ (true).

articles.title: Weight of an index
articles.statement:
The weight of an index $(k_1, \ldots, k_r)$ is the sum
$k_1 + \cdots + k_r$ of its entries.

## Sources

- clause D3 (`2307.09867:D01`).

articles.title: Class numbers of finite general linear groups via OOZ-qMZVs
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a finite field
with $c$ elements and, for $n \ge 0$, let $a_{n,K}$ be the number of conjugacy classes of
$\mathrm{GL}_n(K)$, so that $a_{0,K} = 1$ because $\mathrm{GL}_0(K)$ is the trivial group. Write
$\{1\}^r$ for the index consisting of $r$ ones and $\zeta_q^{\mathrm{OOZ}}$ for the
Ohno–Okuda–Zudilin qMZV. Then for all natural numbers $N \le R$, $a_{N,K}$ equals the coefficient
of $q^N$ in $\sum_{r=0}^{R} (c - 1)^r \zeta_q^{\mathrm{OOZ}}(\{1\}^r)$.

Since the summands with $r > N$ have no $q^N$ term, this is the identity of formal power series
$\sum_{n \ge 0} a_{n,K} q^n = \sum_{r \ge 0} (c - 1)^r \zeta_q^{\mathrm{OOZ}}(\{1\}^r)$.

## Sources

- Benjamin Brindle, *A Unified Approach to qMZVs*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A6, Theorem 20.

articles.title: Number of conjugacy classes of the symmetric group
articles.statement:
For every natural number $n$, the
number of conjugacy classes of the symmetric group $S_n$ equals the number $p(n)$ of partitions
of $n$.

## Sources

- Benjamin Brindle, *A Unified Approach to qMZVs*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A6, Lemma 4.

articles.title: The coefficient of $q$ in $\zeta_q^{\mathrm{SZ}}(1)$
articles.statement:
The coefficient of $q$ in the
Schlesinger–Zudilin qMZV $\zeta_q^{\mathrm{SZ}}(1) = \sum_{m > 0} q^m / (1 - q^m)$ is $1$.

## Sources

- Benjamin Brindle, *A Unified Approach to qMZVs*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A6, Definition of Schlesinger–Zudilin qMZVs.

articles.title: Coefficients of Schlesinger–Zudilin qMZVs as sums of binomial products
articles.statement:
Let $r \ge 0$,
and let $k_1, \dots, k_r$ and $d_1, \dots, d_r$ be positive integers. For every natural number
$N$, the coefficient of $q^N$ in the Schlesinger–Zudilin qMZV
$\zeta_q^{\mathrm{SZ}}(k_1, \{0\}^{d_1 - 1}, \dots, k_r, \{0\}^{d_r - 1})$, whose index lists each
$k_j$ followed by $d_j - 1$ zeros, equals

$$\sum \prod_{j=1}^{r} \binom{n_j - 1}{k_j - 1} \binom{m_j - m_{j+1} - 1}{d_j - 1},$$

where the sum runs over all integers $m_1 > \dots > m_r > 0$ and $n_1, \dots, n_r \ge 1$ with
$m_1 n_1 + \dots + m_r n_r = N$, and where $m_{r+1} = 0$.

These are the coefficients of $X_1^{k_1 - 1} \cdots X_r^{k_r - 1} Y_1^{d_1 - 1} \cdots
Y_r^{d_r - 1} q^N$ on both sides of the paper's identity expressing the generating series
$s(X; Y)$ of these qMZVs as
$\sum \prod_j (1 + X_j)^{n_j - 1} (1 + Y_j)^{m_j - m_{j+1} - 1} q^{m_j n_j}$.

## Sources

- Benjamin Brindle, *A Unified Approach to qMZVs*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A6, Theorem 4.

articles.title: Nonempty Ohno–Okuda–Zudilin qMZVs have no constant term
articles.statement:
For every nonempty index
$(k_1, \dots, k_r)$ of natural numbers, the constant term of the Ohno–Okuda–Zudilin qMZV
$\zeta_q^{\mathrm{OOZ}}(k_1, \dots, k_r)$ is $0$.

## Sources

- Benjamin Brindle, *A Unified Approach to qMZVs*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A6, Definition of OOZ-qMZVs.

articles.title: Nonempty Schlesinger–Zudilin qMZVs have no constant term
articles.statement:
For every nonempty index
$(k_1, \dots, k_r)$ of natural numbers, the constant term of the Schlesinger–Zudilin qMZV
$\zeta_q^{\mathrm{SZ}}(k_1, \dots, k_r)$ is $0$.

## Sources

- Benjamin Brindle, *A Unified Approach to qMZVs*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A6, Definition of Schlesinger–Zudilin qMZVs.

articles.title: Cycle type classifies conjugacy classes of permutations
articles.statement:
For every natural number $n$,
there is a bijection from the set of conjugacy classes of the symmetric group $S_n$ to the set
of partitions of $n$ that sends the class of each permutation $\sigma$ to the cycle type of
$\sigma$: the partition of $n$ formed by the lengths of the cycles of $\sigma$, fixed points
counting as cycles of length $1$.

## Sources

- Benjamin Brindle, *A Unified Approach to qMZVs*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A6, Lemma 4.

articles.title: The OOZ-qMZV of the empty index
articles.statement:
The Ohno–Okuda–Zudilin qMZV of the empty index is $1$:
$\zeta_q^{\mathrm{OOZ}}(\varnothing) = 1$.

## Sources

- Benjamin Brindle, *A Unified Approach to qMZVs*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A6, Definition of OOZ-qMZVs.

articles.title: Ohno–Okuda–Zudilin q-multiple zeta values
articles.statement:
For an index $(k_1, \dots, k_r)$ of natural
numbers with $r \ge 1$, the (extended) Ohno–Okuda–Zudilin qMZV is the formal power series in $q$
over $\mathbb{Q}$

$$\zeta_q^{\mathrm{OOZ}}(k_1, \dots, k_r) = \sum_{m_1 > \dots > m_r > 0}
\frac{q^{m_1}}{(1 - q^{m_1})^{k_1} \cdots (1 - q^{m_r})^{k_r}},$$

and $\zeta_q^{\mathrm{OOZ}}(\varnothing) = 1$ for the empty index. The summands with $m_1 > N$
have $q$-adic order greater than $N$, so the coefficient of $q^N$ is computed from the finitely
many summands with $m_1 \le N$.

## Sources

- Benjamin Brindle, *A Unified Approach to qMZVs*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A6, Definition of OOZ-qMZVs (extended version, `k₁ ≥ 1`, `kᵢ ≥ 0`).

articles.title: Partial Ohno–Okuda–Zudilin sums
articles.statement:
For an index $(k_1, \dots, k_r)$ of natural numbers and a
natural number $M$, the partial OOZ sum is the formal power series in $q$ over $\mathbb{Q}$

$$\sum_{M > m_1 > \dots > m_r > 0} \prod_{j=1}^{r} \frac{1}{(1 - q^{m_j})^{k_j}},$$

the defining sum of $\zeta_q^{\mathrm{OOZ}}(k_1, \dots, k_r)$ with the factor $q^{m_1}$ removed and
truncated to $m_1 < M$. For the empty index it is $1$, for every $M$ (including $M = 0$).

## Sources

- Benjamin Brindle, *A Unified Approach to qMZVs*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A6, Definition of OOZ-qMZVs (inner sums of the defining series).

articles.title: Partial sums of general qMZVs
articles.statement:
Let $(k_1, Q_1), \dots, (k_r, Q_r)$ be pairs of natural
numbers $k_j$ and polynomials $Q_j \in \mathbb{Q}[X]$, and let $M$ be a natural number. The
partial sum is the formal power series in $q$ over $\mathbb{Q}$

$$\sum_{M > m_1 > \dots > m_r > 0} \prod_{j=1}^{r} \frac{Q_j(q^{m_j})}{(1 - q^{m_j})^{k_j}},$$

where the sum runs over integers $m_1, \dots, m_r$ and $1/(1 - q^m)$ is the inverse in
$\mathbb{Q}[[q]]$. For $r = 0$ it equals $1$ for every $M$.

## Sources

- Benjamin Brindle, *A Unified Approach to qMZVs*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A6, Definition of qMZVs (after Bachmann–Kühn), defining sum truncated at `m₁ < M`.

articles.title: Partitions from Schlesinger–Zudilin qMZVs
articles.statement:
Let $\zeta_q^{SZ}$ denote the
Schlesinger–Zudilin qMZV, $\{1\}^r$ the index of $r$ ones and $p(N)$ the number of
partitions of $N$. For all natural numbers $N \ge 1$ and $R \ge N$, the coefficient of $q^N$ in
$\sum_{r=1}^{R} \zeta_q^{SZ}(\{1\}^r)$ equals $p(N)$.

Since the summands with $r > N$ have no $q^N$ term, this is the coefficientwise form of
$\sum_{r \ge 1} \zeta_q^{SZ}(\{1\}^r) = \sum_{N \ge 1} p(N) q^N$.

## Sources

- Benjamin Brindle, *A Unified Approach to qMZVs*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A6, Lemma 3.

articles.title: Recursion for block indices
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $k$, $d$ and a list $L$ of pairs of
natural numbers, the block index of the list with first pair $(k, d)$ followed by $L$ is $k$,
followed by $d - 1$ zeros (none when $d = 0$), followed by the block index of $L$.

## Sources

- Benjamin Brindle, *A Unified Approach to qMZVs*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A6, Theorem 5, index notation.

articles.title: Block index of the empty list
articles.statement:
The block index of the empty list of pairs is the empty
index.

## Sources

- Benjamin Brindle, *A Unified Approach to qMZVs*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A6, Theorem 5, index notation.

articles.title: Block indices for Schlesinger–Zudilin qMZVs
articles.statement:
For a list of pairs of natural numbers
$(k_1, d_1), \dots, (k_r, d_r)$, the block index is the index
$(k_1, \{0\}^{d_1 - 1}, \dots, k_r, \{0\}^{d_r - 1})$ obtained by concatenating, for
$j = 1, \dots, r$, the entry $k_j$ followed by $d_j - 1$ zeros (no zeros when $d_j = 0$).

## Sources

- Benjamin Brindle, *A Unified Approach to qMZVs*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A6, Theorem 4 and Theorem 5 (SZ duality), index notation.

articles.title: The empty Schlesinger–Zudilin qMZV
articles.statement:
The Schlesinger–Zudilin qMZV of the empty index is
$1$: $\zeta_q^{SZ}(\emptyset) = 1$.

## Sources

- Benjamin Brindle, *A Unified Approach to qMZVs*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A6, Definition of Schlesinger–Zudilin qMZVs.

articles.title: Schlesinger–Zudilin duality
articles.statement:
Let $\zeta_q^{SZ}$ denote the Schlesinger–Zudilin qMZV, let
$(k_1, d_1), \dots, (k_r, d_r)$ be pairs of natural numbers with $k_j \ge 1$ and $d_j \ge 1$
for all $j$, and let $\{0\}^n$ denote $n$ zeros. Then

$$\zeta_q^{SZ}(k_1, \{0\}^{d_1 - 1}, \dots, k_r, \{0\}^{d_r - 1}) =
\zeta_q^{SZ}(d_r, \{0\}^{k_r - 1}, \dots, d_1, \{0\}^{k_1 - 1}).$$

That is, $\zeta_q^{SZ}$ takes the same value at the block index of the list of pairs and at
the block index of the reversed list with each pair swapped.

## Sources

- Benjamin Brindle, *A Unified Approach to qMZVs*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A6, Theorem 5 (SZ duality, Zhao).

articles.title: Schlesinger–Zudilin qMZVs
articles.statement:
For an index $k = (k_1, \dots, k_r)$ of natural numbers, the
Schlesinger–Zudilin qMZV $\zeta_q^{SZ}(k)$ is the formal power series in $q$ over $\mathbb{Q}$
whose coefficient of $q^N$, for each $N \ge 0$, is the coefficient of $q^N$ in the partial sum

$$\sum_{N \ge m_1 > \dots > m_r > 0} \prod_{j=1}^{r} \frac{q^{m_j k_j}}{(1 - q^{m_j})^{k_j}}$$

over integers $m_1, \dots, m_r$. In particular $\zeta_q^{SZ}(\emptyset) = 1$.

When the index is empty or $k_1 \ge 1$, the summands with $m_1 > N$ have no term of degree at
most $N$, so $\zeta_q^{SZ}(k)$ is the full series
$\sum_{m_1 > \dots > m_r > 0} \prod_{j} q^{m_j k_j} / (1 - q^{m_j})^{k_j}$. The paper does not
define the value when $k_1 = 0$.

## Sources

- Benjamin Brindle, *A Unified Approach to qMZVs*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A6, Definition of Schlesinger–Zudilin qMZVs (extended version of Ebrahimi-Fard, Manchon and Singer, allowing `kⱼ = 0` for `j ≥ 2`).

articles.title: Recursion for partial sums of Schlesinger–Zudilin qMZVs
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $k_1$ and
$M$ and an index $\kappa = (k_2, \dots, k_r)$ (possibly empty), write $Z_M(k_1, \kappa)$ and
$Z_m(\kappa)$ for the partial sums of Schlesinger–Zudilin qMZVs with bounds $M$ and $m$. Then

$$Z_M(k_1, \kappa) = \sum_{0 < m < M} \left(\frac{q^m}{1 - q^m}\right)^{k_1} Z_m(\kappa).$$

## Sources

- Benjamin Brindle, *A Unified Approach to qMZVs*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A6, Definition of Schlesinger–Zudilin qMZVs.

articles.title: Partial sums of Schlesinger–Zudilin qMZVs
articles.statement:
For an index $(k_1, \dots, k_r)$ of natural
numbers and a natural number $M$, the partial sum is the formal power series in $q$ over
$\mathbb{Q}$

$$\sum_{M > m_1 > \dots > m_r > 0} \prod_{j=1}^{r} \frac{q^{m_j k_j}}{(1 - q^{m_j})^{k_j}},$$

where the sum runs over integers $m_1, \dots, m_r$ and $1/(1 - q^m)$ is the inverse in
$\mathbb{Q}[[q]]$. For the empty index it equals $1$ for every $M$.

## Sources

- Benjamin Brindle, *A Unified Approach to qMZVs*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A6, Definition of Schlesinger–Zudilin qMZVs (defining sum truncated at `m₁ < M`).

articles.title: Block index of a prepended pair
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $a, b$ and a list $L$ of pairs of
natural numbers, the block index of the list obtained by prepending $(a, b)$ to $L$ consists of
the entry $a + 1$, followed by $b - 1$ entries equal to $1$ (none when $b = 0$), followed by the
block index of $L$.

## Sources

- Benjamin Brindle, *A Unified Approach to qMZVs*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A6, Theorem 7, index notation.

articles.title: Block index of a list of pairs
articles.statement:
The block index of a list
$[(a_1, b_1), \dots, (a_r, b_r)]$ of pairs of natural numbers is the index
$(a_1 + 1, \{1\}^{b_1 - 1}, \dots, a_r + 1, \{1\}^{b_r - 1})$, where $\{1\}^n$ stands for $n$
consecutive entries equal to $1$ and $b_j - 1$ is truncated at $0$.

When all $a_j, b_j \ge 1$ this is an admissible index; it corresponds to the word
$x^{a_1} y^{b_1} \cdots x^{a_r} y^{b_r}$ of the space $\mathfrak{h}^0$ of admissible words in
the letters $x, y$, and the duality $\tau$, the anti-automorphism of
$\mathbb{Q}\langle x, y \rangle$ exchanging $x$ and $y$, maps this word to the word of the block
index of $[(b_r, a_r), \dots, (b_1, a_1)]$.

## Sources

- Benjamin Brindle, *A Unified Approach to qMZVs*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A6, Theorem 6 and Theorem 7 (BZ duality), index notation.

articles.title: Bradley–Zhao duality for q-multiple zeta values
articles.statement:
For every $r \ge 0$ and all natural
numbers $a_1, b_1, \dots, a_r, b_r \ge 1$, the Bradley–Zhao q-multiple zeta values satisfy

$$\zeta_q^{BZ}(a_1 + 1, \{1\}^{b_1 - 1}, \dots, a_r + 1, \{1\}^{b_r - 1}) =
\zeta_q^{BZ}(b_r + 1, \{1\}^{a_r - 1}, \dots, b_1 + 1, \{1\}^{a_1 - 1}),$$

where $\{1\}^n$ stands for $n$ consecutive entries equal to $1$.

In terms of words this is $\zeta_q^{BZ} \circ \tau = \zeta_q^{BZ}$ on the space $\mathfrak{h}^0$ of
admissible words, where $\tau$ is the anti-automorphism of $\mathbb{Q}\langle x, y \rangle$
exchanging $x$ and $y$.

## Sources

- Benjamin Brindle, *A Unified Approach to qMZVs*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A6, Theorem 7 (BZ duality, Bradley; Seki–Yamamoto).

articles.title: Bradley–Zhao qMZV of the empty index
articles.statement:
The Bradley–Zhao q-multiple zeta value of the
empty index is $\zeta_q^{BZ}(\varnothing) = 1$.

## Sources

- Benjamin Brindle, *A Unified Approach to qMZVs*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A6, Definition of Bradley–Zhao qMZVs.

articles.title: Bradley–Zhao q-multiple zeta values
articles.statement:
For an index $k = (k_1, \dots, k_r)$ of natural
numbers, the Bradley–Zhao q-multiple zeta value is the general qMZV
$\zeta_q^{BZ}(k) = \zeta_q(k_1, \dots, k_r; X^{k_1 - 1}, \dots, X^{k_r - 1})$, a formal power
series in $q$ over $\mathbb{Q}$, where $k_j - 1$ is truncated at $0$. For an admissible index
($k_1 \ge 2$ and all $k_i \ge 1$) it equals

$$\zeta_q^{BZ}(k) = \sum_{m_1 > \dots > m_r > 0} \prod_{j=1}^{r}
\frac{q^{m_j (k_j - 1)}}{(1 - q^{m_j})^{k_j}};$$

for other indices the value has no intended meaning.

## Sources

- Benjamin Brindle, *A Unified Approach to qMZVs*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A6, Definition of Bradley–Zhao qMZVs.

articles.title: Nonempty Bradley–Zhao qMZVs have no constant term
articles.statement:
For every nonempty index
$(k_1, \dots, k_r)$ of natural numbers, the constant coefficient of the Bradley–Zhao
q-multiple zeta value $\zeta_q^{BZ}(k_1, \dots, k_r)$ is $0$.

## Sources

- Benjamin Brindle, *A Unified Approach to qMZVs*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A6, Definition of Bradley–Zhao qMZVs.

articles.title: Nonempty general qMZVs have no constant term
articles.statement:
For every nonempty list
$(k_1, Q_1), \dots, (k_r, Q_r)$ of natural numbers $k_j$ and polynomials $Q_j \in \mathbb{Q}[X]$,
the constant coefficient of the general q-multiple zeta value
$\zeta_q(k_1, \dots, k_r; Q_1, \dots, Q_r)$ is $0$. No condition on $Q_1(0)$ is assumed.

## Sources

- Benjamin Brindle, *A Unified Approach to qMZVs*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A6, Definition of qMZVs.

articles.title: Membership criterion for partitions in Stanley coordinates
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $r$ and
$N$, a pair $((m_1, \dots, m_r), (n_1, \dots, n_r))$ of $r$-tuples of natural numbers lies in the
set $\mathcal{P}_r(N)$ of partitions of $N$ of length $r$ in Stanley coordinates if and only if
$m_1 > m_2 > \dots > m_r$, every $m_j$ and every $n_j$ is positive, and
$m_1 n_1 + \dots + m_r n_r = N$.

## Sources

- Benjamin Brindle, *A Unified Approach to qMZVs*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A6, Definition of `𝒫_r(N)` (Section 4).

articles.title: The constant series one lies in every space of qMZVs
articles.statement:
For every natural number $d$, the
constant power series $1$ lies in the $\mathbb{Q}$-span $\mathcal{Z}_{q,d}$ of the general
q-multiple zeta values $\zeta_q(k_1, \dots, k_r; Q_1, \dots, Q_r)$ with $Q_1(0) = 0$ and
$\deg Q_j + d \le k_j$ for all $j$, where the zero polynomial is given degree $0$; it is the
qMZV of the empty index.

## Sources

- Benjamin Brindle, *A Unified Approach to qMZVs*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A6, Definition of qMZVs (ii).

articles.title: General qMZV of the empty index
articles.statement:
The general q-multiple zeta value of the empty data is
$\zeta_q(\varnothing; \varnothing) = 1$.

## Sources

- Benjamin Brindle, *A Unified Approach to qMZVs*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A6, Definition of qMZVs.

articles.title: General q-multiple zeta values
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $k_1, \dots, k_r$ and polynomials
$Q_1, \dots, Q_r \in \mathbb{Q}[X]$, the general qMZV $\zeta_q(k_1, \dots, k_r; Q_1, \dots, Q_r)$
is the formal power series in $q$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ whose coefficient of $q^N$, for every $N$, is
the coefficient of $q^N$ in the finite sum
$\sum_{N \ge m_1 > m_2 > \dots > m_r > 0} \prod_{j=1}^{r} Q_j(q^{m_j}) / (1 - q^{m_j})^{k_j}$
over integers $m_1, \dots, m_r$, and $\zeta_q(\varnothing; \varnothing) = 1$.

When $Q_1(0) = 0$ (the paper's condition $Q_1 \in X \mathbb{Q}[X]$), the summands with
$m_1 > N$ have $q$-adic order greater than $N$, so this is the series
$\sum_{m_1 > \dots > m_r > 0} \prod_{j=1}^{r} Q_j(q^{m_j}) / (1 - q^{m_j})^{k_j}$; for other data
the value is a junk value.

## Sources

- Benjamin Brindle, *A Unified Approach to qMZVs*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A6, Definition of qMZVs (after Bachmann–Kühn).

articles.title: Spanning sets of Ohno–Okuda–Zudilin qMZVs
articles.statement:
Let $\mathcal{Z}_{q,1}$ and $\mathcal{Z}_q$ be
the spaces $\mathcal{Z}_{q,d}$ of general qMZVs for $d = 1$ and $d = 0$. Then (i)
$\mathcal{Z}_{q,1}$ is the $\mathbb{Q}$-span of the Ohno–Okuda–Zudilin qMZVs
$\zeta_q^{\mathrm{OOZ}}(k_1, \dots, k_r)$ over all indices of natural numbers with $k_i \ge 1$ for
every $i$ and $k_1 \ge 2$ when $r \ge 1$; and (ii) $\mathcal{Z}_q$ is the $\mathbb{Q}$-span of the
$\zeta_q^{\mathrm{OOZ}}(k_1, \dots, k_r)$ over all indices of natural numbers with $k_1 \ge 1$
